title: Will Johnson | Training Camp 7.29.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Second training camp. How does it feel compared to last year? Uh, it feels good.  I definitely feel much more comfortable.  Everyone has been in good spirits, with good energy, so it's been great so far. Ending the first day with shoulder pads .  How did it feel to have a little energy boost? That felt good.  I mean, we had a lot of energy.  The knocks sounded.  The first game was a bit hectic, but it was great to watch.  Were you surprised to see your high school t-shirt there yesterday? Yes, definitely.  I hadn't seen it since I was back home in Michigan, I don't even know how she got it or where she got it from, but it was something cool.  Do you have one of those? Yes, I have one at home.  I have my home and away jerseys at home.  What about the Buffs? Have you seen them in Arizona? Not much yet, but hopefully we can get fans using them this year.  How much of a better player do you feel as you begin your second year?    I feel much more comfortable.  I feel like my body is in a good place. I feel very comfortable in this defense and I know what my role is.  So I'm excited to prove it on Sundays . Everyone says the game slows down as it enters its second year.  While the rookie year is quite hectic.  Do you feel the same? Yes, definitely.  I felt that during training, how everything slowed down and you're anticipating instead of just reacting.  That allows you to make many more plays. There's a lot of talk about this group of defensive players, who will be there, and what they can do.  What do you think of what this group is capable of?  That shows the depth we have and the talent of the guys in the locker room.  So it's fun to go out and compete every day , challenge each other, and make sure no one gets complacent.  How do you approach that competition when provocations give you an advantage, but without taking it personally ? How do you handle that? Well, I just go out there and try to do what I do and be who I am, and I feel like everything else will work itself out So, how would you rate the defense in terms of its potential?  Because there seems to be a lot of potential, but that has to be turned into production.  How would you see it right now? Yes, that is our main focus. I mean, you know, ball recoveries, that changes the game.  So, being more productive, being more united, and being on the same page, I feel like, as you said, we have a lot of potential in all areas, from the defensive line and the linebackers to the backcourt.  So, as long as we play together and are on the same page, I think we'll make a lot of plays.  Did you have any " welcome to the NFL" moments in any games last year?  I'd say probably against the Rams, the first time.  I had never allowed passes the way I did in that game.  So facing those two guys who are so talented, and with a quarterback like that on the other side, it was definitely seeing what it's like to face that when it all comes together.    Did Mike mention that game to you?  He's talked to me a little bit about what Stafford said about me or things like that, but I don't really want to say it, but yeah, it was quite a positive thing too.  So yes, it was good to know.  What was it like that night after the game when you got home? What was that moment of reflection like for you?    It was difficult.  I feel like right after the game, that night, and even today I hate watching the videos.  So it will always be a motivation to do better in those moments, to be prepared for those moments and to do everything possible to avoid those moments. Trying to remember, did you play in the second game against the Rams? Mhm.  Was it better? Yes, I think I did better, without a doubt. The coach was talking earlier about finding that fine line between obsessing over doing things right and moving on to the next play.  How do you deal with that mindset?  It's a fast-paced game, but you have to move on and at the same time concentrate so you don't make the same mistake twice. Yes, I feel it's just as you said, in terms of being competitive and competing in the locker room.  In other words, you have to stay present and manage what you can control.  Hey, stay in the moment, because thinking about the past or the future really won't help you in any situation.  So, stay in the moment and focus on what you need to do; that will help you win that play.

title: Paris Johnson Jr | Training Camp 7.29.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Coming into training camp, I like to listen to some gospel music. So, it's really the main thing and I've been listening to some like some Jamaican music lately. >> Okay. >> Not that I have any Jamaican roots, but I don't know. It's been a kind of like vibe relaxing music cuz you get in here, you know, the rap music plays pretty quickly. >> Yeah. >> So, it's just a different kind of um vibe going. >> Yeah, I like Fred Hammond, Kirk Franklin. Those are my go-to gospel stations. >> Um yeah, all those yeah, those people you named um but I would say I don't I don't really remember them all by name, but it's like I listen to the same 20 songs that I I listen and it it just gets me going, you know, the same way that that that rapping gets some people going. I feel like just the gospel gets me going like that spiritual fire, you know what I mean? >> Yeah. If you could trade libraries with anyone in the the locker room, who would you trade music libraries with? >> Uh um mhm It's a good question. Somebody currently here right now? >> Anybody. They could be standing here, they could not be. You just know what they got in rotation. You've been in their car, you know what they play. Yeah, it could be Mark Dalton. We don't know. You know, it could be coach LaFleur. >> Mhm. Uh I'll say coach LaFleur only because I haven't heard any of his music, but he named somebody today as one of his favorite artists and I've I have not heard of maybe like Benny Boone or something. >> Oh, Benson Boone? >> Yeah, Benson Boone. I just heard that name for the first time today. >> He does like backflips off pianos. >> Yeah, I don't even know >> why somebody would attempt that, but yeah, I mean, so I'd probably trade with him just to find out what that's about. He seemed pretty animated about Benson Boone. So, I guess find out who that is. That'd be an interesting trade. >> Awesome. >> More so just to see what it's about. Awesome. >> So, when you guys put the pads on and coach LaFleur admits that 11 on 11 is his favorite drill, so when you get a lot of padded opportunities doing 11 on 11, how much does that help the continuity of the offensive line specifically? >> Yeah, I mean we love being able to play 11 on 11 cuz that's just real football. You know, anything else is kind of like uh kind of too orchestrated. You know what I mean? Whether offense wins the defense wins, it's not real football. But 11 on 11 is as real as it gets outside of Sundays. So yeah, that's definitely the most fun part of the day. >> Chemistry is it's critical with an offensive line. I've heard coaches say it's not just about your five best, it's sometimes about your best five and how you guys play together and understanding the unspoken word, the spoken word. All that gets developed in training camp. >> Yeah, that's the truth. Being able to get a lot of reps um with these guys, especially with Isaac him coming in and him playing side by side, all that's just developed um well so far. But again, it's it's still early on, so I'm excited to see how that continues. >> Yeah, and what has to happen for you guys to continue for you guys to be a consistently great offensive line the entire season aside from health? >> Yeah, I mean I think right now just starting to win win today. I think being able to win today is the main goal. It's about again, about to repeat myself for the third time again, being able to win today and then again tomorrow be able to come in with a mindset to watch, learn and reflect. And if you made a mistake, not make that same mistake again. And I think that and I think that's growth. So I think growth is what's going to be able to allow this offensive line to be able to do what we want to do. >> It looks like you guys are going to have a really fun running back group to block for this year. I mean there's I mean this decimated last year by injury and now with the emergence of Love and the signing of Algiers, looks like it's going to be a potentially really fun group to block for. >> Yeah, I'm excited for the group of guys that that we got back there toting the ball. Now those guys are all excited to be able to share the ball to get downhill and we're excited to block for those guys.

title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference 7.29.26 | AZ Cardinals

Um that's that's part of the human interaction. Sometimes you know that someone needs something. Sometimes you know to stay away. Um and each guy's a little bit different. So uh being in that receiver room for a lot of a lot of my career. Um you you you go kind of one day at a time, one player at a time, one play at a time. >> He's obviously a very cerebral and calculated player in terms of how he approaches the game. C can that have a flip side where he can like get in his own head in terms of negative plays? >> Uh that that's you're right. He is a sub cerebral guy. Excuse me, I can't even spell it or say it. I'm just talking in general over the time being with players is where is that fine line where it's obsessive and it locks you up, but also, you know, where it just gives you that edge. And each guy's a little bit different. And I can think of a bunch of guys off the top of my head where man it it it worked for them to to you know find that edge and there's others that just overdid it and they were locked up and um so yeah I mean I think all those guys that just understand the game it's it's you know finding that fine line and try to help them as a coach get to that point but ultimately they're the ones you know thinking about it when they're away from us as well. How >> cool is it when you see teammates all going out like Marv yesterday after the drop just touching him up consoling him just saying hey get the next one. Yeah, it's it's great. I mean, he's just he's just about it, you know? And so, uh, it's been good to see him through the, you know, late parts of July. Uh, so we need to continue to go like this. >> It seems like you guys really like Isaiah Adams and what he brings at right guard. Um, he's had some inconsistencies throughout his career, also some strong stretches. What is it that you guys really like about him and what he >> Yeah, I think he's a he's a strong and sturdy dude on the inside and you think about his journey right from from Canada and Illinois and all the things and you know kind of um getting getting kind of that next level education of football a little bit later than some of these other guys and so you knew there was a quote unquote developmental aspect of him when he was coming out and I just think there's been there's been times when you watch it again not being here but where you just saw you know really good play And now then it was, hey, how can we consistently have this really good play? I think every single day has been a learning opportunity for him. And I think uh he's he's just continued to get a little bit better every single day. >> When you watched back the tape on from last year, like what was the difference in him from early in the season when he did get benched to then later in the season when he seemed to find his way? >> I I don't know. There's so many factors with that. I mean, you you could go off the silent tape with that, but uh there there there was there's the continuity thing is real. You know, we're always going to be next man up because that's the league and and you know, ultimately you're going to have a ton of uh you're you're going to have injuries. Hopefully, not a ton. Uh knock on wood, but you know what I mean. There's going to be guys at at at every position that are going to um that get hurt at some point. And that happened amongst this whole roster, but particularly up front. And so just not combination blocking with the same guys week in and week out. Like as you string those practices together and then spring those you string those games together ultimately you're just going to build confidence with each other and with confidence becomes belief. And um you know I don't know if that was able to happen with a lot of our guys last year. And so uh you know again that's all I can speak on but but you saw the talent you saw the talent coming out and again just uh it's been a pleasure working with him and in his approach. >> You've been in a lot of training camps. been around a lot of really smart football minds, but nothing can really prepare you as a first time head coach going into a training camp. Has everything gone according to plan for you? Like, do you still kind of have to pinch yourself and be like, "Okay, I'm the head coach of the Arizona Cardinals," or do you still feel like everything's really on track and felt like >> Yeah, I mean, you try to reflect every single night when you go back um and and you know, have a little bit of me time, if you will, because you don't get much of that anymore. used to be able to just kind of close my door a little bit for a couple hours and think about offensive football, but that's not necessarily the case, even though I try to, but usually someone's at the door or something like that. I'm just looking at Mark. I'm not saying it's Mark. Um, but uh, no, it's um, but but yeah, you try to reflect on it, but again, I I try to just take it one day at a time. Um, you know, lean on the people that that have been here, lean on the people that have been at other places, reflect on my own, uh, you know, personal experiences in the other places, talk to the, you know, the veterans, stuff like that, and just take it one day at a time. Like, can we just handle today? Like, these guys, I don't I don't want them worrying about tomorrow. Like, my message say to to today to him was, hey, we had a a good padded practice yesterday. I I like the physicality for day one. I like the juice for day one. There was a lot to clean up and now we're coming back for day two and there's going to be considerably a lot more reps today. Um, and then today, tomorrow ends up being a jog through, but we can't worry about tomorrow. And stress plus rest equals growth. Well, today we got to stress ourselves. Like, we have to stress ourselves. We have to continue to move the needle forward. And then tomorrow we get to rest and and have uh more physical rest while still tapping into the mental and then finish out the block. But ultimately, now tie it back. All you have to worry about today, stress yourself. All right? uh push yourself to the limit today within the confines of taking care of each other while also being physical. >> You got to know Walter Nolan's personality very well. >> I have. >> How would you describe him? >> Um all ball stud. Um loves it and he can be as good as he wants to be.

title: Coby Bryant discusses his leadership goals | Press Conference
text: How did you handle the uh up downs buying into this? >> Yeah. Um I'm actually going to go up to DA's office and tell them that was pretty pretty easy. So, >> [snorts] >> uh I'm not going to do that. I'm just playing. [laughter] But it it wasn't it wasn't bad, man. It's a mindset thing, honestly. Um like I told the guys, we're going to deal with way harder stuff than 40 up downs is just uh allowing us to buy in and uh you know, nobody was on their own out there. We're all together, so >> wasn't bad. When was the >> last time you did? >> Honestly, I couldn't tell you. probably be little league, but um you know, I ran a lot of heels over the over the break. Um so, you know, that wasn't too challenging. Like I said, it just was a true testament who's been working. So, >> PA said that you you epitomize what they want to do at defense. How would you describe that? >> Um honestly, it's just a blessing coming from him, honestly. You know, ton of respect from from DA, honestly. Um and that's, you know, why I'm here to, you know, bring guys along. you know, we got a ton of ton of great players throughout this team. Um, especially on defense as well. And um, you know, we want to be rep well known as not just, you know, um, Coach Ben and the offense, but especially, you know, powerful on defense as well too. You know, we want to create our name as far as the turnovers, the play style, uh, the mentality. You know, that's something that we want to bring to this team. >> You said you were talking to the guys about encountered during the season. >> Are you asserting yourself already in a captain type role? >> Yeah. Yeah, for sure. Honestly, um I mean that's the mindset I've been had since I've came into the league. Obviously, as a rookie, it's a lot harder. But now that it's year five, that's something that I take pride on. That's actually on one of my goals. I write my goals out every year and uh put them on my window. Uh my mirror, I'm sorry. My mirror, uh my binder, that's something I always keep. And um you know, a captain is something that's on there for sure. >> Any other goals written on that sheet? >> Uh I can't tell you all of them, but um definitely to win another Super Bowl is on there for sure. Yeah, >> when you talk about play style. How do you describe yours? >> The biggest thing I want to do is um, you know, be known for like energy, that's something that I've always want to, you know, be known for. I feel like it's it can be contagious and like I said, is bring other guys along with me as well and that's something I want to do. >> Dennis was talking about the importance of consistency throughout the entire defense. When you think of like because he was so complimentary of you, when you think of like consistency every day, what do you have to do? What do players have to do to make sure you remain consistent? >> The biggest thing is just taking it one day at a time. It's day one. You know, a lot of guys have energy and, you know, full speed today. Um, the biggest thing is, like I said, I want to tell the guys is let's see how you feel day four, day five. It's it's a mindset thing. Just take it one play at a time, one day at a time, and um, you know, just know what your responsibility, help guys along with you and um, bring them along as well. >> I know it's early, but is there something that you and Dylan have kind of locked in on right away that you were like, "Oh, we're going to be really good at this." >> Yeah, for sure. For sure. He's he's very knowledgeable. Like I said previously, he knows the game. You know, I don't really have to tell him too much. Uh we're on the same page every snap of the ball. We can communicate off the field as well, too. Um he's going to be a great young player for sure, and I'm excited to play along with him. >> Kobe was the rep, I think, in the first team period. I think y'all was in man and you and Jaylen Johnson after the play kind of pointing to each other about either how y'all pass it off, how y'all wanted to pass it off. What's been the process of kind of getting on the same page, communicating with your teammates? >> Yeah. Yeah, it's been a a great communication. Honestly, that's especially on the back end. That's something we have to do. as safeties, we have to communicate to everyone and um you know, all of us have been on the same page from OTAAS up until now. Like I said, it's only day one, so we got to keep building that. >> How do you build the cohesion as a secondary during camp over the next six weeks and trying to get everybody kind of locked in together? >> Yeah. Um just like I said previously, just one day at a time. Um like I it's early right now and just keep competing, you know, you know, it's like I told them, stand the book, continuously work hard each and every day. And um you know, we're all, like I said, we're in this together. Nobody's on their own. Ask questions. I even told the younger guys, just ask me as many questions. Text me, whatever. You know, come to my room and, you know, we can study, plays, uh, whatever, whatever the case may be. >> This is super early, but what have you noticed or gotten to know about Caleb Williams and who he is a leader? >> True. True. Like I said, true leader, true competitor. I love that about him. He was dialed in today. He was locked in the locker room today. I was trying to mess with him a little bit, but he was too locked in. So, maybe I thought he was going to throw me one today, but he didn't. Um, but honestly, man, I'm excited to be here and play with him. Um, he's he's bright future. Like I continuously keep saying, he's the sky's is the limit. Not even the limit, but he's he's going to be a great quarterback for sure. >> When you decide to go to a place, um, how important is it that they have quarterbacks that you think that can >> Yeah, for sure. It's very important. I've been blessed to play with some good quarterbacks as well. And um just playing with somebody so young is exciting, you know, just to be able to witness his growth in the league and see see that it's going to be special for sure. >> Yeah, I know Money speaks loudly, but if you had gotten an offer from a place that didn't really have an answer at quarterback, >> that disqualif would that have been disqualified? >> Uh see see what you're doing right there. But um [laughter] honestly, I'm I'm just wherever whatever they needed me at doesn't matter. This was just a great fit. I'm blessed. Um, obviously want to give a ton of love to Seattle. Um, you know, I've been there for four year. I was there for four years. Nothing bad to say about them. Great organization, great teammates, great quarterback as well, and the opportunity was just better here. And, um, I'm excited to be a part of this organization and play with Caleb and the rest of these guys. So, you know, it's definitely a great always a great feeling to have a great quarterback and leader as well, too. >> Back to last season, what traits did you see when y'all were going through camp that you want to instill here in this defense? Yeah, just building a connection uh early early enough to honestly like for me I have to be I'm not more so a big talkative guy. Um so that's something I'm have to be more vocal and um to the guys and just bring us all together you know whe whatever the case may be go to Top Golf or bowling whatever case may be outside of the building. That's something that we have to do is you know be together you know because at the end of the day we're all out there together. So that's the biggest thing. Did the coaching staff encourage you to do that? Are you kind of just figuring that out on your own that that's sort of your role? >> Um, both I would say, but more so that's something that I've known since I've been in the league or seen since I've been in the league for 5 years. That's something we have to do is not just be connected in the building, but outside the building as well, too. So, we're brothers at the end of the day and you know, we're in this together. >> Couple more emphasis to add team speed. Can you already feel that when you're out there in the first training camp practice? >> For sure. For sure. That's back to what I was saying. you know, day one guys we just have on helmets, guys are out there flying around. Uh it's good to see, you know, honestly, but the biggest thing is when we put on pads, um just, you know, the the mental aspect of it is training camp is long. Uh it's tiring, but you know, you have to push through and uh that's back to the mindset aspect of it is just keep keep going honestly, one day at a time. >> Last one, Chris, what are your impressions about Jaylen Johnson? What do you think of him from afar as you watched him play before? >> Yeah, for sure. I've been watch this tape since college. uh elite competitor, dominance in man, can tackle, can make make plays on the ball honestly and uh we we connected right away early. So uh me and him have a great connection early. Obviously more room to grow and you know keep connecting as well too but excited to be playing with them. >> Thanks guys. >> Yeah, thank you.

title: Caleb Williams on starting his third NFL season | Press Conference
text: What's up everybody? Good to see everybody. Glad to be back. Let's get it rolling. [sighs] >> [gasps] >> Your head coach mentioned that one of the goals like that your your next level one of the things you mentioned was coverage recognition. >> Mhm. >> Where do you think you are with that and how difficult is that with so many defenses doing so many so much disguising and and different looks that they're going to give you obviously? >> Yeah. Um Uh it's not like I haven't played football for the past many years or so and so um it's it's it's more or less what he's saying is taking a step up in that in that direction. Um you know, pre-snap procedure and all of that has been a lot better than you know the the first time that I started it. Um and started doing that but you know, it's it's more have an idea what they'll be and things like that. You know, plays get a little bit more detailed. Um he's adding more on my plate of of figuring out uh the coverage before and have an idea of of where I can go with the ball faster sooner and sooner. Um I I haven't thrown a lot of picks in my career is is because um I can see the coverage and and and feel the coverage. Um and so it's a little bit more detailed from play uh play to play and and specifics within the play uh you know, towards the coverage that we're attacking um and then add more more plays in there so that uh we can kill and alert and and and check to these different you know, man checks um you know, cover two checks one high whatever whatever case may be. So it's it's a little bit more of that um but um you know, we're excited about that. I'm excited. Uh the the challenge that that he's get you know, he's giving me uh to to be able to take the next step and and progress uh is is you know, what I'm most excited about and and it's going to be hard it's going to be tough just like it is every year and so uh that's that's what you embrace that you would that's what you enjoy um because when it shows up on game days and Sundays and whatever day that we play on um you know, it's it's it's very rewarding. >> Jalen, your your sack total came way way down last year independent of the play caller and the improved protection. What was your interpretation of how you got better in that area of reducing that number? >> Yeah, getting the ball out, um and and whether it's it's making a guy miss, um throwing the ball away, dirt in it sometimes. I know sometimes it may not look like that, but dirt it sometimes. I had a couple of those today. Um just getting the ball in my hands and dirt in it saving for the next play. Um just trying to play smart football. And then other than that, just just being better at, you know, when when I lose my feet or um you know, something happens and and the coverage isn't there, O line maybe, you know, a little leaky or so. Just want to check down and get those guys the ball. Um have have positive more positive uh plays even though the play may not be designed to go to that person. Um when check downs and things like that, have more positive uh small plays. Um so, that's that's a part of the goal this year. >> Guys who get sacked as much as you did your rookie year get scarred by it. >> Yep. >> How did you avoid that happening to you? >> Yeah. Um the the trust, the faith uh between my O line, the trust and faith between my myself and the running back. Uh the trust and faith and and and learning the offense, um and being able to help, uh knowing where it's going to come from uh before it happens. Um and then being able to maybe take a step over, get out, uh step up, anything like that. Uh just knowing where the hots are, uh just having a better idea with that. And then, you know, hopefully this year uh just doing a better job with, you know, maybe changing a protection, getting us out of something. Um you know, just to be able to get the ball out my hands and and and, you know, protect us, protect O line, protect, you know, running back, all of us on the team. And um I think that's going to be a a goal of mine this year also. >> You know, the best >> Go ahead. >> The best way to go of of 70%. I'm sure that's in the back of your mind, but how do you balance, you know, being cognizant of that without sacrificing or losing any bit of your natural ability or natural desires to, you know, hunt big games or whatever? >> Yeah, if I hit I think I I don't know how many passes I threw last year, guys, but probably threw 400 something, 500 passes or so. If I hit 90 more, we're at 65. >> Yeah, but I'm not even really harping on you getting the number or not. What I'm saying mentally does that affect how you go about playing the game? >> no, no, no. Just hit the easy ones. You know, when they're there, when they're there. Be in rhythm with myself. Be confident in my guys. Be confident within the play. Deliver a good ball. Deliver a catchable ball. And then from there when things happen, I put on the cape and and go do my thing whenever that happens, but it's not it's not something needs to be on or showing at least until the moment shows up. >> We know how much really just puzzled by what was happening. >> Cuz you'd been a very accurate passer at >> Now do you feel like with Ben you have a clear cut idea of what has hindered you in that area and what is the road map to fixing it? >> Yeah, part of it's just confidence in the offense and and and not Ben, but the offense in the sense of me knowing where I'm supposed to go with the ball, not second guessing, being decisive. You know, eyes being on the on the right spot, things like that. Not not having to react so much in the sense of something shows up, oh, I got to react. It's it's more or less of I know this is about to happen. Let's deliver this guy a good ball. If it you know, if he covers down, I know where you know, the next guy's going to be or whatever the case may be. You know, who we're high lowing, you know, who we're reading off of. All these different things. So, it's just gaining and gathering a better understanding of the offense so the confidence grows within myself and the receivers. You know, second year receivers, most of the guys out there so it's second year or more. The confidence with them, the confidence within themselves to be able to run the right route. How to run it, you know, and and and creating space to when you know, when they're running a route and they're not just running a route off the board. So, a lot of confidence goes into the work. A lot of confidence goes into to myself and then and then to coaching and you know, everybody else. >> You and Ben last year You something to the effect of that Ben had coached you so hard that you thought he didn't like you. >> Is he still communicating with you the same way? >> Oh, yeah. >> Or you're just taking it better? >> Oh, yeah. Well, I just I I know uh we have a real common goal. Um and it's to find a way to make the Chicago Bears uh champions at the end of the day. Um and so, what he says um everything he says and what we've been through like I said, everything he says and and and what he says to me I I'll I'll do it at 200% and and uh you know, won't look back. And so, that's that's kind of how it is now. Um if he if he yells and curses at me or anything like that, I know it's it's for the greater good of the team. And so, uh whatever whatever it takes is is what it what it's going to take. >> You wore the C on your chest as a captain and but you're two with Ben, you're three in the league. Yeah, how much different does the leadership aspect feel for you and your comfort in that role? >> Yeah. Um it's it's been able to step up and and speak up more. Uh been in this uh been in this league for 2 years, but also playing I've played I've played a bunch of games now. Um and so, I know what losing looks like, I know what winning looks like in this league. Uh we haven't won the big one yet, but um you know, we we won a bunch of games last year. We lost a lot of games my first year. Um and then and then now having year two in the offense, a lot more confidence in what I'm saying uh to the guys out there. Um it it's starting to sound more like the coaches, um the steps, alignments and things like that. So, uh just just find a ways to be more on top of that um you know, day in and day out. Um been able to uh help those guys whenever they ask a question. Um and then and then from there um just just leading by example is one of the biggest ones. Um I've always said that and then lastly, uh when something needs to be spoken about or said to um a teammate or or or a coach if, you know, we're [snorts] having an issue as a team, uh be able to to go to them and and and speak to the coaches or uh speak to the team. >> You mentioned how much confidence you built with Cole Kmet towards the end of last season. I imagine that's grown even with our four months working together. What are your visions for who he can become for you this year? >> Yeah, he can become the the best tight end in the league. Um I think he is. Um but stats and um us going out there and proving it is is what it's going to take and uh to be able to do that we got to put in work. We got to build the connection, uh hang out inside and outside the building, uh have tough conversations or have open communication, you know, throughout the year and and and throughout camp. And so, uh it's going to be exciting. It's going to be fun. Um he's an easy target to throw to and I got a bunch of those guys out there um that's that's equipped and ready to go. >> So, various skill set-wise, what do you what do you like about what he gives you? >> do everything. Um he can run every route. Um there's been times I think since we had him on a post route um and we came back after after um after the game after after we ended up winning that game and came back and was like, "If you ever see that, you know, with a guy out there and he wants to not believe in that, you know, put it up there and give him a shot." Um he's such a big target, easy target, runs right uh right the right route, nice routes. Um and then and then other that he can he can run block and um disguise things. So, um you know, he's a he's a all-encompassing uh tight end. >> You've had three different centers in three years. What have you learned about building that relationship and how's that going with you and Garrett right now? >> Yeah, it's been great. Uh we had a a slight miscommunication today. Um something that he's um you know, something that's popped up uh throughout his career. Uh he's he's had a long enough career. I think it's nine years or so. Um so, he's been with many different quarterbacks and um under center, things like that. So, something that popped up that that's happened, you know, with other QBs and um just us getting on a small uh same page on on those small things and then um you know, when those when those moments show up, just being able to communicate with each other. Obviously, it's frustrating and you know, you don't want to have miscommunications. You don't want to do that, but it's it's the point of camp. It's the point of practice so that when you go out there on Sundays and between those white lines and 60 minutes, uh you know, you're you're um if not perfect, damn near perfect. >> You said that he heard that Luther Burden was texting his quarterbacks over the summer trying to get him to throw, too. What have you noticed about the demeanor of him being a target that could potentially just ascend this year in year two? >> Yeah. Uh, we all believe in Luther. Uh, the whole org, um, his teammates, me, uh, coach, coaches. Um, so it's it's it's up to us to put in the work, QB, wide receiver, um, and it's up to him to to make sure he's in the right spot. And when he catches the ball, um, he said it he said it one of his first times out, uh, he's a problem. And so, just got to give him the ball. Uh, yes, he runs great routes, he loses defenders, um, you know, he's smooth in his routes. And so, uh, be able to deliver him a good ball. Um, but I'm excited for him. I'm excited for all the guys. I'm excited for, um, our core, um, our young core that we have, uh, Colston, Luther, Rome. Uh, we got Xavion. Uh, I know I know old man isn't isn't really a part of the young core, Khalif, but uh, um, you know, we got a couple other guys out there that are are excited. I'm excited about Cole Kmet. Um, so, um, we got a young core like I said, and we're going to, you know, we're going to try and use that to our advantage and be explosive and and have fun doing it. >> Do you feel different a different I guess anticipation of what this team can be because of the success that you had and also the understanding that you have with >> I think, um, the success part, uh, doesn't mean anything towards this year in the sense of we can go out there and we can lose every game, we can go out there and win every game. Um, and that's up to us as a team. Um, so the success part doesn't affect us this year. Um, so it's it's being able to find ways to get better than last year, find ways to communicate better, um, run routes better, um, defensively, special teams, pin guys if we punt, all the, you know, all these small things that that come together, be able to win games. Uh, even even off the field things, like us us being connected better, um, you know, hanging out more, uh, being able to build that relationship, you know, that trust, um, you know, to be able to win games, uh, cuz those situational moments that we had last year, we may not have as as many or we may have more. Um, and so it's being able to fight through those and and and be better than we were last year. And so, um, I think, uh, I think it all starts back over. And so, that's what we're focused on. We're focused on, uh, being better than we were. Uh, we have guys in the building. So, uh, being better, you know, from last year. So, being better than we were last year, but um, it's it's the small details. It's us coming together, uh, on and off the field. It's it's us having open communication, following the details the coaches give us. And then, uh, go out there and execute and and have fun doing it. >> Did you do anything >> Will Hewlett and Tom Houseley in the past off-seasons. With Did you work with them again this this off-season? And Did you guys do anything differently or did you work with anyone new in addition to them? What What did you guys do? >> Uh, work with them. Uh, those are my guys. Uh, you know, they were they were they've been great to me. They've been great for me. Um, there's a bunch of different, uh, small things that that we've adjusted, uh, throughout my training and things like that. More, uh, you know, more my routes. Also, just me being in the offense now, just being a little bit more comfortable, having a little bit more command over it. And so, uh, knowing where guys are supposed to be, landmarks and all of that, steps. And so, uh, in the trainings, it was a little bit more me commanding it, um, and them just, you know, sitting back and watching and and being able to, uh, if I miss a pass slightly inside, cuz we're we're big on putting the ball in the right spot here. Um, and and so, uh, if I miss a ball inside, why did I miss? You know, figuring out, you know, that feeling. So, that if it shows up in a game, practice, it's me being able to adjust and correct. >> Did you do anything different along those lines this off-season training? Like, did you feel sort of more like a vet in the off-season or just up playing what what you got to do to get ready? >> Uh, yeah. Uh, just just figuring out my schedule a little bit better. Um, when I'm going to train, uh, when I'm going to relax, uh, how I'm going to train, you you what works best for me and my body, >> [snorts] >> how to eat, >> [clears throat] >> and things like that. Uh lost some weight, so it's it's good. I'm excited about that. Be able to move a little bit better. Be a you know, be smoother. Um um you know, all these all these different things. Uh just being able to also bring that into the facility uh with the strength staff and things like that. Things I've done, uh things that work well with me and being able to um adjust and and and be better for the season. >> How much did you lose? >> Uh 10 10 10 to 15, something like that. >> How'd you do it? >> Uh yeah. Uh eating at certain times, um going to bed and not eating after 7:00 and you know, just eating consistently, eating well. >> What was the >> the miscommunication >> Rome was open with his frustration about the injuries last year. You've been talking about he's kind of got a new normal that he's got to deal with. As a friend of his, how you helped him along and as his quarterback, what can you do to make this training camp uh pointed pointed in the right direction? >> Yeah. Uh ensure confidence that the ball is going to come to him. Uh he's one-on-one, the ball's going to come to him. Um runs a nice route, gets open for us, uh creates a little separation, ball's going to be there. Um so on my part, delivering a good ball. On my part, finding ways to be better uh for him and the guys. Um and then and then from there, uh we we talk we talk we talk we talk. Um we talk about the routes. We talk about how to run them. Uh like you said, his new normal. That That's That's his new normal and that's okay. Um and and it's it doesn't look any different. Um so uh that's what he said, but it doesn't look any different out there. He looks He looks like normal Rome Odunze. So um you know, my thing is just ensuring confidence that the ball will come to him. Run a nice route, uh create a little separation, I'll put the ball where the ball needs to be. Um and then um if I don't, um we draft drafted you um really high for a certain reason because you're special. It's to go make that catch. Um I believe in you. Um I believe that you're going to either make it or it's going to be incomplete. Um, and so, um, just ensuring the confidence is showing the belief in him. Um, and when the ball goes to him, um, I know it's going to be either caught or incomplete. >> Awesome. Thank you, guys. >> Awesome. To the Bears. Thank you, everybody.

title: Dennis Allen excited to start developing Bears’ identity | Press Conference
text: Couldn't be better, man. Huh? I think this is training camp number 25 for me in the league. Um so, I've been doing this a while. That's a lot of huddles that's been broke um in 25 years. So, uh but just like every year, you know, excited about, you know, getting back and getting started. Um you know, we we we've got a ton of work ahead of us. Um and and um and we're excited about kind of getting to work and and getting going and and developing the identity of the 2026 Chicago Bears. Um you know, look Last year has no bearing on anything that we have going forward. Um we're not promised anything. So, uh we got to put the work in and we got to we got to work to get better. And uh you know, when you look at it, um we got eight I think 42 players on defense here in training camp. 18 of those are new faces in the building. Um so, roughly half of uh what we have here is going to be new faces in the building. So, uh there's been a lot of change. Um um and um and we'll have to go through the evaluation process and see where everybody fits within uh within the scheme and within what we're trying to get accomplished. Um and then we'll we'll find out by the end of training camp who's the right 53 players for this football team. >> Coach, are there any up downs on the itinerary this morning? >> Um yeah, we'll start that today. >> Yeah. Are 18 new guys ready? >> Um it's everybody. So, if you're if you're uh planning on practicing today, then we'll do our 40. >> Who's going to get the first look at nickel? >> Uh listen, we're going to go through a lot of different players. Um you know, um Kyler um obviously is going to start on on PUP, so we're going to look at a lot of different players that to play the nickel position and and uh uh so, you'll see that change throughout the course of camp. >> What's the challenge of that spot with a rookie like Malik? >> Um well, look, there's a lot of stuff that goes on at that position. Um you know, when you play outside at corner don't take it I don't want this to seem wrong, but things don't happen quite as fast. Obviously, the speed of the receivers on the outside edge um you know, uh that's coming at you fast, but in terms of when you play inside in the nickel, you get things that are happening on the outside of you. You have things that are happening on the inside of you. You got more responsibility in the run game. You know, so there's just a lot more that goes along um you know, with playing that position. Um look, the kid's smart. Um you know, we'll give him a look at it and and see where he's at and and uh let let the competition throughout the course of training camp kind of play out. And uh I think you know, evaluation something that takes time. Uh it doesn't happen uh you know, in in a day or two. It happens over the course of time and we'll let that that time play out and uh we got we got a lot of time, you know, between now and the start of the season to try to figure a lot of these things out. >> In these practice settings, how do you evaluate edge rushers? I know you're not going to have pads on for a couple of days here, but what are you looking to see that might translate? >> Yeah, look, um uh mechanics, you know, we're we're looking for pass rush mechanics. It's hard to really it listen, it's hard to evaluate a lot of stuff, all right, when you're practicing in underwear. Um and so we'll we'll we'll be able to have a better feel of what we got in the run game, what we have in the passing game, you know, when we start putting on the pads, uh that's where where really kind of determine um what you have. And so, you know, this is this really is kind of a ramp-up period. We're kind of getting sea legs up under us a little bit, and then we'll be ready to go for real when we really hit Monday, but Yeah, so we're we're we're looking for for mechanics and an understanding of relative wrestlings. >> Coach, you talked to a lot of familiar faces still at the defensive end. I did Could each Could Could each person get a plan for the off season, and is now kind of where you see exactly how much >> Yeah, we we we we we've done this the last couple of years. you know, when we when we get through with the season, we we go back and evaluate everything. And then each individual player has an individualized plan of action of the things that they did well, the things that we need to improve on, and how we're going to improve on those things. So, Yeah, everybody's got an individual plan, and some of it is collective as a group, and then then a lot of it's individualized. >> Coach, how do you recreate that turnover-hungry mindset when you have so many new faces in in that DB room? >> Yeah, you got to live it every day. Um and and Look, you you you get the things that you emphasize. Um and so, that's that's part of the culture of our defense that that runs through the vein of our defense and and you we have to practice that way every single day. And uh that has to be the mindset. That doesn't guarantee anything. but if you don't have that mindset, then they're not coming. So, we have to we have to practice with that mindset. >> Jaylon was far from healthy last season. What does a healthy version of Jaylon Johnson do for you as a defensive coordinator? Yeah, look, Jaylon's a good player. Um and and I don't think he was fully healthy last year and we're excited about seeing, you know, what he can do. I don't know that that I've had an opportunity to see up front what he looks like fully healthy. So, it's kind of hard to answer that question just a little bit. Um I'm hopeful that um you know, he can be healthy and stay healthy and and be a uh a productive player like he's been in the past. >> What does Devin Bush make you guys better and in what areas? >> Well, I think number one, I think speed um and athleticism and coverage. I I think those are two things that he really brings to us. you know, that that I think can that I think can help us. Um I think one of the things that we've we've looked at is, you know, we're we're trying to improve our team speed and I think he's he's a guy that can do that. >> Four seasons. There's been a lot of talk about Kobe's play style. What did you see from him in the [clears throat] spring and what what do you think will happen here in the you know, July August period when you when you start playing a little more real football? >> Yeah, uh I love his play style. Um I think it epitomizes the way that we want to play the game. Um plays fast. He plays violent. Uh uh He's smart. Uh he's instinctive. He just does a lot of really good things. He was an impressive guy to watch on tape and and I think when you watched him on their defense, I thought his play demeanor was contagious. Um and and that's kind of what I'm hoping that he brings uh and I and I believe it will bring that type of mindset uh you know, to our team. >> Describe the demeanor that you saw on the play on the tape. >> Yeah, like tough, nasty, violent, physical, all those descriptive terms. I mean, you know, you you'll you'll find plays like as a safety, you know, you're you find yourself running the alley a lot and tracking inside out on the ball and and so um you know, I just I can think of a few plays, you know, in my mind right now where you just see him and he's flying downhill from a middle of the field safety and making tackles two, three yards, you know, down the field. Um and so that's the that's the mentality that we're looking for. We're we're we're not looking to you know, run up there and get on the side of somebody and try to drag him down. We're trying to knock him backwards. Um and I think that is something that he he's going to bring. >> With Eli out, I'm assuming that Deion will get the first team reps at defense. What are you looking for from him at this early stage of development? >> Yeah, just continue to get better every day. You know, I mean, let let's don't let's don't try to set all these lofty goals on what we want to do or how we want to do or where we want to see somebody, you know, six weeks from now. Let Let's just come out every day, all right, and get a little bit better every day. I think grasping the system, understanding the things that we're going to be asking him to do, um and then playing with a with the speed and athleticism and then let your natural football ability, you know, take over. So, um I I I'm excited about him. I like what I saw in the spring with him. and I think uh you know, mentally I think he's he's going to be, you know, able to handle everything. So, I think he'll he'll be a guy that that, you know, I plan on him picking things up pretty quickly. >> How valuable will coach be for Deion as he makes this transition? >> Uh yeah, I think I think extremely valuable. Uh you know, I think, you know, with all these young players, you know, having a veteran presence in the room that's done it, that's done it at a high [snorts] level. He happens to have just come off winning a Super Bowl, so he understands what that looks like. Um you know, I think that's important for all the young guys is that we have some veteran players to kind of show them the way uh and lead them in the right direction, you know? And and look, but you've been in areas and teams where, you know, you have guys that lead them in the wrong direction, you know? But I think we got I think we got the right guys in our building. >> We heard a lot We heard a lot >> the emphasis on the coaches to coach better. Do you have the talent on the roster where coaching better should make the difference on defense? >> Uh yeah, look, I think when you when you get through okay, you evaluate everything, okay? And I don't think in any fashion we can say it was good enough, all right? Um now, we took the ball away better than anybody else in the league. Um and so that that was that was good, but there's some areas that we have to improve on. We have to improve on how we teach it, on how we coach it, we have to improve on how we play it. You know? And I think it's it's an all-encompassing thing in terms of uh you know, what we have to do. I think um uh we we got damn good coaches. >> Um along the same lines, we've heard a lot in the offseason about a focus on fundamentals when it came to the pass rush. Where will we see that showing up in camp, and what do you want to see in training camp? >> Well, we we talked about focusing on the the fundamentals in in in everything. Um look, pass rush, you know, there's a lot been made of the pass rush, right? Um there's no example of team defense that it's better exemplified than in pass defense. Because I don't care how good your pass rush is, if you don't cause the quarterback to have to reset or get to a second or third read, you're not getting to him. Um and I don't care how good your coverage is, if you can't get to the quarterback and disrupt him, they're going to throw completions. So, I think we got to get better at pass defense, all right? And I think that's both elements working together. Um and so, I think that's what our focus is. Our focus is not necessarily, you know, this area or this area. It's completely as a team, how are we going to uh improve as a team? And I think we all take a part of that. Coaches, players, scheme, fundamentals and technique, all those things play a part in that. >> Last two, Carl and Nick. >> What would it look like for Austin Booker to get to the next level? I'm just wondering how high up you think he can go. >> The things I just talked about. The the the fundamentals and the technique. Where do we have to get better, okay, as a defense? Consistency. Okay? How do we hit our target, all right, or have an acceptable play more consistently? Well, one way you do that is through your fundamentals and technique. And so, when Tiger Woods was at the top of his game, okay, he said he was great because he could repeat his fundamentals better than any of the other golfers on the PGA tour. And that's it I mean, it sounds simple, all right? And in theory it is. In application, it's much more difficult than that, but the more that we can, as 11 guys on the field, the more that we can repeat, all right, our fundamentals and techniques, all right, the better we're going to be. >> And so, what what's your vision for who Tyreek Stevenson can become? yeah, I don't I don't know if I really have thought about, well, who can he who can he become? I think he can be I think he can be a starting caliber corner in our league. Um and I think he can be a starting caliber corner for us. Same thing we just talked about there, it's the same thing with Tyreek. Tyreek needs to be more consistent. There's plays I can make you a tape of Tyreek from last season that you would look at and say, "Ooh, that's pretty freaking good, you know?" But it's the lapses in consistency that we have to improve on, and that really, at the end of the day, that that runs throughout the vein of the defense. If we're going to improve, okay, as a defense, we got to become more consistent, more efficient. Um and that's really what we're going to focus on during training camp. So, we got a few days to try to get that done. All [snorts] right? Appreciate you guys.

This one's got to be super exciting because of where the Bears finished a year ago. >> One of the most exciting as a broadcaster that I've ever lived through. You know, last year Ben Johnson came aboard. We had a lot of new personnel and we began the relationship from a dead stop. Now this year we know a lot about Ben Johnson.
