Yeah. When I came to the Bears after the 1984 season, they went and got beat in the NFC Championship game. Then we went on to win the Super Bowl. And then you go to training camp in 1986 as the defending champ. And I want to reference something Ryan Ples said that I really liked. Someone asked him a question about hunting or the hunted. And I'm glad he talked about we're always hunting. And I think that's the right frame of mind that you have to have from the top on down. You can never get content with where you are. You got to be aspired to know where you're going. And I and I really enjoyed what Ryan polls when he the way he answered that question. >> And Ben referred to it too as a hunter's mentality. What is that? He goes, "That's for the team. You're not going to tell us what a hunter's mentality is." But you've been in that position. What is a hunter's mentality? >> A hunter's mentality is the way football changes year in and year out, Jeff. We have new coaches. We have new players. there's a new philosophical thinking and the way that Ben is approaching the offensive side of the football because he's a little bit more alerted to what these guys are. You know, he talked about it um when he answered Stacy's question about what Caleb can be and where this kid is going. Um so, you know, we know a little bit about everything, but I would I would the one question I would like to ask Ben because Ben made references Yeah. You know, we saw Jedric Wills throughout the offseason. We know where Braxton Jones is. We know where Theo Benedet is going to be when they're talking about the left tackle specifically. Do we know Ben Johnson? Is there a layer of Ben Johnson that we're yet to get to know? And I would be interested to see how he would answer that question about himself because um I love everything that I've learned about Ben from the moment he took the podium last year in his introductory press conference and up to where we're at right now. >> I would get I would venture to say there is another layer or maybe many. >> That's a Jeff Jonia question when you get him in front of a mic behind closed doors. >> All right, good news. Chicago United Airlines is getting brand new planes with all the bells and whistles like Bluetooth connectivity screens at every seat in a room for everyone's roller bag. United proud to fly the Chicago Bears and you too. Tommy, you've alluded to both Ryan Poles and Ben Johnson. So, without further ado, let's run those interviews backto back uh for you the fans to get a a little bit of taste of what they're thinking as we head into the first day of mini camp, excuse me, first day of training camp and then we'll respond. First of all, here's general manager Ryan Ples. I I do want to start off by sending our thoughts and prayers to Eric and Mia Benemy. Uh they mean a lot to us here. Obviously going through some hard times. Um so I want to make sure I start off by saying that. You know, as we start training camp, I want to thank our crew here um that set up campus. Obviously, it's a lot of work to to get this thing going. And plus, we had the storms yesterday, so there's a little bit of cleanup underway uh to get us started. Um, and as I think about campus 2, the other topic is just thanking George McCassie family, Kevin, uh, for their support in our football team. Um, you guys will notice we got two brand new fields on three and four totally resided. Make sure our players are in good, you know, on good surface. And, um, you also notice the state-of-the-art uh, film setup that we have on all the fields. Again, making sure that our coaches have the film right after practice so we can get to work. Um, obviously excited to to kick this season off with training camp. I think there's some really good competition on our roster and obviously when you have competition, uh, you get growth, you get development, um, and you get to find out what you what you have on your football team as we prepare for this upcoming season. Uh, in terms of the injuries, want to go through the designation. So, TJ Edwards, uh, is going to be NFI. Um, he's got a right calf. Um he was training off off site, came back in with a sore calf, soft tissue. We don't see that as anything major. Um shouldn't be too long with that. [clears throat] Uh Keshan Elliott um has some discomfort. His back, we took care of that. Um he's in really good shape. If you saw him walking around, you would have no idea. He's running. Obviously, there's a return to play uh protocol where you're getting back to be a football player in terms of your strength, your conditioning. Um, so he'll be in that. Um, Kyler Gordon on PUP, uh, with his calf. [snorts] He was here all offseason training, uh, getting right. Um, we had a delay in that. Um, all hands on deck to get him back. Coach alluded to it before in terms of his availability. Um, or the lack thereof. Um, obviously he's frustrated, we're frustrated. We just want him back. He helps our football team. Um, but we have to move forward with with the guys that we have and when he's ready to go, he'll be ready to go. Um, everybody here is is putting all their time and effort to get him back right. So, that's where that's at. Elijah Hicks has some discomfort in in his shin. We got that taken care of. Um, so that's going to take a little bit of time, but he's on the men. He's walking around. We don't see that as anything major. Um, and then our guys that had surgery, Noah Su, um, he's rehabbing on his way back, but he'll be PUP. Aziey's doing a great job. He's working his butt off. Um, he looks good, so he he's, uh, working to get again back into being a football player again. And then lastly, Shamar Turner. Um, he's working to get back as well. He did some really good work this off season. He's starting to move around really well. Um, again, I don't have timelines for all these guys, but they're they're on their way back. So, I'll open up to questions. Do >> you have a minimum amount of time you expect Kyler to miss here at the start of camp? >> I don't I really don't know. Um, he's got to get right. And I think the important thing that we've all talked about is when he gets back, we need him to stay back. >> You mentioned the frustration factor obviously on both sides with [snorts] Kyler Gordon and you guys. Has he done everything that you guys have wanted him to do as far as rehabbing and getting better? >> Yeah, like I said, I think he gave up a lot this break to stay here and and put the time in. Um, that's what he did. Um, and again, a little bit of a repetitive situation there that we got to get fixed. Um, and then when he gets back, he's going to have to earn that trust back and that dependability. So, you know, because we got to put all the guys in a good position to be successful and the up and down moving guys around is is really tough. So, he'll have to earn that back when he gets back. considering how long this has gone on for him, >> has there been some type of disconnect between him and the team at some point to explain why [clears throat] this is >> Yeah, I think that's a frustrating thing is I think the communication um in terms of the plan our guys have put together has been on point, but it's it's just hasn't stuck. So, again, we're turning every stone to get that thing right. >> You get you talked about him being here late in the offseason. He didn't show up on time for the offseason program. Is it >> talking about last year? >> Yeah. Does he do you need more consistency from him? >> Yeah, this year's been consistent. Like I said, he stayed here the whole whole break trying to get right. Um, we got to keep that uh consistent as we move forward. >> Ry, one guy you did not mention was Dio. How encouraging has it been to see him and what what did you see from him in the spring? >> Yeah, D did a great job with his return to play. Um, I think it's always good if you can get one of the guys that was injured in the season to be in that vet mini camp at least. Um, where they can start I think the part that we don't talk about enough is just gaining your confidence back as a football player. There's some balance of body control things once it starts moving uh where it's more reactive than proactive. Um, so he was able to get that phase in and then add another five, six weeks of of training. So it's really positive. Um, obviously we'll keep on him as we go, but really encouraging encouraged by not only his work that he put into it, but our staff important to him to get him right. >> We've talked to you about the pass rush all off season. How important is Dio's development during camp uh for you and and whether you weigh, can you add, should you add? >> Yeah, I think really the development of all those guys is going to be really important. um you know, sweat. I'd like to see him continue to to improve and and take what he did last year and add to that. Um you know, we don't talk about Booker like last offseason he was coming on strong before he had a little bit of an injury there that kind of set him back, but he was able to kind of help us down the stretch. Uh so he's another guy we're taking eye on. So I don't think it's different than any part of the roster. We're going to evaluate and see how they do. Um and then if we got to make adjustments or obviously investigate what where we can get better, we'll do that. That's not a but that's not a decision you plan on making anytime in the next couple of weeks. That's more toward the end of camp. >> Yeah. I've told you all for the last four or five years, we'll we're going to investigate any opportunities to get better. Um but at the end of the day, we got to make sure we know our our team. Um so we evaluate on a daily basis and and see what we need to do. >> With the few veterans that are out there on the end, you know, how do you decide whether that's a fit not only for you but for them too? I imagine that some of these names are household names that might not be comfortable with a very with a smaller role. Do you know what I mean? >> Yeah, I mean we can cross that bridge if we ever needed to to go across it, but um yeah, everybody, you know, we're looking for competition, guys, compete and and really fall into the role to help us win football games. >> You mentioned a couple times the growth you saw from Caleb last season as a professional. What was most notable to you about the strides you saw him take? I think what we saw down the stretch is like the desire to win, the [snorts] desire to win, and I and I think we'll see development in all those, you know, other areas, uh, the technical areas. Um, understanding the offense, defense, Ben's done a great job with him, and I I expect him to continue to develop, but I think at the end of the day, we want our guys to have a strong desire to find a way to win football games, and that was clear to me. >> As you've watched him and Ben grow together, what's been uh the reason in your eyes that that relationship has worked the way it has? They both want to be great and win Super Bowls and that's all that matters. >> How does your perspective change at this time of year when you go from being the hunter to the hunted in the division? And does that alter anything you do? >> No, I think it's important to have the mindset that you're always hunting. Um, and that's what we're going to do. I'm sure coach will talk about our mentality as we move forward, but um, we're going to be hunting at all times. As you head into this season, is there every position group that you look look at that you saw last year and said, "We nailed it this off season that's exactly where we wanted to improve and we were able to do that." >> You know, I feel really good about the competition across our roster. Um, I've learned being in this league long enough that, you know, to sit here and feel comfortable today could change tomorrow. Um, so we stay on edge for all of these positions because you might be deep today and you might be thin tomorrow. So, we're just going to keep at it. Um, so I don't think I ever feel comfortable with with anything. So, um, but I love the competition that we have across the board. >> From your perspective, what do you want to see of Caleb entering this camp and heading into year three for him? >> Yeah, I just keep it broad just to continue to get better. Um, you know, be a master of his craft. Um, if he does that, we'll be in good shape. How are you how are you looking at the left tackle competition? >> Yeah, it's it's going to be a great competition. Um I think you know we got Braxton in a really good spot. Probably the healthiest he's been since his first year. Um so he's going to compete and he's got a lot of snaps under his belt. Um Theo's done a great job. Like see what he's done with his body this off season and he's just continues to get bigger, stronger, faster. Um understand what we're trying to do. I was really encouraged by Jedric Wills and his progress that he's made. I think he's put over double digit lean mass on his body which was something we were looking forward to as he gets to getting back to what he was. Um so that whole group and then you know Azy's working his tal off. So you know we get a couple layers to that and we'll see how it all plays out and Karan Karan as well. >> Ryan, what's the uniqueness of Garrett and then Logan behind him and how how you kind of envision your centers? >> Yeah, you have a guy with a ton of NFL experience. um just played in the Super Bowl. Um I think he's one of those glue guys for offensive line that brings everyone together. Um has a ton of knowledge and wisdom on how to play the position, especially with a [snorts] young quarterback behind him. Um and then Logan's hungry. He's got great football character, strong uh from a physical standpoint, is in a really good place, but obviously as a young center, you know, this game's a lot different at this level. Um, but we expect again competition there um as we go. But really happy with with how Bradberry's been going about his business. >> When you talk about Caleb's intensity and desire to win and how encouraging that is to you, are you seeing a connection between that and his understanding of how important just mastering some of the basics and some of the less exciting parts of the job are to those goals? >> Yeah. And again, I'll let you hit that with with coach because he sees it closer than than I do. But um I think anytime these guys mature, they start to realize um what the work looks like and those small little details matter when you show up on game day. Um and again, I expect him to continue to grow in that area. >> Ryan, been at a point now in your roster development where you have, you know, veterans [snorts] starting in place, but you also start to acquire younger players for the future. You look at the depth at center like Stacey just asked. You look at tight end, maybe linebacker. How do you evaluate that process in terms of when the time may come to transition to the younger guys? >> Yeah, it goes back to competition. Um, we're going to let it play out and see where they're at. Um, obviously, you know, if the young guys haven't played a lot of football before, it's going to take a little bit of time to understand what this game's all about, but we just we we look at the competition and and how that stacks up and if guys are separating themselves or not. Um, it's always a tough call again when you haven't played NFL snaps. Um, it's very different than even the preseason. So, you know, I think what's really important at this time is being really good evaluators of your own roster. Um, so we got to be honed in on that and that's coach and I talking through this whole process. >> With your with your desire to to keep Darnell as a kind of core piece for you going forward, what is the next frontier for him and his growth as as a tackle? >> Yeah, I think it's just consistency. We all see the the the flashes and and the stacks of plays that he puts together and it's really impressive. Um, can he be consistent day in and day out? That's the key part for Darnell. Is that a deal that you would like to get done sooner than later with Darnell Reich? >> Uh, I think there's a window to get a deal done and and then, you know, at some point we got to go play football. Um, so we'll we'll figure that part out. Um, but obviously, I think I've said it before, Darnell is a guy we want here long term. Um, takes two sides to get things done. Um, but at the end of the day, I don't want any distractions or anything like that. So, when it's time to go play football, we'll go play football and and keep it moving. But, um, yeah, he's a guy we would like to hear for a while. Ryan, we talked Ben about Luther Burton and his excitement about Burton in the off season. [clears throat] From what you evaluated in college and from where you think his ceiling is, how far along is he and what more is there for him to do uh at the NFL level? >> Yeah, we we got to go play games and he's got to, you know, finish this thing off. But if there's a guy that I'm really excited about, it's Luther Burton because of his just how much he's grown from the day he walked in this building. Um, I mean, he was I heard he was just texting and calling these quarterbacks just looking for an arm to throw to him every day of the week. Um, the guy loves football. He's passionate about it. Um, he wants to help this team win and he wants to be the absolute best receiver he can possibly be. and uh you can feel the fire um inside of him and and uh I'm excited to see that that show up. >> This place is phenomenal. We're we're in tip-top shape and uh every coach, every player, they have every resource that they could ever ever need to to get better over the next six weeks and and really for the whole season. So, we're really excited about that. Speaking of excitement, um a few things about training camp that just get me get me going. Uh the first one is our team. Obviously, this is uh this is our chance to forge our identity. And you know, a lot of coaches come up and they say, "We're going to be this, we're going to be that and the other." And and yet this is where it all all happens. This is uh we got a whole different group of guys than we did a year ago. And and this is where it gets fun is call it half the roster was here, half the roster is new. Um there's a lot of getting to know each other and yet uh you know it's it's a chance for us to create a new chapter of Chicago Bears football, the 2026 version. So excited about that. Excited about the competition that's going to unfold as well. You just talked to Ryan about uh some particular spots where that might occur, but for each player it's it's an opportunity to earn a spot on the roster. It's a spot to earn a role. Um could be a starting spot, could be depth piece. Uh, of course we know special teams plays a huge part of that as well. So for for us as coaches and personnel staff, I know we're really uh going to be having our lens out and evaluating each and every single day. Um, and then finally, I I'm really I'm really excited about this coaching staff. Uh, the continuity that we have is a little bit unique in the NFL right now. You look around, there's 30 plus new play callers in the NFL. And fortunately here we we were able to have a lot of the same faces come back and and with that uh I really expect another layer of sophistication to occur within this building and and with our players. Um I've already felt it over the course of the springtime. Uh I feel it right now getting ready for training camp. Uh there's things a year ago we're trying to speak the same language. Now we're we're past that and everyone's kind of reading each other's thoughts and so um on with the the elementary is a thing of the past and we we can level things up as a coaching staff as well. So it's a really exciting time to to be here and with that I'll go ahead and open it up >> with the success and the momentum that was built last year. What in your mind are the ingredients to sustaining it going forward? I know last year's in the past, but how do you >> Yeah, it starts all over again and and we talked about this when last year ended. Um it's a brand new group of guys. We're in a race right now to develop the same chemistry that we had a year ago. I thought that was one of the things that was our secret sauce was guys playing for each other. We had a really close-knit group and and here it is. This is uh this is the time of year where you stay in a hotel or you go on the road for some joint practices like we'll do later on in camp and and uh we got to come together as a group and there'll be some trials and tribulations. Uh coaching staff, we're going to apply pressure and stress on these guys. I think that's where uh the best version of yourself comes forward. And so um yeah, I I don't think there's you talk about sustaining success. Well, shoot, we we're starting all over again. That's been the consistent message. >> Ryan talked about the hunter mentality. How do you describe that to your players? What that what that >> Oh, man. That's for team meetings. We we keep that there. Yeah. [clears throat] >> Caleb, what are kind of the things that are kind of top of your checklist for him maybe that might not have been on last year's checklist now? There's a little more comfort in the system. >> Yeah. Yeah. He and I were just talking yesterday about that is, you know, I I have this urge as an offensive guy to want to continue to evolve and uh you can say innovate and push the limits a little bit and yet at the same time in the back of my mind what's what's best for him is to continue to bank some of these reps. He's had two off seasons and one training camp so far and a full season obviously um to where he's had a lot of the similar concepts repeat for him and now we're at the point where he's not thinking about the play call. He's not thinking about the cadence, the motion and all the the jigma before the snap. Things are starting to slow down. And so what we need to see here in camp is that anticipation take it up a notch. Um, I think with that the coverage recognition gets taken up another notch. I think there's other ways we're going to continue to challenge and push them. Um, more of which are going to happen postnap. Last year we talked about that pre-nap operation quite a bit. Feel a lot better about that this time of year um than we did. And so now we're just moving on to the next stage. >> You feel it and the continuity that you guys have. Will camp [snorts] look different? >> Uh, yeah. I mean, every camp looks different. I mean, the way it's laid out in terms of having these two away joint practices, particularly week two and week three, it it is going to be different. Um, I'm I'm excited about that, though. I think it's a great chance for our team to come together. Uh, you know, when you go on the road in particular, there there's there's really not family, there's it's you, it's your buddies, it's the hotel. And, you know, I think it's a great great opportunity for us to bond together. So, um, that'll be different, but I mean, the pillars all stay the same. I mean, it's going to be a physical, it's going to be a tough, it's going to be a demanding uh ordeal. Anything worth doing is is going to be challenging. Um, these guys all know that, and I I think they embrace it as well. >> And now that you've had time to to really spend with Caleb over the last really year and a half, what what are you what do you deem his elite traits to position? >> Oh, shoot. Um, I mean, it's he's got it all, Stacy. he there there's really nothing I don't think that he can't do. It's just elite arm talent. Um playmaking ability, escape ability, um you know, he he has his legs that he can hurt a defense with. I mean, there's just so many layers to who he is as a player. Um I think that that word consistency comes up over the course of a 60-minute game or more if we need it to where we're playing highlevel quarterback play throughout that game. I mean, it you see flashes of it and and yet we're trying to tap into that where we're just consistently um delivering the ball where it needs to go, giving it to our guys around us and then uh we all know that he has that that ability to put on that Superman cape when when the time calls for it. >> Do you feel any differently? Do you feel any differently about the left tackle position today than you did on this day last summer? Um, I would say I I've got a better feel for our guys. I mean, there's a number of them that were here last year. You know, Jedri's really the new face. So, um, I I feel better about uh Braxton in terms of his health and his his outlook. So, I feel like he he's got another um another step up in terms of his confidence level than than he did a year ago at this time. Uh, you know, Theo was a guy last year I didn't know a whole lot about. I've got I got high hopes for Theo as a as a player in this league as well. I mean, I can go on and on and on. So, I I know those guys a lot better and and I think another year of mentorship under um Dan Roshar and Kyle Dean is going to do nothing but but help all of them play better. >> What's been your message to Kyler Gordon? >> Get healthy. Ben, with the uncertainty of of when he'll be available to you, what's your vision for fortifying the depth there so that you have options? >> Yeah, we we'll see. I mean, we got we're we stock back up in that DB room again and uh we'll see how it all plays out and and you know, there'll be certain players that certainly flash here and we'll give them opportunities to run with the ones um you know, while while Kyler's out and we we'll see where it goes from there. But we have a lot of options from from rookies all the way to some of these veteran players, the uh free agents that we brought in. Uh I think we're going to we're going to have a healthy competition in that room. >> Coach design your system around the players that you have. But, no, it's it's all love uh with Ocho, you know, he he been a guy I've been able to, you know, lean on most of my career since I was a rookie. hit him up in the DM, ask him questions, he always gave me great feedback. Um so, yeah, got a good relationship with him. >> Have they been kind of creative with you this off season playing around with different things? Do you like moving around? And what does the game look like from that different perspective? >> Yeah, I mean, I'm still feeling it out. I'm still feeling it out. Um they did a similar thing with with Jalen Ramsey in the scheme when he was in LA. So, just seeing the plays he made at that position at the nickel position um and moving around is kind of made me more open to it and, you know, I'm starting to get a good feel for it and it's it's pretty fun playing in there instead of just, you know, sitting in the boundary all game. >> Mike said that y'all Mike said that y'all were on the same side of the field now sometimes. What is it like trying to communicate with him? Do you have to figure that Is that a new part of y'all's relationship to figure out? >> Yeah, definitely. It's it's kind of weird cuz we used to just go on opposite every time, but, you know, now I got to communicate with him a lot um with different formations and stuff and yeah, we talked about how how weird it feel, but, you know, we got to get used to it for week one. >> J'sean, is there a guy outside of like Aches and Pizzle or T-Mac and Jaylen that really stood out to you wide receiver wise over the summer? >> Yeah, I mean, all of them all of them really doing their thing. Uh J'sean, I I already knew about him cuz he was on the practice squad last year. So, I had to see him down there every day. Um and Mechie been making a lot of plays out the slot. Uh we still got Jimmy. See how See how much gas he got in the slot. So, you know, it's a competitive receiver room and you know, it's good for us just cuz we get more work uh whoever lining up out there. So, it's good for us. >> You said you're getting used to playing in that slot spot at Did you play it ever back college or when was the last time you've ever remember playing there? >> Yeah, I played my freshman year of college, I played at nickel and then in 2022 here, I played a lot of nickel, but it's this scheme a a lot different than old schemes, so it's still a little bit of an adjustment. >> What kind of nuances you got to figure out of this scheme compared to the other times you played there? >> Yeah, a a lot of 2022 is just a lot of dropping to a spot. Zone drops is your job, didn't really change much, but in this defense you know, one motion could switch your whole job and responsibility, so kind of just getting into the playbook more, you know, as a corner, you don't you only got three jobs, you know, you don't you don't have to think that much, you just go out there and play, but at nickel, you got to kind of know what's going on with each motion and be able to switch your job, cuz if you don't, you mess up the whole defense. >> What are your three jobs? >> At corner, I mean, it's cover four, cover three, cover two man. Um, we got the same agent. Um, and I got a chance to get with him this off season, we got some work in and I just talked about talked to him about what they were trying to do and how he how he thought how he played in the slot, how he thought of the techniques. Um, I mean, it's been serving me well so far. >> How does it free you up potentially to make plays, I guess, cuz you're going to to both directions when they're throwing at you? >> Yeah, I mean, just being able to, you know, make plays in the pass game in the slot and the run game, playing behind the line of scrimmage a little more, you know, blitzing a little more, it it would make it a little bit more fun. >> We've We've seen flashes of the blitzing ability. Was that kind of part of the math in putting you there because you can you have I mean, you have the ability and go out there and do it now. >> I mean, yeah. I mean, you have to talk to coach E on that one, but I think so. I think I'm a pretty good blitzer and good at disguising and stuff like that, but yeah, I think so. >> J.C., this is this Friday. I think we Last year we wore the game uniforms, too, so it it kind of gave you like a scrimmage feel. title: Dave Canales: 'Finally feels like camp' | Carolina Panthers
text: All right, finally feels like camp. We got a little sun, little heat, little humidity. Guys got some good work today. Ended with the nice move, the ball period. Um that was very competitive and uh again just trying to, you know, harp on uh just penalties, you know, just little things that come up, keeping the line of scrimmage clean. It was another pretty good day, but in the move the ball, guys get tired. Um we had a couple of pre- snap deals there. So, uh try to hit the guys on that and uh really nice finish. Uh Bryce Amac in the back of the end zone on a little double move. So, uh, uh, a way to way to go for the offense to just kind of finish the day that way. But they went back and forth. The energy was right from the beginning, uh, starting in team run and, um, the guys got after it today. So, I'm really proud of the group. Um, questions. >> Obviously, there's been a lot of injuries. How do you feel they've responded to injuries, especially when you're not stopping drills and going back out there in the passing game is what it was after Chris Long. >> Yeah. Uh, Chris same knee. So, um, just something happened. He felt weird on it. Sat down. Uh we took him in. We'll get a full evaluation and get a picture of that and we'll give you guys more information there. Um yeah, some this and that. We, you know, with Mitch Evans, it was uh it was ended up being kind of a low ankle sprain. So, we're we're optimistic we can turn him back around and and get them back out there for FanFest. Speaking of which, FanFest Friday night, uh 7:30, a great event. Um the last couple of years, there's been a really great showing there. Um and uh we try to simulate a game as much as possible and that's a I love that. It's a challenge on me to try to make sure I throw different situations at guys, place the ball in different spots. We'll have special teams. Uh there'll be a couple of, you know, trick plays on offense, on special teams, some things that we've been kind of, you know, cooking up in secret, not telling the other side about it. So, uh the defense has some pressures that they got up their sleeve as well. So, um just a couple of things to, you know, to keep it exciting and, uh hope that anybody's listening, you know, comes out and uh supports. It's going to be a lot of fun. >> Will there be a P practice? >> Absolutely. Yeah, we'll we'll pad up and it'll be like an inner squad scrimmage. So, it'll be all but just live tackling to the ground. It's going to be physical. We're asking the guys to square up and show me you made the tackle. Um, so it'll be a physical day and uh we're going to put it in the evening so the guys can start to get used to doing that work later on because we do practice, you know, from 10 to about noon. >> Was that knee injury something that he came into camp? Did he tweak? >> He did not. It was just something that kind of started to get sore after the first couple of days. Um and then we just, you know, he mentioned it to us. We started to look at it and um you know, we we put him through some some good uh recovery stuff and and de loed him for a couple of days, got him back out there and he couldn't finish the day. >> Was it the left knee? >> It's the same one. Yeah. >> Yeah. >> Dave, it seemed to an untrained eye that Bryce had a pretty spectacular day. I wonder if you could talk about Bryce and then also what JC Horn has looked like to you. So, >> yeah. I mean, first off, it's great to have Mike and JC back out there for the for the full practice. It makes things harder out there on the perimeter and, uh, makes you have to, you know, uh, question whether you want to target that receiver out there. And so, um, that's what we're used to. And, uh, with the pressure unit that we have, um, the different packages we have to be able to to have those guys sitting out there staring at the quarterback, I can tell you from personal experience, it's it's not comfortable. And so, it's good to have them out there. Uh Bryce is continuing to just take the next steps. What I what I see from Bryce right now is just ownership and mastery of the concepts and now I just see the uh the timing uh the rhythm and just the meu factor with his guys and watching him throw anticipatory balls to T-Mac to Jaylen to David Moore uh showed up again with another touchdowns like one one a day it's vitamin D so Demo shows up and makes a play. Um, so I just see his level of of comfort uh really showing up with the guys and I'm excited to as we just continue to build on that. >> It was a pretty good day for the backups. I mean, Kenny and and Haynes both were pretty accurate today. You're bringing Kyle Tras. What's the thought process there and how much does having four preseason games kind of factor into that? >> Yeah. Um, first of all, I get to talk about Will Heriger, our QB coach, doing a fantastic job getting all those guys ready. They're into it. Um, they have tools. I'm really proud of how they're handling the blitz pickup and pressures and having solutions um all the way from Kenny down to Hannes. Um what whatever it might be, whatever the pressure might be, they have an answer that goes with all the prep, all the meetings, and bringing it alive on the field ultimately. Uh Kyle Tras, somebody that I love, had a got a chance to spend a year with him in Tampa. And um you know, brought him in to work him out, see where he's at physically, and you know, maybe it's the Hall of Fame game. And on top of that, it's just being ready for you. You you don't know. You never know what happens, but it's good to just have guys who know the system uh to be ready and to be available. And I'm just glad to be able to just spend a day with Kyle. Uh you know, he'll be working out here in a second right behind us. And so, um really happy to have him here. >> You mentioned the the chemistry between Bryce and his guys and the late touchdown to T-Mac. He also had one a few plays earlier when Mike Jackson was on team. Looked like Bryce just kind of bought him time and got it in there. How exciting. to see plays like that where it's is trust, it's timing, it's just all that building up. >> Yeah, it feels great. It feels great to know that these guys have had the they've put the time in, they put the work in, and um through the offseason, you know, they were able to get together on their own this summer and and just continue to work on that uh those connections. And then also the defense, a couple of really great rushes and Bryce had to move off the spot and that's where he's special. Um he was able to kind of slide to the left, buy him some time, and get the ball down the field. So, um, but those are those are the ops that we need and it brings out the best in all of us. You know, um, our outside guys going against Mike and going against JC every day is fantastic and of course Will Lee having to deal with our guys as well. Uh, it's going to bring out the best in him and and that's what we look for for competition >> back on those corners. You guys obviously locked up JC Mike Jackson in contract year. How would you describe the level of priority for getting him? >> Mike's one of my favorite guys. Um, again, this is just a a negotiation thing. This is really not my world. And so, I think they'll continue to go through that process and make that decision when the time's right. >> Dave, I know you talked about FanFest, but it is the first time you'll be in that stadium in front of fans since the playoff game. Just how excited are you to to be in that sort of environment again and give that to the guys? It's fantastic and and having a taste of what it feels like to be in the wildard round to win the division. Uh hosting a playoff game and uh the support that we got from our fan base, you know, the as people asked me like what was that game like? The the ones who weren't able to be there, it was just like it was special from, you know, from pregame as our groups came out, DBs, wide receivers, the big boys come out together, there was just a welcoming from the crowd that was already there. Um the the energy was right and the guys could feel that. they come bouncing out of the tunnel a little different when they have that kind of support. And so that's the last thing in our guys' minds. And as I ask them, let's move on. This is 2026. This is a new season. Nothing is guaranteed. The work is today. I know that in the back in the back of their minds, I know they can feel that and they're excited to get back into our stadium, play ball like we know how. And uh I'm look I'm excited about and looking forward to a really good turnout so that the the energy is right in there. Yesterday you said you wanted to watch the film before you kind of diagnosed Monroe's day. What did you see on film and if anything what did you see today? >> Yeah. So from yesterday or from the day before? Yeah, it was yesterday's film. Um having a surface to get on on top of to get his big mits in there helped him and he was able to play comfortably. Um there were a couple of times he got a little bit behind the rush. He's so athletic. He's able to get his big body back in phase uh to to create that pocket width that we're looking for. And I'm really really encouraged, really excited for where he's at. >> I know you said you wanted to be part of Kent's story, but how has he affected the story of training camp so far? >> Uh just the way that he prepares. Um he's in there early. He's ready to go. He knows the script. He knows what's happening. He's asking great questions. He's bringing things up from places that he's been in the past. It's exactly right. Um, as the backup quarterback, that's one of your jobs is we're all in there in that room to support Bryce. And his best way of doing it is to make sure that he's on his stuff and that he's on time and on the money and and pushing the practices so we can evaluate because even though you can't take every single rep, when Kenny goes out there and continues to move the offense or make a concept come alive, that's valuable film. Those are valuable cutups that we can use as teach tape for now and for the future. And so it's so important to have him here and he's done a great job. >> Dave, Jim Reed seemed to make several catches out there today. How much is he making his case right now and what have you seen from him that stands out? >> Yeah, just seems given everything he has. I mean, separates at the top. He knows what he's doing. Uh, first and foremost, he's a guy that we can count on. We can really spot him in and play at any different any position across the the receiver room, whether that's X or F or at the Z. So, he studies that way. Um, and the bottom line is we throw him the ball, he catches it. You know, in the definition of wide receiver is receiver and he does that. And the quarterbacks love throwing to him. That goes for Bryce all the way down to Haynes. So, uh, he's really making a case for himself. >> Dave, did you have to breathe a sigh of relief today on that special teams drill when Jonathan slipped and was downarily? >> Well, JB's going to have to tell me that he really wants to do it. uh because we need him we need him to be ready to see the different returns but at the same time we're bringing him back in phases you know so uh that was just another football playing you know and um we all have to kind of move on from that him as well and just say hey stuff happens on the football field you know just keep playing fast uh trust it and uh your body will just continue to catch up to it >> will that conversation be like with him you said about the return possibility >> he's going to have to beg me he's going to have to beg me to get out there because uh I know what an impact he can make on our offense. And uh we feel very confident in Trevor in what he's done uh last year as a punt returner and a kick returner. And we have some other young guys too that we really want to evaluate. So uh I I would not anticipate you'll see Jonathan Brooks in the preseason returning any kicks. And once we get into the season in a competitive moment, he's going to have to come up to me and grab me by the shirt and say, "I'm taking this one with Trevor." So um but yeah, he's Jonathan's doing a great job. He had another great day, full day of practice, uh played physical, made an unbelievable catch on a go ball. If you guys saw that along the other sideline, got his feet in, which just goes to show some of the other things that he can bring to our offense. >> Why has it been important for Luke Forner to get all the first team reps and what has he brought to the protection calling and just kind of the the O line in general with all this moving and shaking there? >> Yeah, the center position is about command and that's what Luke has. He gets up there, he gets us directed, and we play fast. And he's connected with Bryce. They've talked a whole bunch about just working on different cadence usage, protections, things that they're going to do, um, having a plan. Uh, he's a very cerebral guy, so he's always asking those questions. Now, what if this happens? How do you see us handling that? And so, we've had some great conversations as a staff with him as well, not just with the players, but uh, whether it's the quarterback or the center, they are kind of that liaison to the rest of the group as they go in there. so that we're on the same page. >> Coach, uh, you brought up Demo earlier. Um, and >> it's a really young, pretty young receiving room. He's really standing out as the vet in there. How important is it for the rest of that room to have his presence and his mentorship there? >> It's in I mean, that's really his goal. That's really what Demo has done for me for a long time. and um we drafted him in Seattle in 2017 and uh out of East Central Oklahoma and really had to teach him everything and he was a big athlete. He was about 230 lbs, six feet and ran 4-3 and uh they handed him the ball, they threw it to him how they could and I was the receivers's coach at the time. It was my task to teach him how to just be a receiver in the NFL and and that was a process and it took him the better part of a year and a half, two years to really get to a point where he was reliable and he was stepping up. So he's been through it. He knows the challenges of figuring your body out, what works for you. Demo goes about 215, 213. He changed his body by the way he works, by the way he eats, how he takes care of himself afterwards, how he studies and prepares so that you can be available to pop in really at different positions. Andy's valuable on special teams because he can do different things that way. So, he's setting the example and showing them guys if you want to have a chance to make this team, this is the path. And uh he's making it hard on everybody and he's competing just like they all are. And he keeps making plays and at the end of the day, you can't ignore the film. Um and so I'm proud of Demo and the man that he is. >> Do you think that the fact that you kind of built him up as a receiver helps him tell the other guys like this is what coach is going to want out of you? >> Absolutely. He knows what to expect. He knows the standard of work. Um, and he knows how to approach it every day. So, and you know, anybody can can prep themselves all summer and do it for a couple days, but when you get 13 15 days into camp, your routines are what save you. And that's where Demo really uh is one of our best examples of how to handle yourself. >> Thank you very much. >> All right. Thank you. [music] [music] >> [music]

And I'm really really encouraged, really excited for where he's at. >> I know you said you wanted to be part of Kenny's story, but how has he affected the story of training camp so far? >> Uh just the way that he prepares. Um he's in there early. He's ready to go. He knows the script. He knows what's happening. He's asking great questions. He's bringing things up from places that he's been in the past. It's exactly right. Um, as the backup quarterback, that's one of your jobs is we're all in there in that room to support Bryce. And his best way of doing it is to make sure that he's on his stuff and that he's on time and on the money and and pushing the practices so we can evaluate because even though you can't take every single rep, when Kenny goes out there and continues to move the offense or make a concept come alive, that's valuable film. Those are valuable cutups that we can use as teach tape for now and for the future. And so it's so important to have him here and he's done a great job. >> Dave, Jim Reed seemed to make several catches out there today. How much is he making his case right now and what have you seen from him that stands out? >> Yeah, just seems given everything he has. I mean, separates at the top, he knows what he's doing. Uh, first and foremost, he's a guy that we can count on. We can really spot him in and play at any different any position across the the receiver room, whether that's X or F or at the Z. So, he studies that way. Um, and the bottom line is we throw him the ball, he catches it. You know, in the definition of wide receiver is receiver and he does that. And the quarterbacks love throwing to him. That goes for Bryce all the way down to Haynes. So, uh, he's really making a case for himself. >> Dave, did you have to breathe a sigh of relief today on that special teams drill when Jonathan slipped and was downarily? >> Well, JB's going to have to tell me that he really wants to do it. uh because we need him we need him to be ready to see the different returns but at the same time we're bringing him back in phases you know so uh that was just another football play he lost his footing you know and um we all have to kind of move on from that him as well and just say hey stuff happens on the football field you know just keep playing fast uh trust it and uh your body will just continue to catch up to it >> will that conversation be like with him you said about the return possibility >> he's going to have to beg me he's going to have to beg me to get out there because uh I know what an impact he can make on our offense. And uh we feel very confident in Trevor in what he's done uh last year as a punt returner and a kick returner. And we have some other young guys too that we really want to evaluate. So uh I I would not anticipate you'll see Jonathan Brooks in the preseason returning any kicks. And once we get into the season in a competitive moment, he's going to have to come up to me and grab me by the shirt and say, "I'm taking this one with Trevor." So um but yeah, he's Jonathan's doing a great job. He had another great day, full day of practice, uh, played physical, made an unbelievable catch on a go ball. If you guys saw that along the other sideline, got his feet in, which just goes to show some of the other things that he can bring to our offense. >> Why has it been important for Luke Fortner to get all the first team reps and what has he brought to the protection calling and just kind of the the O line in general with all this moving and shaking there? >> Yeah, the center position is about command, and that's what Luke has. He gets up there, he gets us directed, and we play fast. And he's connected with Bryce. They've talked a whole bunch about just working on different cadence usage, protections, things that they're going to do, um, having a plan. Uh, he's a very cerebral guy, so he's always asking those questions. Now, what if this happens? How do you see us handling that? And so, we've had some great conversations as a staff with him as well, not just with the players, but uh, whether it's the quarterback or the center, they are kind of that liaison to the rest of the group as they go in there. so that we're on the same page. >> Coach, uh, you brought up Demo earlier. Um, and >> it's a really young pretty young receiving room. He's really standing out as the vet in there. How important is it for the rest of that room to have his presence and his mentorship there? >> It's I mean, that's really his goal. That's really what Demo has done for me for a long time. and um we drafted him in Seattle in 2017 and uh out of East Central Oklahoma and really had to teach him everything and he was a big athlete. He was about 230 lbs, six feet and ran 4-3 and uh they handed him the ball. They threw it to him how they could and I was the receivers's coach at the time. It was my task to teach him how to just be a receiver in the NFL and and that was a process and it took him the better part of a year and a half, two years to really get to a point where he was reliable and he was stepping up. So he's been through it. He knows the challenges of figuring your body out. What works for you? Demo goes about 215 213. He changed his body by the way he works, by the way he eats, how he takes care of himself afterwards, how he studies and prepares so that you can be available to pop in really at different positions. Andy's valuable on special teams because he can do different things that way. So, he's setting the example and showing them guys if you want to have a chance to make this team, this is the path. And uh he's making it hard on everybody and he's competing just like they all are. And he keeps making plays and at the end of the day, you can't ignore the film. Um and so I'm proud of Demo and the man that he is. >> Do you think that the fact that you kind of built him up as a receiver helps him tell the other guys like this is what coach is going to want out of you? >> Absolutely. He knows what to expect. He knows the standard of work. Um, and he knows how to approach it every day. So, and you know, anybody can can prep themselves all summer and do it for a couple days, but when you get 13 15 days into camp, your routines are what save you. And that's where Demo really uh is one of our best examples of how to handle yourself. >> Thank you very much. >> All right. Thank you. >> Thank you. >> No questions. Cool. a lot of different uses with JC and how that affects you and Willie this off season. What has it been like to kind of play around with some different formations out there and how does that change game? >> Oh, cool. That's cool. Um, now like me and JC are actually on the same side. So, we talking in between the play u how he like to see certain things like letting them know I just play off him like so it's kind of cool. >> Talk like that really during a game. >> N Yeah. Yeah. So, it's kind of like it's like basically we talk about football all the time, but now we're actually out there together and like trying to make sure we see the same thing the same way. >> How often do you think you guys will be aligned that way? >> I don't even think about that. Like if they do it, they do it. If they don't, they don't. Yeah. >> What have you been your impressions on? >> Uh my young he uh real funny. Will been balling though. like he just come to work every day like he listens and he tries to apply um like whatever we tell him. So that's cool. >> You said he's funny like you smiled immediately >> cuz he be calling me old. So like and I did that to Tay. So now I'm on the other side. So it's kind of funny. >> You feel old. >> No, I don't feel old. But you know he be like it what was it on like the day he was talking about like when he was in college and he was like I played for the O2 Miami. Like he just crack jokes all day. Yeah. So it's fine. >> How older are you than him? >> How old is he? >> Oh, I don't know. I'm 29, so I'm assuming he probably what, 23, maybe 24. So yeah, >> Mike, uh, you and Bryce were having some jawing after one of the plays. What were you telling? >> Which one? >> I don't know. You were pointing that direction >> today. I don't even >> I don't know. I be talking to everybody out there, so ain't no telling what I was saying. >> Will's 23. >> All right. So, six years old. >> There was a play where you were covering T-Max pretty well and Bryce was able to get it in there from a corner perspective. I was saying make the play, but like what is it like to see that connection between them? >> Oh, he should have caught the ball. He I messed up. I almost cussed. I I messed up. like he shouldn't have caught it. Like I just got to be better with my technique. Like the day I dropped the pick, had a flag and gave up a pass. Like I don't do that. So I just got to come in here basically like lock more in like cuz that don't happen. >> Have you seen a jump though from this offense and rising those receivers? >> N cuz we lock them up every day. [laughter] >> So we don't supposed to. Mike, do you feel like last year with how well both you and JC played that you guys collectively, the two of you finally got two roses? >> Uh, you know, I don't really care about that. Like, so for me, it's kind of like if you know, you know. Like if you feel like we the best duo, then cool. If you don't, that's cool. So, more focus on like this year. had a couple practices now in Dece. It's dope cuz he's always in them dig windows. Like he told me um that he used to play receiver. So like and I I see it because like normally linebackers have issues with coverage just the position, but like he honestly be at each landmark. So, it's like it makes sense why he's able to get there and he's always in the first window and then sometimes he even gets to the second window. So, that's cool. >> That last question. Do you guys feel like you're the best duo? >> For sure. >> Got to talk about Sorry, you got JC right there next week. You also have back out there last. Yeah, like we was talking today on the field like now we can really push each other like cuz we've been around each other long enough where nobody takes it personal. So like sometimes it might be one cussing out another or all three getting on to one person like regardless we know it come from a place of love and just trying to get better. >> Somebody a lot of people think about player contract. >> Do you think about that like you still have something in the book or do you just compartmentalize and and allow others to your agents or whatever? Um, I just kind of look at it as it is what it is. Regardless if I feel like I did or I don't, feelings don't mean nothing in this business. Cuz if feelings did, then everybody be worth 200 million. So my job is just to come play ball. And it's like if I have days like I did today, then I ain't going to get what I want. So I got to lock in and like just go play ball cuz at the end of the day, the money going to be there. Like I'm a hustle. I'mma always make me some money. So I ain't really worried about that. It's more about this ball. >> You sound sort of frustrated about your individual performance today. Is that >> Yeah, cuz I don't I don't I don't play like that. Like I take pride in not giving up passes, catching picks. Like it shouldn't take a day like this for me to go and then have 10 straight great days or you know, whatever. Like it should just be every single day. Like that's what the great ones do. Like they don't need to get hit in the mouth to then wake up, all right, now I'm want to fight. like no, like that was last year. Now it's time to move on. Like throw the first punch. >> Have they given you any indication, Mike, that they will extend you before the season or do you think you're going to have to play this year as a contract? >> I'm playing this year as a contract. They haven't said nothing. >> That's your That's your plan. Yeah. like it was anymore. >> It's no motivation cuz at the end of the day like every year is a contract year literally like cuz the way my deal set up if I didn't do what I was supposed to last year I wouldn't be here. So, it's like just go play ball. Like the money going to be there that like don't get me wrong, it's it's one of them things like yeah like I'm on the tip of the iceberg but I'm so far away cuz if I'm more worried about the money then plays like days like today going to start happening in the game and then it's going to be where you don't even deserve no contract. So it's like clean what I did up today and then move on. So when the game come I'm in my flow state. I'm in my bag. I could just go play cuz if I do what I supposed to regardless the money don't going to come no matter where it's at. >> Yeah. You say that very clearly your more performance is top of your mind not necessarily contract. >> Are you hopeful that you can stick around with these guys? >> To be honest I don't even think about that cuz like the way my career has been set up I've never had the privilege to think about the next year. So it's kind of hard to like do that now. Don't get me wrong, like yes, I would love to be here, but I just never been in that position to even say that. So, it's kind of it it's weird even like thinking like that. >> You think you're kind of close to being in that spot the way that you've kind of formed the last couple years? >> I don't I don't know. Like, cuz it's like it's a business. So regardless of how I think and how I feel, like they have a plan, I have to make sure my ball is great enough to where if they do say they don't want me here, I go somewhere else and play good football. Like just how like Seattle traded me here. If I if I was in my feelings about that, then by now I wouldn't even be here. So, it's kind of like just focus on the day and like clean up the stuff you messed up today and at some point, you know, like the money gonna come because the money is really just for like life after football. Like, if I sign for 200 million a day, I still got practice tomorrow. Like, I can't go on vacation. So, it ain't nothing really to worry about. >> Sorry. Sorry to belver this, but just to clarify, have they told you that they're not going to extend you prior to the season or is that just your read? >> We haven't said nothing like nothing was said. >> Is that a mindset yourself? I know you said you've never had a lot of people that did this. >> Kind of just growing up like they say don't count your eggs before they hatch. Don't put all your eggs in one basket. Like just focus on it's always like focus on today because we don't know what tomorrow can bring. Like so for me it's kind of like just play it cool. Like stay true to me. I've never been one to complain and oh I'm not getting my way. Like I could have easily set out and but I love football too much. So it's like if you was that person in 2018, 2013, and back in 03, be that same guy today. Just cuz like I got a voice and like when I speak, people will listen. Don't mean you got to get in your feelings and take advantage of it. Like no, I still be you. >> JC, can you take us like what happened with the toe or the foot? Like what what led to the injury? >> Uh just offseason work, you know, a little a little minor hiccup. Um I could have could have came back and you know played, but it was just playing safe. So I'm I'm 100% I'm ready to go. You guys got off to a really good start. I mean, obviously you watched the first couple of weeks. Seems like the offense is starting to hit its stride. What did What have you noticed about Bryce in this practice, but also the weapons on the outside? >> Yeah, he got a that's what I noticed. He got a lot of weapons. You know, all those guys can go. Um, and I kind of noticed from Bryce just trusting his receivers more, just putting the ball in the air, letting them go make plays and they whooped our ass today for for most of the practice. Um, but you know, it's it's good to see that too, just because, you know, we know we coming in with some some firepower on the offensive side of the ball and it's gonna help us on Sundays. >> As those guys have matured, have you seen kind of competition coming out here in these practices kind of leveled up? >> Yeah, for sure. You know, especially putting the pass on just made the energy go up and uh like you said, they Coker getting older, you know, this T-Max second year, so guys just more comfortable um in the scheme and Bryce getting on uh getting his connection with those guys good and you know, it's showing in practice. defense has kind of offense has won the last few days as as a leader on the defense. Do you get worried about that or is it just the es and flows of training camp? >> Yeah. No, I ain't I ain't worried about it. You know, we going we going to get our fair share of wins, too. It's all good. >> JC, you were uh you made the the top 100 list this year. Do you think people are finally outsiders taking notice of what you and you and Mike collectively? Also, >> I don't really care to be honest. you know, as long as my coaches, you know, know what type of player I am, front office know what type of player I am, I I really don't get into what the media think or where I'm ranked. It is what it is. >> You see it though. You you pay attention. >> Uh not so much this year. Um I'm I'm trying to stay off it a little more. You know, I'm probably going to delete all that going into the season cuz, you know, I'm too competitive. I I reply to some of them and then Bruce hitting my phone getting on me. So, I'm I'm going try to just stay off of it [laughter] and not not look at it this year. you talk about your Madden rating yesterday said he needed to to update your your Madden rating. >> Yeah, as soon as he walked over there, I told him to don't even walk up to me until you make me at least a 90. But no, it's it's all love uh with OO. You know, he he been a guy been able to, you know, lean on most of my career since I was a rookie. Just hit him up in the DM, ask him questions. He always gave me great feedback. Um so yeah, got a good relationship with him. >> J, they been kind of creative with you this offseason, playing around with different things. Do you like moving around? What does the game look like? that perspective. >> Yeah, I mean, I'm still feeling it out. I'm still feeling it out. Um, they did a similar thing with with Jaylen Ramsey in his scheme when he was in LA. So, just seeing the plays he made at that position at the nickel position. Um, and moving around is kind of made me more open to it and, you know, I'm starting to get a good feel for it and it's it's pretty fun playing in there instead of just, you know, sitting in the boundary game. >> That Mike said it meant that y'all are on the same side of the field now sometimes. Like, >> what is it like trying to communicate with him? Do you have to figure that? Is that a new part of y'all's relationship to figure out? >> Yeah, definitely. It's it's kind of weird because we used to just going opposite every time, but you know, now I got to communicate with him a lot. Um, there's different formations and stuff and yeah, we talked about how how weird it feel, but you know, we got to get used to it for week one. >> JC, is there a guy outside of like team and Jaylen really stood out to you wide receiver? >> Yeah, I mean all of them all of them really doing their thing. Uh Jim, I I already knew about him cuz he was on the P squad last year, so I had to see him down there every day. Um and Mie been making a lot of plays out the slot. Uh we still got Jimmy, see how see how much gas he got in the slot. So, you know, it's a competitive receiver room and you know, it's good for us just because we get more work uh whoever lining up out there. So, it's good for us. >> You said you're getting used to playing in that slot spot. Did you play it ever back in college? I mean, was the last time you ever playing? >> Yeah, I played uh my freshman year of college. I played at nickel and then in 2022 here I played a lot of nickel but it's this game a lot different than those schemes. So it's still a little bit of an adjustment. >> Kind of the nuances you got to figure out from this game comparing the other times you played there. >> Yeah, a lot of uh 2022 is just a lot of dropping to a spot. Zone drops your job didn't really change much but in this defense no one motion can switch your whole job and responsibility. So, kind of just getting into the playbook more. You know, as a corner, you don't you only got three jobs. You know, you don't you don't have to think that much. You just go out there and play. But at nickel, you got to kind of know what's going on with each motion and be able to switch your job because if you don't, can mess up the whole defense. >> What are your three jobs >> at corner? I mean, it's cover four, cover three, cover two, man. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. It's like it's pretty easy, but yeah, nickel is a little more difficult. >> You think it's going to elevate your football IQ? How dive in a little bit more? Um, I always thought I had football IQ and I was able to pick up on stuff pretty fast, but now I just just putting it to the test a little bit. Yeah. >> Did you talk to Jaylen Ramsey after they showed you those cut ups and or not? >> Yeah, I've been talking to Jaylen since, like I said, since a rookie. Um, we got the same agent. Um, and I got a chance to get with him this offseason. We got some work in and I just talked about talked to him about what they were trying to do and how he how he thought how he played in the slot, how he thought of the techniques. Um, I mean, it's been serving me well so far. >> How could that free you up potentially to make plays, I guess, cuz you're going to both directions when they're throwing at you? >> Yeah, I mean, just being able to, you know, make plays in the pass game, in the slot, in the run game, playing behind the line of scrimmage a little more, you know, blitzing a little more, it make it a little bit more fun. >> We've seen, we've seen flashes, the blitzing ability. Was that kind of part of the map putting you there because you can you I mean, you have the ability to do that and feel it out. I mean, yeah. I mean, you have to talk to Coach E on that one, but I think so. I think I'm a pretty good blister and good at disguising and stuff like that, but yeah, I think so. >> JC is Friday. Just how excited it's your first time in that stadium since the playoff game. How excited are you to get in front of the fans and kind of feel that energy? >> It's going to be cool. I think we uh last year we wore the game uniforms, too, so it kind of give you like a scrimmage feel. Um, and it's at night under the lights, so whenever you get a chance to play football under the lights, it's always fun. in front of the fans again that were that were so great in that playoff. >> Oh yeah. Yeah. It's it's going to be fun having them out there too. Um like you said the playoff game. I never seen the bank like that. Um so hopefully they can they can come out and turn FanFest up a little bit. >> Going back to sorry was that something was like sit you down. Hey, we're going to start doing this or was it just in practice like hey JC get over there. Let's try this. >> Yeah I mean we didn't tried it out. Uh we did it a little bit last year um in practice and just uh flirted with it, but you know this year I'm this is my first time really just staying in there and you know playing almost every down in there. Um but yeah, we'll we'll see where it takes us as far as you know how how it work out during the season. >> With him doing that, it means a lot of trust for the rookie he will leave. What do you kind of see from him so far and on the field? >> Yeah, he he he doing a great job out there. He doing a great job. you know, uh, he kind of trying to get used to giving up catches and, you know, getting scored on sometimes, but, you know, I try to just remind him that's a part of the NFL, like those guys get paid, too. Uh, you can't lose your confidence. You got to keep showing up every day and, um, just keep trying to get better and focus on your process. But, you know, he he doing a great job for as far as a rookie coming in and getting thrown with the ones. >> Appreciate y'all. [music] Heat.

title: Atlanta Falcons players speak to the media following the first practice of AT&T Training Camp
text: How was uh practice and just in terms of the way that the it was able to operate with the quarterback shuffle that's happening right now? >> Yeah, um you know, I felt like it was good uh just to get back out there with the guys. Um obviously day one um getting the the wrinkles out um and hitting the ground running. Um it it's good to see Mike out there um doing what he can do um in individual drills RBA um and seven-on-seven. And then you know, it's a next man up. Uh it's a next man up league honestly. So uh it it was pretty cool to see, you know, Cooper come in here um earlier today um and get reps in there get reps in there at practice with us. Um But yeah, it it it's good to see, you know, the guys back out on the grass um and getting back to work. >> When did you meet Cooper? >> Um in the huddle. Uh Yeah, it was it was my first time. I I walked over this morning at at about 6:50 7:00 and he was out there trying out. Um and then I had the first time I talked to him was in the huddle. Yeah. >> [snorts] >> When it comes to the the role of the receivers through kind of this this time period where things are shifting with the quarterback, this may sound silly, but is it really just like catch the ball when it's thrown to you? But like what are like what is the the role of of y'all's group and what are y'all working on amidst all of that? >> Yeah, um you [clears throat] know, I feel like for us one thing we we really preach um is control what you can control. Um and what we can control as receivers is going out there and getting open um and and catching the ball. Uh it doesn't matter who's under under center, who's throwing to us, whether it's our receivers coach, um whether it's one of the quarterbacks, quarterback coaches, it doesn't matter. Uh get open and catch the ball um and make a play for the team. Uh so yeah, we go out there control what we can control um no matter who's back there. Um but it but it it's good, you know, getting reps with all the guys, uh because honestly, you never know what can happen. I've seen some crazy things happen in this league. So, it is good to to get reps with everyone. >> Johan, you've done this for a little bit now. What's your mindset heading into this year in particular, new atmosphere, new change for you, kind of a turning of the page, if you will? >> Yeah, you know, I I came here um to to have a role in an offense um because I know the the capability that I have in myself as a player um and you know, this coaching staff, they saw that in myself as well. Um so, you know, I came here to to be a guy in this offense who's able to make plays and help our team win a lot of football games. Um I've been at the top of you know, I've seen what it what it takes to to win the big game and make plays in the big game. So, you know, I'm here to to bring that experience to these guys, to to the guys who haven't done it um and be outlet for the young guys, but I'm I'm here to make plays. That's what this coaching staff brought me here to do. Um and that's what I'm going to do. >> Speaking of the coaching staff, obviously, you guys have had a lot of dialogue so far and we're just getting started in camp, but your first impressions of what they want in this offense, what are they from you? >> Yeah, right now, we're big on, you know, our our operation, getting to the line of scrimmage fast, making sure we break the huddle fast, communicating, all the little details of what it takes to be a good offense. That's really been the emphasis early in camp and all throughout OTAs. Obviously, you know, execution is a big part of offense. Um but right now, we're we're really focused on the operation and getting those little details right because without those things, you know, you really can't be a good offense. >> I think I mentioned earlier that the the exposition here is still really up in the air. What does that mean? Like how does it What is that kind of like I guess for you as a receiver? >> What was that? >> So what what Mike said earlier is that the X position is still like an unknown here. Like what does that mean? How does it Yeah, just like how How does that look? Like I mean it seems like you would kind of want to have that all all known by now, I'd imagine. >> Yeah. Um, you know, we like I said, we're just controlling what we control. Um, going out there every day and you know, putting our best foot forward um and just trying to make plays and figure out those things as we go. Um Yeah. That's all I really got to say to it. >> So is it just not knowing the the role like what's asked for the position or is it not knowing who'll be out there? >> Yeah. Um, I'm honestly not sure. I can't speak too much on on what he what he meant. Um But yeah, I Yeah, I honestly don't know. >> How much do you guys cross train at the receiver positions? >> Um, a lot. Um, especially myself, um a guy who I feel like, you know, one of the reasons why I was brought in here was because of the way I can play at every position on the football field. Um, so yeah, learning every position uh as a receiver is huge uh just because it it gives a lot gives us a lot of versatility uh to do things as an offense. Um and we want to move guys in certain places obviously um to to create better mismatches for us. Um so it's a big thing for us to to be able to learn all three positions and honestly know what the tight end is doing as well. >> How distinct are those positions? Those three different spots. >> Um, very. Um, you know, you you got your F who's inside, um your X who's usually in the boundary, um and your your Z is a guy who's moving a lot. Uh that's kind of our move guy. Um, so being able to to learn all three of those positions is is critical for the success of our offense. >> Is there one you like better? >> For me it's it's whatever they put me out there at. Um, I feel like I can go uh make it happen anywhere. Um, and that's what I'm going to do. >> What do you think about the potential on this team with all the talent you have on offense from yourself, from Drake, from Kyle Pitts, Bijan Robinson? Just like how good do you think this offense can truly be? >> Yeah, I mean, it it's really fun to be able to to look at those types of things and you know, when you look at it on paper, like we we have a lot of guys who can make plays. Um, and it's even cooler to see it in person during OTAs. Um, seeing guys make plays. It was cool that we all got out there at OTAs to to be together. Um, and and see those guys make plays do what they do. Um, and then you know, that's why they're so special. So, it's I think it's a really cool opportunity we have. Um, and it was a really good job by the staff of putting it together. Um, so I'm excited to see what we can do. >> You've seen a lot of really good wide outs up close, like Warren Brown-Smith. When you see Drake London, what jumps out? What about him do you look at and say, man, that's why he's so good? >> Yeah. Um, I feel like for me it's his basketball background. Um, how he obviously he's big. He's 6'4, 6'5. And his basketball background, you can tell that he was a a guard. Just the way he moves and how he's fluid in his routes. Um, and then obviously he has the ability to go up and high point the football like no one else. Um, so it's it's pretty cool to to be alongside of him and watch him. Um, and learn some things from him. Um, whatever he he learns from me. Um, it's vice versa. So, it's it's a cool opportunity to be playing alongside of him. >> I've kind of heard about how like a release can be compared to a crossover a little bit. >> Right. >> Is that accurate? Is that how you view it a little bit? >> Yeah, for sure. Um, it's kind of like you're playing basketball without a ball in your hand. Um, and like you it's it's as simple as trying to make the guy in front of you go the opposite way of you're going. Um, and that's really all release movement is. Um, it's really basketball without the ball. >> You have your crossover? >> I did. I did. You can fact check that. >> [laughter] >> Still have it? >> Uh, probably not. >> John, we're talking about your confidence, obviously on the court, but on the field, you're clearly confident in what you can bring to this offense and just to the game in general. Where does that confidence come from for you? >> Um, I feel like it's the work. it's the work that I put in. I I know, you know, I prepare for these moments. whether that's my hands, my route running, the long days in the summer putting in the work. And you know, every everyone puts in work, right? We're we're in a profession where, you know, you'll get exposed if you don't. But I just know how hard I go. I know what I put into this. I know how much I care about it. Um, that's truly where my confidence comes from. Um, and then, you know, being around guys like I mentioned this before, like A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith. you know, drops drops can be a big thing for a receiver, right? And you talk to those guys about it and it's like I don't I don't care. Like it happens, you know, we're all human. You got to move on and go make a play.
