Um, so being able to pick up things like that throughout my career and then, you know, just the the work that I put in, um, I feel like that's where my confidence comes from. >> Why does this feel like a good fit for you? just talking with the coaching staff before I got here, um, the the vision that they have for me, um, and the things that they saw me doing in this offense, I felt like it was a a good fit for me. Um, and that was, you know, my position versatility, being able to move everywhere, um, make plays down the field, intermediate, short. And, you know, being able to to be one of the guys in the offense. Um something that, you know, I I haven't really got to got to showcase since, you know, early in my career. Um so, yeah, that's that's why I'm here. >> How much different is this offense than the one you were previously? >> Um it's not too different, honestly. Um you know, we're going to run the ball. Uh that's a main emphasis for us. Um we have one of the best backs and I think the the arguably the best back in the NFL. Um and I played with a good back in in Saquon Barkley, so you know, I know what it's like to run the ball, run the ball, and when you get your shots and your opportunities, you take them. Um and you make plays. Uh I know I A big thing for me is I know Drake is is going to be a guy who's, you know, getting coverages rolled to him. Um I'm going to be able to play one-on-one. Um and I got to make those plays for the team. Uh when I'm when my number's called upon, that's what I look forward to doing. >> Reporting yesterday getting the team back together and and just kind of the excitement level of of this crew getting back to it. >> Yeah, it was awesome awesome opportunity to uh to get back in the building. I've been itching at the bit um just to get back in the building and get on the grass, you know, if uh my off season was very well and uh enjoyed the time off, but, you know, it was time to start the roll and start the ball uh get the ball moving. >> Yeah. Where were you this off season? Who were you working with and and in preparation to get to this point? >> Yeah, I've been around here. Um had opportunity, you know, to be able to train in the building, had the opportunity to be able to train down at UGA and uh a couple guys uh that stuck around in the area um that we got the off season work together, so. >> Now that you have 1 year under your belt and with training camp, was there anything that you did differently this time or you were prepared for whether it's essentials or just preparing yourself for today? >> Yeah, you know, uh truly getting off season. That's how I prepared myself. Um having, you know, going in from my rookie last year, uh going into that transition of playing college football playoff game, preparing for the draft, getting drafted, reporting for rookie camp, getting to camp, reporting back to camp. You know, there was just non-stop football and didn't have the opportunity, you know, to fully enjoy that off-season. So, this year I had the opportunity just to rest, relax, get my body underneath myself and and regain so I could be prepared for the season. >> Teemu, I saw some video where you were working on your pass rushing moves. How much of that have you spent time on or or, you know, you're attempting to to learn more moves as far as coming up with a signature move? What's the deal there this off-season? >> You know, just working. Football is football, so keeping sharp in my craft, honing in on my craft. Being able to play my position, you're going to have to do that. You're going to have to be able to fend the run and be able to pass rush. So, just doing the things that, you know, being prepared for the season. >> As you continue to ramp up this weekend, still waiting to put the pads on, what are you specifically focusing on in anticipation for that? >> You know, going out there and attacking, you know, having the opportunity to be on the field with the guys is is a awesome opportunity. You know, we had a long off-season and had opportunity, you know, just to learn each other, learn the new teammates that I've I've had and learn the new coaching staff, Coach Stefanski and the new staff that he's brought in. You know, just going going day in day out, you know, learning each other and finding what compliments each other. >> It's a good bonding time as well. >> Most definitely, you know, having opportunity to to get to know everybody, get to figure out who and what people are fighting for is a great opportunity for us. >> Teemu, there's a lot of anticipation that you're going to ramp up what you're going to be doing. I know you can play on the edge and dominate there, but you were such a great player off the ball as well. What do you anticipate from that? >> Yeah, I'm I'm really I'm open and embracing the new role that can embark on my journey. Awesome opportunity that me and Coach Brick have, you know, spoke about and play the program and the the playing style that we will have this year. You know, I'm really excited for the role. >> Teemu is your new position coach. Can you kind of tell us a little bit about him, his coaching style, and kind of what it's been like even so far working with him? >> Right. I had awesome opportunity to know and get to meet Teemu last year as him being the assistant D-line and helping out with us a little bit. But now him being our position coach is awesome opportunity. I really enjoy Teemu. He's not only a great coach, he's a great player, well, great person. Having him in the room, you know, it's just not a a player-coach relationship. He understands, he's played this game, he knows the ways and different ways that people learn. He's willing and open to embrace with everybody's learning development and things like that. And of course, here getting on the field, he's also a great He's great work. >> I was talking to Britt, this had to have been during the spring at some time about Teemu coming in for that role and taking over. And he was talking about how cerebral Teemu is and how how he feels like he sees the field and sees the the play so much differently than maybe someone who has coached that position in in the past. Right. Um have you seen that from him? Just his like ability and intelligence to to be able to see the the big picture. >> I have. You know, Teemu doesn't not only know what's going on on the D-line and the outside backer, he knows everything what's going on within the defense, which is a great aspect and characteristic for coach to know. You know, having to know what the linebacker and the corner's going to do makes it easier to break it down and understand for the outside linebacker as well. If this guy's going to do this, you should be able to do this. And being able to make the call before you or before you even see it. So, he helps out a lot of just showing you know, pre-snap indicators and things like that. And having our tools and honing our skills of being able to be prepared for the play. >> Same driving classes, James Pierce. Is it Is it good to have him back out here in person? >> Yeah, it's great to have him back. I'm you know, my brother and I'm happy to support him. >> Second year you've been here. Do you feel like you're comfortable as far as showing your leadership skills? I know know, look at you sometimes trying to find your way and not step on anybody's toes, but did it come natural or is there something that's a fantasy or a brick that actually you do more? >> You know, something I ask myself to do more. You know, that's part of my my standard, it's part how I roll, how I keep my hold myself on a day-to-day basis. You know, as I said plenty times, you know, I was born into it. My dad being a a college football coach and watching him lead his football team and uh being at Georgia, being named captain of the team, you know, going through my hard days there and and leading us to SEC championships and and winning and things like that. Um you know, last year of course, going into my campaign, I I you know, finding my way, but you know, throughout the year I've gained that confidence of figuring out how I can be able to lead this football team and of course going into year two, uh I plan to do so. >> What's the difference between playing in 15 and starting the nine games you got a chance to start last year? >> You say that question again for >> Being that you got to start in nine games, you played in more, but the the games that you started, what was the difference that you got out of last year you bringing to this year? >> The same the same in mentality of just getting after it. I mean, I don't see a difference of starting the game um or you know, not starting the game. As long as you're in the game and contributing to playing the game, I feel like you should you go out there and do what you got to do. >> Who make [snorts] this year? >> Um two rookies and James Pierre. Sorry. >> Jaylen, I got a feeling you work pretty hard in the off season. You never shy away from the work. What did your off season look like? >> Right. Had opportunity, you know, just to rest, relax, um having the time to spend time with my family, um getting back home some, you know, uh settling in uh here, um having an opportunity to take a couple trips. Actually took a trip uh by the USO um to Japan. Um great opportunity just to go on uh three different uh bases, US bases, Navy base, the uh Army base and the Marine base. Um and it was awesome opportunity that I uh I encourage people to go and and and go see our troops overseas. Um it means a lot to me uh that the love and support that I had there was even shown. So, the blessing that I had to go and see them was was great. And then, you know, getting in that work. So. >> What was it like sharing that experience with John Harbaugh? >> We love Abe around here. >> love Abe. He's a true character, but not only true character, he dropped gems that I picked up not only within the football game, but within life. I see him as a older mentor for me. You know, I I and I appreciate the relationship I have with him. >> What does Dad think about your first year in the NFL? >> Dad Dad he's a coach, you know, he he will be Dad first. You know, and of course I've had It was It was a good year, but of course, you know, this we don't we don't try to lean on the past. You know, we just keep going and push to the future. >> How are you feeling about these earlier practices? Last year they were a little bit later in the day. Any I know you're used to the heat, but any advantage to starting a little bit earlier? >> Yeah, you know, it's great, you know, opportunity for us to get in that work without a melting. >> So, our early start's great, you know, but I know that we have a couple afternoon practices in the year to get us regimented to the heat. >> You're eight going into training camp. I mean, just how does it feel I mean, think back to like your first year to now. Just what is it How different is it? >> Uh a lot and I'm I just you know, I it's such a reflectiveness of like you go in the first day and so you still have the jitters, the fun and Jake and I always joke like, can I still do this? Like if I can I do I know how to play still? And then you go out there and it's like, okay, get the first reps under you and then it's kind of like riding a bike. Um but it was a it was a lot of fun today and like every day it's always fun to just be back out here. >> Where does this rank on weird days? You've got one new quarterback, three quarterbacks are down, Breshad is watching. Does it feel weird from your perspective? >> Uh a little bit. It feels new, but I think part of it also is just like with the new staff and with Coach Callahan, I think that kind of blends right in. So, there's a huge learning process for myself. So, just kind of really focused in on like our individual and and stuff like that. And that's been been good. I think Cooper Rush is I did not not yet. >> After this. Yeah, he's awesome. I got a text from my brother though. He played with him with the Cowboys and said he's a great guy. So, there you go. Looking forward to it. What's the role of the offensive line during this? I know it's just day one and there are a lot of things that are changing behind y'all at the quarterback position, but as a collective group and I know you're still trying to figure out what kind of what to do without Caleb beside you. What's the role of the group right now? I think just to play well consistency. I think offensive line is always judged on how consistent you play. There's no highs or lows. And so, trying to get that and work with each other and kind of form our identity. I know we we know what the standard that we want to play at and so getting to that point is kind of our job now when we're working. So, the fastest we can get to that and hold that, that would be be great. >> What's the biggest goals you got for yourself? And just the rest of the line coming in. >> Mhm. >> You feel like you want to get to the end of training camp having >> A mastering knowledge of the offense. I think you know, you year one with anything there's going to be learning and so get to be the best I can be as quickly as possible and then try and help guys around me to bring our room together and then development on the field just kind of locked in every day and coach Callahan's been great with technical stuff and so always improving skills. So, trying to get to that point now. >> How much different is it? >> It's it's definitely different. I think the workman like attitude is similar but the drills and stuff you know, I was doing the same individual for five years. So, it was like you know, kind of yeah, knew it. And so, thankfully this spring kind of went through the growing pains but now kind of I felt really comfortable today and know what coach Callahan expects and what he wants from a drill and look forward to getting the feedback in a little bit of how it went. >> Hey Chris, what have you seen so far from Michael Dorrell kind of holding down the fort right now with Tyron Smith? >> He's been great Um and just the same thing like getting the mental stuff down for us and then we can communicate how we want to do it with each other. And so like I said like we know what we need to what it takes and what it needs to be done. Um and so just like those twist games, the exotic looks we're going to get. Um all that's real really soon. So communicating that so we can you know get it right. >> I know obviously you guys always work out but do you feel like there's more of an emphasis with coach Stefanski on like lifting? I just feel like we always hear about him wanting to be bigger and be stronger and and lift more. Do you feel like there's more of an emphasis there? >> Uh I think so. I think it's consistency like with the lifting through this and the really um stressing the importance of it to maintain your strength deeper in the season. We were joking that this is always the best you're going to feel and best you're going to look and then you look at a picture of yourself in December and you're like not so good. And so [laughter] um that's just the consistency uh in the weight room which makes you more durable, makes you more in shape and leads to better performance. >> This is your third year with Mike going into this season. >> With everything he's gone through especially with the ACL, how have you seen his mindset kind of change or evolve as he continues to be you know the guy that wants to get back and be the starter? >> Uh his confidence around the building is great and just his personality connection with guys um and his attitude, the stuff he's been able to overcome and then the attitude that he came in today with and you know whatever setbacks he's had in his career, he's always overcoming it and has come in with a great attitude and he did that again today and so you just really want the best for him and so I think he put his best foot forward and you know kind of looking forward to see where that goes. >> There's a lot of rookies right now around this team. You're in year eight. What do you say to those rookies that like you know I've been here before, I know what it's like, what to expect? >> Uh you got to take it day by day and like meeting by meeting and really focus on be present. And so when you're present in what you're doing, um um, that's a good way to attack it and I I have said this that like I I had Alex Mack and Jake Matthews as great role models for myself. So I try and do or share some of the things I have learned from him and like one of the things was just like write down like what you want to improve on today and like pick that thing and work on that thing and then like you know, we have X amount of reps here, we'll have a 45-minute walk-through where you'll get 30 reps or even if you're not getting the reps, watch somebody and see how they do it and so, um, you slowly build and build like that and then do you have to take care of yourself because you know, everybody's happy and excited today, but middle to end of next week, you know, it's it's it's hard. It's hard to bring your best, but that's where you separate yourself is when, you know, it's not feeling so good. >> What are some of your takeaways from the way that Callahan operates so far? >> He's great. I mean, he's got a real intensity to everything and you know, the passion that he still has for coaching and I don't want to speak for him, but I mean, observing it, you can tell he's got that passion and energy, um, and the detail and just such a wealth of knowledge and he's showing guys from all these different years and the reason why, you know, things have evolved in his coaching and why he and then he explains it, um, has been a great resource and a great tool and so I'm so thankful, uh, that I get to work with somebody like him and uh, he's he's really good. >> You talk about the grind of camp. What do you actually like about camp? Like what's your favorite thing about it being back? >> I think the spending time with each other and you're just you're working and it's okay to fail. Like you're not you don't there's not like a deadline where like if, you know, I got beat on Wednesday, like Sunday comes really fast and you can develop and learn new things and so, um, really kind of pushing that, um, is fun and you compete against the guys and make ourselves the best we can is probably one of the the highlights of it. >> Chris, Jake Fisher is back with the team as one of the leaders. What do you kind of want to see from him as he gets reintegrated to the locker room? >> Uh, we're just treating him like a normal teammate. Um, I'm not going to comment on like any of the stuff off the field, but um, you know, he's come in and he's done a great job working since he's been back and so, um, you know, he's come in and, you know, the same as everybody else. And so, I think coach has set that expectation for all of us of what we want to be as a team and what he wants each one of us. And so, it's the same expectation. >> With Callahan, uh, very, very well-known guy. He's He's coached for years and years and years. I'm curious, what about him do you like? What jumps out to you? And what do you kind of see and it's like, okay, this is why he's been so good for so long? >> Very detailed technique-oriented, but like it's not that he he goes with the times. He knows how to adjust to his room and like get the best out of everybody. If it's advice he's looking for or advice we're looking for, we all just pick off of each other. >> Have you kind of gotten to see already cuz he's kind of well-known as a guy who can really grow talent? >> Are there ways you've seen in you already here? I I I know you got here late in camp, but you can kind of see, man, he's already gotten me better? >> Yeah, for sure. Uh, just like different techniques and things that I I haven't known, I've never been taught before. So, just like picking those things up and just sticking to them and just like being more detail-oriented than I was before, you know? >> You talked about the humidity, how it affects you. We saw when you kind of threw up, but still was [snorts] blocking at the same time. Do you think you would get some points for that? >> Uh, no. >> No, I don't. I mean, I feel like uh, if you want to fight, you know, that's what you got to do. You got to push through things like that. But that last rep was as you've seen, it came about of me. I said, drink too much water, it's going to come about of you. uh, man, just like I said, I'm trying to pace myself throughout the practice and not put too much on my stomach with this humidity. >> What do you feel like you bring to this O-line room? >> Uh, athleticism, uh, fun experience, and just, uh, like trying to be a leader, you know? That's That's one of the roles I want to step up into this year and just, uh, be a leader, be one of those guys people look up to. >> With, uh, you being here the amount of time, what kind of culture have you seen from Coach Baska that you're building here in the room? >> Uh, attack, man. Attack. Uh, just being smart with everything we do, attacking everything we do, and just being diligent, you know? Diligence is big and just make sure you detail-oriented and make sure we doing it together and one as a team. >> What kind of person and player have you seen out of mechanics over the last few days here? >> Oh, man, he's been working. I He was out here before everybody. Uh I went in to do some stretches this morning at 8:00. He out here running laps. So, that That should tell you a lot about him and what he's about. >> How does a left handed quarterback like playing right tackle? Is it weird for >> Uh no, just because like playing so so much of both throughout the years, it doesn't really like affect me. I say right tackle does a lot A lot does happen faster, in my opinion. So, uh just like just knowing who's back there and just being aware. >> How How was practice today just in terms of the way it was executed cuz obviously you have these quarterbacks who are kind of in and out. Obviously, Cooper didn't have much time here. Were they able to kind of get with the flow and carry things out as they should be? >> There was definitely a good flow. I I I'll say as a O-lineman, especially if you're tired, you don't really realize who's back there for if they're rotating like that cuz they all have pretty much the same cadence and they've been in the same rhythm. So, I'll say everybody's on the same page. >> Today. >> Today, uh I seen him on the news and when we were out there, he was like, "New player." I said, "Oh, cool." We said, "Hey, how you doing?" It was pretty cool, yeah. >> Has that like ever happened to you before in your career? >> Um I mean, yeah, you know, being This is my fourth year, you know, guys come come and go. So, uh just being able to like be a open hand and a leaning shoulder for them guys just in case like they don't know. Like I I don't know too much about what's going on. So, I'm still learning from the guys every day. So, hopefully he could pick up off of me as well. >> Who are you rooming with? >> Uh Later. I don't know. Everybody been in their room for real. So, it's like you don't really see who I didn't see who was in the room cuz I think I was like the first one in the room. So, I don't even know who was in there. I went straight to sleep yesterday. >> What do you bring to camp usually? >> Uh just a pillow, blanket, my iPads. >> Okay. >> That's it. I'm >> No, I'm not a big snack guy. Yeah, I don't really bring too much of nothing. Like I don't try to I don't want to get too comfortable, you know. I want to I want to feel the camp vibes, you know. I want to feel like the work, you know. >> What would a successful camp look like for you? >> Uh just getting better every day. You know, you're going to have good and bad days being consistent. Just consistently getting better every day, every day. And just like learning how to fight, keeping the good energy, and bring the guys up around you. >> How do you like survive the grind? Cuz it can be long. >> Uh you got to love it, you know. You got to get You got to fall in love with the monotonous things. And when you when you not in, you got to take those vicarious reps, you know. Just Just falling in love with the process. That's That's how you going to love in the grind. >> Jake's a long vet in this league. Has there been anything that you've been able to learn from him yet just in talking with him or >> Man, I think if you ask Jake, I probably ask him a question every 2 seconds. It's just like, "Hey Jake, how do you approach this? How do you approach that?" And you know, he tries to give his tips and stuff like that, but he also tells me like, "Hey, you're a different player than I am." And you know, like we have different niches. So, just picking up what I can and then applying it to however benefit me some somewhat, you know. >> How's it How's it feel to come back home? >> Uh feels good, you know. I got my family the right down the road, you know. I went to Grayson right down the road, so that's really a blessing to just play for the home team and just not have to worry about getting tickets to nowhere, so that'll be cool. But, you know, just not letting it become a distraction as well. Just cuz like, you know, family's close and it's easy to just say, "Hey, can you come over there da da da?" But no, I just I just want to keep that focus and keep it keep it the main thing.

title: Michael Penix Jr. & Cooper Rush reflect on first practice of AT&T Training Camp | Atlanta Falcons
text: How did your kind of the first day of uh practice go for you? >> Yeah, it was awesome. Um it is great to be back be back with the team. You know, um we we we grinding right now. You know, obviously camp starting so I'm be seeing these guys all day. So, I'm super excited. You know, everybody everybody came in with a lot of energy today and um we we had a pretty good practice. >> When did you learn that you were kind of more cleared for this for 11/11? >> Uh like a week ago. Yeah, so I yeah, I saw my doctor and he he just let me know um you know, just just want to like air on the safe the safer side, you know, just to make sure that, you know, I'm I'm where I need to be physically and mentally, you know, to before I go out there and and uh take those next steps. >> How hard was that to swallow though cuz obviously you wanted so bad to to play 11/11 for a while now. >> Yeah, I mean it it's tough, but at the same time like I I feel like um your health is is is the most important, you know, and you know, for me I I I want to take that seriously. Obviously, I have a long injury uh history so the the the last thing I want to do is try to rush back just just to get out on the field, you know, I want to make sure my body is healthy so that whenever I do get on the field, I can give it uh give it this team 100%. >> any similarities or differences in your recovery this time? >> Um it it's it's a little bit different. Uh I think my last two I was I was probably cleared by now, but you know, obviously um this is third ACL so um we we not taking this one lightly. So, we we got to make sure we take all the right steps so that uh whenever I do come back I I'm where I'm where I want to be. >> Mike, this morning Coach Spavital um complimented your ability to kind of both handle rehab and preparing for the season. How do you juggle kind of those two important aspects? >> Yeah, um well, I can't even think about the season until I'm recovered. So, I I guess that's the that's the way, you know, I I I can't be on the field unless I'm I'm 100% healthy so I got to make sure I take the rehab process, you know, um seriously and make sure I attack it hard each and every day. So, I'll say that's all. >> They giving you any like benchmarks like, "Hey, if you can do this by then, maybe you can get cleared?" >> Um right now we just seeing seeing where I'm at, you know, and and just you know, just trusting the process, you know. It's more seeing how how how my body is feeling, you know, with these practices, but um I know I was told that like another 4 weeks possibly going into that next stage, but at the same time there it could be earlier, you know, it's just depending on you know, how my body is doing you know, throughout this whole camp uh process. >> How's it feel differently just in training camp when you aren't able to get the the full reps? Like what are you maybe doing differently and kind of taking in during camp? >> Uh just a lot of mental reps. A lot of mental reps, you know, even whenever I'm not in I'm still you know, back behind the quarterbacks that that is in and I'm I'm back there you know, looking at the defensive structure, you know, thinking about the play call cuz I'm getting the play call as well, so I'm thinking about the play call and you know, and what I would do if I was in that situation. You know, obviously it's it's not the same cuz you're not in there, but you know, as best as I can, you know, mental on the mental side of it I try to take that seriously and you know, so I can get those mental reps so that whenever that time do come, you know, I'm I'm already mentally there, you know. >> What's kind of your reaction to just kind of the unique quarterback situation going on right now? You just added Cooper in and then Josh Rosen who can't play right now just with everything going on. Like how's that? >> Um NFL football. Um you know, uh you know, Trevor came in earlier this year and he was awesome, you know, um I love Trevor as a person as a player, you know, but um you know, we we [clears throat] had we moved on and we got Cooper and you know, he's been great today, you know, I just met him out there on the field today for the first time, so um but he he's been he was awesome all day, you know, he he was um he's very sharp, you know, obviously he he's been in the league for a while, he's played football, you know, um he he's played in games, so he he's he's a vet and uh you can tell and you can see that, but he he's He's great, he's going to be a great addition and with with Tua and stuff, you know, he's fine. You know, he has some stuff he's going through but he'll be back out pretty soon. >> Michael, you mentioned in the past you've been cleared by this point. Like when you when you went to see your doctor, I don't know if that's exactly how this works, but what did you feel kind of like when you were moving the way you need felt that, you know, you could be cleared I guess if if it had to be? >> I mean, I don't know. I mean, I'm not a professional in that space. So, uh for me, I'm just trusting him, man. All that he can go off of it is what he sees in me. So, whenever he saw me, it's like whatever he saw, he that's that that was the decision decision that he made based on what he saw with my body. So, but he did say I am further along than what he expected me to be. So, I feel like I'm in a great spot, you know, but like I said, man, just just controlling what I can control and going out there and attacking each and every day with my rehab process so that I can get back healthy. >> Like you played in a a number of offenses in your career. What do you enjoy most about this one so far and being coached by Alex as well? >> Yeah, it's been great. It's very versatile, you know, and I feel like Tommy, he's going to do a great job of getting everybody giving everybody opportunity to to make big time plays and you know, that's what it's all about. You know, trying to get the the playmakers the ball, you know, the best way you can and I feel like we have a a good a good scheme and I feel like what we're going to do this year is definitely going to highlight all all of our players and it should be a good year all around for everybody. >> What are your thoughts on chemistry, continuity and timing that you and Tua have been a little late getting started with the receivers? >> What's with the wide receivers? >> Oh, man, we we've been building that all all off season, you know, me and Tua both we throwing with receivers in the off season as well, too. So, as that's nothing. That that all comes comes whenever we get back on the field, you know, obviously we do a lot of routes on air and stuff, too. So, so that we can get that timing down, you know, so it's it's just football. >> Like obviously the beginning of your training camp was different like we're illustrating, but what is your favorite part about this time of year? >> Uh, just being just being in the locker room with the guys, you know, uh I'm going to be seeing them all day. So, uh just you know, just that that chemistry that bond, you know, that's what it's all about, especially during camp, you know, cuz it's every day not always going to be um no sunshine and rainbows. It it might be it might be tough and uh but to know that you got your brother uh by your side, you know, doing it with you, you know, it's it's definitely something special about that and and the bond that that we build being here together all day in the locker room and and on that field it's it's just definitely it's just going to make our team better. >> Michael, what do you feel like is more about how the mental aspect of your game that's always been something that's kind of been there for you? How do you stay sharp in that regard, especially right now? >> Yeah, uh just like I said, just taking those mental reps, you know, even whenever I'm not in, I'm still taking those reps mentally and just making sure that um I'm being intentional with with every rep, you know, whether I'm in or whether I'm not, you know, being intentional with um individual drill work, you know, whether it's, you know, doing um handoffs with the running backs or even routes on air, you know, just being intentional with every rep, you know, that's that's what's going to keep me where I need to be. >> Michael, we saw you in all OTAs in the spring and everything. The doctor says like, "Hey, maybe another 4 weeks." That's got to make you feel like >> Yeah, I mean, it's a maybe, you know, he said it could be earlier, too. Um but I wouldn't say it's frustrating because at the same time, you know, like I said, I I care about getting back healthy, you know, cuz the last thing I want to do is get out there and not be able to give my team 100%. So, um I feel like that's that's only right for for the team, you know, that's only fair for the team that, you know, whenever I do come back, I'm I'm 100% for them. >> As you sit here today, when do you expect to be healthy enough to be at least competing fully with Tua? I I don't know. Like I just like I said, man, I'm just running my own race, you know, just taking it day by day, you know, I'm just trying to get better each and every day. That's what it's about. You know, it's it's not no set date where it's like, "Okay, this day you're going to be good." Like, no, it this it don't work like that. You know, sometimes the body reacts great, sometimes it doesn't, you know, so you you never you never really know, but at the same time, like I said, I just got to do what I can to make sure that I'm taking the right steps and continue to move forward. >> Your next check-in with your doc, when will when will he look at it again? >> Yeah, he'll he'll see me before the season start. Yeah, for sure. >> like physically is missing, like that's preventing you from being like fully 100%. Like, is it the cutting? Is it the like being able to feel good every day? Like, do you still kind of feel sore after practice? Like, what's missing? >> Um, to be honest, I I've been feeling really good. Um, you you have to ask my doctor for that cuz [laughter] that's that's just stuff that he saw, but with the timeline that that he he wants me on, you know, so I'm I'm just, you know, doing what I can each and every day, but I feel great, you know, I feel like I can do everything, but at the same time, you know, I got to still be smart about it, you know, I can't afford to have somebody, you know, trip and fall and land on me right now, you know, just stuff like that. So, I'll say more contact aspect of it. Um, probably if if you want to highlight something, I would say the contact aspect of it. You know, that's what you you want to stay safe from right now, at least for, you know, another couple weeks. >> Is it going to be different coming in as a a married man now? You had a great exciting off season. How was the wedding? >> Yeah, it was awesome. It was awesome. Um, yeah, I'm I'm excited, you know, you know, my my wife has been amazing and it's just a blessing to be able to be married and finding somebody that you can spend the rest of your life with, so. >> Rehab, wedding, honeymoon, how's the golf game? >> Yeah, it's it's it's all great. It's all really good. Um, >> Get your picture, did you take pictures down? What's the story? >> Nah, I didn't take them down. Uh, I ain't taking them down yet. He he's he's pretty good. He getting better. That's what I'm getting better than he getting better. I'm like, all right, you He getting lessons, too. I still ain't get my lessons. I I'm slacking. >> Like now that you've been able to kind of marinate over this Tommy Rees offense, what do you think about it? How does it strike you? What do you get excited about thinking about what you're doing in it? >> Yeah, like I said, man, it's very versatile. And like I said, I feel like it's going to highlight all of our guys. But the thing about I I just feel like just the relationship that Tommy has been having with the whole team, you know, just you know, just getting an understanding of you know, what what we're comfortable with. And it's not like an ego thing where like anybody can't go to Tommy and you know, give a suggestion or give a thought. You know, it it might not always go through, but at the same time, you know, he always hears everybody out and you know, he he just want what's best for the team, the same as you know, everybody else out there. So it's awesome to be able to have that. >> What do you think of Ja'Tavion Sanders or Zachariah as a rookie coming in? You know, trying to make his mark in the NFL you want. >> Yeah, he he's going to be a really good football player in the NFL. Obviously, you already know what what he's done in college and his past, but it is definitely carrying over. He can play football. >> Michael, aside from the obvious guys on offense we already know about, who might surprise some fans at home you think that you've gotten the closest to? >> Um surprise some fans? Uh >> Let's go with it in a good way, too. uh I would say, you know, definitely Brian Robinson coming in, you know, obviously we we got Bijan, but at the same time he'll be in rotation, but he he's definitely going to make some big time plays. He he looks really good, really healthy. Uh he's he's going to be really good. Uh and I'm excited to see Jahan, too. Jahan, you know, you know, it's it's up in the air. Nobody really knows what what the exposition is going to look like, you know, but he's been he's been really great. He's been very consistent, you know, all throughout this off season. So, I'm super excited to see him this year, too. >> Who are you rooming with this camp? >> Uh all the quarterbacks. >> Oh, you guys are all together? >> Yeah. >> What is all the quarterbacks? >> [laughter] >> Nah, so uh Jack Jack is the only one that's not in there. Um but I think me me, too, and Coop I think Coop is probably going to be in that room as well. But uh Jack and the rest of the rookies, they've been here for a couple of days already, so he already had a um a room, so. >> What has Jack been like up to for you? >> Huh? >> What has Jack been like? He's kind of the only like, you know, full participant right now. >> Bro, man, Jack's been great. Like like just um kind of just think about it cuz like I was a rookie what, 2 years ago? And you know, just just seeing seeing what he's going through, I was like, man, that was that was me. Like just seeing his development and you know, how he's he's getting better each and every day, you know, it's awesome to see. He's a quiet guy. He's a very quiet guy. Um but at the same time, you know, he he's a competitor and you know, he could play he could play football very well. So, I'm I'm excited to see him continue to grow. >> To go from Division II to, you know, now being the guy taking the majority of the reps out there in the NFL a few months later, that's got to be pretty crazy. >> He holding his own. Yes, sir. >> Is there a snack rule in the room? >> Snack rule in the room? >> Oh, we got to get that going. Cuz I was I was like I was literally just thinking about that last night and I'm like, I'm finna hit up Jack and be like, you got to bring some cuz I had to bring stuff. So, he >> he got to be a trail mix or curry. Yeah, he got to bring some. Yeah. I appreciate you guys. >> What has today been like for you so far? >> Yeah, it's been fun. >> When you woke up, did you know you did you have your coming here? >> Yeah, we got in late last night and then it was a it was real early morning, still on Central Time a little bit and getting all the paperwork, physical stuff done and they said practice was at 9:00, so it was quick. >> Where were you at 24 hours ago if you don't mind me asking? >> Uh in Dallas, back home in Dallas, uh working out pretty much. >> What was your reaction when you saw like a 404 area code or whoever, you know, call you about, you know, coming to play for the Falcons? >> Yeah, it was awesome. Uh my agent called me and said, you know, they're reaching out and um you know, we're in the middle of the workout and said, all right, let's cut that short. We're going to go catch this flight really fast and get on the flight, get here. Uh so, it was good. >> How How was day one? >> Fun. Fun. It's a good reminder of like, especially when you're out of it for a little bit, how much you love it, how special it is. just feels right. >> Is there anybody here on the staff in the locker room that you have a a connection with previously that can kind of be a little bit of a an early lifeline for you? >> Yeah, I mean, I know I know Reese and I know uh RP, Robert Prince, from uh RP from Dallas for a few years. Um roster-wise, don't really know anyone. I was going through it to see if I knew anybody and no, so but uh those are two coaching staff connections I kind of have and it'll be fun. >> How do you kind of like manage like literally being the new guy and not knowing too many people? Like do you go around just introducing yourself all practice or like how does that work? >> Yeah, I met a lot of people today. Um it's been good. The support staff and equipment and training and all those guys are on it. Um like I said, things happened really fast. Uh it was really well done and uh football has a way of, you know, bringing guys together quickly, so I don't think it'll be too bad. >> How did you play in the league for a while? How does that experience allow you to do in this situation >> Yeah, you can definitely rely on it. You know, you've played with a bunch of dudes and um third string, second string, first team, you know, I've done it kind of all and it just gives you some perspective. Just go out there and play and enjoy it and uh realize how special it is. >> When in the drills you've done like during like have they given you play calls to call in the huddle or are they like how is it trying to >> Yeah, we called a few today. Um got out there and ran a couple team team drills, which is fun. Uh they gave me the nice basic ones luckily. So, it was good. >> Is the terminology like common enough across in the NFL? >> Uh I mean, I've heard it here and there. It's kind of new for me. I don't have much crossover. but you know, you've been around enough, you can kind of put things together pretty quickly. >> Have you been like through anything like this before where it's like so quick? You get a call, you join a team right away. Like >> Uh no, cuz I mean, last time I did this was COVID and you had to take a week-long of COVID tests and it was different and it's much slower process. So, this is the first time doing this. >> And did the Falcons explain to you at all kind of like role or your expectation or what's kind of like the quarterback situation right now? Like what they expect from you? >> No, I mean, they you updated me on you know, Michael and Tune and what's going on there and just kind of ready to get going, come in and come in and go. >> Is it kind of like hard to believe that like, you know, you're coming in maybe as like a third or fourth quarterback, but you'll be getting a lot of reps right now through training camp? >> Yeah, those reps are huge, especially trying to learn the offense and things those are very valuable. They're hard to come by in camps and I do not take them for granted. >> What have you seen from the guys around you? Obviously, Tune and Mike are out at the moment. What have you seen from the two of them and then Jack? >> Yeah, looking forward to you know, getting in the meeting rooms. That room's important, you know, and I'll see how it goes in there and get to know those guys. Obviously, they both have had tons of success in their career and getting to know Jack. Um looking forward to it. It'll be exciting. >> What's the What's the mindset going in? Are you Are you saying like, "Hey, I can I can go and I'll win this job over the next few weeks and be the you know, week one starter?" >> Yeah, we'll get We'll get to that eventually. [laughter] Right now >> I know you've been here for 5 minutes. >> Yeah, it's uh No, it's kind of reminds me of you know, when I first started undrafted, you come in and it's a whirlwind and you know, been down there before and you just go and play ball and see what happens and then um so looking forward to that. Like I said, it was really cool to be out there and kind of remind yourself um how fun it is. >> Anything else? >> What's like the first thing now when camp's over? What do you have to focus on cuz you're you're brand new. Do you have to figure out where to stay or what do you have to >> Yeah, I haven't got to those those guys yet. They uh I'm assuming they'll I assume they'll be reaching out soon. I have no idea. Packed for a week, so >> All right. Thank you. >> Good luck. >> Thanks. Thank you. >> Yep. Thank you, guys.

title: Head Coach Kevin Stefanski AT&T Training Camp Press Conference | July 29, 2026 | Atlanta Falcons
text: Exciting times, obviously, anytime you're you're starting training camp, so uh guys are ready to roll. We had an early report with the rookies, which I think is always beneficial, so for the rookies, for the coaches to knock off some rust, and then vets reported yesterday, and uh >> [clears throat] >> had meetings yesterday, had a conditioning test yesterday, then we'll uh go into practice this morning. Um Guys have the right attitude, really pleased with how they all came back, and uh we're ready to get to work. But, with that, I'll take any questions. >> I don't know if you heard a few minutes ago, I know you did not say that Mike Penix is not cleared for 11-on-11s just yet. Uh can you expand on that a little bit? >> Sure. >> Do you know when that might happen? >> Uh I don't know the exact date on when that would happen. Uh all along, as you guys can imagine, um I we have put total trust into Mike and the medical team and and and his uh the doctor performed his surgery. So, I'm very, very comfortable with where we are and the plan that we have. Um also, I know how Mike and he has the absolute right attitude, which is he's going to keep grinding on every single day and get better every single day. So, when that time comes, he'll be a part of those type of drills. In the meantime, uh he's working very, very hard, and he's working very hard in all aspects of of what goes into playing quarterback. So, uh yes, not in team drills, but I I don't want to lose sight of what he's able to do um in the building, in the weight room, out on the grass. There there's So, he's he's uh attacking this, and I I appreciate that. >> He'll still be doing what we saw him doing in the spring, essentially. >> That's right. That's right. >> Do you expect Tua to get most of the reps in, or is it going to be dispersed also with Jack Plummer? >> It'll be dispersed uh throughout. Uh I think Tommy and Coach Van Pelt have a great uh great plan there. Tua is dealing with an injury right now. It it's not long-term. He'll be out there sooner than later. Uh but, we'll uh we'll work through that in the next couple of days. >> What kind of injury is he's yelling what you say an injury, upper body, lower body? >> [laughter] >> It's like hockey, right? Lower body injury, upper body injury. Uh it something flared up. He will be back shortly. >> Did it happen while he was like this off-season, like when like away from the >> A few days ago, I believe. Yeah. But he he's you know he he'll be ready to roll. >> On Mike, he's kind of what plan did you try to have or I guess the plan that you had for him, how much is this kind of a of a problem? I mean, does it hurt you >> No, no yeah. >> him cleared by >> I would definite definitely would not characterize it that way. This is all part of the plan moving forward. Um again, I think every player, every injury you treat differently and you treat based on on the the how the person's doing, the the checkpoints, all these things. He's hitting every single checkpoint. So, um I'm very very confident in in the plan. >> Is there a point that you would need him cleared to say you can play early on? Week one, maybe even >> Yeah, of of course there is, but what what I want to say is that's really not my focus. It's not Mike Penix's focus. Uh our focus is literally on today and getting better today, which again, that's the only only thing that that only way I know how to operate and the only thing that Mike is really worried about right now. >> So, will he practice at all today? >> I'm sorry? >> Will he practice at >> He will not. >> Okay. >> Yeah. >> And so, who will be getting reps during 11-on-11? >> Uh so, we have some options there. Matt Ryan's not one of those options but before you guys ask, uh no, Jack Strand uh obviously on the roster but there's a couple more things we may do here uh in the near future. >> And then just to follow up on that, Travis Etienne got released today. What was the situation there with his injury and why was he released? >> Yeah, just injury related uh unfortunately. >> Going to OTAs, um you got to spend more time of course with Bijan. What have you learned from him and what surprised you if anything? >> Uh you know, Bijan from the moment I I the job uh just have he's been awesome. Like I remember meeting him in the locker room for the first time. Just the right attitude, you know, and then just to see him in these settings. While it's not football, you know, in the off-season program, it's it's not tackling and those type of things, but you see a pro. You see a guy that's handling his business. So, what I see from Bijan, I see from a lot of guys on this team. They have the right attitude. They're diligent about their work. They They take their job seriously. They push each other. So, he fits in really well in that regard. >> Did everyone report? Like everyone's here? >> Yes. Yes. >> Juwan is out, I saw. Um where is he kind of at in his process for recovery? >> Doing well. Got to see him work a little bit yesterday, I guess. So, he's doing well, getting better. Different guys come in at different stages of their rehab. So, there's some roster things that you have to do in camp with the PUP and those type of things, but feel confident in all those guys. They're all They're all really progressing well. >> Is that kind of a one-year spot now? Is that Mike Jerrell, who kind of is in that Yeah. And and you know, that's Coach Callahan. You can't just say, "All right, it's this guy." You have to work everybody in there. And And I think Coach Callahan has a very good plan on on not just moving guys in one spot. You got to be ready to play all across that line. >> I kind of wonder, is it more pressing for a lineman to return earlier on just to try to help cohesion up front, to try to help him acclimate? Like is is it more important for a guy like him to be out there now? >> I hesitate to say it's more important uh by a certain position. You know, I know every coach wants every player out there for every rep. So, that's the ideal, but that's not reality. So, we'll work based on the guys that are available to us. And this is good for us as players and coaches. This is the NFL. You have to adjust. There's guys that in the first play of the game, they're unavailable for the rest of the game. So, you got to adjust. You need to move guys around. So, that's nothing new to football. So, we we embrace that part of football cuz you better get good at it cuz sure enough that's coming when the season rolls around. >> Going back to Mike, you talked about his mindset. Other than that, maybe elaborate on that a little bit. What's impressed you the most about his approach to this entire situation? >> Yeah, I haven't gotten the sense really from Mike at any point that the injury was affecting his preparation. So, he's he's rehabbing an injury, but the way he attacks his day-to-day from meetings to what we do again on the grass, he's a consummate pro, very very intelligent. You know, has been in different systems, so it's he can talk through the nuances of certain schemes that he's been exposed to, if you will, but very very very intelligent player. >> With James Pierre-Louis, will he be more involved than he was in mini camp as part of the group? And and how are you just generally proceeding with him at this point? >> Yes, he'll be out there involved practicing uh proceeding normally. You know, he's he's obviously part of the team. We'll we'll see what news comes down the line, but that's really not his focus, not my focus. >> Is Tua going to be out there today? >> He will be out there for a portion, yes. >> Will if we look at him, could we see what Really, is there a reason that we're not you're not telling us? >> Well, no, sorry. Okay, that's a good question. I think in this part of the season, we don't have to divulge every part of the injury. So, I would tell you something flared up with him. I'm also not a medical professional, so I don't want to misspeak to you guys. Uh I just have a communications degree, so that's not my area of expertise. But, I would tell you he's he's getting better and he's getting better and and I expect him to be out there shortly. >> You seem to be taking all this in stride, but have you ever opened up a training camp with a UDFA as your number one? >> NFL, brother. I mean, that's like we're just talking about this is the NFL. You cannot predict what's coming. I don't have a crystal ball. I tell the coaches this every year. There's stuff coming that you can't predict and and you take it for what it is and and um you got to trust in the people around you and and understand that that's that's just how it goes. >> But but that feels a little extreme. Three three you know, it's your fourth quarterback on day one. Is that you're not >> not phased. >> So, if you're optimistic that Tua could be back sooner rather like could we see him this week? Like is something >> You don't want to put a timetable on it, but yes, uh shortly. Uh sooner than later, yes. >> Given my experience training camp, you begin to ramp up the X's and O's, you ramp up install, all that kind of stuff kind of accelerates. Does this affect any of any of that idea of what you want to >> It does not affect that, but to that point, Arch, you know, I made tell the coaches because our off-season program was so strong from an attendance standpoint, I felt like we covered a lot of ground. Training camp, you go a little bit faster. You don't maybe in the off-season program, you go slow and and and that's the right thing to do. You have time and you're diligent about putting it together. Now, when you get to training camp, those installs come fast and furious and that will not slow us down. >> James, do you have a sense of when there might be a decision? >> Yeah, bless you. I do not. Um I'm I don't have a sense of when that would come. >> Did you get everything accomplished in the off-season you wanted to? And if so, what what area maybe are you most confident about? How much do you know maybe an area that's you we better this area pretty good going into camp, we can look at the other stuff. >> I do think I feel very comfortable with what we accomplished in the off-season program. Uh then you finally get to get pads on out here. So, every team is you don't really know your team until the pads go on. And and what you do in the off-season program is great. It's it's safe. It's it's the way to do it. I believe in it. But, now that the pads come on, you can run the ball, you can stop the run, you can blitz, those type of things. So, later in the week when the pads do come on, I think you'll start to see that from the football team. And then you'll learn about the football team. And I don't know that it's fair to say absent having pads on, I don't think it's fair to say that you know exactly what your team is and how you're going you know, how you're going to win in this season. I think that's part of training camp is is finding out about your football team. >> With A.J. Terrell, look like he was practicing mostly on the outside during the off-season program. Is that something just to kind of get him ramped up or is that how you where you see him operating? >> I think he will be outside and inside. It's not that he's a one position player. With any young player, you want to get them comfortable as you grow their role. And it's up to A.J. Terrell or any rookie to earn that role. And we have to give those guys an opportunity to show what they can do. And and that will come over time. >> Coach, you hear a lot of second year with the team coaches saying first year, you know, we were just getting acclimated, hadn't been in the building, hadn't run camp, everything else. Like, you know, it's amazing what we didn't know yet, we know year two. Are you Is that lessened by the fact that you've been a head coach and you've been through that whole process and you know, why maybe it can run smoother, but it's still your first day here in Atlanta? >> Sure. I I think every year stands on its own merit stake. I don't know that year one challenges to year five challenges. It's the NFL like we're talking about. There's things that that you as a team you have to navigate. I'm very, very confident in the people in this building. Very confident. That's the locker room, that's the coaches, that's our staff, our personnel group. Then we got to go get to work. And and that's where I would tell you I really appreciate this football team, these players, what what they're about. Our guys like to work and that's kind of what I believe in. That's what we'll do out here on the field and when it comes time to keep score and those type of things, we'll get there. But prior to that, we got a lot of work to do. >> What do you most when you say our guys like to work, what do you base most of that on? >> Yeah, the fact that they're they're here, this off-season program, how they're here, how they're working, watching them in the weight room, watching them push each other, what they what we'll do out here on the field won't be easy and and how they embrace that, how they attack the meeting rooms and and lock in and are diligent about learning and and diligent about, you know, learning different roles if you will. So, a bunch of professionals that that that I really appreciate. >> Right now, you only have one quarterback able to take, you know, this full reps right now with Jack Plummer and you haven't or signed anyone else, right? >> something should happen here in the near term. I don't have confirmation just yet, but we'll get another person in here. >> Coach, if I don't know if you want to share, but if you could, what were some of the goals, expectations that you laid out with your team through the first few days that you want to make sure you guys accomplish on the right foot? >> I I think, DJ, every team has that first meeting where you talk about rules and and all that fun meeting that you slept through when you were a player. But I think for us, the the goal every team talks about the goal. It's easy to talk about, but we're really focused on what's in front of us in the work. So, that that's the that's the mindset, that's the message to our players is is worrying about what's right in front of us and and that's this practice at 9:15 and and and pushing each other throughout this day and and the work that we get done in this day. So, that's So, the message, making sure that we keep our head down. >> Has anything changed about your approach as far as learning things over the years and how you approach >> Yes. Uh I I think year to year you better be looking at your all of your operation and what you do and what you can do better. Uh I'm very fortunate to be around coaches that are truth-tellers and coaches that that I I feel confident can tell me what they think and things that we need to do more of or do less of. So, I've certainly over the years looked at different ways of of practicing and getting guys getting guys ready for a 17-game season plus that you know that something that you can earn that that those other games that you can earn. So, uh I do think uh how we've structured the training camp it is is getting our players ready, getting our bodies, our minds calloused up for for that that long journey. >> What are your expectations of the intensity level of these guys coming off of day one through this first week? >> Yeah, intensity will always be high whether we are in helmets like we are today, whether we're in shells in a couple days, whether we're in full pads, whether we're at walk-through. The intensity has to be there. That that cannot wane. Uh obviously, what we do, the physical nature of what we do will will be dependent on the tempos that that we're uh adhering to that specific day. Uh but I I expect our guys to be locked in from the jump. >> Anything else? >> Okay, appreciate you guys. Thank you. >> Yeah, thanks. We're good. >> See you. >> I

title: Head Coach Jesse Minter Provides an Update on Nnamdi Madubuike | Baltimore Ravens
text: I'm going to start off, really by thanking everybody in the organization, facilities people, equipment staff, all the people that, you know, just just help us be able to have this training camp, to have the setup that we have, have the facilities that we have. They make it super easy and simple for us to be able to do our job from a football standpoint. So, just just major shout out to them. Really good first day, really good energy. You know, I felt like said this before like the off season really gave us a foundation to be able to you know, hopefully hit the ground moving. Um and so there's going to be a ton to learn off that first day's practice film. That's what training camp is about. We look forward to that. But we have the mentality right now, you know, one day at a time, one step at a time, one little process at a time. So, we'll go in, we'll be able to watch the film, we'll be able to walk through some stuff, we'll be able to install for tomorrow's practice, and be ready to roll. So, with that, open it up for questions. >> Jesse, we saw Nnamdi out there, which looked like it would be a good sign. What did you see of him, and does this mean that if everything goes well regular season, he'll be ready for that start of the regular season? >> Yeah, Nnamdi has has now passed the physical and and come off of the PUP list. You know, it's look, it's still a process to get ready to play football, and that's something we're going to they're going to work through over these next couple weeks. I think everybody has a has a good feeling about how he where he's at and and where it's headed, but again, like those things there's a timeline involved, and that could that could you know, whatever. So, super exciting to see that dude out there with with his jersey on and his helmet. He looks great. He's been working really hard, and I think there's positive things to come with him. >> Jesse, what's the plan on possible for a couple weeks? He may just focus on individual plays, right? Is that kind of what you're hearing? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, again, like an individual coming off what he's coming off of, our ability to get him ready for a long season, Um, when he's had when he's gone through the things in the off season that he's gone through, I think that is uh our job, you know, to to protect the player and look out for the player. Um, and so we'll try to do that to the best of our ability. >> Hey coach, what is the biggest message you wanted to give your players when they walk on the field today? >> Honestly, just uh the mentality that we're trying to take, man. It's a day-by-day process. Um, you're not going to win because we're the Ravens. We're not going to win because we have XYZ players. We're not going to win because I'm the coach. Uh we're going to we're going to, you know, create our success based on the standards that we create, the process that we go through every day. How much better can we get between now and September? Then how much better can we get between now and November? Now and December, now and January, all the way through to February. So, that's really what we're focused on. Um, competing with each other, making each other better, uh but also connecting and and and developing real strong bond amongst the team. So, that's our that's our main objectives. >> Coach, with um the more probably more of a technical question, but what have just if you've seen probably from him, how much he sort of lifts the energy being out there? What kind of involvement have you seen from him kind of, you know, day one and leading up to this point? >> Well, Lamar is incredible. Um, again, best player in the league. Um, when he's out there and he's, you know, obviously really engaged like he is, uh he makes everybody on the field better. So, he makes the offense better. He makes the defense better for having to defend that type of player. all he's got to do is be himself. That's that's what he's proven that he is uh over the course of time. Um, I do think sometimes when, you know, you're trying to learn new things, like it really energizes you because you know that there's like a uh requirement to get where you want to get between now and the game. So, I just appreciate the way he's gone about his business and uh you know, he does a great job, man. Just from being himself and the spirit that he brings, making everybody else better. >> Coach, you know, you've had some time to adjust to the head coaching role in spring and in mini camp, but you know, especially on a day like today, do you kind of reflect on how different the approach is for you? Kind of it looked like you're kind of taking soft eyes to the whole operation, kind of stepping back. How different is it from what you've done before? >> Yeah, it's certainly a little bit different just from a job description standpoint, what I'm responsible for. You know, I feel like I'm responsible for how the whole team plays and whether all three phases, the style that we play. I'm not going to micromanage every scheme on all all three phases of the game. You hire people to do a great job. Obviously, I'm I'm going to have a more of a focus on one side of the ball. Um But it But it's my job to get us to operate the way that we need to operate, to to play the way that we need to play, to prepare the way that we need to prepare. And so, that part is awesome, man. It's awesome to, you know, watch our offense operate in a ball security drill or routes on air. Um To see see it go back and forth in team periods of, you know, different sides making different plays. Um And so, you know, the spring sort of gets your feet wet, but certainly, man, just the the appreciation I have for this opportunity on the first day of training camp when you realize, you know, that this is here and that all this is going on and all the fans are here. Um You know, much appreciation for the opportunity. Yeah, I think, you know, it's the first day, you know, and you're trying to communicate, you're trying to be on the same page when the ball's snapped. You're trying to execute a little bit without without pads on in certain areas. That's That's harder than others. Um But man, I just want us to have a growth mindset on defense, come out here, learn from what happened, go in and study the film, get a little bit better. Um You know, look, we got a long way to go, you know, and I don't think anybody would tell you otherwise that's a part of this group. We got a long way to go. We're here to work. We're here to improve every day as much as we can. But I do feel like we got the guys to do that and the guys to put a unit out there, you know, weeks from now that'll play the type of defense we need to play. >> The only guy we didn't see that's not on a reserve list was Calais. Can you what's his status? >> I would say you know, similar just in a sense of dealt obviously he dealt with um you know, personal like tragedy over the summer and you know, so from a preparation standpoint that that um you know, took up a lot of his time and his mental focus and energy. Again, we're here for Calais to get ready at the rate that he can get ready at. This guy it's a different than a 25-year-old that's played, you know, maybe only a year or two. This guy's got so many banked reps of experience of getting himself ready in camp. We're going to work together with Calais to to have a great plan to again have him ready for September, December, January, February. So that'll be a focus for us over the first couple weeks of camp. >> Jesse, having again kind of reflecting a little on a big picture but to have to be able to share this your first camp with your dad, to have him here at you. Take a moment if you like this is awesome. >> Here we are, Dad. You know, this is just like as a kid, you know, I was going to training camp wherever he was coaching. And so you know, I'm the kids running around on the field after practice. And so now to to to have that with him who I've learned so much from, who I share so many things with, you know, who we talk about a lot of different things. Obviously makes it really special. So yeah, it again just just a ton of of appreciation for what we got going on. >> In terms of how you wanted to run the camp, did you kind of pull pieces from all the different places you've been? I mean like do you have every day of camp planned at this point? >> Yeah, um it's definitely you know, I think again like as you go through this I do think when, you know, you have aspirations down the road to end up here that you you know, you start to keep notes and notebooks of things that you like and don't like and scheduling ideas uh from different people that I've been around. Um, and so yeah, it's it's uh you know, hopefully very intentional uh of what we put together for the players to be able to perform at their best. Um, that's really the simple bottom line of all the decisions is does it does it drive performance? Um, and so that's really, you know, do have it all mapped out? I think again, the ability of any good coach is the ability to adapt and adjust and move as it goes. Uh, but I you know, you put a lot of time in in studying and energy and communication with people to try to find out the best way to do it. Um, here we are. >> Have you decided about when your first padded practice will be? And do you look at that totally different than what we're seeing out there with the pads? >> I would say the first padded practice not as much. It'll be it'll be on when the rules tell us we can be in pads. Uh, but again, just like you try to you know, ramp into the first practice. I think once you have the pads on, there is like a a day or two of ramping into that. You know, you don't all of a sudden want to start banging your heads against the wall. Um, and so again, everything's intentional. We need a practice at a physicality level that we want to play at, which will happen I think over the course of camp. Um, and I think sometimes you got to really tame those guys down on the first day of pads to uh again, try to try to man, have this thing be with where longevity can win, not not just not just today. >> Jesse, you coach obviously very high-level players in the Chargers, but you know, there's so many vets in this group that have kind of been very close to the mountain top, played in that AFC Championship game a couple years ago. Guys like Lamar, Kyle, do you sense anything about their intensity, their kind of hunger to get to the Super Bowl, and and do Do you sense other guys feel that? >> I mean, I think I think if you asked every single player in the National Football League right now that they have intentions of trying to help their team get to the Super Bowl. I do think your experience grows, your focus, and where your energy's at. And so, this is a group that is I would say really hungry, not thinking about the the end goal yet. I think they know that that's what we all want to want to do, but a willingness to go day by day and focus on the process and build build this thing up so that when those moments happen that we'll be at our best. So, I have a ton of love and appreciation for those players and their experiences. I asked them a lot, you know, about things that they're thinking about. And so, it's great to have a bunch of guys that have been through some battles and have some scars of getting close or having seasons where they're, you know, way up there and then it doesn't happen. So, I think all those experience help you help you grow. >> Kind of off of that a little bit, just focusing kind of on Lamar and as players stack years, do you think the urgency kind of increases well? In your communication with him, either by the text or talking, have you sensed that urgency and has has Super Bowl even come up in any of your conversations with him? >> You know, I think honestly for me to answer that is a little bit unfair just because I haven't been around him the last 4 years. he is really really hungry. He He's got a lot of intent right now of what he's trying to get done. Can't speak for, you know, I thought he was like that as a young player, you know, so I think I think he's such an elite competitor and wants to do that that that's always been his goal, but I do think again as you go through things and as you have ups and downs and you kind of learn your, you know, that your career may not last forever and you and you have you know, these goals that you want to accomplish. You sometimes your focus narrows and I would say that uh he's got a real narrow focus on what we're trying to accomplish and definitely appreciate that from your quarterback. >> Coach, obviously as the head coach you have more say on situational stuff, clock management, timeouts, fourth downs. What sort of prep have you done this offseason regarding that and how important are the next five weeks regarding that? >> That's a great question. Uh you know, all kinds of prep as as far as um Charlie Charlie, our game management person, does a phenomenal job like have these meetings every few days trying to trying to create scenarios off of previous film and in our head uh to talk through that with not only myself but Declan and Weave and and uh co-cap. So, um that's something that we're that we've had a major focus on between the end of the offseason program and now. And then you get a chance, you know, situations you get a chance to practice them all. Um but it's really hard to create the sense of urgency and like the realness of that happening. Um and so you try to teach them as best you can, try to learn them as best you can, try to anticipate as as things come up in a game what might happen. and it's something that I think I learned a ton about when I was here the first time. Um and so this was always an organization I felt did a great job in that regard ahead of the curve maybe back in like '17, '18, '19. Um and so I learned a ton here and I've tried to do that at the other places. Uh and so it's a it's definitely a challenge I'm excited about. >> Coach, you guys made a pretty big addition at center with Ethan Pocic. What did you like about him and you know, can you share with us what the plan is for him knowing he's coming off of the big year? >> Yeah, I I think uh it's competition at a place where you know, you have some good players. You might not have as established players that at some other positions. and so you're bringing in a guy that's got some uh skins on the wall, has played a lot of football. Again, another one of those guys that you know, it's our job and his job and our performance team's job to help acclimate him back into football coming off the injury that he's coming off of. So, another guy we'll be working closely with as far as the amount that he's doing over these first couple weeks. Uh but I expect him to to jump in there and compete for that position and uh we'll see the best man wins. >> All right, thanks coach. >> Thank you.
