title: Kyle Hamilton: ‘I Wanna Win’ | Baltimore Ravens
text: some things to go, but he was out there fully dressed as someone who's probably seen him a lot in that locker room trying to get. What do you think it means to him? What do you think this means to the team seeing him return? >> Yeah, I think it's a great thing just seeing him out here in the building in the locker room. He's such a vibrant personality and you realize when he's here when he's not here and that's all for the better when he is here. You know, he's never bringing any sort of negative attitude and it's just awesome seeing him back out here going through the process. Was it a surprise when he showed up or you he knew he was going to be here? >> You know, I mean during the time he was dealing all that stuff. It was middle of the season, so I mean check in on him here and there, but at the end of the day, that's his business. I'm not trying to put myself in his business. Also, HIPPA, so not trying to violate any HIPPA rules, so just do my job. Kyle, just knowing how dominant of a player he is and just accomplished in the past, how big of a person does get to >> Yeah, I mean, you know, he's one of the most talented people at his position in the league, and I don't think it takes a a genius to realize that we'll get better when he's on the field. So, um, you know, it allowed for a lot of younger guys to step up and get some reps, some much needed reps going into this year, but, you know, we're all hopeful to get them back as soon as possible. >> Taking getting used to having your defensive coordinator is not the play call, the head coaches, it's a different dynamic or what is different about that? Anything for you personally? >> Yeah, I've never had that in my football career. Um, you know, Jesse makes it somewhat seamless and the adjustment process was minimal if there was any. You know, we came in and just announced to the defense, "Yeah, I'm calling it. Weave is going to help out a ton and all these other guys in the room are going to be integral in every part of what we do, but he's calling the plays." And the at first we were I don't know, nobody was really thinking that much of it really. You know, it just kind of happens and he's over on the side calling the plays and we're just doing what we got to do. But at the end of the day, as long as play is getting called, then I think we're we're having a good time. >> What's your take on the tournament? >> Yeah, I think it's a very positive outlook. I think it's a glass half full optimistic type of outlook and I think that's something that, you know, guys don't take lightly. It's a it's a stressful league we play in. It's a stressful job. I mean, as stress was, playing professional, I guess, tag for a living is, but um you know, it's it's it's kind of a pressure cooker that we live in on a daily basis, and he tries to take a lot of that out of it by just, um maximizing our opportunities when we're out there. Uh understand that we have to work hard, but at the same time, he takes care of us and um puts us in position to be successful and doesn't put everything on our plate every single day. you know, it's little little things at each time and I can see us slowly crescendoing throughout the season. So, um I'm excited for the outlook that he has and the outlook that everybody on the team has. >> You know, I know you guys aren't hitting yet, but obviously one thing or two things you can check is now is communication and also are guys where they're supposed to be. I know you guys are going to look at films right now and see how you did, but just be playing live on 11s. I mean, where do you guys feel as a defense on those two things? right now. >> I think we feel really good. I mean, the guys who've come in that haven't been here, learning a new system have learned it in I think like record time since I've been here. You know, like Jaylen Hawkins comes in and he's barking out calls like he's been here my whole time that I've been here and it's really helpful and I think that kind of pushes me and pushes people who have been here to kind of keep a standard up. Um, you know, and we're all pushing each other every day. I feel like the defense specifically is at a level right now where communication is very high and at this point like you said that's really all you can do. Obviously work technique and man-to-man stuff, you know, ramps up throughout camp, but just communicating and being on the same page and we have a bunch of just qualities about a good defense that we preach in the meeting room that we've always preaches and first thing is communication, connection, and you know, you're not going to get very far if you don't have either of those. So, I think we've done a great job of that so far. Kyle, you've been here obviously a handful of years and you're going against Mo in practice during that time. What have you seen from him, you know, this year maybe compared to past years or is anything kind of stood out? Obviously, like we know his talent, but is there anything that just kind of stands out to you when you when you watched him? >> Yeah, I think he, you know, it's the one I guess just technically schematically the under center. Uh, it feels very natural from my perspective for him. um just play fakes, uh running out or running out of every handoff like he has the ball. It's just little stuff like that that he's been very intentional about. Um from a I guess ability standpoint, you know, I feel like he's he might have gotten faster somehow. Um I don't want to age him, but he's turning a certain age next year and you know, it doesn't seem like that. You know, he's uh we'll keep that age between us, what what age he's got to be, but he uh I feel like he got faster. I feel like he ran today. It was really fast. I don't know if you guys saw that, but maybe that's just how he always runs, but he's he's uh just like our season. I feel like he's going to get better throughout the whole year. And the more comfortable he gets in what they've got going on, which I have a ton of faith in. I'm talking to those guys, they have a ton of faith in it, feel like he's just going to get that much better. >> Why do you think Lamar has been able to have so much early quick success with new offensive coordinators installing new systems as he's going to have to do again this year? Yeah, I mean at the end of the day, you know, schematics, they play a big part, but I mean it's it's jimmies and Joe's. It's not X's and O's. You can have a bunch of bad players out there with the best scheme in the world and it's going to look horrible, but you could have some holes in a scheme and you got Lamar Jackson, you might want to MVP and go really far. So, I mean, scheme is scheme, but Lamar is Lamar at the end end of the day. And, you know, he's a very gifted, talented human as well as athlete. and you know, you throw in the kitchen sink and he'll make a good meal out of it. Kyle, >> you mentioned guys on defense learning quickly. Anything that surprised you about working with Jesse, working with Pete, just how quickly some things have come together that you've seen so far? >> Yeah, I think it's, you know, there's been no, I guess, abrasion or kind of friction between players and coaches with installing new stuff and then kind of unlearning old stuff that we've had. And that's been ingrained here since for a long time. We've been running pretty much the same system since Ed Reed and Ray Lewis were here. We just kind of tweaked it a little bit. Um it's kind of grown and evolved throughout the years, but you know, we give our two cents on stuff that obviously has worked Jesse in LA and he's willing to compromise on it. Um in a sense that to make it easier for us to understand because obviously it's different players. But, you know, it's been really refreshing to see that and, you know, see that he's willing and we even all of them are willing to kind of hear us out. Not saying that it wasn't like that before, but new coaching staff, you would think they come in and be like, "This is how we're doing it now." But hasn't been like that at all. >> Is it is it like going to Is it like going to a new school at all where the routines just feel maybe a little little bit off, a little bit different or really not? >> You know, I mean, all the logistical stuff is obviously different. Like, we practice at a different time. We might meet at a different time. Meetings might be a different length. I mean, at the end of the day, it's still football. I I think, you know, players win the games and I think coaches prepared the players for the games, but I mean, on Sunday, it's us out there. So, no, no, not to discredit the coach staff we have, the coaches that staff that we had in the past, but you know, at the end of the day, it's on us and they can only do so much. So, um, the day-to-day stuff is obviously different, but I still think we go out there and we make the plays. Kyle, two more guys along those lines. Um, I forget if you were asked this during the offseason, but you know, you leading during that first game and having to watch the defense struggle, like how did that kind of resonate with you and maybe what kind of lessons this devastating to to be like a little bit more fulf? >> Yeah, I think it's it's a very detailed oriented and it's it's very detailed with the ones, twos, threes, and whoever may be out there. because obviously as you know it's not an if but when injuries happen in our sport and somebody's going to have to step up at some point in the season. It could be halftime week one. It could be week 18 to keep your season alive. Um to that point I mean we lose people like Rocoan or >> the wood >> like Rocoan or whoever like leaders of our team offense, defense, special teams. Obviously, those are going to be big holes to fill, but fill, but at the end of the day, you're supposed you're expected to come in there and do your job. So, I think it's a detailed thing that has been emphasized so far, and it's going to pay off >> laterals in in training camp here. Do you have any specific aspirations as you adjust to this season? >> Um, I mean, I want to win. I think I'm trying to do my best, whatever that may be. I don't have that down yet to a science. Haven't won anything. So, I'm just trying stuff out, but do whatever I can to help guys in there be successful. Um, you know, young guys jump to the second year. That's like L Malachi, Keandre, Keith Martin, those guys like help them throughout this camp cuz they're so talented. Like Malachi, I don't see a reason why he can't be the best at his position in our league. Um, he has all the talent, all the mentality, just the approach to the game that I mean, very soon here, I wouldn't be surprised if he's best safety in our league. So, um, just like seeing potential like that, I feel like throughout camp try my best to, you know, raise those guys level and bring the potential out. >> Thanks, Kyle. >> Appreciate y'all. Find the switch at six.

title: Why the Zay Flowers Extension Is Close to a Done Deal
text: LA Langly to Zay Flowers and the potential timeline and contract extension discussion that continues. It's really been a major point um of discussion this off season knowing that he is gearing up for for year four. He changed representation over a year ago now. He's coming off back-to-back 1,000-yard seasons. He is the Ravens number one, Jeff. Uh any anything change along these lines of just You've shared a lot of thoughts. Even Eric has shared some thoughts recently uh in a local interview on the fan referencing that he he would like to get something done before the start of the season. Um Your your thoughts on this? >> I think this deal gets done. I really do. I mean, I say that partly because you know, when you're on this beat for a while and you deal with Eric DeCosta for a while and you start and you know, you kind of interpret some of the things he does. Eric's not going to create expectations in the media. He's just not going to do it. It's not going to make his life any easier cuz if you speak really optimistically about something that it doesn't happen, you you get the fallout. And it's basically like you create expectations. And you know, our you know, uh love Cordell and he went on with Cordell and um you know, I guess it was uh Vinnie, too. And he said um you know, he spoke optimistically about it. And I think what changed or what changes is the timing. You know, players want these deal Player who wants a deal wants his deal done before he steps on the practice field, usually. And I'm not saying there's going to be a line drawn in the sand. There's going to be a hold-in situation. But this is the time you hammer out deals like this. And Zay Flowers has been clear. He said the right things publicly. Uh from the sounds of it, he really wants this deal done. And the Ravens love Zay Flowers. They love everything about him. He's well on his way to becoming the best homegrown receiver they've ever had. They appreciate everything about him. The new offensive staff loves him. And you know what? There's a quarterback who also needs a contract extension, who also loves him. So, um you're going to pay. The wide receiver rate keeps going up. You know, I don't know that a deal's imminent in terms of, "Hey, could get done like, you know, any moment here." But, um I would have to assume they've put in enough legwork there to kind of knock this out in the next couple of weeks. title: Bradley Chubb: "This Is Really Dope To Be A Part Of This" | Buffalo Bills
text: All right, back here on OneBillsLive. Chris Brown, Steve Tasker. Welcome to day one of training camp coverage here at St. John Fisher University. And set to pull on He's going to do the Chris Collinsworth slide here on Monday Night Football. Bradley Chubb joining us here on set fresh out of the showers and squeaky clean. We appreciate that, believe me. We got some big offensive lineman in here coming right off the field. They're sweating bullets and they stink to high heaven. So, I appreciate you considering the hygiene factor joining us. So, thank you >> for that. I appreciate it. >> Yeah, welcome. It's good to see you. >> Yeah, good to see you all >> And I have I know the first thing you got to ask is how things are different. You're You're wild You've been around the block a couple of times in the league. You've seen a lot of training camps. How you know, we're going to ask you about how this one's different other than the weather. >> Yeah, the weather is one thing for sure. But I'll say traveling. Traveling in being in a secluded location with the team. You know, we had road trips and stuff like joint practices, but I feel like you know, going to a college like this which is a beautiful setup by the way. They do a great job setting up for us. I didn't realize it was going to be as good as it is. But coming here, being in the dorm rooms, kicking it with the guys kind of everyday thing is is a is a dope experience and I feel like that's something I haven't had in the 8 years prior to this. >> rare. >> Yeah, it's very rare for sure. >> Yeah, there's only a handful of teams that still do it. Bills being one of those teams. I guess there are some congratulations in order. You got engaged this this uh >> Married in May. >> Yeah, got married on in in May. >> And you got married in May, yeah. >> Married in May at the end of OTAs and mini camp. Turned 30. New team. It was a lot of stuff that that was new for me this offseason. So, it was a a good one for sure. >> And also you're going to jump into a new stadium with the team. Have you been through it? I mean >> Yeah, I went through it when it wasn't fully done yet. So, I'm excited to see it all come together, all put together. So, I know it's going to be Oh man, a spectacle. >> So, let me ask you because you know, you have a a crunched and condensed calendar here. Did the honeymoon happen or is that going to happen later? [laughter] >> Yeah, it did. It did. So, like I said, we got married in May and then right after OTAs took that week and did the honeymoon and also kind of celebrated my birthday, her birthday at the same time. So, it was it was a good >> nice. >> all-in-one trip cuz our birthdays are 2 weeks apart. So, it wasn't that bad. >> Yeah. >> So, are you guys the same zodiac sign, too? >> Okay. Okay. Look at that. Yeah, Steve loves that stuff. >> I hate that stuff. [laughter] >> You can you got some attention when you reached out to T.J. Parker. You guys spent some time together. And for a guy like you, you were with with um Von, right? I mean, you had a guy that did that for you. Now, you're paying it forward for a guy like T.J. Um how important was it for you as a young guy? And what did you kind of impart on T.J. and gives you know, kind of expand on that relationship? >> Yeah, man. It's a very important. I feel like you know, coming into the league the vets I had were you know, second to none. I had like I said, Von Miller, Shaq Barrett, Shane Ray, Derek Wolfe. All those guys coming from that Super Bowl 50 team in Denver. They were still sticking around and kind of you know, just giving the game like we weren't the best team, but you know, we had the that vet presence and it it really instilled a a lot in me as a young guy. Showed me the way, showed me how to operate, showed me how to treat the guys coming up after you. And I feel like that's kind of been my main thing since you know, I hit year three, year four. Just try to be the best vet I can be because I had such great examples ahead of me. So, and with T.J. like I said, I I've seen a lot of him in terms of his you know, just willing to get better willingness to get better. And I wanted to pour into that as much as I could. You know, he's always asking me questions even if it's not about football, just life stuff. And just trying to you know, help him out the best way I can. >> I know leadership is not a new thing to you, but you're you're the new guy in a new place. But I I'm sure you've looked around on the defensive side of the ball. There is a lot of youth on that side. How even as the new guy do you take it upon yourself to kind of help lead a group? I mean, I know you have Ed and Greg who've been here for a little bit, but how do you take that upon yourself in a new environment to still lead? >> I take it So, like first of all I rely on those guys Greg and and and Ed and just try to see like, you know, what's been what's kind of been the thing the theme here what's kept you guys so close cuz when you look at the Bills defense that D-line is always like this, you know what I mean? Even when I first got here those guys were joking with each other and always sitting together always doing stuff together. So I kind of leaning on to those guys and try to like pick up what I could and then implement what I know into that, you know what I mean? I'm not trying to come in and be oh this is my D-line now like we're doing this like that's not that's not how you lead. I feel like you got to kind of kind of sit back and and observe first and then you know see, you know, how you fit my leadership styles into what we already got going on. >> You mentioned the relationships that the D-line had how they hang out and they do stuff. What about this this overall culture you've been on a couple of teams now and you've got to had a chance to experience different head coaches and different cultures. What jumps out at you the most maybe both positive and something that you'd like to impart on this team from what you've learned? >> Yeah, I feel like uh the team itself is is a lot closer than I've been around. You know, I've been around with the guys where you know, our defense is really close so our D-line is really close our outside linebackers are really close but like I feel like that it intermixes here a lot. Um you know, the offensive lines hanging out with the DBs and and you know, it's just it's >> They're crossing sides of the ball. >> sides a lot, yeah. Positions you wouldn't even think hanging out always sitting around eating lunch together always sitting around eating breakfast together. So I found that really cool and then when I first got here man Dion was like, hey we love each other here man. So whatever you need just let me know and I you know, you see him, you know, leading his way bleeding into the whole team and it's just really dope to see really glad to be a part of this and you know, like I said implement my style into this. >> I know you and Josh came into the league together just two picks apart. I'm sure you've heard the story. So Brandon Beane is desperately trying to trade up to go get Josh. And he's on the phone with John Elway in Denver. And John Elway says, we'll give you pick five if our guy isn't there. You were their You were their guy and you were there. So they picked you at five and then Brandon had to scramble makes a trade with Tampa and gets Josh at seven. >> How crazy I mean for us as Bills, you know, followers and and fans and stuff it's crazy that you're both here now. For sure. I mean pick five and pick seven in the 18 draft are on the Bills roster. I don't know if that's ever been communicated to you, but how does that how full circle does that feel, you know, knowing you guys went in two different places back in 2018 and now you're on the same roster? >> Now for sure it is full circle. Not because I didn't I didn't know that story at all. Um but it's full circle because when I got to Denver, you know, they had been like dying to get a quarterback, you know, and um you know, I was the pick there and they were like, "Oh man, we should have got Josh Allen." Everybody So, you know, I heard >> Yeah, yeah. After after after the fact you heard it, right? >> Right, right. So, me and Josh kind of been tied in that, you know, our my whole career. Um so, just to be on the same team now, same you know, same goal, same mission is dope to see, man. Just to see how he's blossomed over here in Buffalo, man. I know um you know, when I first got here there was a lot of like, "Oh, what is this guy doing?" But year nine and he's the best quarterback in football. So, I'm glad to be on this side. >> and he lets John Elway know about it every chance he gets, too. >> No doubt. [laughter] No doubt. >> So, you're So, you are a new guy here, but also a new head coach. So, it's new for you. Everything's new for you, but how has it been for, you know, the other the guys who have been here like Josh, like Deion about how the new regime, the new coaching staff, how you know, how's that change been going for everybody, not just new guys like you and the rookies, but what are the veterans saying about you know, how what a new experience it is or how it's going in a different direction? >> they say it's fresh, you know, it's it's a fresh a breath of fresh air. You know, they've been do you know, locked in on doing something so for so long and even Joe when he gets in in front of us to talk, he says, "Hey man, I know it's a lot of stuff the same, but like this is year one for us as a as me as the head coach as this team this is our first year doing this." And not to give an excuse like, "Oh, we're going to have ups and downs." But it's just like give that fresh energy and that fresh um, know, atmosphere in the room. and I feel like everybody feels it. Um, nobody's trying to like, oh, but last year we did this. But it hasn't been any of that, which is, um, you know, cool to see because like I said, you got vets in the room who've been doing it for so long, they, you know, you want to resort to what what you know, but everybody's been buying into the change, and, um, it hasn't been, I don't know from previous regime how much change, but it seems like it's a lot of new energy, a lot of new, you know, um, mojo going in. I'm excited about it. >> Your DC, Jim Caldwell, uh, played for 10 years in this league more because of what he had between his ears for sure. Um, than anything else. Sharp tack. I'm just curious, like his early messaging for you guys. Joe Brady this morning said after the coaches assessed everything in the spring, they may trim the menu on defense back a hair, and maybe that's because of all the young guys you got on that side of the ball. You don't want to throw too much at them so they're drinking out of a fire hose. >> Right. >> Um, how do you feel his messaging has gone in the early going with what he's asking of you guys on the defensive side of the ball? >> like it's going well, man. Um, yeah, it's a lot because like he like I said, he's so smart. Like you just said, he's so smart, he knows the game like inside and out. So, when we're installing things, he's installing it like from a from why he's doing it, you know? And it's I feel like being in the league so long, you always got the coordinators you're like, why are we doing this? Like I get the call, but like why are we calling it? But as he's installing it, he's telling us why we're doing it, for what situations, and and and I feel like his, uh, football IQ is bleeding into the defense, bleeding into us because, you know, we're playing smarter. We're not just going out there and and following the line that's on the on the on the playbook. And I feel like, you know, once you kind of install it like that, it makes it a little bit easier for sure to like understand it and and get the rhyme and reason why we're doing things. And, you know, it's it's, like I said, he's got a lot of going on in that head, so it was a lot at first, but I feel like, you know, as we start to get comfortable with it, you know, get more reps on this practice field against other teams in the preseason, I feel like it's going to be, um, night and day. >> Give us your thoughts on the guys around you, the D-line, the the defensive tackles, nose, and on the outside linebackers, that five-man front. What are your thoughts about those guys, the group, the attitude in there, the personality, and maybe the production that you can see on the horizon? >> Yeah, the group is amazing, man. Like you said, there's a lot of young guys, but there are I feel like there's a lot of young guys that play some ball, you know, with Deion, with um you know, you got Ed, of course, being there for a long time. Landon Jackson played a lot of ball before he went down last year. Um and you know, you got Z-low, got all the all the different guys in there that are hungry to for their opportunity. And it's been fun to to see them work, to see them stick together, like I said, hang out with each other. The personalities been showing in everybody. Nobody's like reserved. Everybody's kind of just being themselves. And um you know, like I said, it's it's been dope to insert myself into that, you know, um be a part of their their careers at such a young age. And uh like I I'm year nine, so I just try to be the the vet presence in the room as as well as I can be. >> I know, you know, Coach Leonard has the call, and the call is the call, but how much freedom do you have within this scheme? Because we hear Joe Brady, it's one of his mantras, be you with us. How much freedom do you have within the calls to do what you do, to be the effective player you've been the last nine seasons? >> Yeah, I feel like we got a lot, you know. Um yeah, it's the call, like I said, but he gives us the the why we're doing it. So, if you have a if you see what you see, we've been playing ball for a while, take what you see, you know. And I feel like that that applies to all all the front five, and then even in the back end. I I feel like in the back end they got to be a little bit more reserved, you know, with the coverages and stuff, but uh up front he just wants us to be aggressive. And um like you said, you got the play call, you got the play sheet, got the lines on it, but we don't always have to follow those lines. It's about playing free. >> Michael Hoyd has made a remarkable recovery. >> You're familiar with that. >> Mhm. >> Um and I know he kind of did his in the middle. >> Where was like you had a long-term injury as well. Just seeing him recover from that, number one, and then number two, that's another guy with a lot between the ears. Ivy Leaguer, the whole thing. Calling the pass rush games and stuff. How beneficial is that to have a player on the field who can give you a change a half a second before the snap and say "Flip it." or you know, whatever the change in call might be cuz he sees something and you guys can trust it and know we're in the best call possible on this down and distance. >> No, for sure. Just Just to speak on the recovery, I love when people, you know, get counted out and have an injury and like, you know, everybody's against them and they just pop up and right back to form. So, to see him back out on the field, he was, you know, kind of teetering in OTAs as an individual with us, but he was still recovering, but to see him out there full speed now is is been dope to see, man. I'm so happy for him because I know what what that process is like. I know what it what it takes to get back to that field. So, to see him out there is dope. But, um to the point of uh you know, him in the pass rush games, um we're just now getting that rapport, you know. Uh he wasn't out there in OTAs and stuff. So, I'm going to see that come a lot alive a lot more during this training camp and I'm excited to see it. I know um in the past watching film, like you said, he's he's quick to change it and he's quick to, you know, give hand signals to the guy next to him and they had success with with that in the past. So, I'm excited to to, you know, get on board with that. >> So, we had the draft day story where you and Josh were in the same conversation. Um give us an idea of what the conversations were like when you were game planning for Josh Allen for this offense and what you found once you got behind that curtain and now you're on his side. >> Yeah, I would say game planning for him is the honestly the worst thing ever, man, cuz >> [laughter] >> the coaches like they just want to I feel like it they just want to cage him in, which if you give him too much time, then he's just going to sit back and dice you up. And then you can't also just rush willy-nilly because if you take the wrong rush line, he's just going to make you pay with his feet. So, game planning is always the worst, man. It's It's one of those things that you just can't can't be right, you know? And And to to be on this side of it now, I can't wait to see him take that cape, you know, take and cape [laughter] on and make some things happen. >> Yeah, exactly. >> Yeah, we have seen over the course of his career where you've seen it kept where you'll have the they have the perfect defense call, they got him, and then all of a sudden it turns into a touchdown. And that that's hard to stand. You got defensive coordinators over there going what we doing here, you know? >> It's a lot more fun watching from the bench this >> There's been some times I haven't had him in my class when he just gets the ball out and touchdown. It's just like, all right, and then he just looks at you. I was telling somebody, he doesn't really talk much junk, but he just like give you a little a little look or a little word that just pisses you off. >> I've had him on this side. >> Yeah, you're on the right side of the ledger this time. Bradley, thanks for joining us. We appreciate you rapping with us here on day one of training camp. That's Bradley Chubb, Bills outside linebacker joining us here on day one of training camp on One Bills Live. We'll take a break and be back with more, including more news from the field when we return.

title: Brandon Beane: “There’s Always An Excitement Around Camp” | Buffalo Bills
text: With all the care, with all the newness that's happening, there's still some carryover. How do you approach How do you view this camp with the new coach, um mostly new pieces in place, and yet with some familiar faces and new challenges? >> Yeah, John, I think um there's always an excitement around camp, right? It's an It's a fresh start. It's a new start. You kind of you had the offseason to kind of do most of your roster building. Doesn't mean we can't do anything at this point, but uh you you you've built your roster up, and now you're getting into pads, and you got your rookie class that you've only seen in t-shirts and shorts. And then this year, you're right, we got a new element of a a new head coach. Um some coaches return, but a lot of new faces, especially, you know, on the defensive side of the ball. Um we've switched to a 3-4. Um and so there's a new system being installed, and there'll be ups and downs. It won't be perfect along the way, but that's that's exciting that, you know, to kind of watch uh this group come come together as a whole, and then what does this new defense look like? Um how does Joe balance the head coach, play caller, um all that stuff? I mean, I think he'll He's got a great plan. He's worked really hard this offseason. I'm excited to see um how he's leading our team. >> What are your expectations out outside and externally are still the same that this team is is is very good. What are your your expectations about this team? >> Yeah, I mean, my expectations are it's it truly is you know, an oxymoron, but it's it truly is one day at a time. Like we're one day we just finished one practice. Um and I mentioned some of the things that I'm excited about, but we've got to do it. You There's no quick you know, build a team, build the camaraderie, um the glue. You know, in the season you're going to have ups and downs, right? It's a long season, and so that's why we like coming here, getting away. I know a lot of teams don't, but um you know, Joe and I talked about that pretty quick after he was, you know, named the head coach of what what will be our plan and and I love coming up here and was glad that that he thought it the same. I just think it's it's hard to build a bond, and so this is exciting for us. And yeah, we're not up here as long, but every you know, there's a good plan of of not going back and forth, just everybody kind of staying here and as if we're you know, I know the Giants are going to Greenbrier or something like it's kind of treating it like that, even though we're a lot closer to home. >> How have you seen him take ownership of the team and establish standards, hold guys accountable? What have you seen over these last several months here? >> Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, it's interesting. You we all, you know, before I was a GM, you think, all right, this is how I'm going to do things, but you when you're the assistant GM or the director of football ops or wherever I was along my way, you have to follow, you know, what the people above you are doing. So, it's been fun to see Joe, while there's similarities of what you saw as a quarterback coach and a and a coordinator, there's also now like, I'm in charge of this whole ship and and and this not just the offense, now the whole team and the defense and um Joe has a great way about him. I think you guys have been around him. He's He's got a natural presence. Um he can be firm. He's a good guy, but he will be firm. I saw him jumping some dudes today. I think he's got a good balance. And um again, there will be ups and downs in camp, there will be ups and downs as we build this team. And obviously, you know, a 17-game season, there will be ups and downs. So, he'll have tests along the way, but I thought he did for a first-year head coach, I thought he had a great plan. I mean, you go back to the interview process and you're listening to these coaching candidates of how they want to how they want to take this team to the next level, which is what we're trying to do. Um talking about it and and then doing it is not always easy. And I thought Joe um was very real in his interview and very authentic and had a plan and it it hasn't just been hollow words. He's been methodically doing that step-by-step in his own unique way. He's not coming in saying things didn't work. I'm going to blow it up and do I want to just do it with a lot of the things that have done well and then I want to put my tweak on it and and make it make it the way I think is how we can go win a championship. >> There's been so much talk about Keion. Going back to the things that have happened the last couple of years at the press conferences, how do you think that he's handled it? What's been your messaging to him? And what kind of a year does this need to be for him? >> I think if you if you know how you know, depending on everyone's relationship uh with Keion. If you if you know Keion through 2 years, right? And this is year three. If you know him the way I know him and the way I think a lot of the guys and his teammates know him, you feel a guy who's really matured. Like the light it is come on. He understands some of the things that he could have done better along the way. You know, I think back to when I was 21, 22, there's things that you know, I God, I probably should have done that a little bit better. And so I like to remind everyone uh was his first 2 years perfect? No. But if you just talk to him and around him, you feel you feel a guy growing into his own, comfortable in his skin, and just like I know that I can't do the same things that I did the first 2 years and expect to have success on the field or in the locker room with my teammates. And his teammates see it. He dropped the first ball today, and I saw like three guys come over there and dap him up like that. Josh comes right back to him the next play, a much harder play, and he makes it. And which was funny, what Joe Brady said to me after warm-ups was like, "This will be a test. So, this is good test. Like, put the ball down." As he says, uh we don't get to predict, you know, we don't get to choose the weather. It's It's our job to go out here. He goes, "I'm going to be curious someone slips and falls, someone drops a ball, someone fumbles a ball, how they do the next play." And I literally thought of that when that happened to Keaontay. He dropped the ball. So, I'm watching him in the huddle. I'm watching him the next play. And Josh went right back to him. So, I'm very proud of where Keaontay is. Um he could have taken the negativity from the the press conference thing, the season, the benchings, whatever has happened to him. He has had the most positive outlook on things. And And I think, not only myself, I think everybody in this in this organization is excited. He's still got to go out there and do it. And And nothing's given, but I think he's done everything that he could control up to this point. >> Brandon, as you look at this defense, it's young. What do you want to see out of their growth over the next month? >> Yeah, I mean, I think some of the things, Maddie, is we've got some guys in in, you know, slightly new positions, whether it's guys that have always had their hand down, now they're standing up a little bit. Um you know, some guys that were maybe playing more outside, sliding into, you know, a different spot or or or or vice versa. So, I think just the first thing is the front and how these guys fit. Uh then you go to, you know, the second level with the backers, um, you know, from that standpoint. And then, you know, the safety's obviously Cole's going into his third year really showed some things this last year. Um, we think we've got some really good depth in the safety room. So, how does that all play out play out, you know, alongside him? And then, some some young DBs, uh, a D offered in here. So, we've got some new faces, um, that John mentioned earlier. We've got, you know, we've got some guys that have been here and a Greg Rousseau, Bradley Chubb's been talked about him in his leadership. He takes T.J. Parker, you know, down to Florida with him this summer. And, you know, I talked to Bradley yesterday about him. Just, he's impressed with T.J.'s commitment. And, you know, for a young guy, feels like the the light's on. And, and so, you know, I commend T.J. for going, "Man, that's a guy I kind of want to follow." So, I'm excited about a lot of things. I'm excited about pads. Just as, you know, we're not there yet with the ramp up, which I think's good. Um, the old days of just throwing pads on right away. You know, we'll ramp them up the next few days and then get into pads next week. But, I'm excited about all that. I'm excited to watch Jim, you know, use the different packages and putting guys in different spots. We talk about positionless players. And, as I said, you know, we've got some safeties that have some good experience in this league. And, what are some different ways he can use them as we build this roster and decide, you know, who the the the best 53 players are. >> Brandy, can I go back to Keanu for a second? Because, while I understand you're saying he's a year free and things he would have maybe done differently and all. But, you know the way this league goes, right? Expectations become it's things don't wait for anybody. Do you need more out of him this year? Or, do you have higher expectations for him this year because you've seen his progress now coming into the the third year of a, you know, rookie deal? >> Yeah, I mean, I think if you just um, if you handle the things the way he's handled them this offseason up to this point and and I don't I'm not really concerned that he won't. Obviously, you know, it's still got to play out, but I think those things will come. If you just prepare, do the right things on the field, off the field, I think the rest will come. I don't think he's he's come up short with his ability. You know, I think he's shown plenty of things going back to his rookie year before the injury we talked about. He didn't come back as well after the injury, but if you watch those games, watch him progressing, he was doing it. The rest of that year didn't go as well. Last season, game one, Josh went to him in some big moments, made some big plays in the in that comeback at the Ravens. Then things kind of fell off. So, I think when he's done things the right way, which he's it's he's doing that and it's he's the light is on. I think that will naturally come. I don't I don't know what my expectations are. I just I'm not concerned that he's not going to do things the immature things that popped up from time to time the first 2 years. So, I think by being as mature as he's shown this offseason, that those things will take care of itself. >> Given the severity of Mike's injury, is he ahead of schedule? I mean, can he be ready for the start of the season? >> Mike's one of those guys you got to hold him back. He would practice every rep today if he could, but these guys are still trying to tell him. So, we're still trying to to be smart with him, but he feels very confident. He's I'm not going to say he you know, you'd have to ask him this, does he feel exactly the way he felt prior to the injury last season, but I know he's been confident. He's been here the whole time. He was here this summer. I'm excited about watching him continue to get better. When you take that much time off of football Like that itself, injured or not, um it takes time to kind of get back on the bike and get going. So, I think he'll he'll be getting his legs, getting his feeling, all that. I think we'll all continue to see him get up, get you know, get better, get into games. We'll try to hopefully keep him healthy and and get some preseason action just to get the rust off there, decide what he needs to be prepared, and you know, hopefully he's good to go for week one. That's uh that's what we believe it'll be, but um time will tell. >> I'm going to go out on a limb and say you expect I think I saw >> You expect Dalton Kincaid, assuming he can stay healthy, that this is going to be the breakout year. Now, I know he had a really good rookie year, but the last two have been injury-marred. Do you expect if he's healthy, he's going to be a starting tight end for you guys? >> I mean, we believe Dalton. I mean, I think you you just said when healthy, he's done he's done really good things all the way back to his rookie year, Sal. Um so, he's he's worked really hard. I think if you uh you know, I when he came back the other day, I was like, "Dude, you you're looking chiseled." Like I made him take his shirt off, and then he asked me to take mine off, and I said, "No." Um but uh in all seriousness, he he went out to California after the season, and I'm sure he took a little time, but he trained. He trained really hard, and he's grown into his body more, and and he knows what it takes. Um you know, the things that have happened to him haven't been from a lack of preparation or lack of effort. He's done everything he could. Um sometimes it's like a you know, this is a car crash type of a game. It's physical. And so, hopefully, you know, we can keep him healthy. If we keep him healthy, I think we'll see the guy that has shown a lot, you know, over his first, you know, few years. >> Brandon, I don't think we saw Tre'Davious White take any team reps today. Anything we read into that? >> Um he was just uh you know, some things you know, as as in his training, just he's he's fine. We're just trying to ramp him up properly and make sure he's he's good to go. So, he'll he will you you guys will see him over the you know, the next week or so gradually go all the way back into you know, to doing that and Dorian will be on a similar a similar thing as well. >> As of Dorian's recovery and Terrell's, that opens the door for Caleb. >> Yep. >> Right? What have you seen from him and how big of an opportunity is this to take hold of? >> Yeah, I think Caleb had a good spring. It's t-shirts and shorts, so we all I have to look in the mirror and say don't, but I thought Caleb did a really nice job. Got some opportunities to you know, be the play caller in the huddle so to speak and and you know, runs out there today with the with the first group and it's a we got to get him in pads and see what that looks like in t-shirts and shorts. I think he's you know, he's doing a nice job you know, for a young guy. Uh don't want to jump to conclusions, but we'll see. But he's he's going to get opportunities. I think there's several guys that you know, that's what we always say. You you know, next man up, be ready. Take advantage of your reps. Don't count them. Just take advantage of everyone you got and and to this point, I think he's done that. >> If you think about That's right. If you think about Ed Oliver's top five games of his career, I think you'd call him a game wrecker if you were looking at the film. Can he do that over the course of an entire season and does the does this defense need him to do that over the course of an entire season? >> Yeah, I mean I think that's one of the things um you know, Ed was one of the first names that Jim Leonard brought up you know, and you know, I think I can you know, I know what this guy does well. I've watched the film. I've studied him. Not that he didn't know him, but I know him even better and I think I can get him more opportunities in some one-on-one matchups. Ed as a one-on-one guy is tough. You know, I think he if you watch the film he faces a decent amount of doubles and which is smart by teams to do that and that's where, you know, you love that Jim already has that in mind early on. I'm talking about back in January, February as this coaching staff was was being assembled. Um and that hasn't changed. And so yes, I think Ed can be a, you know, I mean the year how many sacks did he have the year after we did his deal? It was it was close to 10. So, I think you've seen plenty of Ed that that he can do it and obviously he's still learning this defense, but I'm excited for him, you know, and I'm excited for Jim and how he's planning to use him. >> Hey, how do you feel about the depth at corner outside of the top guys? Benford, Hairston, Igbineghu. >> Yeah, I mean we talked about back to draft day, John. Like um that's had me giving me the most angst, which was why I was you know, aggressive for for Igbineghu to to add him to the mix and um it's a position that you know, whether it's the luck of the draw or whatever, we've we've come up short in the playoffs of having all the healthy bodies we need. You know, and so I've tried to make sure you know, again I went through who we had in camp last year we felt really good about, but uh the injury bug hit us, you know, starting here with with what happened to Max and and it kept going. So, um it's something we'll monitor. I like the guys that we have and then are there in there competing. If you can tell me they'll stay healthy, uh that would be great. Um and you know, I think Will Greenberg and his staff did a real good you know, a really nice job this off season of being intentional with with a lot of different things and including, you know, that area as well. So, um I like the depth, but it can get thin there fast. It's a hard position to play in the league. That's why you see corners get paid a lot of money. And so, we'll we'll monitor it and and there'll be some good battles as to who's going to, you know, be some of those back end guys to help make us make this roster. >> If you have an injury there, is is Tre'Davious White the first call you have to make? >> We love Tre'Davious and um, you know, we we we constantly keep contact with guys like Tre'Davious. You've seen us bring back again, the Poyers, the the Micahs, the Jordan Phillips. I'm I'm missing guys, but um, we love guys that have been here and have been stalwarts for this team and and so, uh yeah, I'm I'm sure, you know, Tre'Davious had probably teams reach out uh and we've stayed in contact with him through the off season and check on him and I'm sure he's probably working out somewhere right now that as we all know Tre'Davious. So, yeah, you you keep a that's our job is to keep a running list of of players at each position and you're naturally going to lean to someone who you know has done it recently for you and has success. >> I know this is the position battle you're most excited to watch this camp, whether it's, you know, starter, lower on the depth chart, is there just something you're really interested in? >> I think I'm most interested in what I was telling Maddie earlier, just in this defense. It's a you know, I feel like I know the offense better. Um now, the left guard battle on offense, uh you know, that's a that's a premium spot that we need to make sure we're we're good there. Our number one thing is to protect protect number 17. Um but beyond that, I'm excited about this defense and how Ed Oliver fits. Sorry, hit something. Uh how Ed fits, how you know, the rest of these these D-linemen, the the Dion Walkers, um the um T.J. Sanders, uh Landon Jackson, you know, obviously Chubb's new here, Rousseau, more stand up than he's to. I'm excited to see how all these pieces are being used, how they fit, what is their best fit. You know, we like versatility. We want these guys to be able to play multiple spots. Is is Deion Walker's best spot at nose? Is it Is it 4i? It You know what I mean? I think several guys Land and Jackson falls in There's There's several guys that um fall into that. So, I'm excited to see those guys and I don't think that's going to be determined in in one or two practices. That's going to carry through the preseason and and will be part of you know, what we're trying to figure out what's the best group, you know, to assemble as part of this 53. >> I'm sure the Jets are not showing everything in the defense really on. So, what is that balance for you as an evaluator of knowing, you know, he's going to keep his cards close to the chest until it gets closer to the actual season and trying to determine how guys look? >> Yeah, I think, you know, you do your best. You know, Joe will have some you know, some physical practices as we go and you and you ones versus ones. So, you're trying to emulate the best you can. You know, we have a scrimmage against Cleveland lined up. So, we'll try and do some things there, you know, in that practice and and then you kind of get to that third preseason game and that's one of the big things you talk about is who are the guys we still need to see and are they in certain positions we need to see them? Um and that's kind of the conversation. So, if we feel like, "Hey, we don't have it all answered going into that third game." You may see some guys still playing that you're like, "Man, I'm surprised that guy's playing in the third game." That means we're still trying to figure out uh what their best role and best fit is for this team and this defense. >> You mentioned the competition at left guard. Corbett played three different spots for Carolina last year. What did you and your staff see from him that gave you confidence that if he were to be the one who who won this job in camp that there would be a seamless transition? >> Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, you do research on these guys, Lance, and you try and find out and and all the way back to his college days, like he's a pro's pro. Um good teammate, good leader, smart. To be able to play that many spots, you know the intelligence is there. It's It's not easy. And then he's got the physical tools uh to do that as well. You're always looking for guys that can can play center um that you only get to you know suit up eight guys. So, as many guys that can snap the ball is helpful or play multiple spots, especially if you're not a starter. So, all that was very attractive. Starting, you know, if he wins the job, it's not going to be big for him. He's had a lot of starts in this league. And, you know, right now he's battling a young guy in Alec who's trying to who's been that extra O-lineman for us and has spot started, even went out to tackle for us in the Pittsburgh game. So, um it's kind of fun. You got a young guy versus a veteran who's done it. And, you know, I think Austin's going to come in here like everyone with a mindset, I'm going to win the starting job. But, if he doesn't, he's he's going to be a good teammate and he'll be ready when his number's called. >> Frank, Frank, uh uh quick center Frank Frank, uh the draft pick played center on the national championship team at Georgia, the Bulldogs. I'm just wondering, was was he under consideration for the uh opportunity to uh start at center? Or cuz he's still on his rookie contract? >> Yeah, I mean, uh you know, unfortunately with Said last year, he had the the calf injury, which was a big setback for him. He did it the week leading up to training camp a year ago, and he missed the whole preseason uh to the point we were still having to ramp him up as the season got started. And then, you know, fortunately for us, Connor stayed healthy through the year, so he didn't have the opportunities to play. Played in the last game, thought he did a nice job, but um you would have loved to you know, for him to not have had that setback. Nothing he could do. He was doing it training for football. It happens. Um but, you know, he was a He did a great job for Georgia. He's smart. He's he's a leader and all those things and and so this is a big year for him year three to come in here and show in camp show in these preseason games what he can do. And I think there's some good competition there, you know, between him and and we brought in Lloyd Cushenberry. And obviously we want Connor to stay healthy, but but things happen. So Settle have a you know, great opportunity this preseason. >> CJ Gardner-Johnson is a very interesting guy and he's been polarizing. He's been in some places success places teams have moved on from him. When you have a guy like that and you think about bringing him in, what is the research intel process like for you as opposed to maybe just a guy that you know, might just be a street free agent who's out there sometimes. And how did you arrive at that decision to bring him in? >> Yeah, I mean Settle we you know, all the way back to when we're doing our free agent meetings and our pro scouts are going through the guys who are you know, haven't signed extensions. These are the guys and so when when you get to safety, you're talking about each guy and then we kind of present to the coaches like, hey, take a look at this guy. Think he kind of you know, can do this and this. These are his strengths. These are his weaknesses. Talk they watch and then we kind of compare notes and then you you know, when you get to free agency, you have discussions of uh this guy's going to be out of your price range. This guy's not. This guy's going to add, you know, an athletic skill set. This guy's going to you know, he's going to be more of a box safety and and so I think when you get to Chauncey, he was a guy that um you know, some of you know, he's had success. He he's bounced around but not because of the lack of talent. He's he's made big plays impact plays. He can find the ball. He's a ball hawk. He will you know, he will strike you uh to say it politically correct, but he he he will knock it you know, knock your head off. And that's you know, he brings a great skillset to you know, to the position. Yes, you're asking around to people you know that have been on teams and and I would say a lot of things were very positive. He's super competitive and sometimes his competitiveness maybe maybe he went a little far or whatever, but I thought it you know, his off season he came in here and we talked about those things before we signed him to make sure we felt it that's why we it wasn't one of those you agree and sign before you brought him in. Like we brought him in, we spent a whole day with him and I thought he was open and honest about things that he thought he could have done better. And then maybe he thought things were he didn't mean things were interpreted differently maybe in some in some situations than what he was trying to do, but I think he understands this point of his career like he's he's not at the end. He can still play, but he's got to make sure he keeps it within the lines and and so we talked about all those things and if he can do that you love that edge. I mean when you walk into a guy like him I've had guys on different teams. You walk into a hostile environment. I mean week one we're going to be going to Houston. That's going to be a hostile environment loud place. Like you want an edge. You want to hey it's us against the world that that mentality and he has that mentality. He he has no fear. You know, he's a guy that you want you know, in a street fight so to speak you know, and so those are the things that are attractive, but yes, like all players he has to keep it with you know, we want him to be you with us is one of Joe's slogans like we want him to be himself, but just make sure it stays you know, within the boundaries. >> Brandon, one of the issues for Josh Palmer last year was availability. How would you grade his health going into camp and were there discussions about the ways things the club could do to support him to be more available than he was last season. >> Great question. Yeah, I mean, Josh, I thought he had a good start to the year. Um we go to Atlanta, and he it I think it was a hip-drop tackle that that got him that turned him out of the game. And so, it got him in three areas. And unfortunately, you know, we shut him down at the end of the year. I give him credit. He fought through it. It was tough. That's tough mentally on you because I think with Josh, you know, when you sign a contract, that was his first big deal coming off of his rookie contract, you want to live up to it. These guys, they're they're prideful guys. You You got Man, they they I mean, just like when I took the GM job, I'm like, "Man, that's That's lofty expectations. I don't want to let anyone down. I don't want to let my teammates down, my staff down." And so, Josh, his first thing he doesn't want to let his teammates He wants to let them know, "Man, I I came here. I want to be a part of this." And so, um this offseason, he was still working back from the ankle. It was still giving him some problems. That's the probably the thing that lingered the most through the season um that we ultimately shut him down for. Um but I think he's healthy. Talked to him yesterday, he's in a good spirit. And he's excited about his opportunities. And hopefully, you know, hopefully something like that doesn't happen. I think if it if it doesn't and he can stay healthy, the ball will find him. And you know, as the you know, the the ball kind of bounces around. Sometimes it's going to the tight end, sometimes it's going to the receivers. If if he stays healthy, I think he'll you know, he'll be able to help us. >> Uh obviously, Terrell's on PUP, but how's his recovery going? >> Yeah, I think he's He's doing really well. this guy's been in the building like if all offseason, you can set your watch to about 6:00 to 6:05, he's pouring a salt bath in one of those aluminum tubs, you know, just he's just a one of those guys. He is like steady, kind of how he, you know, even when he made the practice squad, there were a couple of times he was frustrated he didn't make our roster, didn't change his approach. It's frustrating to have an injury that's a 9-month to a, you know, to a year, whatever they take sometimes, but you wouldn't see it on his face. He's just like, "I'm going to work. I'm going to work. I'm going to work. I'm going to control what I can control." And so, his teammates see his work his work ethic and know, you know, they're going to be excited when he gets back, but I think he's done a really good job. I wouldn't want to put a timetable on it yet. You know, I wouldn't project him to be able to start the season. I think it'll be one of those things he'll start the season on pup, and then we'll just keep ramping him up, and when he's ready to go, we'll we'll see if we can get him out there.

title: Josh Allen: “We’re Excited To Be Back” | Buffalo Bills
text: Do the squeaks get louder? >> Say it again. >> Do the squeaks of the fans get louder? >> Yeah, I think so. I mean, people are excited we're back. We're excited to be back. That we had a a good productive first day. Um actually there's always things you want to clean up, but uh loved how the guys were flying around today. >> What does a productive first day look like for you when it's a new off- not a new offense, but you know, Joe's first day? >> Yeah, I think it's just guys buying in and and being convicted about what we're doing. Um the trajectory of what this team needs to be, how hard we need to practice. Um you know, nothing that we did last year carries over to this year and you know, uh it's going to take everybody and everybody's going to have to buy in. >> How excited are you to see Dalton Kincaid looking healthy? >> Love it. Yeah, he's uh he's a special player. He really is. I know we've been we've been saying that. Um you know, he's he's been fantastic for us last last couple years. Um I feel like he gets better each and every year. Um and just another year with him learning learning his body language. Um Um he's flying around. It's it's awesome to see. >> Whitner, when he's not out there, is there a noticeable difference to you in how the functionality of the offense operates? >> Um I mean, I know there are some pretty uh good statistics that backed up when he was on the field and the success that we had as an offense. So, yeah, we we want him out there. Um you know, he wants to be out there and he like I said, he looks really good right now. >> How do you get expectations to match the trajectory or vice versa? >> Expectations from who? >> Your I'm Yeah, the external, internal. Um this team is coming into the season once again being pegged as a a a a con- a Super Bowl contender. So, how do you get that, even though with a new coach with all the changes that have happened, you get that to match the you know, trajectory and expectations? >> Again, we're we're not really focused on on trying to match those from the outside world. Um internally, we have our own expectations. We talk inside that locker room of of the team that we want to be. But, you have to go out there and earn it in each and every single day, and that's what we plan on doing when when we're here at camp and throughout the preseason. >> You got plenty of reps with DJ Moore during the spring. Curious the process of picking building off that foundation and continue to work together over these next several weeks. >> Yeah, again, still learning him. Um, just trying to get on the same page, and I feel my myself trying to be like perfect when I'm throwing him in some of the routes on air. And today I walked up to him and I'm just like, "Hey, I'm just going to throw it. Like, I'm going to pick a spot and and let it go, and I'm not trying to aim it anymore." Like, and I felt like once I said that, like things kind of clicked for us, and again, just each day that goes by, we're going to try to continue to get more comfortable with each other. >> Is that unusual to have with a receiver where you're like, I'm trying to be perfect and I don't want to say in your head, but like a little more having to step back and do that? Is that normal? >> Yeah, I think it is. When you when you bring in a guy like him, um, a guy that it's obviously been really good for a long time, and you want to go out there and like, you want to play well for him. You want to show him like, "Hey, like, this is why you're here to be this guy." And um, but at the same time, it's just like, just go out there and play football, you know, on on both ends. And and you find a way to get open, and I'm going to give it a chance where you can catch the ball, and um, make a play for us. >> Josh, I know this is the time to test out new things, but how will going up against a new defense help your game and the offense at all? >> Um, I mean, I think this is a a type of defense that we're going to see throughout the year a lot. Um, so to have those repetitions in terms of the coverages, the fronts, um, the different pressures that we're going to see from from our team is going to help us, uh, come season time. Um, you know, I'm all for making it as exotic and complicated right now, and and allow things to be really fast firing early on, um, because things will eventually slow down once you see see it all. So, um, very happy with our defense is doing. They they make it really hard for an opposing quarterback and I'm just happy that I get to get to go against it. >> Hey Josh, off of that question, did it ever get stale in the eight years of going against Sean's defense every camp, every practice? I mean, did it Was there a point where you were like, "Yeah, I've seen this 9 million times." >> I don't know about stale, but there was a a point where it's like, "Yeah, I've I've seen it enough." Um, where I know the calls that you're making, which as a quarterback, if you know the calls, it makes it fairly It makes it easier. I'm not going to say it makes it easy, but it makes it easier. Um, which I'm still trying to listen for some of the calls that we have, but no idea what's going on yet. Um, which is good. Yeah, I mean, it's you're going out there, you're reacting. Um, you're trying to you know, dissect the defense before you snap the ball and post snap, you're trying to make really quick, informed decisions and um, it makes it, like I said, we want those bullets being fired early and and often and allow things to be hard right now because uh, eventually they will slow down. >> How different is camp, going to camp as a dad, as a 30-year-old and with a new coach? >> A lot of firsts, no doubt. Um, it's exciting. Um, obviously I miss my family. Uh, but, you know, to be here with the guys, like it's not like we're we're going to work and and we do have a set of goals in mind that we want to accomplish and in order to do that, um, there are sacrifices that you have to make and everybody in this locker room is making sacrifices right now and um, you know, I'm just trying to give everything that I got for this team. >> Does it feel different going into a training camp with a different head coach? Like are there things you've noticed that are different or you already know Joe so well that there's anything like that? >> Yeah, I mean, I I know Joe extremely well, but in terms of scheduling, um, like we talked about this earlier in OTAs, just the vibe, the the energy, um, you know, it's different. It's not I'm not saying it's better, it's worse, it it's different and you know, as a new head coach for a team, I I think that's a smart decision to things different. You know, this isn't the same place and you have to make it feel differently because you know, doing the same thing it obviously didn't work. So, got to got to change it up and try to find new ways to to make it work. >> When we talked to Joe before practice, he was saying his emphasis to him was just to be himself. How did he do that? >> He's just again, being himself is is being out there talking talking crap to the the quarterbacks. Um didn't see him celebrate for the defense as much. He wants the offense to look good right now, but once the the offense is going to go in a good spot, he's going to probably turn his attention to the defense and and cheer when they, you know, bat balls down and uh have interceptions, but hopefully, you know, those don't happen too often in camp. >> You said so many times that you trust Keaontay, you know, out of the field. He has the first play I think in 11 on 11 or whatever you said on Saturday where he had a drop and right back to him on the next play. Is that kind of showing him and has he earned that trust? >> Absolutely. You know, he's put in the work this off season. Um he continues to get better. He continues continues to, you know, master the offense and the role that we're asking him to do. and he's just again, he's working extremely hard and um I think people see that. I respect that about him. He's never once put his head down and pouted and and woe is me and it's it's always, "Hey, I'm I'm going to figure this thing out." And when you have a guy that's willing to put in the extra work that you you you start pulling for that guy, but again, I understand his body language now. I know where he's going to be. Um you know, back shoulder balls are some guys aren't easy to throw to, but he's got such a big frame where where those are something that he's got to be very very excellent at. And but it takes reps to do that and I'm glad we got that >> Josh, that that left guard spot, I know David Edwards played a pretty significant role in communications and things like that. What's on the plate of those guys battling for that job? >> Um I'm going to think just owning up to uh the responsibility of what that position entails. Um you know, we ask a lot of our guards uh you know, in run schemes and in pass schemes and um yeah, it's just whoever goes out there and competes the hardest and and obviously plays the best is going to get the the spot, but um feel very confident with you know, who we got out there right now. >> Josh, you worked with Joe Brady as a quarterback coach and offensive coordinator and I know it's early as a head coach, but how is he persona-wise, presence-wise? How is he different as a head coach than maybe in those other roles? >> Um I I just think he relates so well to to each and every guy in the locker room. Um he loves football. He loves learning defense. He loves learning new offense. Um you know, he's adaptable. He he communicates well. and I think again that that is him. He He's a fast talker, especially when he gets some caffeine in him early in the morning in our team meetings. I'm sure he's talked about that with you guys. Uh but he just loves football. He works extremely hard. He's always in the uh the facility and um you know, he he took a little break obviously as we all did this last and took took like a week or two to himself and his family, which was good to see cuz get done with the season, he did the whole interview process. He like he he's been doing it nonstop, so um to to get a little reset was obviously good for everybody including him. Um but now that he's back and ready to to roll, I called him a couple weeks ago and he's already back in the building, so he just works extremely hard. >> How was the Josh, how was the continuity coming since somebody that you already know is now coming in as the head coach? How does that help you and your teammates? >> Yeah, I mean in terms of being the quarterback, it helps with the verbage in the offensive scheme that we've kind of had in. Um you know, we we are changing a few things. We are going to have different wrinkles and and and make this offense our own as you do each year. Um but again, it's just coming out working hard, working for the guy next to you in the locker room and um just trying to put our best best stuff on the football field. >> Joe said several times before you said we've never been here. Like trying to not make it like another year at St. John Fisher in this. Just tell us just about how the players receive that message of there sort of being a break between then and now. >> Yeah, I mean I I do think there is a lot of turnover in this team. There are a lot of new new faces. Um so this is, you know, year one for them. This is year one you know, in the Joe Brady era and you know, what he's doing again it's going to take the conviction to buy in in order to achieve what we want to achieve and it's going to take everybody in this locker room to do it. >> Josh, speaking of buying, how do you see this team buying into that coach and the new vision and new energy? >> Yeah, I think it's the way we went out there and practiced today. It's guys flying around. It's putting the ball down. Um We're going to get weather in Buffalo. We understand that. I know we're in Rochester right now, but you know, guys didn't blink. took visors off, took the gloves off and and just put the ball down and played football. So that's that's what we're looking to do. >> Josh, not ninth year for you. Does camp help sort of a reset? You know, cuz you've done a lot of these things even with the changes over and over again. Does being in a different spot like this like a bit of a reset for you to focus on things you really want to focus on with this year? >> Absolutely. title: Exclusive Interview with Todd Monken
text: joined here in studio by the head coach of your Cleveland Browns, Todd Monken. Coach, good to see you, man. We got a good group of guys that like to practice. It seemed like, you know, other than Malik, you had everybody ready to go at least at the beginning of practice today. >> No, that's you know, we're we're we're not really banged up. Malik's the only one on PUP, so we've got everybody. That was nice. Everybody passed the conditioning test, which was great, and which I expected. >> Yep. >> And um No, it was good today. And and that's why you that's why you go 90 minutes the first day, you know, you you don't need to do it the first day. Offensive installs really quick game in third and medium, so you don't have a ton of routes that are down the field. text: Welcome back to Cleveland Browns Daily, brought to you by Bally Bet, and there's no sure bet than Browns five-time Pro Bowl cornerback Denzel Ward. Yeah, you're quite young. >> Yeah, yeah. No, it's it's it's good, man. It's exciting. You like I said, I've been with the team for a long time, and just trying to be that leader for the team, and you know, that playmaker out there that they need. You've got the consistency of B Lynch, which is great. We love B Lynch. That's what camp's about, just getting better and getting ready for the season. And like I said, we got a lot of talent on the offensive side at the receiver position, so just to be able to go out there and go against all the different body types and and players is going to be exciting. >> What's it mean to kind of have for the first time, and it's been a long time, think about Greenbrier, think about last year Carolina and Philly. It's been a long time since we've actually had a training camp here. To be able to be back in front of these fans that I know you love, in your hometown, home area, all of that. Are you excited for that kind of just All right, we really don't have to go anywhere this year. >> I love that. Just be at home, you know, get the dog pound out here, get everybody out here, and practice on our field. So, it's good not to go anywhere and just stay close. >> I know that the veterans probably do not like the fact that this is going to be a little bit more of an intense camp, you know, than it's been in years past with Todd Monken. What have you kind of gleaned from him in terms of his leadership style, his directness, and then the fact that we're going to get this team ready to play football. >> yeah. I think that's the biggest thing. He he's showing like we're going to get this team ready to play one way or another. We all here working, long practices, long everything, you know. So, just coming out here, competing, and like his I like his directness, like you said, and just how he has a team rallying together and going out there and playing. >> I just like seeing you smile from here [laughter] to here, man. Thanks for being here today. >> Thank you, man.

text: Really wasn't much different than when I got here 5 months ago. I can't remember. What did I say? Um yeah. The players decide who plays. >> Do you mean first game of the season or first game of preseason? >> First game of the season. All right, we especially at quarterback. >> On the way back to uh the owners' meetings uh the practice, you noted that you would not be able to do equal reps, obviously, for these guys. He had a big smile on his face uh yesterday. It's been something that I know Andrew's been working on and uh I know we're we're fired up. >> When you were the offensive coordinator with the Ravens planning to play the Browns, how did you uh scheme with Denzel Ward in mind? first of all, it became a little more difficult when they added when they when we added Tyson.
