That's and his ability to break on the ball so you can't be late with your throws. I think you got to be careful that down the field cuz he's going to track it and he's going to compete. Those were the things that, you know, um that that we were I wouldn't I would say afraid of, but obviously had to be, you know, wary of cuz of his speed to be able to track the ball. >> What's the thought process of only one joint practice day with the Cardinals? >> Well, I think it's gotten to that with all teams. I think most teams now end up with one practice. End up going a day early or they come a day early and I would guess that probably it's cuz I don't know what percentage of but I always felt like the second day is when all the fights started. You know, guys get pissy the day before and then the night meetings and you start huffing and puffing and you go back the next day and it's like you've seen the movie Slap Shot when the Hanson brothers drop the gloves. It's like, "Shit, the national anthem started and you're already fighting." It's like you're already telling them be careful. I mean, so I think it's gotten to that a little bit to where you just go one practice. Um we would have liked to have practiced with the Bears. It just didn't work out with them. We we we we would have liked to have gone. We're going to go a day early and have dinner up there, but it didn't work out. >> So, you didn't get to see a lot of it for I don't know if you saw any of Harold Landry during the off-season program, but that's all I'm running around last week. So, how's he look for you and you feel like he's going to be a focal point of what you're trying to >> Oh, yeah. Looked really good last week. And he's still a young player, still a developing player. But, what a great mindset, wants to be better, works awfully hard. You guys have seen him. One thing I didn't know that I saw last year is his yards after contact. Like, I didn't see that in Bowling Green. Maybe I didn't study it uh hard enough. I don't I don't know. I didn't see that. And then, man, is he hard to tackle. As he develops his route running skills, uh I wouldn't say he's a match-up guy yet. That's not I think he's going to continue to develop as a blocker, but I think you get him the ball and I think he's a hard guy to bring down. I think he's a powerful, powerful man and only going to get better. >> Good. One down. >> That's it. All right.

How much does that mean to you to not only be one of the more better leaders on the team, but to to continue playing in your hometown? >> Yeah, it's exciting. Everybody trying to say I'm old, though. I'm not I don't feel I'm old. I still feel good, but no, it's exciting just to still play for my hometown team. Uh, like I said, being an Ohio kid and just working towards my goals. So, you know, I got the contract, but you know, I just enjoy playing football and I'm glad to continue to do that. >> So, now that this is done, when you look back to the off-season, it did seem, you know, a little odd that you weren't here for the OTA and stuff like that and I know you explained And then you didn't really participate in In retrospect, were those things a little bit related to the fact that you were trying to get this contract >> Yeah, it was it was related. It was related to answer your question. >> Hey, ESPN did an annual survey among coaches, executives rating every position. You came up seventh >> Yeah. >> Six pretty good ones ahead of you, though. Do you think that is fair of ranking for >> I feel like I always get get kind of put down in the rankings lower than I than I should be. I'm not sure why it is, but you know, it's a lot of talented guys, but I I do feel like I'm the number one guy in the league. I feel my numbers speak for itself, my play when you turn on the tape, but like I said, there's a lot of great players, a lot a lot of number one corners out there in the league and I just happen to be one of them just like other guys for other teams. >> So, I mean, there's just been so many changes obviously for the defense over the last six or however many months. Like, what gives you confidence that you as like a leader can help kind of keep that standard what it's been for like one of the top units in the >> Yeah, I think starts with myself. I got to uphold the standard that I've been playing at it for a team to play on a high level and bringing people along with me as as well as that goal and as I'm playing well, that's going to bring everybody else up as well. >> Do you think this new coordinator will play as much press man as Schwartz did? >> Uh, potentially. I do I really love the plays that he does have in, so I'm looking forward to getting out here and practicing them and going through them all, but we just got to wait and see what how how it's going to go during the game. >> I know you already were when you signed the last contract, but how's it feel to be the highest paid guy at your position? >> Yeah, it feels great. That that was always my goal to be the highest paid again and to make that happen. And I'm glad we got it done, but like I said, my most important thing I just enjoy playing the game of football. So, I'm grateful for the the money, the extra the raise they gave me in in money, but now it's time to play football and do what I love. >> You worked a lot last year good time of year on securing the ball. >> Between thirds you're always catching the ball first down. >> And I don't know how many interceptions you had. >> So, what's the state of your interception game do you think? >> When you say the state of it what do you mean? >> Can you get more? >> I feel like yeah, I feel like I could definitely get more. Like I said, I I always invite more targets. I you know, I want more targets get more action on the ball, but yeah, I could definitely get more and I need to get more and that's going to be the goal again going in this year to get more interceptions. >> You talked about your role as a leader on the team when there's so many young guys brought in the last couple years. It kind of feels like there's a transition happening in terms of like culture and you got taught here now. What role can you sort of play in trying to help build a new culture here? Yeah, I think just continue to be myself, you know, lead how I lead. I feel I've become more vocal, but just continue to play well and playing at a high level and like I said before bringing people along with me and you know, just continue to be myself and I feel that's going to help bring everybody up. >> How do you feel you and Tyson Campbell seem to be a lot of uncertainty as how the backups unfold and nickel back? >> What's your opinion of having seen through the spring season of the depth >> Yeah, no, we we going to be good. Of course, you going to you going to think that that lose some guys and you know, the depth is not as well, but guys been playing well and I think we going to be we going to be good. >> Is it almost a kind of badge of honor that you don't get a lot of interceptions because they are thrown to the other side? >> Yeah, but I I want some action though. So, I do love love when they throw the ball at me. You know, I don't to throw the ball at me in this camp. You know, I don't want guys to go away from me just to soccer practice as well and and get reps on task. But yeah, it is it is a badge of honor, you know, it's respect and I'm grateful for that respect. But I do love being in the action though and making plays. Mhm. Yeah, I think it shows that we're still competing to win, you know, it's not I don't think I see a lot of people talking about we're trying to rebuild and and and tank or something like that. But I think it just shows that we trying to rebuild bringing in a great player like Jadeveon Clowney, you know, he's still a talented player. Myles Garrett is obviously Myles Garrett, he's going to be who he is, but you know, we still a talented team and got talented players. We just got to go show that and play together. No one player wins the game, you know, it's a team team sport and we all play together all 11, we going to be good. I just pretty much focus on where I'm at like I'm here, cool. You know, if it came to the point to where I needed to be traded then I think I'll I'll focus more on it then, but that didn't come about yet and I I can still get traded, you know, that's the NFL, things happen. And but I just deal with it as stuff come, you know, you can't can't worry about the what ifs all the time, you got to be in the moment. Great, I think he's been great so far just the way he's been rallying the team. I think it's going to be a tough camp. I do feel it's going to be a tough camp. Uh but uh I'm excited for it. >> Good? >> Mhm? >> What about Mike coming in and >> replacing Jamie? >> Yeah, no I'm I'm excited to have him. Uh like I said, I feel he got a lot of good plays and plays that I'm going to enjoy and can make a lot of plays in. So, I'm practicing them and uh going through it with the rest of the team and uh going from there. >> What about the young guys they brought in >> like Austin you're looking forward to going against those guys >> uh in practice? >> Yeah, for sure. Those guys are going to They're going to make me work. I'm going to make them work, too, though. But, I'm looking forward to going against them. Uh you know, they got a lot of talent, a lot of different body types. So, uh just being able to get different work from all those players is going to be fun. >> I know you addressed this a little bit, but what kind of changed for you or what made you still really want to be here even though Miles is gone? Cuz there was a point where >> you know, that was going to kind of rattle you a little bit. >> Mhm. Yeah. >> And then this year >> it was kind of a surprise. So, what what kind of changed in your mind about that? >> Um mhm. I think really just thinking about like I'm I'm from Cleveland, you know, this is this is the city I'm from. I've always played in Ohio. I'm a Ohio kid. And uh I'm just It's just grateful to be able to come and play uh for my hometown team. You know, not many people get to do that. So, just to be able to to get back to this city um I feel that deserves it deserves win deserves a lot more. Uh I just want to be a part of that uh once we once we get the get this thing going. >> For you, what's >> The last one. >> knowing that you're the longest-tenured Browns player on this roster. >> Mhm. Say Say one more time for me. >> What's it for you? What's it like knowing that you're the longest-tenured Browns Browns player on this roster? Yeah, like I said, everybody keep thinking I'm old, you know, but uh I'm still young and still and still and still ready to play. But, uh now like I said, I just um knowing what's coming, you know, knowing what to expect out here and what to do and stuff. So, just trying to be a leader uh for the team and uh just be myself. >> Appreciate it. >> Thank you, guys. Appreciate it.

title: Cowboys Players Talk First Training Camp Practice | Player Interviews
text: How do you feel? Just talk about your health and what you are. >> Feeling good. Feeling good right away right now. >> How does it feel to feel good? I mean, you've been >> I'm feeling really good. I mean, >> Obviously, being out there with the team is it's just excitement of being out there healthy and ready to go. >> I mean, yeah. It's just I'm just ready to go, you know. Uh it's been a long time coming for me. It feel like I've been Well, last time I played in since December. Been on the field, so feel good to be out here. >> Is there anything you can't do? Is there any strenuous things that anything like that? Are you all >> Oh, no. We feel good. Full go. Just limited reps, but full go. >> What do you think going against, you know, George and CD and these guys I can do for your game and the rest of the corners out there? >> Oh, you know, we're one of the best in the league, so it prepares you for each and every week cuz you know we're going to see guys like that every week. So, I see them every day in practice, man. It's going to be good. >> How do you feel with this cornerback group? Obviously, you know, a lot of change, new defensive coordinator. Just how are things starting to feel this starting camp? >> Uh it definitely like competition, you know. Feel like a lot of guys come coming here and make plays, so feel good coming here every day and know who who's going to be who's going to be who today. >> Jourdan, speaking of competition, just talk about the jump that you might see Jourdan Lewis making. Obviously, he didn't have an off season last year because he was recovering, but he's fully healthy. What are you seeing from him that's going to help him kind of fire out of the gate this year as opposed to recovering last year? >> I mean, he feel more prepared and now now he has that experience, so he knows what what he's going to get into, so each day I see him every day taking out little steps and steps and just getting better. >> Does it feel weird being the, you know, the older guy in this cornerback room? >> I mean, yeah. It definitely came It definitely came quick. You know, I'm only in year five, but it feels good, you know, to be one of the the guys Some of the guys come to cuz of just all my experience. >> What's the biggest piece of advice you have for the younger guys? >> Uh just be ready for anything, you know. You never know what's going to come up. >> What is healthy? Are you feeling like you can be back to pick six Bland, you know, all-pro Bland? I you know, that I'm sure that's the goal, but how do you feel about being getting back to that level? >> I feeling pretty uh pretty good. Uh real good actually. Uh probably I feel right now I feel way better than I was the first time I had the surgery, so feels real good right now to be back. >> Is you are you susceptible to get it done again? Or what what's the mindset on on that injury? Cuz it was same injury two years ago and you had it again. Is it you confident it won't happen again? I guess where you are with that. >> Oh yeah, now I'm confident right now. I mean as soon as this whole rehab I had no hiccups like last time, so it feels way stronger. >> Daron, how how frustrating was that experience though have you know having the same injury again? Having to go through all that. I can imagine it'd be frustrating. >> I mean yeah, it's very frustrating cuz also it was my first ever injury and be able to miss games like that. Um it was real frustrating trying to get back on the field and and you know I'm always one guy I always try to push himself to be better and so it's hard to stay take that step back sometimes. >> Yeah, what did you learn I guess from the first time going through it to the second time and how do you think that's maybe helped you now? >> Uh listen to my body. >> [laughter] >> Every year for each position group I'm sure that room changes just because you have different players coming in and different leaders stepping up. position of the group this year. And how how do you describe the the temperament of the the room this year and how it might be different from previous years? >> Um it's just energy, you know. Uh I uh I try to get everybody on the same page, get everybody ready and keep that mindset of being confident in everybody. So it's been feeling really good right now about about the whole room. >> What are the added benefits that you get when your defensive coordinator is a guy that his depth of experience comes from your position in the secondary? >> Oh, it's it's great, you know. Uh you get somebody that has the same mindset as you and knows what what's going to happen in the games and what you should do and shouldn't do. So it just helps you keep keep you on uh your toes. >> Daron, your coach is really elite >> Yes, definitely. >> What have you been able to like learn from him just so far? >> Um just the temperament, you know. Uh having the mindset of being a corner. Uh not not worried about what's going to happen out there. >> Daron, very basic question but after the last few years, how motivating is this off season this season coming up for you? >> Oh, real Trying to get back to my my real self and uh just be be ready. Just feel comfortable. >> Is there anything you've done to maybe, I don't know, manifest that or is it just it's very just hey, I just got to go out and do what I got to do? >> Hey, that's really just go out there and do what I got to do and just take it day by day. Thank you, man. >> No problem. >> So you can So you can Before I let you go, you can really relate to Coach Parker. Is that what you're saying? Your position and everything. >> Yeah. Oh, yeah. You know, defensive guy, corner guy, so uh it's great to have a a coach that that like that and like Al like I had when I had Al it was it was great to have somebody that knows the position. >> Mhm. You've obviously played against Dak and CD and these these guys. What's it like practicing against them? >> It's fun, man. It's fun. Everything about our practices and everything is about competition. So, uh you know, that's what I'm that's what I'm bred on is uh competition. So, it's been fun, bro. It's been fun. >> What are your early impressions of the defense? You're obviously here cuz they had defensive issues last year. >> Uh defense is flying around right now. Obviously, it's first day. We we had a couple mistakes, but flying around. Um CP getting us right in there. So, pretty good. >> A lot of rehab work for you in the spring. How do you feel physically? >> Feel amazing, bro. Just telling coach uh earlier today I'm blessed to be out here. It's a great opportunity and I'm ready to go. >> Kelvin Downs was lining up a lot of different places. Obviously, you guys want to be very versatile. But in terms of just his ability to kind of already be at a versatile standpoint, >> how impressive is that? >> Oh, it's real impressive. It's real impressive. Um when he can do multiple things like that, it makes our job a lot easier on the back end. Um so, having a guy like that that can just move around and be versatile is is always good for our defense. >> You guys had great communication during mini camp. That was one of the things that stood out. How has that transcended to the first day here and and where do you guys think you are in terms >> One more time? >> How has your communication kind of transcended from where you were in mini camp from a team perspective? >> Um I think it's just more of a confidence thing now. Guys are just louder with the with the communication. Guys are just echoing it a lot more. So, yeah. It's a great first day. Um we expect to build on it. >> Jaylon, this is the 20th year the Cowboys are here in California. So, it's kind of old hat to us, but for someone who's experiencing the first time, the layout, the fans, just how it's all put together, and the format, what are your thoughts? >> It's amazing. It's a little surreal, you know what I mean? Everybody out here, so much media, but um it's a blessing, you know what I mean? Uh and I'm I'm glad to be a part of it. >> When you were in high school in LA, where were you when the Cowboys were up the road in >> Yeah, uh I was in Downey. I went to Downey High School, so um never really heard too much about Oxnard, never really went to a camp, but uh yeah, it's a it's a blessing, like I said, to be here. >> Dak Prescott showed up with that Super Bowl T-shirt on. What does that say about the confidence he has, and what do you think the message is to the team? >> That's the standard right now, Super Bowl. We've been talking about it all off-season. Guys have been getting together in the off-season, working out together, and that's been the message, is Super Bowl, Super Bowl, Super Bowl. >> And what does that mean to see your quarterback wearing that? >> Uh it's big, it's big time, you know what I mean? When a leader when our leader is wearing that, um and and and showing that message to the team, uh guys follow. So, it's big time. >> What do you remember from a scouting perspective going up against the Cowboys last year, and and then having a chance to play George Pickens and pretty much those guys right there. That was the big the big thing that I remember is uh George Pickens, CeeDee Lamb, uh Dak, you know, those are the uh the guys that's making the plays and doing all the doing all the right things. So, when I come to this team and my thing is just to follow those guys, lead and uh follow their example. >> It's one thing to see it from the outside, and then to see it in the same locker room and same team. What What's the most you've learned about this offense maybe compared to what you thought going up against them? >> Uh I mean they just got guys everywhere, man. Guys everywhere. Uh obviously you got Ferg at the tight end, um great running back and Javonte. Um you know, the whole offense is pretty much set. Uh now it's just time for the defense to to get on board and uh communicate, do what we got to do in order to get that Super Bowl. >> Shanahan wants to battle against that fatigue factor, so he's increasing and ramping up the conditioning aspect. >> like that? >> Heck yeah. Heck yeah. Anything to uh help us get better in any type of way, I'm game with it. >> I've seen the contracts for safeties continue to increase. Grant Delpit got a deal. >> Yeah. >> Derwin James and How have you seen in your time playing the position >> that value change around the league? And you are valued. >> Do you feel that as well? >> Oh, for sure. For sure. Uh guys look up to me in the room, you know what I mean? And once again, like we're talking about with Caleb, it's just a versatility thing, you know what I mean? So, when guys can go and play multiple positions, nickel, safety, free safety, uh corner at times, you know what I mean? Uh it just makes the team that much better. >> Let's talk nickel specific positions specifically. >> How important does that become in in today's NFL? >> Oh, it's very important. It's very important. Um if you don't have a good nickel, you probably not going to win any games. So, having Caleb at that position is is real big. It's real key. >> You've heard so much about the offense and how uh prolific that has been and how far the defense needs to come to catch up with that. >> For sure. >> feel like there's any pressure on you being one of the new guys to come into this fold uh on getting this defense right? >> Not at all. Not at all. No pressure at all. Football is football at the end of the day. It's just uh about communication, about leading the team the right way, and about just doing our job. Just doing our job. >> What does Christian Parker emphasize the most with the secondary? >> Uh communication. Communication. Getting everybody on point, especially with the safeties, getting everybody on point, making sure everybody's in the right place, and just uh like I said, doing our job. >> What do you think about the travel you guys have? Cuz you got two practices >> uh up front, and then you got to go to Seattle, you got to go to Rio. You just >> Then you come back from Rio, you got an early game, and then you got a then you got a short week. >> What do you think about the schedule and how you like >> I love it, man. I love it. Uh schedule is good to me, you know what I mean? When we get to see different looks early early on in the in the preseason and everything like that. Uh we get to travel and see those different teams early. It's It's always a good thing, you know what I mean? To get a a different look from our offense. >> What about getting your body rested and and the re- well, the the conditioning part of it for the travel? Cuz even though you are flying now >> you know, uh charter, still it takes a toll a little bit, no? >> Uh a little bit, but that's just part of being a pro, I feel like. You know what I mean? Is uh making sure your body is right, taking care of it, and uh you know what I mean? Making sure you stay healthy. >> Have you played overseas before? >> I have. All right. Well, not overseas. I played uh played in Mexico. I think it was I think it was 2023, I think it was. Yeah. >> That's a lot different than going over. >> For sure. For sure. For sure. >> You were called last year >> Uh-huh. You were asked to be on the council. >> Thank you. Yeah. >> Being on the council, uh you know, for in your first year here, can you just talk about that? >> About the leadership council? Uh it's big time. You know what I mean? Guys look up to us. You know what I mean? So, um anything to help out the team in any way, any anything to uh you know, just be a leader in that way, um it's big time. >> Is it easy to do in your first year? I mean, like what what what do you think happened this offseason to kind of show the coaches players that? >> For sure, I think it's I think it's an easy thing for me to do. You know what I mean? I've been a leader uh when I when I was on the Cardinals as well. Um I was a captain on the Cardinals, so um coming over here, this is no no step down. This is the same thing. Just keep keep being that leader. Uh-huh. >> Is it weird that the Cowboys were the last team you beat? >> Uh no, not at all. Not at all. N- Not at all. Not at all. Uh I'm glad to be a part of this team, and I'm glad to be going against the that type of offense every day. >> First day of training camp, how'd it go? >> It went good. Uh um I feel like we all made each other better, you know. We saw at the end of practice we, you know, ran some cross fields trying to get our conditioning together. So, we had a good overall day of practice as a team. >> What's been just your overall mentality kind of going into this? Obviously, Shady said there'd be a competition. How's What's your mentality going into it? >> I mean, the same as every day, you know, coming to work and get better, you know, trying to get 1% better every day. >> What do you need to see from yourself at the end of training camp to look back and say, "You know what? I did everything I needed to do in training camp to be where I need to be going into the season?" >> I mean, more technically sound, you know, more confident in the playbook and the scheme, and you know, overall just a better player, you know, it takes a You know, it's a process, of course, and you got to take it day by day, you know, one foot in front of the other, but at the end of the day, you know, I'm trying to get to a certain point where I feel good about going into the season. >> Shady talked about that he wanted to ramp up the conditioning program for you guys. Do you agree deal with that? >> I agree with it. You know, it's not it's not fun. You know, it's not easy either going through a full practice and doing what we just did, but it's going to help us, you know. Um you know, the first thing that goes is the mind, you know, when you get fatigued. So, if we eliminate that, then we'll see what heights we can reach. >> First round pick, is it motivating or that that that got you competing for your job? How do you How do you [clears throat] view this opportunity? >> Uh just the same thing. Just come to work and get better. >> You mentioned that the mind goes first in terms of the conditioning and stuff like that. Does that play a little bit into like consistency at the end of the games in terms of >> Absolutely. Yeah, absolutely. I mean, at the beginning of the game everybody's feeling fresh and you know, you got your legs under you, but at the end of the fourth quarter, you know, overtime, when it gets gritty, you know, you got to really pull the dog out of you to be able to fight. >> What do you expect from yourself in year three? You know, a lot of people talk about Llima year three as the year that, you know, everybody see everything. >> Yeah, just keep progressing along with my development. Appreciate it. >> How would you compare how you're feeling this year's camp compared to where you were at last year? >> Uh it feels like year three, you know. I'm not all the way where I want to be yet and that's what camp is for, so I'm still trying to get better every single day, but it feels like I'm going into my third year in the NFL and you know, things are going down for me and I'm learning more every day. >> You said that during I think it was OTAs and mini camp that you're working on improving strength. How have you seen that impacting and how much different or stronger do you feel like you are now than you were in maybe your rookie year? >> Yeah, it's I don't want to say night and day, but I've definitely, you know, put on grown man strength, you know, the necessary strength that you need to play this position at this level, you know, it's not just being strong, it's being like super duper strong and [clears throat] you know, the guys that we're blocking every single play are freaks of nature themselves, so you know, being able to sustain that for a whole play and a whole game and you know, that last 10% of the drive, that's where that extra strength kicks in. >> This team's got a lot of travel ahead of them. >> Seattle twice, you know, the schedule. How do [snorts] you get your mind wrapped around all the travel you have to do? >> I mean, we you know, we got a great staff and you know, the people around, everybody involved in this organization is great and you know, they're going to prepare us whatever way we need to and I guess uh hydration is going to be big for the whole entire team, especially being on the plane that long, you know, so even y'all, you know, being out there, y'all are going to have to hydrate as well, but it's a team effort, for real. >> You know, Dak showed up with with a Super Bowl shirt on. How much is Super Bowl being talked among each other? >> I mean, you know, that's our goal at the end of the day and I know that's everybody else's goal in the NFL, but I I feel like it's about us right now, you know, it's our process, how we go about things and you know, what we're trying to accomplish as a team. That's our goal and you know, to see our quarterback come in with that type of confidence just gives us the confidence to go out there and give it our all every single day. >> Going into year two, y'all you had an immediate change on the offensive side of the ball, offensive line, coaching staff. What does it mean to have continuity from year two to year three with Kellen Moore and Mike McCarthy? >> Yeah, they're amazing, bro. Like, honestly, like, I couldn't ask for a better staff to have around us, you know, they're very personable, they relate to us, they actually are friends with us and, you know, it just makes our offensive line room that much better because, you know, we can be real with each other and, you know, that's that's all you really want out of a coach, you know, somebody to be real with you and, you know, always be honest with you instead of trying to sugarcoat things. >> Would you say you guys are ahead of the run game based off what you did this past season? A year ago you maybe didn't know about the run game, but today you do. >> You said what? I'm sorry. >> Your run game. You you know more about it now than you did a year ago at this time. Do you like where it's headed? >> Um last year doesn't define us this year, so you know, we're trying to rewrite the whole script, you know, we got a new identity as far as, you know, our run game goes, uh pass game and everything, so we're trying to find that now, but I'd definitely say we're off to a good start. >> What's that identity? >> What's the identity? Fast, physical, violent, imposing our will on opponents, you know, Dak has a new saying, Gotti, you know, greatest offense there is, so that's the standard for us. >> What's Dak's saying for y'all? >> Gotti, ask him about it. >> All right. >> G O T I. >> Okay. >> Or if Gotti? >> Yeah, Gotti. That's his little thing now. >> Greatest offense there is. >> Yes, sir. >> That's awesome, man. Appreciate you. >> Yes, sir, appreciate y'all. Y'all have a good one. >> Appreciate it.

title: Highlights From Day 1 of Training Camp | Inside Cowboys Training Camp
text: [music] Inside Cowboys Training Camp presented by Ford is brought to you by AT&T. Connecting changes everything. and by your North Texas Ford dealers. Ford is the best in Texas. >> Welcome back to Inside Cowboys Training Camp for Rockstar, California. Day one of practice. Tommy Y alongside Patrick Walker and Nicole Hudson. Let's go ahead and take you right to the practice fields here. Team portions going on here on day one. No pads on just yet. That'll come later this week, but still an opportunity to get on the grass for the first time as we take a look at the second team offense. Joe Milton leading the charge here this time around. But it'll be him and Sam Howell competing for that quarterback two job. >> Yeah, I think that >> No, that's going to be an interesting backup uh battle and I don't think enough people are actually speaking about that. We know what Joe Mill can do as far as his arm strength. He has an absolute cannon. Needs to kind of tweak his accuracy a bit. Sam How been in the league longer, has more career starts, a little more accurate, but doesn't have the same cannon that does Milton. So, that'll be an interesting battle. >> Now, it's just about rounding out the game for Milton. really making sure that those touch throws and easy stuff is able to happen as there's flags in on this play. He completed that pass quickly to Turpin and like you saw on that play, the zip that he's got on his ball is is really something that that stands out. But it's a matter of controlling it, making sure you use it in the right moments. That time though, without a flag probably would have worked out okay for Turpin. That's Devin Moore, the rookie corner who would have been there on the tackle. >> Yeah, I think I saw actually an edge uh come around the corner there as well on that pass. But you're seeing Joe Milton be a lot more, like you mentioned, accuracy is there. His release is a lot faster. He's reading the defense a lot better as well. That was something that Shotti really wanted to emphasize this offseason. >> And Brian Shanheimer not pleased with the look there. So they'll go back into the huddle. Interesting there. See TJ Bass 66 in there taking snaps at center. This is something Brian Shanheimer talked a little bit about last year and now he's getting reps here as Milton rolls out. Le a foul there in his face and that's Michael Trigg, the undrafted free agent from Baylor on the catch. Patrick Trigg is a guy that a lot of people seem to be excited about. It's the athletic plays, the highlight tape that you saw at Baylor, but some of the easier stuff like that, the quick play action, that's what you really want to see from him here in camp. >> Yeah, Trigg is an absolute freak of an athlete. I mean, when you look at his tape from Baylor and even prior to transferring to Baylor, his ability to attack at the point of catch and, you know, shake defenders and will be tacklers. He's a dynamic talent. Footwork is there, route running is there. He's going to have to probably earn his way onto this team through special teams, though. >> DJ Rogers, the undrafted free agent from TCU, also there in the mix. He's in on this play blocking as the handoff goes. Not too much going there for Israel Abanaconda, the secondyear man out of Pittsburgh, who the Cowboys acquired during the year last season. They liked him a lot in the pre-draft process. >> Yeah, Israel Abaconda. I mean, he's been taking a nice little mix of second team, third team, a little bit of first team reps as well. Uh they're getting him really repped in because the question is who is running back to, right? Obviously, Malik Davis, you know, was there when he needed stepped in uh when Gavvante Williams obviously not there, but you don't know what Jaden Blue is going to be. You don't know what Phil Moff is going to be, but like you mentioned, special teams going to be key for that running back two spot. >> Back to the ones here. Dak Prescott who turns 33 today in the shotgun as CD Lamb comes across the formation in motion. >> Play action. Prescott gets pressure from Rashawn Gary. Here's a deep shot looking for Pickkins. It's a little bit far. Kaylin Carson in coverage, but Rashawn Gary was literally biting at Prescott's ankles on that play. >> And you love to see the pressure getting back there, but you also love to see that Dak stood tall and delivered the pass. You could argue that it was slightly overthrown. You could argue there would have been 17 flags on the field by the time Kaylin Carson finished that rep against George Pickkins. Nonetheless, these guys are getting after it early. >> Always good to see pressure. We saw it a little bit early on in training camp last year and then it didn't really translate into the season, but they feel like this pass rush group is a little bit rejuvenated. So now under center for Dak Prescott, Phil Nafa, the second year back out of Clemson. Behind him there's Jake Ferguson in motion. He'll go back the other way. Straight drop. Quick throw. That's CD Lamb. And that's the bread and butter really of this Cowboys offense. >> Yeah, nice connection there from Dak to CD. You missed that a lot obviously this off season, but I mean you saw earlier as well. Couple of drops from CD, a couple of drops from George Pickkins, but his first day of practice, right? But nice connection there from Dak and CD. >> But you know that goes with, you know, shaking off the rush. These guys are out here. It's day one of training camp. Yes, they've had OTAAS. Yes, they've had mini camp. Yes, they've had throwing sessions in the offseason. However, this is where the rubber starts to meet the road as far as timing goes. >> Couple of injured guys back on the field that we didn't really see as much of during the spring. Donovan Azaraku number six, Don Bland on the outside corner here as Prescott takes a shotgun snap. It's a quick dump off to Phil Mafa that really didn't have a chance to go anywhere. Kenny Clark was in the back field, but the rookie Jan Barham gets credited with the tackle. >> You know, Barham, I think he's going to impress a lot of people as early as year one. and as an inside linebacker. Obviously, he got a ton of reps as an outside edge guy with Michigan, but Cowboys have a different plan with him. Christian Parker does. And I mean, this is telling of what that plan is going to look like. Barham is going to be tasked with disrupting the back field early and often throughout games. >> And Barham was an inside backer, too, at Michigan. They switched him to edge a little bit later this year, but he did play there last year and the two years prior when he was at Maryland. Prescott back in the shotgun. Jaden Blue, the secondyear man from Texas in the back field as it's a bubble screen to Cavante Turpin and he's dangerous if he can catch the outside. That time though, Maris Bell is able to track him down. >> I've got to ask you guys a question. I'm sorry because I've noticed that they're doing so many different movements across the line of scrimmage, three four down off three down linemen, four off uh outside linebackers, excuse me. But when you talk about the different type of looks and different pressures, what are you liking so far from this unit? >> I mean, it's early. Obviously, it's early, but you know what I like is the fact that they are playing multiple as Christian Parker and uh Brian Shottenheimer promised and they're also giving multiple deceptive pre- snap looks to try to throw the quarterback off and I think you're going to see more and more of that. Something that the Cowboys have lacked uh in a big way over the past few seasons. >> Now it's Sam Howell's turn. the quarterback from North Carolina. The Cowboys acquired in free agency. Spent last season with the Philadelphia Eagles and now squarely in the mix for the backup quarterback job behind Dak Prescott. Patrick, what does he need to do to beat Joe Milton for this job? >> Be consistent. He really just needs to be consistent. That's something that Joe Milton struggled with last season. We'll see if he improves upon that this season. But, you know, Joe Milton had flashes uh in preseason games. He had flashes uh out here in training camp. However, he also had some hiccups he had to overcome. Sam Howell just needs to be consistent uh consistently good I should say stack good reps >> that time nothing going downfield for Howell Sam Williams got there for the quote unquote sack. You won't really be seeing much of that. You obviously can't hit the quarterback here but Williams back on a one-year deal. Really has been good on special teams the last couple of years for the Cowboys. They're hoping he takes the next step as a pass rusher. >> I mean you need him too. I mean obviously he had four sacks in three straight two straight seasons the year before last. Obviously last year that depth was a lot different, right? Having to compete for that defensive ends position, but now they're having him do a little bit more of what he did in college, right? Standing up and rushing the passer. That's what I really love to Sam Williams in on that pass as well. I mean, he's active. Uh, so I I love to see what Sam Williams is doing, guys. >> Israel Abonaconda again there on the quick screen. We're seeing a lot of the quick game here today. Just screen passes, bubble screens, running back screens, trying to get this quick passing game working. typically the stuff that you see on these first couple of days. >> And you know what I love that Tommy because what does it do? It strains the linebackers. It puts stress on the linebackers and it forces the linebackers to have to cover side to side. So if anything, the screen passes, the bubble passes, they're going to test out these linebackers and let's see who emerges in that depth chart. >> Handoff here from Howell. And that's a solid carry right there from Dominic Richardson, the undrafted free agent rookie out of Tulsa. another contender in this running back room for Dallas, but he'll have a lot of work to do. And like most undrafted free agents, special teams is obviously a quick route to make in the 53. All right, we'll take a look at one last play here before we get out of here. >> Sam Howell Richardson again in the back field. There's Luke Skoonaker here >> with the offense lined up in line on the right side of the offensive line. Troy Sean Holden in motion. Quick play action and there is Scoon Maker on the catch. >> Just a quick dump. >> Talk about someone who needs to have a breakout season of some sort. Luke Scoomaker most certainly falls toward the top of that category. You know, the former second round pick going into a contract season. He's going to have to show up and show up big, especially with a guy like Brevin Spanford and we talked about Michael Trigg kind of breathing down the back today. >> All right, that'll do it for today's episode of Inside Cowboys Training Camp for Nicole Hudson, Patrick Walker. I'm Tommy Arsh. We'll see you tomorrow. >> Inside Cowboys Training Camp presented by Ford was brought to you by AT&T. Connecting [music] changes everything. And by your North Texas Ford dealers. Ford is the best in Texas. Closed captioning by the Texas Lottery. Play the games [music] of Texas with the Texas Lottery. Play today.

title: Brian Schottenheimer: "Everything Is Earned" | Press Conference
text: Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News. Brian, can you uh give us your thought process on how you did the training camp schedule? It's like you have two practices and you're off and then you're off again on Sunday. I don't know if that's because of the travel you have to do. >> No, it's a great question and I'll answer it. Uh it goes back to the whole thing that Calvin we're always evolving. Uh I just, you know, talking to some of my peers around the league and how they do things. I got a bunch of different options and uh I'm always looking to grow and get better and um really what we like about this schedule is, you know, you go two practices in a row. Usually it's a medium and then kind of a another medium to hard. Then they do the stay day, so they're able to kind of get their legs and bodies back. And then um after that, you know, we come back with another hard one leading into a player's day off. So, four-day cycle. Um you're able to get your install in based off first, second down, third down, red zone, two-minute uh in that four-day cycle. And then we come back off of the player's day off with a review day. So, have them put out and uh work really hard. The other thing I think you guys are going to notice uh just uh that I'm really excited about doing some sports science stuff. Uh we're going to condition these guys during the ramp-up period. Uh I think it's important to build the engine uh of these guys when they're fatigued. Last year you guys remember I put them on a line cuz I was pissed off. Uh I'm not pissed today. I'm happy. It's the first day at training camp. And uh but we're going to condition. It's well planned out and uh again the numbers are showing you, "Hey, let's get these guys in tip-top shape." Why? Uh the best teams in the league are the best conditioned teams and we want to be able to, you know, outlast everybody. >> The amount of travel you have to do even out here like you got to go to Seattle then obviously you got Rio. This is How much does that concern you in in terms of your sports science staff and kind of work all that in? >> Yeah, I mean we're on it. Uh shoot, we sent a team of about 12 to 15 people down to Rio and uh we're working through the logistics of cargo ships and things that you have to do to send some of your stuff down there cuz customs is hard, but uh it's part of the game. I mean it it really is, you know, coaching in Seattle, you go East Coast, you know, here we've got a lot of travel and it is what it is, but I guess the positive thing is, you know, we we're out here, we go to Seattle, we come back, we go to Arizona, and then we go home. So. >> Clarence Hill, DALLAS Cowboys. Just administratively start off will everybody be cleared to practice today? I know you said it yesterday, just double-checking. >> Yes. >> It will be no Everybody will be good to go. Uh yesterday you mentioned that practice will be more physical. What does that look like? How does that manifest itself in this day and age of being physical in practice? >> Yeah, a few more padded practices, uh a few more 2-hour practices. I think I shared with you guys in the spring I'm not a big 7-on-7 guy, uh but we'll have a few days that are 2-hour B-type practices where we're going to do 7-on-7 and 9-on-7. Uh you know, part of our winning edge we believe is, you know, owning the line of scrimmage. I'm really excited about those battles of watching our offensive line compete against a what I think's going to be an elite defensive line, and so um you know, you'll you'll you'll see a lot of padded work and um it's cuz we got to build some calluses and uh get ready. >> Brian Lindsay, The Athletic. What is the benefit to a team going to training camp with no distractions or no lingering business issues to take care of? >> Uh I mean, I think that's more of a issue for you guys. I mean, you know, we're we're we're we're we're built to deal with it, you know? I mean, we know there's going to be storylines, we know there's going to be things, but like we focus on the guys in that room. Um our guys are in a really good spot. I think the confidence is high. Uh we're as close of a group as I've been around, quite honestly, and so um again, I think it's, you know, a storyline's going to pop up at some point, and we'll be ready to handle it, but right now we're just enjoying being back together and getting a chance to go out here and compete. >> Having everybody available to practice, what does that do for you as a coach when you aren't having to navigate injuries or whatnot to do get going with what you want to do? >> Yeah, I I think it gives you a chance to create some real position battles, you know, because you're not limiting guys. I mean, unfortunately for some guys in the past, right, they've been in the middle of these position battles, but they can't compete, you know, they're getting two reps here, four reps there, but you're they're they're limited. And so, I think you're going to see the the the purity of our roster where we stand. I think we're really talented roster. There's some great position battles that, you know, we're excited to see and um you know, we just, you know, we know that, you know, when we go through these days, there's going to be some guys that get dinged up a little bit and uh you know, it gives other guys chance to step up. >> Jamison with The Athletic. Uh Now that I mean, you haven't had a full year with Quinnen Williams, but is there anything that maybe you've learned about him of of beyond him just being the the outstanding player that he is? >> Yeah, how much he loves football. Um you know, he's an incredible teammate. He's one of the most I would say humble superstars I've ever been around. You know, he truly is. I think being in New York and unfortunately not being a part of playoff teams, you know, he's to the point in his career where, you know, it's not about money, it's not about sacks, it's about wins. And I love that cuz when you combine that with certain guys like Dak Prescott and other players, um that's what they they want to lead the league in is wins. And um he's just uh awesome family man, you know, great teammate, but uh the the play speaks for itself. >> And then with him, uh can you speak a little bit about uh having his locker moved from where it was last year and now where he's in the middle of the room with right next to Dak. >> Yeah. >> Um I think he deserves that. I think, you know, we wanted him to be able to you know, touch a lot of different people and um you know, when I first met, you know, Quinnen we first sat down after the trade, the thing he said, he goes, you know, coach, I I really want to impact other people. And it was a hard time for us. I mean, he came in right after um you know, we lost MarShawn. And so, imagine you're a player like that, you're coming in, you're trying to find your way and impact people, but I think he's really um at that stage of his career where um that's important to him and so we wanted to move him. I never like to rinse and repeat things. Uh I'll take that opportunity, John. I wrote them down. Uh but the leadership council, he's a big part of it. So, we've got four guys on defense. Um before I get into it. So, again, this was me with my list, the coordinators with their list of guys that we felt would again, impact the locker room in the right way, speak up when they needed to uh to me and other people. So, on defense, it's Quinton Williams, Kenny Clark, Rashan Gary, Jaylon Thompson. Uh on offense, it's Tyler Booker, uh Jake Ferguson, Tyler Smith, Javonte Williams, CD and Dak, the birthday boy, and then you got Bryan Anger for special teams. So, um it could have been 15 names, but I had to cap it somewhere and um I felt that these guys were the perfect fit. It's their council. It's not mine. They run it and uh you know, we've got a few of those guys that report to me every couple of weeks and issues and problems and things that uh we'll try to address. >> Nick Eatman, Dallas Morning News. What's your telegram? What's your scope on this running back room heading into camp and you know, with the limitations on physicality out here, how can you hope to get the most out of that battle here? >> Yeah, I'm excited about Nick. You know, I think you know, Jayden Blue's a guy we've talked about from the minute he stepped on campus. Uh it's interesting talking to Christian Parker a little bit yesterday actually about some stuff and you know, he said, you know, Jayden was a guy that going into game one, they were very concerned about. You know, they had been around him, you know, they'd seen him. Andrew Mukuba, the safety was with him at Texas. That shows you that he's a guy that we need to take the next step and I think he's going to do that. Um he understands his role, but uh he's exciting. Uh Phil Mafah, he's a guy we're very excited about. They're very different. Um and then, you know, the guy that never gets talked about enough, you know, is Malik Davis. You know, I mean, all this guy does is go out and score 40-yard touchdown runs on Thanksgiving Day and you rushed for 100 yards on Christmas Day. He must be the holiday killer, but I mean he's just in the special teams. So, Yeah, I'm excited about that group and that battle and there there'll be plenty of time to, you know, along with the preseason game see the physicality from that group. >> What's it going to look like out here as far as training multiple guys with that green dot and then finding the one guy to do it? >> Yeah, it's going to be busy, which is good. Uh we'll take turns. We rotate guys like I said, Mike and Dimes they move around at different spots. So, they're interchangeable now, which again I think we learned last year we did not do a very good job of myself included of training different guys to do it and uh again, it doesn't have to be a certain player. It doesn't have to be the Mike linebacker. It could be a safety. It could be different people. Uh it's going to be someone that's on the field all the time. Uh but uh I would say we've got three or four candidates that we're really excited about and uh but before I say their names I'll I want to get a couple days in the practice. >> Tommy Ayers, dallascowboys.com. Bryan, you've said in the past that you don't really like seven-on-seven. I know it's part of what you have to do now. So, when you do have to do it, what do you kind of look for and take away? I know it's begrudging, but what what's positive for you from it? >> You know, if you're installing passes, new concepts, new wrinkles, Tommy, I think it's good. Um Christian Parker loves it. He's a secondary coach, so he loves it. Um they usually love a lot of our concepts, which is why I think he likes it. Uh but again, you want to see quarterbacks being efficient. You want to see the ball coming out. Um it's a great opportunity to work your scramble rules because quite honestly in seven-on-seven they're going to cover a lot of things because there's no play fakes and things like that. So, uh it's good, but I just think quarterbacks in this league with the way the pass rush is in the NFL, they need to be sitting in the pocket. They need to be, you know, uh affected by the time clock of that and I just think uh they get a false sense of security. So, we'll do it. We do it more to get the nine-on-seven than we do it to uh just do 707. >> And then whether it be conversations with your sports science department or just what you saw last year, how do you help these rookies who have never done an NFL training camp before kind of get up to speed a little bit? >> Yeah, education started in the spring. It started in OTAs. You know, their schedule's a little bit longer than the the vets. You're allowed to keep them a couple hours more and so Brian Wandzilak and his staff do a great job along with the the you know, Scott Seidenberg and the sports nutrition of teaching these guys. I hit them this morning on you know, using this hour, you know, that we have between you know, finishing up meetings and going to practice. There's about an hour. What's your routine? What's your plan? You know, like don't just go back and lay down in your room. Like get in there and get stretched out and get your mind right, get taped. Um and for those guys they use the vets a lot. Hey Dak, what do you do? Hey CD, what do you do? George, what do you do? And I think you know, they'll figure that out as we go. >> Uh Bill Bill Jones, CBS Texas. Uh >> Hi Bill. >> Looking at your uh leadership council there, uh one name >> like it? >> What what name really sticks out to me is because of his youth and that's Tyler Booker. What is it about Tyler that's impressed you so much and others uh from a leadership standpoint with one year here? >> We knew what we were getting with Tyler Bill, you know, when we drafted him. We knew that he was an elite person, elite human being. He was all about our five core values of putting the team first and working hard and competing and he loves football and and he's about the brotherhood. Uh you can't go into any meeting room that Tyler Booker's in and uh if you ask for an opinion, his hand's shooting up and he speaks with conviction. Yeah, I I don't I can't say enough great things about him and uh he was one of the few no-brainers. I think every single one of us had him on there and that says a lot for a guy going into his second year. >> Kim Player, NFL Network. Hey coach. Uh yesterday you were talking about Christian Parker's organization and plan for practice. Why is that important and what is he doing that's so different than some of the other defensive coordinators you've worked with? >> I think I would start with the exposure, the guys he's been exposure exposed to. You know, Vic obviously gets the first nod, but you know, he's been around Vance Joseph, he's been around all these great defensive minds and uh a little bit like myself, you know, when you're around these great minds as a a position coach a want-to-be coordinator, you're grabbing and stealing things that you like. You're constantly writing down, "Hey, I like this. I like that. Hey, I would do this differently. I wouldn't." So, there's a there's a expedited understanding of what you want to do. Like there's a philosophy. Um and you see that from CP and I think it's because he's thought about this for five or six years, but not only that, he's been exposed to some great defensive minds and but what I love about him is he's going to take good ideas from these people, but he's going to do it his way. Like I think if you ask Vic Fangio, Vic's going to say Christian had a huge voice in what they did in Philadelphia and um certainly uh I think he'll lean on his staff, you know, whether it's Derrick Ansley, Cheddar, he's going to do the same thing that uh that his predecessors have done. >> You've sat in on a lot of his meetings. Has there been a moment in one of those meetings where you found yourself pulling him off to the side and wanting a little bit more detail? >> Detail? No. Absolutely not. Uh there's certainly things that I give him feedback on. Hey, what about this? What about that? Hey, maybe think about this, but in terms of the detail, the way he >> said you're like, "You know, as an offensive guy, that's something I want to drill down on." >> Oh, absolutely. Yeah, those conversations happen all the time. I think that's one of the other things, you know, and these will come to me as as we go through training camp, but like, you know, I want to spend, you know, in the evening time 20, 30, 35 minutes watching film with Clayton and watching film with Christian and just talking ball. I mean, just whether we grab a couple Miller Lites, shout out sponsor, you know, and we just watch some ball. It's you know, like that's how we get on the same page. And hey, I really love this concept. Well, why would you do that? Oh, if you do that, I'm going to do this. It's like a chess match. And so, I'm really looking forward to doing that and I think that's I can do that this year because, again, of my confidence in Clayton and then, obviously, I'm much more involved in the defense. >> Uh Joe Take it. >> Joe Trahan, WFAATV. Coach, this is about uh Caleb Downs. Such a smart young player. Is part of your job trying to have him not try and do too much too soon? That's part one of the question. Part two, what do you want to see from him once he gets on the grass? >> Um no, I I I I think at the end of the day, we're not going to overload Caleb Downs. That's our job as coaches. Uh we have a huge Uh we have instincts that say he can handle a lot of this stuff. I think, you know, when you go to Alabama you play as a freshman, there's in maybe one of the most complex defenses there is. Um what we saw from him in the spring and what I want to see from him uh out here is just to get better every day. I think the fundament- The mind works incredibly fast. I mean, the way he sees things, the instincts, his ability to diagnose, the communication. But it's the fundamentals. We've We've We're teaching him some things he hasn't done at Ohio State or Alabama. And so, those are the things, whether it's a scoot technique in coverage, uh how we play bunches and stacks, things like that. Uh those are the things that that we expect to see out there when we get going. >> Kristi Scales, Cowboys Radio 105.3 The Fan. Since uh special teams is the pathway for so many of these young guys, who do you hope that's already one of your core guys steps up and kind of serves as as that war star since C.J. Goodwin isn't here anymore? >> Yeah, uh number one, I'm I'm thrilled for C.J. I called C.J. when he decided to retire and thanked him for all that he did and uh wasn't just as a player but as a leader. Uh Couple names popped right into into my brain, so I'll go with them. Brevyn Spann-Ford, you know, um tireless worker, one of our offseason award winners uh for the way he trained and worked in the offseason. Another offseason award winner, Hunter Luepke. He's a guy that can do everything for us. Um from playing fullback to being third down back to being a single back, quite honestly, running the football and check-downs and things like that, but on special teams, he's a difference-maker. Um and then this last guy would be Ryan Flournoy. Now, Flo's doing so well as a receiver, it's a little bit harder to use him, you know? Nick asked me all the time, I'm like, "I don't know, man. He's pretty good." Um but uh I think that's because of, you know, but he wants to do everything. He just plays the game the right way with that violent physical nature. So, those are the first three guys that popped in my mind and they all have that so those same leadership qualities of CJ, maybe a little different. Brevyn's kind of in your face. Flo's more direct. Um and then Hunter's kind of a quiet assassin. >> Tim Cowlishaw, Dallas Morning News. Hello, Bryan. >> How we doing? How many days [clears throat] you got still printing? >> What's that? >> How many days you got left? >> Seven. >> Okay. >> But it's close. >> Okay, seven. Let me write that down. >> I got scriptures. >> It's available. you've mostly coached teams like younger quarterbacks in your career, young Russell Wilson, Brandon Weeden, Landry >> Are we on deadline? >> You now have a 30-year-old man >> at quarterback. What is unique about working with Dak and what or what is maybe the same about >> a guy. Him at this age >> Oh, man, I could go on, Tim, about Dak forever. Uh I just love this guy's curiosity for getting better, you know, the way he works, the way he trains, the things he's doing to take care of his body as he gets older. Um and that's not just Dak, that's, you know, some of Dak and I's biggest fights are about reps, you know, and so you know, as he gets older he's figuring that out, but like just the way this guy works, man, the way he attacks his craft. I kind of sit by him in in offensive meetings and Clayton probably gets angry because he and I are just kind of talking about different things, but the leader, the man, and I'm just really proud of the guy, the way he's taken the changes we made last year of playing more under center, Tim. That was a little bit different for him. I mean, with Kellen we were more I was here, we were more gun and spread out and things like that. Now we're more cut splits and movements and actions and it was not an easy transition for a guy that had been doing it at a high level and playing at an MVP level a couple years ago with with Kellen and Mike and I think he showed that, you know, that versatility to be able to do both is pretty cool. >> Sam. Coach Quinn talked before in Dallas to talk about you guys have a mantra or theme this season and you mentioned the trash talking with some of the other guys different with Christian Parker. You looking forward seeing how this defense challenges your offense out there? >> Uh, yeah, I mean, we we never back away from the central theme of the program, which is compete every day. We've got, you know, a number of things, but I actually shared with the guys today one of the things when I was thinking about just training camp and and stuff like that was that I shared with the guys today was everything is earned. Yeah, I really think that, you know, all 31 other teams are doing what we're doing. Head coaches are standing up here, they're making predictions, they're talking about their roster, how good it is. The players are are are training and getting ready to go out to have practice and all that stuff. And we talked about what makes us different and hopefully it's the consistency that we work at, you know, and we're not going to have perfect days all the time, but I think if if you're consistently consistent throughout the course of training camp and you have a lot more good days and bad days or five, six, seven good days in a row and maybe have an off day. And then we have to be willing to do things that maybe other teams don't want to and that is part of the conditioning, that's part of the physical practices. So, you know, whether we adopt it and use it all the time, but it's something I shared with them today and I I I I believe it. I think, you know, none of those guys have gotten here without having to earn it. >> Uh Joe Hoyt, Dallas Morning News. You guys haven't shied away from your expectations for Kaevon Downs and your optimism there. I think I know the answer, but how is he kind of handled those expectations and what does that told you about him? >> Yeah, I I you know, maybe it's coach [clears throat] speak. I'm not trying. I I don't think we can put anything on Kaevon Downs that huh is above what he expects for himself. Uh he's a young player, he's a rookie, he's going to make mistakes, but like I said in the spring, I'll say it again, Kaevon's not going to he doesn't repeat mistakes. Uh and um that is a sign of a young man that understands X's and O's in football and he's wired the right way. Uh if you haven't been around his mom and dad, I think you guys have in the press conference, his sister, um his brother, obviously, but yeah, he's uh his expectations are probably a lot higher than any of us have for him. >> You guys brought back Will Grier to coach after he retired. Obviously, you had some interest in doing that a little bit earlier this off season. Um why was that move there and what have you seen from him from the coaching standpoint already? >> Yeah, I told the guys yesterday, I said, "Hey, I got some sad news." I said, "Will Grier's retired." I said, "But we got some good news. Will Grier's joined the coaching staff." And uh you know, we tried to get it done and uh at the end of the day, Will wanted to go play. You know, we wanted to do it before and I get that. Like, when you're done playing, you're done playing and um I think the draw of being able to come back here and work with this team and this group of young men I think he's going to be an outstanding coach. You know, you see these guys, it wasn't my journey at all, uh but like you see the, you know, Davis Webb's of the world, you see these guys that go shooting up the ladder and Kell I think was that way, you know, when he was here. Um I think the same way about Will. I think uh you know, Will Grier's going to be a terrific coach and he'll probably be calling plays in this league in the next 6 to 8 years. >> Brad Brad Sham, Cowboys Radio 105.3 The Fan. You said a few minutes ago this is one of the closest teams you've ever been on. I'm wondering since they've never played a game together and half of them have virtually just met, how can that be? >> Uh the time spent in and away from the building. You know, I mean these guys they play golf together, they go to dinner together, they have people over their house. I mean, and that doesn't happen by accident. It happens by guys stepping outside maybe their comfort zone and saying, "Hey man, you guys want to go get a beer? You guys want to come over? I'm having let's you know, let's do a crawfish boil or something like that." Um it's intentional. And I think it's intentional, Brad, because we talk about it. You know, and it's not something that we leave it to them. I mean, they have to obviously take the step to do it, but it's something that we talk about. Um we think that kind of brotherhood is what's going to close the circle for us in this pursuit of a championship and because there's going to be adversity, but um you can't read those names and it's not just those guys. I mean, but those guys understand what it takes to and what it means to have a close-knit, strong culture. >> Hey coach, Patrick Walker DallasCowboys.com. Circling back to Tyler Biadasz really quickly. Goes without saying replacing a future Hall of Famer is, you know, one of the most daunting tasks especially for a young guy rookie. You guys are still trying to sort things out in the post-Tyron Smith era at left tackle. How impressive is it that one year later no one's talking about concerns about replacing Zack Martin going forward and what can Tyler Biadasz be in year two under Connor and Klieman? >> Yeah, again, you know, I think when you look at the strides Tyler made last year in the pass protection. He's always been a mauler. He's always been a mauler. That's what people loved about him at at Alabama. Um the ability to to to move into that spot and take over for an incredible player like Zack. Uh but again, when you're wired the right way, you don't he's not competing against Zack, he's competing against himself. But the pass protection is really what excited me throughout the year, Patrick. I mean, this guy was going up against some elite pass rushers inside and he started using his hands better, moving his feet better and another year working under Connor Riley with some of those fundamentals. I think he's ready to take huge strides. >> Mike, you see box four. In what ways does Tyler Guyton need to improve to become a more reliable player for you at such an important position? >> Yeah, it is important position. It's a awesome battle that we're looking forward to with you know, Tyler and again, my philosophy is always be straight up and honest with Tyler. And so we've communicated with Tyler that it's going to be a competition. Here's what you need to do better. You know, he certainly had a few nicks and bumps and bruises that have limited him, but there's a consistency or lack thereof at times with his fundamentals. He is one of the most talented athletes I've ever been around at left tackle. Like just the feet, the ability to move, the size, all that stuff. It's a process and it's hard when you're in and out of line up at times to find that consistency, but that's what he needs to do. And he's going to get challenged against some really good edge rushers and that's where the padded practices kind of come in. >> Uh last year you seemed to be a little perturbed by the fights >> I can't hear you over Morgan Wallen. >> [laughter] >> Last year you [clears throat] seemed to be a little perturbed by all the fights you had in practice and uh this year you want to have two hour practices more physical. How much do you talk to your guys about their behavior out there on the field? >> It's a great point. I haven't talked about fights yet. Hopefully there's none today. Um now I look, I want our guys to play on the edge. I don't want them to go over the edge. My whole thing with the fighting is it's no different than a game, right? If you let them throw punches in practice, guess what? They're going to probably throw punches in a game and then you're going into a third or fourth quarter of a game and one of your best players or one of your starters is out of the game and so uh we'll we'll we'll discuss that and uh uh again, the biggest thing for them is the discipline that not throw the punch. >> Lindsay. >> Coach Tomlin, I know Jerry touched on it yesterday, but how have you seen George respond since the tag? And what do you anticipate seeing from him during training camp? >> Uh George Pickens today, and I told him this, so he's not uh he was as dialed in in meetings as I've seen him since he's been here. just following along, questions. Um I think you're going to see a very motivated George Pickens going into the season, and I think that's uh great news for us and maybe bad news for the rest of the league. >> All right, we're going to have to roll the >> Thank you, guys. See you all tomorrow. Remember, it's not punishment when they run.

title: Quinnen Williams: "I Want to Be Here for the Long Haul" | Player Interviews
text: Calvin Watkins, Dallas Morning News. >> Um seems as if there's another player your position getting some big money and Stephen Jones said he would like to maybe take care of you. Your thoughts about your position and how the salary structure is moving up. >> Yeah, it's it's pretty cool, man, to see the guys get paid, you know what I'm saying? Especially like Jalen Carter and Jeffrey Simmons. And them two phenomenal players, phenomenal guys, man. I watch their film all the time, especially with CP coming over and all the things that Jalen Carter do, man, he's well deserving of every penny he he's got and earned. And just fantastic watching him on film, trying to see what I can take from his game and put in the same scheme that we kind of running right now. So, it's been phenomenal just watching them guys on film and learning from them guys and for me right now, man, I'm just trying to stay focused on the training camp, enjoying Oxnard, enjoying having one of the best quarterbacks in the league and the one of the best offense in the league and just enjoy building this defense and trying to get this defense in the right direction. So. >> How's just your position evolved? Cuz usually in defense we talk about the edge rushers get all the money, but now it seems like guys like you are moving up a little bit. >> Yeah, it's evolved tremendous. I was joking with Kenny Clark about like how it how how far the defensive tackle market has come since he was he was coming in and things like that when it was sitting at like what, 17 million dollars a year was the highest paid and it was like Fletcher Cox and like Aaron Donald, those guys. And now we're at 38. So, we were just laughing joking about that, man, and it just phenomenal to see like the the the impact that my position, defensive tackles, they're making. Like you always see like the guy the teams that's in the Super Bowl has phenomenal D-tackles. With Seattle and the Eagles and Kansas City the few years, man, and those guys being very effective and things like that. So, that's that's all I focus on, man. I just focus on bringing the impact to this team, bringing the impact to this defense and trying to get this team going in the right direction. So, another D-tackle being in the Super Bowl soon. So, that's all I'm focused on. That's all I'm really worried about right now and just enjoying this weather, enjoying going against Tyler Smith every day, Tyler Biadasz every day. Just enjoying the hard work and the camaraderie that it all come with being a Dallas Cowboy and being here in Oxnard, so. >> Turning to the Dallas Cowboys, have you had any indication >> [clears throat] >> that you'll get done with your contract anytime soon? Have you said you had talked to the Cowboys already? I don't know what you probably had talked to I just want to know what you know about your >> I I I truly I truly don't know, man. I let them handle that. Like I said, man, I'm just truly enjoying being here, man. I'm enjoying being on the Dallas Cowboys. First first training camp, first time in Oxnard, first time kind of being in a sense where we can get better and trying to get better on defense especially with the new guys coming in, with the new staff coming in and just kind of focus on getting this defense going in the right direction because we have a great offense. Everybody know we have a great offense. And it's our job on defense to to win championships cuz that's the saying, so we got a long way to go from last year and I'm just extremely focused on that and extremely dedicated to that, so. >> You got first time Dak Prescott in the mid camp that we all know. You've never been to playoffs. You know, you want to get to playoffs and you want to get up and win the playoffs. What you talking about never been to the playoffs and hopefully having a team that's already talking to Super Bowl winning the playoffs. >> I definitely I definitely never been to the playoffs, man. And as a competitor, man, I want to win it all. Like I compete in this sport. I'm a ultimate competitor and I want to win every single game if I can. I was I was bred to win from Coach Saban and do the things that we can do there at Bama and I wanted to bring that same mentality especially to this defense because our offense have that mentality and just trying to develop a new defensive culture, a defensive mindset. And we got the right guys on defense. Got Kenny Clark, Rashaan Gary, two unbelievable leaders. Caleb Downs, the unbelievable college leader and coming to the NFL ready to learn. And our defense as a staff is unbelievable, too. So, really just focus on, man, getting that side together and doing the things that we can do to carry our weight on this team because the offense is for sure going to carry theirs. >> Considering that history, how disappointing has it been to not been in the playoffs in the last few years? I mean, I You know, that's a different thing you have to deal with. >> Yeah, honestly, I haven't thought about it since I became a Cowboy. Um just because it's so it's so it's so it's so refreshing being here. Um knowing that you have guys with the same like-minded with that that you have. Um especially on that offensive line, man, you got guys on that offensive line who want to get better um with themselves, who want you to get better. Um in their in their own in their own instincts. And you got an offense um uh leader like Dak Prescott who's going to come out and push you to the the best of the best as a defense every single day because he wants you to get better cuz he knows defense is winning championships. So, um being being a part of a group, man, that has the same exact mindset that I have when it come down to winning, when it come down to winning the playoff, when it come down to being ultimate competitor, is unbelievable and refreshing to me. So, >> Yes, quite a bit. You mentioned all these other guys being leaders. Obviously, you're a leader, too, on this team. How do you think your leadership has grown and evolved throughout your career? >> I It's grown tremendously, man, especially cuz I came in especially in the NFL like a leader by example. I always was the guy that was going to be on time, the guy who going to set the standard for everything when it come down to being on time, working my tail off and things like that. Um so, I've been around a bunch of great leaders, a bunch of great players um in this league. And just learn from those guys. I had C.J.
