Mosley, Frank Gore, Tyron Smith, uh just name a few great leaders who taught me so much about trying to get that vocal leadership out and trying to develop a vocal leadership. Um reading books and things like that. So, um it's it's definitely been helping me being around great people and great leadership. And also, it's easy to lead when you got guys who have the same mindset like that we have here. So. >> And you know, you got thrown in the mix last year at defensive tackle. Where do you think you and Kenny are now going into this year? And and how much smoother do you think that that that'll be now you got a full off season >> I think it's going to be extremely smooth, man. Like having a full off season together, we we both went to OTAs for majority of time and got a chance to jail with each other. And now we at training camp with each other. Not just Kenny, just the new defensive line coach, the new the young guys that we drafted as in that defensive line room. And even bringing in Tito, even bringing in having young Jay in there, man. It it's it's phenomenal having those guys in there and getting a chance to work and jail and and build chemistry with each other, man. Because like I said, it's super easy to be a leader. It's super easy to kind of come to work and work hard when you got guys with the same mindset as you. But if you got guys you got to drag along and really babysit, it's kind of hard in that case. So, we have a bunch of guys on our team and our room that have the same like mindset. And those to me goal is to win. So. >> Tommy Ayers, dallascowboys.com. Whether you have the contract conversations now or later, is Dallas where you want to be long term? >> Oh, for sure, man. Especially being here with these guys, man. You got a phenomenal group, man. Phenomenal staff, man. Organization wise, man. It's unbelievable, man. And then having guys that you can call and lean on like DeMarcus Ware is one of my guy. It's unbelievable, man. So, like I said, man, I'm not really focused on no contract. Like I I definitely want to be here for the long haul. I definitely would enjoy and love being for the long haul. But I want to win. And that's kind of the only thing I'm really focused on is winning and kind of getting this defense in into the groove where we can win football games for this team. So. >> Nick Eatman, dallascowboys.com. Whether or later, is in the training camp and now with one practice under your belt, what does that look like for you? Is it How different is it compared to last year? >> Can you repeat that again? >> The runway you have into this season. Obviously, it's a good thing compared to being traded mid-year. >> Yes, sir. >> Uh what does that runway look like for you though? Like through this point and now having a practice on the field. >> Just Just competing every day. Like I said, man, we got a great interior like we got a great interior offensive line and offensive line in the whole, man. You got one of the best interior offensive guard over there. Um so, I feel like I'm one of the best D-tackles in the league and um just getting a chance to go against him every single day is going to make me better. Getting a chance to talk to those guys every single day. Getting a chance to just be a comrade amongst the defensive line, amongst the defense. Getting a chance to just lead and push each other to the right direction because we have the guys who know how it's supposed to look to win championships on a college level, win win playoff games or NFC championships from Green Bay, those guys. Um so, just getting a chance to really jail our mindset as a defense and then getting a chance to just compete against one of the best offense in the league and just and just really iron sharpens iron is going to make us even better and uh hopefully make it them even better. So, >> Uh Joe Hoy, Dallas Morning News. You mentioned that you want to be here for the long haul and that you want to win. When did you really get sold on the belief that you could win here, that the Cowboys were a place you could >> I think when I got traded here. I think when you when you get traded and somebody put that belief in you. When you get drafted and traded, it's kind of the same same uh I guess feeling. Um when somebody believe in you to help to know that okay, you're one of the guys I feel like you can help us win and help us achieve the goal that we always want to achieve. So, as soon as I got traded, I wanted to be here. Like I wanted to be here for the long haul. I didn't want to just come and just just play around. I I want to be here and win. I want to win for the organization because it has a winning culture. Um it has a winning history and I want to kind of bring that back uh here and I kind of want to win for not only uh me myself personally, but guys like Dak Prescott who works his tail off and been here 10 years and you know what I'm saying, deserve a Super Bowl and guys like CD who's a five-time Pro Bowler and been here five years and who deserves a Super Bowl. And you just see those things like that and you just see how how great they was last year and the defense wasn't so great. So, it just urges me personally to get this defense together. So, the hard work that they put in won't just be hard like go to waste anymore. >> [snorts] >> Thanks Slater, NFL Network. Has there been a particular interaction with Christian Parker that stands out to you? >> I just think his swag, man. Every day he comes ready to work. Every day he comes just with a swag and a mentality to get better and to be the be the best that he can be. And that's just amazing, man. I love he like to laugh and joke. And I just I just have fun with this staff, man. And these guys are super prepared, super ready and from a winning culture. They They know how it feels to win. My defensive line coach won a Super Bowl with the Rams. CP, of course, won. Ben Solak won a Super Bowl with the Eagles and they know how it's supposed to look. They know how all pro look. They know how pro bowlers look and they know how a great defense is supposed to look. So, just trusting in them to kind of guide us in the right direction and to turn us into those same Super Bowl winning defenses. So, >> You say that you read a lot. Is there a particular book that stands out and sort of guides you? >> It's not a particular book. It's just kind of one of those things like I be strolling on Instagram or my wife will send me a book and I just kind of glance through it or read it or clip note it. >> [laughter] >> It just finds some different nuggets I can pull out and just to help me be a better leader or a better person in general. So, >> Is there one you're leaning on right now and nugget that's getting you through camp? >> Just the playbook. >> Just the playbook right now. So, >> Mike Dusey, Fox 4. Coach Shurmur this morning mentioned how you're one of the more humble stars he's been around. That humility started at a young age. Where Where did it come from? >> I just I think it's truly come from just everything that I've accomplished and everything I get to do is a blessing. Um, so I just kind of carry that mindset of it could be taken away from me any day. Uh, so enjoy it, enjoy the people around you and um, make a difference in anybody's life, make a difference in somebody else's life, uh, um, that you come across and I got it, I live by this code like treat others how I want to be treated. Um, so even when I'm giving constructive criticism on the field, um, I always had that mindset of like treat that person how you want to be treated. So kind of even if I'm upset at that person or if I'm upset, just kind of take a deep breath and give that person constructive criticism how I want somebody to constructive criticize me. So I kind of just live with those values and try to apply those things when I do my leadership or how I go by my life. So

title: Detroit Lions players meet with the media | 2026 Training Camp Day 1
text: Just going back when you hear back surgery that's probably something that's a little scary at that >> Sure. Um just talk about the the rehab process of we saw you out there in the spring just how you're feeling now and I've cited you kind of backwards like >> full time. Yeah. Uh Brett Fischer and I started back on January 4th about 5 weeks after my surgery and going ever since. They've had to tell me to get away from the building for my breaks. Other than that, I've been here and emotionally, physically, mentally feels really good to be back. >> A couple of fear that that that came over you with the initial diagnosis. Did you have to calm through some of those emotions? >> Yeah, if you've ever had a nervous system injury, just waiting for the nerve strength to come back, being told it might not come back, all those feelings of maybe not being able to play again. It sucks sitting on the couch. My wife got the uh the short end of the stick with that. Every night I'd be telling her like, "Man, I really hope God allows me to get my nerve strength back and get to play football again." She's like, "You're fine. The doctor says you're going to be fine. Stre, you know, training staff says you're going to be great. You're going to come back be great." So, shout out to her. Shout out to Brett Fischer. The entire athletic training staff. It's just amazing through this process. >> When was that point that you knew, okay, I feel? >> Yeah. Well, the nerve strength came back in phases. Started with the glute, then worked on the hamstring, then the calf. So, like honestly, probably just two or three months ago, the full strength came back and you could see like the muscle at atrophy start to, you know, diminish and grow that that strength back. So, I mean, I've had three or four good months under my belt of running, cutting, sprinting. Uh, now I'm hitting obviously going to be in pads soon, so I'm excited. >> There's no lingering pain or discomfort or anything like that. >> No, no, I feel really good. I was running around, bending well, moving well. Um, no, good so far. >> What have you thought about just Drew's offense overall? Obviously, when you look at some of the tight end production, Arizona, some of that was the injuries they had obviously, but a pretty tight end friendly offense. Is that maybe a good way to explain it? >> Certainly. Um, I think the league is gravitating towards tight end play right now with the 12 and 13 personnel, which is exciting for us specifically, but I had more of an outsers view in the springtime during OTAAS. I was off to the side and I got to watch mostly and now to get to be a part of it. Um, just super amped to work with them. >> A lot of your teammates getting rewarded. Obviously money is not the motivation but it's a business. >> Sure. >> Well, would you like to get that done sooner or later or what's your was that any motivation as well? I know that the game probably you know but just was it >> I think everybody that's on the roster money is motivation. This is our job now. Get to uh provide for your family is incredible. But for now I'm just going to let my agent and the organization handle that. >> Sam, is there a sense of purpose you feel with this group coming in after missing the playoffs last season? >> Of course. Yeah. I think going 15-2 the year prior, winning the division, um you know, getting the one seed and then fourth place in the division, nine and eight, missed the playoffs. Uh the drastic drop off in production and the wins. Um I think it's definitely like a motivating factor for us and I think you can see it um today honestly like we're flying around. The conditioning test was crushed yesterday. Um I got to sit back and watch the vets. I ran it the other day, so I got that out of the way. [laughter] Um, but yeah, like I think guys are in incredible shape right now. We're all very motivated and this group is hungry. >> You mentioned Dan said earlier today in the press conference to us that there's a little bit of a newness. Did you sense that a little bit of a youth movement? I mean, obviously you're now kind of one of the establishments of this group. What do you see as far as that newness? >> I mean, every year it's a new team. There's fresh faces. It's exciting to have Drew in the building. you know, Shep's a secondyear coordinator now, a lot of trust in him. So, I think there's there's trust to be built, a lot of opportunity for guys and um I think it's an exciting spot right now for the Detroit Lions. You talked about coming in and guys crushing the test, you know, do you think early on, like now that you have a chance to look back last year, like you guys set the tone early enough last year, like what what do you think you guys can change to, you know, not get off to the get off to a better start? Yeah, I looking back from the nine or 10 games that I played in, I think situational football certainly could have been better. And that's really where you get wins in this league. Playing better on third down, the red zone, converting on fourth, short yardage. Uh, I think the defense would reiterate the same thing to their side of the ball. So, I think that's the first step in us becoming a great team again, and we'll obviously address that throughout camp. >> You mentioned guys, >> you mentioned opportunities. He's sitting in the tight end room with Jackson Lee now. I mean, just like what have you seen out of him and his organ like what he brings to the >> Yeah, >> I remember transitioning from wide out to tight end in college and it was a big jump. Um, very excited for me cuz he's an incredible athlete. We keep urging him to understand like playing tight end, you're going to lose some battles to bigger, stronger, longer guys. and um it's unfortunate, but you got to pick yourself up out of the dirt and do it again. So, I think he has a lot of room to grow. Again, incredible athlete and uh very high ceiling as a tight end. >> Do you kind of remember the moment that you had that in college? Is it against a teammate or >> Yeah, AJ Anessa throughout fall camp in college would just like throw me into the dirt and Tristan Worfs would trample me soon after. So, that was a lot of fun to have like size 16 or 17 cleats from Worfs in your back um as like an 18-year-old kid. So that was probably my moment. I think he'll have plenty of those unfortunately, but it's only going to be better for him. >> Day one being back. Just what's it like with this group again? >> H feels good. I was joking around with the guys in the spring. I was like, I see you two days later. Um two days from now when OTA's ended and it just it flew goes by so fast. Um but excited to be back, excited to get back to work. Um even today, short practice, no pass, but you can see the competitiveness out of everybody out there. Uh it feels good. Weather is good coming from Florida, so this right here feel like winter to me. So, uh, feel really good. Like I said, super excited and, um, you know, ready for it to be a great camp. >> How are you embracing obviously in a an increased role this year, being, you know, in the nickel sets this year, being a guy that might play, you know, close to 100% of the snaps. >> Yeah. Um, a day at a time. Um, you know, I go back and I watch film on, you know, Alex and how he did things, his technique, uh, what made him a great player. Um, it's just kind of mimic that. Um, and be the best I can be. Uh, learning each and every day. I know it's a it's kind of the role of going from, you know, Sam to Will. You know, it's one of the thing, it's an adjustment, but, um, I've been doing it since I've been here. Um, so I wouldn't say it's easy. It's a lot lot of things to learn for sure, but um, you know, it's not foreign to me. Um, I'm super excited for the role and for the challenge. Um, got to come out here and earn it every day. That's why I told myself um, I just take I want to take myself back to, you know, when I first got here and how I had to, you know, work my way up to to be where I am. And um and that's just my mentality all camp and the whole season is I got to earn it each and every day, which I will. Um but I'm super excited for the role. Um you know, it's I'm learning a lot from um you know, obviously from Jack who've been out there playing Nickin uh base, learned a lot from Shep, a lot from Ham, uh Dave Caro, um a lot all those guys in the room. So, you know, they're they're going to get prepared to be able to do it. So, >> Dan spoke about getting back to 21, 22, getting back to the basics. At what point do you feel like you got away from that? I mean, obviously you guys had a lot of success with it. >> Um, if >> you all get away from that, how do you get back to that as a team? >> I think that I feel like we we didn't get away from it. Uh, I think that's kind of, you know, kind of downplaying, you know, the way we work. I would just say that, you know, sometimes things can get complacent and I don't think that we ever did, but, you know, in the in the image of the outside world, it's probably probably what people see, but it's not what it is. Just getting back to the basics. I remember when I first came in here, it was just hard-nosed football. It still is. is in all the years I've been here, it's still been hard nose football, but just getting back to our technique, being sound and getting back to what we do. Uh, bringing back oldfashioned football and that's, you know, ready to hit and ready to go out there and compete. Um, and bring the thumb to our opponents. You know, that's what, you know, Den has installed in all of us since I've been here. Um, and just basically just getting back to the bases, getting back to who we are and our identity. Um, I'm super excited about it. You know, you can tell just the the emotion and the and the things on Dan's face that he's ready to go and that just if that doesn't get you going as a player, then you know, something wrong with you. But um I'm super excited and I'm ready to get back to the the the small minute details for sure. So >> you guys have come in as the hunters and then it kind of shifted quickly after you made it to the NFC Championship game to being the hunted. Where does it stand now with this team and the mentality as you go over this season after missing the playoffs last year? >> I think that every team know when they come to come play the Lions that they have to bring it. I think that mentality hasn't left. Um, and you know, and we're and and when we play you, we going to make sure that you feel it. And you know, Dan said something about, you know, we want to make teams feel like if they if we do lose, and not saying we will and we won't, but if we do, they got lucky. Um, and um, and that just let you know everything you need to know right there. I mean, I feel like it feel good to be teams want to come in and give us their best. Um, that just makes us better, makes us even hungrier and and really starving to be able to play against those teams. But, um, I'm super excited. Um, I know the team is super excited to get back to what we do and, you know, and and we're ready to, you know, dominate the season. So, >> how much of an additional hunger is there having missed out on the tournament last year, as Dan likes to call it? >> Yeah. Uh, you can feel that energy inside the building. Um, we're not accepting nothing nothing less than than what we what we know we what we are. Um, and guys will get left behind if you're not here to to work and get better each and every day. um and and build that that that trust in in the coaches and the players, then you just won't be here. Um, so it feels good. Obviously, it's competitive guys out there trying to make the team and become starters. So, um, you know, even though we're competit uh competing with each other, we're also, you know, picking each other up and and this is a true brotherhood in that room. So, yeah. >> Got a chance to start six games last year, play really well, six starts. A little different this year coming through a season with an opportunity to play a much bigger role than that even it seems. Just how excited are you for that opportunity to to kind of win that number two spot and play a huge role in this defense? >> Just looking forward to competing with these guys, man. Coming out every day, you know, competing against the offense, competing with the guys in our room, you know, we're all fighting for, you know, opportunities to play and uh to make this team. Campbell was saying as well, he addressed all about, you know, the Terry situation as a team. TA I mean just um uh from what I know of TA man just a really good dude um a young guy um that I have a lot of you know love and respect for um he's going through a hard time right now I don't know I don't I'm not I don't know any specifics or anything like that but you know um definitely going to miss him definitely going to miss him >> what have you noticed maybe different re-energized of Shep heading into into year two in that in that position >> definitely just you know his um that was last year was his first year being a coordinator so him coming into year two you know more experience you know, definitely more energy. He had energy last year, though. But, um, just coming out, you know, just just, you know, really growing and, you know, coming to himself as a as as a coordinator in this league. >> What was your big focus this offseason? You've been doing this obviously a long time, but where was an area that you maybe saw, uh, this is something focus >> Just wanted to get more comfortable with the defense. Um, how important is this time of year to get that chemistry with the safeties as as they're kind of working things out there? extremely important, you know, on the field, also in in in in the classroom, you know, um talking to different guys, asking guys how they see certain things, you know, um their perspective on certain calls and certain routes and certain route combinations, you know, understanding how they're going to play certain things. And then that, you know, helps me to play faster, helps, you know, the corner to play faster. Whenever you know where safety is and the corner and the safety knows where the corner is and where he's going to be, we all can play faster and, you know, play as one. >> How important is it to have a couple veterans back there? >> It's really nice. It's really nice, you know. Um, it's really it's been refreshing playing with those guys. All those guys, man, they're all they're all vets. I'm going to miss him as a as a teammate and as a you know, somebody who whose locker was next to mine. So, I'm definitely going to miss him. He's going through a hard time right now. You know, I wanted to be able to just go out there and I want to be able to make the points in my head. You know, things just to be automatic. And, you know, we're still working to that point. I'm sure there's plenty on there that I need to improve and, you know, try and write everything down and be better on that the next day. And I'm sure uh Ben Barts was telling me, he said it's everything keeps popping up like gophers and you just got to keep whacking each gopher like every everything that comes up and you know eventually you'll look back at yourself and uh you know you you'll see that you become a whole different player and you know that that to me is very satisfying and in being a better player you're that much better of a teammate. What was it like now as training camp begins to be in the room with him as he's given one? >> Uh, yeah. I mean, it's, you know, it gives you goosebumps a little bit. How much personal responsibility do you feel in fixing that? >> I mean I feel it's you know as any player you know it's it's a it's a duty to your team duty to God duty to your family. whoever it might be, you have a duty to be the best player that you can be. title: Dan Campbell Press Conference | 2026 Training Camp Day 1
text: You know, we we uh guys really did a hell of a job, man. Uh we Everybody made their weights um and passed conditioning tests. We looked good all but one guy. Um so, ready to go. Obviously not pads today. We'll work them up. We're in acclimation. This is uh hour and a half practice. Um but but we're really ready to go. So, you know, it's hard to believe we're in year six um for us. Guys are excited. Coaches are excited. Um And so, so it begins. So, I'm going to open this up. Is Paul in here? >> Nope. >> The one day? Dude, unbelievable. I was going to give her the first question. Okay, all good. All good. This is like the one day she's never made it. Okay. No worries. Um Okay, questions. >> We start with the the five injury guys. I think we probably expected Branch of of all of them, but but the other four, where's where's Kirby at for you in terms of being ready at some point this camp? And then the other three, um Izien, Mahogany, and Conklin, uh any long-term concerns with with any of those guys? >> Okay, Kirby it it'll Everything that I told you in the spring is still applies to that. You know, we're still We've been working to this, but we're still in this Okay, he's starting to He's running on ground, man. We're starting to do change of direction some of this, but we're really We're not going to grind this for another two or three weeks, man. So, I cannot give you a true answer. He's working his tail off. He's not really had a vacation. He's been here with our guys busting his tail. Uh so, he's putting in the work. He feels pretty good right now. We're but there We got a long way to go and we there is still an unknown. But But I like where he's at. We like where he's at. Branch is is doing well. Um you know, he he's going to we obviously PUP, there's no setbacks. Um Take it as it comes. And we'll see. I'm sure late training camp, maybe maybe early September you can start practicing. We'll see. But he's doing well. Um Who else? Izzy just had a little flu bug. We're going to make sure he's good to go. Hopefully by Friday we get him in practice here. Um Mahogany needs a couple of days and then he'll be ready. Um who else? Oh, Conklin. Conklin's going to probably be about 2 weeks here, somewhere in there. He's running. You know, he got a little calf back in the spring. We're hopeful, no setbacks. We're trying to be smart with him, you know, but hopefully get him back as soon as possible so we can we can get some reps on him. Am I missing anybody? I think that's it, right? >> Curby is it um How much What is sort of the plan of when you want to get him out or when you think you need to get him out before camp to give him that balance of getting ready but seeing if you you know, seeing how much he can do. >> Well, I've already To me, if we got him back for the first game, that that would be a bonus. I mean, that would be a like woah, okay. I don't expect that. I'm not looking for that. I feel like he's more on the Branch plan a little bit. And that's is if everything goes well and everything goes according to plan with him and and we got everything on our side. But he's doing well. >> And the other you know, issue of the off season. Obviously you guys made the decision to part ways with him. Can you just address that and why why you decided to go that route and what changed from you know, the last time we asked you about him? >> Yeah, so I addressed the team last night over that, you know, it it's it's stinks. You never want to let go of a player. Especially somebody that you've been around for for a here and you drafted and all that and uh it's unfortunate that we made the move we felt was best for us. >> Is there any concern with you know filling that spot and some of the guys you got as far as filling that second spot? >> No, I you know, we're fired up. Look, it's it's one we got Branch back. We went and got McReary. We knew we'd get Rakell back off injury. you know, we drafted Abney. You know, certainly Dorsey's back. So, you know, Ironside's is back. We We feel pretty good in that room with the competition and those guys between veterans, young guys and uh and uh ability. >> You guys are pretty good about rewarding your top guys, you know, rewarding all the top guys. Obviously you got some extensions coming up. Jahmyr Gibbs is kind of the the talk of the off season a little bit. Is there any concern that that uh might lead over into any anything at all or is that something you guys want to do sooner than later or just what's what's kind of the update on his situation? >> No, I would say um of course we you know, you guys know how we feel about Gibbs um and all of our guys, LaPorta, Branch, all you know, um and so we'll we'll take this as it comes. This is uh you know, this will this will kind of continue. It'll It'll come as it comes. I think that's the best way to say it. And so, you know, this is uh this is both both sides working through something and and uh and we'll take it as it comes, but um that's where it is. >> And obviously you guys did a lot of revamping on your offensive line. Um how soon do you think you'll know what you have there, how it lines up and are you confident it will be significantly better than last year's? >> It's uh yeah, well Joe, it's a good question. Um I wish I could tell you we're going to know within three or four days, you know. I know this, we we got four days before we even get the pads, you know, so there's there's a week that you're not going to truly know. Um you know, so so you don't know. I know this as fast as we can get them in the secondary to work together. You know, okay, these are the guys. Now, we need them to work together and get as many reps as we can. So, look, we're trying to get We're trying to figure this out as fast as we can. It's pretty exciting, really. It really is, you know, cuz there is There's a lot of unknown. And but we really like the guys in the room. And uh and we feel like it's uh it's kind of like we just talked about with the DBs. It It's a good veteran group and Samarius, but yet young guys that are unknown, unproven. They got an opportunity. Um so, yeah, I feel like what what comes out of that room, those five, is going to be uh is going to be better than what we had last year. It's going to be an upgrade, and not just a little. I believe that. >> And McCreary, um you you talked about him as kind of nickel first guys when they first got in the building. Does >> I'm sorry. >> Ebner and McCreary. Does Does the plan change at all with them? I know you talked about the ability to flex outside. Is there an early camp plan to maybe see what you got there just in light of, you know, shifting personnel at the cornerback? >> Well, they will take some outside reps. You know, McCreary's played out Look, so has Ebner in college. Now, I know he just stepped in the our building, but but they'll take some of those outside reps. We still want to, you know, let them sink their teeth into some of this nickel. And look, we're going to let Raik Straw take a little nickel, too, on some of this stuff and and see where it is. But but all those guys got to be prepared to go outside. Um you know, the guys we know who will stay outside right now are are Reed and Rock, you know? And then those other guys need to be able to Let's see if they can do some stuff inside. >> With Raik Straw >> it seems like the the staff has been pretty steadfast that he's an outside corner. Just what have you seen from him in your first 2 years that makes you think that that's where he will stick eventually? >> Well, I There again, the injury uh just kind of the injury history with him has not allowed us to really see everything that he can do. But we know that's where he he banked a lot of reps in college was outside. you know, he look, he's got excellent feet, his hips, um just man, his change of direction, he's got ball skills, he can track the ball down the field. So, there there's just things that that you know, he's got about him and there's a natural ability to him um that that you feel like is conducive to playing outside. And that's probably that's probably where he'll he'll have most of his time. But yeah, let's see what he can do inside, too, you know. Look, he's going into year three. although he hasn't banked a ton of reps, it's just man, there there's you begin to mature and you grow and we feel like just from what he is internally, I'm not talking about the football player, but just you do. You you you know, you mature, you grow, you learn, you And so, we're pretty excited for him this camp to see what he's got. >> All the drives that you have into all [clears throat] the drives that you have into this facility, all your first days, I think you've said excited, you know, 10 15 times already, which we expect and you you should be. But what makes the excitement for this year, this first day unique? >> Man, I I don't it's just I don't know. This feels like there's a little bit of a transition. Like this is a it's uh there's a newness to it, you know. Um and there's a reset on on you know, it's a little bit like, okay, we still have our core crew, you know, the guys that that you guys know that have been here since '21. And then we stacked on top of that. Um but then we made some moves here, you know, particularly this year, this offseason. And so, it it's there's a newness to it. There's there's a little bit of a youth movement um that's up to us to get these guys developed. Uh, and that's that's pretty exciting, but also knowing, man, I want to get back to what we did in '22 a little bit, you know, and summer '21, probably more '22, but just get back to the basics of what we are. And so, that's exciting. That's exciting. And to know you're cutting these guys loose, these guys that were puppies at one time, it's all theirs now. It's all Saints and Souls and Hutch and Jack and you know, that's exciting. >> Hey, I just want to say >> I got you. >> You [clears throat] got me? Okay. >> I got Oh, okay. Uh, so the other day Kirby Joseph uh, tweeted about Jackson Meeks and said that was somebody that you need to watch out for and it seems like there's a transition for him from wide receiver to tight end. Do you see this as like a um, hybrid situation where he could maybe turn a 12-13 personnel play into an 11 just by going into motion, that sort of thing or or is it you know, where do you see him and his role? >> Yeah, I I think that's that's what we want to find out. We want to find out if if um, if there's something in there that that he could be kind of this hybrid, you know, H-back tight end, big slot, you know, big skill. Um, felt like his skill set is can be showcased better at this role, at this position. You know, asking things that he does well. Now, look, he's going to have to do some dirty work. There's there's no there's no way around it. Uh, in training camp for the reps, preseason games, but there's things that that we'll ask him to do to see if he can do it, you know. And we just felt like this was this gives him the best opportunity to be the type of player that he can be, but also maybe help us see if there is something there. So, yes, absolutely. >> Uh, Dan, obviously today's a beautiful day, but when it is really like hot, humid like it was a week or two ago. How do you balance getting the work in with player safety? And since you started playing and through coaching, like what's the biggest thing you've learned about you know, training in the heat? >> Yeah, well, we haven't had to do it. I mean, look, where I came from New Orleans as a coach last and I mean, we we did everything outside and and we practice early in the morning. Look, we practice early here. So, even if it is a hot day, most of the time you're you kind of avoid it here. Um but I think the the thing to keep in mind is, man, I I am so conscientious of that and and being smart uh with our guys, understanding what we have to do. But then, remembering back to two-a-days and 3-hour practices at 3:00 in the afternoon, you know, and and it was like, dude, you're you're getting 50 reps in the morning and you're getting 40 in the afternoon and by the way, you're not warming up or stretching. You better be ready to go. We're not going to waste 10 minutes on stretch for 3-hour practice. We got too much to do. So, not saying we're doing that. You can't do that anymore, but don't forget, man, the body can go. The mind controls the body. You can do more than you think you can do. These guys are in damn good shape and now we got to get them in football shape and and we'll work them to that. >> Hey Dan, you made a decision yet about playing the starters in preseason? I know during the last camp you said you were thinking about it more. Have you decided yet if you're going >> No, not I mean, look, I would like to, you know, but there again, this thing moves as we get through um get through these practices, you know, what do we look like? Who needs work? Then, do they need to play together? Um you know, is or are there players that aren't getting enough intensity in practice, you know? And the only way to get them there is they have to play preseason games or we got to go live or you know, so we'll work around that stuff. Um right now, I I like to, but but we'll see how it goes. >> Thank you sir. >> Okay. >> [music] [music]
