And maybe that's the par of the norm for any herniated disc injury that requires surgery, but it definitely resonated with me like just how severe and um like uncertain this this outlook was for Sam after surgery. So, to eventually get that full strength back, obviously, was very freeing, very liberating for him. And then, the other thing that stuck out to me about Sam today was he was talking about how the Lions can reestablish themselves as the contenders they were in '23 and '24. And he said it starts with situational football. And he mentioned four areas. He said, you know, we got to play better on third down. We got to convert more on fourth. We got to be better in the red zone. And we got to be better in short yardage. And those are relevant coming from Sam because those are four areas of the offense in which he is deeply involved. He has a a real impact on the field in all areas of those games. And he's right. He's absolutely right. In 2024, I didn't get a chance yet to look up short yardage. Maybe one of you guys can. But in 2024, the Lions were fourth in the NFL on third down. They were seventh on fourth. And they were third in the red zone. And that was obviously with a healthy Sam LaPorta and a fully healthy offense. Last year, they fell to 20th on third down, 15th on fourth, and eighth in the red zone. So, a regression in all of those categories, and I would bet those regressions were even sharper when LaPorta was out for the final, what was it, 10 or not eight, nine games. So, getting him back alone, I think should help those should help solve those issues right away. >> I don't need to say anything again about the numbers with and without LaPorta. I mean, I think illustrated it pretty clearly last week. They were last in the NFL in tight end production in the weeks that he was out and by a significant margin. So, getting him back is is obviously huge. I appreciated, I guess, the the personal touch to Sam's session today, you know, just listening back to it and, you know, expressing that fear, you know, kind of making light of of it a little bit in hindsight and and joking around with the comments you you mentioned with his his um his partner. Uh I think just adds an important layer of humanity that sometimes gets lost both media and fan base with these these players and I don't think I realized how extensive, I guess, the the nerve stuff was. I think we knew herniated disc and I've never had any of that, but a really good friend and and my wife have both dealt with um you know, herniated disc kind of dipping into the spinal columns and what that does to nerves and, you know, the way it's kind of been explained to me like when the nerves are are agitated in that way and causing pain, like the the reaction of them is to turn off, you know, and just to and you lose feeling in whatever body part that extends to often, you know, legs, sometimes arms, whatever it is, and some nerves don't turn back on. Like, they die. And so, it's it's really understandable that, you know, as Sam's probably Googling, as we all do when we have medical conditions and reading the the horror stories like I I understand why he panicked, you know, the friend I mentioned like he has no feeling in his foot. He has drop foot and he's had it since college. Um and that's that's crazy. Like to never regain your your ability or your strength in your ankle to ever have that again. Uh that ended your career as a football player. And so um I don't think people fully appreciate how good Brett Fisher is, the the Lions director of sports performance. I know they get a lot of criticism for uh some of their their injury issues which I I still would contend is largely bad luck, but the way people in that building talk especially people that were there pre-Brett Fisher and post-Brett Fisher, the way they talk about him, the way he builds out plans uh long-term and short-term for rehab and maintenance uh was really really critical for a guy like Frank Ragnow to to get past his darkest days of his career and and get the best out of himself again towards uh the end of that career like is extremely valuable to the Lions getting these players back and you know, I I think it's really good. I think Sam looked a little rusty today, but that's to be expected, right? Like you're uh you've had a long layoff and you got to get back into the flow of things and I I have no doubt by the time week one rolls around he'll be uh close to if not at peak performance. >> Yeah, well said Justin. And if you want a good laugh, go go watch the Porters press conference and go to the very end when he's talking about how Jackson Meeks might learn that you sometimes get beat as a tight end and Sam was talking about how he learned that lesson at Iowa trying to block A.J. Epenesa and then what happened with Tristan Warfs trampling over him after almost every snap. But yeah, it was fun to see a a light-hearted human side of Sam again, kind of the Sam that we got to know as a rookie. >> Did you not think, oh, that's where your back issue started when you got stepped on repeatedly by Tristan Worth?" >> No kidding. >> Well, I do to kind of close out the show here. Will, you you got to break down the the R&R. I mean, we talked about it in the group chat, but I'll give you the floor here. >> Yeah, so we as we do every year, this morning recorded our Fox 2 Lions training camp special, which will air on Fox 2 tonight at 7:00 in 21 minutes in fact. So, make sure you sit down and watch that. As a little tease, I want to I want to take you guys inside something that Dan told us that I think he intends to tell the team, but he hadn't yet as of this morning. And it sounds to me like a little bit of a team motto for 2026. I know Dan isn't necessarily huge on those, but I think last year's was what, hunting season? And the year before that was was we want more. Well, we were talking to him this morning and I think it was Woj. Of course, it was Woj. He asked him if he's feeling the heat from the outside or any pressure after last year's 9 and 8 last place season. Honestly, a perfectly reasonable question. And Dan said among other things that my you know, the pressure or heat from me comes from letting players down. You know, that's that's where it always stems from. It's nothing about job security or outside noise. But he eventually went on to say, "I haven't told the team this yet, but man, I want some R&R." And you're like, "What are you talking about?" And he says, "Man, redemption and respect." He said, "That's what this league's about. You want to make your mark. That's the type of team that you got to be and you got to do things a certain way. So, you know, he says, 'I feel pressure not internal not externally, but internally. Like from myself to get us back to where we need to go.'" And I mentioned Colton the the mentality comment in wanting to sort of reprise the Lions identity from '22-'23. I I I also asked him about that and and how he wants that to show up. How does he want that to manifest itself in training camp, obviously, and then over the course of the season? Cuz make no mistake, dude, these guys are going to go at each other in camp. No joint practices, they want to control the the the tempo and the heat of of of the these next 5 weeks, and I think Campbell's going to crank it up pretty good. And he said that like the undergirding all of that talk about getting back to who they are is we are not going to beat ourselves. Like that is the focal point. And he's like, you got to be very disciplined to practice like that if you want to play like that. And he also said, "I want teams to know, if you're going to beat us, you better have the horses A, and B, you're going to need about 20 things to go your way. That's the mentality," he said, Cole. And he said, "Um of course we want to win the division, we want to make our mark in the playoffs. Of course we want a Super Bowl, but if we go back to what it was, what I started with." He said it was you you're going to know that you played us, and you don't want to play us again. And if you do beat us, it's because you feel like you got lucky. If we do that and get back to that," he said, "everything else will handle itself." So it's it's sort of a combination of that violent, nasty, relentless play style that those guys were able to summon based on their backgrounds in '22 and '23, and this idea of playing more cleanly, more crisply. That also evaded them last year, and um you know, I think it was reflected sometimes in offensive line penalties. That's part of playing a more disciplined brand of football. So as much as he wants this team to to get back to its meanness, he also wants it to get back to its its cleanness. And I think if they can do those things, that's when teams will feel like, yeah, we need everything to go our way this week to beat this team. >> It sounds like it's rubbing off on the players. I mean, just listening to LaPorta talk today and mentioning like the situational football and the things we need to do kind of between the margins to get better and you know, not beat ourselves like like they did it last year. Sounds like that message is already being received by the players. And one thing that stood out when you said that, you said you having the horses and needing like 20 things to go your way, that got them pretty far a couple years ago when they went to the NFC Championship game. The 49ers not only had the horses, but they literally needed 20 things go their way to prevent the Lions from getting to the Super Bowl that year. So, if that's sort of the the type of season we're talking about based on this new mentality and maybe the you know, renewed um, you know, winning between the margins, like that sort of mentality. >> You combine that, you can have, you know, pretty good year and you know, set yourself up for playoff success in ways that that obviously wasn't there last year and the year before. So, um, if it works out that way, man, you could have something pretty special on your hands. >> Did we uh, we come up with the name for Kyle's next beer at Dog and Pony? >> Oh, respect and redemption. I like it. Well, he could do it, too. One could be respect and one could be redemption, but you could only have one if you order the other. It it has to be a package deal. >> No, that that would be like >> Like a black and tan. >> Yes, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah. >> It could be a layered beer. [laughter] >> No. >> Kyle, are you listening to this? >> Oh, he is. >> Kyle knows the respect and redemption for me when I go to Dog and Pony Show Brewing. The The night I'm drinking is the respect, and then I wake up and the next day's redemption. >> I'm going back. >> Yeah, we can do that. >> They thought they got me. So, uh, Kyle knows all about that. Shout out to him, man. Uh, we I got to get back out there, actually. I'm going to go up there with him soon. So, shout out to Kyle, man. >> Oh, nice. >> Dog and Pony Dog and Pony Show Brewing. >> I got to get me some Colonel Lagers. I'm a little bit short right now. I got to go get some. >> Yeah, me, too. I'm low, too. And they go quick, you know? It's easy. They're good drinking beer. >> Yeah, well, you have some friends over, everyone's getting Colonel Lagers, good times, you know? And and yeah, I got to I got to hit up Kyle again. We got to get back up there. Got to make it happen. >> I uh, I really quickly want to just make a a point about redemption cuz I I do think it starts with Dan Campbell. Um, and it I look back at the John Morton hire and I know I'm going back and and replaying something that's that's old and been talked about, but like that that's arguably and and maybe not even arguably Dan's biggest mistake in in this job was that hire. And I think he got a little locked in on that hire. I think very similar to the way that Bob Quinn got very locked into the Matt Patricia hire, right? Like it just he had eyes for one guy and couldn't see maybe some of the the the pitfalls that possibly would come with that. And look, he he corrected obviously very quickly and and pulled the reins back from uh the play calling reins back from Morton, but I it was almost too late, right? And so you lost that season because of it and I'm a big fan of the the Pessen hire. I, you know, we'll we'll see how that plays out, but I feel like that was kind of the start of the redemptive arc of this team was fixing that and then extending to Brad. He got put in a little bit of a tougher spot with the Ragnow retirement, but fixing that offensive line, you know, you've got an offense that I mean, statistically didn't take the hugest step back, but like talking about that situational football again, right? Like the third downs, the uh the key plays at the key times, like it just wasn't there. The the efficiency of the ground game just wasn't there. And so when I look at redemption of this team, I to me it starts with the redemption of this offense. I I think the unit's going to be really good this year. I have a lot of faith in the moves they made. Um, and so you you pile that into everything we've talked about, the mentality, and I think that's kind of the heart of where them getting back to where they are were comes from for me. >> Yeah, I'll I'll leave you guys with this Campbell quote also from our Fox 2 show. Go watch it. It starts at 7:00. Go watch it. It starts at 7:00. It's on Fox 2. You can stream it, too. As as understated as as Dan has been this offseason for good reason, he is determined. You you can really feel it when he speaks to to sort of reestablish the Lions into this juggernaut. And he said today about 9 and 8, it eats at you and it comes in waves. He said there is an embarrassment to it and I'm responsible for that. And I'm going to be one of the ones responsible for getting it back to where it needs to be. So, look, obviously a long long way to go. Everyone's hopeful and optimistic on the first day of camp, but um I was definitely struck today at the podium and then during our show at Dan's like adamant intentions to restore the Lions to what they were and who they were over the first three years of of their contention phase. >> Those are some bars right there. All right, Dan. >> Right, dude. He was going at it. I was like, "Just take the mic." >> No doubt, bro. No doubt. >> I love it. Uh again, big big shoutout Kyle, Dog and Pony Show Brewing. Shoutout to PrizePicks. Again, all you people that tune in every single week and support the channel. Uh we will be back next week. I know we kind of stay fluid, you know, we got training camp. So, if there's ever a change, you guys will be the first to know. Uh but until next week, we will catch you all. >> Peace. >> [music]

title: Jordan Love: 'There's always a lot of excitement, lot of energy on Day 1'
text: Jordan, does it always feel like first day of school, something like this for training camp? >> It does. Um, you know, it's one of those things where it's just a lot of excitement. Everybody's uh happy, happy to be back together, get back on the field. Um, obviously we get the fans out there now at practice, so uh there's always a lot of excitement, a lot of energy on day one. Um, and it's it's just fun to be playing ball again and be back with the guys. >> Jordan, you had some offensive line movement last year. What would it mean to get a group of guys like I know there's still have a couple guys out, but if you get a group of guys that stays at the same spot and work together, what does that do? >> I mean, that's huge. That's that's what you want. Um, you want to be able to have just that continuity where you're playing with the same guys throughout the season. Obviously, we know injuries, things like that happen throughout the season, but uh it's always a goal to be able to try and be the healthiest team. Um, and like you mentioned, just a lot of moving parts in the O-line past couple of years, guys, you know, having to play multiple positions throughout the season. Um, I know that's a challenge. It's a challenge on a lot of guys, especially when you go from like the left side of the line to the right side, so uh I think for those guys, if they can stay in one spot throughout the whole season, that's when you're at your best and I think we'll be able to um build on a lot of areas. Um, but obviously, we'll we'll see what happens. Things happen throughout the Um, so you want to have guys that, you know, have experience playing different positions and can step in whatever their name's called. >> Jordan, you said in your camp a few days ago that you just love the group that you have. What most excites you about this specifically? >> Yeah, a lot. Um, just looking at around at each kind of position we have. We got a lot of playmakers, a lot of guys that uh also have been here and been in this system. And uh we've we've played a lot of ball together. So, especially in the receiver room, um tight end once we get Tucker back. So, uh there's a lot of things that just, you know, you get excited about. It's not your first time going out there and playing with these guys. Uh so, we get some stuff to just continue to build on uh some of the last seasons we've had. >> When you see Tucker running full speed, hitting the pads, you know, only what is it, 9 months after post ACL tear. What comes to mind for you? >> No, you get excited obviously seeing seeing that type of stuff. You know, you got to you know, kind of temper those those things because you know, it's still process. You know, you're coming off a very serious injury. Um you want to make sure he's back 100% healthy. Um we could go on through the season cuz we'll need him for the full year. So, um you know, he's in a great spot. He's been he's been working all off season um to get to where he's at now. So, uh for him it's just staying ground. >> You were nothing. Now you're the longest tenured player in the locker room. This group just at this point, you know, where are you How do you feel comfort level being the quarterback of this group? Just you know, how are you feeling just leading this franchise? >> Yeah, no, it's crazy to think about for sure. Um hearing that, you know, I remember my rookie year when I got here I was literally the youngest guy on the team. Um you know, played with a bunch of older guys and obviously in a room with Aaron Rodgers. So, um you know, a lot has changed and I feel like the time has has kind of flown by in the 7 years. So, uh you know, it's it's different. You know, obviously a lot of a lot of faces, a lot of people have came came through the building and um it's been a lot of just kind of turnover. So, um you know, it's one of those things where you know, guys are now asking me for advice, things like that, which um is always part of the process, but it is definitely weird to hear that I'm I've been here the longest. Um it doesn't feel like that, but uh it's one of those things where you know, I'm I'm now at that point where I'm I'm trying to get these guys on the same page and and give as much advice as I can can't as I can. >> How is Josh Jacobs doing and what is it like to still have him out on the training camp field and everything? >> It's great having Josh out there. Um you know, we we know what type of player Josh is. So, I'll be able to continue keep building um as we start training camp. Um it's great. It's great having him there. >> I know you haven't gone against him a ton yet, but what are your early impressions of Brandon Facyson >> Yeah, um obviously OTAs we were we were watching him um and he he made a lot of plays out there. He did a lot of good things. Um you know, he is a very talented corner. Um so, I think he'll be getting some more reps. I'll be going against him a lot more during training camp and you know, I'm just excited to see the progression. You know, it's one of those things where camp and OTAs are one thing. So, you got to see how, you know, how guys play when we get to to live, but he's done a lot of great things. I'm excited to see how he keeps building. I think for him, for all the rookies really, it's just about, you know, trying to learn the playbook as fast as possible, be dialed in and and just understand the mentally what you got to do on each play. Because I think that's just the biggest challenge for for everybody because it's so new. But talent-wise, athlete-wise, you know, he's a great player. >> Jordan, I know it's only day one, but it looked like you already had some Adam moments with the defense today. Were you happy with how everyone on offense responded? It felt like you got the ball on pretty quickly. >> Yeah, no, it's great. You know, day one, you never know what to expect. And so, you know, we obviously had a red zone day today. Yeah, we made some some plays. We had a couple touchdowns early on. I think the last period, you know, wasn't as, you know, crisp as the earlier period. So, some stuff to clean up there, but I like it. Whenever you can score some touchdowns day one, you know, I think it just sets you off on the right track. Guys making plays. You'd like to see, you know, us hit the ground running from where we left off at OTAs and that's kind of how it felt today. So, day one, see how we keep building, but it's always about trying to find ways to just improve on the little things and just keep stacking days throughout camp. >> Jordan, what have you learned from past training camps that tells you what you need to get out of this camp and preseason? Like, what do you want to get out of it? >> Yeah, I mean, I think there's always goals you have as a player and then I think as a team it's just every day is a new install. Every day is new plays. So, it's staying on top of the playbook and being able to go out there, run the plays. Obviously, like I mentioned, kind of find, you know, okay, this look good versus this defense. This is where I need to go and just understanding what you need to do on each play and then trying to, you know, kind of flush all that and move on to the next day of install and and be able to just keep going each day and keep stacking stuff because, you know, once we get all the installs in is when we get to some of the move the ball periods and everything's in really. So, it's that's when it gets fun, but I think every day is just a new challenge of trying to just you know, get on the same page with everybody, make sure the timing's right, make sure we're all communicating the same way and just all seeing seeing stuff the same. >> Do these receivers come to you with questions or do you have to get after them like, "Hey, you know, if you've got a question, ask me. Let's let's talk about this." And then how's the progress with MG so far? >> No, it's great. Now, these these guys are great. I think as a receiver you you want to be on the same page with the quarterback. You want to get the ball as much as possible. So, anytime there might be, you know, we might be seeing stuff different, you know, we're talking right after the play, "Hey, this is what I saw right here. This is kind of what I want you to do." Vice versa. So, we're always talking after the play. It's nice when you get that little break and when the other group's kind of go, you can go back, we get the iPad right there, we can watch the play unfold and talk about things right there on the field, which is nice. And then we get back to the meeting room and talk about it again, but now all these guys are hungry. They want to they want to ask questions, make sure we're on the same page and that's how it's supposed to be. >> Jordan, go ahead. >> Earlier this offseason Matt talked about kind of breaking the offense down back to its base principles and building it back up. You mentioned running some new plays. How involved in that process were you this offseason? >> Yeah, you know, I think that's that's always the goal I think for the offseason, especially with coaches, you know, they're they're diving back into everything we ran the year before, seeing what works, seeing what might not have worked, and and just kind of [snorts] looking at what we did consistently at a high level. And you know, I think that's what Matt wanted to dive back into and really just continue to build our offense around the staple plays that we run because like I said, we we get into it in in OTAs and training camp where we're putting everything in and there might be some plays that you get in the season you're just not running that much. So, it's almost a waste of time to be running it during training camp and getting reps that we're not really going to be running. So, for him it's really just diving back in, seeing what we're going to continue to run and and building off that stuff. And uh Matt keeps me, you know, very involved in all that. You know, we talk so much throughout the off-season on uh this is kind of what we want to build on. These are the plays we might be taking out. What plays do I like? What plays do I not like? Um so, I got a good say in that, but I mean I'm I'm right there with him. There's a lot of stuff you you get into it so many years, you put so many plays in also throughout the season that you kind of just carry over for the next year, which are plays you might run only versus certain looks on defense. So, uh just really diving back into what works and and building off that stuff. >> Jordan, what was your reaction when you saw the devastation just down the road in Appleton and Nashville due to the tornado? >> Yeah, it was uh it was crazy. Um to see that uh to see, you know, the the videos coming after the fact of just the destruction um to a lot of people's houses, you know, it's it's very sad to see, obviously, with it being right there in Appleton, um right down the street from us. So, uh you know, thoughts and prayers are going out to everybody. Um it's just it's a it's a natural disaster that is just it's it's it's tough to see and tough that, you know, I know people are going through a lot. When you lose your house, you lose everything that you got in your house. Like uh that's a that's a tough situation. So, uh thoughts and prayers are with everybody down there. >> Gus was telling us that the only way to fix, you know, the the the end of game situations and how you guys have to be better at that is you have to be more intentional. How do you feel like you guys in this off-season have been more intentional about that? >> Yeah, I think those are things that it's tough because there might be instances where you you only practice some of these end of game plays maybe once or twice in certain situations. Um and they obviously come up in the game. Um so, it's it's hard to emulate sometimes these end of game situations. Um we try and do it all the time by doing two-minute drill. Um kind of put ourselves into some of these last-second situations to be able to get these plays off, but um I think it just comes down to everybody understanding what the situation is and having that intelligence to know what we're trying to accomplish as a team. Um, what So, we're all on the same page. Uh, we've had a couple of instances where, you know, you look back at the Cowboys game last year where, uh, you know, we barely got to playoff to be able to get the field goal at the end. So, um, just, you know, the operation of plays before leading up to those end of game situations is just so critical that you got to be on point. You got to execute at a high level and everybody's got to be on the same page. So, um, as much as we can, we try and emulate situations throughout practice throughout the course of the season, but uh, there's instances where you might be in a situation you've never practiced for and guys just got to be able to think for themselves and understand when we have that couple seconds in the huddle for me to be able to communicate kind of what the situation is and what we're trying to do. >> Jordan, is there mentality part of that too, though? Like a killer instinct, so to speak. And is that maybe a harder thing to develop than the situation type stuff that you're >> I don't think the killer instinct's the hard part. I think everybody's kind of got that. Everybody wants to win the game. We know what we're trying to do. We're trying to go out there to win the game. So, that's not the issue. I think it's more just understanding the situation and making sure everybody knows. Like in some of those situations, do I got to Am I trying to get out of bounds? Am I trying to get down to save as much time as possible? Running the ball in? Like all those little critical coaching points that we talk about that you just It's hard to get as many reps on. So, uh, I think the killer instinct part, I think everybody's got that and and we're all trying to go out there and win the game. So, that's the easy part. >> Jordan, you told us in the spring that Marshawn's nickname is the Heat Cannon. With With everything that he's gone through, I mean, does it does it put a smile on your face just to see him in the huddle with the ones, you know, getting getting some opportunities? >> Yeah, I don't remember saying that, actually. Um, I don't know who said that. Somebody else did. No, um, it it's awesome, you know, obviously, like I mentioned, that the goal for everybody is to stay healthy as possible. Um, you want to be on the field. You want to be available. That's how you get better. Um, so, when you're missing time, it's just tough. It's valuable reps you're missing. Um, and obviously, we know Marshawn's has gone through his fair share of of things. So, to have him healthy, to have him out there, is great. And obviously, once we get into preseason, going into the season, that's the guy we need to have out there because I know he's he's going to be a a special playmaker. He's somebody that can can make those big explosive plays in the run game and the pass game. So, I think for him, it's just trying to find ways. I know he's been working hard at it. He's just trying to find ways to stay healthy. >> What's your confidence level in Jordan Morgan now at full-time left tackle? >> It's good. I think for him, you know, him being able to stay in one spot. I know he's been moving around a lot. Guard, tackle, left side, right side. So, I think for him to be able to sit in the one spot, you know, back to what he That's the position he's most comfortable at, I believe. So, I'm excited. I'm excited to see him. Obviously, he's got some experience in the game. And now, to be the guy out there at left tackle, it's just about building on that stuff. And once we get to the season, just going out there and hold it down on my blind side. But, I'm excited for him. >> Jordan, when you first got out there, I counted 37 different secret handshakes. >> 37? >> 37. >> How important is the fun side of the culture in comparison to the focus? >> Man, that's important. I mean, we're here all day with each other. So, we get a lot of time to to spend with the guys. And you know, we talk about all the time as a team is just trying to have that bond with everybody on the on the team because you know, those are the most special teams when you want to play hard for each other. And you love being around each other. And you you really have that love for each other. It's easy to go out there and and have fun on the field every single day. So, makes it fun to come to work every day. But, you got to have some fun out there. You got to do the little things. You know, we make some handshakes just to you know, have those little moments we can we get with each other before we do run tracks. But, that's when you get to have a little bit of fun. Fans get to see that stuff. They like it. So, you know, we we enjoy it. >> How do you feel like you and Matt LaFleur's relationship has grown the most from when you first got here to now? >> I think it's grown the most in just understanding for me, understanding what we're trying to do as offense, what he's trying to when he calls plays, what his mindset is when so we're kind of thinking the same. And for him, understanding, you know, what I like, what I like what what what plays I like running. What I like when we're getting certain looks on defense. So, just that feel we have for each other where you're kind of in each other's head already knowing when he calls a play, already know what he's getting to. So, we can speak the same language, but I think that just comes from being together for a long time. Obviously, we're in the meeting room together. We sit right next to each other. And we have a lot of talks, just being able to bounce plays and ideas off each other. But, I mean, I think everything helps, you know, having him around, being with the same coach. I think he's a phenomenal coach and it's just about building on things we've done in the past and trying to be the best version of ourselves each day. >> Two more. >> How different is training camp feel this year now that you're a new dad? >> It feels a lot different. Out there, we there was a lot I was saying there's a lot of babies out there today. So, it's cool to see, but for me, you know, it's just knowing that I got, you know, a little one at home that, you know, eventually will be looking up to me and watching everything I do is definitely special. But, it's it's amazing. I love it so far. That's all I can say is it's been great. >> You get to stay at home for camp, right? >> We do, yeah. >> probably experienced the whole dorm thing, right? Cuz that was all virtual. >> Yeah, I never experienced St. Norbert dorms. When I got here rookie year, it was COVID, so we we stayed at home for the first couple of years and then we've been in the hotel for the past couple years. So, you know, we're a lot of be at home again, which is it's nice. It's nice to be able to sleep in your own bed. You can never beat that, so.

title: Devonte Wyatt describes emotions after signing contract extension
text: Who's the first person you called when you got off the phone? >> My mom. >> What was that conversation? >> I was like, "Mom, we made it." >> [laughter] >> I was like, "We made it." But yeah, I just told her I I just told her like, you know, I was I was I was able enough to get a uh extension and she was happy to hear that. I was too. >> The way you were playing before you got hurt was pretty high level. Can you What does it take to get back to that? And then what's the next step to get there? >> I mean I mean just being confident like, you know, don't I just say just being confident and going through this whole camp and and not trying to focus on the injury. Just, you know what I'm saying? I actually feel great like just doing the work I had out there, but I mean, I feel like it's back to normal. All right, so. >> Devante, do you do you feel like you feel any any more pressure than you did before? >> Nah, I mean nah, I mean it's reason why they you know, it's reason why they gave me the money cuz they know what I can do. So, I mean, so I just got to go out there and do my job really. That's it. No pressure at all. >> What was your What was your You mentioned calling your mom. What what was her reaction? >> She started screaming. >> She started screaming and crying and that's when I started crying. So, yeah, that was that was that was the that was her reaction. >> What what does that mean? When you think about the journey you've been on now, what what What does that hit you in terms of like the meaningfulness of it? I mean, it's it's obviously more than just money. It's kind of the >> Yeah, I mean, you just yeah, all the hard work I put in like, you know, just on the off season, going through the season, the the injuries, and you know, just stuff like that. Just knowing just knowing I still still able to get what I got is a blessing like no matter what it was. I was it's a blessing. >> Devante, it's a whole different What's it been like being a Green Bay Packer? >> I love being Green Bay. I don't Look, that's why I signed that deal cuz I don't want to be nowhere else but here. So, [snorts] I'm happy. >> You said you didn't know if the extension was coming. Going back to last Thanksgiving, how many doubts were there? >> man, that was the that was the lowest of my life like I ain't never I never had a major injury. Like this kind of was like my first major injury, so it was a I was definitely at the lowest like after that because I definitely was like the top three pro bowlers, like but it was just like after that injury it's just a lot just went down for me, but you know it's just coming through OTAs and the progression of my ankle is like amazing, so I feel great. >> What do you remember about the play? >> The play? >> Yeah. >> [snorts] >> I try not to remember it. So yeah. [laughter] I try not to remember it. But I mean it's football, things happen, so I can't I can't do nothing about it. >> Cuz that's one of those where it's like no doubt it's bad right away. >> Yeah, it's just I can't >> You know right away I'm guessing that >> Yeah, I was playing hard and you know it's just part of part of football. Like you just never know. Like that you can't you can't let that stop you though. >> What did they end up having to do or did they have to have to have something fixed? >> Uh like what they have to do to my ankle? >> Just a couple screws and bands and stuff like that, but it's back fully healed and it's bone looking good, so I'm happy. >> How do you feel now? >> I feel good. I actually feel feel great like flexible and still um it's feel it's it's feel normal. Like it don't feel like no injury or like nothing happened. Like going through the process, yes, but like now today it feel great. >> Is there a plan for when you might start doing team? >> Uh no, not yet. I don't I don't We got to talk to the uh training room staff about that. >> What is uh different or possible for you in a Jonathan Gannon defense? >> Uh just a lot of I mean just the the front like you I can play it all. Like I can go from nose to three to five to nine. Just being all over the field. Like so you just never know. And it's it's like a hard defense a hard front to block, so like it's going to have a lot of more a lot more one-on-ones, especially when we get Michael back, so it's going to be great for me. >> What what has Ziaire been like in your early time with him, especially since you're right next to him? >> very vocal. I like I like that like he's very vocal. He's, you know, a leader, definitely a and he, you know, he's a support he he he support me a lot. Yeah, he support the whole team actually. He's happy to be here and you could tell. >> How's it been with Hargrave, too? You know, kind of adding him into the mix with the guys. >> That's my guy, man. I learned a lot from Hargrave just power rushing wise and the vet the veterans the vet he the vet that he have in them and and he's just a great guy, a great funny guy and somebody just enjoy to be around. Like, I love him. >> Did you ever come across Solomon Thomas before this as far as getting >> No, I No, I always watch him on film and stuff. Like, I always just watch him on film. So, I never like my first time actually meet him in person.

title: Matt LaFleur: 'We got to show that daily improvement'
text: What're you looking for these first few days before you really get rolling? >> There's a lot of things we're looking for. First First off, just in terms of the energy that we bring each each and every day and like I told the team, I think it's a reasonable expectation that we we got to show that daily improvement. Um the urgency that how we how we uh approach everything we do. And so, um but I think the guys are excited and I know I'm excited um to get back out there and and ready to roll. >> As fans watch practice, they get used to watching two-minute drills, really competitive periods at the end of practice. But in in light of trying to finish more this year, will the fans notice anything in practice as you try to focus in on >> Well, I think I think there's a time and a place for all that. Um I always like to have a competitive period each and every day. I think just where we are as a team, I mean, you guys saw the the injury list for for opening day at camp is is pretty extensive. So, we're going to temper back on some of those competitive periods at least early on until we get the pads on. >> Now, how do you plan to handle the kicking competition? Will they kick the same days? Kick every other day? How how will they go head-to-head? >> Uh I think it's it's going to be the best way I could put that. It's going to be very fluid. Uh there could be some days where they both kick. Um you know, Cam's got a good handle on it, obviously. Uh with with Matt out there, it kind of throws a wrench in to some of the things we wanted to do. Um but, you know, yeah, it's there's always competition, whether it's a kicker, every position on the roster. Uh certainly, you know, we drafted Trey, so we we definitely have high hopes for him and understand that with all young kickers, there's typically some growing pains that are associated with that. But um yeah, just want to push him to be his best. >> Now, what was your reaction to D'Wayne getting that contract extension? >> Oh, I was super fired up. I mean, just it's always cool to see your guys get rewarded for the work that they put in. And it's not, like I told the team, it's not just just by the work you do on the field. It's your actions off the field and what what kind of teammate you are and I think he understands the responsibility that comes with that in itself and in terms of being a leader in that room and helping some of those young guys along. >> Trey isn't your first rookie kicker that you've coached. What have you learned from your past experiences, maybe with honors and Brandon, that might help kind of with the patience required? >> Well, I think every situation's a little bit different, but I I I think it just kind of tempers your expectation level a little bit and understand that there could be some some moments that that uh aren't favorable, but you just you got to live through it and um I think the talent we all see the talent. It's just, you know, can we harness that? And it's like every every player out there, you know, you just you got to have a level of consistency that's conducive to winning. >> And did the Musgrave thing catch you by surprise at all? And if so, how does that change, you know, where you are with your time out? >> Yeah, I I think so. Um but it is what it is. That those are the circumstances. All you All you can control is how you respond to those. Um so, I'm excited that it's going to be opportunities for these other guys to see what they can do and and how they can contribute. But certainly, you never want to see a guy as like he he's I know he he may not have the production um that certainly he wants uh up to this point in his career, but I do think that he's a I mean, he's he's got a legit um premier trait in terms of the speed and you got to account for that um on play. >> How is that why you dropped out of mini camp for this injury or is this something totally different? >> No, that's that's exactly why. >> That with Mike out, what do you want to see from that group in camp as they look to get their opportunities as well? >> Well, I think we all know what type of player Mike is. He's a game wrecker. So, I think again, it's other opportunities for other guys to showcase what they can do and there's a lot of youth in that group. Um, and some guys that have been here for a couple years that are just chomping at the bit to show what what they can do. >> How are you on your two rookies in that group, Chris McLaurin and De'Andre Houston? >> Yeah, I mean, we've we haven't seen these guys in pads. So, I think we all got to temper our expectations um, in in that regard, but I think early indications from uh, being in just shorts and a t-shirt have been have been positive. >> And you at the at the fall meetings you talked to those guys about there were some guys that were unhappy with their roles and it took its toll on your team. You're a player's coach. You seem genuine in wanting to have guys all feel like they're invested and have a role and are important to your team. You also can't have guys being ticked off. So, how have you kind of can you change your approach as a coach because you kind of are who you are and at the same time that you said that that was problematic. >> Yeah, I I think that um, I think role clarity is key. I think that that's our job as coaches. Like, "Hey, here's your role. If you if you want a bigger role, then you got to go out there and do it at the end of the day." So, that puts them onus on the players certainly they got to have their their opportunities whether it's in practice or in the those preseason games to start to establish themselves a little bit, but um, you know, it is what it is at the end of the day. Our job is to put the best out there to give us the the best opportunity to go win football games, and that's what we're going to do. >> But you don't you don't want to change who you are, right? Like there's a reason why guys went to bat for you with Ed last year after the season because they believed in you and the way you do your job. So you have to stay true to who you are even if there were some challenges from Ed. >> Yeah, 100%. I I I think that you are who you are, and certainly I I do take great pride in how we go about our business. It's not just me, it's it's everybody. It's but it it's how we communicate to the players, and then, you know, just be direct in terms of here's how we see it, and now it's on you to go if if you don't like that narrative that's been painted, it's on you to go change it. >> Matt, over your tenure as head coach, how much has training camp changed for you in your plans practices during COVID? You've had really veteran teams, really young teams. You've had a lot of injuries, and starting after this year. >> Yeah, I think every year you you got to evolve, and then and we talk about it all the time. It's either adapt or die. I mean, you can't control who's available, who's not available. Certainly the medical isn't in charge of that piece. and all you got to you have to adapt as a coach and try to make it work at the end of the day, and and our job is to push our guys and get a little bit better each and every day. >> Matt, are there any limitations or rep count on Marshall Lloyd in camp as he gets started? >> Not per se, but I think we have learned from our experiences. I I think we want to gradually get him more and more involved, and and and see where it goes. >> You know, speaking of Lloyd and and Oliver as well, been injured a bunch, healthy now. Do you have much of a feel for what you know those guys could give you on on Sundays, or is this It's month to kind of show you what they can do. >> I think it's it's going to be they they got to go out and prove it. And just the availability piece is as important as anything. Certainly, we've seen flashes from both those guys what they are capable of doing, but you got to be available in order to do go do that. >> Any concern with the Javon Hargrave injury or just him being on the physically unable to perform list to begin? >> Um no no long-term concerns. And he's a veteran guy that's you know, that's been through it. So, um certainly it it is new. I mean, it's a new place for him. And even he was telling JG, he's like the scheme's a lot different than it was when when we were together in Philly. So, yeah, there there's going to be a little bit of a learning curve, but uh nothing that's that's a long-term concern for for us right now. >> Does the uncertainty with Josh's situation in any way kind of affect how you treat Marshaun and Kevin? You got to make sure you have a running back in place for for the season, but you also obviously want to be cautious with him. >> Yeah, I mean, um yeah, I think more or less, it's I would say in regards to Marshaun specifically, it's how can we give him and increase his volume each and every day and and what we're we're allowing him to do at practice. >> Matt, your old DC, Jeff Hafley down there in Miami, made some headlines because he's incorporating live tackling into his procedures there. Did you ever lobby for that here and have you talked to Gannon about the possibility? >> No, he it's not surprising when you have a young roster, and certainly we've done some of that in the past. Um we did it shoot, going back to the the COVID year. Uh we had some live tackling situations in Lambeau uh to try to get some of those young guys. And when you have a young team, and you know, sometimes you just you take the gloves off a little bit and uh let it rip, but um you know, I think even last year we had I want to say on family night we had a live situation, so we'll sprinkle those in and it's more centered around our younger players to try to get them primed and ready to go cuz I mean, shoot, we'll be we'll be tackling in those live situations here in a couple weeks. >> Coach, what goes through your mind when you see the devastation just down the road in Menasha Appleton? And do you know if there are any plans for the Packers to help those victims? >> Yeah, that it's terrible. I mean, certainly never want to see it wherever it's at, but it it hits a little bit different, I would say, when it's closer to home. you know, it affected a couple of my close friends. Just they they had some some damage done to their their places and um it's sad to see and certainly I I would think that we'll do something as an organization. >> Matt, what does that do for you and the organization the way Tucker Kraft has come back? Like, Brian was just in here saying that we're going to see him sooner rather than later. He's on track just the way he's attacked his rehab. What How does that warm your heart, so to speak? >> Uh Tuck Tuck's a guy that he doesn't shy away from the work and he put the work in. I mean, he he always since the day he got here, he's he's been a worker. And he was here all summer grinding away to put himself in this position, so that'll certainly be a huge boost for our football team when he's available. >> All right. Last two, please. >> Matt, how excited are you for Jordan Morgan to kind of fill in at that left tackle role and solidify himself as a long-term option there? >> Yeah, I think he showed a lot of good things in the spring. I think he it's it's his most natural position. I mean, certainly he's got time on task throughout his college career there. Um but ultimately, like like I said before, I mean, you got to prove it when the pads come on. >> Do you get just as excited for a day like this as you did when you started here in Green Bay and still just as excited? >> Oh, absolutely. I told the team yesterday I I this is as as excited as I've ever been coaching this football team in my time here and it's because of the people we have in the room. I mean, players, coaches, support staff, everybody. Um so, we're we're just ready to go. >> And I I asked Woody this earlier, too. I know you're not going to say Super Bowl or bust up there or anything like that, but you had a pretty darn good football team at 9-3-1 last year when the injuries hit even harder. From a 30,000-ft view, what kind of team do you think you're starting camp with? I know lots of things have to go your way to get to where you want to go, but what do you feel about what you have? >> I'll be honest with you. I'm not even focused on that. Like, I want to focus on the day-to-day and just push these guys and they push each other um to be the best we can be and I think that's like I said, that's a reasonable ask. We got to get a little bit better each and every day. Um but I am confident in the people that we have in the room to field a pretty darn competitive football team.

So, there shouldn't be a ton of mistakes, you know, but there'll always be a couple procedural errors here and there, but we didn't have any false starts today. That's number one, I think, getting back into it. Usually those come with with the twos who haven't heard the cadence very much, going against live defenses, and you know, we didn't have any today, so that's that's positive. We got to continue that. There shouldn't be any. Uh but you know, we also had a couple motion errors, one one by me, and you know, a couple others by by receivers, so we got to clean that up, but you know, overall it was a productive day. >> Did you guys feel like you had an edge out there, or was that I mean, is that >> Number one sure had one today. Number zero did, too, so you know, those those two are two of the best in the league, and they're going to be going at it every day, so whenever those guys need to get excited to get better, go ahead and do it. >> Do you like that? Is that good, do you >> To some extent. When it starts to uh interrupt practice, not too much, but if you can you know, maybe punch somebody in the face in about you know, 15 to 20 seconds, and then get back lined up, that's probably ideal. >> DJ had another good year last year. What do you What do you Where do you see him improving, and where do you see him growing as he's getting older? >> He understands his leverages. He understands what teams are are trying to do from different splits. You know, his ball skills were great last year. You know, he's one of the best players at his position in this league, and um you know, really from from day one Ja'Marr and I felt that way when he first here and he's just continued to improve and evolve in his role and it's been fun to see, fun to be a part of, exciting to see. So, I'm excited to to see what he becomes even more this year. >> You've played against him a couple times on the other side of the line up with Dexter. What's it like just seeing him in front of you day one of training camp? Is there any difference or >> Yeah, he got back there pretty quick a couple times. You know, we're actually that thing out. Um you know, make some blind throws today. Just because of how big he is and you know, he pushes that pocket, gets close to you and um you have to to be able to throw around him, throw without seeing. And that's a it gets you ready for the games, but that's a challenge. Uh so, that's going to be a big part of our our team this year. I'm excited to watch it. >> One of the topics that seems to be something discussed the last couple of years is the running back spot and is that a position that you invest in and and the value of a running back? From your perspective, you played with a lot of good ones. What does Chase Brown do that makes him worthy of an investment at a position where it seems like, you know, it's not the same as far as what people think of a running back? >> He does everything. He's complete back. He can protect. He trains as a receiver all off season and you wouldn't know that he was a running back when he's out there doing it. He make makes people miss. Um first guy almost never brings him down. He's smart. He cares about it. Um I I think there's very few backs in this league that you can say that about. And when you have a guy like that, it's uh you don't have to take him off the field. You can put him in on so many different packages. You can build packages for him in different places on the field. Um you know, obviously we're going to try to get the ball in number one's hands as many times as we can, but I think a close second is Chase Brown just because of how explosive he is and what the things that he can do with the ball in his hand. Um, and he's taking a leap every single year and that's been exciting to watch and you know, I can't say enough good things about him. >> Could Chase be on the same level or Chase is Tee? I mean, obviously there's Jamar, there's Tee and Chase. Do you rank those in your mind or >> You certainly I don't think you rank them, but you know, we wouldn't be as good of an offense as we are and that we plan to be if we didn't have Chase, I know that. Um, and like I said, I don't think there's there's only a couple backs in this league that can do all the things that he does and probably doesn't get as many opportunities as as he should because of the other guys that we have. But he just makes big plays when he when he touches it. >> And the protection with what you're playing with right now. You said you were going to take some time to decide if you wanted to do that. >> No, the the foot feels great. I'll I'll play with protection in it for for the rest of my career just cuz why not? You know, I don't want it to happen again, but it feels good. >> Audrey had a tough year last year. He said multiple times that he he struggled. Have you talked with him since the end of the year? Do you have a sort of expectation for him to sort of bounce back this year? >> Yeah, we're counting on Audrey. He knows you know, his role and you know, he's going to have limited opportunities because of number one and number five, but you know, there's always spots where where guys get injured and you know, then he's thrusted into a much bigger role and a a featured role. And so he's he's ready for that. You know, he's worked really hard this off season. He looks great. you know, today was the first day, so I wasn't super dialed in on him, but the spring that he had I think was his best spring. And you know, he looks fast and explosive and I'm excited to see what he can do for the rest of the >> Sorry, Joe. What's your comfort level on under center play action and has it grown? >> Yeah, I'm very comfortable. I can do whatever is asked asked of me. I [clears throat] have and and I will. you know, we haven't done it quite as much over the last several years and you know, we'll see what we evolve into this year, but if that's what's needed, that's that's what I'll do. >> What were you dialed in on today? What So, what were you dialed in on today like you said? Were you um, any any receivers or any plays or just >> No, I'm just getting our just getting our feet wet. Um, just wanted to to throw it around. It's always you know, you can throw as many routes on air in the off season as you want, but then you know, you get a live rush out there and the timing's a little different, so you know, you feel that and then you adjust in your individual drills and try to replicate that and get that muscle memory going. >> They invested a lot. What did you see in all of that out there? What what y'all want to accomplish on the first time on the field? >> Yeah, the D-line certainly size size difference from last year is the most glaring thing. You know, the pocket was um, a little different today. Tough to tell when you don't have pads, but you know, I'm excited to to see what those guys can do. >> Does that all serve as a reminder of kind of where you feel like this team should go when you see it all on the field for the first time like, "Okay, they invested in this. We've got to make sure we maximize this." Is that >> Yeah, we we know that you know, we have all the pieces that we need and we just have to make sure that we're pushing each other each and every day to to grow and improve and get better, and we'll get to where we want to get to. >> You throw it against every DB, every great DB in this league. Even today, do you see the windows tighter, the you you and the competition at those positions covering your receivers? >> Yeah, I mean, the biggest thing was when you have the D-line that we have now, you just have to get it out faster. And you have to anticipate those windows, whereas you know, usually you want to maybe take another second and and see that window where, you know, there were a couple throws today that I couldn't couldn't see the guy I was throwing to, and I had to, you know, trust my eyes and trust my feet and throw it in a spot, just because there was somebody in my face [clears throat] or around my feet, and and that'll make me better. >> After the little skirmish, your first two passes went against DJ. Was that intentional or coincidence? >> I guess we'll never know. >> Thanks, Joe. >> Thanks. Thanks, Joe. >> [snorts]

title: Joe Burrow Reacts to Bengals Training Camp Day 1, Ja'Marr Chase & DJ Turner Altercation and More
text: Now, the last two days it gets uh you get antsy cuz it's like you're in the football mode, but you don't really have anything. And yesterday we weren't in till what? it's like what do you do the rest of the day cuz you're in the football mindset, but then you don't really have much going. Thank you. >> Seemed like the intensity was out there pretty good for day one. What did you think? >> Yeah, I mean this isn't where if the intensity's not great on day one, then you're in trouble. That's you know, kind of a given. It's is the intensity still there on day kind of determines if you're going to be a good team or not. >> How how much stock do you put in having competitive camps the intensity you mentioned and all of that, but the the competitiveness, how much stock do you put in that? >> Yeah, I mean you have to you have to go best on best if you want to get better, and the better players that are on the other side, the better you're going to be day in and day out, and uh the more improvement you're going to have at the end of camp. You know, guys now know how to do it by themselves, too, but uh when you can get those competitive reps in in August, that'll pay dividends. >> Good to see Eric All out there early. Thoughts [clears throat] on him being back? >> Yeah, it's great to have him back. Uh you know, obviously you know, he had a lot going on with his knee, but I wouldn't you wouldn't know it by looking at him. He looks good. He looks fit, fast, explosive, so you know, he'll play a big role for us this year. >> You know, you've been on record saying how talented this team is as talented as the Super Bowl team from the '22 season. Can you talk about how cool was just to see everybody and just the real feeling of all that talent on day one? >> Yeah, it's an exciting feeling. Um but like we talked about today and and yesterday, it doesn't matter now. You know, we had a great offseason on paper, but you know, now we have to go and and put all these pieces together and have individual improvement, have cohesive improvement, and you know, find out who we are as a team and gel. >> What did you do the last couple of weeks before mini camp? >> You travel a bit, you know, took a little break and then, you know, we were back at it and uh got a lot better. >> There was a lot of like galaxy stuff on IG. Any particular reason for that? >> Got a cool telescope. >> You got a telescope? >> Yeah. Pretty cool. >> What kind? >> I don't know what kind it was, but >> what prompted that purchase? >> I just thought it was [sighs] cool. Just gather cool things as you get older, man. It's like uh I don't know. Just find some cool stuff that I like. >> So, what are you looking at? >> Galaxies, um nebula, planets, moons, all the above. >> Aliens? >> Hopefully one day. >> Is it something you always wanted or did you get the urge one day? >> Kind of always wanted one. >> Last year, you ramped up how much you played in the preseason and your workload. Were you happy with that and are you hoping to kind of follow that same replica this year as far as how much you you feel like you need to play to get ready for the season? >> Yeah, we'll see what Zach says. We'll see what we end up doing. You know, I thought it was good for us. Um you know, the more times you can have game speed reps, the more acclimated you'll be come week one, so I'm always uh pushing for it and and willing to do it, so we'll see what we decide. >> Did you think last year was about right? >> Yeah, I thought I I I thought last year was good. >> What's a what makes for a good first week of camp when you look back at the games you all played? >> Um well, you're just kind of getting your feet underneath you. You know, you're back to to day one install stuff. Um so there shouldn't be a ton of mistakes, you know, there there will always be a couple procedural errors here and there, but we didn't have any false starts today. That's number one, I think, you know, getting back into it. Usually those come with with the twos who haven't heard the cadence very much, going against live defenses, and you know, we didn't have any today, so that's that's positive. We got to continue that. There shouldn't be any. >> [snorts] >> Uh but uh you know, we also had a couple motion errors, one one by me, and you know, a couple others by by our receivers, so we got to clean that up, but you know, overall it was a productive day. >> Did you guys feel like you had an edge out there, or was that I mean, was that >> Number one sure had one today. Number zero did too, so you know, those those two are two of the best in the league, and they're going to be going at it every day, so whenever those guys need to get excited to get better, go ahead and do it. >> Do you like that? Is that good, you >> It's that when it starts to interrupt practice, not too much, but if you can you know, maybe punch somebody in the face in about, you know, 15 to 20 seconds, and then get back lined up, that's probably ideal. >> DJ [laughter] had a really good year last year. What do you What do you Where do you see how he grew, and where you see him growing as you get into this season? >> He understands his leverages. He understands what teams are are trying to do from different splits. You know, his ball skills were great last year. You know, he's one of the best players at his position in this league, and um you know, really from from day one Jamal and I felt that way when he first got here, and he's just continued to improve and evolve in his role, and it's been >> [clears throat] >> fun to see, fun to be a part of, exciting to see, so I'm excited to to see what he becomes even more this year. >> You played against him a couple times on the other side of the line. What was that like? What's it like just seeing him in front of you day one of training camp? Is there any difference? Or >> Yeah, he got back there pretty quick a couple times. You know, we're going to get that thing out. Um, you know, make some blind throws today just because of how big he is. And, you know, he pushes that pocket, gets close to you, and um you have to to be able to throw around him, throw without seeing. And that's a like it's ready for games, but that's a challenge. Uh So, that's going to be a a big part of our our team this year. I'm excited to watch it. >> One of the topics that seems to be something discussed the last couple of years is the running back spot, and just is that a position that you invest in and and the value of a running back? From your perspective, played with a lot of good ones, what does Chase Brown do that makes him worthy of an investment at a position where it seems like, you know, it's not the same as far as what people think of a running back. >> He does everything. He's a complete back. He can protect. He trained as a receiver all off season, and you wouldn't know that he was a running back when he's out there doing it. He makes people miss. The first guy almost never brings him down. He's smart. He cares about it. Um I I think there's very few backs in this league that you can say that about. And when you have a guy like that, it's uh you don't have to take him off the field. You can put him in on so many different packages. You can build packages for him in different places on the field. Uh you know, obviously we're going to try to get the ball in number one's hands as many times as we can, but I think a close second is Chase Brown just because of how explosive he is and what the things that he can do with ball in his hand. Um and he's taken a leap every single year, and that's been exciting to watch. And you know, I can't say enough good about him. >> Could Chase be on the same level of work versus T? I mean, obviously there's Jamar, there's T, and Chase. Do you rank those in your mind? Are you Are they all >> You certainly I don't think you rank them, but uh you know, we wouldn't be as good of an offense as we are and that we plan to be if we didn't have Chase, I know that. and like I said, I don't think there's there's only a couple backs in this league that can do all the things that he does and probably doesn't get as many opportunities as as he should because of the other guys that we have. But he just makes big plays when he when he touches it. >> Any protection equipment you're playing with right now? You said you were going to take some time to kind of decide if you wanted to do that. >> No, the the foot feels great. I'll I'll play with protecting it for for the rest of my career just cuz why not? You know, I don't want it to happen again, but feels good. >> Andre had a tough year last year. You said multiple times that he struggled. Have you talked with him since the end of the year? Do you have a sort of expectation for him to sort of bounce back this year? >> Yeah, we're counting on Andre. He knows um you know, his role and [snorts] you know, he's going to have limited opportunities because of number one and number five, but you know, there's always spots where where guys get injured and you know, then he's thrusted into a much bigger role and a a featured role and so he's ready for that. You know, he's worked really hard this off season. He looks great. you know, today was the first day, so I wasn't super dialed in on him, but the spring that he had, I think was his best spring. And you know, he looks fast and explosive and I'm excited to to see what he can do for the rest of the year. >> Sorry. What's your comfort level on under center, play action, and how has it grown? >> Yeah, I'm very comfortable. I can do whatever is asked asked of me. I have and and I will. and we haven't done it quite as much over the last several years and you know, we'll see what we evolve into this year, but if that's what's needed, that's that's what I'll do. >> What were you dialed in on today? What So, what were you dialed in on today? Like you said with um any any receivers or any plays or just looking >> No, just getting our just getting our feet wet. Um just wanted to to throw it around. It's always you know, you can throw as many routes on air in the off season as you want, but then you know, you get a live rush out there and the timing's a little different. So, you know, you feel that and then you adjust in your individual drills and >> try to replicate that and get that muscle memory going. >> They they got some work in this spring and summer and you guys have been working out together in the off season. What's it like seeing it all out there knowing what y'all want to accomplish on first down? >> Yeah, the D-line certainly um size size difference from last year is the most glaring thing. You know, the pocket was um a little different today. Tough to tell when you don't have pads, but um you know, I'm excited to to see what those guys can do. >> Does that almost serve as a reminder of where you feel like this team should go when you see it all build in front of you like, "Okay, they invested in this. We've got to make sure we maximize this today." >> Yeah, we we know that you know, we have all the pieces that we need and and we just have to make sure that we're pushing each other each and every day to to grow and improve and get better and we'll get to where we want to get to. >> You've thrown against every DB, every great DB in this league. Even today, do you see the windows tighter, the you and the competition at those positions covering your receivers? >> Yeah, I mean the biggest thing was when you have the D-line that we have now, you just have to get it out faster. And you have to anticipate those windows, whereas you know, usually you want to maybe take another second and and see that window where, you know, there are a couple throws today that I couldn't I couldn't see the guy I was throwing to and I had to, you know, trust my eyes and trust my feet and throw it in a spot just because there was somebody >> in my face or around my feet and you know, that'll make me better. >> After the little skirmish, your first two passes went against T.J. Was that intentional or coincidence? >> I guess you'll never know.
