Um, and I think our all of our guys can play and and if we can get those guys on the field um more often than maybe we have in the past, I think that's a good thing. Obviously, we have it's only one football, so there's some balance of like, okay, we have some really good receivers as well. So, I think those are all things that you think about and you work on through training camp and you just experiment with and um the more we can do personnel wise, the better we're going to be just to keep the defense uh guessing and not knowing really what we're going to do. >> Trevor, was there is there less experimentation though with the passing game this camp because you've had a whole season in it and you're sort of really honing in on the stuff that works. Yeah, I think there's definitely honing in on stuff that that works, but it's also a lot of I wouldn't say experimenting, but working on things that we know we need to get better at to have a better offense, whether it's explosive plays down the field, some of the deep shots that we talked about in the spring, um to just some of the run game stuff that might be plays that we've done in the past, but maybe we're doing more of because we think we're better at, you know, those concepts. So, there's a little bit of that going on and then you're always trying to add little wrinkles here and there. So, I'd say it's a mixture of all that. >> How do you feel comparatively to years past day one of training camp? >> I feel really good. You know, I didn't think I had the best day today necessarily, but I I feel like this whole off season and and even today, I threw it well and just just missed a couple, but um I feel really healthy. I feel like I'm in great shape. Um I think I'm throwing it as good as ever. I think the chemistry with the guys is is really really good. Um I like where our team's at. So, you know, I'm excited. Really excited for this training camp. first time in eight years that you don't have Travis in the back field as a as a teammate. Um, coming out here today, what any weird feelings about that or what how'd you feel? >> Yeah, I mean, uh, not something that I thought about right away this morning when I woke up just cuz he's been gone for the spring, too. So, uh, that's a guy that I obviously I miss and we have a great relationship. Always rooting for him and we'll see him, you know, this preseason which will be fun to to catch up with him and see him a little bit in New Orleans. So, um, >> yeah, it's it's different and, you know, it's an opportunity for these guys to step up and and get a great opportunity to to make some plays and to play more. And I think our running back room is really talented and diverse and can do a lot of good things. So, obviously, we're going to miss Travis, but, you know, show goes on and we got to figure it out. >> And I was going to ask you about the running backs that you have, you know, other than Bash who comes back and a couple of others. What what are your your assessment of what you see? >> Just a really well-rounded room. I think Bashial obviously the you saw a little bit of what he can do last year when he got some carries. Really explosive, great vision inside. Obviously has the speed as well to, you know, to hit these home runs and I think his the steps that he's taken in protection this offseason have been great and he's gotten a lot better. So I think he can do more and more. And then obviously Laquent I think catching the ball in the back field, he's he's much improved. He was already he's good at it, but I think he looks even better this year. And protection stuff, he's always on it. one of the best pass protectors, maybe the best in the league. I mean, I' I'd like to see one that's better. Um, just always knows what to do. He's a hard runner. He's physical. You obviously getting C-Rod back in. Uh, DJ Dallas, we got a lot of guys. Getting Crod back and healthy is exciting. And he's a big physical runner. So, I think we got a well-rounded room. >> You're coming off of one of your best seasons. What's been the focus for you this off season to continue elevating your game? I think just the mental side and um staying sharp on everything so I can play fast like I was at the end of the season and the chemistry and just the rapport with me and the skill guys is so important and and just really tapping into that all throughout training camp and making sure that um we're on the same page cuz you saw when we started clicking at the end of the last season, you know, how efficient and how sharp we were um and some of the plays we were able to make. So just starting that now and trying to practice like that every day, you know, so we can start the season that way and not take a few weeks to get there. >> However, you interceptions last year um after playing 17 games, you a lot of critics were on you about turn turn the ball over. Do you think you have silenced those critics and how do you keep them silenced this year? Yeah, I mean I think 12's a little more than I'd like still, but um yeah, I mean I think that that's something that has been a huge talking point in my career and um rightfully so. You got to take care of the ball. So I think that's something I've worked really hard on my entire career and I think the last few years, a big one is especially fumbles and taking care of the ball in in the pocket and when I'm running cuz that's one that you can control every time you have it. You control how you protect the ball, how you secure it, how you tuck it. Um, and then obviously the interceptions, playing quarterback, it's going to happen. I think what type of interceptions are they? You know, are you getting fooled or is the DB making a good play? Sometimes you're just going to miss a throw a little bit. DB makes a play. Um, but limiting those bad decisions, limiting the ones where I feel like the defense fools me and um limiting the ones that are just unnecessary, red zone ones or or something like that. So, uh, I think there's different categories for all those, but taking care of the ball is super important. How optimistic are you that this offense really can function high level right from the start the way it did at the end of last year? >> Very optimistic. I mean that's the expectation for for us. I mean um to be honest, we should be able to do that and we should do that day one. So uh and not every day is going to be perfect. We're going to have some days we got a good defense, too. So have some days like today the the guys on defense made some great plays and had some adjustments and made some really good plays on the ball. That's going to happen. But for us to operate smoothly, get in and out of the huddle, to know all the checks, to know all the changes that we're making at the line of scrimmage, get the ball snap, to play clean football, I mean, that should be automatic. And then I know the plays will come and we just got to keep working um keep working at that and building the chemistry. >> It's a good feeling to have that, right? >> I mean, it's been sometimes not like that. >> For sure. It's a good feeling. And even to start last year, we were still swimming a little bit, trying to get the system down. And to start the season, we were um a little sloppy, a lot of penalties. So, I think that's definitely an area of improvement for our offense is is play cleaner, be a smart team, be really good situationally. >> You you've been in Parker a couple years now. You guys have continued to get reps together. That chemistry is just at a place now where it's higher than it's been before. >> Yeah, it is. I mean, every year it's gotten better and better, but especially after last season with all the reps that we accumulated over the last nine 10 games. I mean, and just the guy the way the guy works. I mean, he he's always he's always down to get extra reps after practice. He wants to talk after every rep that isn't right on the field. Um I mean just the way he communicates with me. Um he's just a professional. So I think it was only a matter of time before that started to show that chemistry and the way we work together um started to pay off. So just proud of that guy and uh love working with him. >> CJ Williams had the sliding catch today. It seems like he's made a play just about every day that we've been out here. What have you seen from him? man. He's just a he's a good example of a guy that's just knows what to do, always in the right spot because he studies so hard. I've been really impressed as a rookie how he's come in and really gotten the playbook down pretty quickly. You know, I haven't seen him make too many mistakes and running the wrong route or blocking the wrong guy and he knows what he's doing and he studies. So, then I think that's letting his his talent show because he's in the right spot and he has the opportunity to make the plays. So, he's just got to keep getting better every day. I like what I see from him. I mean, he's he's a really good player and he can definitely help us. >> What's kind of the biggest thing that you're going to look for over the next couple of weeks before the season starts? >> I think it's just trying to be that consistent group and then starting with me, even just individual in our position room. Um, just trying to be so consistent every day and do all the little things right. Um, and then as an offense, holding oursel to that standard as well of, you know, the splits, the motions, when we're getting the ball snapped, being in the right play all the time, the progressions, all that stuff. just being super super sharp while it is more of a controlled setting cuz you don't get this time back. Before you know it, we're going to be game planning for Cleveland and um this time to really work on our offense and our system um without the game plan element is going to be gone. So, just taking advantage of >> Was the first time in three years that you're coming back without having to nurse an injury back to health again. So, how are you feeling? Are you ahead of things? >> Feel great. It is, you know, grateful that I'm healthy. I feel really good to get an off seasonason to to train and um to not have to just rehab and try to get back healthy, but to be healthy and just get stronger and, you know, work on my game and my fundamentals. I mean, it's a good feeling. So, just excited to feel good. >> You recently secured the highest top 100 selection of your career thus far. Is it rewarding knowing that your peers view you in such a high regard? Yeah, I think it's it's always a cool thing when when peers think highly of you and um sorry, you know, I think it's uh yeah, I think it is what it is. Definitely it's definitely a respect thing that is appreciated and if it does feel good, but at the end of the day, got to go prepare for this season. >> Thanks, guys. I appreciate it.

It was as much as I could to to to to learn because coach Spags expects a lot out of us and um I got a lot of work to go and um I've came a long way but I also got a big jump ahead that I'm I'm going to take. >> Is that just a result of you're in your playbook and something pops in your mind or you watching films? >> 100% all the above. Just uh trying to figure out every way to to learn and to be the best that I can. What do you want to get most from yourself out of this training camp to prepare yourself for a new role this season? >> Yeah, I mean um there's a lot that you could pick there. I think for me is how can I be my best self in terms of my role in this defense and being able to maximize that as well as how can I make the guys around me better? And um I got a lot of experience in in in being around different play uh different sets of teams and of of units. So, you know, I feel like I'm in a good spot and I feel like we've took a great first step and look forward to the rest. >> You said you said something that stood out. The the DBs in the room were a lot more quiet than you're used to. I've known DBs to be, you know, outspoken. Why do you think that is? >> Um, I I personally think just like they bring in the right people here. Um, the department staff, their the culture here is set. So, they have they want certain type of guys here and the trajectory of where they want them to be at has been phenomenal here. So, you know, I just think they bring like-minded people here and that's kind of how they've have done it here and I respect it and obviously they had a lot of success and I look forward to being a part of that. >> Well, a couple more. >> When you went out with those guys, you have a favorite memory when you took the DVDs out once a week. Do you have a favorite memory or something that stood out? >> Uh, nothing crazy. Um, no, no, nothing crazy. just uh getting to know them more more as people outside of the building. Um guys have different things and different journeys. I like talked to them about they they were all like they're all NIL babies most of them. So like I'm I didn't have the NIL. I was living off as fast checks and I thought I was rich still. So like I would talk about that and they're like dang fast what is that? So like just stuff like that. Like so you know they're all NIL babies. They got a whole bunch of money. I was trying to buy a burger from for five guys. >> Wrap up here. Kyle Hamilton said you you've been his biggest influence in football. He was going to quit football the other day and you didn't let him. You kind of elaborate on that? >> Uh yeah. I mean I was a senior. He was a a young talented freshman coming in. Um kind of just growing in his in his space and um you know it got hard. You know football is a tough business. It's a tough sport. So me being as a you know a friend and a and a teammate wanted to make sure you know a guy like that with that much potential like you got to believe in yourself. You got to let things go and you just got to play. And as you can see, you know, he's he's one of the top guys. So that's my guy and hopefully I can continue to be that guy for anyone else in the in the building and I'm grateful to just be in this position. >> Thanks. >> Thanks, guys. You're well known for being just such a patient runner. Is that something that you learn and develop? Is it natural or and how do you feel like it's going to help you fit into this offense? >> Yeah. Uh I just believe over the years, you know, running the ball since growing up and just working with my pops. Uh just seeing the defense is I believe that's how I really learned how to be patient or, you know, explosive. It just depends on what the play what the play is honestly. And what you ask for the second question? >> Yeah. Is that something you feel like feel really feels like fits into this offense that you could add something to? >> Yeah, definitely. Um I feel like that helps the O line. You know, sometimes you got to be fast, but others you got to be patient and, you know, let the blocks develop and and just hit the hole. >> You think you could make in the passing game as a receiver and and even just staying, you know, on third down and blocking? >> Honestly, I uh I believe I can make a positive impact on anything, you know, whatever whatever they need me to do, that's what I'm going to do. >> And your first impression book Trey Camp, what have you heard? What have you learned about the process? >> First, sorry, sorry, what? >> What have you learned about Trey Camp? You heard about it obviously, but your first experience here. What do you think of everything that goes along? >> Yeah, definitely. Today was more of a chill day, you know, acclamation period, getting used to everything, but uh, you know, I already heard the things about how hard it'll be, how hot it'll be out here, but, you know, I feel like that's going to get us ready for the season and the games. >> What's impressed you most about seeing Patrick from maybe day one of OTAAS to even what you're seeing right now? >> Uh, just the leader he is. You know, we already know he's a great player. you know, he I see why he's a great player because the way he practiced uh the way he leads the team and you know, the energy that he brings every day. >> When we had ended up here at Catio as a leader, I guess why is that important to you to make sure that all the running backs are in order and feel like they have confidence? >> All the running backs. >> Why is that important to you to to sort of mold the younger guys and just make sure that they have confidence? >> Yeah, definitely. Um we don't want it to be a drop off anywhere. you know, if you know, my helmet gets messed up or something, I come out of the game or emit uh Mari comes out of the game, we know, we want everybody to be able to produce just like the first person. So, I believe that's why it's good to have everybody on point. >> And if you seem to tour Kansas City almost time here, what's really stood out to you? >> Uh really the barbecue obviously. You know, that's what they talk about the most. So, that's what I really want to try. Um the barbecue obviously meeting the people around here, you know how the fans are, you know, uh they're really dedicated to the sport. So it's great to see that. >> You don't have to name a restaurant, but back for ribs burns. What's your favorite part? >> I I'll say I like ribs. That's what I've liked since growing up. So I had to say ribs for sure. >> You're coming off You're coming off a Super Bowl year. The Chiefs obviously didn't have a year that they wanted last year. Can you feel that in the building and you kind of bridge that gap? >> Yeah, definitely. you know, they uh you know, we they want to win, you know, and they've won many Super Bowls before. So, uh definitely you see the work ethic that's going on around here. Everybody wants to compete and win, and you know, we'll go out there and see how we play this season.

title: Chiefs Mosaic Training Camp Opening Press Conference - Mark Donovan | JULY 29, 2026
text: [music] >> Mhm. >> [music] [laughter] >> Check with the boss. Hey. Good morning, everybody. I'm Pat Dillon. I'm with Mosaic Life Care and proud to officially welcome all of you to our 16th training camp, believe it or not, here at Missouri Western in St. Joe, Missouri. You know, we're proud to have you. Today, we're going to hear from our CEO um Mike Poore, CEO of Mosaic, and and Chiefs president Mark Donovan. And to kick off the press conference, I'm honored to introduce interim president of Missouri Western, Pat Lillie. Uh Pat became interim president of Missouri Western in May of this year, May 11th. Uh he brings decades of executive leadership experience and strong understanding of Missouri Western uh in his role and his his uh background here in the region. He previously served as president CEO of the St. Joe Chamber of Commerce for more than 18 years, chief administrative officer for Triumph Foods, and city manager for the city of St. Joseph. So, Pat has a Uh Pat and I both have a long background of involvement in in St. Joseph, Missouri. So, he um he served on the board of Missouri Western State University Board of Governors, including a term as chair. So, Pat, welcome to your role, your first press conference for uh Chiefs camp, and uh we'll you have let you go ahead and kick it off. Pat. >> Pat Lillie. >> [applause] >> Pat, thank you. I You know, when Pat Dillon gets up to introduce you, you always get a little worried, but uh I appreciate that, Pat. Well, welcome, and uh we are pleased to welcome back the Kansas City Chiefs for the 16th training camp uh here at Missouri Western. Uh the enthusiasm that the Chiefs bring with them and their fans uh frankly is a great way to wrap up our summer here, and to begin our school year, which will begin toward the end of August. It also gives us an opportunity to showcase our campus, and I hope those of you that are here that have not been here before take a little time to enjoy the campus and in the community uh as well. Uh since we are an applied learning institution here at Missouri Western, I think it's worth noting that we have dozens of interns uh who are students at Missouri Western, as well as institutions from across the country that come here to work with a first-class organization uh like the Chiefs. I can't think of a better internship, frankly, uh than to work uh for the Chiefs. Uh you know, when you look around uh the campus uh as camp is as camp is occurring, obviously you see a lot of people in red and what have you, but you may not see all the work that goes on and has been going on for the last uh several months. It it really is uh a a heavy lift, if you will, uh for so many here at the university that I want to say thank you to. But, it's one that we really enjoy and one that we appreciate doing uh on behalf of the community. And speaking of community, I will say as well that having camp here is really a community effort that includes the city, the county, the Chamber of Commerce, the Convention and Visitors Bureau, and particularly uh Mosaic Life Care. All of whom have been here from the very beginning. With that, I'd like to turn it over to Mike Poore, CEO of Mosaic Life Care. >> Hi, everyone. I'm Mike Poore, CEO of Mosaic Life Care, and uh I'm honored to actually represent the 5,000 caregivers of Mosaic Life Care. We are happy to be back into football now. And uh uh we want to welcome the Chiefs, um the uh Chiefs Kingdom, and all the fans uh back uh to St. Joe, Missouri. And we're here to take care of them with our Mosaic Life Care uh caregivers uh as an organization. Now, we just broke ground on a $71 million uh cardiac center of excellence, and we are very proud of that. Uh it's part of our commitment to the community, where we are building something sustainable, just like the Chiefs. Now, we don't get a ring or a a trophy, but uh the team comes in and works hard every day to take care of our community. So, we look forward to a great camp, um a a great season this year and we're uh we're all good fans to make this happen. So, I it's my pleasure to introduce Mark Donovan, president of the Chiefs to come up and do some comments. >> Morning everybody. Um, thank you for being here. I want to thank Mike for the introduction. That's always good to see you. Um, feels like camp officially begins when Pat Dillon gets behind this microphone. So, glad you're here. Um, Pat, it's nice to meet you and thank you for being here. Um, I want to echo at least comments that and acknowledge that um, we really appreciate that it is a community effort. And the entire community of St. Joe, >> [clears throat] >> every civic organization, the citizens, our fans who are here, we really appreciate the welcome they give us and the energy they give our players and coaches every single day. Um, kicking off today with our season ticket member day, the first of a couple. Um, one of the things we're really proud of and excited for. Um, pancake breakfast for all of our season ticket members have become a very big and popular day for us. If you haven't [snorts] been down to watch some people flip some pancakes, you got to come down and see it. Um, but it's a great way to start the camp and really kick things off for our season ticket members. I typically start with football and where we are. I'm going to take a second and just acknowledge that we've had a really busy summer as a region and as an organization. We've been working with the folks in and around the World Cup for about four and a half years and to be able to host the World Cup as a region has been something that we've been really excited to be a part of. I want to congratulate the entire Kansas City region, the organizing committee on pulling off just an epic event. I believe that it's put our region on a level internationally that it's never been on before. Um it was a huge challenge and one that I was really proud our team was a part of to help pull off. Um when you think about the number of people who came through here, um that's one measure. You look at the ratings, that's another measure. I think the one thing that uh some people need to acknowledge is the level of exposure that Kansas City got internationally is one of the things we strive for. We talk a lot about being the world's team, and I think the World Cup gave us another opportunity to show how special this entire region is, and how it capable this city and region is to host events what like the World Cup. We'll talk a little bit later about our stadium project. Events like the World Cup and our ability to pull that off successfully actually accelerate the ability to host even bigger events at the new facility that we're building. So, I'll get to that in a bit. Um I want to stick back to camp for a second. Um we are excited to be back here. We're excited to get going. We have 18 open practices this year, um which I believe is the most in the National Football League. It's something that is core to our brand and core to our experience and really core to our founder that our our fans are our lifeblood, and we want to do everything we can to expose our team to them. Um and this is probably the best way to do that on an up and close and personal way. special thanks to Coach Reid and Brett Veach for understanding how important this is and how understanding how important the access is. Um you know, we're going to have another hot day out there. This will be the first real practice for the players as a team. These are long, hard days. And the fact that our coaches Clark really communicates to our players how important it is to take care of our fans when they're out here. And that goes to a thanks to our players for staying the extra time after practice to sign autographs after every practice to make our fans feel special because they deserve to feel special cuz they give us the ability to do what we do. Um if you'll allow me, I'm going to read a couple important reminders that are I want to make sure I get right about camp specifically. >> [snorts] >> All tickets must be reserved in advance. Tickets are free with the exception of 3 days when there's a $7 per ticket fee. Uh there's a parking fee every day for per car. We have those two exclusive season ticket member days that are already both sold out. Um I think this is a really important one if you guys could get help get this message out for our fans. If you go to chiefs.com/trainingcamp, you got all the information in terms of practices, hours, access. Um you do have to reserve your tickets in advance. Um there are a few days that are about sold out, but there's still tickets available for most days. So, go on there, get your tickets, and come up and see us. >> the other thing about that website is today's a good example of it. Enabling the push notification is really important for our fans. Um we're going to get some weather here that's going to roll in. Uh we're hopeful it's going to miss us, but the push notification gives us the ability to really communicate quickly with our fans what we're doing, if the guys are going to be out, if they're going to be in, um and give them updates as they go here. It also gives you all the rules and regulations, clear bag policy, um all the things we typically do. I'm sure we're getting in some questions later about more of the specifics, but >> I'll say this, we're really excited to be back here. We're really excited for the support that everyone gives us. I do want to take a second and thank Andy Carter, the AD here, his entire staff. Um I say this every year, but we should say it more than we do. The amount of work that goes into the day-to-day for our players and coaches to allow them to be able to get through the 2 and 1/2 3 weeks up here, the people nobody ever sees, the people behind the scenes. Andy and his team do an amazing job for us and we really appreciate it. With that, I'm going to ask Mike and Pat to come back up and we'll do our annual photo and take some questions. >> Might be doing one at a time. Maybe one at a time. Everyone stand in front of this. >> Yeah, that'd be great. Just kind of right in front of them. Awesome. We'll go look right here, gentlemen. 1 2 3. We'll do one more. 1 2 3. Do one more. Yeah, 1 2 3. Perfect. We're going to take one more with >> Yeah, so Mike I said >> My fifth jersey. >> There you go. >> 1 2 3. We'll do one more. 1 2 3. Awesome. >> All right. Now we'll do one now with that. Take a slice out of here. Yeah, we'll get a switch out of here. >> Okay. >> Yep. >> There we go. >> He's got to do what they tell you. >> Okay, let's switch them right here, gentlemen. Okay. Awesome. >> Thank you. >> All right. Uh we're going to open it up to questions. Uh training camp questions for any of the three speakers. Uh we'll take a few minutes for those. Anyone has anything? >> I'm sure you're glad the fans are going to come out for training camp, but over the last few years with the team having so much success, what do you what do you see as the measure of that success when it comes to fans coming out and the differences in training camp versus not playing preseason football? >> Yeah, I think that uh you know, last year's last year. And that's the way this team is looking at it. And that's how we look at it. I think for the most part that's how our fans are looking at it. Um today's first day. Uh I would tell you that, you know, the early results on uh ticket request are pretty consistent. Um and you've seen that over the years. Um it real quickly just to give you some gauge on sort of how consistent and how faithful our fans are. And one of the things I'm really grateful for, uh you know, I first got here in 2009, uh we were kind of a struggling football team. And um if you go back and look at the records of 2006, 7, and 8 going into that season. So, I asked our team to pull out um a stat that we track across the league called watch, attend, listen. So, do you watch games? Do you attend games? Do you listen games? And if you look at the last 10 years or the 10 years before that, the Kansas City Chiefs fan base is 100% consistent. It stays at the same level. It doesn't matter about the record. Now, there's obviously, you know, some ticks in that up and down. Um there are a lot more ways to track it now, but uh we we have felt the support. We continue to feel the support. The traffic we see, the things we measure are consistent or up. one of the coolest things about the NFL is everybody's 0 and 0 right now. And everybody has an opportunity in this league to hoist that trophy at the end of the year. And we're looking forward to doing >> Mark, with the success I would say the new infrastructure that you have going [snorts] on in Kansas City >> and the prospects of you eventually maybe host training camp there in the >> Yeah. >> How do you view the next 5 years? Is this something that you view the next 5 years as being in St. Joe as a partner? And how do you view the long-term vision of it? >> Yeah, let me answer that directly. We absolutely view it as being with St. Joe's and being a partner with them for the next 5 years. I think one of the things that has been really great about this relationship uh and again, I'll go back to history, right? When we first signed this deal, um there were a lot of questions on if we were going to be here for 5 years. And to be here 16 years later and say we're still here and we still enjoy it and it still works for us, it has to work for them, too. Um and over the years, I think what we've done is established a really good rhythm in how we look at this on both sides, a really good understanding of each other's businesses, and if you follow our business, you see a lot of things have changed over the years, uh specifically the number of teams that have gone back to their training facility versus going away. Uh it's increased exponentially. And my limited knowledge, just in learning it from the folks at Missouri Western and some other universities that we work with, is their world has changed dramatically as well. Um when you think about the funding and the government funding and the things that they need to do. So, I think that base, that foundation, understanding each other's business is really important as we go forward. Uh we've adjusted some things in our agreement to address that. And I I just want to be clear it's been on both sides. Like we've done more in the past year than we'd ever done as an organization to support them. They've done more for us over the years to support us year in and year out. And I think that's what makes the organiza or the partnership work. Um we'll do that again this year. At the end of the year, we'll sit down and say what went well, what are the things we can work on, what are the challenges we face, what are the challenges we face, and then hopefully we'll continue on. We have a multi-year agreement, um and we expect to be here for a long time. I will say this just cuz it's the obvious follow-up question, you know, with the training facility being built in Olathe, we as an organization have to look at everything we do with options. So, that training facility is going to be designed with the ability to host training camp. We have to have that option. Who knows where we are in 5 years. Um, but that decision will be made year four and year five as we go into that building because, you know, depending on the head coach, does he still want to go away? Does he see the efficiency? Um, those things will factor in. We just have to have the options. Yeah, the way that it's currently planned is um, and look, we've looked as you know, Sam, we've looked across the league at how other teams have done this with their training facilities and one of the things we've done is design it so it has enough seating. Um, now it won't be a college stadium necessarily, um, but it'll be enough seating to host a big number of our fans for every single practice if we want to. >> Are you concerned the state of Kansas is having trouble selling bonds for the new stadium? >> Uh, we are not concerned about the ability to sell bonds for our stadium. Um, if you look at um, the market and you talk to the experts in the market, um, the combination of the fact that sports-anchored real estate is probably the hottest market in real estate right now and the power of the National Football League, it's a pretty compelling, powerful partnership. Um, and all the indications that we have received are that it's going to be a very strong market. >> Anything else camp-related? Anyone? Hold on for a few minutes. >> Let's talk about the I wanted to ask you about the the renderings. There's certainly a heavy arrowhead >> What's the balance behind >> Yeah, one of the things we were worried about. You can imagine, you're in a vacuum, there's six or eight of us who are working with two different designers on um, all the options. And one of things we did two really important things on the front end in giving them direction when they put the designs together. One is we shared the CSL study that we did with our fans. And we want them to have all the detail and all the specific information they gave to us. I think I've shared with you all before, you know, the three big takeaways from the study. There was a ton in there, but the three big takeaways were it needs to be louder louder. Um and the tailgating has to be as good or better. Um and the rest was just that they trusted our ability to give them something they're going to be proud of. Um so we gave them that. Um And we went to a pretty broad group of potential designers and you can imagine the designs we got were all over the board. There were some really futuristic things, there were really some traditional things. And one of the things we sort of centered back on was we have to honor the legacy of Arrowhead. But we have to show a bold and innovative look at the future. And that was a challenge for our designers. Like do it. Here's your do both of those things. And there were various degrees of that. I'll go back to the vacuum comment which is, you know, you're sitting in that room for four months. Look at a design after design after design after design and we kept zeroing in on like we got to get the balance right of honoring Arrowhead but also looking at the future and um I thought David Manica and his team did an amazing job of really um accepting that challenge and distributing it. One of the more um satisfying parts of the feedback we got after we released the renderings was that was one of the first comments from most of the fans. It's like wow, I see Arrowhead. Um so we're really excited about what we were able to accomplish and the work we did with Manica. >> Our Kansas City you mentioned the um earlier this announcement on the sidelines of practices. >> How would you characterize the uh competition Yeah, this is going to sound a little self-serving, but it's hopefully more a credit to the team around us. We're doing a lot in a very short period of time. So, we're trying to figure out who the best designer is for our stadium, what the real estate uh development is going to look like, the land acquisition for the stadium. At the same time we're doing it for the practice facility. Um so, the competition was uh very competitive. Um a lot of really talented people. It's an interesting space because some of the people who competed on the stadium also competed on the practice facility. Some people just competed on the practice facility cuz that's their expertise. Um I think with both situations, we had to look at it holistically. And by that I mean that you got to get the absolute best stadium design in that situation. We also challenged on the stadium side, design the parking lot. And one of the things that I don't think people realize is that Arrowhead is amazing for tailgating. If you look at it from a drone, it's really not set up great from a parking It's set as a parking lot. Think about like there's not a real straight, open pedestrian walkway to any of our gates. Well, now we're on a blank canvas. So, we we asked the designers like when you think about the stadium design, think about designing tailgating. Think about designing the lots to take into account all those things. So, we did that with the stadium. We did the same thing with the practice facility. We said, "Think about the practice facility as you've got to build the absolute best, most functional, efficient place where we can conduct our work." It also has to be fan-facing. And we got a real estate development around it that could include a high school football stadium, an indoor sports facility, and real estate. And that's what gets us excited, and that's what gets the designers excited. So, long-winded way of saying it was a very heated competition. Happy to be with Populous. Um they competed in both stadium and training facility, and their team on the training facility side really separated themselves pretty quickly. >> From my understanding, you're in the early stages, when do you start to be proactive with maybe post-2031 for the whole adjacent events and >> Start the question again, sorry. >> Despite being in the early stages, >> Oh. >> yeah, when you when you start to be proactive about events that you may be able to do that you're not able to do now? >> Yeah, we had this conversation last week. Um we have been in discussions with the NFL about Super Bowls in '33, '34, '35. We have been in discussions, very preliminary discussions, but we are aggressively pursuing Final Fours. Uh if you know anything or follow anything about the NCAA, um you know, they're going to go out with a bid here. Um and the thing about it is that if you're the NCAA, you're trying to sort of put stability into your future planning. So, they're trying to lock in all these dates. we don't have a building yet. And we don't want to be knocked out of those cuz they've locked in so many so far out. So, we're actually we were in discussions with the NCAA last week about could we bid on these dates that our stadium will be done by then, but it's not done right now. Um so, they were appreciative of that. I think uh you know, we've said to Kathy Nelson and the team there, we said to the folks who help us with these kind of bids that we're going to be very, very aggressive. Um we're probably going to be early bidders on most things. Um acknowledging that doesn't really enhance our chances of winning the bid. Um cuz if you're I've been on the other side of that, and you really want stability, you want predictability, um you want certainty. Um so, it'll be a challenge, but we you know, when we did this deal, we we made the commitment that we're going to be really aggressive. And we think that this facility is going to be have the ability to host all kinds of events, and frankly, you think about the events that we're talking about bidding for right now, 95% of them, we wouldn't be able to bid on them because we don't have an indoor stadium, so. Yeah, we looked at it. Um >> I think uh there are a number of reasons that came into play, obviously cost is one thing, efficiency is another. Um I I mean, behind the scenes I would share that we talked to every single team that has a retractable roof. And I don't want to put words in their mouth, but it was pretty clear it's not worth it. Um and if you think about how many people actually use it and retract it that often, it's pretty small. Um and on the positive side, the technology you think about this, guys, we're we're 5 years away, right? We're in the design process. We just finished our design, now we get into the details of it. The technology is changing so rapidly, and a fixed roof today versus a fixed roof 5 years ago is significantly different. A fixed roof 5 years from now is going to be significantly different. So, we think the technology is going to continue to enhance that. Uh that's one of the things about our renderings, like being able to we really challenged the team and the technology piece and the roof people um on we wanted it to be as transparent as it possibly can be because flyovers are so important to our game day experience. That's one of the reasons we cut the windows out at the ends, so you can see out there as well. so, I think that technology is going to change. If you look at the roofs today, you can kind of see a flyover. We expect that our roof you'll be able to see much more of a flyover. I'm not going to see say it's going to be crystal clear because you do have some requirements in terms of code and what you have to have in terms of filtering. >> What's the likelihood of natural grass? >> Yeah, so back to I answered the question earlier about training camp and having options. we we had designed the building to be able to do either. Uh our preference and we stated this publicly as grass. We want to figure that out. So, uh Stephen, if you're asking me today to bet, I feel pretty strongly that we're going to be playing on natural grass. Um back to the comment I just made about technology 5 years from now, um you know, we're we're in the middle with other NFL clubs who are in the same process we are who are going to build domes, like can we figure out a way to grow grass indoors? So, uh we'll continue that process. Uh you may or may not know this. Um our friends in Populous uh shared this with us and have offered to take us down there to see it. In New Zealand, there are two rugby stadiums today. They exist. They play on them today. They grow grass indoors. Um so, the technology is there, right? So, you just got to figure out can it adapt to our climate, our building, etc., etc. The The building is designed today to um be a grass field. We just roll it out like Vegas does. Um Arizona does it as well. Um but, we have some flexibility on that. So, and the other side of that is I don't think we'll end up here, but the other side is to be consistent on tracking technology and changes, you know, you look at what FIFA did. You look at what um the technology is with hybrid fields and turf fields and turf technology. We'll look at that as well. Um but, our preference is grass. >> Well, did did Pop have that meeting with the team last usually does before camp. >> Yeah, so Clark is going to meet with the team tonight. So, he'll do his annual address then. >> Related to that though, you're in a unique situation to see how both Clark and Andy responded to last season. And I know you mentioned earlier the idea that last season's last season. >> Right? Just curious what you would have observed in each of their responses to how it went after successes >> Um I'll take that two ways. The first is I think how they responded is a good example of one of the things I believe that make us successful as an organization. It's very consistent. Like there's no surprises. >> Um they both responded kind of the same Significant frustration, disappointment. Um we had much higher expectations. Andy had much higher expectations. Our players had much higher expectations. Our you know, Clark and his family had much higher expectations. So, it was similar. I think the second part of that is what another thing that makes us special is I mean, on the plane ride at home what are we going to do to fix this? And what do we need to do to fix it? And I think that's an important point, you know, to have that open communication where you know, we're in a room talking about what do you need to fix this, right? What do you need, Brett? What do you need, coach? what do we what are we going to change to fix this? Right? So, um those are the conversations that were um you know, driven by Andy. Like I this isn't happening again. Um and then I would just say you've probably have seen a little bit. I mean, mindset is the theme this year, but the mindset of this team right now is I saw it last night. I got to speak to the team last night. And um you know, there's a different tone. And I think it's commitment. >> What did you want to get across last night when you spoke? >> Um so so my message to the team is much more um focused on making them aware of the resources and the opportunity that's in front of them. So, you know, these our entire team, our entire organization, I mean, the opportunity that we have, the state that we're on, um the success that we've had and also the business and the team populated that we've built creates all kinds of opportunities for these guys. And we have resources for them. We want to take advantage of those, but we also, you know, there are a lot of guys in that built in that room who haven't been there before. Um so we want them to know and be aware of the resources that we have at their um disposal. You know, they're they got a lot coming at them. And one of my messages is our job is to eliminate distractions for you. And we got 300 people back in Kansas City. All they want to do is be good teammates to you. So just tell us what you need. Um so the awareness of the resources and then communication channels, open those up. >> Has the work at Arrowhead post World Cup >> Yeah, thank you for asking that. Um just to give you guys perspective, our team, our operations team has done just an amazing job. I mean, you think about 4 years of construction in between seasons. Um [clears throat] think about getting ready with all the things we had to do. And if anybody went to the World Cup matches, you saw Arrowhead just looked very different. Um that's a lot of work. Um so they were grinding >> all the way through World Cup. And then just [snorts] to be able to celebrate 415,000 people from all over the world coming through our building. Um and all that created. These are the people who make that work. Think about this. The day World Cup ended and everybody's celebrating and patting each other on the back, they have about 28 days to do about 22 days of work to get ready for the NFL. So, they went from full sprint to full sprint to get ready for our first preseason game. And here's a perspective that I appreciate. At the end of that second full sprint, welcome to the NFL season. So, that team deserves acknowledgement and that team um frankly deserves a couple days off at some point uh cuz they've been grinding, but they've they've done an amazing job. We are in great shape. Um you know, the field had been taken out and replaced. People don't obviously know all the details, but you think about a soccer field is entirely flat, like level flat. A football field has a crown, so you're taking that out, taking all the technology out, putting the new one in, getting that right, putting the grass in, making sure it's growing correct. You're putting back all the seats that were out so that every single one of our season ticket members sitting in the exact seat they sat in last year without any change. You're fixing all the signs, taking all of that back down, and then there's there was a lot of stuff behind the scenes that were suites and clubs that media tribune that was put in there. You got to replace all that. So, it's a lot of work, but our guys are going to get it done. >> Mark, what was your perspective once the city won the World Cup? >> Um I pride. You know, to be part of this. I mean, the the amount of work Matt Kenny from our team deserved a lot of credit. He think about the timing of this, and I'm telling you way too many stories, but think about the timing of this. Like, we get the first I think the first discussion about World Cup was 2017, something like that. It was crazy how long we've been doing this. And [snorts] we were trying to figure out stadium, where you staying, where you going, getting through a vote. And I just went to Matt and said, "Look, here's your opportunity. I can't do this. I I got to focus my time on stadium. I need you to step up." And he did. And he took over the World Cup and he's been sort of our point for it. Um So, really proud that all the work that was put in paid off. Really proud of this region and proud to like prove some of the things many of us have been saying to the world and to the other markets in the US and to the big uh event planners is Kansas City special. You just got to come see this and you got to give us the opportunity. I remember when we we went to the NFL to Clark and I went and had a meeting with Roger when the NFL draft was announced that it was going to Vegas. And this was right about the time they had just, you know, finished the stadium. And we went there, I don't want to say angry, but um competitive. [clears throat] Um saying like, you got to start thinking about markets like Kansas City for the draft because you're not going to give us a Super Bowl and you're going to give Vegas a Super Bowl. So, you're going to give draft and Super Bowl like be equitable and um even then we had to convince the NFL that the draft would work in Kansas City. And then we pulled the draft off, right? We had to convince FIFA that World Cup would work in the smallest city they've ever been to in the US. And not only do we pull it off, but we dominated. And I think I'll go back to what I said before that puts us on a different level now. And that feeds right into the timing of this new building. So, it's a really proud that we were able to pull that off and what it means for our future. >> One more question on the stadium, the budget, I wonder if it's the same after you're going through this design process and you envision the cost changing. >> Very typical in these situations where you know, there are two different competing forces, right? There's a designer and there's a construction manager. So, we took the last two designs to two different construction teams and said bid it and us what it cost." And not surprisingly, they were way over budget, but they looked really cool. So, uh that's part of the process is you have to sort of engineer some of the cost savings into so, um we'll be very close to budget. we got some work to do to get there. Uh one of the biggest things is we got a massive parking lot. And it's a blank canvas, which is great, but you know, you got to also build infrastructure and a lot of things that cost a lot of money. So, um we'll get there. Um if you know, I've worked with Clark for 18 years. We'll be really close to budget, trust me. >> All right, Paul Haywood close up. You spoke to this a bit, but I I wonder if you could elaborate on on ways you think the World Cup has boosted the the World's team mission, despite the fact you don't have Arrowhead, Kansas City stadium and things like >> Yeah, number one, it put us on a map internationally. [clears throat] Um not only the exposure of the matches, but the exposure of and the awareness from social media content of foreign visitors to this region and the comments they made about Kansas City, which goes back to that pride point, but think about the things that you heard from those people like, "They're so nice here. It's so easy here." Right? All things that we know are true. Um but that was on an international stage. I I would give you this one This probably goes way too deep on strategy. Um but when you think about the commitment that Lamar made to being international and growing internationally and the the vision that he had to say, "That's where our growth is." In the '70s, he's saying this. Um and then you think about the commitment that we have made, the resources we put against financial and personal resources against growing and setting that goal. Um I know a lot of our fans are like, why do you spend so much time, you know, on international and branding? But, think about this. Just from a statistic standpoint, so so the things that we look at that justify not only why we're doing it, but why the NFL is doing it. The World Cup final rating in the US was 62.5 million people. The largest in the history of soccer in the US by a wide margin. The NFL will tell you correctly. The Super Bowl last year was 125 million. Double. Biggest, strongest, we make we make the statement a lot about how powerful the NFL is in the US. That Super Bowl did 125 million US. That Super Bowl did 200 million worldwide. 62.5 62.5 million people watched the soccer final in the US. 1.5 billion watched it around the world. Why do we want to be the world's team? Cuz that's the opportunity. That's why we're doing all this, cuz there's a huge market out there that we need to take advantage of, and things we've done are working. And we're going to continue to be committed to that, and you know, that's sort of our North Star. >> All right, guys. Thank you. >> Thank you for being here, guys. Enjoy camp. Come have some pancakes.

title: Raiders Training Camp Is Here! Plus, Kirk Cousins and John Spytek Join
text: Welcome in everybody. It is day one of Raiders training camp practices. I'm Amber Theo Harris along with THE HALL OF FAMER Eric Allen getting ready to head back up to Canton in just a couple of days, but you're just here with us now. We're excited to be talking about the Raiders. >> Um, well, you have to start out with Clint Kubak. This is the first time we're really seeing him out there running a training camp practice. He is one of six new head coaches in the NFL, but he looks like a veteran. We've seen a lot of new head coaches take the field with the Raiders and this is a welloiled machine from what we're seeing early on and what we saw throughout the off season. Uh just getting to know Clint a little bit over the last couple of months. What are your first impressions about his approach? >> He's he's all about football. >> You know, the little side talks and things like that. He has dialed in. He's all about football. Kind of been really really uh doing an outstanding job of kind of changing the mentality of this building. And you know, we've gone through coaches, we've gone through staffs, just so many changes for this football team. Finally, it seems like we're all on the same page. And I think that is really important for all this young team. Everyone coach wise is under 40. >> So, you need to come in kind of build that relationship, build that foundation. I think he's done a very good job so far just making it sure that the first things is first. It's about football. All the other stuff can kind of outside the building and everything like that can kind of handle itself. I think he's doing an outstanding job of making sure the foundation is built here and it's solid. >> Well, I'll tell you the the newest additions and the things you look at right away is the fact that Kurt Cousins is running with the ones. Yeah, >> the the switch though, the offensive lines coming in with the ones and twos, how quickly and efficient they were. That doesn't mean he's getting the starting nod for day one, for week one, but what do you expect to see with what they are calling a quarterback competition? >> Yeah. But the question that's being asked and it and I don't like this question. Uh, do you win now with Kirk Cousins or do you develop Fernando Mendoza? I think that is the wrong question. The wrong question. Cuz the right question is who can you win with now and that might be Fernando Mendoza. You don't take a quarterback number one in the NFL draft if you don't think he is ready to play in the NFL. The determination comes in camp whether or not um you think he is the best option for week one to put him in the best position to develop. And we've seen everybody from the number 11 pick Bo Knicks to the number three pick Drake May just went to the AFC to Super Bowl. Um they they're throwing them and I don't like the word throwing them out there. They are playing them because those teams felt they were the best opportunity to win and they won in the NFL. >> They earned that spot not through where they were drafted but how they performed in practice. And I think that's the one thing that everyone is torn about because because you're drafted in a certain spot, you're supposed to start automatically and it's not about that. That draft spot gives you multiple opportunities if you fail. That's what that draft spot does, right? It's a great point. >> But when you come in, it's about earning your opportunity to line up on Sunday when the games really matter. And I think that's the one thing that everyone needs to understand. All those things are going to be critiqued in these next three and a half to four uh weeks in order for you to make a decision on who that starting quarterback's going to be.
