Let me uh let me tomorrow, you know, if you in this sit I'm like I get it." Um, but yeah, it's been with every coach. That's something that I mean that's literally all the way back to college days with coach Kraton. He used to I mean had to kick me out of practice all the time. But it's growth, you know, you focus on getting better and trying to be the best version of yourself. That's all I can do. >> Early in the process, what have you thought about all the new additions on the defensive side of the ball that's running with you? >> Um it's been great. You know, uh obviously it's, you know, we're not in pads yet, so I think you you figure out, you know, your identity, especially um once the pads come on and you see people's physicality and the the type of competitors competitors they are. Um, but it was awesome just seeing, you know, that, you know, it's a funny story. It was back in uh back in OTAAS, but I was out there doing a walkthrough and I'm getting in a stand. I looked at him and started just laughing out loud and I don't even know why, but I just He's like, "What are you laughing at, bro?" I'm like, "I've never seen a linebacker that big. Like, I've never played with a linebacker that looks like the size of me." And he's like, "No, bro. It's going to be different." You know what I mean? So, it's just cool. You know, there's so much uh so many new faces and and a lot of really talented guys on all three levels. And um you know, for me it's it's the best. You know, we want the best guys out there, the guys who are going to you know, jump on the grenade and and be in the foxhole with you. And um you know, we're you know, that's what training camp's for. You figure out who those who those guys are and then you know, through the season, um you see how everyone progresses. So um it's exciting. >> Hey Max, from a from a physical standpoint after the injury and surgery and the rehab to be able to go right now at this point at the start of camp, how significant is that for you? What do you mean? Are you asking like how I feel or >> Yeah. After after going through everything with with the surgery and rehab to be 100% as camp starts, how does that sit with you? I mean, obviously >> it's No, it's it's a blessing. You know, it's an absolute blessing. I feel great. Um, you know what I mean? There's a lot of, you know, the physical part is the physical part. You know, you're going to have to go through the grueling rehab. I mean, first two months of offseason, I'm I literally can't bend my knee and I'm in a cast. I can't I mean, you could hardly sleep. I I couldn't I literally couldn't sleep for about a month and a half or so. Um cuz you can't move your leg, you can't walk, can't put any pressure on it. And like I'm so used to being so like self-sufficient and self-reliant on stuff and I got to ask everyone around me like and I feel like an irritant. You know what I mean? Like that that part of it that nobody really gets to see is like Rachel's, you know, doing double triple time taking care of the baby and she's also taking care of me. I'm like a big ass baby. I'm stuck on a damn couch. I can't do anything. And you know what I mean? It's like that those those are the things that people don't really get to see. Um and the you know the emotional the mental part of it. Um and it it forces you to you know make a choice of like how you're going to attack you know the whole process. So you know it's been I don't know over 7 months now and you know we're out here and the goal was the goal and you know we're we're out here flying and I I feel incredible and it's it's not just me you know what I mean? It's obviously I'm the one that's got to do, you know, all the work, but ultimately um there's so many good people in my corner that um helped me along, you know, the process this off seasonason and I can go on and on about those those guys, but um I didn't do it alone and obviously Ra being, you know, the mother of the year and, you know, wife of the year taking care of me and helping me during the whole thing was incredible. So, um it's a blessing, man. I love this game. And, you know, I heard all the noise and and all those things, but you know, everyone knows like my back's against the wall. That's that's when I'm at my best. I love the pressure. That's what I live and thrive on. So, um it just added added points and gives me a little bit more reason to go out there and and whoop past. >> Turn around, Max. A quick turnaround coming back to Vegas. What does this city mean to you now after everything you've been through this off season? >> Yeah, I mean it's I I love the city. You know, ever since I've been out here, it's just been it's been incredible. You know, Las Vegas is the greatest city in the world in my opinion. you know, I've been in a lot of places and, you know, they've always had my back and it's not just Vegas, it's Oakland, it's LA, it's, you know, Raider Nation runs deep. It's all over all over the world. So, um, all the fans supporting me, I appreciate it. And, um, you know, everybody that shows up, you know, we want all the fans to fill that that Allegiance Stadium with silver and black, you know what I mean, not all the other colors. And, um, that's up to us as a players and organization to, you know, win a lot more football games so that, you know, that happens. >> We get into a report five days early for camp. How much did you benefit from >> I thought it was awesome. You know, I was actually really excited about that just so I can kind of get a head start on on the vets. You know, I I didn't have any OTAA reps. Like I didn't have I haven't played football since literally last year. So, um I was excited to get back in the building, kind of get warmed up again, get back out there. I did a walk through on Friday, um you know, with all the rookies and you know, doing all the you know, all the workouts and stuff with the rookies. So, um, I felt like a felt like a rookie again, which is a little weird, but, um, it was awesome. You know, just kind of get my feet wet, you know, before the vets get got in town. >> And Max, right on that, you're talking about, you know, being here with the rookies. Uh, it's very well known that you like to mentor, you know, you hold Sack Summit. How does it feel to mentor this new group of young guys and what does that mean to you? >> Um, it means, you know, it means the world. You know, we need everybody um to win and we're ultimately we're here to win. You know, we're all on the on this path together. um whether you're a rookie or a 10-year guy, it doesn't it doesn't matter. You know, you got to come in with the mindset that you're going to help, you know, win football games. So, I think this rookie class has been awesome so far. Um we'll learn a lot about everybody, you know, you know, more as as this, uh camp goes on and season goes on, but so far they've been awesome. Um I think we have, you know, the right character guys, but ultimately we got dogs, you know what I mean? There's a lot of guys that play football at a high level and they got to you know prove that you know to the to the vets and to the um to these coaches and you know I feel like they're doing a good job of that. I think the work ethic when you know that's one of the hardest things either you know you come in with that mindset you're going to put in the work or you're you know entitled and think you you know got the answers. I don't see any of that um with these rookies. So they've been awesome. I've I've got to spend a ton of time with them. I' like I said I feel like a rookie. I've I've been at the M hotel and doing my thing. You know, I'm the only vet there. So, it's me and all the rookies has been for it feels like for a while now and and and they've been they've been awesome. >> Sam, last question. Last question. Sam, >> Max, can you just talk a little bit about your mindset entering this year and are you a guy that kind of sets personal goals for yourself? >> Yeah, my mindset is, you know, I want to be the greatest at what I do, period. Um, write it in my journal every day. I want to be the best in the world at my job, and my profession. And, uh, that's why I work the way I work. Um it's going to take every single one of us. Um obviously it's it's all about the team. We want to win and ultimately that's all that matters. So me doing my part and some is something I'm going to push for every single day and and you know greatness is measured by how many people you inspire. So I want to bring as many guys with me and uh as many coaches as many people in general that I can um you know raise their standard and way of you know thinking. You know, I feel like ultimately you have, you know, every day you have 24 hours to make a decision. You know what I mean? You could push things down the line or all right, tomorrow I'll put put in that little bit of extra work or I'll, you know, maybe next week I'll do the extra running. Like, no, you know what I mean? You got to do it every single day and have that mindset where you're going to have growth on a consistent basis. And, um, I feel like you can accomplish anything in the world. So, my mindset coming into this, like like I said, like obviously everyone's talking about he's got a chip on his shoulder. I always got a chip on my shoulder no matter what. So, um, yeah, of course I felt, you know, the whole situation, talked about it a million times. I'm, you know, done talking about it, but yeah, of course, there's added, you know, added, you know, u motivation, but it's beautiful. At the same time, I love being doubted. I love being told I can't do something because I know I'm going to go to the end of the world to make it happen. All right. Thanks, Max. Appreciate it. Holy

title: Justin Herbert & Derwin James On Training Camp Day 1 | LA Chargers
text: Just in first day here today, is it different? Is your Does your approach change? >> No, the approach doesn't change. You know, it's always business and it's good to see everyone back and you know, I thought we got great work in this off-season and you know, looking forward to putting a a camp together and I'm looking forward to a good season. >> What What are your conversations with Mike McDaniel been like? >> Just in the quarterback room, out on the field and you know, listening to any advice he's got for me. Just still picking up the offense, doing everything I can to to master it and he's got a great feel for the position and and the offense. So, you know, he's he's been such an honor to work with. >> Just what's that process like picking up this offense? Where do you think you are right now? I know it's day one of camp, but you've had the playbook for a bit. >> Yeah, you know, I thought having the off-season and then a month off was great to be able to go through our iPads, look exactly at everything that we need to and and you know, go through it a second time in camp and I think guys have picked it up really quickly and a lot of the rookies have as well. So, that's always a good thing and definitely fast to go out there and just go play football and and you know, I thought that was really great to see today. >> What are your odds of getting in some pre-season games this year? >> Sorry, can you repeat that? >> What are your odds of getting some reps in pre-season? >> I don't know. I I think coach Harbaugh would have a better feel for that, but I'm not opposed to it at all and whatever he he says, you know, I'm good with. >> How did everything feel timing wise with the adjusted stance? >> Yeah, that was good. You know, definitely had you know, a few weeks to work on it as well when I was back home and you know, I thought it was a great time to be able to you know, master in my my footwork and and then to come back out and just play fast and not have to worry about it. I thought it was really helpful. >> What are you doing with Tyreek Hill and I saw you guys almost connected on that deep ball across the middle. I know it's early, but has he impressed you at all with his speed? >> He's going to be very good. Um we we saw it early on that he was going to be um He's he's skilled, he's fast, he's he's going to make a lot of plays for us. So, I'm really excited about him. >> Justin, is there something about Ben Herbert that sets him apart in his role from others you've dealt with? >> Yeah, maybe just his first name, but um I think uh you know, he's done so He's done such a great job and and uh his motto of making people harder to break is is is so true and we we go into the weight room and and he's so dialed in and so focused that uh you know, he's about as focused and um as hardcore as I've seen a strength coach and I I think that's exactly what we need, guys. Take it very serious in there and uh you know, we get better, we get faster and stronger and and that's all you can ask for. >> Did you know anything about him as a player? >> I did not, actually. Um but I will do my research. >> Did you have more anxiety around the proposal or your first NFL start? >> Uh the proposal, for sure. >> Are there any things in particular that help you like stay focused on football or you know, block out outside noise when you need to? >> Um I think practice is a great opportunity for that. I I think going through practice and understanding that it's rep by rep, one play at a time. Um never look too far ahead, never look back and um do your job at each play and I think that's been really helpful for me. >> When you go home, who do you throw to? >> Uh my younger brother. Um he's on the practice squad with the Jags right now and uh great tight end, great target and uh he never gets tired of catching passes. So, he's always good to have around. >> So, you don't have to go to him to get any extra >> No, he's always asking me to go out there. So, yeah, he's uh he's driven and um good brother to have. >> Thought that you put into the timing of the proposal. I wanted to just quickly as opposed to say during the season. >> Yeah, I thought about it a lot. >> to prepare for your first start? >> For sure. That was a >> Did you have 90 seconds for your first start? >> Not even, probably. >> [laughter] >> That's good. What do you uh, expect to learn about the offensive system through training camp? Because obviously, you know, you guys had spring practices, but there's no pads on. It's hard to maybe glean as much from the running game or even maybe the play action game. So, what are you sort of expecting to learn that you maybe weren't able to learn during the spring? >> I think more full speed reps. I think being able to see it, um, with an offensive line, with, you know, a defense flying around there. I think that's you do your best to, uh, understand the offense, work through it, and then you go through live practice, and and I think that's the the best opportunity about camp is everyone's going full speed, everyone's trying to get better, and, um, to have those opportunities, that's when we really get our work in. >> Did you feel like doing working on the footwork by yourself during summer break, did you feel like you got like more polished at it, like significantly better, like compare like where you were at the end of OTAs to maybe now based on that work that you did by yourself over the >> Yeah, you just get to the point where you're not thinking about it, and, uh, you go out to practice, and you're just throwing the ball. And and now you can worry on mechanics, how am I throwing the ball, where is it going, the routes and things like that, where as opposed to, you know, months ago was making sure that your your feet are lined up with the routes, timing. Um, so there was a lot that went into it, but now it's just playing football. >> Today, did you see a difference in terms of when receiving the beginning of the ball, and maybe how that transition could be beneficial? >> Yeah, I think there was a few reps today where, um, you know, you're playing in time, and they're given the ball in an opportunity where they can turn up field, and they can make something happen. And, um, you always want to avoid throwing late over the middle, and and throwing them into a defender. And so, anytime that I can get Q or Brennan, um, any of those guys opportunity to turn up field, uh, which I I thought we did a couple times today. So, it was good to see in just playing fast and getting the ball out as quick as I can. >> Jim talked earlier about the team having a sense of urgency, something that Sean talked about and some other players this season. Do you feel that there's a sense of urgency to to win this year? >> I think there was always a sense of urgency. I think, uh, you know, every year you're you're doing your best, working as hard as you can, and, um, you know, I think the guys are focused and dialed in this year, and, um, you know, I thought OTAs went great. Camp, I'm looking forward to all the work that we're going to put in and um, you know, I think guys are really excited about it. >> Does having this be a home Super Bowl add an extra level of incentive? Is it something that you've thought about? >> Um I think we're kind of focused on camp right now and each practice as they come they're um you know, they're intense and and they require a lot of focus and so for us to be able to take it one practice at a time you stack that stack enough practices like that, you know, you never know where you're going to find yourself. So that's our focus right now. >> When we talked to like Rashad and Joe guys like they say they can't wait for the pads to get on. Is that something that you look forward to as well? First game guys. >> Yeah, I don't I don't mind it. I don't really have to tackle or hit anyone with them. So I whether I'm throwing without pads or with pads doesn't make too much of a difference to me. But I think it's cool. Especially for those guys running the ball, tackling, you know, it's part of football that you can't get without pads. So I think it's helpful for them. >> In this offense who are you excited to see the most in that is going to benefit from it? I mean besides yourself but like I mean your the weaponry that you have. >> With pads? >> Or just like in being in this offense in general. >> Oh yeah. Like who do you think is going to >> Yeah, I think I think the receivers and the tight ends are going to you know, benefit hugely. I think Brennan and Q, DD, those guys that are just so talented and able to you know, break tackles and turn up field and I think um Dave and Charlie you know, we're going to try and get them the ball as quick as we can because they're athletic guys that can turn up field and make stuff happen. So if I do my job of getting them the ball early, you know, I I think that's the best I can do. >> Just how how would you assess how deep you guys are at receiver and tight end as compared to other years you've been under center? You mentioned Brennan but you know, Trey in year two, Q continuing to develop Lad and just a kind of revamped tight ends room. >> Yeah, it's you know, it's a great problem to have to have so many guys like that and you know, I saw it during routes on air today where you know, usually I throw to the the starters and I'm throwing you know, six or seven passes to the receivers and and you just feel comfortable with Trey, Dre, La, DD, and Q, and all these guys, and they've done such a great job of picking up a an offense so quickly, and um you know, they've they're all they all have different skill sets, and so I think it's so helpful to to an offense to have all those types of guys. >> Are there certain goals or benchmarks you want to hit by the end of preseason or even just today goals you came in with? >> Um I think getting the ball out as as quick as I can, you know, it's something Mike and I have have talked about of avoiding sacks, avoiding hits, things like that. So, um you know, it's on me to play in timing, get the ball out quickly, and uh allow the receivers to to turn upfield. >> Does some of the lot of this stuff hinges on the ability of the offensive line to protect you. How have you What's your feeling about those guys, the guys that are coming back from injury and that sort of thing? That's got to be a key role for >> Yeah, it's it's an incredible group of guys. You know, I'm so fortunate to play behind that offensive line, and um you know, it's on me. It takes everyone. It takes the tight ends, running backs working on protection, and um you know, they're smart. They're they're incredibly athletic as well, and it's a great group of guys that uh I feel comfortable with talking about um and when we get to line of scrimmage, everyone's working as one, and uh then it's my job to get the ball out, step up, find the soft spot in the pocket. Um so, I'm looking forward to it. >> Just the Mike McDaniel's energy at practice is noticeable. He runs around or talking to different players or you putting them through warm-ups. What's it like to experience a coordinator with that much energy? >> Yeah, he loves what he does. He loves football. He loves being here, and he he loves his team, so it's it's really cool to be a part of, and um you know, it makes everyone want to work harder for him, and and the respect that we have for him as a coach and as a as a a teacher and a um you know, as a person. Um you know, we're really fortunate to play for him. >> How would you describe your relationship with him? I know it's early, but what's it been like over time since he showed you that hot topic of plays and stuff? >> Yeah, it's awesome. I've I've really enjoyed playing for him and and talking with him and um you know I could tell that we were going to get along really well early on and he's he's been great. He comes into the quarterback room all the time, talks to us, hangs out with us and it's definitely good to have a guy like that around. >> What was it about him that made you realize early on that you guys would get along well? >> Just personality-wise, you know, I think how much he cares about football, his family, things like that. I thought we were really similar you know, I could tell that I was really excited to play for him. >> Jim says that you and him are the smart you and Mike are the two smartest people he knows and you guys get talking about football he sometimes doesn't know what you guys are even talking about. What is that? What do you think he means by that? >> I would say Mike is definitely the the smartest. I I appreciate that coach but I don't think I'm quite there yet. I think it's just a feel for the offense and talking about how you see things and you know, I think coach Harbaugh has has such a great feel for the game too cuz he played and he's he's played for so long and understands pressure and and you know, blitzes and things like that and and throwing behind an offensive line. And so I think it's really cool to be to be able to have both of those coaches that have different backgrounds, different understandings of the game but have both been so successful and to have two guys like that I think it's really helpful. >> Do you think it helps having somebody that's been in the trenches like Jim different than like maybe somebody who had a coach who has never played before? >> Yeah, I think it's really helpful. I think you know, there's so much to football that you can only learn by being out there and and going through it and I think he's seen it all, he's coached it all, he's he's he's done everything, he's been at the highest level. He's been at college and you know, I think he's he's gained so much experience as a coach, as a player that he's just got a great feel and so I love being able to talk with him about it and and all the great things he's got about football, life and everything else he talks about. >> I know it's only day one but the relationship with Tyler the obvious stuff how's that going? >> It's been great. Uh, Tyler has been awesome. As soon as he came in here we got some snaps, and it was like we'd he'd we'd taken a bunch of snaps together. Um, you know, he's he's he's smooth, consistent, and um, you know, he's a great offensive lineman, great center, very good communicator, um, and definitely a very smart man. >> With the tight ends, Justin, it just seems like it's a position of varying styles, strengths. How is similar or different is is this year's room now compared to last year's, but just in terms of having Charlie and and David versus sort of what you had in the past? Does it feel different and ask him, you know, what Mike and David asked him to do? Is that Is that different than what you've had in the past? >> Yeah, I think it's it's really cool to have Charlie and David. They're both so talented, and being able to throw to them, um, in camp and and today, you can just tell that, you know, they're different players. They're they're fun, they're very athletic, and you know, I think they're going to add a whole 'nother dimension to our offense. >> Do you think Charlie's been [snorts] kind of underrated in terms of what Did you get a chance to see what he did at Iowa State versus what the Ravens asked him to do and kind of how you visualize or envision his role in this offense? >> Yeah, I'd watched him for the past, you know, I think he's been in the league for 4 years, maybe 5. Um, I've always thought he was very talented, and I I see him run routes and what he's able to do, run blocking, pass blocking, and uh, you know, I think he's going to have a a very good year. He's very talented, and I'm really excited to get him the ball. >> How did it go today? >> It [clears throat] was amazing. It felt like the first day of school, for sure. >> What's different about this season? How does it feel different, or what do you think it is? >> I'd say the confidence that we had in the spring and uh, building up from there, and then just the coaches and the depth we have. I feel like uh, it it's been good. >> We see you working out with a lot of the younger players, but what kind of things do you talk to them about? >> Uh, just trying to give them the experience that I have, uh, just playing. It's my ninth season, so it's just trying to pass down any knowledge that I can, cuz I know when you're younger, your brain is kind of moving fast. You're just trying to get it right, so just trying to help them in any way I can. >> What do you think about this third safety battle that's going on? You you're closer to nickel. You got a bunch of guys back there. You got Tony, you got R.J. going on second year. You got Dennis as a rookie. What's your What's your read on that battle? >> What I like, no one is hating on the next person. Everyone is helping each other even in the meeting rooms, there's things you don't see. Everyone is rooting for the for for each other and it's been a great battle and I feel like we that's a great problem to have. That's what I saying with the depth and all those guys can play and the best guy going to play. >> How was the defending offense today? >> It's good. They're giving us a lot of looks, McDaniels motions, shifts, so playing against a complex offense like that, it makes us better and um I feel like we we we're not at our peak yet, which is which we don't have to be right now. That's what training camp for and I feel like we're getting better every day. >> Have you ever practiced or worked with a coordinator like Mike like you see him running around and talking? Can you describe this experience? >> Uh he's just he's all hands-on. He's I feel like he's almost out there running a route how close he be to the receivers sometimes, but he's he's all he's like three we're about to bomb y'all right here, we're about to bomb y'all and then it'll be a quick game. So he's playing mind games, so it's kind of cool though. >> Vernon, I got to meet a really big fan of yours, Susan Tamala. She's would tell anybody in earshot about how you FaceTimed her a little while ago and she she just got a hug from you. What does it mean to you to hear stories like this from fans when you guys get to interact so close and personal? >> Uh it means a lot, man. Those are the people that are buying the jerseys that are out there supporting us, camping out there, so just to go out there we want to win it for them, you know, not just ourselves and our families, but for them because a lot of people take pride in this team that's why I want to go out there and give them my all. >> What do you think you're going to learn about Seattle as a play caller through training camp? >> Uh confidence, um he's he's not holding back, he's not shy and I feel like a lot of people going get to see who he really is this year and I'm I'm confident in him. >> Like at this stage as a defense do you guys kind of know the wrinkles that he's going to bring to to the system or is there still like a bit of a a process to figure out exactly what that's going to look like. >> I feel like it's a process. I feel like coach Harbaugh's message is like a plane and I feel like, you know, the the roster's at 90 something right now and a lot of guys, you know, is going to get cut to 53. So, I feel like a lot of the stuff we will do game plan wise will be coming up later anyway. So, we just building a base, man. Building a foundation, picking up where we left off from OTAs and I I feel like we're in a great spot. >> How is Chris balanced knowing that you guys have a lot of the same personnel and were very successful last year versus him kind of uniquely putting his own stamp on the defense? >> Um I feel like uh I feel like he's not no one's going in into a into a comfortable like no guys out there comfortable and I feel like every guy's open even coaches is open and he's he's all he listen to the players also. Like he's he want information back from us cuz we out there playing. So, I feel like it's been a great balance of just us and him and he's not putting nothing nothing too much on nobody play. >> There have been a couple contract negotiations and you've gone up to 2020 and had a bit of a holding situation. Any advice for for Tuili as he kind of goes through this process of the business in the NFL? >> Uh it's just the process of it, man. The team loves him. We love Tuili. Like I I knew the team loved me, too, when I had the same similar situation, but sometimes that stuff take longer, you know, to iron out, but man, everyone knows we love Tuili here. I'm pretty sure they love him up there, too, and he loves the team. So, it it'll get worked out. It'll work itself. Mine's got worked out. I was confident in it and I can't wait to have him out there. It's just part of the business, man. >> What did you say to Justin after the proposal? >> I was like, "Oh, man, congrats, man." I was happy for him. I was 27, 8:00 a.m. when I seen it. I was like, "Man." He told me he was going to do it a long time ago, but he finally did it, man. I was it it was fun to see. >> Saw him with a pick today. Just what are you expecting from him and and Cam you know, entering into year three together? >> This year three, this usually when you know, you got to take that next step and I've been telling them, man, year three is a pivotal year. Not to say any year is not pivotal, but I feel like this is kind of how you shape your career on who you going to want to who you're going to be. And I I expressed that to them. And um every day I just try to push them and challenge them in the meeting rooms, uh challenge them to make calls. And um I feel like they they making a lot of plays. They made plays in the spring. Uh even D-Jack, all those guys are making plays. So, the the more guys we can have making plays the the better success we'll have. >> How have those guys responded to that kind of message? >> Oh, they they they took it all in. They they're not like uh getting defensive. They're not getting sensitive. When when when I challenge them, they challenge me back, man. text: How much do you think how much you think six weeks just helped your movement like we saw you move around the pocket you had the scramble today just felt like your off schedule movement was very different than what we saw in the spring. >> Yeah, I feel like I made a lot of good progress last six weeks. Um So, yeah, I think every time you do it, you get more and more you get a little, you know, a little stronger, a little better, a little more uh more used to it. So, um I think those are two two really good players. It makes a big difference uh I think when you have two uh really good corners like that. >> Does it help you throughout camp? Kind of iron sharpens iron type thing? >> Yeah, I mean, I think so. Anytime you're competing against good players, we've got a good defense. They're they're two good players, but we got a lot of good players over there and and Lou does a really good job with his scheme. So, um I think going against them every day helps us um tremendously. >> Daniel, you know, you got a second chance here after you know, things didn't really work out in the past, but you didn't get to finish the job, obviously, because of last year. It's uh it's motivating uh for me just yeah, knowing knowing um you know, how we how we started and and the level I thought, you know, we were we were all playing at um as a team and then you know, we had we had some stuff knock us off, but I think it's motivating for for myself, motivating for all of us to know what we can be um but there's a lot of work that goes into to doing that and sustaining that through an entire season. So, um yeah, I think we're all uh extremely hungry and motivated. >> And you said Monday on uh Pat's show that even if you've been cleared to do everything, that maybe there are still some boxes that you feel like you need to check. What are the What are the things that you're looking for as you go through these practices over the next couple weeks to I guess maybe check any boxes that just haven't been checked yet. >> Yeah, I mean, I think it's just similar to the progression over, you know, the last 6 weeks from mini camp to now. Um I think, you know, you're doing all the same stuff, but just feeling better doing it, feeling quicker, more explosive. Um you know, and that's a that's a process, a gradual process. I think being out there playing football, uh getting those reps, you you get more and more used to it and it'll it'll come. So, um I yeah, I mean, boxes to check, I think it's it's more like a a feel and a I think just feeling a a gradual improvement um over time. >> You guys like in Florida, what do you feel like you got out of that? >> Um yeah, it was great. We had um great participation, tons of guys showed up and um and worked. You know, we got a lot of good work on the field. Um you know, and and uh and it was good. Now you have that time invested with each other working together. Does today feel like a big moment for you? You've been on the field now for a couple months.
