title: Colts head coach Shane Steichen impressed by Daniel Jones, first training camp practice
text: How we doing guys? Great to be back here at Grand Park. Really good first day. Really pleased with the guys effort today. Great energy out there. You know, obviously thanks to Grand Park. We've been here for many years. Obviously before I was even here, but just a tremendous facility that they open up the hospitality Grand Park gives us year in and year out. It's been tremendous and looking forward to another great camp this year here. >> How do you think Daniel looked today throwing around? >> I thought he looked really good. Obviously his first day back, team periods, the way he was throwing the ball, completed a lot of passes, moved well, did some movement stuff with him, handled all that well. So really pleased with where he was at today. >> Can you see you see this progress all through from the surgery on? What do you look for today, tomorrow, a week from now? >> Just consistency with coming back from the injury, you know, gaining that strength back. Obviously he looked pretty good today, but obviously you know, it's day-by-day process with that. But he did a hell of a job today and so we're just going to continue that growth, you know, look through it. >> When he gets flushed out of the pocket and scrambles, do you want to see those little like check boxes? Like you want to see him >> He had one of those today. You know, he got out of the pocket and ran you know, for a few yards there which was really good to see on his first day back. >> In his career, the thing that he's probably been maybe critiqued on is just like year-to-year consistency. Good year followed up with a bad year. What goes into that with a player? >> Well, I think it's just it is it is consistency what you said. I mean it's it's going out and completing passes and putting your you know, team in a position to win every single game. And that's what consistency looks like at the quarterback. It's moving the ball up and down the field. It's getting in and out of the right play, you know, completing passes, keep the chains moving. And he did a hell of a job with that last year and so we're continuing to do that you know, this year. >> So how do you think DJ's rehab, all that has kind of just galvanized the group knowing how hard he worked to get back to this? >> Yeah, I think it means a lot to our group and our guys in that locker room to see the hard work that he's put in to be where he's at right now, you know, doing full team reps, you you eight months, whatever it is post-op from his surgery. Um it's a credit to him and the work that he's put in to be able to be out here to start training camp. Um it's it's pretty impressive. >> And Buckner's well, I mean, neck surgery at the end of December. He's I mean, not in 11s, but he's he's back. >> Yeah, he's back, you know, and he's worked really hard as well. You know, those guys that I always say, the guys that work hard, you know, guys that play in this league for a long time, they have a level of consistency. Um it's really what it comes down to. The hard work, the effort they put in, it's no surprise these guys play for as long as they have. And when they go through injuries, um those guys that are committed to getting back, they do everything in their power to do it. And Buckner's one of those guys, and so I'm not surprised that he's back out here, either. Obviously, we're going to work him back in slowly as this thing gets going. Um but it's awesome to see him back out here. >> Do you have a timeline on when you would expect to be able to get him back into 11s, or what are you looking for talking to him about? >> Yeah, that's a good question. We're going to play that by ear with him. You know, we want to get him to week one, for sure, obviously. So, we'll be smart with him. Um that'll be a conversation with myself, the trainers, and him, too. It's his body. Um but working him back into individual drills right now, and then see where that goes, you know, throughout training camp. >> How are things going at wide receiver? I mean, you had some interesting combinations out there, a little different. >> Yeah, for sure. Right now, you know, we've got moving parts right there, and guys are moving around, and uh you know, got to step up. And there's some competition in that room right right now that we're excited about, but um excited about Downs right now, you know, obviously, a guy that can play inside and outside now for us, and his role's going to improve um this season for us, which we're excited about, and um Duece's a guy that's got to step up, and Treadwell, and Westbrook, and the rest of those guys. So, I'm excited about that group, and they're going to compete like crazy during training camp. >> And in Josh's first year, in particular, we saw the explosive plays from him, maybe a little less last year. Is there more of that that you guys can get to? >> Yeah, I think so, absolutely. I think, um you know, when you look at the room right now, obviously, Tyler Boyd was a big piece of our offense last year. Um and so, that was an another element that, you know, probably took away. You got one football, you got a lot of guys to get the targets to. So, um you You losing Pitt was, you know, hard. Um so, there's got to guys that got to step up. And Downs is going to be one of those guys that's going to step up for us this year. >> Obviously different story lines this year, but compared day one this year to day one last year, what's your level of excitement, confidence in this team? >> Well, I was really excited. I was really pleased really with day one practice. Uh, it was really smooth. Uh, really really no mental errors. You know, it was pretty clean. I thought the guys flew around a lot of plays on both sides of the ball. You know, having Sauce and Mooney back out there together, um, with the ones, those guys were both making plays on day one, which was awesome to see. Offense made some good plays. JT had some huge runs. Um, overall I thought it was really clean. >> You're in your fourth year. You're in your fourth year at the year. You guys didn't have any major coaching changes. Um, most of the starting offense is the same as last year. What is that level of consistency year to year? Uh, how's that helping you guys kind of hit the day one >> It's a great question. I think it's huge. I think it's very beneficial. Just even the way we started practice today with Daniel coming back, the offensive line intact, the tight end, the running back. I mean, there are some checks at the line of scrimmage that Daniel made to get us into the right play, which we hit some big plays today. And that doesn't just happen. That's come from reps and being together and the consistency and everyone being on the same page. So, I'm very excited for that. >> When you go into camp knowing who your starting quarterback is, does that help get you guys um, further down the road building the offense or working guys in? >> Yeah, good question. No doubt about that. Yeah, there's no doubt about it. So, obviously knowing Daniel's our guy going into this year, um, the conversations that are taking place, um, with the offense and how it evolves through training camp and during the season, um, is going to be big for us. >> Moving from safety, what went into >> Um, you know, Ben's Ben's kind of a jack-of-all-trades. He's a Swiss Army knife. Um, he does a lot of different things for us, uh, through special teams last year on the scout team. So, playing safety, you know, obviously you have so many, uh, you know, practice squad players. And so he would go both ways for us, uh, last year. And he made a ton of plays, uh, on the scout team. And so we switched him over to offense. Um, so it was exciting to see him out there. He had a catch today. Um, he's going to continue improve and grow in that role. >> Shane, you just have Are you going to rotate AR and Riley? >> Yeah, those guys Yeah, those guys will rotate. You know, I'm really pleased with where AR is at coming off the eye injury, you know, in the spring and then going into training camp. And Riley, too, making good strides as well. So, those guys will rotate. Those guys compete. And I'm looking forward to that competition with those two guys. >> Denzel Tucker, I think going back to the spring he's had a few of those those high snaps. I mean, he's a talented guy. How do you get that under control? >> I think it's reps. It's repetition. It's really what it comes down to. Obviously, getting those reps, you got to go through it. You know what I mean? And there's going to be some of those snaps, some bad snaps, but that's what practice is for and you know, we got to work through those and you know, be consistent doing it. >> Can you just talk about Kaden Curry and what I can infer with those guys on the offensive team? >> Yeah, I think Kaden Curry, first and foremost, you know, a tremendous player. Had a hell of a career at Ohio State. Obviously, a local kid here. But saw a lot of good things in the spring from him. Very smart, cerebral guy. Understands it. I think he's got really good instincts, as well. So, I'm really looking forward to seeing him come out here and compete, you know, in this training camp and earn a spot and earn a role on this team. >> Looks like we've got a couple more. >> Will he be one of those places where we're looking for guys like Kaden? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, some of those guys, that's how it works out, right? You play special teams and then you earn your role. You see it all around the league, but you never know how this thing plays out. You know what I mean? He could step up early and be a guy for us on defense. You never know. >> You guys yesterday about talking about finishing at the end of the season. What are you guys implementing on day one to kind of get to that point? >> Well, I think it's a little bit We talked about developing a find a way mindset. You know, that's really what it comes down to is finding a way and it's my job as a coach, you know, during practice to put those guys in position, right? To develop that mindset, you know, and that starts in training camp. It's always about, you know, establishing our identity, who you're going to be as a football team. You know, tough, physical, fast, all those, you know, coaching cliches you hear, but it is the truth. We got to go do that every single day. Bring great energy. Be elite communicators at everything we do, day in and day out, so we can get to where we want to go. >> You mentioned last one here. >> Saw some Moody. I think that kid sitting in the game they really play wires together. Lots was talking about how >> they could tell like Pat was frustrated through that game because of those guys. Do you remember that? And I don't know what do you take away from that and hoping to spin forward to this year? >> Well, you got two guys that have been All-Pro players at points in their career. And they're really elite players. So, to have two elite corners that can lock down a guy one-on-one on the outside is going to be huge and beneficial, you know, for our defense. So, I'm really looking forward to those guys being out there together, you know, for the full season. >> Okay. All right, thanks. Jonathan Taylor's on next here. >> All right, thanks, guys. >> Appreciate you.

title: Indianapolis Colts Training Camp: Daniel Jones practices with no restrictions
text: Hey, there Colts fans. We are back for day one of the Colts training camp for the 2026 season. We're here at Graham Park. I'm Nathan Brown, one of your Indy Star Colts insiders here with Joel A. Erickson. The big story of the day today, of course, Daniel Jones back a full participant on the field for day one of training camp. Not even yet 8 months removed from tearing his right Achilles. Uh we got to see him scramble. We got to see him um run around in the pocket a little bit. Looked a lot like the Daniel Jones of old. >> Yeah, I I thought there was a big difference between what we saw in the spring to what we saw now. In the spring when he moved, it was still a little herky-jerky, not real smooth. Uh he could move and do some stuff, but it it kind of looked a little bit ginger. Today, you know, he we saw him roll left. We saw him roll right. Um he didn't quite throw great uh on his move left. I don't know if that was a movement thing or just he didn't really have a receiver open on the play. But the scramble was another one. He said, you know, he kind of wondered if Shane Steichen would be mad at him. He didn't. Um It's it's remarkable the way Achilles tendon injuries work now, but it does seem like he's in a much better spot. Although I think he does have some somewhere to go still. >> Yeah, and we've got still several weeks. We're about 6 weeks removed from the start of this season. He said that internally um from a strength strength standpoint, a mobility standpoint, there's still maybe some internal boxes for him to check, but he participated in 11-on-11 drills for the first time since he tore that Achilles um in Jacksonville on December 7th. Again, we're still more than a week away from even hitting that 8-month mark. Not long ago, this felt like um a year-long injury process, and now we're not even short of 9 months, [snorts] we're short of 8 months. Um and he feels back to um the the old Daniel Jones. He did not say if he will participate in preseason games. He said that's going to be up to Shane Steichen, so we'll see uh where the organization goes with that. Um but uh a great at least a great day one for him. What more do you feel like you're looking to see or would like to see from him as we get through the next couple days camp? >> strength in the calf. He was moving well today, but I do think you can see a little bit that he's not quite the same. He said he still has to get some strength back in the calf. It's going to be harder to do that now that he's doing football. Um but and you got meetings and everything like that. You can't focus as much time on the calf, but I do think that's the key and you kind of have to get it done before the season cuz once you get in the season there's going to be other injuries and nagging stuff you have to deal with. It's going to be a little tough. I forgot to tell Nathan about this. We did it last year. I'm going to give you my play of the day real quick. Uh Trey Washington making a pick on Riley Leonard. Leonard held the ball too much uh too long today. Uh it cost him Trey Washington sliding under a receiver to make a pick. That's my play of the day from the first day. >> I liked that um late practice Daniel Jones scramble out to the right. It reminded me a lot of some of the plays that we saw uh in his last truly healthy game in uh uh in Europe against the Falcons. There were a couple big plays there and there was no hesitation today. He took off. There were was spent some time looking for receivers. Um decided there was no one there. Immediately made the decision to go toward that right sideline. Um probably would have been close to a first down if we were really tracking all of that closely. Um and looked a lot like some of those big play moments that he had right before some of these injuries started to derail his uh 2025 season. >> Four days of practice in a row to start. We're going to be here for all of them. For the New Star, I'm Joe L Ericson. This is Nathan Brown. >> I will. >> How much do you think How much do you think six weeks just helped your movement? I mean we saw you move around the pocket. You had to scramble today. It just felt like your off-schedule movement was very different than what we saw in the spring. >> Yeah, I feel like I made a lot of good progress last six weeks. Um yeah, last time I spoke to y'all I was cleared to do stuff, but still I think um there's a process in you know getting back and feeling more comfortable getting some of the strength some of the twitch back, and um yeah, felt good out there today. Um and I'll continue to make steps kind of throughout camp. >> Daniel, in the spring, what did you have? >> [snorts] >> Now you were kind of on restrictions in the spring. How grateful were you for that just that moment, the ability to not have Shane basically tell you, "Don't do that." >> Uh yeah, I was wondering if he was going to say something to me afterwards. He did He didn't, but uh yeah, I felt felt good. I mean, that's stuff that I've done a lot, you know, you you build it into your drill work, into, you know, your your rehab, and and all that uh stuff I've been doing. So, uh felt good doing it, and it's good to be able to do it in the more uh football setting. >> Have you noticed the start working drill scramble work like that back into things? I know this is the first time we saw you do it do it in 11 on 11s, but >> Yeah, I mean, I was doing that in the spring uh with the trainers and with the uh with everybody here. So, um yeah, I mean, it's something like I've been cleared to do for a long time, but like, you know, like I said, it gets better and better the more you do it, and and kind of build the strength back, build the the twitch back, and um yeah, so it definitely feels better than it did 6 weeks ago. >> Have you been working on your timeline, whatever you want to call it, that you'll do things in practice that you're used to doing, and you don't think about it, or you get confidence in pivoting and rolling out that maybe you had to have confidence to do that again or not? >> Uh yeah, I think um I had, you know, have confidence in it, you know, it's not not a uh not a lack of confidence necessarily. I think it's just building the building the strength back, you know, and and building the repetition, and um you know, getting your body used to doing it again. Um so, yeah, I think every time you do it, you get more and more you get a little, you know, a little stronger, a little better, a little more uh more used to it. So, you know, like I said, I'll continue to do that over this training camp, over the 6-week period before we before we play our first game. >> Daniel, do you want to play in the preseason, and how will you convince Shane to actually let you do that? >> Um yeah, I mean that's that's up to Shane, you know, that's that's Shane's call and and um I'll be ready, you know, I I feel good and and um but that's, you know, a team decision in a lot of ways and and Shane makes those, so um whatever he decides I'll be good with. >> [laughter] >> I don't I mean I don't know. I mean I think um you know, we got we got a few weeks to figure that out. >> The point of having guys like Sauce and Wooly together is to make life difficult for quarterbacks. So, lined up against them, what's been your impression of them together so far? >> Yeah, I mean good. I think um for one, their length and size I think is a huge a huge part of playing against them and and um their building ability to disrupt receivers at the line or at the top of their break or uh throughout the route, so um I think those are two two really good players. It makes a big difference uh I think when you have two uh really good corners like that. >> Does that help you throughout camp? >> I think so. >> Iron sharpens iron type thing? >> Yeah, I mean I think so. Anytime you're competing against good players, we've got a good defense. They're they're two good players, but we got a lot of good players over there and and Lou does a really good job with his scheme, so um I think going against them every day helps us um tremendously. >> And you know, you got a second chance here at you know, things maybe didn't work out in the past, but you get the first job obviously but the last year. I mean how much does that aspect motivate you at all? Just You came here you know, to be their guy and to get the first one. >> Yeah, I think absolutely. It's uh it's motivating uh for me just yeah, knowing knowing um you know, how we how we started and and the level I thought, you know, we were we were all playing at um as a team and then um you know, we had we had some stuff knock us off, but I think it's motivating for for myself, motivating for all of us to know what we can be, um but there's a lot of work that goes into to doing that and sustaining that through an entire season. So, um, yeah, I think we're all, uh, extremely hungry and motivated. >> I know you said I know you said Monday on, uh, Pat show that even if you've been cleared to do everything that maybe there are still some boxes that you feel like you need to check. What are the What are the things that you're looking for as you go through these practices over the next couple weeks to, I guess, maybe check any boxes that just haven't been checked? >> Yeah, I mean, I think it's just similar to the progression over, you know, the last 6 weeks from mini camp to now. Um, I think, you know, you're doing all the same stuff, but just feeling better doing it, feeling quicker, more explosive. Um, you know, and that's a that's a process, a gradual process. I think being out there, playing football, uh, getting those reps, you you get more and more used to it and it'll it'll come. So, um, I yeah, I mean, boxes to check, I think it's it's more like a a feel and a um, I think just feeling a a gradual improvement, um, over time. >> Daniel, Florida a few days like in Florida, what do you feel like you got out of that? >> Um, yeah, it was great. Uh, we had, um, great participation, tons of guys showed up and um, and worked, you know, we had a lot of good work on the field. Um, you know, and and, uh, and it was good. I think those those trips are valuable for the time on the field, but probably more so for the time off the field where you're, uh, hanging out, going to dinner, uh, you know, play golf and just spending time together, you know, outside the facility. So, um, you know, really appreciative of all the, you know, the, you know, one, the participation, the energy, how excited guys were to do it, and, um, I think it was a a valuable trip for us. >> Daniel, let's take a couple more. >> New season, new camp, certainly, but given the way that you guys started the season last year, in particular offensively, what are the things that you're trying to replicate and do, but then also improve upon so you're able to sustain it even more effectively too. >> Yeah, I mean, I think every year's every year's new and and we've got to we've got to start from from square one, you know, and that's what today was. I mean, that's what the spring was, but that's what today is, too. So, you know, we'll start and and we'll have you know, a lot of the same guys are back, so we'll we'll start to um accentuate their strengths and and what they're good at and and help them uh you know, put them in the right position to make plays and then, you know, we've got some new guys and we got um you know, a different different feel in some ways, too. So, we'll look to um look to make the most of that, as well, but I don't think it's about recreating anything. I think we've got to look to to build it and uh make sure we're ready to go. >> You mentioned the change of the order you would change that you spent a lot of time together by this time last year, obviously, but it was your first year. >> Now you have that time invested with each other, working together. How much more of an understanding and you know, speaking the same language you kind of have working together >> Yeah, I mean, I think, you know, obviously, you feel like you're a little bit ahead of where you you know, where where we were last year. you know, learning the offense and and you know, I was competing to play, you know, splitting reps, so um I think, yeah, it it it's helpful to have that experience underneath you, things to reference, um things that have worked in the past. I I mean, you just accumulate a certain amount of reps and experiences and um I think that's helpful to uh to build kind of on, you know, build on going forward and and seeing what we're going to what we're going to do and what we're going to emphasize um at this point. I think, you know, obviously, you're a little bit ahead of of where you were this year this time last year. >> I know you want to talk about the fact that you were >> the last one there >> in 11-on-11 work um today. Did today feel like a big moment for you? You've been on the field now for a couple months. Did it like Was this a a big moment for you this morning getting back and actually getting to do that or does it just kind of feel like another day? >> Um I I it definitely was a goal of mine to be back for the first day of training camp, so you know, there's some satisfaction in in that and and being back for the first day. But, it's still a process, you know, there's still still a lot of work to be done personally, you know, with my with my process and then as a team. So, we're just starting out and and it's good to have a you know, important to have a good first day, but there's a lot of work ahead of us. >> Going back to December and January, at what point did doing this and accomplishing this feel like a realistic goal for you? >> I mean, I felt like it was realistic from the from the beginning, you know, I think after talking to doctor you know, the doctors and trainers, PT. I felt like it was realistic as long as I you know, stuck to the program and and you know, checked all the all the marks along the way. So, yeah, that was my goal from the beginning. >> Hey guys, uh great to be back um here at Grand Park. Uh really good first day. I'm really pleased with the guys effort today. Great energy out there. Um you know, obviously thanks to Grand Park. We've been here for many years obviously before I was even here, but just a tremendous facility uh that they open up the hospitality Grand Park gives us year in and year out. It's been tremendous and looking forward to another great camp this year here. >> How did you think Daniel looked today just moving around? [clears throat] >> I thought he looked really good. Um obviously his first day back team periods the way he was throwing the ball completed a lot of passes moved well did some movement stuff with him handled all that well. So, really pleased with where he was at today. >> You've seen you've seen his progress all through from the surgery on. What do you look for today, tomorrow, a week from now? >> Just consistency with coming back from the injury, you know, gaining that strength back. Obviously, he looked pretty good today, but obviously, you know, it's day-by-day process with that. But, he did a hell of a job today and so we're just going to continue that growth you know, and look through it. >> When he gets flushed out of pocket and scrambles, do you You to see those little like check boxes like you want >> Yeah, absolutely. had one of those today. Um you know, he got out of the pocket and ran, you know, for a few yards there, which was really good to see on his first day back. >> In his career, I mean, the thing that he's probably been maybe critiqued on is just like year-to-year consistency, you know, good year followed up with a good year. Like, what goes into that? >> Well, I think it's just It is. It is consistency, what you said. I mean, it's it's going out and completing passes and putting your, you know, team in a position to win every single game. And that's what consistency looks like at the quarterback. It's moving the ball up and down the field and getting in out of the right play, you know, completing passes, keep the chains moving. Um and he did a hell of a job with that last year, and so we're going to continue to do that, you know, this year. >> So, how do you think DJ's rehab, all that, has kind of just galvanized the group, knowing how hard he worked to get back to this day? >> Yeah, I think it means a lot to our group and our guys in that locker room to see the hard work that he's put in to be where he's at right now, you know, doing full team reps, you know, 8 months, whatever it is, post-op from his surgery. Um it's a credit to him and the work that he's put in to be able to be out here to start training camp. Um it's it's pretty impressive. >> DeForest Buckner as well. I mean, neck surgery at the end of December. He's I mean, not in 11s yet, but he's he's back. >> Yeah, he's back, you know, and he's worked really hard as well, you know, those guys that I always say the guys that work hard, you know, guys that play in this league for a long time, they have a level of consistency. Um it's really what it comes down to. The hard work, the effort they put in. It's no surprise these guys play for as long as they have. And when they go through injuries, um those guys that are committed to getting back, they do everything in their power to do it. And Buckner's one of those guys, and so I'm not surprised that he's back out here either. Obviously, we're going to work him back in slowly as this thing gets going. Um but it's awesome to see him back out here. >> Do you have a timeline on when you would expect to be able to get him back into 11s, or what are you looking for, talking to him about? >> Yeah, that's a good question. We're going to play that by ear with him. You know, we want to get him to week one for sure, obviously. So, we'll be smart with him. Um that'll be a conversation with myself, the trainers, and him, too. It's his body. Um but working him back into individual drills right now, and then see where that goes, you know, throughout training camp. >> How much is going on at wide receiver? I mean, you had some interesting combinations out there a little bit there. >> Yeah, for sure. Right now, you know, we've got moving parts right there and guys are moving around and you know, got to step up and there's some competition in that room right now right now that we're excited about, but excited about Downs right now, you know, obviously a guy that can play inside and outside now for us and his role is going to improve this season for us, which we're excited about and Dulan is a guy that's got to step up and Treadwell and Westbrook and the rest of those guys. So, I'm excited about that group and they're going to compete like crazy here in training camp. >> And in Josh's first year in particular, we saw the explosive plays from him, maybe a little less last year. Is there more of that that you guys can get to? >> Yeah, I think so, absolutely. I think you know, when you look at the room right now, obviously Tyler Warren was a big piece of our offense last year and so that was an another element that you know, probably took away. You got one football, you got a lot of guys to get the targets to. So, you know, obviously losing Pitt was you know, hard. So, there's got to guys that got to step up and Downs is going to be one of those guys that's going to step up for us this year. >> Obviously different story lines this year, but compared day one this year to day one last year, what's your level of excitement, confidence in this team? >> Well, I was really excited. I was really pleased really with day one practice. It was really smooth, really really no mental errors, you know, it was pretty clean. I thought the guys flew around, a lot of plays on both sides of the ball, you know, having Sossamon and Mooney back out there together with the ones. Those guys were both making plays on day one, which was awesome to see. Offense made some good plays. JT had some huge runs. Overall, I thought it was really clean. >> You're in your you're in your fourth year here. You guys didn't have any major coaching changes. Most of the starting offense is the same as last year. What is that level of consistency year to year? How does that help you guys kind of hit the day one >> That's a great question. I think it's huge. I think it's very beneficial. Just even the way we started practice today with Daniel coming back, the offensive line intact, the tight end, the running back. I mean, there were some checks at the line of scrimmage that Daniel made to get us into the right play, which we hit some big plays today and that doesn't just happen. That's come from reps and being together in the consistency and everyone being on the same page. So, I'm very excited for that. >> When you go into camp knowing who your starting quarterback is, does that help get you guys further down the road building the offense or working guys in? >> There's no question about that. There's no doubt about it. So, obviously knowing Daniel's our guy going into this year, the conversations that are taking place with the offense and how it evolves through training camp and during the season is going to be a big force for >> Ben talked about his transition to safety or >> Yeah. >> What went into that? >> You know, Ben's Ben's kind of a jack-of-all-trades. He's a Swiss Army knife. He does a lot of different things for us through special teams last year on the scout team. So, playing safety, you know, obviously you have so many you know, practice squad players and so he would go both ways for us last year and he made a ton of plays on the scout team and so we switched him over to offense. So, I was excited to see him out there. He had a catch today. He's going to continue improve and grow in that role. >> Shane, do you just have Are you going to rotate AR and Riley? >> Yeah, those guys will Yeah, those guys will rotate. You know, I'm really pleased with where AR's at coming off the eye injury you know, in the spring and then going into training camp and Riley too making good strides as well. So, those guys will rotate. Those guys compete and I'm looking forward to that competition with those two guys. >> Daulton Tucker, I think going back to the spring has had a few of those high snaps. I mean, he's a talented guy. >> How do you get that under control? >> I think it's reps. It's repetition is really what it comes down to. Obviously getting those reps, you got to go through it. You know what I mean? And there's going to be some of those snaps thrown bad snaps, but that's what practice is for and you know, we got to work through those and you know, be consistent doing it. >> Can you just imagine what specifically like Caden Curry with those guys have to do to make the team? >> Yeah, I think Caden Curry first and foremost, you know, a tremendous player. Had a hell of a career at Ohio State. Obviously a local kid here, but saw a lot of good things in the spring from him. Very smart, cerebral guy understands and I think he's got really good instincts as well. So, I'm really looking forward to seeing him come out here and compete you know, in this training camp and earn a spot and earn a role on this team. >> Looking like you got a couple more? those places where >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, some of those guys, that's how it works out, right? You play special teams and then you earn your role. You see it all around the league, but you never know how this thing plays out. You know what I mean? You can step up early and be a guy for us on defense. You never know. >> Chris made a good point yesterday about talking about finishing at the end of the season. What are you guys implementing on day one to kind of get to that point? >> Well, I think it's a little bit we talked about developing a find-a-way mindset. You know, that's really what it comes down to is finding a way and it's my job as a coach, you know, during practice to put those guys in position, right, to develop that mindset. You know, and that starts in training camp. It's always about, you know, establishing our identity, who you're going to be as a football team. You know, tough, physical, fast, all those, you know, coaching clichés you hear, but it is the truth. We got to go do that every single day, bring great energy, be elite communicators at everything we do, day in and out, so we can get to where we want to go. >> You mentioned Sauce and Sauce and Woolen. I think that Kansas City game is the only game they really Yeah. >> Uh Linsley was talking about how they could tell that Pat was frustrated through that game. Kind of what was going Do you remember that and I don't know, what do you take away from that and hoping to spin forward to this year? >> Well, you got two guys that have been all-pro players uh at points in their career and they're really elite players. So, to have two elite corners that can lock down a guy one-on-one on the outside is going to be huge and beneficial, you know, for our defense. So, I'm really looking forward to those guys being out there together, you know, for the full season. >> So, miss it? >> Oh, yeah, of course, man. It's always It's just when it when it comes back around, you can't believe it. You've been training all this off season and now you're finally like back and not that it didn't mean anything before. You you were always training for something, but like every rep now means something. There's no There's no do-overs. >> How do you feel coming in physically? I mean, you you take good care of your body. You you played mostly injury-free last year for the first time in a while. I mean, do you feel like that? >> Definitely. I mean, whenever you come out the season healthy, then you can get right back into not really I don't want to say back to 100%. You get back to strengthening those ankles, those joints, those knees, hips, everything that kind of takes a toll throughout the season rather than rehabbing an actual like specific injury and then getting into your regular program. So, it's always nice to get right into a nice and easy relaxing off season and just gradually build up. >> Jacquizz, what went into your decision? A couple running backs who want contracts right actually right away. What went into your decision to just pick up and go out to practice? >> Yeah, I have faith. I mean, I've had some good conversations and I have faith between my agent and front office. Like I said, I've already said I would love to be a Colt for life. So, I have faith that things are moving in the right direction. >> So, maybe something >> Maybe if you talk to him. >> They don't listen to >> You know, you got tenure here, man. Look, they Hey. >> I did. There's so much continuity on the offense. Like the the coaches are all back. Most of the line is back. I mean, Jaylen Travis started four games last How important is that to carry all that over from one year to another? >> It's very important but every every year is different. Every year is different. Every team is different. But, it's important that when you have pieces from the previous year, can they bring along the guys who maybe had one or two starts last year or new guys in the building? Can they bring those guys up to speed with our program, how we go about running our scheme so that we're all on the same page. So, you love to have that continuity from last year but you know, it's just going to it's going to be a little bit different. But, can you bring everyone up to speed on the same page? That's the biggest thing. >> Jacquizz, you've been through quarterbacks in your career here. The value of having continuity, they T.J. He had back. How does that impact your ability? >> I mean, that's that's a major piece. I mean, you talk about the offensive line. You talk about having, you know, a running game. You talk about having a number one wide receiver. I mean, you need to have a guy at the helm under center who can operate the offense efficiently. So, we talked about continuity, bringing someone back who was doing that at a super super high level last year is huge. It's very huge and then it's on us, you know, the guys around him to be able to help make his job easy easier as possible by being in our right spot, making sure we're at our right depth. And it's just those little things that makes his job easier cuz there's a lot that goes on at that position. >> Daniel, you're a health guy and you preparation he's 8 months out of an Achilles. Are you a little bit surprised that he's this far along? >> I mean, I don't know how the knock on wood, I don't know how those um injuries go, but I just do know I hear about timelines and I know the worker that he is, so the fact that he is back out there right now, it doesn't surprise me cuz I know the worker that Daniel is, but like I said, I hope I don't have to go through any of that ever, but um I know Daniel was more than equipped, as you guys can see, to to fight through that and be able to be back out here. >> your first training camp as a parent? Does that change anything for you motivationally when you step on the field? >> See, so this is I did a not a study, but I looked back. A lot of guys who who's had children in college and even in the pros, usually they go crazy the next year and then it comes out like, "Oh, they had a child." So, hopefully that's the case for me. Uh but no, I'm super blessed. I'm very excited. >> I'm very excited um for for her to start experiencing that. I mean, obviously she won't be able to remember anything right now, so hopefully I'm here long enough to where she can still see me in the blue and white and run around and take pictures with blue and she'll remember it. >> Do you think Mr. Daniel in his comeback he comes up here and he's, you know, he's very sort of soft-spoken with us, but like I suspect he's probably pretty motivated, you know, like there are people who say, "Oh, you're you're injury prone or this or that." I mean, what what do you say? >> I mean, obviously not and not even with other people. I mean, it's to himself because he knows the level that he can play at. I mean, obviously you guys saw the last year and unfortunately like these things happen and these things happen and and you hope it never comes in your career. You hope it's down the line, but he's someone who's fought back before and I just think he's like it's the same thing this time and I'm going to come back even better than before just like I did the last time. So, I think it's yes other people but more so it's to himself like hey, I'm going to get back to the level I know I can play at. I just think we've continued to play at a high level um not only myself but plenty of other black backs in the league. I think they play at extremely high level at all different ages. So, I just think that was a probably a time period back in the day where there may have been a blimp you know with a couple of guys but I think now I mean it doesn't matter what age you are. If you're an elite guy, I think it shows on and off the field and think we're continuing to prove that. Well, well Saquon's not as old as Derrick Henry. Derrick Henry's doing something that's crazy and I think people need to take notice. So, he's someone who who's really at the helm of that cuz I don't even think Saquon is is 30 yet. I'm not quite sure maybe 29 but Derrick is like 32 just went for like 15, 1600. I mean he's he's not stopping. So, I just think year in and year out those guys you mentioned and a few others no matter if they're from 25 to 32, they continue to play at a high level. So, at the end of the day I mean analytics doesn't really matter. If you're a baller and you can help your team win, you're an elite guy amongst a very difficult league. I think it's worth something. I mean you got to. I mean obviously I've gone against not even going against Derrick a few times but been on the other side and been able to sit there and watch him you know real live game and then talk to him in the off season about his training, his diet, his mindset. Um but then obviously there's some things you can't control. Uh he's 6'4, 250, so that that always helps. Um but when anytime that we can all like help each other and pick each other's brain, it just elevates everyone as a whole. And I'm talking about the running back group as a whole. Well, I mean I've gone for 1,600, 1,800, 1,500, and we we have not, you know, made the playoffs yet. So, looks like I need to run for a little bit more. You know, maybe I need to do my job a little bit better. Just maybe that might put us over the edge. Maybe that might help someone else make another play. So, the yardage is is is very fun. It's always great making big plays cuz ultimately it's helping the team win. But when the yards don't translate to wins, then they're just stats on a sheet. Thank you very much. All right, we're good. It's a beautiful to see. Just seeing both of them there, healthy, um locking up. And that's like the expectation that we we know that they can do. And seeing that was like, "Okay, it's going to be a fun year." That that started up. Just seeing that day one made me just be like, "Okay, this is going to be a fun year having them back." And even just every piece on our whole defense, the uh the depth that we have in the secondary, I know it's going to be a great year for Right. They've always been motivated. They've always been like, you know, top of the line when it comes to people that work hard, people that are focused and everything. and just last year was just a year where they unfortunately had a few injuries and you know, whatever people thought they were still in here rehabbing hard and you know, everything. So, those are two guys that work extremely hard, they're extremely professional. So, it's something really cool seeing them both healthy and ready to go at the start of camp and knowing that we have a full training camp all together with the whole secondary being able to grow and build from what we've seen glimpses last year, but now we have, you know, a full off season to get healthy and everything and get your bodies prepared. So, it's fun to see that now. >> How do their leadership skills, their kind of the way they hold themselves, how do they compare and contrast on and off the field that you have two star guys like that in your locker room? >> Um, let's see. Sauce is a little more outgoing. Mooney is still outgoing, but not as, you know, outgoing. You know, not as, you know, out there, but both of them are really really great leaders. Both of them take pride in their work. Both work extremely hard on technique and not just athleticism. You know, two stars, two former All-Pros. A lot of them, you know, just around the league are all focused on athleticism, but they're both technicians. So, it's it's just cool to see how detailed they are doing everything that they do. So, they compliment each other well and they're both, you know, motivated to go out there and be the best. >> the rapport in that secondary safety group like with you as leaders as well? Like how do how I know we're early days in camp, how does that kind of operate and what do you like about the makeup of that room right >> Um, it's just a lot of confidence in the room. I think the the best part about it, nobody's overstepping trying to be, you know, an alpha. Everybody's a leader in their own way. Me, Mooney, Sauce, just really everybody. All we're vets. Jonathan Owens. We have a lot of good vets in the room that have been around football for a long time. So, I think everybody's, you know, leading where they can and nobody's overstepping and I think that's a good good thing in a room for we all everybody has a voice. >> You guys played corner last Um, I think it just eliminates threats. Um, I think having two star corners, two number one corners like Mooney and Sauce, and then, um, being able to play man can, you know, eliminate threats on the other team, but it also opens it up for when you do go into zone, and you know that we can we can play man if we want, but they're also really smart players. We have really smart players on this whole defense where we can make it look like man and go play zone and all other offenses won't know because they're expecting us, because of personnel, to be able to play man, which we will. And you know, we already know Lou, he prides himself on that, but also being able to mix things up. I think it really puts a whole menu together for us on defense. sort of condense Exactly. Right. I think, yeah. Like I said, they eliminate threats, and their two top receivers will be at least competitive. And it'll be it won't be easy downs for anybody going against them. So, for me as a safety, that frees a lot of things up for me where I don't have to worry about the outside as much, and I can help more on the inside, whether it's nickel or on a a good tight end where, you know, they have more space to work. So, it's a lot harder of a cover for the nickel or for the down safety. So, I think every it complements the whole defense where everybody will can have more help in other places when we know that certain things are going to be locked down. One tips and overthrows, I think having competitive, um, people that are, you know, being sticky on routes causes more tips, more PBUs, which also lead to tip balls, and that's where a high percentage of interceptions and turnovers come in the NFL. It's not people making spectacular plays, jumping routes, but a lot of it is just a tip ball from good coverage. And I think um just being able to mix things up, play man, and play zone also mix up a quarterback's mind and be able to go play multiple um coverages to where now we're able to make plays in zone, and then when we are in man, they they have to test their best receivers going against our best DBs. And that there's going to be turnovers there, too, when we make plays. So, I think there's a lot of ways to do it, and it just comes from our preparation. >> So, with the sticky coverages, that's where >> And that Yes, and that's where it makes my life easier. They're sticky, a lot of overthrows, a lot of, you know, disruption at the line of scrimmage. Quarterback has to take a chance, and I can get an overthrow. And so, for me as a safety, having people that are, you know, locked down like we have is that makes it my life a lot easier. >> All right, thanks, Dane. >> Yeah, thank you guys. Appreciate it. >> Thank you.

title: Nick Caserio on Tank Dell, C.J. Stroud and Training Camp | Full Q&A
text: Good >> morning. Welcome to training camp. Appreciate everybody being here. Uh hopefully everybody had a good summer. Excited to get started uh with this team with this season. Uh you know, 25th season for the organization. So that's uh you know, key marker there. Uh, I'd say personally, uh, begins my 26th season in the NFL. Um, honestly, it's it's really a blessing, uh, to be in this situation, and being in a position that I'm in, um, to have the opportunity, um, that I have, um, in front of me. Uh, certainly don't take take it for granted. Um, you every year is important. Um, 26 seasons, it means I'm just getting getting older. Uh, so, uh, but, uh, you know, we're looking forward to getting started here. I'd say you really training camp starts Monday. Uh this first few days is to kind of get everybody back moving around. But I mean training camp really starts on Monday. Uh you know once we put the pads on. Um as far as the team is concerned um a couple just housekeeping items I figured I'd just uh address here. So we've got a couple players um on the physically unable to perform list. NFI list. So those are league determined list just based on their situation or category. Um the two players obviously EJ you know is probably a little bit more longer term. You'll kind of see where he is uh later in the season. Um and MJ um really kind of working his way back there from the injury he sustained uh against Jacksonville I believe there you know mid-season or whatever it was. So making progress. There's a chance we'll see him in training camp. Kind of see how how it goes there. Um and then Jay Null um you know honestly happened three four days ago. I mean he's got a little bit of an issue with his finger. He was catching passes. He must have caught it the wrong way. So short term, not real concerned. Probably be a few weeks. Um kind of see how he progresses. Um as it pertains to Tank. Um so he's not on the PUP list. I'd say Tanks work really hard to put himself in a position. I say he still has some work to do. So you're not going to see him practice like he won't be on the practice field. He still has some things that he has to go through. But the reason that we're kind of keeping him alive and keeping him off the list because it enables him to participate in some drills or activities that you otherwise wouldn't be able to participate if you were on a a reserve list or active PUP list. So whether it's our walkthrough, whether it's our precision check, some other things. So like you won't see him practice like you're going to watch practice and wonder where Tank is and say, "Wait a minute, Tank's not practicing." Well, it's by design. So, he's got some ramp up work that he's still going to do, but there's some other things that we can do with him to kind of incorporate him into some I would say team slashcrossover walkthrough type situations. So, I'd say I just want to have some clarification just so you guys had kind of an understanding of kind of those particular situations. Um, so you know with that I'll take some questions. I mean Jonathan like go ahead take the first question. you know, for Tech to get this far, what was the approach to get him back and what would you say about how he's progressing? >> Yeah, really just one day at a time. Obviously, he sustained a pretty significant injury. Um, hasn't played football in a really long time. Uh, there's been some ups and downs. I'm sure once you have the opportunity to visit with him, he might express those, but his attitude has been great. I mean, he's been in the building every day, you know, there's some stops and starts, but I think when you endure an injury of that nature, how significant it was. I mean, it's it's a long road to come back. Um, I mean, it's credit to him. It's credit to our training staff. Um, the fact that he's even in a position where he's probably gonna have an opportunity here at some point here to practice. So, um, Tank's a great kid. Um, from the day we drafted him to where he is now, his attitude hasn't changed. Um, I think he's probably more anxious than anything else to to go back out there. But, we never pushed it. We never pressed it. We never put any timetable on anything and kind of let the player like work with this training staff and when they're able to do something, what can they do? Then we'll keep uh keep the progression moving. So, um but yeah, like I said, he's probably got, you know, another week or so here of work until we actually see him on a practice field. But, you know, it's credit to him and it's a credit to a lot of people in the organization. Go >> ahead. And when it goes to CJ Stout, Nico Ryan's a lot of his teammates on the race off season. What have you seen from CJ kind of he is on the fifth drop since he has exercised? What's the big picture as you guys as a player and your traction? >> Yeah, he's had a really good off season. Uh it's probably the best offseason he's had since he's been here. Um he's had a good attitude. He's been consistent. He's got the right mindset. Um I'd say we've definitely had productive conversations over the course of the spring. So, I mean, there's a possibility that something could come to fruition. So, we'll work through it and, you know, see what happens. >> After the progress made over the past three years, a lot of outside expectations for the next step. What are your expectations for this team? >> Yeah, I mean, the expectations are the same. Like, we can't control what people say outside of the building. I think we're proud of the program that we've built. I think we've been one of the most consistent programs in the NFL over the last three seasons. So, what's this season going to look like? I have no idea. like nobody really has any idea. I mean, I don't think last year as we were sitting up here, anybody thought, you know, Seattle and New England would be playing in the Super Bowl. So, our approach is try to have a good training camp, try to take it one day at a time, be consistent with our performance. I mean, we want to play with precision, effort, and physicality. So, we want to try to work on those things here in training camp. Like, all we can control is our performance dayto day. Like, we can't worry about a month from now, two months from now, four months from now. So, what's set outside of the building, like we can't control that. I mean, that's for all the talk shows and the radio shows. So, um, we try to keep our focus short term and kind of where we are right now and, you know, just take it one day at a time. >> Nick, would you say that CJ's had the best offse you've seen? What makes you say that? >> Yeah, I mean, he was here, he was healthy. Um, you know, he's had a good attitude, he's had a good approach. I mean, I think he started working in February. Um, was here for the full off season. You know, offse every offseason's a little bit different. Um, you know, so I'd say year two in the system. So, kind of build on some of the things that, you know, we did last season. So, I mean, he's had the right approach. He's had the right mindset. He practiced well. Um, you know, so I mean, training camp is kind of another step for our team. I say the spring was kind of a foundation just kind of get everybody ready for training camp. So, this is kind of a next step for our team in terms of our overall preparation. Um, I mean, the reality is 19 practices and three preseason games before we play one of the best teams in the NFL right in the home opener. Um, so I think, you know, we just want to keep the whole team moving forward and there's an individual component. You know, a player has to improve and a team has to improve and you know has to improve and hopefully we make enough improvement as a team to put ourselves in a position, you know, where we have an opportunity to be competitive, you know, each Sunday. >> How would you assess uh year one big day on offense and what what's the next step? What does the offense need to do better this year compared to last to get where you all want to get? >> Yeah, did a lot of good things offensively. Kind of got off to a slow start as a team. Um, you know, I think kind of midway, probably from about midpoint of the season to the end, you know, we were one of the better offenses in the league. Um, you know, we played more consistent. Um, so, you know, we'll see. I mean, just go out there and, you know, get put a foundation in place here. You know, systems in place, kind of make a couple tweaks and adjustments here. But Nick's a really good coach. Um, he's got a good attitude. He's got good energy. Um, has a lot of respect to the players. So, I mean, go out there and training camp, it's about the players, but it's about the coaches as well. So getting back into your routine, calling plays, reacting to the situation. We have a lot of unscripted periods where do we'll have the coordinators just call plays. So you just try to prepare, then you go back, hey, you know what? This worked. All right, maybe go back, make a tweak here. Um, I'd say the core foundation of what we're going to do offensively will probably be installed within the first two weeks. And really, it's about what the players do well. So what do the players do well? And then we're going to build the game plan and the offense accordingly. So um, you know, excited about the opportunity Nick has in front of him. excited about the opportunity, you know, for the whole coaching staff. >> Why does elevating Jerry to quarterback coach help make that goal maybe get achieved? >> Yeah, we'll see. I mean, you know, Jerry's a lot of experience. Jerry's a smart coach. He's got a, you know, very background in a number of different systems. So, in the end, you know, Demo felt like that was the right thing for us to do. So, you know, excited about the opportunity Jerry has in front of him. >> We know that CJ's contract has been one of the favorite stories about this this team. When you go into these contract negotiations, not just CJ specifically, but when you go into contract negotiation extension with these players, how much of it is based off of the past and how much of it based off the future when you're getting into the years and not >> Yeah, you take all the information in and just try to make the best decision possible, have an understanding of what the market is, what are the dynamics. It's not necessarily about what other teams are doing. like we're focused on the Texans and we're focused on doing what we feel is best for our team. So there's a lot of contracts that get done in the offseason. You have free agency, you have extensions, you have contracts that get done in training camp, you have contracts that get done during the course of the season. I think one of the things that we've shown is we're pretty flexible. So engage in the discussions, try to figure out if we can agree upon a certain level that everybody's comfortable with and we can arrive at that end point, great. If we can't, then you know, maybe it's at a further point, you know, down the road. So, I'd say to your question, Sard, we try not to over complicate it. You know, don't don't overthink it. Just take the information and we're making an assessment about what we think potentially we have in the player, what it's going to look like moving forward. Doesn't mean we're going to be right on everything. Absolutely not. But we just try to make the right decision with the information that we have in real time. And if we got to make an adjustment along the way, then we'll make an adjustment. the investments you made in the offensive line of the offseason, is there a point in training camp where you hope five guys sort of emerge and is there sort of a a moment where you hope that's already occurred? >> Yeah, it's a good question. Uh probably take a little bit of time here, a few weeks, because the reality is the inside positions, you're going to have a lot of movement. You're going to have multiple players with their hands on the ball. You're going to have multiple players kind of rotating at the guard spots. Um I'd say to a certain extent, probably be the same at tackle. I mean, I think Taye, like unless something were to happen, he's probably gonna be left tackle. Feel like we got pretty good competition there at right tackle and Trent and Braden Smith. Um, and we have a number of players that we think we can that that can help us inside. So, it'll take a little bit of time. Probably wouldn't read too much into who lines up where the first day training camp and it's going to be an evolution. It's going to be organic and there's going to be things that happen. Guy gets injured, something happens. We're going to have to make an adjustment. Um, so at some point here, you know, hopefully toward middle towards the end, you know, we have an idea of who the five are going to be, but the reality is probably going to need eight and there probably going to be a lot of players that rotate that, but at some point as we start to maybe start to think about getting ready for Buffalo, there's some things that are going to be in place practice-wise, so focus on Buffalo. So hopefully, you know, we have a group in place that we think we're going to be able to play with, you know, the first week against Buffalo. >> You talked about the implementation of the offense starting off. Is that going to be a a an excessive amount of emphasis on the running game to try to sort of balance out uh just going to have to work it out with with the five or the eight that you just mentioned? >> Yeah, you emphasize everything. I think every team kind of goes through an installation. You have kind of core runs, you have your core passes, and you try to marry those up and then try to figure out, well, you know what, looks like we might be pretty good at this and maybe we're not going to be so as good as that at that. Um so it's a process. Um, it's no different this year than it is any other year. So, what can the players do? What are the players good at? What are some of the things that we feel we can emphasize? You're always going to have a core foundation that you're going to want to be able to utilize, especially the first three or four weeks of the season. You're probably going to focus on your core, make some game plan adjustments specific to who the opponent is. Um, so, you know, hopefully, you know, we're good in the running game, hopefully we're good in the passing game, and, you know, we take care of the football. Um, ultimately offensively it's moving the ball, scoring points, and taking care of the ball. So, however we do that, some games we might have to run it 50 times, some games we might have to throw it 50 times. Whatever the game calls for, whoever the opponent is, then hopefully we can bob and weave and and play accordingly. >> Following up on something you said earlier, you know, if this negotiation with CJ Stra representation continue, would you continue that through the season or is that something you table um after? >> Yeah, we'll see. I think we'll take it one day at a time. Like I said, we've had pretty constructive discussions here over the course of the spring. So, I'd say, you know, there's a possibility something can happen in training camp. text: Oh, yeah. That's right. >> Well, when it comes to building your team for you, what do you do each year and what do you do this year to try to get a little bit better? text: Good morning. Fire away. And from our first day of practice today, I thought it was a lot of good back and forth. It's not about just one moment when you get into contract negotiations. It's about the entirety of your work. Wide receiver room, they continue to impress every day. See what they do well and see how we can use them to our advantage in our offense. Brevin? Oh, always. I love Brevin. I love Brevin. I'm always excited to see Brevin out on the field. Brevin never has a bad day. So, you know, just knowing what he's been through, you know, as a player, the the difficult spots, the hard hardships that he's went through and the end with the injuries. To see him back on the field rolling, it's always a fun sight to see for me. Great question. Biggest biggest difference for me, as a head coach, is it's truly just leaning on my assistants more. Understanding that, man, we're all in this together. I got great people who work around me and I don't have to do it all. All right, and I can truly lean on our guys, truly assist our coaches as best as I can, and just be more open to moving around, working with our entire team. So, there's a little more freedom, I would say, as the fourth-year head coach of doing it. The guys have done a great job in all phases, being able to sit in in different meetings, offense, defense, special teams, just being able to move around, and uh it's it's been it's been a cool growth process for me, just learning that you can less is more at times, and that's what I'm learning most. Getting us there right now, huh? No, it's uh >> [laughter] >> definitely positive. Yeah, we're we're excited about the guys that we've added uh to our team. Each year, you have to you have to build a team each and every year. All right, so, we'll see how this team gels, how this team comes together, and it's always in my mind, it's always a goal of coming together to do something special. All right, and how quickly can we bond, how quickly can we grow throughout camp, and we'll see how far we can take it. All right, appreciate it, guys. Yep.

text: What's up? How you all doing? >> Nick said earlier today that he's had good conversations with David about a potential a potential deal. How does that perhaps make you feel? So, um I'm letting them handle it and seems like everything is going great. >> And maybe you answered it, but how do you balance, um you know, keeping that that and not allowing the pressure maybe the pressure of that influence what you're trying to do on the field? >> Yeah, I think pressure is part of my job, you know, so um that's just something I think is part of the gig and something that I'm not, you know, naive to, but also I've learned you got to keep the main thing the main thing and you know, just focus on one day at a time, one play, and uh the football is what's got me to even having the conversation to be able to get a second contract. So, um I got to focus on football. >> Is there a point here in the preseason where you would no longer want to hear about that or talk about that? >> Not really. I mean, I I'm le- leaving that to David.
