So, can you talk about where you are and how you feel going into this sports training camp? >> Yeah, I feel great. Um I think uh I've taken steps in the offseason of like what it looks like to be, you know, um if you're going to be in one place, multiple places, whatever it is, you got to get the work done. So, I think I've been able to do that. Um and yeah, I've grown as a as a man. Um I've grown in my in my faith. I'm growing in, uh you know, my my football ability. So, uh I think I'm taking strides just as a person. >> So, that's James over the last 3 years. What are your expectations for this team as you start another camp? >> Uh expectations just to take one day at a time, one play at a time, and then see where we are at the end of camp. >> Why do you think it comes to compartmentalize and what Jeff was talking about? DeMeco Ryans was just saying how work takes care of itself, what you do on the field, you earn the contracts. Is that kind of the approach to say that it will take care of itself as long as you play well and do everything you're supposed to do? If it's going to happen, it's going to happen. >> Yeah, I think that's exactly right. I think, you know, what I've done is what I've done on the field and what I will do, you know, we'll we'll see. So, I think, you know, I've had some some success and I think, you know, I'll continue to have success as a quarterback in this league, so I'm excited for the future, you know, and past all the contract stuff. I I love playing football. >> And it's the accident of all of this second year with you. What have you seen as far as some of the adjustments that have been made and especially some of that that catered to you? >> Yeah, I think, you know, last year was, you know, kind of just getting the foundation of the system down and now you know, I think our step for him and I is just to take the step on what I like to do on in and out of plays and how I see the game on flow of the game on, you know, different downs and distances, so I think we'll be able to do that this off season, but we we took strides in OTAs and we continue to do such. >> Say, how much how much do you have to look forward to from your running back position this season? >> Um I think just playmakers, guys who, you know, can take care of the ball, have explosive plays, and you know, help in pass protection and and I think, you know, we have the guys to do it. >> A lot of guys say you've had your best off season and you didn't commit to being a good teammate. What have you done or not chosen not to do this off season that has allowed that to be your you're the in your career? >> I don't know. I kind of I think I've been kind of consistent. Uh just I don't know. I I feel like in when I was coming off my rookie year, it's my first off season, so I really didn't know what to do. Second one, you're trying to tailor it to like like exactly what that looks like. And then this last one is like, okay, I have an idea. So I think anything in life it just takes time, but I think I just was consistent the whole time and um you know, just focused on me and you know, getting better as a my faith, my family, and then with football. >> And then once you evaluated you know, the last season and then you take a look at the off season to work and improve, what did you work on during the summer in order to come back this season? >> Uh faith, family, football. There's There's There's little things in there, but that was mostly the big things. >> If you can elaborate a little more as far as maybe some specifics, when you talk about football and things that you saw in yourself when you looked at yourself in the mirror and said, "Okay, maybe I should do this better, or this is where I want to improve on to be able to, you know, get some more wins." >> I think I'll probably keep that to myself. But there's There's a bunch of things that I worked on, pocket movement, a bunch of different things like that. >> I want to talk about your maturation now. Specifically when you come into the line of scrimmage, your pre-snap reads, and how do you think you're seeing it now? Is it Is it sort of like doing this, or has it Have your eyes sort of focused and picked up that you can anticipate some things more now? >> Um yeah, I think I've always kind of been talented in that area. So I don't think I really had an issue in that. Um but I think I can grow always. So I mean, I I see myself getting better at it. Um and just, you know, getting the guys lined up and in the right position to make plays. Uh yeah, I think, you know, we brought in some guys who want to win, you know, who have experience in the playoffs, have of in, you know, big games. So um I think they're going to come in and help and um I think, you know, we we've we've we have a better roster than we even did last year, so I'm excited to, you know, get going with these guys. Uh I expect him to, you know, be a a dominant force, a you know, a guy who can, you know, make plays first, second, and third levels. Um and I think, you know, he's gotten better. I think he's learning and uh he's listening more and wanting to, you know, um you know, take steps on where he can grow past this, you know, the things that he's already good at. Yeah, I'm excited. I think there's a lot of experience up there. Um I think it's something that, you know, I'm comfortable, you know, um and I'm happy with, you know, the maze the moves we made, so um I'm excited to, you know, get some guys up there who, you know, want to, you know, do everything and, you know, want to be the running football, pass protection, everything. Uh yeah, I think just quickness, you know, maybe running the ball, getting out the pocket, extending plays. Yeah, it's been great. Um he's a great guy, somebody who's played a lot of meaningful ball, uh who wants to do everything and that we ask him to do, so got to spend a lot of time with him this off season and um you know, um funny dude, great guy, great locker locker great locker room guy, so excited to get rolling with him. >> This is your first off-season without Jarod. What was it like the process of having to say goodbye and how confident are you in Jerry pulling that weight? >> Yeah, it was tough, you know, Jarod has been, you know, in my life since I was 16 and then he was in my career since I started in the NFL. So, very talented, very very talented coach, somebody who has played the game, who sees it well, who who really helped me, did a great job you know, I think, you know, he's going to do amazing things in his career. I see him being a top offensive coordinator in this league one day and you know, God willing a great head coach cuz I he has that type of mindset and just his his ability to see the the field and the game and you know, help the quarterback. But then yeah, Jerry's come in, you know, he's more of a system guy, somebody who is you know, been in the system a long time, has really helped me in that area and you know, I think he's he's been Somebody who communicates very well and has done a great job, you know, trying to figure out who I am as a person and then who I am on the field. >> Nick told us this morning that we won't get a chance to see Tank early on as far as practicing on the field. As one of his closest friends, what have you seen from him as far as his, you know, coming back, him and his what he's been doing in the off-season to be able to get himself prepared to come back to training? >> Yeah, he's done a great job, you know, he's close to, you know, returning and he looks great. I think he's, you know, just getting some of those kinks out, you know, some of those little details that he wants to feel a little better in, but I think he looks amazing and I'm just excited for him, you know, to get the peace of mind that he can go play again and be 100% while he's doing it. All right, yeah.

title: LIVE: HC DeMeco Ryans, C.J. Stroud, and Will Anderson Jr. address the media
text: Good morning. >> Fire away. from our first day of practice today, I thought it was a lot of good back and forth. Offense made some plays, defense made some plays, special teams guys did a really good job of executing as well. So, from what I look for the first day, when you talk about communication, guys working together, being on the same page, we we achieved that today. Now, as I mentioned to our guys, is how do you build on the next day? And that's what you look for in camp. It's a steady build. And how do you continue to improve each day? >> How do you see the success that you have over here compared to last? >> Offensively, we've done a really good job today. Pre- snap was excellent. Guys were on it. Guys were getting the line properly. Guys were playing fast. And that's all I expect from all three phases. Like we want to be a fast, aggressive team. To do that, you really have to own the communication, the huddle. That's where it starts. We own that process the right way. We'll get to the line of scrimmage. We'll play fast. >> With the progress your team has made over the last three years, what are your expectations for the squad during this year? >> Each year for me is different. When we speak about expectations, right? My expectations have been high. Year one, they were high. Year two is I don't when you guys ask me about expectations, the only thing I know is high expectations. That's why we do what we do, right? to achieve the the ultimate goal. So, it's a process. It's a build to get there and we're not afraid of the work that it takes to be put in to get there. And that's what we're achieving day by day. We'll keep chopping one day at a time to be our best come week one. >> I know it's early, but what are some of the things you're looking forward to seeing from the running back? >> From the running back group, I'm excited to see the guys just how fast they're playing. I see Woody, he looks faster. He's making, you know, more decisive decisions like cuts. Jaw is looking good. Of course, Montgomery has done a really good job. So, it's a really good room of running backs and I'm just excited to see them continue to improve on those fine details. Like, can we improve in our reads? Can we improve in our pass protection? Can we improve in the screen game as well? So, I'm just excited to see the growth of that group throughout camp. What are the challenges that faces as he tries to compete before starting out and possibly at a position that he hasn't quite played before? >> When you come out to camp, everybody's competing. So, our rookies, you know, if you just attack it the right way, I tell our somebody has to be rookie of the year, right? Somebody rookies play well every single year. And it's not where you're trying to go out and attain that. is just man, are you just locked in on the small details, what the coaches are asking you to do every day? You have a competitive spirit, right? You have a willingness and a want to to succeed and do great, you're going to do that. So, for all of our rookies, Keelin, Marlin, everybody, right? They just have to come out and just work hard at their craft and they'll be exactly where we need them to be. You got a bunch of guys behind Aziz and Henry. What's kind of the charge for those guys as you try to figure out who slots in behind Aziz and Henry >> with the linebacker spot? We're in a a really good situation with Aziz and Henry. Those guys have played a lot of ball together. They're they're very tight. You can see the connection on the field that they have off the field. That's a really great group of guys. I enjoy seeing those guys work. I enjoy seeing their leadership to see the way Henry and Aziz communicate daily. It's been fantastic to watch. So those guys who are taking reps behind them, they just have to look at those two guys and see their leadership, see how they approach every day with a man a positive attitude. They want to be great every play. If they those guys attack that, the the roster it'll sort itself out. >> You know what it's like to have a contract or extension looming, you know, your head from a head coach standpoint. What was some of the advice that you gave to CJ to tell him, you know, block that out and, you know, block that part of the business aspect out of it and just want to play? >> When it comes to contracts, I really don't get into a lot of deep discussions with guys when it comes to the contract situation because I truly believe the contract is you get the contract by what you do on the field. It doesn't matter about what you say, what I say. It's about how you perform on the field. If you're worthy of getting a contract and you deserve it, it'll it'll happen for you. But if you're worried about it, worrying is not going to change anything, right? It's about the actions about you put in and it's about your body of work and experience and what you've shown. It's not about just one moment when you get into contract negotiations. It's about the entirety of your work. >> Wide receiver room, they continue to impress every day. someone different making a play, you know, every day. So, it's uh it's an exciting room, I think, to for us to see how they develop throughout camp, but I'm I'm excited to see, you know, not only them perform in camp, but also just to see them get into some live preseason games, right? We put a lot on our wide receivers when it comes to coming out of the huddle, aligning motion. We put a lot on their plate. So your mental game has to be on point to play wide receiver and then you have to be physical and grimy enough to block in a running game to make our team. So we have a lot of guys who have that mindset. So it's just it all sort itself out with you guys. How impressed have you been with the work that you put in to even get back to this point after all this? >> I miss Tank. We're excited for Tank to just get back out here in the training camp. He's on his own ramp up schedule, but it's excited to just have him. He's eager to go. And the thing for Tank is like Tank is a smart player. We know how dynamic Tank was when he was out there, but again, he hasn't played ball in over two years. So, it's important for him and to get those we do our walkthroughs to get those reps, get in the huddle, get the call, get out of the huddle, go line up fast, adjust and motion. So, it's important for him to get all of those reps because he's missed so much time of playing football. So, you know, my mindset there is to get him as much football as possible and build them up until he's able to get into our team drills and we'll see how he progresses uh next week to see how if he's able to get out there or not. going back to March when it first became known that to you all that David Montgomery might become available. What in particular intrigued you about him? >> What intrigued me most about David Montgomery was as going against him, seeing the success that he's had, seeing the nature at which he runs the ball. He just he fits the brand of football that I want to play. And we know it's no secret that we needed to improve our running game. It's It's not been good enough since I've been here. It hasn't been good enough. So, to make improvements in the run game, running game, you have to get players who can run it. And that's what David, he's shown the success, no matter where he's been, he's always been successful running the football. And just to see the way he works every day. Positive guy, dialed in on the details, a great guy. And we couldn't have added a better guy for our running back room, for our offense, just the way he's as businesslike with his approach. What are some of the differences you've seen from last year coming into this year? From last year to this year, I I can see Nick truly growing, you know, as a leader, as a play caller. We've added more volume to our offense, right? And it's basically for on what our guys have been capable of doing, offensive guys. It's the second year around, second time around going through an install learning, it's it's easier for those guys to get moving at a faster pace. And so the volume is up. Guys are executing at a high level and he's able to, you know, do more things, more creative things. And he's been studying all off season, been calling me, blowing my phone up, and I had to not answer him. I told him it's break time. [laughter] I want some break time with my family and he's still dialed in on football. So I'm excited to see Kayle's growth and his his process. As we all your first time calling plays, there is a it's like any job you do, right? The more time on task, the more experience you get, the better you get at it. And he'll be uh much better this year. >> What does it take to run the ball effectively? What do you think, John? >> Block well, run well. It's not that it's not that hard. It's a mindset when it comes to the run game. You got to play physical, right? O line starting with those guys. You got to be physical. You gotta play with the proper hat placement. Your footwork has to be dialed in. It has to be right. The backs have to run great tracks. They have to know when to make the right decision with their cuts, with their vision, their read. So, it's a it's a lot that goes into it, but not to over complicate it. You got to block the guys in front of you and you got to run like you want to get every single yard that's out there. talk about the offensive line. There were a lot of obviously focus and attention on that with the offseason changes made. What are your I expectations, but what do you your thoughts about that group and >> our offensive line? I I feel like we have a a deep group. I feel like we have a lot of guys who are capable of going out and starting for us. got a lot of guys with experience and it's a good problem to have for us. It's a matter of figuring out who that best five guys will be, right? And it's exciting for me to try to see guys in different positions uh to see how how it all gels together. And with the O line, every year that I've been in ball, you know, someone goes down, somebody has to step up and plug in. So, the versatility that we have is is unique as well. We have guys who can play multiple spots inside. We uh got tackles who can play on both sides. So, I'm I'm excited just as well as everyone is excited about how the O line is going to shape out because when we talk about the run game, how we can improve, it starts there and I think we have the guys who can do it. >> Would you say Will has picked up where he left off from the offseason program? >> Will has definitely picked up disrupting plays left and right. So, he's he's definitely wrecking havoc again as he always does. And that's the I can talk about Will all day, but his mindset, his approach, how intense he is on the field, you guys see it, but it's the same way in my meeting rooms. He's on the edge of his seat. He's locked in every single word that I that I say in the meeting, and he's taking it to heart. It means a lot to Will. He's truly passionate. He cares a lot. He cares about seeing Houston be a successful franchise and there's no guy that cares more than him and I want all our guys to see how he operate every single day. I can highlight him every day because that's how I believe it should look when any job you're doing, right? The passion that Will exudes about his love for the game and his love to continue to exceed and get better. I think we all can learn from it. I learn from it. You bring that passion and juice every day to what you do. >> We talked previously about Jerry Shaflinsky when you when made him the quarterback's coach. Since that time, his work with CJ, their collaboration, what have you seen from Jerry's coaching style, his impact with CJ? >> Jerry's done a really good job of that's his communication skills. He's done a great job of communicating with the quarterbacks, communicating with myself. Um, you know, just the daily meeting structure, what they're doing, like very detailed coach. And I think you'll see that in our quarterback's play this year. They're bonding. They Jerry's done a great job. Even when he was working with those guys last year, he did a really great job. Jerry has a really cool demeanor about himself. He's been in the game for a long time, coached for a long time, coached a lot of great guys. And I just love his approach. I love his demeanor. It's never too high. It's never too low. It's exactly where he needs to be for those guys. And those quarterbacks can lean on Jerry at any given time for the support that they need. Ever since the World Cup, the players have been really pushing for grass versus turf. They saw that's possible in the stadiums. Do you have that conversation with your players? Are you asked about that by anybody in the building? What's your take on grass? >> Whatever's out there, grass or turf, whatever we play on. I'm happy I don't make those decisions. So, we'll be we'll play fast on whatever it is, grass or turf, we just need to play fast. Go ahead, bud. group this year. What's your expectation from that? >> I expect our tight ends to play much better this year. Uh starting with our coach, James Ference, passionate coach, guy who's played the game for 10 years. He brings that energy, brings that passion, knowing what it's like as a player, right? And he's doing a great job pouring into those guys. Kayle's working with the tight ends as well. And the group, we have a really deep group. I mean, we have, you know, six, seven guys there who can go play for us. So, that's the exciting part about it. All different guys. And you talk about passing game, blocking game. We got a plethora of guys who should allow us to do some cool things when it comes to 12, 13 personnel. So, I'm excited to see our usage and how guys, you know, just thrive in camp, see what they do well, and see how we can use them to our advantage in our offense. Bre. >> Bre. Oh, always. I love Brevin. I love Brevin. I'm always excited to see Brevin out on the field. Brevin never has a bad day. So, you know, just knowing what he's been through, you know, as a player, the the difficult spots, the hard hardships that he's went through in the end with the injuries to see him back on the field rolling, it's always a fun sight to see for me. >> DJ, what's the biggest difference for you as a coach? What's been the biggest learning lesson for you guys? >> Great question. Biggest biggest difference for me, you know, as a head coach is it's truly just leaning on my assistance more. Understanding that, man, we're all in this together. I got great people who work around me and I don't have to do it all right. and I could truly lean on our guys, truly assist our coaches as best as I can and just be more open to moving around working with our entire team. So that's a little more freedom I would say as the fourth year head coach of doing it. The guys have done a great job in all phases, being able to sit in in different meetings, offense, defense, special teams, just being able to move around and uh it's it's been it's been a cool growth process for me just learning that you can less is more at times and that's what I'm learning most. >> Obviously just getting started, but you got to feel really good about 3 to where you get over the getting us there right now, huh? >> No, it's definitely positive. Yeah, we're we're excited about the guys that we've added to our team each year. You have to you have to build a team each and every year, right? So, we'll see how this team gels, how this team comes together. And it's always in my mind, it's always a goal of coming together to do something special, right? and how quickly can we bond? How quickly can we grow throughout camp? And we'll see how far we can take it. >> All right. Appreciate it, guys. >> When it comes to building, what do you do each year? What do you do this year to try to get a little bit better? And you already talked about the contract doesn't change something for you, but just in terms of football itself, how do you try to get better? >> Yeah, most definitely. I think OCAS is a very important part of the process. Um, you talk about coming back in after a season. I think coach Rod and I think De Mo is his processes of helping his players get better is taking them through a pro. And so sitting down with coach Rod, going through my pro of finishing at the top of the rush, bending, taking the ball, like that's something that, you know, during this offseason I really worked on, you know, bending more, you know, bringing that trail arm, not letting it get stuck, and finishing on the quarterback. So just as far as like continuing to grow my game. Those are the areas where, you know, I've been practicing that and, you know, helping it show up. >> Well, ever since the World Cup, a lot of players have pushed for grass. Do you have a preference? Do you ever bring that to anybody's attention? >> Oh, yes, most definitely. Oh, most definitely it is. I would most definitely say grass. Grass 100%. I think it's just the natural feel of grass. Your feet not getting stuck in the ground like in turf. I mean, I had two high ankle sprains up in Metife because of the turf. And I think grass is just a better better option, honestly. >> Can you talk to anybody here about that? >> Uh, I mean, not really. I mean, at the end of the day, it's up to them. They'll figure it out. But, you know, just control what you can control. Go out there and play and do your job. What goes into how important? >> Oh, it's very important. I think, you know, I've been talking about the process a lot. People only think it's the processes on the field, but in order to get to the destination that you want to get to on the field, it's off the field stuff. So, it's watching film, taking care of your body. So, those little things, those little small details that will make the process go. You can't get to the destination unless you're taking time and watching film or you're taking care of your body, getting in the weight room, getting bigger, getting stronger, getting faster, improving in areas. Like for instance, like upper body was something that I really wanted to try to continue to grow in my game. And this offseason, that's something I really focus on is my upper body. So like those are the little things that's very important to the process of getting you out here on the field and being at your best. >> You guys begin this camp with Super Bowl expectations and how can this camp lay the foundation for however high your expectations are for this team? >> Yeah, most definitely. Coach talked about putting a bull on a ring. That's something that we're striving for. Something that's never been done in this city. They bring something special back to this city and I think everybody's aware of that. I was just talking about telling the guys yesterday, the seriousness of what we're trying to accomplish here, man. Like be a part of it. Like you're here for a reason. And I think the expectation is like nobody outside of this building is going to have a higher expectation than what we have in this building. But I think we did a really great job of laying the foundation of who we want to be as a team. Um what we want to accomplish as a team. And Swarm is our foundation. So, like I say all the time, it's like when everything goes wrong or we not doing this that, we have a foundation to lean back on. And I think that's why we've been able to be so successful, you know, my my four years of being here because De Mo has did a really good job of laying the foundation down. >> Last year, your parents talked about evolution for you. You even, you know, took that word on yourself as far as evolution. Year four for Will. >> Year four, man. and just I guess just to continue to just wreck havoc in all phases of the game. But I think one thing that I really want to step up on and it's something I wrote down on my goal sheet to just just becoming a better leader, you know, better chance of just connecting with the guys and really, you know, being more vocal and really, you know, being hands-on with the guys. You know what I'm saying? Like really like taking the young guys under my wing. And Kaden has been a great addition to our room because it's given me that that time to really like have a rookie. Like I've had a rookie, but like he's he's kind of different. You know what I'm saying? He's a high draft round pick. I mean, he's a high uh draft pick and he they come they expect him to come in and play. So, it's my due diligence to help him out and help him reach every goal that he wants and show him the way. But, he have he has Ralden I mean Sheldon, he has um De Hunt. So, he has a whole bunch of guys that help him. But, I think that's just one area that I want to evolve in is just being a really great leader. >> You know, how is your role as a how's your role as a leader different than maybe it was last year? you know, often your defensive line. Talk about that being your >> role. I think that's the thing. I think that's the thing is just like not just worrying about the defensive line, but the whole team in that aspect like not just speaking up when it's time to speak up in the defensive line, but speaking up in team meeting, speaking up when we out here on the field, speaking up when we're doing team periods, like, hey, let's take a pause. So, just things like that. >> Being a leader, do you think by leading and helping to teach it can help you even improve yourself? >> Oh, of course. I think that's the thing about leadership. Leadership, you're always learning something every day. You're always growing every day because within leadership, you're learning so much about yourself because of the people that you have to deal with and they're helping you learn about yourself because everybody's different and everybody requires a different type of leadership you have been able been able to add more and more to your game this year. How how much will be able to utilize your skill set? >> Yeah, I've been I've been I've been on him a little bit. I was like, "Coach, what we got?" Every day, every every time I say, "What we got? What we got?" But I think that's the great thing about this defense be because we have so many great players and we can do so many great things with this defense and change the looks up so much. It allows everybody to have a different play or a different thing. And I think that's where we really thrive in is like, hey, we got Will, we got Denil, we got Sheldon, we got Kamar, we got Sting, we got Aziz, all these guys can do different things. So different packages, all that type of stuff coming into place when helping all of us succeed. >> When it comes to CJ, you guys came in together and you've had successes together. What advice do you give to CJ as you compartmentalize or he does contract versus on the field and just kind of like stay the course? What do you do as far as as a friend, as a teammate to kind of give him some advice on this or what would you say? >> Yeah, most definitely. And I think CJ does a really good job, man. Obviously, we have a very similar mindset and CJ's a big guy and it's I really don't have to tell him this, but it's we do talk about it. He's just like, man, control what you can control. And I think he's been doing a great job of that. He controls going out there on the field, playing his best ball, helping his team win a lot of games, and that's what he's been doing. That's what he's going to continue to do. And everything else is up to God. He's faith-based. I'm faith-based, and we know we put our trust in God. Let him handle the rest, and we'll get the results that we want. So, it's not about man. It's not about anybody else, but how we're how we're going about our everyday process. And I think he's been doing a hell of a job this offseason about going through his everyday process, leading the offense, leading the guys in the locker room, and getting everybody, you know, on board with what we got going on here. >> Four years into the league, how does it feel to you when you hear younger players as far as high school and some of you would probably say I want to be like Will Anderson Junior. >> It's kind of crazy. I was just talking to Rank on the sideline. I was like, "Dang, bro. I'm really going into year four. I'm old." And he was like, "Bro, you're not old." But man, it's special just because like, you know, I was walking out on the field. I was like, "Man, like look at all the hard work that you put in. like I never thought I would be here, but enjoying the process, enjoying the ride and like knowing that deep down inside my purpose is to be an inspiration and to be a positive influence on my community and on the younger, you know, community to show like, man, like this is how you're supposed to do it cuz I had guys to show me how I'm supposed to do it. So, I it makes me feel good because I want to walk in my purpose and I'm really big in my faith. So, that's something that, you know, I take serious is walking in my purpose and helping a younger generation. >> You are LeBron's fourth child. >> Have you done man. Uh >> I got a chance to catch up with him, man, and it's it's exciting. He I'm excited for him. Uh hopefully he do big things there. I know they got a great squad, and I can't wait to watch him do his thing there. >> Guardian cap. >> Oh, I've been had a guardian cap. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I They just put it on my helmet, man. >> You talk about improving this season. You talk about the things that you do. being off the field. What What are your personal goals? What do you shoot for accomplish? You want to go out there defensively of the year? >> Enjoy the process. >> That's my goal, man. I'm not even trying to be smart, but like I I I think when you, you know, when you start to look at the outside factors too early, like right now in training camp, I'm not really looking at any of those things. Like I'm worried about like how am I showing up in the run game? How am I showing up in the pass game? How am I showing up being a leader? And then once those things come into place after training camp, then I start building my goals. But I kind of like try to focus in on everything doing training camp, make sure I'm getting my body right, and then that's when I set my goals. >> What do you guys need from your office? >> What we need from the not just them, but what we need from the whole team is everybody buy in. Everybody be detailed in their assignments and their jobs and their responsibilities. It's not just one side of the ball. It's just not offense. It's us as a team. We go as we all go. So when we get to these big games, everybody needs to execute better. Everybody has to be detailed and everybody has to lock into a certain level of focus to help us win these games. >> Appreciate y'all. >> Thank you. You said earlier today he's had good conversations with David about a a potential deal. How did that perhaps make you feel? What do you think about that? Then I got a second quick question after that. Um, yeah. I mean, I think, you know, everything has been great. Um, you know, I'm focused on ball, trying to do what the best, trying to just hold my my bargain down on just the football side and do what I can, you know, and what I should be doing as a as a quarterback of this team. So, um, I'm letting them handle it. And seems like everything is going great. >> Maybe you just answered it, but how do you balance um, you know, keeping that that and not allowing the maybe the pressure of that influence what you're trying to do on the field? Yeah, I think pressure is part of my job, you know. So, um that's just something I think is part of the gig and something that I'm not, you know, naive to, but also I've learned you got to keep the main thing the main thing and, you know, just focus on one day at a time, one play. And, uh, the football is what's got me to even having the conversation to be able to get a second contract. So, um, I got to focus on football. >> There a point here in the preseason where you would no longer want to hear about that or talk about that? >> Not really. I mean, I'm leaving that to David. I don't really have that answer for you. So, >> CJ, you talk a lot about your teammates, how much they've seen you just grow from last season, the offseason grow. Can you talk about where you are and how you feel? >> Yeah, I feel great. Um, I think, uh, I've taken steps in the offseason of like what it looks like to be, you know, um, if you're going to be in one place, multiple places, whatever it is, you got to get the work done. And so I think I've been able to do that. Um, yeah, I've grown as a as a man. Um, I've grown in my in my faith. I've grown in, uh, you know, my my football ability. So, I think I'm taking strides just as a person. >> Over the last three years, what are your expectations for this team as you start another camp? >> Uh, expectations just to take one day at a time, one play at a time, and then see where we are at the end of camp. When it comes to compartmentalizing like Jonathan was talking about, Miko Ryan was just saying how the work takes care of itself. What you do on the field, you earn the contracts. Is that kind of the approach to say like it will take care of itself as long as you play well and do everything you're supposed to do. If it's going to happen, it's going to happen. >> Yeah, I think that's exactly right. I think, you know, um what I've done is what I've done on the field and what I will do, you know, we we'll see. So, I think, you know, I've had some some success and I think, you know, I'll continue to have success as a quarterback in this league. So, um I'm excited for the future, you know, and past all the contract stuff. I I love playing football. >> Excellent. What have you seen as far as some of the adjustments that have been made, especially some of that that cater to you? Yeah, I think you know last year was you know kind of just getting the foundation of the system down and now uh you know I think a step for him and I is just to take the step on what I like to do on uh in and out plays and how I see the game on flow of the game on you know different downs and distances. So, I think we'll be able to do that this offseason, but we took tries in OTAAS and we continue to do such. >> Um, I think just playmakers, guys who uh, you know, can take care of the ball, uh, have explosive plays, um, and, you know, help in pass protection and and, um, I think, you know, we have the guys to do it. A lot of guys say you've had your best offsemates. What have you done or not choose not to do this season to be your best? >> I don't know. I kind of I think I've been kind of consistent. Uh just I don't know. I feel like in when I was coming off my rookie years, my first offseason, so really didn't know what to do. Second one, you're trying to tailor it to like like exactly what that looks like. And then this last one, it's like, okay, I have an idea. So I think anything in life, it just takes time. But I think I just was consistent the whole time and um you know just focused on me and you know getting better as a my faith, my family and then with football. >> Having said that once you evaluated you know last season and you took the offse to work and improve what did you work under in the summer in order to come back this season? >> Uh faith family football there there's little things in there but that's mostly the big things. If you can elaborate a little bit more as far as maybe some specifics talking football things that you saw yourself, you look at yourself in the mirror and say, "Okay, maybe I should do this better or this is what I want to improve on to be able to, you know, get some more wins." >> I think I'll probably keep that to myself, but there's there's a bunch of things that I worked on, pocket movement, bunch of different things like >> Now, particularly when you come into the line of scrimmage, your pre- snap reads and how do you think you're seeing it now? Is it is it sort of like doing this or has it have your hours sort of focused and tightened up that you can anticipate some things more now? >> Um yeah, I think I've always kind of been talented in that area. So I don't think I really had an issue in that. Um but I think I can grow always. So I mean I see myself getting better at it. Um and just you know getting the guys lined up and in the right position to make plays. conditions. How much do you feel? >> Uh, yeah. I think, you know, we brought in some guys who want to win, you know, who have experience in the playoff, have experience in, you know, big games. So, um, I think they're going to come in and help. And, um, I think, you know, we we we we have a better roster than we even did last year. So, I'm excited to, you know, get going with these guys. in his second year. What are your expectations for him? >> Uh, I expect him to, you know, be a dominant force, a, you know, a guy who can, you know, make plays first, second, and third levels. Um, and I think, you know, he's gotten better. I think he's learning and, um, he's listening more and wanting to, you know, um, you know, take steps on where he can grow past just, you know, the things that he's already good at. >> CJ, he's made a lot of with the offensive line in the years since you've been here. They seem to really focus on it this offseason. What do you see different up front and are you excited about? >> Yeah, I'm excited. I think there's a lot of experience up there. Um I think it's something that, you know, I'm comfortable, you know, um and I'm happy with, you know, the m the moves we made. So, um I'm excited to, you know, get some guys up there who, you know, want to, you know, do everything and, you know, want to be running the football, pass protection, everything. Johnson. How do you think your game? >> Uh, yeah. I think just quickness, you know, maybe running the ball, getting out the pocket, extending plays. >> How have you been able to grow a relationship with David Montgomery and what has that relationship been like? >> Yeah, it's been great. Um, he's a great guy. somebody who played a lot of meaningful ball uh who wants to do everything that we asked him to do. So gota spend a lot of time with him this offseason and um you know um funny dude, great guy, great locker locker a great locker room guy. So excited to get rolling with him. >> This is your first off season without Grod. What was it like the process of having to say goodbye and how confident are you in Jerry pulling that away? >> Yeah, it was tough. you know, Grod has been, you know, in my life since I was 16 and then uh was in my career since I started in the NFL. So, very talented, very um very talented coach, somebody who's played the game, who sees it well, who who really helped me, did a great job, and um you know, I think, you know, he's going to do amazing things in his career. I see him being a a top offensive coordinator in this league one day and, you know, God willing, a a great head coach because I he has that type of uh mindset and just his his ability to see the the field in the game and, you know, help the quarterback. Um but then yeah, Jerry's come in, you know, he's more of a system guy, somebody who is um you know, been in the system a long time, who's really helped me in that area. Um and, you know, I think he's he's been great. um somebody who communicates very well um and has done a great job, you know, uh trying to figure out who I am as a person and then who I am on the field. >> Nick told us this morning that we we won't get a chance to see tank early on as far as practicing on the field as one of his closest friends. What have you seen from him as far as his, you know, coming back, him, uh what he's been doing in the offseason to be able to get himself prepared to come back and train? Yeah. Uh he's done a great job. You know, he's close um to, you know, returning and it looks great. Um I think he's, you know, just getting some of those kinks out, you know, some of those um little details that he wants to feel a little better in. But I think he looks amazing. Um and I'm just excited for him to, you know, to get the peace of mind that he can go play again and be 100% while he's doing it. All right.

title: LIVE: Texans EVP/GM Nick Caserio addresses the media
text: Good. Morning. Welcome to training camp. Appreciate everybody being here. Uh hopefully everybody had a good summer. Excited to get started uh with this team, with this season. Um you know, 25th season for the organization. So, that's uh you know, keep marker there. Uh I'd say personally, uh means my 26th season in the NFL. Um honestly, it's it's really a blessing uh to be in this situation, to be in the position that I'm in. Um to have the opportunity um that I have um in front of me. Uh certainly don't take take it for granted. Um you every year is important. Um 26 seasons means I'm just getting getting older. Uh so, uh but uh you know, we're looking forward to getting started here. I'd say, you know, really training camp starts Monday. Uh this first few days is kind of get everybody back moving around, but I mean, training camp really starts on Monday. Uh you know, once we put the pads on. Um as far as the team is concerned, um a couple just housekeeping items I figured I'd just uh address here. So, we got a couple players um on the physical unable to perform list, NFI list. So, those are league determined lists, just based on their situation or category. Um the two players, obviously EJ, you know, is probably a little bit more longer term. You know, we'll kind of see where he is uh later in the season. Um and MJ um really kind of working his way back there from the injury he sustained uh against Jacksonville, I believe, there, you know, mid-season or whatever it was. So, making progress. There's a chance we'll see him in training camp. Kind of see how how it goes there. Um and then Jaylen uh you know, honestly, it happened 3 4 days ago. I mean, he's got a little bit of an issue with his finger. He's catching passes. He must have caught it the wrong way. So, short-term, not real concern. Probably be a few weeks. Um kind of see how he progresses. Um as it pertains to Tank, um so, he's not on the PUP list. I'd say Tank's worked really hard uh to put himself in a position. I say he still has some work to do. So, you're not going to see him practice. Like, he won't be on the practice field. He still has some things that he has to go through. But, the reason that we're kind of keeping him alive and keeping him off the list because it enables him to participate in some drills or activities that you otherwise wouldn't be able to participate if you were on a reserve list or active PUP list. So, whether it's our walk-through, whether it's our precision check, some other things. So, like, you won't see him practice. Like, you're going to watch practice and wonder where Tank is and say, "Wait a minute, Tank's not practicing." Well, it's by design. So, he's got some ramp-up work that he's still going to do, but there's some other things that we can do with him to kind of incorporate him into some I would say team {slash} crossover {slash} walk-through type situations. So, I'd say I just want to have some clarification just so you guys had kind of an understanding of kind of those particular situations. Um so, you know, with that, I'll take some questions. I mean, Jonathan, like, go ahead take the first question. >> You know, for taking it this far, what was the approach to get him back in and what would you say about how he's progressing? >> Yeah, really just one day at a time. Obviously, he sustained a pretty significant injury. Um hasn't played football in a really long time. Uh there's been some ups and downs. I'm sure once you have the opportunity to visit with him, he might express those, but his attitude has been great. I mean, he's been in the building every day. You know, there's some stops and starts, but I think when you endure an injury of that nature, how significant it was, I mean, it's it's a long road to come back. I mean, it's a credit to him. It's a credit to our training staff. The fact that he's even in a position where he's probably going to have an opportunity here at some point here to practice. So, thanks a great kid. From the day we drafted him to where he is now, his attitude hasn't changed. I think he's probably more anxious than anything else to to go back out there, but we never pushed it. We never pressed it. We never put any timetable on anything. And kind of let the player like work with the training staff and when they're able to do something, what can they do? Then we'll keep keep the progression moving. So, but yeah, like I said, he's probably got you know, another week or so here of work until we actually see him on a practice field, but you know, it's a credit to him and it's a credit to a lot of people in the organization. Go ahead, Aaron. He has had a really good off season. It's probably the best off season he's had since he's been here. He's had a good attitude. He's been consistent. He's got the right mindset. I'd say we've definitely had productive conversations over the course of the spring. So, I mean, there's a possibility that something could come to fruition. So, we'll work through it and you know, see what happens. Yeah, I mean, the expectations are the same. Like we can't control what people say outside of the building. I think we're proud of the program that we've built. I think we've been one of the most consistent programs in the NFL over over last three seasons. So, what's this season going to look like? I have no idea. Like, nobody really has any idea. I mean, I don't think last year as we were sitting up here that anybody thought, you know, Seattle and New England would be playing in the Super Bowl. So, our approach is try to have a good training camp, try to take it one day at a time, be consistent with our performance. I mean, we want to play with precision, effort, and physicality. So, we want to try to work on those things here in training camp. Like, all we can control is our performance day to day. Like, we can't worry about, you know, a month from now, 2 months from now, 4 months from now. So, what's said outside of the building, like, we can't control that. I mean, that's for all the talk shows and the radio shows. So, um we try to keep our focus short-term and kind of where we are right now and, you know, just take it one day at a time. >> Nate, would you say that he just had the best off season you've seen? What makes you say that? >> Yeah, I mean, he was here, he was healthy. Um you know, he's had a good attitude, he's had a good approach. I mean, I think he started working in February. Um was here for the full off season. You know, the off season every off season is a little bit different. Um you know, so it's a year two in the system. So, kind of build on some of the things that, you know, we did last season. So, I mean, he's had the right approach, he's had the right mindset. He practiced well. Um you know, so I mean, training camp is kind of another step for our team. I'd say the spring was kind of a foundation, just kind of get everybody ready for training camp. So, this is kind of a next step for our team in terms of our overall preparation. Um I mean, the reality is 19 practices and three preseason games before we play one of the best teams in the NFL in the home opener. Um so, I think, you know, we just want to keep the whole team moving forward and there's an individual component, you know, a player has to improve and the team has to improve and the unit has to improve and hopefully we make enough improvement as a team to put ourselves in a position, you know, where we have an opportunity to be competitive, you know, each Sunday. >> How would you assess year one of AK on offense and what what's the next step? What does the offense need to do better this year compared to last year where we you want to get? >> Yeah, did a lot of good things offensively, kind of got off to a slow start as a team. Um, you know, I think kind of midway, probably from about midpoint of the season to the end, you know, we were one of the better offenses in the league. Um, you know, we played, you know, more consistent. Um, so, you know, we'll see. I mean, let's go out there and, you know, go put a foundation in place here, you know, systems in place. Going to make a couple tweaks and adjustments here, but Nick's a really good coach. Um, he's got a good attitude, he's got good energy, um, has a lot of respect for the players. So, I mean, go out there and training camp it's about the players, but it's about the coaches as well. So, getting back into your routine, calling plays, reacting to the situation. We have a lot of unscripted periods where DeMeco will have the coordinators just call plays. So, you just try to prepare, then you go back, hey, you know what, this worked, all right, maybe go back, make a tweak here. Um, I'd say the core foundation of what we're going to do offensively will probably be installed within the first 2 weeks. And it really it's about what the players do well. So, what do the players do well, and then we're going to build the game plan and the offense accordingly. So, um, you know, excited about the opportunity Nick has in front of him, excited about the opportunity, you know, for the whole coaching staff. >> What does elevating Jerry to quarterback coach help make that goal maybe get achieved? >> Yeah, we'll see. I mean, you know, Jerry's a lot of experience, Jerry's a smart coach, he's got a, you know, varied background in a number of different systems. So, in the end, you know, DeMeco felt like that was the right thing for us to do. So, you know, excited about the opportunity Jerry has in front of him. >> We know that C.J.'s contract has been one of the biggest stories around this team. When you go into these contract negotiations, and large as C.J. is, specifically, when you go into a contract negotiation as an player, how much of it is based off of the past, and how much of it is based off of the future, and getting into the years and how long you're going >> Yeah, you take all the information in and just try to make the best decision possible, having an understanding of what the market is, what are the dynamics. It's not necessarily about what other teams are doing. Like, we're focused on the Texans, and we're focused on doing what we feel is best for our team. So, there's a lot of contracts that get done in the off season. You have free agency, you have extensions, you have contracts that get done in training camp, you have contracts that get done during the course of the season. The one of the things that we've shown is we're pretty flexible. So, engage in the discussions, try to figure out if we can agree upon a certain level that everybody's comfortable with. And if we can arrive at that end point, great. If we can't, then, you know, maybe it's at a a further point, you know, down the road. So, I'd say to your question, start we try not to overcomplicate it. You know, don't don't overthink it. Just take the information and we're making an assessment about what we think potentially we have in the player, what it's going to look like moving forward. Doesn't mean we're going to be right on everything. Absolutely not. But, we just try to make the right decision with the information that we have in real time. And if we got to make an adjustment along the way, then we'll make an adjustment. >> The investments you made in the offensive line in the off season, is there a point in training camp where you hope five guys sort of emerge? And is there sort of a a moment where you hope that's already occurred? >> Yeah, it's a good question. Uh probably take a little bit of time here, a few weeks. Cuz the reality is the inside positions, you're going to have a lot of movement. You're going to have multiple players with their hands on the ball. You're going to have multiple players kind of rotating at the guard spots. Um I'd say to a certain extent, probably the same at tackle. I mean, I think Tay, like, unless something were to happen, he's probably going to be left tackle. Feel like we have pretty good competition there right tackle and Trent and Braden Smith. Um and then we have a number of players that we think we can that can help us inside. So, it'll take a little bit of time. Probably wouldn't read too much into it who lines up where the first day of training camp. And it's going to be an evolution. It's going to be organic. And there's going to be things that happen. A guy gets injured, something happens, we're going to have to make an adjustment. Um so, at some point here, you know, hopefully toward middle towards the end, you know, we have an idea of who the five are going to be. But, the reality is probably going to need eight. And you're probably going to be a lot of players that rotate in that, but at some point, as we start to maybe start to think about getting ready for Buffalo, there's some things that are going to be in place practice-wise, so we're focused on Buffalo. So hopefully, you know, we have a group in place that we think we're going to be able to play with, you know, the first week against Buffalo. >> You talked about the implementation of the offense. Starting off, is that going to be a a consistent amount of emphasis on the running game? You try to sort of balance that out. You're just going to have to work it out with the with the five or the eight that what you just mentioned. >> Yeah, you emphasize everything. I think every team kind of goes through an installation. You have kind of core runs, you have your core passes, and you try to marry those up, and then you try to figure out, well, you know what? Looks like we might be pretty good at this, and maybe we're not going to be so as good as that at that. Um so, it's a process. Um it's no different this year than it is any other year, so what can the players do? What are the players good at? What are some of the things that we feel we can emphasize? are always going to have a core foundation that you're going to want to be able to utilize, especially the first three or four weeks of the season. You're probably going to focus on your core, make some game plan adjustments specific to who the opponent is. Um so, you know, hopefully, you know, we're good in the running game, hopefully we're good in the passing game, and you know, we take care of the football. Um ultimately, offensively, it's moving the ball, scoring points, and taking care of the ball. So however we do that, some games we might have to run it 50 times, some games we might have to throw it 50 times. Whatever the game calls for, whoever the opponent is, then hopefully we can bob and weave and and play accordingly. >> You're commenting on something you said earlier. You know, if this negotiation with C.J. Stroud's representation continues, would you continue that through the season, or is that something you table um after >> Yeah, we'll see. I think we'll take it one day at a time. Like I said, we've had pretty constructive discussions here over the course of the spring, so I'd say, you know, it's a possibility something can happen in training camp. Um if it doesn't happen in training camp, then we probably have to make a decision about, you know, what we feel makes the most sense. So, like I said, try to take it one day at a time and, you know, if we reach an end point, great. If we don't, you know, I think everybody understands what that, you know, will entail as well. Well, yeah, you're going to have five players that you're going to put out there week one. So, you're going to have five starters and then you're going to have whoever six, seven, and eight are, they're going to have to fill the backup roles understanding that those players might have to go in and play extensive snaps two, three, four, five games or whatever the case may be. So, um, again, you're going to see a lot of people, a lot of players in and out at multiple positions. So, talking about the offensive line, you know, with their staff competition there. Say there's competition at the punting position as well. So, we have two players there. We're probably not going to have two punters on the team. Like, if we do then, you know, we're probably not making a real smart decision. But, anyways, so get through the first couple weeks of camp, get a lot of people in and out. We'll evaluate, the coaching staff will evaluate, the personnel staff will evaluate, and just making sure that, you know, we're making the right decision understanding that whoever is in this building, the expectation is that they're going to probably play meaningful football for us at some point. title: Texans among several teams interested in Jadeveon Clowney: breaking down potential reunion chances
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. One of the questions I get frequently is the veteran pass rusher market. Would the Texans be interested in perhaps bolstering the third defensive end spot? So, right now, obviously, as you know, they have all-pro bookend tandem with Will Anderson Jr. and Neil Hunter, the best pass rushing tandem in the NFL. But, what about third defensive end? And my update is this. They do have interest in former Texans top overall pick and three-time Pro Bowl pass rusher Jadeveon Clowney per multiple league sources. So, does that mean he's coming to the Texans, Aaron? That's your next question. Not necessarily, but there is interest. So, it's very interesting to me that the Texans are interested in Jadeveon Clowney. And he's interested, too. And essentially, they've become his hometown. He lives in Houston. He trains in Houston. But, they're not alone in interest in the former top pick of the draft. The guy from South Carolina that made the big hit against Michigan, knocked his helmet off, and had had his moments here before the trade to the Seattle Seahawks. Texans could ultimately never agree to a deal with Clowney at that time in terms of a long-term extension, which he wanted. But, it just never worked out. So, could there be a reunion in the offing? Maybe. Maybe is a very important word. It all depends on if the Texans want to compete financially with teams that are willing to commit more. One of those teams that's very interested in Jadeveon Clowney and has been throughout his free agency is the Cleveland Browns. So, the Cleveland Browns had him in for a visit. And another team that's interested are the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks, the team that he was traded for. And they're not the only team. There's other teams involved. And it's a growing list, as you see. Some teams are losing pass rushers. Nick Skurton out for the season. Looks bad with Stephon Gilmore Stephon Gilmore Stephon Gilmore with the Carolina Panthers. The New Orleans Saints just lost a good defensive player today, Bryan Bresee. So, there's a lot of injuries, and I can tell you this, Clowney is in shape, and Clowney is coming off of a good season with the Dallas Cowboys. So, one of the Dallas Cowboys wanted him back. They say he doesn't fit their scheme. They want a bigger type of edge rusher, but he had a good season with the Cowboys. So, he's 33. He's entering his 13th NFL season. Obviously, he's not young anymore, but he's still pretty dynamic, and he's had a great year training with veteran trainer Ben Fairchild. So, as he told me in the off season, he stands on his grind, quote. He's got a lot left in the tank. He says, "I don't know if other people know that, but he knows it. He's confident that he can prove that to people and show people that he can do it." So, last year, when they managed him on a snap count, 44% of the defensive snaps, eight and a half sacks, 41 tackles, he had 12 tackles for losses and 10 quarterback hits. It was his best year since 2023 when he was with the Baltimore Ravens, another team he would be interested in, but hasn't stepped up as of yet. When he had nine and a half sacks and 19 quarterback hits, one of his best years. But, the final game of the season against the Cowboys, that was vintage Clowney. Unblockable. They had no answers for a Clowney. Absolute menace. Six tackles, two and a half sacks, one forced fumble, fumble recovery. Was chasing down quarterback Jackson Dart and running back Devin Motor Singletary. Talk about a motor. Clowney still had a motor. And obviously, thoroughly liked being a Dallas Cowboy. Has the background in 4-3 and 3-4 defensive schemes. Feels pretty scheme flexible, and is a fit in pretty much any alignment. As he told me, "Ain't no scheme I can't play in. Well said by JD. 3-4 to 4-3 to whatever damn scheme they have. He says he can not just play in them, but dominate and do his job at a high level. Came off a great season. He wants to do it again. He said, "Teams know I'm available. I walk in every year and play well in every scheme, every team." He just wants to continue to do that, show people wrong, that prove he can still play at a high When you think about Clowney, this is where things stand. Yes, things can change pretty quickly. So, Texans have not moved on him and he hasn't been in with another team at this point, but he has options, I'm told. So, that's where it stands. So far, could there could this happen? Could JD Clowney be a Texan? Uh I'd like to be very realistic when it comes to free agency with the emphasis of the word free cuz it's up to him and it's up to the teams. But yes, the Texans, they have offered preliminary offer and so have other teams. So, he's got action. It's just a matter of picking what's the best financial deal versus other things. Trying to win a championship and you know, going where maybe there's a good playing time situation for him. How much does the third defensive end play for the Texans? Do they need a player of Clowney's caliber? Perhaps maybe they get Dominique Robinson and they have you know, Dylan Horton. So, yeah, they could use some depth. They're one injury away. And you know, knock on wood that that wouldn't happen to anything to Danielle Hunter or Will Anderson Jr. But what if it did? What's the depth like? What would they do? text: Now is training camp is it more significant now that it's training camp season just 6 weeks away? >> Oh yeah, um it was fun, man. Getting out here with my brothers. Like I said, um only thing is, a different voice. Um so they they're not the same person, you know, so he might call something else. I don't know what Mike would call cuz he's not he's not here. I mean, very smooth? >> Yeah, it was smooth. It was it was fun, man. Like you said, just the um the energy out there, just the the leaders and the captains, you know, just everybody being healthy and being able to be out there, you know, that's that's a blessing. >> Have you ever been around a camp that starts with first drill is 11-on-11? >> Um I mean, no, but that's fun, though. I mean, that's good. I mean, you know, more seven-on-seven. Um Cuz the linebackers don't like that. You know, they like to depend on D-line. I always give them a hard time about that, but you know, it's good playing 11-on-11 cuz that's what we go out there and play. Um but I mean, I rather do 11-on-11 anyway. >> Dillon, when you you do 11-on-11 off the start off the jump like that, is that to see where people are at and where they know what they're doing and stuff? You think it's like a little test run? >> Um probably. Um I like 11-on-11 cuz, you know, you can run the ball. You can't run the ball seven-on-seven. So, um I prefer that and I like um you know, O-line being there. Like, I like more realistic. So, if it was up to me, I feel like doing 11-on-11 way better. Oh, it was good, man. Like I said, just, you know, first day. I feel like first day. Um I feel like, you know, we we was we was decent. Is there anything specific you delve into to prepare for the game? >> Everything. Um I mean, that's like I said, I try to get better every year. Um in every aspect. title: Yahoo Sports' Jori Epstein on Training Camp, Vikings Quarterback Competition, Expectations for 2026
text: It's the first day of Vikings training camp. I am joined by NFL writer, senior NFL writer Jory Epstein. And Jory, you've been out here, I mean, you've been here for two days now. I have. You are about to start your big camp journey all over the NFL. How many How many camps do you normally go with every year? >> It looks like we're going to get to 16 during camp. We did three OTAAS, so 19 total is the plan. >> Okay. That's incredible. All right. So, starting out at Minnesota, what was the strategy there? >> Yeah, I mean, you guys have a quarterback battle in case anyone's heard. And also just from a standpoint of like, okay, go here. Go to Green Bay. I can drive to a bunch of teams from here. But I think what's going on here is really interesting for me. It's not where are the answers, it's where are the questions. >> What questions do you have then? >> Yeah. I mean, I think the biggest question is Kyler or JJ. And I think it's interesting to me at this point, clearly we're not deciding anything right now, but to me it's okay, the staff has an understanding to some degree of what JJ looks like in this offense. So what does Kyler look like in this offense when it's going a little bit more full speed? On the other hand, how has JJ improved his mechanics? Because the windows that you're throwing to in college are not the same as the NFL, and now he's had a year to see that. So, it's fun to see not just how they go about it, but also what are those decision-m processes by the coaches to have the competition. >> I want to ask this question twofold, but we'll take two separate times to answer. What did you learn from listening to Kyler Murray today? >> Yeah, I think from listening to Kyler, he was like, I looked at that playbook every single day for the last six weeks and now it's kind of in KO's hands. But I think throughout the time and even when he was talking to y'all during OTAAS, he's confident and he says, "I believe I can do this." And now it's not about, "Oh, I'm trying." He he didn't say, "I'm trying to show I can be the starter." He says, "I want to prove to my coaches and my teammates what I can do." But I do think he believes he can be a starter. He was the number one overall pick for a reason, >> right? Okay. So, on the flip side, we had JJ McCarthy at the mic as well. What did you learn from him? >> Yeah, JJ talked a lot about he's like, "Look, after that hand fracture, there's kind of this element of now you can get back into the footwork and the techniques." And anytime you have an injury, it really does slow your development and your progressions. And so I think that the first year as well as what he was dealing with last year did influence that. And now he's hoping, can I have a healthy year so that I can show what I can do when I'm not injured? >> Right. He seemed very confident at the podium today, especially after what they were able to do at the end of last season. Part of that confidence is is having Justin Jefferson as a wide receiver. So are you guys able to catch up a little bit? What are some of the things you were trying to to gauge from Justin? Yeah, I think it's interesting if you're Justin, how are you managing this quarterback competition? And he's like, to me, it's less about I need to see the quarterbacks. Now, the more the quarterbacks need to see him, but there is an element of quarterbacks are going to have different rhythms, different timing, and he has to be able to be on the same rhythm and timing with both of them to see who's going to be out there. And realistically, in the NFL season, they're both going to be out there at some point. >> So, obviously, you have a good pulse on the NFL as a whole going into the season. I mean, so early on because we're just starting camp, but what what is the perception of this Vikings team heading into 2026? >> Yeah, I think this is a team where you don't really have questions about the defense any year cuz Brian Flores is going to have them ready and just the style they play. It almost not that it doesn't matter who's in, but the guys are going to be ready. You have a ton of weapons, but you're in one of the toughest divisions and you have been every year and you saw Caleb Williams really break out last year and you see what's going on in Green Bay and so I really think the question is in a tough division, can you separate? because it's not like this is going to be a 4-in team, but the difference between nine and 11 might be the difference in the playoffs. >> All right, final question. You also got a chance to talk to some of our head brass. You heard uh Nolan Teasley and Kevin Okcon at the podium. What were some of your uh takeaways for that duo heading into this year together? >> Yeah, I think that this coaching staff is excited about how both quarterbacks are going to be better from this competition. And I think there's also this belief that it's not just about what's going on in the passing game, but also Frank Smith, associate head coach, assistant head coach. I think he's an underrated part of what's going on this year. They really feel confident in what he's going to do for the run game. And I talked to players also who said, "Look, the way that we're going to be marrying the pass in the run and disguising what we're doing, we think that will help us a lot." >> All right. Do you think that could be a big boost from what you've seen previously? >> I think so, and I think that they believe that it will. >> That's awesome. All right, Jory, thank you so much. Really appreciate it. Of course, you can check out our work at Yahoo Sports and we'll continue more interviews just like this as Vikings training camp rolls on. Thanks for having me.

title: Justin Reid on energy, Julian Blackmon | Saints Training Camp 2026
text: Hated. We made it. You guys feel the energy in this building right now? It's freaking awesome, man. Yeah. >> Starting off day one with that kind of vibe, that kind of energy. >> Huge, man. Get to see if guy What guys showed up in shape, what guys, you know, need a little work, and you know, I get to go out there and play some football, man.
