So, it was exciting day today, fun to get out there. Feels like the understanding of the defense and each other, and offensive players I'm sure will say the same thing. The understanding is so much better, and that excitement is showing up, man. We have the right pieces, we have a lot of young talent, a lot of guys showing up. And it's just good, man. It's fun to be out there. >> What's the biggest difference between Kellen Moore from year one and year two? >> Uh No, no, you know what? Like the the standard's always rising, and I think that there was a little bit of grace in the beginning, right? Because you're learning something new, and you're trying to see what you got. And you know, the standards are known now about what we expect to be, but he's the same guy, man. He he has been cool, calm, consistent, which is, you know, in my opinion, the best thing you can ask for someone to be your head coach cuz you know what you get. You know what to expect. The same day it's going to be the same thing. Um and you just can continue to do the same thing. Get reps on reps and, you know, build that build that uh base level up. >> When you look at the secondary, maybe on the outside, obviously, there's questions about like which who they would be in your three, Quincy, and Sinker, and I guess that star role. >> Yeah. >> What do you see from the inside with that >> Yeah, I see I see a bunch of dogs ready to get in the fight, man. I see a lot of opportunity. Um Sinker moving to star is about, you know, we want to He's a good player and we want to find a way to get him on the field. Julian got hurt early last season, week one. Um but Julian's also a good player and we want to find ways to get our best players on the field all at the same time. And Sinker's versatile, he's fast, he's smart, he's a willing tackler, um and he can play the job well. He has the right stuff for it. So, excited for him to get in that position and uh be able to shine. And his path is kind of reminding me of my own path because my second year in the league I also went from playing safety my second year, I played star. And then third and fourth year, I went back to safety again. So, it's fun seeing his journey. Um he's going to be a He's going to be playing in this league a long time. And let me tell you about Kool-Aid McKinstry, though. Kool-Aid McKinstry is a baller, bro. From what he did in OTAs to what he's doing today, I mean, it showed up again today. That cat is going to be something special, man. I'm excited about what he's going to do this year. He's been putting in the work. He's been grinding hard. It's showing up. >> We talked about Julian once already, but you didn't get a real chance to get that gold with him last year. Is there you made him a defensive second defensive back field. How exciting is it now to to get him back and and to run it back? >> Yeah, absolutely, bro. You don't know how many handshakes we came up with, bro. And then we didn't get to use any of them, you know, we didn't So, we got we got a whole armory. We got a whole armory of celebrations that we're going to be throwing out this season, but uh he's like my best friend on the team, bro. Smart player, we're dynamic. We can play both sides. It's kind of like we get on the field, it's like, "Hey, you want to play on left side or right side today?" "Ah, I'm feeling this side." "All right, I'll do the other one." So, that communication, um we truly cheer for each other. Like there's zero animosity. Like I love when he makes plays, he loves when I make plays. So excited to be back there with him. >> And on the handshakes though >> One more time? >> Martin Emerson Jr. What does he add? >> Yeah, he adds he adds he adds physicality, he adds length. Um the biggest thing right now is him getting caught up on the playbook. But you can see his confidence level from right now from where he got where he started with us in the middle of OTAs. He's taking a big leap and he's made some plays today. I love the way that he gets out of his breaks especially as a big tall cornerback. It's impressive the way that he transitions. And I'm excited for him to come out and help us out too. So we have we have like the secondary in my opinion should be a major strength. Uh the 2026 Saints, right? We should have we have depth, we have a lot of players that can play. And we need to find a way to get everybody on the field. >> So on the handshakes, you and Julian have a list of handshakes. Is that Am I understanding that correctly? >> Yeah, we got a whole armory. >> So it's like that depends on like yeah >> No, we'll just we'll we'll say we'll say it before the play. Like like hey hey, uh this series if we do something we're going to do this one, right? It's like yeah, it's just the back of the head thing. >> not tied to this is the interception celebration, this is the PBU celebration. >> It's it's it's you know, and we're going to be it's not it's not it's not strict. >> [laughter] >> You know, so if in the moment in the moment we might be running up to each other we might just say, oh uh the basketball one, you know, like we might just say it to each other before we do it and then we'll just do it. >> Okay. >> What could you could you put a number [snorts] to it? >> Uh how many we have? >> We have five right now. >> And you're trying to build more? >> Yeah, just me. Just me and him. Yeah, I got got at least one with each of the guys. Still working on the ones with the the rookies. Um but all the year two and above players got at least one. Oh handshake? It's like you know It's not like it's it's it's muscle memory, honestly. You don't even have to think about it. >> What what was the when you made that transition from safety to the playing in the slot, Like did you feel what what what's the biggest transition in that? >> Well, this is how the closer you get to the ball, the more you have to feel. There's less reading, there's more feeling, right? So, the farther back you can read more cuz you have time. The closer you get to the ball, you have to react more. So, the closer you get to the line of scrimmage, you have to see the puller and just go. And you got to just trust it, right? Cuz if not, you're going to get sealed, you're going to get um caught, right? And if you want to make a play, you got to have that that quick trigger and just kind of go and let it happen. And trust that, hey, if I'm fitting my gap, I'm fitting my gap, but it's it's better to go fast and make a decision now, so that the person behind you can play off of you, than it is to hesitate and be caught between two gaps, and now the person behind you is also confused on what you're doing. Right? So, the closer you are to the the line of scrimmage, you need to go faster. The farther you are back, you can take your time more, you can read the gaps, read that, okay, cancel, cancel, cancel, cancel. This one's the open one. I'm going to go fit here. All right. So, yeah. >> Is is there a physical component to it, too, or is >> Oh, yeah. If you if you if you if you don't have dog in you, like, nickel's going to be a hard sport. Like, you see some some nickels are coverage guys, and you know, if I'm offensive coordinator and I see a coverage nickel on the field, I'm going to run the ball at him. You know? Why would I throw at him, you know? If you're forced to on third down, that's one thing, but first and second down, then I'm going to run at you, you know? And I feel like offensive coordinators are going to test and see who find out who the soft tackling DB is and spend their whole game plan running at them. And that's why I emphasize so much with the DBs. I've never been a part of a secondary where we had a guy on the field who was afraid to tackle, cuz it doesn't work. As soon if your corners and your star tackles, then offenses don't have a run game. When they don't have a run game, they don't have a play action game. You know? It all feeds into each other, right? So, it's a big deal to have a willing tackler on the field in that position. And Saint, you know, comes from being a safety, so tackling's not going to be a problem for him. >> Because the way that you guys do play, you play a lot of zone, you are kind of farther back, but seems like you have established that physicality. How are you guys able to do that when you're maybe starting from a further back point or whatever that physicality still still has? >> Yeah, you know, it's it's it's really it's really it's really willpower. It's it's a willingness thing than anything else. Like you got to be willing to put your face in it. That's just kind of how this game goes, you know? If you don't If you don't have it inside of you, you don't have it inside of you. And if you do, you do. >> Just from last year, too. Every year we see teams kind of go from worst to first in the league. Um Patriots last year went on to win the Super Bowl. Why do you think this team could be one of those teams to make that kind of turnaround? >> Because we have the right pieces. I mean, the foundation is set. We went, I don't know, five or six or whatever on last at our one point in the season at the end of the year. Um we have a young quarterback who is playing lights out right now. And, you know, the biggest thing for him is to do exactly what he was doing before, you know, cuz he's continuing to build, don't get comfortable. And he He knows all this, and he's been preaching and he's been breaking down the huddle. So, he's stepped into that leadership role. He's ready for the moment, you know? So, that's a big deal. Number one, you have to have a guy who can play quarterback. And I feel like we got that box checked. Then you got to pack your defense. Defense feels like, you know, the way we stopped the run, top three in the league in the second half of the season. We got to bring defense by defense with you. And then you need some playmakers on offense. We drafted five wide receivers this year. So, we Kellen's been adding some fire some firepower to that offense. And, you know, once you put those things together, you usually get a good deal. >> What why did the team buy even the vets like you bought into Tyler Show so quickly this season? >> Cuz he's just he you you know what it looks like. You know, as a veteran player, you can see similar attributes on guys that you played with, and you know what intangibles translate well and which ones, you know what I mean? Is it okay, yes, time to develop that. But certain things like the flight of his ball, it's a piercing ball, but it's also very soft, which is very wide receiver friendly. And that like it's it's easily catchable for wide receivers. Some guys in the league throw the ball too hard. They throw bullets. And then they make it the wide receivers' fault that they dropped the ball. This is the NFL. You should catch it both ways, but if you can assist your guy in, you know, catching the football, that's just more points on the board. That's more yardage. That's more points on the on the board. That's more yardage. All those things, right? So, his ball flight and his decision-making and decision-making comes with more experience and he's gotten better with that, too. But, his ball flight and his intangibles, um he's more athletic than people give him credit for. His ability to scramble out of the prot- out of the pocket and be creative. It is those things that help you win. >> You talked about his last year at this time. >> Yeah, huge. I mean, the the biggest jump that you can see right now is his leadership. His command of the huddle, his command of the offense, his um confidence to stand up in front of the whole team and break down the huddle, right? That's been a major jump and that's what you need out of your your general on the field. >> What's the biggest difference defending him this year compared to last year before he came in? >> Um Well, this is the same objective. We're going to try and make it harder on >> We're going to try and make it as hard as we possibly can. Uh we're going to throw every look at him because the more things we throw at him, the more he'll get used to seeing it. Um but, it's worked for us, too, you know? We can um we're just going to continue to to sharpen each other up that way. >> Have you been on a team that's gone to more Super Bowls? No. I haven't. Yeah. Texans won the division, won the division, then we like, you know, two bad years. Then the Chiefs run Yeah, three two rows and yeah. So, yeah. This will be the first time. But, it does give me perspective, though. And that was the cool part about last year. There was a couple points like I remember going to Saturday Saturday walk-throughs about that midway point of the season that like I stepped in front of the team and I was like, "This just doesn't look right, you know? It doesn't feel right. It doesn't feel like a championship walk-through. Like guys aren't in their stances consistently. Like it just it just feels a little bit loose." And I'm all about loose as long as the details are tight, right? But it felt loose and chaotic, right? It didn't feel that the right feeling and you know, I asked Kellen for permission to say something in front of the team and he allowed me to do that and then it started cleaning up and I think that that also it's just it's just the mental things that help you translate into cuz the margin between winning and losing in the NFL is very small. It's not big at all, right? And it's the details that matter more than anything. You can steal reps in your walk-throughs. Like at this point in my career, I believe in walk-throughs more than anything. Early on training camp, you got young players. You got to see what they got. You got to see if they can physically hold up and everything. Once you're a guy, you know that you're physically you physically match what it takes to be in the league, right? It's the mental side of it. How fast can you think? How fast can you act on those thoughts, right? Because if you are able to see something, diagnose it and make a move, you're going to make the play. And if you hesitate, they're going to make the play, right? And I think that you win those reps in walk-throughs more than you win them in full-speed drills because it allows you to actually see what a guy is thinking. You can evaluate. I know that his eyes are in the right spot because he didn't waste any steps with his movements, right? Kind of hard to see that full speed. >> Do you remember when that >> I can't name the exact week, but it was about the midway point. Yeah. >> You had said Taysom Hill's leadership and you're not the only one who has said that today. Aside from just breaking down the huddle, what other ways has he stepping up as a leader? >> Yeah, I mean, he brought all the wide receivers out to San Diego. You know, that's a veteran thing to do. He brought the entire wide receiver staff out there to continue to get work in the off-season, to continue sharpening each other up. That's not something that every cat does, you know? You have some quarterbacks who just go home or work one-on-one with themselves or whatever, whatever, but he's been bringing guys along with them and he's stepped into the role well. And the way he embraces the city is is just awesome, you know? Like people in New Orleans know how much like what it means to have, you know, your stars embrace the city and he's done a great job of that. Um so I think he he's the right man for the job. >> Let's talk about the maximizing of of walk-throughs and just now and you praised that clearly in the press earlier. Is that I think kind of like minutia, finer detail thing you're seeing him >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I mean, across the board, like Cooley Cooley's mentality this year is serious. Like, every rep he has been serious. Locked in. Right stance, right eyes in the right spot, communication. It's been at a really fun level, and it's fun to play with him. >> Eye discipline for the DBs obviously such a such a huge thing. Is that like an experience thing, or are there things that you can work on to try to progress that a little bit? >> It's a little bit of both. It It's a little bit of both. It's It's not It's not exclusive to guys who played multiple years in the league. It's just It's just something that you have to continue to be on top of, because it's easy to have good eye discipline, and throughout the, you know, the waxing and waning of the season, to just very slowly lose it. You know, it's very easy for that to happen, and then, you know, just having the ability to refocus in and, um, do that. And I know Grady does a really good job with that, too. Um, being on the cornerbacks specifically about their eye discipline. Um, because this defense relies heavily on the corners to play well. Uh, this defense does, cuz the corners are in a lot of one-on-one situations, and they have to win. >> How would you describe the identity of your y'all's group, the defense? >> Um, electric, together. Um, we have a ton of fun, and like, really I'd say controlled chaos. Controlled chaos is the best way to put it, because you want guys that, man, fast, loose, physical. Um, we want to make a statement physically against everyone we play against. And, you know, you're going to remember that you played the 2026 Saints. You know what I mean? You're going to leave a couple marks here and there. Um, but it's fun to see the mental side of it take the jump that it has in OTAs, and, uh, this first day out on the field. There's still a ton of work to do, of course. Um, but it's fun to see that mental leap that the defense as a whole has continued to, um, continue to raise with. >> As a Louisiana native, what was it like your first year in the Superdome? And what are you looking forward to in your second year? Hopefully, you know, a better team and looking forward to >> Yeah, you know, like you know, my first memory of the Superdome was It was like that two that early that sorry that late 2000s era. When it was just it feels like a parade in the Superdome. You have the umbrellas, you have the people with the costumes, you have people throwing popcorn, confetti, whatever, you know, you got the the old music and the na na na na na na. You know what I mean? Like all of that stuff, man, and you know, you you still felt that last year, but it didn't remind me of my childhood. You know what I mean? And I wanted to look like what it looked like for me when I was a kid. You know what I mean? So that kids today can have that memory. You know what I mean? And they want to keep pushing it forward, right? So it's a lot of that and I know that winning helps a lot of that. You know, you want the city to be proud of you and that's what we're looking to do. >> And when you mentioned catching the ball so I promise this is not a smart ass question, but How does the safety know that the zone quarterback was catching the ball? >> You can see it by flight. I mean, you want to you have conversations with um you have conversations with wide receivers and the wide receivers usually, you know, they're grumbling about it. You know, some wide receivers grumble about how hard the quarterback throws the ball or whatever, but usually if you have a conversation with wide receivers, they'll tell you. But two, if you're watching it, right? So there's like there's like different You have like a ball that's a laser that just looks like a blur, right? That's probably thrown a little bit too hard. Then you have a ball that is off, but it's just too high and it just looks like it hangs up in the air for six, seven seconds, right? That's a DB's dream. Those are interceptions, right? Then you have the one that's right in the middle that, you know, it it isn't floating. It's still piercing. It's a tight spiral, so it's still piercing. It doesn't hover in the air, but it it just comes down gently to where it just makes it feel like the wide receiver has time to nestle it into a cradle rather than feels like you're trying to stop a bullet from hitting you in the face. All right? It's kind of like that difference. >> It wasn't cuz you were intercepting them a bunch of times. >> No, no, it isn't it isn't that. It's mainly the conversation with wide receivers, but I'm going to try to get my hands on one or two just to make it hard on them. Yeah. >> You're a golfer. It's kind of like a golf shot, right? You use different shots. >> Mhm. Shot shapes depending on the moment. >> Right. >> Mhm. >> So, you're kind of parking the ball. >> Put them clubs in the camera up for the time being and just kind of set it hard. >> Yeah. Yeah, you know, I I played I played Oakmont on Thursday and that was my last hurrah trip. So, they're going to get put up for now and we're going to focus on football and make sure we get this thing right. >> Side quest on pause. >> Huh? >> Side quest on pause. Yeah.

It takes time to understand like the ins and outs of why, when, how he's doing things. So I think everybody you know, had a good feeling about that. You know, it just had to equate to wins and I think just obviously I mean talking to everybody you know, throughout the OTAs in the off-season everybody had a good feeling even better feeling than we did last year about what what could happen this year. Um but that was just an example of just like you know, one thing the Titans do that and that was a that was a cool part is we were all competing, you know, the Titan in the state, you know, beat our record of whatever the farmers walk was. And once something else other than that happens, then we adjust. >> So, when you said you better than you ever been, are you talking mentally and >> Yeah, I think I think mentally. I think mentally and physically. I think just cuz I a lot of things, you know, I think in the football world, a lot of guys get caught up in in, you know, and I think we we've we've heard it since we were little, like eat, sleep, drink football, eat, sleep, drink football. And I don't think that's ever been my MMO. Like I've always had a lot going on off the field, whether it's, you know, family, business, things like that. So, I think this off seasonason along with like training and and getting ready to play, you know, I just kind of like a a lot of other things that I've been that I've been doing these past couple of years, like I kind of gave it a little bit more time and energy and focus and, you know, it just it just felt good to kind of like have other things that, you know, you you you can use to take your focus off of like a contract situation or a a potential chip being on my shoulder. You know what I'm saying? So, like I just feel I just feel good. I feel energized. I feel refreshed. I got a Zoom call in like 25 minutes for something like, you know, it's just I'm cool, man. I feel good. >> Just the clarity. >> What can it be? >> You and you and Hn together. What do you think it can be? >> Man, I mean Travis is a great player, you know. I think um a lot of my career has been, you know, me and someone else, me and Mark, me and Latavius. Um you know, so like there's there's I have no issue with that at all. You know, whatever the whatever the role is, whatever the the the snaps are, like I'm good with it. Like I said, like I say every year, and y'all probably tired of hearing it, like whatever I I need to do, that's what I'm here to do. >> Does the clarity you receive, sorry, does the clarity you receive like also include the how it'll exactly work with him? Just kind of the maybe the split or like the how like the flow? >> Yeah, I mean I I really I honestly I have no clarity in that cuz I don't know when like what what the what the game plan is with that, but I mean I'm here to work. So he here to work. Same thing with Kendrick. Same thing with Devin. Like everybody's, I guess, figuring out roles. So, um, I'm good. You know, I'm here. I'm working. I'm going to do what I got to do. >> What's your favorite part about those splits? Like, what what's the best part of getting to not having to carry the load? Uh, I just think honestly, you know, in those situations, like back when me and Mark were going, like you feed off of each other, like somebody in the same room, it's different from like me feeding off of Mike T or like a Chris Abby or something, but like when you in the same room and you kind of doing the same thing and like I can look out and shoot probably see Trev and I know the play is called and I'm like, "Oh, I know he about to hit this." And then it's like, "Okay, now I'm about to go in and I know I got a play called and you kind of just it's a different type of energy when you're feeding off a guy in the back field." um in the same back field with you. And then it again it just it kind of like alleviates some of the some of the strain, some of the pressure of you know having to take on a full load. You know, I think every good team in this league, you know, you got to you got a one, two, three good runners. Um and it just it just helps the whole offense. >> What you said about like overall I mean the additions and what do you >> man I nasty. I love I love him you know. Um Eric back he good. It's good to see him healthy. Um, you know, I mean, all all those guys are ready to ready to play. I mean, they they itching. I uh Caesar and them was talking today and they were like, man, all right, this the part where we protect our shoulders until we put shoulder pads on. So, you know, them them dudes is like itching. They were they ready to put shoulder pads on already and it's day one. But, I think they ready. I think they got a lot of uh a lot of energy and a lot of um drive to kind of, you know, undo the the the wrongs of last year. Kind of like, you know, the the rushing our rushing wasn't too good. you know, some of our pass wasn't too good. Um, just our offensive efficiency wasn't good. And I feel like they take pride in in in thinking that, you know, it starts with them. So, they ready. Them dudes is ready. >> You said in recent years that you wanted to be used more efficiently in the offense. Do you feel like this setup, you were talking about the role with with Travis, you feel like this setup provides an opportunity? >> Yeah, it could potentially, you know, like I said, day one. So, we'll see. We'll get into it. But I think it uh this situation kind of offers a uh potential for, you know, like I said, that kind of efficiency to to kind of manifest. >> Something Mickey had said something about how like your consistent indications that you wanted to stay here in New Orleans meant a lot to him. I think the fans get to see what you say at the podium, but how much do you get to indicate that behind the scenes as well? >> Uh not that much. >> Yeah. Do do you try to make sure that's at the forefront in any conversation that you have with them, or is this the where you get to put I feel like y'all kind of get it out of me more than like upstairs. I don't think >> I ain't going to lie. I pro I don't think I've ever had like a one-on-one with Mickey where I'm like I want to be in New Orleans so much like you know but I think I think they understand that. They know that you know but I've never like sat up there with with Sean and been like go get New Orleans tattooed on my chest like I but you know I think I think y'all know me long enough like this kind of this where this where I am. You know I think I've done a lot here. Um it's a lot of love here. um not only on the field but off the field. So this where I wanted to be. >> So you're saying we do our job getting y little it's a little give and take. >> Hey what's been your reaction to like the fans and just how they wanted you back and like when you sign Oh yeah response did you get back from there? Um, you know, usually a lot of my it's most of my friends like sending me all this funny stuff like you know I think we got some aggressive fans so uh you know even one even one of my best friends I had to tell him uh chill out on the Instagram cuz you know Alex running the Instagram he Alex felt like he was talking to him. But uh no man I think you know again it's like a connection for through football and through a lot of that stuff off the field like man I I I've kind of like planted some roots in this community. Um and it's I think it's with me it's a lot it's it's personal you know I feel like everybody think I'm their cousin or they grandson or they they son or you know so it's it's it's love. It's love in that regard um when it comes to the fan base and you know I appreciate it. So I mean when you're out out and about in town though I mean like what kind like you're in the grocery store like >> when I'm when I'm out oh man >> what kind of stuff you hear in there >> everything I mean shoot people be inviting me to their house everything like I mean it's just nor I I don't even want to say it cuz it's just so it's so normal to me now like it's not it's not surprising to me like you know it's any I'm talking about any any given day somebody might ask me if I need something or if I it's just anything anything it's like every time I see somebody it's like I've known them for 20 years. Alvin, getting back to uh Drew Brees. You remember the first time you met him? >> Uh first time I met Drew, it's my rookie year I came in. We were about to do I think the receivers were going out to do like routes and they were like go out there with him. And I'm like play receiver. So I went out there and Drew was like what's up? And I'm like what's up dog? Dabbed him up and he was like all right go run a Harvey. I'm like all right. And that was it. I remember though. Yeah. we go straight to business. But n saying all that to say like it's just Drew a regular guy. You know what I'm saying? Like cool dude. Um definitely uh appreciative and blessed to have been a part of his had a part in his story. And I mean he he had a part in my story. You know what I'm saying? So uh congrats again to Drew. Congrats to his family. excited for us opportunity to be gold jacketed.

title: Saints QB Tyler Shough on working with Drew Brees, stepping up as a leader, Jordyn Tyson + more
text: How excited are you just to be out there, anxious? Like describe the emotions of day one this year and maybe how it's a little different than last year. >> Yeah, I think everybody's just was super anxious to get back out there. I think from off off-season perspective um we checked off a lot of boxes from just connecting with each other, having fun, but also competing, getting better. So um now it's kind of a sense of urgency where we're you know, we're going to watch film. We're going to have a lot of one a lot of stuff back, but then like you said, you know, looking back from last year um we're still trying to figure out the huddle and trying to figure out the cadence and um myself still trying to figure out everything. So um I'm going to make mistakes. Everybody's going to make mistakes, but I feel I feel like this um this training camp we're we're all kind of striving to really get better and put it together. >> I think I saw you like in one of the uh one of the team drills or seven-on-seven. I think you were over the wide receivers and you're kind of shelving like what you want like in terms of how to run a certain route or something. Doing like that kind of stuff it it does it just feel like it's an ease to now assist, you know, you are running this thing. It's an ease to kind of talk your way like kind of get everyone organized and it's it's a lot better than what it was like last year because you didn't have that kind of say in doing that. >> Yeah, I think there's obviously previous reps to look back on and um you know, having that familiarity with the offense. So you know, having you know, a guy like Jordan, you know, who's running plays for the first time and being able to kind of talk to him through the thought process, but also um a lot of great stuff was done too and kind of prop those guys and um I can continue to um do that and get better and maybe you know, take ownership for something as well. Um that's what practice is about, you know, being able to talk with each other and go out there and um you know, kind of re-evaluate what had happened. You know, we're installing plays. Um it's not always going to be perfect. So how do we kind of put that rep in the bank and and keep going? >> How was the experience of the throwing sessions out in on the West Coast? >> It was awesome. It was um just so much fun. I think it was so worth it just spending time with each other. You know, I got to spend a week with Juwan and our whole families, you know, living with each other every single hour every day and you know, it's irreplaceable. You know, we're we're out there with all the guys, you know, working out, having fun and that was kind of one of the biggest takeaways from I got from Drew was that this is kind of where the magic happens and you know, there's 31 other teams doing training camp, you know, doing the same thing that we are, but how do we kind of spin that time as much as we can to to to get better. >> That that connective or that connection that you're building with all these guys, is that a big part of why you know, Kellen talked about weathering the storm last year why that was successful? Is that connection? >> Yeah, you have to. I mean, there's going to be we're all going to make mistakes. I'm going to throw an interception, guys are going to drop a ball, we're going to have a a misroute or a misblock and we got to be able to talk through it and it only happens, you know, if you know each other and at least have that respect and you know, obviously friendship and brotherhood. So that's all that's all going to happen and we can lean on each other when times are tough and also when we have some success, how do we kind of shift our focus forward and I feel like Kellen, the whole staff and and the whole team has done a really good job of prioritizing that. >> Tyler, obviously this is a good problem to have with like a lot of a lot of different receivers you guys added to the room, perhaps H and O fan, Oscar Delp, all that stuff. But like do you kind of consider like got a lot of mouths to feed, like how do I make sure everybody's happy or do you just kind of just go with what the play tells you to do? Like how how do you kind of keep that? >> Yeah, I think it's a good problem to have is when you have a lot of talent, but it's also you got to play football and and those guys understand that you know, you're not ever going going to get a perfect look per se, but you're going to have to do everything you can to do your job and you know, everyone's super great about that. You know, you got guys like Travis and AK and they're super talented and they aren't going to be taking every single rep, but you have you know, equal talent there and can bounce ideas off of each other and same thing in the tight end room and and receiver room and and obviously the O line. So it's my job to continue to get better myself, but also give them those opportunities. >> What stood out in your interactions with Jordan Tyson in his first day of kind of going to complete workload? >> Yeah. Um one the ability is there. He's got obviously all the talent in the world, but but two he he really wants to be great. And that's probably one of my favorite things about him is that he's such a good dude, but I feel like we share this common elk of, you know, we're never satisfied and he he's 21 years old and, you know, has every right to um maybe think you have made it, you know, you get drafted in the first round, but he's, you know, he understands that there's so much more to go and and for all of us. So, he's going to do a great job of um just continuing to get better, you know, and like all of us. >> How did that come across during the time when he wasn't able to be out there through OTAs? >> Yeah, I I mean his curiosity, you know, whenever it's out in walk-throughs, he's, you know, taking mental reps um in the film room um just talking to me, you know, we're hanging out with each other um he's obviously I mean he hasn't really missed a missed a beat, missed a rep. So, kudos to him for his preparation, um but also being able to kind of understand that, you know, we're all trying to get better and um it takes all of us. >> I'm sure you're still learning each other, you and Jordan, but have you started like getting a glimpse at what he does well? If you had describe from what you know now the things that he on the field, the things he does well, what would what would you say they are? >> Um I think separation. Um I think he does a really good job of separating line of scrimmage and then he's really consistent with his hands as well. So, um I think the the tough the tough part right now is we're installing plays, you know, we're going to have to sit different routes. So, you're not going to see a full gambit of maybe everything within a whole season, but um him being able to have that savviness um and understanding on certain plays, but you know, have the ability to get open and um it's he's very he reminds me a lot of of C O and um in that way and in their their ability to change direction, but also kind of give a really good burst. >> Jordan, what does it mean to you to have the confidence of all the veteran players in the locker room to be their leader to lead this team. >> Um I I feel like I got to do, you know, a better job and continue to do a better job every single day. You know, I want to take ownership and be a leader for for all the guys, but I feel like we have a really good group that um kind of takes that load and um and takes the the ownership of of everything. So, we got guys like Cam Jordan coming back. You know, Chase Young has been um in the league for a while doing a good job on the defensive side and Kaden Ellis as well, but you know, for the offensive group and um you know, equally we got Eric McCoy and Juwan and I think we're doing a really good job of being able to kind of bounce ideas off of each other and um but at the same time, you know, I want to do everything that I can to to make sure that we have that sense of urgency, but also the want to get better. >> Tyler, what's it like what's it like going against the defensive secondary this year? >> Say again. >> What's it like going against a secondary this year? >> I mean, it's obviously still early on, but even throughout OTAs and right now there you can see the talent and and the the veteran leadership of those guys and and you know, Jay Reed and Julian Blackman are are, you know, you don't ever know where they're going to be at sometimes. They do a really good job and um and Kool-Aid I think he's done an excellent job uh this whole offseason and then my my guy Quincy, um he's he's stepped up for sure and I'm excited to see what those guys do and and Yonas included, you know, they have a lot of a lot of talent and I think having that year under their belt, you know, gave them a lot of confidence and um really excited to see what they can do. >> Tyler, what are some pitfalls you maybe have to avoid from, you know, a lot of people talk about the year one and year two growth, but it doesn't always happen. Like what are kind of some things uh you need to avoid to like kind of on the negative side that are like to ensure that you're taking the steps that you want? >> Yeah, I think for me it's just uh it's every single day is finding one thing I can kind of focus on and get better and um I think you look at it from a holistic perspective and you can look at last year in multiple ways where you you know, we were at the bottom of the NFC South. It wasn't a good year. Um so, I think there's a lot of stuff that we can build off of and as a whole team and myself and um it it still feels like a year one. You know, I I have a the the bank reps on some of it, but I've still only played a certain amount of games and I feel like myself I have a lot more to learn and a lot more to grow and I think as a team, you know, we feel the same way and and that's that's exciting at the same time. We want we want that, you know, expe- experience and expectation, but we also want to get better. >> One of those things is probably not good to wrapped up in >> Yeah, I mean I think you you use the experience that you had and the learning lessons that we had, but also shift our focus forward and understand it's a whole new year and a and a new team and I think that's, you know, what we're looking forward to. >> Mickey was saying >> working with Drew Brees this summer and was there anything that he did in his routine that you might be able to incorporate in your routine? >> Um one on one it was it was awesome just him taking the time out of his schedule to come pour into us, you know, for you know, as a former, you know, Saint and former obviously current Hall of Famer, a former NFL player and then him being who he is and the connection to here is even better and uh like I said before the biggest thing I kind of took was the time investment with each other in the off season was the biggest Um and then also I got to talk to him last year throughout the throughout the season before I played just about his routine and it was it was really cool to be able to kind of utilize some of those things and kind of come take it into my own routine and and also be able to come compare what I've already done as well. >> You said before that for sure how much he was actually going to work out with y'all. Were you surprised he's at least one day with the picture that he was like >> Yeah. >> kind of always >> Uh I was fully expecting not to be there. He He know he was going to be in Dallas for the World Cup which he was and then, you know, might have been out of town and but it's just a credit to him for showing up and and I mean we were working out with his with him and his boys and he's pushing him really hard and he's, you know, coming to our throwing sessions and being able to talk to us. So, um it it was really cool. Um I mean, we're like like that's like our hero, you know, fans growing up and watching him. And especially for Trav, it was really cool. He's like, "Man, that's Drew Brees over there. I got to go get a picture." I was like, "Dude, he's like going to talk to us. You're good." >> [laughter] >> He's like, "He's going to come over here." Like, you don't have to He's going to He's cool, man. And I was like, he didn't know he was going to be there. So, um but it was fun. It was fun being able to have all those guys there. But, at the same time, it's just a a piece in the puzzle. And um it doesn't matter if we don't get better in training camp. >> What are Coach Moore's strengths? The fact his demeanor doesn't really change. Like, you got off to a slow start, he seemed the same. When you were winning, he seemed the same. Is it that even-keeled demeanor that that's helped the team? >> Yeah. Um I think it it's just a it goes to show his experience and understanding that the the NFL season's a roller coaster. And And you have to be able to um manage the highs and and ride the lows and and do everything that we can to make sure that we're one, we're getting better every week. And then two, achieving our goals in the long run. So, um one, we weren't able to do that last year. But at the same time, he kept us really motivated and and ready to go. And um for me, that was really good to learn cuz um I felt like regardless of the the outcome, um my process and and how I approached it um was beneficial. And that's my whole goal is I mean, I I played nine games. I'm going to make a lot of mistakes. And I got to be able to kind of keep going um and understand that, you know, relying on each other that way is going to be key. >> Mickey Mickey Loomis was saying yesterday that one of his goals in the front office was to get more explosive as a team. He's drafted a lot of lot of guys with big 40 times and everything like that. Do you like Can you see that on the field when you've been working at OTAs, mini camp? >> First day of training camp. >> Um I mean, everybody. I think from a defensive side, too, you see the the the break on the ball. You see the the way we've been working in the off season. And obviously, offensively, you know, the get-off from the line of scrimmage. And um I think they're really obviously everyone has ability in the NFL, but I think the thing I'm, you know, really proud of the guys is, you know, the the people who we picked up. Um, one, they really wanted, like I said with Jordan, they wanted to be really good, and same thing with Travis and Noah. Um, they're just great dudes, so you wouldn't think that, you know, these are like all-pro players, you know, the way that they act, but they carry themselves in such a high way. >> Do you think that story of last year's Patriots and some of the universal themes that emerged from there, kind of dramatic year-to-year improvement, are relevant in any way to this team coming into this year? >> Uh, I don't think it has any effect on us just cuz we're a completely different team, but it also, um, is just an example of that, um, it's a new team and we're trying to get better every single year. We have high expectations for ourselves. Um, but we also know that we have a long way to go, um, from where we want to be. And, you know, we were at the bottom of the barrel in a lot of our goals and certain situations last year, um, starting fast, you know, certain red zone, um, middle-eight situations, and um, and, you know, that starts with myself, so uh, we have to get a lot better there. >> Uh, spending a week with Jordan and his family, do you guys like living in a house together? How did How did it kind of affect >> Yeah, yeah, it was, um, shoutout to my uncle, my uncle James. He He has a house in La Jolla, so we he was able to open his house up and we we stayed there. Um, it was great setup, so we got to be able to spend time, go down to the beach, and then, um, go work out together, so we definitely got to make it a a yearly thing if possible. >> Did you learn anything new about your teammate living in a close quarters like that for a week or anything? >> Yeah, yeah, we we were playing some family games together. Um, we were playing like Clue and Domino and stuff like that. And then, also learned that a lot of guys are are afraid of the ocean whenever going in, and we had Barry on trying to run in the waves and just getting taken out, and um, and Jordan as well, but it was it was fun, so uh, you that's like what I was saying before, you learn a lot about each other, you know, we can kind of you know, whenever we mess up or we have a great great rep, we can kind of go back to on um to that time spent together. >> You mentioned um playing with D kind of in the fall on through. Given what's going to happen next week with the coordinator and all that, then do you look at that and bring in motivation knowing what you you Yeah, I mean, he said it yesterday when he came here. I don't know if anybody saw him making a play or anything. >> Sure. >> next week. But is that is that motivation in some way? >> [sighs] >> Um I don't know if it's motivation, but more of just just awe and respect. It's, you know, talking to him, you know, I'm nowhere even in the stratosphere of where that, you know, he was able to achieve and um you know, he spent a lot of time in San Diego and he had a lot of ups and downs and um and I was being able to talk to him about that and um come here and obviously a lot of people doubt him and continue to take, you know, answer the bell and I think his mindset, um his approach is is is is very unique and one-of-a-kind, so to even be able to talk to him, honestly, was really cool and um yeah, right now it was it was good to shift our focus um back to this as well cuz to take that and um be also applied to ourselves cuz we have a a long way to go as well. >> How about the finish on that set? >> He's uh he's kind of legendary to be a competitor. Did you Did you see any shades of that during the workout set? >> Yeah. Yeah. That was a good one cuz we were doing like farmers walks with like kettlebells and um so I was working out with him and Drew in the group and he had his like 12-year-old son and he like made him go all the way around the building and I was like, "Oh god." Cuz I can't like not get my butt kicked by a 12-year-old kid and and Drew. So I'm just like but I have to do a heavier weight than him, so I'm I grab like the heavier ones and me and Drew are walking and he's just like going like this and I'm trying not to trying not to die and um I was like, "We were just supposed to go like to the cone and back." And Drew's like, "No, go all the way around." So, I' was like, "All right. Sorry, man. I'm going with you." Um but that was just an example of just you know, one thing the tight ends do that and that was a that was a cool part is we're all competing. You know, the tight ends they, you know, beat our record of whatever the farmer's walk was. So, >> [snorts] >> I feel like that's the the benefit of doing stuff like that is one we're having fun, but then other part of it is we're trying to compete against each other. >> You see Drew throw left-handed? >> No. No, he did he didn't throw it around. Um he was he was just left-handed with us, but I've heard I've heard the lore. It's pretty good. >> How big of a factor is living in the same locker room and the same system? >> I mean, I think just from a time on task perspective and and and reps, it's um it helps out a lot. Uh I think being able to just have the comfortability, you know, with a lot of the guys in the playbook from the the huddle mechanics, cadences, stuff like that, but we also, like I said before, we also have a lot to uh to chip away at. So, and there's you know, like I said, it's a new team, so we have a lot of new faces that we have to kind of help bring on board and and including myself. So, um it's it's exciting and I think more than anything and um right now Kellen's doing a good job of keeping us focused on that.

title: Justin Reid on Year 2 with Saints, setting the standard, Julian Blackmon & Jonas Sanker and more
text: How important is that? Starting off day one with that kind of vibe, that kind of energy? >> Huge, man. That's what you want, man. It's like the first day of school. We back in the building, everyone's excited to see each other. We're talking about, you know, "Oh, I did this in the off-season. I did this." Get to see if guy What guys showed up in shape, what guys, you know, need a little work, and you know, I get to go out there and play some football, man. And um man, it feels like it's been months, and you know, after a while you start getting that itch that you just want to go out and play again, be with your brothers, be on the field, and go play some football, and we got to do that today. Maybe a little too physical for not having any pads on, but you can expect that. Guys are excited to be out here and uh compete and perform. >> Justin, what what is it about this day one that contributes to that vibe beyond just being the first day about this group? >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's it's it's uh it's confidence and passion in the work that we've done. You know, um last season, uh a lot of it was setting the foundation, and that foundation is showing up right now, you know, year two in the system for everybody. The communication level is so far and beyond what it was last year when everyone was still trying to learn each other and learn the playbook. And instead of feeling like we're starting at ground one, feels like we're starting at ground seven, right? And we have to just keep building behind that and building it up. Um so, it was exciting day today, fun to get out there. Um feels like the understanding of the defense and each other and the offensive players, I'm sure, will say the same thing. The understanding is so much better, and that excitement is showing up, man. And we have the right pieces, we have a lot of young talent, a lot of guys showing up. Um and it's just good, man. It's fun to be out there. >> Justin, have you noticed Have you noticed a big difference between Kellen Moore from year one and year two? >> Uh No, no. You know what? Like, the the standard's always rising, and I think that there was a little bit of grace in the beginning, right? Because you're learning something new, and you're trying to see what you got. And you know, the standards are known now about what we expect to be. But he's the same guy, man. He he has been cool, calm, consistent, which is, you know, in my opinion, the best thing you can ask someone to be your head coach, cuz you know what you get, you know what to expect. The same day, it's going to be the same thing. Um and you just continue to do the same thing, get reps on reps, and you know, build that build that uh base level up. >> When you look at the secondary, maybe on the outside obviously people have questions about like what role they will be in your grading. Quincy, Sinker, and I guess that's the star role. >> Yeah. >> What do you see from the inside with that >> Yeah, I see I see a bunch of dogs ready to get in the fight, man. I see a lot of opportunity. Um Sinker moving to star is about, you know, we want to He's a good player and we want to find a way to get him on the field. Julian got hurt early last season, week one. Um but Julian's also a good player and we want to find ways to get our best players on the field all at the same time. And Sinks versatile, he's fast, he's smart, he's a willing tackler, um and he can play the job well. He has the right stuff for it. So, excited for him to get in that position and uh be able to shine. And his path is kind of reminding me of my own path cuz my second year in the league I also went from playing safety my second year, I played star, and then third and fourth year I went back to safety again. So, it's fun seeing his journey. Um he's going to be a He's going to be playing in this league a long time. And let me tell you about Kool-Aid McKinstry, though. Kool-Aid McKinstry is a baller, bro. From what he did in OTAs to what he's doing today, I mean it showed up again today. That cat is going to be something special, man. I'm excited about what he's going to do this year. He's been putting in the work, he's been grinding hard, and he's showing up. >> You also have Julian once already. He didn't get a real chance to get that go with him last year as a remaining defensive secondary defensive back field. How exciting is it now to get him back in into a running back >> Yeah, absolutely, bro. You don't know how many handshakes we came up with, bro. And then we didn't get to use any of them, you know? We didn't So, we got We got a whole armory We got a whole armory of celebrations that we're going to be throwing out this season, but uh he's like my best friend on the team, bro. Smart player, we're dynamic, we can play both sides, and it's kind of like we get on the field and say, "Hey, you want to play on the left side or right side today?" I'm feeling this side. All right, I'll do the other one. So, that communication, um we truly cheer for each other. Like there's zero animosity. Like I love when he makes plays, he loves when I make plays. Um so, excited to be back there with him. >> Julian, I have a question about the handshakes though. >> The defensive set to be >> You have this year, Martin Emerson Jr. >> One more time? >> Martin Emerson Jr. >> What does he add? >> Yeah, he adds he adds he adds physicality, he has length. Um the biggest thing right now is him getting caught up on the playbook, but you can see his confidence level from right now from where he got where he started with us in the middle of OTAs. He's taking a big leap and he's made some plays today. I love the way that he gets out of his breaks especially as a big tall cornerback. It's impressive the way that he transitions and I'm excited for him to come out and help us out too. So we have we have the secondary in my opinion should be a major strength of the 2026 Saints, right? We should have we have depth, we have a lot of players that can play and we need to find a way to get everybody on the field. >> So on the handshakes, you and Julian have a list of handshakes. Is that am I understanding it correctly? >> Yeah, we got a whole armory. Yeah, we got a whole arsenal. >> on like yeah, like >> No, we'll just we'll we'll say it we'll say it before the play like like hey hey this series if we do something we're going to do this one, all right? It's just like yeah, it's just the back of the head thing. >> not tied to this is the interception celebration. This is the PBU celebration. >> It's it's it's you know and it's going to be it's not it's not it's not strict, >> [laughter] >> you know? So if in the moment in the moment we might be running up to each other we might just say, oh the basketball one, you know? Like we might just say it to each other before we do it and then we'll just do it. >> Okay. >> What could you could you put a number to it? >> Uh how many we have? >> Yes. >> We have five right now. >> And it's just you and him trying to build more? >> Yeah, just me. Just me and him. Mhm. >> Is that do you have a handshake with like each of the DBs too? >> Yeah, I got I got at least one with each of the guys. I'm still working on the ones with the the rookies. But all the year two and above players got at least one. >> How big is that playbook? >> Oh, handshake? It's like you know, it's not like it's it's it's muscle memory, honestly. You don't even have to think about it. >> What was the When you made that transition from safety to to playing the slot, like what's the biggest transition in that? >> Well, this is how the closer you get to the ball the more you have to feel. There's less reading, there's more feeling, right? So, the farther back you can read more cuz you have time. The closer you get to the ball, you have to react more. So, the closer you get to the line of scrimmage, you have to see the puller and just go, and you got to just trust it, right? Cuz if not, you're going to get sealed, you're going to get um caught, right? And if you want to make a play, you got to have that that quick trigger and just kind of go and let it happen, and trust that, "Hey, if I fill my gap, I fill my gap, but it's it's better to go fast and make a decision now, so that the person behind you can play off of you than it is to hesitate and be caught between two gaps, and now the person behind you is also confused on what you're doing, right? So, the closer you are to the the line of scrimmage, you need to go faster. The farther you are back, you can take your time more. You can read the gaps, read that, "Okay, cancel, cancel, cancel, cancel. This one's the open one. I'm going to go fit here." Right? So, yeah. >> Is Is there a physical component to it, too, or is it like >> Oh, yeah. If you're If you If you If you don't have dog in you, like, nickel's going to be a hard sport. Like, you see some some nickels or coverage guys, and you know, if I'm offensive coordinator, and I see a coverage nickel on the field, I'm going to run the ball at him. You know, why would I throw at him, you know? If you're forced to on third down, that's one thing, but first and second down, no, I'm going to run at you, you know? And I feel like offensive coordinators are going to test and see who to find out who the soft tackling DB is, and spend their whole game plan running at them. And that's why I emphasize so much with the DBs. I've never been a part of a secondary where we had a guy on the field who was afraid to tackle, cuz it doesn't work. As soon If your corners and your star tackles, then offenses don't have a run game. When they don't have a run game, they don't have a play action game. You know, it all feeds into each other, right? So, it's a big deal to have a a willing tackler on the field in that position, and Sankey, you know, comes from being a safety, so tackling's not going to be a problem for him. >> Because the way that you guys do play, or you play a lot of zone, you are kind of farther back, but seems like you have established that physicality. How are you guys able to do that when you're maybe starting from a a further back point or or whatever, that physicality still applies? >> Yeah, you know, it's it's it's really it's really it's really willpower. It's it's a willingness thing than anything else. Like you got to be willing to put your face in it. That's just kind of how this game goes, you know? If you don't If you don't have it inside of you, you don't have it inside of you. And if you do, you do. >> It goes to last year, too. >> Every year we see teams kind of go from worst to first in the league. Um Patriots last year went all the way to the Super Bowl. Why do you think this team could be one of those teams makes that kind of turnaround? >> Because we have the right pieces. I mean, the foundation is set. We went, I don't know, five or six or whatever on the last at that one point in the season at the end of the year. Um we have a young quarterback who is playing lights out right now. And you know, the biggest thing for him is to do exactly what he was doing before, you know? Just continue to build, don't get comfortable. And he he knows all this, and he's been preaching and he's been breaking down the huddle. So, he's stepped into that leadership role. He's ready for the moment, you know? So, that's a big deal. Number one, you have to have a guy who can play quarterback. And I feel like we got that box checked. Then you got to pack your defense. Defense feels like, you know, the way we stopped the run, top three in the league in the second half of the season. We got to bring defense, pack defense with you. And then you need some playmakers on offense. And we drafted five wide receivers this year. So, we Kellen's been adding some fire some firepower to that offense. And you know, once you put those things together, you usually get a good deal. >> have the team bought even the vets like you bought into Tyler showing so quickly, it seems like? >> Cuz he's just he you you know what it looks like. You know, as a veteran player, you can see similar attributes on guys that you played with, and you know what intangibles translate well and which ones, you know what I mean? It's like, okay, yeah, it's time to develop that. But certain things like the flight of his ball. It's a piercing ball, but it's also very soft, which is very wide receiver friendly in that like it's it's easily catchable for wide receiver. Some guys in the league throw the ball too hard. They throw bullets. And then they make it the wide receiver's fault if they drop the ball. This is the NFL. You should catch it both ways. But if you can assist your guy in, you know, catching the football, that's just more points on the floor. That's more yardage. That's more points on the on the board, that's more yardage, it's all those things, right? So, his ball flight and his decision-making, and decision-making comes with more experience, and he's gotten better with that, too. But, his ball flight and his intangibles, he's more athletic than people give him credit for, his ability to scramble out of the prot- out of the pocket and be creative, it's those things that help you win. >> You can talk about where he was last year at this time. >> Yeah, huge. I mean, the biggest jump that you can see right now is his leadership. His command of the huddle, his command of the offense, his confidence to stand up in front of the whole team and break down the huddle, right? That's been a major jump, and that's what you need out of your your general on the field. >> What's the biggest difference defending him this year compared to last year the first time we played him? >> Um Well, this it's the same objective. We're going to try and make it harder on him. We're going to try and make it as hard as we possibly can. We're going to throw every look at him because the more things we throw at him, the more he'll get used to seeing it. Um but, it's worked for us, too, you know? We can um we're just going to continue to to sharpen each other up that way. >> Have you been on a team that's gone from worst to first? Have you seen it? No. I haven't. Yeah, Texans won the division, won the division, then we like, you know, two bad years, then the Chiefs run, yeah, with three Super Bowls, and yeah. So, yeah, this'll be the first time. But, it does give me perspective, though. And that was the cool part about last year, there was a couple points like I remember one of the Saturday Saturday walk-throughs about the midway point in the season that like I stepped in front of the the team and I was like, this just doesn't look right, you know? It doesn't feel right, it doesn't feel like a championship walk-through. Like, guys aren't in their stances consistently, like it just it just feels a little bit loose, and I'm all about loose as long as the details are tight, right? But, it felt loose and chaotic, right? It didn't feel it had the right feeling, and you know, I asked Kellen for permission to say something in front of the team, and he allowed me to do that. And then it started cleaning up, and I think that that also is just it's just the mental things that help you translate into cuz the margin between winning and losing in NFL is very small. It's not big at all, right? And it's the details that matter more than anything. You can steal reps in your walk-throughs. Like, at this point in my career, I believe in walk-throughs more than anything. Early on training camp, you got young players, you got to see what they got. You got to see if they can physically hold up and everything. Once you're a guy, you know that you're physically you physically match what it takes to be in the league, right? It's the mental side of it. How fast can you think? How fast can you act on those thoughts, right? Because if you are able to see something, diagnose it, and make a move, you're going to make the play. And if you hesitate, they're going to make the play, right? And I think that you win those reps in walk-throughs more than you win them in full-speed drills because it allows you to actually see what a guy is thinking. You can evaluate. I know that his eyes are in the right spot because he didn't waste any steps with his movements, right? Kind of hard to see that full speed. >> Do you remember when that uh >> I can't name the exact week, but it was about the midway point. Yeah. >> You had said Kellen has stepped up his leadership, and you know the only one who has said that to them aside from just breaking down the huddle, what other ways is he stepping up as a leader? >> Yeah, I mean, he brought all the wide receivers out to San Diego. You know, that's a veteran thing to do. He brought the entire wide receiver staff out there to continue to get work in the off season, to continue sharpening each other up. That's not something that every cat does, you know? You have some quarterbacks who just go home or work only with themselves or whatever whatever. But he's been bringing guys along with them, and he's stepped into the role well. And then the way he embraces the city is is just awesome. You know, like, people in New Orleans know how much like what it means to have you know, your stars embrace the city, and he's done a great job of that. Uh so, I think he he's the right man for the job. >> You talked about the maximizing of of walk-throughs uh just now, and you had to praise the Kellen McKenzie earlier. Is that like the kind of like minutia, finer detail thing you're seeing him >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean, across the board like Cooley Cooley's mentality this year is serious. Like every rep he has been serious, locked in, right stance, right eyes in the right spot, communication. It's been at a really fun level and it's fun to play with him. >> Eye discipline for the DBs obviously is such a such a huge thing. Is that like an experience thing or are there things that you can work on to try to progress that a little bit? >> It's a little bit of both. It's a little bit of both. It's not It's not exclusive to guys who played multiple years in the league. It's just It's just something that you have to continue to be on top of because it's easy to have good eye discipline and throughout the, you know, the waxing and waning of the season to just very slowly lose it. You know, it's very easy for that to happen and then, you know, just having the ability to refocus in and do that. And I know Grady does a really good job with that, too, being on the cornerbacks specifically about their eye discipline because this defense relies heavily on the corners to play well. This defense does cuz the corners are in a lot of one-on-one situations and they have to win. >> How would you describe the identity of your y'all's group, the defense? >> Electric, together, we have a ton of fun, and like really I'd say controlled chaos. Controlled chaos is the best way to put it because you want guys that are fast, loose, physical. We want to make a statement physically against everyone we play against. And, you know, you're going to remember that you played the 2026 Saints, you know what I mean? You're going to leave a couple marks here and there. But, it's fun to see the mental side of it take the jump that it has in OTAs and this first day out on the field. There's still a ton of work to do, of course. But, it's fun to see that mental leap that the defense as a whole has continued to um continued to raise with. >> As a Louisiana native, what was it like your first year in the Superdome? And what are you looking forward to in your second year with hopefully, you know, a better team and moving forward? >> Yeah, you know, like you know, my first memory of the Superdome was It was like that too that early that sorry that late 2000s era when it was just it feels like a parade in the Superdome. You have the umbrellas, you have the people in the costumes, you have people throwing popcorn, confetti, whatever, you know, you got the the old music and the you know what I mean? Like all of that stuff man and you know, you you still felt that last year but it didn't remind me of my childhood, you know what I mean? I wanted to look like what it looked like for me when I was a kid, you know what I mean? So that kids today can have that memory, you know what I mean? And then they want to keep pushing it forward, right? So it's a lot of that and I know that winning helps a lot of that, you know, you want the city to be proud of you and that's what we're looking to do. >> And when you mentioned the catchable ball that Chuck throws, I promise this is not a smartass question but how how does the safety know that his own quarterback throws a catchable ball? >> You can see it by flight. I mean when you have conversations with um you have conversations with wide receivers and the wide receivers usually, you know, they're grumbling about it, you know, some wide receivers grumble about how hard the quarterback throws the ball or whatever but usually if you have a conversation with wide receivers they'll tell you but two if you're watching it, right? So there's like there's like different you have like a ball that's a laser that just looks like a blur right? That's probably thrown a little bit too hard. Then you have a ball that is soft but it's just too high and it just looks like it hangs up in the air for six, seven seconds, right? That's a DB's dream. Those are interceptions. Right? And then you have the one that's right in the middle that, you know, it it isn't floating. It's still piercing. It's a tight spiral so it's still piercing. It doesn't hover in the air but it it just comes down gently to where it just makes it feel like the wide receiver has time to nestle it into a cradle, right? And then feels like you're trying to stop a bullet from hitting you in the face, right? That's kind of like that difference. >> So it wasn't cuz you intercepted him a bunch of times that you knew >> No, no, it is it isn't that. It's mainly the conversation with the wide receivers, but I'm going to try to get my hands on one or two just to make it hard on them. Yeah. >> You're a golfer. It's kind of like a golf shot, right? You use different shots. >> Mhm, shot shapes depending on the moment. Mhm. >> Similar kind of arc of the ball. >> Put the clubs and the camera up for the time being and just kind of put that on hold. >> Yeah, yeah, you know, I played I played Oakmont on Thursday and that was my last hurrah trip. So, they're going to get put up for now and we're going to focus on football and make sure we get this thing right. >> Side quest on pause. >> Huh? >> Side quest on pause, yeah. Yeah, yeah. But, off days are off days, though. >> Off days are off days, but you know, the rest of it. Yeah.

title: Saints DE Cam Jordan on Year 16, loyalty to Saints, team's mentality, coaching staff, Brees and more
text: Is it important for you to be gainfully employed by this team 16 >> Would you be 16 years? I never had to leave. Um on on the chance that I I was going to leave, it didn't happen. So, there's no need to talk about it. Uh at this point, I'm I'm black and gold through and through and I'm able to say, you know, for my entire career I played for one team. Unless they decide to trade me this year, that'll be weird. Cuz then I wouldn't go. I'd have to walk off and never look back. But other than that, um just knowing that you know, I'm uh I'm valued in this team. Uh I can bring value to this team. And I think this team has uh has their eyes on the prize. I talked to these guys um in off season like I was still a part of the team. Still in the still in all the group chats. I had to leave one of them. I left my D-line chat for a couple days and I signed back. I was like, "Well, never mind. Add me back in." >> [laughter] >> But um when I think about what this team can do, we're on the cusp of realizing our potential last year. And that's all you can hope for is is knowing that you have major potential that you have to achieve. >> Is that something you ever talked to Steve about, your dad? >> Uh Steve uh my dad Yeah, of course. You know, he I think after 13 years with the Vikings, he had a he like went to go visit the Chiefs or something along the lines of that and it didn't work out and he was like, "Yo, I'm cool with retiring." Um loyalty runs deep, clearly, as you see with Pops playing like in all 13, six Pro Bowls with the Vikings being in the Ring of Honor. Uh there's a standard for Jordan men. So, I'm telling my son to go play basketball. >> For one team. >> See, thanks. 17 teams. You know what I'm saying? Like we're going to switch up the mold. >> I I again, maybe one I'm not a question, but like every year you come in here talking about winning the Super Bowl. >> Every year? >> I think great. Does that like where did that come from? Was it like the way you were raised? >> You want me to walk in and be like, "Nah, I think we're going to be real mediocre." >> But you don't have to but some people, you know >> I'm I'm going to scream black and gold to a Super Bowl every year, every chance I get. And it's going to take everything in me to to prove me wrong. You know, we went what? Seven games without a win last season. I was still like, "We're going to turn this around." I mean, this we could still go 10 and 7. Uh And we finished up, what? Six and seven and 10? Six and six and 11? >> Six and 11. >> Whatever. Um you know, there was a chance where still in our division, we had a chance to shoot at at our division title. And that would have put us in playoffs. You figure eight wins, what is that out there? I don't care what it is, as long as we win our division, as long as we put ourselves in position to be in the playoffs, we have a chance to Super Bowl. Um this year, you look at our division, I'm I you can name off whoever you want to name off. I look at my team and I see Jordan Tyson, I see Chris Olave, you know, I see De'Von Achane. Um I see that we added a guard in the offseason. I said we you know, we drafted well this draft. Um I'm excited. I see, you know, hopefully uh a major a major difference maker in Tyler Shelke, his confidence, um the way he he processes. Uh you get excited about our offense. You know, you talk about AK, you talk about Travis changed his last name twice. Uh >> Achane. >> Achane now. Um you know, you you talk about a healthy Kendre Miller. Man, there's on paper, we look good. Now, I need on paper to look good on on field when we put the pads on. >> AK, when you driving to the facility this morning, are you reflecting a little bit like >> Hell no. Don't I reflect on nothing. I'm trying to hit somebody in face. Um >> Hey hey look, part of my job is being the best version of me. Part of being a defensive lineman, part of being a football player, NFL player is knowing that any one of your plays could be your last play. You could be on top of the world today, one injury takes you out of it and you will you you know, you will all automatically think about what you could have done, should have done. I leave I leave that drive over to listen to music, talk to talk to a part of the family that's up. And my mom is always up. I'm not sure if she sleeps. Um but you know, it's it's the drive over like, "Hey, just just saying I love y'all. You know, we going to hold it down." And by the time I hit this stadium, I'm thinking hot tub, let's get ready to warm this body up and go get it. >> Uh we just heard like AK talking about like it took a while to like understand kind of like the the why and the vision for Kellen Moore's offense. Is that Is that true on defense with Brandon Staley, just like understanding like exactly how it's supposed to work and and how does it feel going into year two having been in that system? >> Man, I'm a soldier. I'm I'm not worried about the grand scheme of things. I'm Take me any battlefield, throw me in there. If I got to fight in the trenches, we fight in trenches. If I got to fight on on the outside, we fight on the outside. I don't think about the wise. I think about how can I get there and how can I be most effective. >> How different is the outside? >> If I'm on the inside, I'm fighting for my life. >> But all right, so rephrasing that, like year two in a scheme. >> Mhm. >> Like everybody's more comfortable. Doesn't matter it's just like the >> Yeah, familiarity familiarity is definitely helpful. But you I mean we already had a top 10 defense from last year, right? So now we're projecting to to be better. And it all turns you always want to be better than you were the year before. Year one, definitely had some things we had to work out, you know, kinks kinks to to our our trade. And year two you you expect it to be smoother. You got the same edges. Added in Tyree Wilson, added in Anthony Jennings. Man, I mean our our depth at the edge room is strong. >> What's been your Look, not even going off of one practice today, but just like in the time you've been able to spend around Tyree Wilson, what's kind of your your impression of him if you have one? >> Yeah, I mean I think there's there's a lot of potential there. You look at his stats and you know you're going to be like oh that's very lackluster. You you watch him on film and there's there's plays that he pops out and you you look at it like uh just like you probably did Chase Young three four years ago. You say he's got some potential.
