We got to be able to capitalize on it. >> And have you noticed a big difference in Kellen Moore and with the girls from year one year two as far as just being a coach? >> I mean Kellen I think is if anything you could you could tell he's been consistent. I I think there's a there's a mission plan and again winning helps you mold that mission. That that streak at the end of last year allows you to say hey you know this is the tough together to together joy that we're looking for and we now know the feeling of what winning is. We have to be able to capture that and rip replicate that same feeling that same outcome each one of these 17 games. >> You were saying something about yesterday about how he's been told in the past like year three game three losses away from a U game or whatever. Last year everybody kind of held together despite the rough start. Just from the player perspective, why was that different for you all last year? >> Man, um yeah, you seen you see teams fold and give up uh and there was no give up. And you love to see that as a mentality from the team because you know when things are getting good, we can really become a avalanche and really really break down some of the you know some of those close games. All it needs is a little bit of confidence and I feel like I say it every year you know those those close games where you're right on the cusp like, man, I wish we would have won cuz that would have boosted our confidence up, our morale up, our ability to overcome that much more. Um new year new team same mindset. Should I take black and gold to Zubal? >> Cam, we uh we not talking to you again until Drew goes into the Hall of Fame. >> Is that right? >> Yeah, just kind of your thoughts on you know how that's going to be for him. I mean, I know you may be there one day too, but just kind of a guy you spent a lot of time with here of being immortalized. >> Yeah, I mean, we talk about Drew Brees, Drew Orleans, baby. everything to the city, right? Bought his first and only Super Bowl currently to to the to the city. Um most 5,000-yard season from a quarterback and when he left with most touchdowns, most passing yards, most all the all the records. Everything that you think a quarterback should be, he was um without the electric, you know, monikers of, oh, he can make all the throws and he's got this an amazing arm. No, he was as efficient as they come. He was the best version of himself and he gave everything he had to the game. And as a teammate, you couldn't be more proud and as uh as a friend, you like, man, like that's that's such a standard. >> Were you a fan of the movie Demolition Man? >> Hell yeah, ain't everybody a fan of That was prime era Wesley Snipes. >> Wesley Snipes, yeah. >> You know, yeah, I told my wife Demolition Man, she told me uh she told me I was a Golden Lord off of Meteor Man and I was just like I I like, see, you were looking at kid movies and I was looking at action the whole time." Like, and I get it, she's a basketball player, and I'm a football player, so we always And she hooped at Rutgers. Sorry. Yeah, she hooped at Rutgers and got beat by Cal every time she played us, but it's fine. Go Bears. Absolutely not. My kids My kids said I looked weird. So, uh They They've become immune uh to any of my cuts. Uh my son was like, "I want to I want to dye my hair." So, I got I got the glares from wifey. Um and I was like, "Let him dye his hair. Come on. Nobody say anything to La Mirada Mall, you know what I'm saying? Like, it's I was like, "We're trying to go soccer. We're very European right now. He's Dominican." And I'm not black. Dominican. >> Uh >> How important is it for this team to have Al back? >> Man, that's a that that's really the heartbeat of the locker room. Um when you when you talk about ears to the locker room, everybody everybody funnel through, uh it AK AK's a icon. I couldn't I couldn't imagine locker room without him. I know one day there will be, but I ain't got to worry about it right now.

title: Darren Mougey Press Conference (7/29) | Training Camp
text: start. It's always a fun time of year. Um, be back in the building the past few days around the players, coaches, and then to get on the field today, it felt good, you know, always exciting time. Love watching the team kind of take shape through these next four or five weeks, watching the guys compete as we go into the season. So, with that, I'll take any questions. >> What you were enjoying Aaron talked about wanting to take over the defense and be more hands-on this year. And he seems pretty stoked about doing that. We spoke to him a little bit about it. How much will you enjoy watching that unfold and have you noticed any things, you know, already that >> Oh, yeah, I've noticed it. And and you're right, it's been fun to watch. It's it's been, you know, just even through the offseason, you know, I I felt like we had a good OTAs and continued to build on that, but to see him engage with the players in the meetings, on the field, I think you see it today, you you see that energy and enthusiasm with the defensive play calling, him having his hands on it and be kind of in the nitty-gritty of it all. >> How do you define a successful season for the Jets? >> Yeah, you know, I think we're always we want to win, right? And I want to see these guys compete and get better every single day. That's starting today throughout training camp and throughout the season. Um, but yeah. >> And we were we were talking to Garrett Wilson a little while ago and he kind of brought up a good point about some of the new talent that you guys brought in on both sides of the ball coming from other organizations that have had, you know, winning success like we just spoke about and and how refreshing that is to bring that perspective in to some to the guys that have been here that have only known losing. How important is that to be believe and and how much of a factor is that when you're bringing guys in? >> Yeah, I think I I believe it can help. I believe it can help when you bring these guys in that have been part of that. And it's I'm excited to watch it, you know, I'm excited to watch some of these young guys that just got here, how they kind of take shape and and take mold throughout training camp and watch them grow and watch some of our veteran players that have been here and some of the new veteran players that we brought in, kind of their role evolve and how they lead some of these young guys. So, that's all part of the Uh, the thing that I really enjoy during training camp watching those things evolve and how how it comes together. >> Are you feeling a a different level of intensity or excitement this training camp compared to last year? >> I mean, it's day one. I think every year training camp day one is it is exciting, right? And I thought we had a lot of good things throughout OTA with some of the new pieces we had and then I just look forward to continue to um develop on that. >> Talk about scouting and you know, year one to year two jumps for for players. What what kind of a jump do you want to see from Aaron and Glenn year one to year two? >> Look, year one to year two, just kind of speaking on year one to year two. Um having been here for a full year with AG, with some of these players, with my staff, people in the building, there's just a lot more there's a better comfort level going in to a year two. My relationship with AG has only gotten stronger and better. We have dialogue every day. We're we're just much more in sync. Time time on task with anybody does that for you, right? So, I think we all have high expectations uh for ourselves. That's players, that's coaches, um myself included. >> What were you talking about what it meant to get Hall and Tippmann done early and also are there any other guys you'd like to get done >> Yeah, getting getting Breece and Tippmann was important to us and I'm glad we were able to do that. Um it was a really good process. Uh both parties, you know, and I like where we landed with those guys and having those guys, keeping them around, I know they're going to help this team. >> What about are there any current players you'd like to extend? >> I think we're in a good spot right now, but I'll always keep contract stuff kind of in-house. >> I asked I asked you earlier about this a little earlier about the corporation analytics and just like you kind of talked a little bit about that with your staff and veteran market, draft process and just how much you guys have both invested in analytics and how much you kind of use it on a day-to-day basis with that. >> Ab- absolutely. The analytics and the AI, right? I mean, that's been an organizational buy-in from ownership to on the business side. Obviously, coach and I talking about it and we've invested. I know there was an article in the summer about Ejiro bringing him and he's been tremendous. And you know, specifically in my world in in the scouting and the personnel, there's so much data now, right? There's so much data. Whether it's college, whether it's pro, and but how we're deciphering the data, how we're breaking it down, how we're digesting it, how it's getting presented to me is huge, right? And I feel like we have some of the best with Ejiro and Sean and our analytic staff that's breaking down all the data, feeding it to me, feeding it to the coaching staff. Here's what's important, here's what we're doing, but also challenging us on some things and us challenging them and it's a different lens, but it's been very helpful. It's important. On the AI front, I think to this point what it's helped with the most is the automation of things, right? We we we're saving a lot of man-hours being able to automate information and systems and spit it out quickly. So, it's been huge and I and I look forward to the continued growth of the the organization with the AI and the analytics. >> Have you talked to the AI yourself? Have you been >> Yeah. Yeah, yeah, absolutely. Like we we've integrated into our systems. Again, for a lot of data breakdowns, we can just do things a lot quicker and it's allowed for more efficiency, the auto the automation and I toy around with, you know, the chat GPTs and the different thing. We have in-house ones that we can do for different questions, but really it's it's it's all the integrated information, the in-house information and the data points. That's been cool. >> Now, Cam Newton cutting the headlines last month with the stuff with the police down in Florida. Were you disappointed that that your quarterback was in that situation? >> I'm excited about what's moving forward. I'm glad that's behind us. It is behind us and I'm excited for the continued growth through the off-season and training camp. >> How has Adonai Mitchell kind of lived up to your expectations and what do you hope to see as he works in tandem with Eric Wilson? >> I'm excited to see Adonai's continued growth. He had a good a good off-season, good OTAs and expect to see that continued growth through the training camp, and I'm excited to watch him and the entire wideout group kind of come together and see how that looks. >> What are your expectations with Davon Sweat? And where is his conditioning at, his weight, and how do you view that issue? Because it's obviously something he's dealt with in the past. >> All all of those things, I mean, the conditioning, the weight was it was all in very good place. Unfortunately, he had a little hamstring injury while he was training, so he'll start on NFI, but we'll work him back, and and he's going to help this team. >> Do you like the blending of the roster right now? Obviously, you have a very young roster, but you've already added a number of veterans and free agents in the line. >> I do. I I like where the roster's at, and I think you hit it. We've got a good blend of young guys, and and what we believe is the right, you know, mix of vet and and the the right veterans to help, you know, kind of mold some of these young guys and and change the culture, and I'm excited to see how the roster kind of take shape in training camp. This is an integral part of the building that roster. >> How do you feel about the the backup quarterbacks, specifically Kade and and what how he's looked as a rookie coming in? >> Yeah, I'm excited to see Kade. Like I said, like throughout training camp, compete, and the whole room, you know, Bailey and and Brady and Gino, and watch those guys work and compete, and see the growth throughout training camp. >> Last summer, you were you were pretty active. Obviously, Phillips, Briggs, you guys you talked a little bit last summer, but that process, you guys being active you force yourself being active in that kind of veteran market between Cox and kind of some of those younger guys that might get kind of squeezed on the roster. Like that process, for you guys, what's that look like? >> Yeah, it it starts right now, and we'll always keep a close eye on the market and the landscape. Whether it's street or on other teams, every position um I mean, we're meeting daily and having discussions about other other rosters and what's on the street and what what can fit on the team, but it's a fun time of year, and especially as you get those preseason games under the belt, and you kind of start forecasting what teams might do certain moves and having those conversations with teams as we get into those preseason game two and three and if there's any opportunities that, you know, you might have a match with the team to make some moves. So, it's an exciting team. It's exciting time of year and it's fun. >> of speculation about whether the Jets are going to bring in a veteran backup quarterback at some point. Is that feasible and how hard would it be to get a guy up to speed in training camp? >> Yeah, I won't get into the the hypotheticals. I'm just excited to see Cade get his reps during training camp and watch the whole group, you know, Bailey and Brady and Gino get their reps and, you know, develop and continue to improve while they're here. And we'll keep a eye on the landscape as we just mentioned the entire every position across the league on the street. That that's no different for every position. >> What keeps you up at night right now? >> Um, not much. I'm sleeping good. It's the start. It's day one, you know? It's good.

title: Garrett Wilson Press Conference (7/29) | Jets Training Camp
text: How y'all doing? Good to see y'all man, good to see y'all. Good to be back. Nice shirt. >> Thank you. Uh Eric Glenn said you're chomping at the bit. Is it because of the offense and everything like that? How How are you feeling and how eager are you for this season to start after last year? >> I mean honestly it's been it's been brewing since since week eight of last season. I ended up, you know, missing missing the rest of that season. It's really the first time I missed um significant time in my life, you know, so so all of a sudden it makes you look at things differently. You Not that I ever took this game for granted, but but when you miss time like that is you just can't wait to get back and have another shot at it and and um that's how I'm feeling right now, you know, we got another opportunity, a special opportunity to to, you know, turn this thing around and and um I'm excited as I've ever been to to do it this season, man. >> Garrett, what we were just talking about this yesterday, but what was it like walking in the building as a year five like veteran on on this team? >> Yeah, I mean like whenever you think about it it's crazy, man. I I try um I mean there's some things that just come with it with the time, I guess, with the age. Certain young guys come in they look at you maybe for for how to do a certain lift or something like that that just came came without me noticing, right? But you know, that's the reality of it. It is my my fifth year and I you know, I can't believe it, but uh like I just like I just said, man, it it's going to I have a feeling just it's going to be a special year. You get it's the fifth year. I'm excited to get another opportunity to to do what I've always dreamed of and and um you know, just play some meaningful football and and to the winner and and uh we got a special opportunity this year, man. I'm excited for my fifth year. It's It's It's crazy. >> I know it's early, Garrett, but is there anything tangibly different or a feel or a vibe, you know, in the early days of training camp here as compared to last year just around the locker room, around the guys? >> Yeah, um I mean besides you know, the the the stuff they're building and all the the way we got to walk in stuff like that. That's obvious. I I would just say, you know, with guys like Double D and Minkah in the building, and then uh and then Gino on the offensive side, and Tim Patrick, like the these certain guys that that just I don't know, they have no they don't have any any uh past association with the with the last, you know, maybe blunders we've had. And because of that, they're bringing this this winning mindset, winning energy um that that us as the younger guys and and, you know, looking up to guys like that, we trying to just latch on to it and get a better idea of what it takes to to win at that level cuz they've done before done it before. And um I would say that's the main thing. I mean, the energy out there at practice today for a first day, I thought was was was was really good. You know, obviously got to clean up a lot of things, but but the energy and the mindset, the uh the intention was good. So, you know, all things we we all feel good about and and, you know, we'll see how this thing keeps going as we as we uh go along. >> Coach you feel like it's going to be a special year? Like, have you felt this before? I know there was hype a couple years ago, but have you felt this before coming into a season? >> Um I mean, it it feels different this year. It does, man. You know, I don't want to talk about it too much. It just it just does. That's I'll say that. Uh not that any other year I didn't have the same No, it's more just this group that we have, man. We we spent a lot of time together. We've put in throughout these OTAs. Um and just knowing what what AG, Moog, Coach Reich, all their mindset align with ours and just making just the certain conversations that we've had in the team room, whatever it may be. Um They've set They've set the table, right? And and us as players, it's our job to go out now and and then get better every day at this point in the season, and then once the the real season comes around, let's let's be ready to play on Sunday. >> Yeah, Coach AG talked a lot about things that he wanted to change after his first year. Like, everybody, you know, everybody starts out wants to What are some of the things that that you've noticed, whether it's been the offseason OTAs, or even, you know, very early >> Yeah. I I would say just the communication line and and the way uh AG wanted to build, and maybe his I don't know, his his guys on the team that he wants to talk to and get that feedback from and then bounce his thoughts off, you know, we got a we got a feedback group or a leadership group that's been going on through OTAs and and that is just fluid. It's uh It's like we're all aligned and I kind of said that before, but that's one of the main differences I've noticed and maybe it was his first year so he's trying to feel things out, figure out figure out who the guys are that he wants part of a unit like that, but this year we're doing that and we got some guys in there that that just really get this thing like I've said and and they're going to help us, you know, get over that hump. >> How many person in that group that you lost to? >> Uh I mean I'm good. I can I can say the group. I mean the guys you would probably figure. >> [laughter] >> You know what I'm saying? Uh we did just not as We did. >> guys? >> Yeah, exactly. It's just a different the guys in the room, man. Like like I said before, they these guys that come from different spots and and have no association with that with these past few years have a different different way of seeing things, right? And and it's it's been really valuable for a guy like me and Breece and and you know, to to to hear their thoughts and then how they go about practice or or lunch or the locker room and stuff like that, you know, you don't you don't realize it, but that stuff makes a difference, you know, 100%. >> When we spoke to Breece yesterday, he was talking about competing with you and being the best player on offense, too. Do y'all have those conversations and what are the what are those like? >> Nah, he like to talk to that talk to y'all about that. I mean, yeah, man. Uh that's Breece Breece the one, you know, and when you got a bell cow like that that can that can take on the the load that we're going to ask of him and he's and he's proven he can do it throughout these past years and I'm I'm sure he's going to take a step up, you know, he got more to give and I know he's excited about that. Um I am, too, you know, since day one, the first day I saw Breece, I was he special, man. So, the conversations we have I wouldn't say it's straight like that, but along the lines and and and just make sure we're holding our end, you know, everyone's got a job on this team. It's important that we play our role to you know, the top of the line if we want to have a chance to doing what we want to do. So, everyone's got a role. You got to know it. You got to go execute it. So, um yeah, that's how I feel about it. >> And you feel like what do you feel like is the next step for you? >> Uh just playing meaningful football. I got to I got to uh similar to what I said last. Like I got to hold my end with this team. Whatever they expect out of me, I got to do that. If they expect a little more, I got to do that. And um and and and you know, play my role because I believe we got the the places or the pieces in place and and um that'll that'll get us to playing that meaningful football in December which, you know, I've dreamed of of doing for a long time, right? You know, so playing on that high level when when it means a lot. Um so, I'm I'm excited to get back to that. >> Yeah, a couple more. >> You um last time we talked to you, you talked a lot about Frank and the way his offense like playing with power and something you've always wanted. Like it that just seems like such a good fit for like the way you operate. Like it when you're out there, it's just like, man, I've been missing this my my whole career. Like just the ability to work with the coach in the way you do. >> Yeah, man. It's I wouldn't say my whole career. You know, I've had a lot of um I've had some coaches where you know, you can tap into that and it's kind of just getting to know how every coach wants you to go about it, right? And and when you have a coach, it's your job to to you know, do what they're asking of you. So, so that's where you find yourself, right? Um you know, this year I happen to find find myself in offense where he's asking to you know, asking me to do things that if I asked myself to do something, it would be about what would I what I'm doing, right? And that's there's a comfortability there. There's a uh not to mention I love doing it, right? You know, it's fun. And you know, I love playing ball and and when you get to go out and be on the outside and run routes, you versus the corner, you know, that's that's what I I fell in love with this game for, you know, the competitive game within the game, you know? So, um I'm just excited and and like I said, it's it's our job now to go make sure that we go execute what Frank is asking of us cuz cuz you know, what he's asking of us is right, you know, so let's let's go play to the best of our ability and show the world, you know. >> Last one here? >> N N came over >> Say that one more time. >> N N Mitchell came over at mid season last year. How valuable is this off season for him? And then also how can he be an asset to you? AD's a one of those guys, man. He he's he's it's just a a ticking time bomb with him, you know. He's he's put in the work um last year to come in halfway through the season and pick up the offense and and have some some success, make some plays down the field like he did was, you know, that's no easy task. And I thought he handled it really well and and made some plays that, you know, you you I don't know. Like he's he's capable but based on when he got there you might not ask of somebody. Um and then, you know, with this off season and the OTAs he had, man, that boy can can play, bro. And uh it's been fun to watch for me and just just be his teammate and and come back to the huddle after he's playing that play. Y'all I'll miss this. It feel like you know, it's just fun, bro. Watching him and then, you know, then it's my turn and then it's then it's then it's Omar it's fun, man. And that's that's what this thing's all about. And for AD I think um now it just comes down to we got to go put in a good rest of this training camp and then whenever Sunday comes, when our number's called, let's let's do what we've been doing, you know, let's make plays, let's let's make plays on the outside, let's do it when when the world is watching.

title: Aaron Glenn Training Camp Press Conference (7/29) | New York Jets
text: [clears throat] >> It's good to see everybody. Um obviously uh coming back for the training camp is always exciting. Um coach is excited, players excited, uh organization excited. Um and what we want to do, we just want to build off the momentum that we actually had in OTAs uh going into training camp. So, um no slogans, no hype speeches. Uh want to set the tone with the players yesterday and man, we're ready to improve. And that's that's that's what we're trying to do. So, when we can come to the injuries, uh Mazie, he had a hamstring today. I'll check on that, you know, this afternoon and see where that's going. Um Ponds strained a calf. Uh don't think too much into that. I think he'll be just fine. Um PUP Osai, he'll be fine. I think he'll be back very soon. And uh T Sweat in the fire, all right, he'll be fine, too. He had a hamstring in the off season. But um we're going to make sure we monitor that very well and make sure he's fine. So, that what happens when it comes to the injuries. Um other than that, man, again, exciting times all right, for everybody. And um we're just ready to put the work in. Keep our heads down and just put the work in. Any questions? >> So, how are you feeling heading into your second training camp with everything? >> Um I feel good. I I I really do. there was a number of things this off season that um and I told you guys this doing OTAs that I want to improve on. Um and plus, not just improve, I thought some things that that did last year were good. I think we all need to improve when it comes to the processes that we had, but you start to learn different things going through your second year. And to me, that's the most exciting thing that that um um that I'm thinking of right now. It's just some of the things that that I want to implement with the team. Um some of the messaging I want to continue to implement, and just knowing that man, if we could just keep that consistent, man, improvement comes behind that. So, um I'm looking forward to how guys react um from this day forth going into the training camp. >> Does it Does it feel different for you coming into it your second year doing this? Obviously, you went in last year a little bit blind. I mean, you knew someone. >> I think for any head coach going from year one to year two, um you see things uh I don't want to say totally different, but man, there are some blind spots that you probably didn't expect. And that's with every coach. And every first-time head coach uh has told me that. Um and it allows you to go into this year, man, being able to attack those things the right way. So, uh I look forward to being able to do that. Um And then going to your second year, like the process or your processing is a little bit different because now the relationships that you that you have that you have a lot of dialogue with, especially me and Mooj. Um same with the players, being able to bring other players in that that you know that you know that fits what you're trying to do. Um so, anytime going from year one to year two, man, it feels exciting. >> Could you say some of those blind spots? Just if you know a couple of maybe general things cuz obviously you came in here obviously speak speaking of Bill, you got a lot of you know, coached under Campbell and all that stuff. So, a lot of ideas coming in. >> Yeah, and listen, I don't I don't I'm not trying to be a a butt hole, you know, when when I give you this answer, but a lot of that, man, I really want to keep to myself. I don't think it's fair to myself or the team to be to be able to articulate all those things to everybody and give everybody all the answers to uh which I think is the test, you know, for me to improve. >> Aaron, obviously some things happened with Geno in the off-season, and he came up here yesterday, and he addressed that. He said he'd talk to you guys, too. What were those conversations like? What did you tell him? I mean >> Well, I think he did a really good job of the awareness part of it. Of first understanding that man, we built a lot of momentum in OTAs and coming out of OTAs. And man, the distraction happened. And I know he hated that he was a part of that, but thing about it, it's behind him. It's behind him, and we all moving forward. He talked to me, he talked to some of his teammates. Man, we're with him 100%, and then we're moving forward. >> How do you go about building competitive stamina throughout camp? >> It's a really good question. Um because in in camp I would say the first period, man, it's always competitive. Always. Then as camp goes, or as the day goes, man, guys get tired. And that's when you want to see how guys are competing. And that's when I call them head coach call it periods to where man, I'm going to throw some out there for myself, and I'm going to throw some out there for Frank, so the guys can compete. And you want That's how you build competitive stamina. The guys continue to compete time after time. At At the end of the day, man, how we operating, right? And I want our players to operate that way, and that's how we want to build competitive stamina. >> This This being your second camp, how might the messaging to the players how might it be different than it was last year? And And And in what ways might this camp be different than last >> Well, again, I'm going to keep that to myself um when it comes to the messaging, but I will tell you this, the messaging will be consistent. And I want the focus to be narrow for our players. And I think if we do that, right? It allows for everybody to improve. >> What are the What are the What are the challenges? You get two two new coordinators, obviously, and and most particularly Frank. What do you feel like he brings to you? Yeah. And how critical >> Well, I've been knowing Frank for a long time. Obviously, we know he was my teammate and throughout my coaching career, we've always kept in touch. And I think the beauty of of those relationships are is you get a chance to know exactly how he operates when it comes to his philosophy, when it comes to offense. And then you try to see, man, does it match what I think? All right, and for the most part, man, it's right on point. It is right on point. Um and you see exactly how he did when he was in Indy, as far as running the ball, as far as the explosive plays, uh things like that. So, man, our philosophies really match when it comes to that. Uh defensively, man, we all know that Duke was with me for what, 3 4 years in uh in Detroit. So, he knows his defense like the back of his hand. When I have to step out and do other duties, man, he could easily step in and explain exactly what we're trying to do. So, that's a uh that's a comfort for me. That's a real comfort for me. Um but it's really exciting for me to be able to install a defense that I know like the back of my hand. A lot of what we're doing is things that I actually like want to do as far as coming from New uh New Orleans into Detroit. So, if there's an issue, I can quickly fix it. And that feels exciting to me. So, um knowing Frank, knowing what he brings to the table, knowing what Duke brings to the table, and me being able to call defense and fix issues that we have, um man, I look forward to that. I really do. >> Yeah. Sedeeq was obviously back out there today. How good was it to get him out there? And what what uh what excites you most about getting the chance to use a guy with that kind of skill set? >> Yeah, obviously, he's um man, he's big. He's 250 lbs. And he he we know he runs a 4-3. He has really good hands. Um to be able to utilize him in a number of different ways. And again, um I don't want to sit there and talk about how we're going to use him. Um it's it's really exciting. Man, to match him up with the other tight ends that we have, and I think that room is um it's really improving. I really do. Um it's good to have him out there. Um we're going to take it slow with him to make sure he can catch up on everything he needs to catch up with. Um but he's going to be a huge weapon for us, and I'm looking forward to how we're going to utilize him. >> A lot of things a lot of things have changed. Quarterbacks, coaches, we went through a bunch of them personnel. The objectives and the goals, where where are they right now? >> Say that one more time. >> The objectives and the goals for this team in a year or two, what are they? >> Yeah, I and I'm going to continue to be consistent with with what I just told everybody else. It's not fair to myself, it's not fair to the players to um to really give you my message into the players, what our goals are. You know, but I will say this, everybody's goal is to win. Everybody's goal is to do that. Everybody's goal is to to be competitive. Everybody's goal is to improve. All right, and I will tell you that, but when it comes to the specifics of what I told our guys, I'm going to keep that between me and the players. >> What are your expectations for Garrett as he goes into this season? well, Garrett's feeling good, and he looks good. And me and Garrett had a a number of conversations in the off-season. Um and I will say this, he's chomping at the bit. You know, especially with the type of offense that we have, and especially the way that Frank's going to utilize all those guys. And I know you guys heard Frank talk about this, I know you heard the players talk about this, about how the players are able to use their instincts but be disciplined while they're using it. And I think that fits exactly what Garrett can do well. You know, so I'm looking forward to him doing that. >> In terms of in terms of analytics, this off-season it felt like there was a someone has talked about in AI and incorporate stuff like that. How did you guys feel like through the off-season of player personnel, better market draft, and then into you know, in-game stuff? How do you think you can incorporate the analytics and the AI stuff? >> I'm glad you asked that question, because that was um this off-season for me, doing my studying, and my research, so I have my own like way that I study this game. And to be able to back that up, I go to our analytics the analytics department. And when I give them, I don't give them my answers, but I give them like a problem that I want them to take a look at. And I try to see if that matches up. And for the most part, that helps me with my research. And I make sure I question them on how they how they look at the things and I make sure they question me on how I look at things. And we try to come together for an answer. So, man, that was huge for me this offseason as far as the research on man, what are the predictors of winning this league? Like what is that? How does that look? And being able to have an answer for that and being able to articulate that to our players and let that be a focus. Let that be a focus. So, again, I will keep really the messaging to our to between me and my players, but um then that was huge for me this offseason to be able to do that. >> Thank you. A couple more with regard to I mean, you spoke to us earlier in the year about about calling plays and getting into that. >> Yeah. >> Like it's your superpower. I think you used those words. What are the things that energize you most about about getting back into doing that? >> When there's an issue on defense, I can quickly fix it. Cuz I know the defense like the back of my hand. And that feels really really good. That feels really good. And to be able to coach everybody from D-line, linebackers, DBs, to be able to be really specific and this is what I'm looking for and this is how I want to go. And then the players respond to that and knowing exactly what that is. That feels really good to be able to do that. Um I've said this before, I miss doing that. title: Chris Godwin Jr., Bucky Irving & More on Goals in 2026 | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: How you guys doing? This is much better than than normal. All these shades I got over here. It's pretty sick. >> I guess I'll start it. I mean, you you look good. How do you how do you feel? >> Uh I'm feeling good. Uh I'm I'm encouraged by just like the way my body's felt, by the ability to have like a full off-season of training. Um I'm just you know, I'm just grateful to be out there. I guess it's year 10. I feel like it's flown like so quickly. Um but I don't know. I guess it was a gift, too, cuz it's a beautiful day. First day of camp, probably one of the best weather days I've had in camp here, which is I think the rookies are probably getting like a false sense of security, cuz this is not This isn't like camp in Tampa. >> This offseason has been one with a lot of storylines, whether Mike going to San Francisco, Vita Vea recently asked for a trade, and Baker doesn't get an extension. You know in that locker room, guys they talk, and they know what's going on. How do you How do you team not react or react to that? Concerned at all as a leader that that might seep into the culture of this team? >> Honestly, I don't like I'm not particularly concerned. Like like to like you were just saying, like we we talk in the locker room. Like guys aren't oblivious as to what's going on, and we also like understand like it's a business, right? But like none of us, we never question any of our teammates like ability to go out and to perform, or like their desire to to give their all to the team, right? So like we we let the players handle like handle their respective business. Um and know that they're going to give us their all on the field. So I'm not concerned about it being an issue for anybody on the team. >> Being a part of this team, including a Super Bowl winning team for such a long time, uh did it surprise you when that news broke? >> Uh yeah, it was it surprised me, but mostly just because like I'm not like following everything that's going on. You know what I mean? Like I found out the same way everybody else did, but um like I said, it's a it's a business. So it's like things will take care of themselves. Um it's all but it's good it's good to see Vita out here. Like he always looks great. Like Vita's a great personality like on our team. Um Been a great teammate of mine for years. >> What about with Baker? I mean, you've been part of negotiations with this team, but when you do kind of have that looming and in this case, you know, he didn't get the deal he wanted before camp. >> Mhm. >> As an athlete or even like as you look at him, like how how do you handle >> Yeah. >> kind of getting getting maybe what you desire? >> Yeah, it's Honestly, it's tough. Like as a player, like it's tough because like whether you don't feel like you get what it is that you like are hoping to get or like just like the business aspect of it because so many of us like we got into this game playing like for the love of it, right? And then when the business kind of steps in, sometimes it can be frustrating, but uh over the years that I've gotten to know Bake, I don't know if there's anybody more equipped to to handle something like this, right? Like he's the consummate pro. He's going to go out there, he's going to handle his business. Um and like he's going to be the Baker that we all know and love. >> How long did it take you to kind of understand the business aspect of the sport and compartmentalize? >> I mean, I kind of I feel like I learn like in waves, right? Like you get a quick intro like your rookie year because and let me when I first came in it we were we were still doing like multiple cuts. Like it wasn't just like 90 to 63 or or or whatever. Um and so like after a couple weeks guys would just be gone. And so like that's your first intro to like, "Oh, this is a this is a business. Like if you're not performing, they're going to get rid of you." Um and then when I first started going through my own like like contract things, like after my first year after my first deal was done, then you get an intro to like the actual business side of it. And again, it it can be frustrating, it can be um just like challenging because there's uncertainty and you want like security for yourself and your for your family. Like it's a violent game. We don't you don't know how long you'll last. Um so it it it can mess with you, but it's like if you have good people around you, if you have like good leaders in a locker room, people to talk to, then you can like navigate it and at the end of the day you go out there and you perform. Um you just have fun with your guys and let the business take care of itself. >> Chris, what is it like first camp without Mike? How does your leadership role change now that he's gone? >> I mean it's it's definitely strange. Like I think like the combination of like being in training camp and him not being here and then uh like seeing him in like a different shade of red is a is bizarre. Um but I mean again like it's like it's the business, right? Like I I talked to Mike a couple weeks ago and like he's happy, right? And like that's my guy, so if he's happy like I'm happy. And like as far as my my leadership on this team, I guess it doesn't change at all like as far as I'm concerned. Like what I did and what I brought to the team was completely different than what Mike brought to the team, right? So it's not like he's going and I'm like oh I got to step up and be somebody else or somebody that I'm not. Like I just continue to be me and like to me like that's going to be good enough. As I continue to encourage the younger guys, um continue to try to help elevate my game. And it's like if I can bring my the best version of myself, like that's the best thing that I can do for our team. >> Chris, you mentioned he was at media camp. Just you know you followed David Sills' career since you guys you know played against one another back in back in Delaware. Do those old memories come back up when you're practicing with him? And what has it just been like getting to work with him? >> I would say like early on they they kind of did. Like it was like it was a little weird for me because like again like we were going against each other for for years like um like our team I got I guess our teams are kind of like rivals when we're like sixth through like 10th. You know, but again like you're small like you're like little pipsqueaks. Um but so like being on the on the same team with him is cool and getting to see his perspective too cuz he was a quarterback, so how he kind of looks at the game is a little bit different than a lot of receivers and him playing in this offense last year in Atlanta, like I got to pick his brain a little bit on some of the things early on. Um but he's been a great addition to our team, great addition to our room and came in and he just fit right in. >> Chris, another addition to the room is Trent Sherfield. What are your impressions of him, his progress so far, and potential role within the offense? >> Uh I've been I've been very pleased with Tay, man. He's uh he's come in and just kept his head down, and he's worked. Like he has a a great personality, came in, you know, joking, like he's very like vibrant personality. Um He's got a like he's a he's a very big guy, like a legit like 6'4. Um and he moves really good for a guy that's that size. Like he has a lot of twitch, um and his ball skills are like they're they're really good. Like he tracks the ball well. He made a couple plays in mini camp that was like, "Damn, like that's like that's pretty good like for a rookie, man." Um I see him like having like a like the sky's the limit for him, as far as I'm concerned. It's just like anything else, when you come in, everything's spinning so fast, and you're just trying to like find your footing. Um but there's no doubt in my mind that he has the ability to to have a great career. >> Last two for Chris. >> Chris Mec >> Yeah. I think just like in his comfort level, like he like Mec is an incredible talent, right? But like he is also a great student of the game, and I think when he first got here, that was probably the first thing that really stood out to a lot of us was like how he sees the game like as a like as a receiver, it's almost like a quarterback. Um like his understanding of coverages, like his um understanding of how to use like leverage against DBs. Um but just like from year one to year two, though your your like your comfort level jumps dramatically, right? Like everything's not flying around as fast, like you know what's expected of you, you know how to practice. Um and so he's just continuing to take steps further and further, man. I mean, again, really, really excited about about the future for his career, and obviously a great addition to our room. >> What about so what about J'Marr in his year three? What have you >> And have you warmed up to the idea of him calling you "Unc"? >> I haven't I haven't quite warmed up to it, but he's going to do it anyway. Like it's one thing about J'Marr, he's going to do whatever the hell he wants to do. And like may it's like that's that's like my little brother, like and we we're going to butt heads a bunch, but like uh I love J'Marr, man. We spent a lot of time this offseason training together. Um huge personality, huge energy guy. Uh man, like unbelievable talent. Um he can I think I think he's going to surprise a lot of people, but just because like he wasn't able to show a ton of it last year um just like with his injury. But I think like when you get to see him like being healthy and really like the way he's able to stretch the field, like the way he's able to come out of some of his breaks, I think um I think he's very excited to get to show what he can do. Um and from what I've seen, I think he has a ton of ton of potential. >> All right, that's all for Chris. Thank you guys. >> Thank you guys very much. Have a good one. >> No problem. >> How's the shoulder feeling? You look great out there. >> Shoulder feeling good. I just want to thank the training staff, to everyone that helped me on the road to recovery. Just taking it day by day. I just want to give a big thanks to them for helping me get back to where I want to be. >> What is your offseason been like? >> Man, my offseason been great. Uh once I got the the the word that I was cleared, I pretty much got back to my routine. Went uh spent some time down in South Florida, got uh with the coach that I spent my rookie season with, getting back to work with him. So, everything's been great. I mean, our relationship it's been going great. Kenneth is even better person. You all we all can know what he could do on the field, but just having a leader like that in our room, he he's been around some great backs. So, just being able to sync up that knowledge and like I always say, man, it's always good to have two good backs in the room. Uh we compliment one another and uh see how far this thing go. >> With Zac Robinson as the new offensive coordinator. What's that been like and how much different you think this offense is going to be this year? >> I mean, it's been it's been good ever since Zach got here. I mean, you see what he do in Atlanta. Uh he get his playmakers the ball in the best possible ways to and the things that they are good at. So, we just taking it day by day and letting him lead us in the right direction. >> In 2020, you guys had a lot of success on offense, scoring, running the ball, and all that. Once you had that taste of success, and it didn't happen last year, but how hungry are you guys as a unit to get back to what you were able to do and live up to everyone's potential? >> I mean, every season's going to be different. Uh you can't really live in the past, but just being able to lead on our new offensive coordinator to get us some balls in good spots and and put us in the right places to make plays and and we trust him and we we just uh lead him taking it day by day to to execute his plays that he calling and and when it's time for us to go out there and play, we just got to execute at a high level. >> How similar is he and Robinson? >> I mean, he got his own way of calling his plays. I don't want to pretty much put him in lamb in the same category, but they all got their ways of calling their plays how they want to call them. >> Have you noticed anything different from Baker? I mean, I know he wanted a new deal and said all this "Won't be any more negotiation. I'm all focused on football if I don't get a new deal." >> I mean, no, that's the same guy that come in each and every day the same way. I mean, y'all know what this guy do for this football team. He put his life in his line on the body every Sunday. So, just being able to have a guy like that each and every Sunday that know that he got our back and we going to lead as he go. I mean, we don't won't really talk about it. We got to We got to stay focused on what we got to task. I mean, we all know this thing is a business, but we let them them players take care of what they got to take care of. And and when they back, we going to be excited to have them back. We all know what them players mean to this team. So, whenever they get back and and get they whatever they got going on done, we going to be excited for them. No, I don't think I don't pretty much think I changed my running style. I mean, playing injured it kind of change your like different ways on how you go about situations cuz you pretty much banged up, but we play a physical game. I mean, at some point in life or somewhat playing this game, some adversity is going to happen and you just got to be able to know how to respond to it. I mean, I learned a lot about myself. I I mean, I learned a lot. I mean, what this game mean to me. I've been doing this since I was 4 years old and just being able to for the first time being hurt. Being able to also know you more than just a football player and also just being able to to self-reflect on things that you can learn outside of football, but just being able to the to be around my teammates and and know the joy that they bring when you around them. So, just being able to know it like I said, adversity is going to come at some point, but at the end of the day, it is going to determine how you come out of that and it's going to make you stronger. >> When you talk about knowing that you're more than a football player, does that make, I guess, personal growth even more of a priority in the off seasons when you don't have that that day-to-day, you know, I mean, I know that you you work very hard in the off season, but like does that prioritize like personal growth a little more when you have that down time? >> Uh I mean, when you don't got football, I mean, you got to find yourself active. You got to find things to do. But, yeah, like you said, just being able to self-reflect on yourself and and learn and try to try to come up with new things that you want to do and uh learn outside of football. But, like I said, like we're around this game so much and then when it's taken away from you your your mind is everywhere. But, just being able like I said, I don't take this game for granted each and every time that I step on the field. I'm trying to give them my all all for this team and and for this community. I mean, this what I love to do and when I step on the field, I'm going to give them my all every time. >> Lucky, there was injuries all across the board last season on the roster, especially the offensive line, too. What can having a a healthy unit up front do for this offense this season? >> I mean, you like like I always said, it start with them guys up front. I mean, they set the tone. Uh and when them all and when them all guys is healthy and this offense is healthy, I think we could do some pretty good things. >> So, just to be clear, you're not limited at all with the shoulder? >> No, I'm all good. I'm all good to go. >> Okay, I know you used to spend your time talking to Coach Montgomery. Does anybody fill that void for you? >> Uh no, he actually called me the other day, made sure I was up. So, I mean, I'm a I'm a miss him. I I think he's still out there coaching and I'm going to keep in touch with him for sure. >> What time did he call you? >> He ain't call me that early. If I He called me at like 7:00. >> [laughter] >> You guys are really birds of a feather. >> Yeah, we're the early birds, yeah. >> But, you have this X-factor about you that just completely changes the energy when you step on the field. Why do you think that is? >> Uh I'll pretty much say uh I've been doubted my whole life and just being able to to have an edge. Uh I've always been told I'm too small, I'm not fast enough. So, uh things like that it it motivate me and give me an edge when I step on the field. And I also know what I do it for. I do it for the people back home that uh don't really get a chance to make it to the NFL and uh try to give them some hope. So, each and every time that I step on the field, I'm going to give them my all. >> Have you had a chance to go back home? And and what have those folks said to you? Uh you know, I I that's got to be really exciting for them watching you on TV every Sunday. >> I mean, no, I haven't really got a chance to go back home, but uh each and every time that I speak to somebody back home, I know back home they all cheering for me and they all want me to do great, but just being able to try to get them kids uh back in Chicago hope that it's possible long as they just work hard and and and keep everything the main thing. >> Speaking of cheers, when when you make some electric plays at Raymond James Stadium, the crowd goes nuts. They chant your name. You hear that? What does that What does that mean to you? What happens on the field when you hear Bucky Bucky Bucky like that? >> I mean, when I when I make a big play and I hear that, it uh it just give me more juice and uh eager to make another play. >> What was the message from Todd Bowles at the start of camp to you guys? >> Uh what 2026 going to look like. I mean, every season is different like I said, but just being able to the the follow our coaches' lead, to put us in the right situations, to go out there and win football games. >> You guys like Mike Evans and Lavonte David gone, and things, you're starting to become a veteran on this team. Like, what is that like for you helping this team kind of rewrite its identity and and playing even like a bigger role in in the leadership of this team? >> Uh I mean, I won't I won't say I'm there with them guys at cuz them guys them guys play and they did a lot of things for this team, but I'll pretty much say I'm not really a guy that uh that lead with pretty much talking. I'm going to really come up here. I'm going to show up early. I'm going to be here on time. Uh and I pretty much just lead by example cuz everyone on this team got their own motivation on why they come each and every day and give it their all. >> Thank you. >> How well are you settling in? And how much have you learning a new system here in Tampa? >> Yeah, no, it's been a great transition. Um one of the good things about coming here was one of my high school best friends was Koki. We actually went to the same high school, so um kind of having that built in and having him show me around and introduce me to guys and um tell me kind of what to expect and and all that has been great. So, he's been a huge help for me and um kind of preparing for this training camp. >> You're coming here with A.J. Robinson from Carolina. What's A.J. Robinson like as a player and how excited are you to to play with him again for sure? >> Yeah. Uh yeah, and I was with him in LA, too. So, um kind of our journeys have looked a little bit similar, crossed paths a few times now. I'm glad he's on my team. He's kind of scary and uh he's he's just an animal and he's going to do whatever it takes to um help our team win. So, I'm glad he's on my team for sure. >> What does this defense allow for the the linebackers position to do? A little more free range or how does >> Um yeah, it's I mean it's all the above. I think every linebacker position in the league you have certain responsibilities that you need to get guys lined up and then then you got to do your job. So, um for me right now it's getting everybody lined up and getting the right calls out there and then um getting comfortable going to make plays. >> You had a couple big games last year against the Buccaneers and against Baker Mayfield. You had a sack and an interception. What was What was the appeal in free agency to go across the division and come to Tampa Bay? >> Yeah. No, I have a lot of respect for I played I feel like I've played Tampa a lot in my career and played in been with Baker um in LA for his stint and then played against him and just a ton of respect for his love of the game and his just his grit as a quarterback. I think it's hard to find that. Um not not all quarterbacks around the league have that kind of drive and that grit like he does. So, um yeah, just a lot of respect for the guys on this team and I'm excited to be a part of it now. >> From a special teams standpoint, from a special teams standpoint, what are your impressions of Lance Zierlein? >> Uh yeah, same kind of the same thing. I've seen respected him from a distance as a coordinator and how long I mean, I don't know what year this is for him, but um if I have that many years in the league or just at any job and you've still got a job, you must be really really damn good at it. So, um he's I mean, it's like it's his first training camp. He's excited to be here. He's fired up, and um he'll get us he'll get us fire flying around and um making plays and and doing the right thing. So, >> What was Todd Bowles' message to the team in that initial training camp meeting? >> Uh yeah, we got a lot of potential right now, but it's day one. And there's a lot of we got the right pieces. Um there's a lot of guys in the room that can help us win, and but it right now it's just potential. We got to go in, put in the work, and every every team around the league is saying the same thing right now, but we got to do something different and be different right now to separate ourselves. >> This team losing some guys that have been like the face of the franchise between Mike Evans and Lavonte David. Um you know, you're you're part of a group of new veterans that have come in that kind of get to help this team remake its identity. What what is that like for you? >> Um yeah, I think this organization I have a lot of respect for it. Just the continued success that they've had, and like you said, the guys that have been here that help um do that for so many years, and it'll look a little different, but the pieces are still there, and um we brought in the right guys, um the right veterans, A. J. Brown, Al, just all the guys that they brought in and as far as a leadership standpoint, and um just guys that have been there and can help lead this team. >> [snorts] Yeah. It's great. It's my It's my favorite job right now. I love football, but uh that's my favorite job and um yeah, it changes perspective a lot when I come out here and um so yeah, it's been it's been amazing. My wife's been amazing. >> Do you lean on on your teammates cuz you have a lot of first-time fathers that are in this group, too? >> Yeah, no, there was uh a lot of the guys um on the team have kids, so I talked to them and um just kind of what to expect and you think you're prepared and you're not and uh so I I learned pretty quickly, I think, and I'll continue to learn every day, so. Just like football, so. No, you're good. >> You've experienced a variety of systems across the league. How has that really helped you grow in your craft? >> Uh yeah, so kind of now I was with in LA for 5 years and just got really comfortable in that system and then went to Carolina, which was similar cuz it was um a coordinator that had come from that system and this >> just kind of moving on to the next one and the next one, it's a lot of the same stuff, just kind of getting the words down, the checks down, um what falls on my shoulders as um what my job entails. That's different from years past, so um OTAs were great for me. Um and now training camp's huge. I mean, this is this is all we do for I don't know how many weeks. Is it 6 weeks till the first game? 7 weeks? So, this is all we got for 7 weeks as each other, so um we're going to learn a lot about the defense and the ball and and a lot about each other, too. >> Training Mike and Noah? >> Um I right now it's just day one, so um I'll do whatever they need me to do. Um I think being a vet, I think it's expected for me to to be able to kind of transition back and forth and it's it's pretty similar in our system, um so that's been good um to kind of be able to do both and be available at both spots. >> Cross paths at all with with Angeloni before this stop and just putting impressions on him. >> Uh I had not. Um I I mean, it's hard to miss him with his hair. Uh, I don't know who would do that. It's kind of weird to play with that, but Um, no, I I He's a close friend already. Um, just being around him for however many weeks I was here in OTAs, and I'm excited to to play with him, whatever that looks like, and um, just to be on the team with him and share the locker room with him. And in the room, he's a good he's a great leader. He's advocate for the guys. Um, so, yeah, I'm I'm excited to be a teammate with him, too. Thanks. >> Congratulations.

title: Todd Bowles' Takeaways From First Day Training Camp | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: Morning. >> Todd, we didn't see Tristan work out there today. What's his status? >> I tweaked something in the running test. Vita as well, so we left them inside getting treatment. >> Is that for how long they might be sidelined? >> Uh right now, I'm not sure. I'll know more today. I would hope it's not long, but we'll see. >> Is it a hamstring or >> Well, Tristan's >> Hamstring, yes. >> Vita, what's your hearing for him planning to practice today? >> He ran yesterday. He did good in the test, and he tweaked something as well, so he's day-to-day as well. >> So, so just to clarify, so for Vita not practicing, it's strictly injury-related for him. >> Well, he tweaked something yesterday, yes. I haven't been told otherwise. >> Your your reports that Vita Vea wants to be traded, what's your reaction to that? >> Comes up every year. That usually takes care of itself. Our job is to get the guys ready to play for camp. Vita's here. We're getting him ready. He's engaged in the meetings. He understands everything. He helps all the guys out, so we're getting ready to play the season with him. >> I know mini camp he did a holdout, so he was participating in classroom instruction, but just not doing the official portion of practice. What what have you seen from from Vita from then and and then now? >> No, it's been the same. He's been engaged then, he's engaged now. Like I said, he came in in great shape. His weight is good.
