title: Jalen Hurts On His Excitement for Training Camp
text: How you guys doing? It's good to be back. Uh felt like it was a good summer. A really good summer. I've been able to spend time with the guys and really build towards everything that we've transitioned to. Um everybody's, you know, very hungry and excited to go to work. And we really focus on that. You know, I'd say one of my main points coming in, especially talking to to my teammates and getting the a sense of where we are throughout the summer and where we're going is just the importance of discipline and and unity. And you know, I can't emphasize enough how important it is to carry and protect the intimacy of this team and what we do. Um because it takes all of us. And we know that there are challenges that come throughout the year. Um we're not looking forward. We're really just focusing on where we are right now and then taking advantage of this training camp. And so to to come out here and, you know, have the conditioning test and have our first day be out here to, you know, get it in is it's a good good start, good foundation. And we just want to continue to progress forward, take it one day at a time. Yeah, it's um it was something I'm always intentional on trying to get everybody together and spend that time because that's what is a reflection of what comes in the season. Um we were able to get, you know, some of the younger guys together 2 years ago prior to uh the 2024 season. And then there are moments when I have guys individually and I'll spend time with them that way. Um wherever we are. But I think it was it was really good to have everybody all in on it going into this off season and and have everybody, you know, expressing and showing that hunger to to build and kind of learn each other's personalities a bit so we can, you know, go out there and thrive on the field, so I was definitely excited about that and um I I think it'll it'll pay for it. The work will show. >> Going back to what you mentioned in your statement your opening statement about the importance of being close and, you know, being together, was that more of a point of emphasis when you got everybody together? >> Well, you know, I think that's something that honestly it starts from Coach Sirianni and and his message and his first words in yesterday's team meeting was about um being together and being aligned. And when I was taking notes of it, I just, you know, thought about 100% alignment and zero entitlement. And so uh as a team that's that's what everybody's pushing. Um I talked to Saquon and he's talking about just us being disciplined and us going out there and fighting for one another and executing, so you know, that's a bigger picture standpoint and, you know, I think Coach Sirianni is um it's starting with him, obviously, but um we just want to take it a day at a time and being able to onboard everything we're doing and continue to deposit daily. >> DeVonta said earlier that it takes some time for a offensive coordinator, a first-time offensive coordinator, to find a flow. You've been around a bunch of coordinators in your life. From your perspective, what goes into a coordinator finding their flow? >> Yeah, I think I think Coach is going to be just fine. Um he's got a lot of structure and a lot of intentionality behind what he does and you know, I think I'm at a point where I have to help help him and um be of um not influence, not, you know, somewhat service, but you know, kind of hold up my end of it as well because I've experienced it so much. So, I mean, that's all I've experienced. So, I think realistically there's nothing new going into this year. >> Knowing what you know about this offense now, what excites you about what's coming to cut off? >> Say that again. >> Knowing what you know about the offense now, what excites you about it? >> Well, I think the number one thing is the work and the repetition in in getting opportunity to get that in. And so, you go throughout the spring, you take it as it comes, you spend time with your teammates, you grow, you embrace every rep, you're intentional about every rep. Then you come back here and you kind of turn that that that process you extend that process even more. So, I'm not I'm not at the season yet. I'm I'm taking this one day at a time here, trying to build with everybody and make sure we're all on the same page. That's going to That's going to make it go. >> What about Makai this summer? What have you learned about him, the way he works, or anything that's stood out about him as you've been around him longer? >> I think I think all I I think everybody has a passion here. If you're on this roster, you got a passion for the game. The number one thing with Makai, I see his heart, and I see his hunger, and you know, it's a different place to have been in the league when someone's, you know, like Makai's been in high school. So, that's a different place for me. But, to be able to fill those questions, answer those questions, and then provide the insight in what I see, and just really learn each other, right? You know, it's there's definitely a uh a you know, vet role in that in that, and then there's also the reality that we're both young and doing what we're doing. So, we're both learning something new, on boarding something new, and we want to be able to own it and say it's ours and we're growing in that. So, we're growing together. >> What about How What constitutes What about this conversation that you had with August when you were looking at the company? >> A good camp? Um it's I think I think that never changes. It's not about career, but it's just about situation. And so, I think my situation, you know, as a quarterback has just been to get on page get on the same page with the offensive coordinator going into the year, and then carry that throughout the rest of my teammates, so we're all on the same page. So, um I'm always seeking alignment, and then I think with different pieces that come and go, it you know can make that challenge you know or it can make it easier. >> How have you seen Smitty develop in the time since he got here in 2019? What sticks out to you? >> Smooth. I think just smooth. He's always been very polished. You know, I think um I I I I I take a flashback into my time at Alabama where you know, when all those guys declared for the draft he didn't. And so he's kind of always the the one that was taking the backseat a little bit. Um but I know he's always had that hunger. You know, I think his resume and what he's been able to accomplish in his body of work speaks for itself. Being a Heisman Trophy winner, being a champion at every level, um knowing what it is to win. And so those are the things that I cherish and value. And um I also know that he's been very diligent in his work throughout this whole journey since I've known him since I was 17. So um you know, I know he's um he's worked really hard. He's been intentional and you know, we're just going to take it a day at a time. He'd say the same things I'm saying now. >> What's what's what's your view of Jalen Carter here within the last year or two? What does it mean to you that he's come to play here in this city? >> Oh, man. I think um you know, for the for what he represents in sports and sports culture it's it's huge and I think it's huge for the city of Philadelphia. And so it'd be exciting to have a figure like that in the city. What he's done, uh one of the greatest to ever do it. And um I'm I'm I'm excited to to to be a part of that. >> What's the What's the What's your view of Jalen Carter getting his contract? >> I'm excited for him. I mean, you know, one he, you know, congratulations. Um Yeah, my wife had put a $5 bill in my my backpack. a little inside joke between her and I, but I took that $5 bill and I went and gave it to Jalen Carter and I smacked it on his chest and I said, "Let me put five on top of that." So, we just had a little fun, but um you know, he's um you know, he's he's a great competitor, uh great player. He's disrupting practice out there today. I mean, just excited for him to um you know, be able to focus on what's to come and move forward, yeah. >> You spoke to his consistency, Jaylen, but the fact that the offense is so different, is that invigorating to you that that it it is such a different challenge for you every day? >> I mean, what's the challenge is a challenge, you know? You you look at them all the same. You know, you got to look at them the same, but understand you may a vi- they may come with different things. And so, I think my approach is is not changed with that. Um my my my goal is always to get hip to hip with with the coach, um build with the guys around me, and make the most of what we have. Competitively, at the end of the day, the goal is to go out there and win. So, we got to prepare ourselves to be able to do that. >> Like, are you enjoying the center and practicing under center and doing all of those things? >> Yeah, I think it's an extension of what I've done already in that department. You know, it's been an area of my game that I've always had and we just haven't done it a lot. So, um we'll just be putting it on tape more. >> Thank you. Thanks, Jaylen. >> All right, let's wrap it.

title: Jalen Carter & More On the Beginning of Eagles Training Camp
text: What's up? What's up? How y'all doing? Thank you so much, man. >> Thank you. >> You starting it off. >> Yes, sir. >> Yeah, it means a lot, man. First of all, I'm thankful for them giving me the opportunity to come here. You know, even before the draft, my first visit, just having a conversation with them, I knew that it was going to be a lot of trust and love and if I was able to get here, that it was going to go perfect and everything was just going to work out. And uh you know, I know we're here for the contract and the contract is a reflection of the trust that the coaches, the the players, the organization has in me and uh you know, I'm very thankful for that. over the last few months, like I think the team probably wanted the h wanted this to happen sooner. How how were you handling the last few months? >> Last few months I just been working. You know, I had my uh agent Drew Rosenhouse really handling everything and my beautiful mother over there. They did most of the uh communicating and talking and uh they let me relax and uh you know, get my summer work in and come in just ready for the uh start of the season and you know, they got it handled and I'm very thankful for them. I'm thankful for a lot. Matter of fact, let me slow it down. I want to first I want to say I'm thankful for God for putting me on this earth and getting me here. Uh I'm thankful for the coaches, the players, uh the organization. Mr. Lori, you know, he's a big impact in what's going on right now. And uh thankful for you guys, too. You guys put out some good information, some good facts about me and stuff like that. And you know, we all we all one family. >> Was it important for you to be the highest pat? It was important for me to stay here with the guys that I know and been playing with for the last three years. Like I said, I live with my agent and them do most of the talking. The numbers wasn't in my head like that. Uh, and they just came back to me with information and we got the deal done and I'm happy to be here. >> St. Paul said that on the outside don't understand how scared you can be on that field. What is there that's left on tap that needs to be unlocked? >> Man, it's a lot, man. And you know, every day I'm going step by step and I'm humble and I'm put to uh just take it day by day. You know, I still got my guys JD right there. You know, I was there for JD signing and now JD's here for mine and it's a blessing just to see him uh to work with him another couple more years and uh you know, this is uh I'm just blessed, man. I'm just happy that I can stay here and just be with the guys that I grew up with. >> You can get to >> Oh, yes, for sure. I'm working every day to get make myself better either with technique or uh team chemistry or just pretty much everything. Yes, sir. >> How do you keep the money from changing you in a way that you don't want to change? >> I don't really think the money ever is ever going to change me. You know, when you get picked in the first round and top 10 pick, you know, you kind of get a little bit of decent money and that didn't change me. You know, I still came in, I had a goal. I let the team know and the uh defense know that the goal was to get a championship. and you know it happened but it's a new contract and it's time to get more championships for the city of Philly. >> You mentioned Jordan back there watching you. What has he meant you know over the last year you see him you know the way his game elevated? He got a contract extension. Did that push you? What what was that like over the last year? >> You can say say it again. My bad. >> Yeah. I guess generally just seeing what Jordan was able to do this past year. Got a contract extension. How did that you know push you see what he was able to do? How did you kind of work off each other? >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah, we worked off each other for show and JD is like an older brother to me. Like I say, we go way back to when I was going on visits at Georgia where he was my host and he was taking me around. I'm falling asleep in his dorm and stuff like that. And you know, just the moments and the memories that we have and it's just, you know, it's a lot and I don't know. I'm thankful for all of it. And just to see him at the next level, which was all our goals, you know, goal wasn't NIL, get the most NIL, none of that. Our goal is to make it to the league and stay in the league. And that's what we're doing right now. Congratulations to him on his big contract. He told me I was next up and we here right now and uh you know it's a lot going on. It's a lot of love out here. >> You seen you seen guys get signed before you signed this deal. You seen these other players get signed rewarded for their excellence and what the team thinks of them. >> What does that do to you in terms of like looking around the locker room saying I'm a young guy. If I play where I want to play and the team want to be played I'm going to get rewarded too and how the organization treats its younger players and the players who are playing really well. >> Yeah. My goal wasn't to always just come out and oh, let me just be a highest paid defensive tackle. My goal was to build team chemistry and win a championship and I think that all falls in lines to getting me to where I'm at now. That's pretty much the big message to the rest of the team when they see you signing a deal like that. >> It g it gives them confidence in me and then it just bu I need to hear that. My bad. >> So So you're young. So there's like young guys in the locker room. They see that you're using your field. [clears throat] >> Yeah. They do you think that they feel, hey, the organization's going to take care of me when it's my turn? >> Oh, yeah, for sure. And we all built that confidence into each other to where if when it's their time for them to sign their contract, no matter where it's at, you know, we're going to make sure that they get their money and to get paid and things can happen the exact way as going on now. >> What was the moment like when you could share with your family that >> Say it again. share with your family that you got the deal? >> Man, it was crazy. No, like I said, my mom was texting me throughout the day and letting me know what's going on. And then I got my brother texting me, then my dad text me, and then it was just, no, it's all like when I first got drafting, your phone's blowing up and everybody texting you and stuff like that. But, you know, it's all love, you know, and I appreciate everybody who's supporting me all the way through where I'm at now. >> You went through a lot last year with your shoulders. >> Was there a point in the offseason where you said, "All right, I'm good." And you felt >> like you were back to 100%. >> Oh, yeah, for sure. You know, I worried out at this one spot over there in New Jersey with uh a guy named Julian at hybrid performance and he really got me back to where I needed to be. And when I came back in, the coaches could tell that my shoulders was feeling very good. You know, lifting good and uh you know that it was a new season. >> How good day affect you last? >> You can say it affected me a good amount, but uh you know, I'm not letting that get to me. It's a new season. I'm taking step by step to get better every day and uh that's what it is. Yes, sir. >> What's next in your development, do you think? You say it again. >> What's next for you and your development? >> Just getting better every day. You know, this contract is it's good. It's decent. It's it's happy. We can enjoy our time, but we still got to come back out here and practice every day. Get better. Uh it's a new season. You know, it probably bring more odds to me, more double teams and stuff like that. So, I just got to come out here and get better every day. >> What are you going to do? What are you going to do with the $5? >> What type of responsibility? >> Responsibility. It's a lot, but you know, I'm just, you know, staying humble and being calm with I'm not letting it overhype me or anything like that. You know, like I said, I still got to come out here every day. My main focus after this meeting, I'm going to watch film. We're going to get right and then we going to worry about what we can do tomorrow to get better. >> What are you going to do with the $5 bill that Jaylen Herz gave you? >> You seen that? >> Told us about it. Yeah, >> that's my guy, man. You know, he's just so professional when he's around, you know, he just he just it's just a different uh feeling, you know. just I don't know he's just a big role like he's like a big brother also and uh when I talk to him it's just oneonone it's always serious talks just never play around and you know I got a lot of support of him >> you going to spend it or frame it >> $5 I said people to sign it probably worth $500 >> probably ra [laughter] I got it held it's at the house though I literally held it all day it fell out my pockets for teammates giving it to me it was a funny moment though >> how much you helped you first got here who else who else the building has helped you, brought you along, and helped you get to the point where you are getting this >> pretty much everybody on this team. Like the team chemistry is so crazy where you when you getting going to the league, you get told that, you know, it's a lot of individual things that you have to do, but coming here just the Georgia boys and then Fletcher Cox was a big impact, Brandon Graham, pretty much everybody. Like we talked to the offense, you see Jaylen Hurst come up to me, give me $5. uh like he's been talking to me since I got here. You know, we have conversations in the uh cafeteria or just walking and stuff like that. So, it's it's a lot. And Saquon Barkley, I can name pretty much everybody and little moments we had, but it's the whole team. >> Thank you. Congratulations. >> How was day one? >> It was fun. Uh feels like first day of school. Um getting back out there. I mean, just being around the guys again, uh, going out there competing, that's what it's all about. Um, you know, you're gonna have some mistakes on day one. You improve from it. Um, but it's a blessing. We're out here playing a sport that we love and doing with a great group of guys. >> Uh, Lane seemed a little energized by the new offensive scheme. Do you get that same feeling when you have that that newness? Yeah, I mean I think it's pretty cool that you just, you know, it started from scratch again. Uh, learning new language. Um, you know, getting familiar with a new system. Um, and it's fun. You know, when the way you taking notes is a little bit different than you would take notes if you were in a system, especially for as long as he was. Um, but it's going to put you in spot to do something new, something you may not be used to. Um, but as a competitor, you welcome that challenge and I think we're all doing that off the side of the ball and um, we got a great challenge against every single day going against Vic and those guys. >> I know football is fun of mind, but you put your recruiting pitch like now that he's here. What was your reaction? >> Um, I'm excited, Braun, to be here. I don't know if I really put a recruiting pitch out. Um, I got asked a question. Were you one? I think I think you I forgot who asked, but I got asked a question and um, uh, but I'm excited. I think, you know, the city of Philadelphia is is a super cool place to be for sports and how involved the fans are and, you know, having Braun here is is just great for the culture. >> What changes for you in terms of like there being more wide zone blocking and I guess probably more outside zone. What changes for you? >> Yeah, I've always been intrigued with this kind of system. um you know watching it kind of from afar and seeing a lot of guys have a lot of success in it. The thing that changes for me, you know, it's we coach it a little bit different. Um, you know, outside zone and wide zone, it's the read is pretty much the same, but just trying to get more of a one cut mindset. Um, you know, I feel like naturally in my career, especially all of us, unless you in a system like this in college, most of us come from gun and playing shotgun. Well, that's when I was in college. forever ago. So, I don't know what's really going on now, but you're more natural to like a duo or to like an inside zone. Um, and then, you know, when you get into NFL, you see a lot of guys struggle with outside zone in the beginning, but I've been working on that the whole time and just having that one cup mentality, but still doing it in a way [snorts] that I like to get out of the cut and just being efficient and being aligned with the offensive line and in the play and making it work. >> Is that the same where where you get the balls? Does the depth change at all? >> Um, depends depends who you are. Um, I remember I talked to AP. AP he like to be at eight. Um, you know, more times than not you're around seven, seven and a half. Some guys like to be at seven. Uh, you know, you get a feel with it. Um, you know, I might cheat it a little bit if it's third and three. Um, depends on what the defense doing. I might step back a little bit if I feel like that they're penetrating. Um, you know, it kind of that's kind of like the fun part of playing football. You you could play around with that and um, just get a feel for it. Has anyone has anything surprised you now that you've gotten a chance to really learn this game? Anything you didn't expect about maybe some of the advantages it gives to the running game? >> Definitely give you a lot of advantages, especially when you're able to marry it up with everything else. Um, for me, well, that's super close. Uh, for me, um, I feel like I have a chance to be really good in the system, too. Um, you know, you always I know, like I said, I've seen it from afar, but now like actually studying it and working it and and, you know, trying to put myself in the system. Um, I feel like it's going to open up some things that, you know, I may not have been able to show as much in my career. So, I'm excited for that, uh, that part of it, too. >> That usually doesn't happen. How have you been able to do it? >> Um, luck. Uh, I put a lot of work in my body. I put a lot of money in my body. And sometimes you get, you know, in New York, the way I was getting hurt, it was crazy. Um, things you can't control. That's football. Um, I don't think there's really one thing, you know, I can give credit to why I've been healthier here than when I was in New York. But a lot of luck. Um, and just continue to have the right mindset and the work ethic and take care of your body, which I've been I feel like I've been doing like I've been doing that since I was a rookie. Um, you know, that's something you hear vets say right away, take care of your body. So, I always try to ask as many questions I can and you know, I didn't want to be looking back and be like, "Oh, I wish I should have done that." But maybe I'm a little more consistent as I get older in my, you know, my scheduling, my planning, the way I take care of my body. Um, I feel like that's probably the only thing I could think that I've been doing better here than what I was in New York. But a lot of it is just is part of the game and a lot of it's luck. So, got to keep staying lucky, I guess. last year saw an increase in the number of times you were asked to stay in and help out the block versus going to route. Do you think that that's going to change in this offense? See more opportunities? >> Um, [sighs] how do I answer that without like giving too much? Um, yeah, I believe so. I I like the way that um our protection is um kind of friendly to the to the running back. Trying to be careful. I'm not trying to give you too much to be honest day one, but um feel like it might give me a little bit more opportunity to to get out and um be involved in a pass game. >> When you do get out in the passing game, are there a lot of differences or you know versus what you have been doing before? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, day one we played around with a little bit in OTAAS um of you know, finding unique ways uh to get me involved in the pass game. Um, I'm pretty sure we're we might elaborate on that a little bit more, but um, yeah, when you get out, all the routes in every system are pretty much the same. Um, but just doing a better job of getting out. I mean, I think I got to take, you know, responsibility for sometimes last year just being too alert, like trying to do too much and not getting out fast enough. Sometimes that happens. um and then doing a better job of just understanding the pass, trusting the system, trusting O line and getting out and try to be a, you know, a safe spot for for Jaylen. >> What's your reaction to uh uh Jaylen Carter's contract? >> I'm excited. Um he deserves it and you know, I heard what Zach said here and I agree with him. You know, they're not paying you for what you've done. They're paying you for what you're going to do. Um, and he hasn't even scratched like you guys don't understand how scary it actually can be. Um, so I'm excited for him and uh his family and everything and that's a that's a big contract. It's a great contract, but he deserves it. He's a heck of a player and and I believe and we all know it. Um, that is another level that he can take it to and I look forward to watching that. >> Does it provide anything to the locker room and that happens right as training camp opens that that a guy like that is signed? Yeah, I mean something about this organization, something about how we um they just do it the right way in my opinion. Um there's a reason why this team has been successful. I was talking to Dallas and we're both going to year nine and I'm like he's like he's only missed the playoffs once. I'm like, you know, it's not an accident. You know, there's a reason why, you know, Dallas never really had to hit the open market. Lane's been here his whole time. They take care of the guys. Um, and that's not like that anywhere else. And this is not me taking a shot at New York or anything like that. Just speaking just kind of giving respect to how this organization is run. Um, so yeah, you know, that's the you're a younger guy or a guy who's trying to get paid, you see it, you do what you got to do, you're going to get taken care of. How comfortable how comfortable supported is Jaylen in this offense especially under >> um I mean I think Jaylen has done a great job from day one uh to OTAAS we're all being asked to do something a little different but the thing is Jaylen is willing and able to do whatever we ask him to do and um you know he has that he he has that that competitive mindset of just wanting to be great and doing whatever it takes to win but also So, always trying to find ways to improve his game. Um, and he's doing that. So, it's day one and we only have OTAAS and we're going to all just keep getting better and better. >> Remember that how he different here, how takes care of his guys. I mean, in one way I can see like contracts here that proves it. Are there ways leading up to that that he that he shows that how he uh valuable or is it really just what he does once that moment arrives long? Um, yeah, there's more into it. I kind of have a personal story, but rather keep that to ourselves. But, um, yeah, it just how we obviously how he does a great job, but just from everybody up there on the top, like they're it's actually very impressive. Um, and if I ever became a GM or had some got enough money to be able to own a team, I would run it how how they do it here. What up? Welcome back everybody. Good. >> I know. >> I'll break the ice. Um, in years past when we've been asked Nick about the passing game, he said, you know, runs the way AJ Devonte Dallas, obviously things have changed. Do you sense there could be more diversity in the passing game in terms of what we'll see as the season starts? >> Yeah, a bunch of new faces, bunch of new names. Um, you know, our offense we're doing is entirely different. So, under center play action, wide zone consistent with that. And so, yeah, I think far as spreading the ball, I think there'll be a lot of that. You know, each guy getting more touches. So, what I like about this though is that um everything looks very complex to the defense. To the offense, it's pretty uh simplified. So, obviously we got to pick up on communication and and cadence and stuff, but um it's very O line friendly compared to maybe some past years that I've been involved in. So, um man, looking forward to it. Looking forward to the offense. So, first day um you know, guys getting jitters out and um you know, getting the first practice under their belt is big and you know, we're going on the walkthroughs and just trying to get a rep. How is it align? >> Uh I mean it's a lot of it's under center so um far as defenses being able to pick up on reads I believe it's more difficult. Um and for me it's like I always have a presence of a guard and pass protection where I have inside help where I've never had help in my in my entire career in pass protection here. So it's been a lot of games are different for me and Jordan far as other offenses. you see this man, we have a we have ability to um yeah, we just have a lot more inside help and uh when we're under center, it's so hard for the defense to really tell if it's a run or play action, you know, instead of getting off the ball now. It's a lot more hesitation, a lot more reading from them. So, I believe this offense uh does a good job of uh setting us up for success. >> When you talk about presenting a run and pass, similarly, how much work goes into that and how do you make sure that it does present that way? I mean, if we're running wide zone and then we're running wide zone play pass, you want to sell it front side, backside with your demeanor as far as having a low hat. Um, when you have a low hat, it can get the linebackers to bite down thinking that it's run and then you can hit them over the top with an over route. So, you know, you want it to all look the same with our presentation, even in our stance, you know. So, a lot of it's that um, you know, we're getting used to getting in a three-point stance again. We did some with Doug. Um uh not really with Chip, but you know, a lot with Doug. So, uh getting into that and that's really it. I mean, um you know, uh it's fun just trying to learn the the new terminology and and things with that, but it's coming. >> You've been on the receiving end of some some pretty big contracts. What's your reaction to Jaylen Carter's latest? >> Yeah, man. I was happy. You know, I told him his rookie year that, you know, this is where he was headed. Um you know, he had the potential um to obviously be a great dominating player in this league. So, um, you know, I think the way Jordan, uh, Davis carried himself last year, I think that gave him some motivation to to pick up the Annie. Um, you know, and so, yeah, for him, I think, you know, he's only scratching the the surface of what he what he's going to become. He just has, uh, the ability with that size, you know, few guys can move like that at that at that size and weight. So, um, I think this will just be a huge incentive to just keep progressing and become the dominating force that we all know he is. and I just stay consistent with it. >> You talk about pass pro and you know being easier, maybe getting a little bit more help. How about the run game? How different is that for you? >> Yeah, I mean a lot of our landmarks are are really wide um outside zone and and a lot of the run game is built on backside uh cut off blocks from the center guard and tackle. So, uh if if the running back can stretch the front side and get around the edge, uh do it. if you can't, you know, run that S pattern, ride the wave backside, and uh yeah, man, it's a lot of fun. So, uh just for us, uh you know, me and Jordan, man, we're getting to really run, stretch the field, um you know, cover some yardage. So, that way, man, it tires out defenses, makes them cover each gap. Um you know, all the fakes, um motions look the same, so it's hard to differentiate. Uh makes guys hesitate. And so, um, yeah, for us, man, it's, uh, lot lot of running, uh, sideline to sideline, covering space. So, maybe more than what we have in the past, you know, consistently. >> Denny, was this offseason any different for you coming off of what you did last year? >> Uh, no, just motivated, man, to get on the field. Um, and I feel like I was having a really good year last year. Um, you know, not being able to get on the field and help my team, uh, when they needed me most is frustrating, especially, you know, my age. So, um, you know, that's where I'm at. my my goal is to stay healthy, stay on the field, and be the player that I'm meant to be. Um, and yeah, man, it's crazy going in my 14th year, you know. Uh, when you're coming in league, you try to make it to five, and then it's 10, and then Yeah, man. I'm just uh enjoying my time uh with all the new guys, all the new faces, and uh yeah, just take it one day at a time, day one. >> Does it feel like your 14th training camps veterans kind of days off or >> uh I'm not sure. Uh, I have to check I'll have to check with Tom with that, but man, training camp isn't like it used to be, man, when the guys were at Lehigh and two days. It's a lot uh sissified as the old guys say. Uh, so yeah, man. No, no complaints. Um, so yeah, man. Just try to stay healthy and and uh through camp, get better, and get ready for week one. >> Speaking of speaking of a new face, what was how have you seen Markeel Bell make the adjustment to the NFL? What's been your impressions of him? >> Markell's just a great person, man. He's a great student. um you know, works his ass off. Um and really, you know, I think what they did at Miami was very similar to what, you know, Stout had us doing here. So, um you know, he's just he's a very good kid. That's what I noticed right away. Never complaining, always working, always listening, and so he has a lot of maturity, you know, for a rookie. Um you know, compared to some others that we had in the past. So, yeah, man. He's a huge human. Has incredible feet in pass protection. his feet stay really low to the ground. So, he's going to be he's going to be a big problem in this league years to come. >> Across the O line, is it apparent to you how much healthier and fresher this group is this time last year? >> Yeah, you know, I felt last year coming in, you know, um Jery was coming off of um you know, back surgery. I think Landon had some things obviously had the foot later in the year, but yeah, we have uh all guys out there for day one. Um and so yeah, that's big, man. Anytime we can maintain the um you know, the main group of guys in there, get the reps, especially with this do offense, the better we're going to be. And I think with us staying on the field and not missing practice and taking those reps, it builds confidence knowing that we can endure and we can um and we can last, man. And uh you know, a lot of people depending on us, so you know, we need we need to be out there. >> You mentioned that this game prioritizes movement skills, more lateral, you know, kind of running sideline to sideline. How have you seen those guys adjust to that? How do you think overall the group can adjust today? >> Yeah. No, it's I mean a lot, you know, we're changing up some our snap count and our cadence is different than what it has in the past. A lot of procedural pen penalties today, but um yeah, for us it's uh really fatigues guys. Really fatigues the interior lineman. It gets guys gassed. Um and for us, man, it seems like, you know, kind of bootleg landmarks. We're running really wide zone compared to what we have in the past. Um, so a little bit different feel, but I can see where the benefits are going to pay off. You know, we just got to, um, get in a rhythm. Um, get the reps in where we're not guessing. We're know what we're doing. But, I mean, you see it around the league what offenses are doing. So, uh, you know, I'm anxious to see how we do this year and and take it a day at a time, though. But I'm really excited. >> How do you think how do you think Tyler's progressed year two as a starter? He's got that that experience underneath him. >> Yeah, I mean, night day. I mean, I I thought he made a huge jump last year um becoming, you know, a dominating player. Um he's just, you know, you can see the maturity in him now. Um you know, in the huddle, there's not not as many questions. It's a lot more uh better communication. Uh you can see kind of a more calmer demeanor. Uh you know, as the years are piling up, um not as brighteyed and bushy tailed in the huddle. It's more knowing what our assignment is and know what we needed to execute. So, that's been fun playing next to Tyler. I got to see him progress year in year out and he's starting to become the player that, you know, he he knows that he can be and that we all know that he can be. >> What kind of different stresses this new offense put on the line? >> A lot. This offense is really good. um one that's kind of taken over the league and we see a lot during the season and now to have it here at training camp practicing it, seeing it all the time is it's going to be really good for this defense and of course the offense as well. >> What are the keys to not getting tricked by the things that are designed to trick you? >> Uh having good eyes. Um there's a lot of motions, a lot of condensed formations. Um a lot of tight end tight end movement, a lot of receiver movement. Um the run and the play action look the same. the boots. There's a there's a lot of stuff that that go into this offense to making it is what it is. >> What's your reaction to Jaylen Carter one year? >> Let's let's go. [laughter] Uh h happy for him. Um that's a big deal. That's a really big deal. Him making sure he stays in Philly. Um he's a pleasure to to to play behind. Um really looking forward to to his his growth, which is crazy to say. He just signed an all-time contract and there's still room to grow. So super excited for him. and you're year you're >> three in in Vick's defensive scheme. So many of you guys have been here. How do you think that helps as you potentially get better? >> Yeah, I'll say this training camp feels a lot different than the first training camp uh Vic was here. Um we we know our stuff. We know what to expect from Vic. he knows to what to expect from us. And then it's bringing along the new guys that just got here or um have been here for only a year. And um and then continuing to grow and evolve and do different stuff and new stuff and um tweak things and put guys in different positions that um based on strengths and weaknesses. It's really cool >> as as the years since you've gotten here and as this defense grows together. I mean I mean you your first year last year how uh couple off throws in the second group and Quinnon and the recognition Jaylen's getting like what do you what's the sense of how this defensive core is coming together right now? >> Um I I feel like the Eagles have done a fantastic job of drafting good talent that stays here. Um they look to build talent from within, develop um and and just draft well. I mean, it's it's cool that you kind of see this shift from offensive core guys and now we're building the defensive side. Um, it's it's really a well-rounded machine around here. >> Zack, what did you see from Jad as he makes a step going into game two? >> Yeah, I feel like just based on in the meeting rooms, he he he has a full understanding of the defense. He can play um all the linebacker positions if you need him to, and he's versatile. He's continuing to work on his body. Um he he looks a lot bigger going into this training camp. So that's cool to see. I'm just glad he's working hard and um knows he's still got some work for imp room for improvement. You >> say the same about Trot in terms of size. >> Uh Trot always kind of looks the same to me honestly. Um but I know I know he's working. Um but he he's doing what he has to do and he's super smart guy. He's a phenomenal football player as well. When Kobe left, he joked that you were kind of hard on some of the younger guys in that >> who Nico did. >> It's just my personality. I'm a jokester. >> You signed your extension to stay here. What was your message to the contract? >> Yeah. F the first thing I say is congratulations. You deserve this. Um, and then I said, "They're not paying you for what you did, but what for what you're about to do." Um, someone I forgot who told me that when I signed my my deal. Um, but it couldn't be further from the truth. Um, what you did in the past is the past. And, um, they're they're paying you for what they expect out of expect out of you, not only on the field, but off the field as well as a leader in the locker room, too. >> Johnson was just talking about Jaylen Carter in terms of Lane was saying like he's yet to hit a ceiling and he's got a long way to go. you mentioned a lot of playing behind him. What's what what do you see in his future and how uh how much does he influence the game? >> Yeah, the attention he draws solely um is incredible. Uh you got to have four hands on him. Um and that's good for me because it allows me to run through gaps and and play like I do and play free. And then uh pass rush uh in the pass game as well. Slides have to go to him. They're sending the center that way. So we there's things having a player like that can make an offense predictable in ways. >> The time you spent with Jiad last training camp and even early last season, is it easy to kind of recall what it's like to play next to someone like that? >> Yeah, I mean all throughout we've gotten reps next to each other. So it's kind of seamless. Um even with Tro or Nico, it didn't matter who you threw in there, what how you mix and matched everyone. Um it's it's pretty seamless in the way we fit together. >> Thank you guys. Thanks. >> How are we feeling about LeBron being in town? Come on. Come on. Give me some. Give me some. All right. Just kidding. >> Caleb. [snorts] >> Excited, man. Um, you know, selfishly, I want to keep all the Georgia guys together. Obviously, we couldn't keep Nico, but he's out there being, you know, Nico and doing big things, but it's super excited to have Jaylen um for the next I don't even know what year. I'm on year five. So, for the next four years for me hopefully. and um you know the next five for him. So um really excited and I know he's super excited about you know just the whole process and you know we always try to leave the league better than we found it. Obviously he reset the market. He's the highest paid in NFL history and um you know that sets the bar for everybody else and you know the people behind us. So I think that's very important and um you know it's just we just love everything about it. So I know he's ready to work. I know he's ready to show out and be the player that I know he can be. >> Everyone talks about how Yazim hit his ceiling. What is what's next for Jaylen Carter in this next step of his career from your perspective? >> That's more of a Jaylen Carter question. Um, obviously I can't speak for anybody. I can't speak only for myself, but um the sky's is the limit and that's not only for him, that's for me. That's for everybody in the D tackle room. That's everybody on the team. That's everybody in this world. So, um, you know, the sky's is the limit and I'm excited to see where he'll reach and see the we all know the caliber of player that he is. You know, he wouldn't be here. He wouldn't have signed the deal. Um, if he wasn't that type of caliber player. So, um, you know, when he goes out there and he makes an impact like that, like that's who he is. That's what he does. And, you know, we're just all excited for that. >> Over the last three years, have you seen him mature? And if so, in like which ways? >> Definitely. Um, you know, it's more so about just the the process of it all. You know, it's coming into the league, it's a learning process. is you have to learn how to be a professional. Um you have to learn how to navigate things, how to navigate problems that we didn't have in college that we didn't have in high school. And um you know, obviously football is going to take care of itself. We have a great coach and coach Herz, but um seeing him with all the off the- field things and just seeing him just persevere through everything that he's been through, I think that's the biggest thing that I can really give him a take away from. Um I don't like to talk about exit and nose when it comes to people on the team um because there are more than that. But um just know I'm very proud of him. >> How about this offseason specifically? Like obviously you had to rehab the shoulders and you know Nick mentioned that looks like he's in great shape going in. I guess what was your vantage point for the the offseason the work you put in? >> Love the cut by the way. Um um >> still getting used to it. >> Yeah, I know. [laughter] Um but uh you know obviously rehab rehab was the biggest thing. Um getting them back healthy. We need everybody. Um, it takes everybody. So, you know, getting him back healthy and getting him to that place where he can be dominant, he feels confident in himself, feels confident in his body. Uh, but that's just a really big thing. Um, like I said, we're sitting in there for four or five hours just watching film and stuff like that. So, I'm not worried worried about that. He's a smart player. Cerebral is crazy. But, um, it's just really him just being healthy and just coming back and just being, you know, him just being Jaylen. >> Uh, Jordan, what do you what are you kind of seeing from Morrow as far as like what he can do this season and and how hard he's worked during the offseason and everything? >> Um, like I said, man, everybody knows uh the caliber of player that Mo is. um he's really been making waves, especially um I believe last season was, you know, his calling card and, you know, put a lot of people on notice that really wasn't paying attention to him before. But, um Mo is a leader. He's a natural gifted leader. Um and even in the DT room, it's a lot of leaders. It's not just one clearcut. It's not me. It's not JC. It's not just Mo. It's everybody. And um when he takes control and he puts his mind to something and he's super super technical, super competitive and you know I love that about Mo. Like even when it comes to like something like golf like Mo is super technical. So like but that's just the person he is. And so when he goes out there on the field when we're doing our 500 shots after practice we're working real real world situations. We're going out there. We're asking in worst case scenario how can we how can we manage? How can we change this? And um when you have guys on a team that take pride in their technical skills and they take pride in just putting on a good product, Mo is one of those people. And it's not just Mo, it's BY, it's is Tai is is is you are like you are is feeling that same type of pressure. So, you know, it causes us to kind of gel together and like collaborate with each other and we don't mind spending extra time with the BTS because we're all focused on improvement. are all focused on just climbing and how we could just how can we get better cuz you know if you're not getting better you're staying the same or you getting worse. So um Mo is Mo is one of a kind. Um I call him coach Mo jokingly. Y'all know that. But you know he really has the mindset of a coach and you know I just love playing >> beyond the line. Beyond the D line but also the rest of the defensive unit. How do you feel this young coming together and growing up together? There's others that are up and coming. What do you feel like that role is on the field and in the line? >> Uh I love the defense. I love the defense and um going into year this is year three of Vic. >> Wow. Yeah. Yeah, going into year three of Vic. Um, obviously there's a few plays that change to come and come and go, but for the most part, we have the base. The bases, the foundation. We're laying it now. We've been laying it in OTAAS. We've been laying it since he first came. So, we're just kind of climbing and, you know, we just want to, this is the time of the year where we set the standard. Um, how we play. It's a new team, so obviously we're not going to have the same kind of players that we had last year or the year before, but you know, we have the same standard. The standard is the same. The standard never changes. And um you know, I think the defense, and me and Zach talk about it all the time, just how it looks, how it feels. Um you know, it could feel good at OTAAS, but when you come in camp and we still haven't put pads on, but when you go into camp and you really get a feel of like even today, I was telling Z like, you know, we don't have pads on, but everybody's where they need to be. Everybody's where they're supposed to be. Everybody's fitting up how they're supposed to fit up. We don't have pads. So, obviously, you're not going to get that real push and shove, but as long as everybody's in their good spots, we're not in the wrong spots. That's a that's a great day one. We can work with that. We can build off that and we just climb. So, um you know, we're super excited. Um we're just blessed to even be in a position where we can call this defense ours. And, uh you know, when we go and we collaborate and you know, it's top down from the front to the safety. So we just want to make sure that we uphold that standard. We keep that basis strong. >> At 21 years old sitting together in college, you and Jaylen have ever imagined what happened this season. >> Not at all. Not at all. And that's the craziest thing about the league. Um you just never know what can happen. Um if you would have asked me in 2022, 2023, I would wouldn't even think that I would be in this position to be talking to y'all today. So um it's crazy how things can change in under a year and you know just everything. But um it's it's it's an amazing blessing. And uh you know, we just that's one thing that we do talk about a lot is just how long we've been together. Um not just from here, but just college, Nolan College, Nico College, um Keely College. So um Smile College, I could go on and on, but you know, it's just crazy to just be playing with the same guys that I've been playing with, have that same rapport, have that same feeling um going into the offseason the same way. it it's the same process, but you know, we're getting older, we're getting wiser. Um, we're we're we're getting that old man strength. At least I am. So, you know, it's just pretty cool to uh continue just continue this journey. And I know, you know, one day when we hand the cleats up and we all looking back and we're at an alumni game or something like that, we'll be able to speak about this time that we spend together. And um you know, the NFL is NFL not for long. So, um anytime that we get to spend it together, it's a blessing. What's the toughest part been >> from a defensive perspective? What's it like going against this offensive scheme? >> It's cool. Um, this offensive scheme gave us a few fits last year and um, you know, the more that we see it, the better that we become at defending it. And, um, you know, I can't speak for the offense. I don't know whether they I'm sure they like it, but um, it's different. It's different and that's something that we need to we need to see that we can't be used to. We have to switch it up because if you're doing the same thing and expecting the same results, that's the same. Um, but, uh, I would say when it comes down to it, I think we'll be in a good spot going into the season just with this scheme and this schematics and, you know, it's just excited. Uh, I see Saquon running, I see Tank running, I see, you know, a couple passes here and there, uh, route concepts that I'm looking on the iPad. I'm like, "Oh, all right. That's that's pretty nifty." So, you know, it's just a lot of different things on the offense that you get to see and um you know, hopefully they love it and hopefully we get to ride out in the season with it. >> Carter having the full off season rehab. If failing Carter having the full off season to rehab, how do you think having fully healthy will ultimately help you benefit your life easier? >> I can speak for everybody when I say having a full offseason to recover is uh night and day difference. Um it's important. Uh Coach Clay always says you can't make the club in the tub. So, um, the more that you I rather get it out the way in the offseason and when you come back, you're fully focused, fully ready to come back and be dominant. Um, and that's just for everybody. We don't want anybody hurt. We don't want anybody uh, you know, being banged up going into the next season because you want to start fresh. You want to start strong. And so, uh, you know, I think it's definitely well needed, not only for him, but for everybody. >> Ladies first. >> Thank you very much. Speaking of the offseason, I remember you being very sad at locker cleanout that we didn't care about your hobbies. So, how was your off season? Did you learn to play the guitar? Did you get through your bucket list? >> Oh my goodness, you're so kind. Um, I picked up golf. I picked up golf. So, uh, I got fitted for my clubs and OTAAS and uh, I just been swinging since. And, uh, you know, I'm still trying to figure out how I could balance the work life balance um, how I could get out to the course and uh, but it's pretty cool. It's um, one thing that kind of took up from me. I read a couple books. I haven't finished uh fourth wing, so you have to you have to give me a chance on that one. But um yeah, I think golf is the biggest thing. I've been watching it for years, but getting out there and actually playing and getting clubs fitted instead of playing with little tight clubs and stuff like that has been amazing. Um but like that, you know, that's a a skill that you can have for the rest of your life. And I think that was the coolest part about it is that this is not something that I have to be competitive at. Of course, you're going to be competitive. You want to get better. My swing is is starting to dial in a little bit. So, you know, I was I was whiffing the ball at first, but now I'm making consistent contact. Now, Howard sprays afterwards, so you gota you got to chill on that one. But, um yeah, like and that goes for everybody. Find a hobby. Find a hobby. Find something that you enjoy outside of your career, outside of your occupation. Um it it it truly takes my mind. It causes me to relax. And I know I'm doing something a little bit physical, especially if you walking the course and stuff like that, but um hobbies is important and I'll always stand for that. >> Lane mentioned that Jaylen seemed motivated by how you handled your business last year. Is that something that you picked up on and what were those conversations like? >> Definitely. Um and that's not just um JC. That's, you know, everybody that we played with at Georgia, you know, um like my guy Devonte Wyatt um one of my best friends uh Trayvon Walker, we all went through the same process at the same time. So, um, you know, it's easy to lean on each other and it's easy to kind of ask each other and just calm it down. I remember going through my process, I didn't want anything to do with it. I was like, "Look, that's between the office and that's between my agent. I don't want anything to do with it. Just come to me when it's time to sign the papers." And uh, you know, it it's for me it was a world off my shoulders because that was something I just gave it up to God. You know, you just let go and let God. So, um, you know, you feel so worried about it, but when it's finally done, dependence on paper, you feel so much relief, and I'm sure he's feeling the same way. >> All right. Great to see y'all. >> How's your summer off season? >> It was great. It was great. >> Um, how'd you feel the offense? I know it's the first day of practice. How do you think you guys did today? >> Uh, we had a lot of pre- snap penalties. We got to fix that. >> You had the the nice catch from uh Herz over the middle and tight coverage. Please kind of take us through that play. >> Um, just trying to get the timer down. Um, you know, the play calls a little excuse. >> How else do you expect there to be some going? How do you, you know, manage that? Work them through it as camp goes on. >> Uh, it's day one. You know, you you should >> I wouldn't say expect it, but I mean, it happens. It's day one. So, >> I know it's like you said, it's day one, but what do you know about some of your new teammates in the wide receiver room, Hollywood, those guys? Um, everyone loves to compete, man. Feel like we have a great group. A lot of guys in there that's played a lot of football. Uh, you know, guys just want to come out here and compete and I think that's the fun thing about it. >> How do you think you can complement each other like Hollywood get down the field different things? What do you see the guys compliment each other? >> Um, I think everybody, you know, can do everything. I think that's the great thing about this group. Everybody can do everything. So, just getting everybody up to speed. Um, you know, everybody have their growing pains on whatever it is in offense we were trying to get down. So just helping everybody get through everything that they need to. >> We know the difficulties of learning a new offense. How would you describe it so far in meetings and on practice when someone asks you what this offense looks like? >> Um I say, you know, you just it's bas it's basically the terminology. Uh you know, same stuff called different ways. Um called different things. So just getting the flow of how Sean is going to call it and you know and the new words and things like that. your relationship with Shawn Manion, how is it growing and what are your observations how he's handled the offense so far? >> Uh, it's great, man. He he's doing a tremendous job, you know, getting everybody up to speed. Um, helping everybody understand the small details of the offense for Jaylen as far as >> um I think he's doing great. >> Having a different play caller almost every year, is this the biggest adjustment as far as offense that you guys have experienced? Um, I like I said, I think the biggest thing is, you know, finding his flow, understanding how he's going to call it, the new terminology and things like that. Um, I think that's the biggest thing about it. You know, when you kind of don't know what the flow is, you kind of don't, you know, know what to expect. Um, you know, it's it's going to get some you have to grow and learn. So, I think once you get the understanding of how he wants to do things, I think it becomes easy. >> You've been around a lot of coordinators in your football career. How does one find their flow? Have you witnessed someone find their flow as play golf? >> Uh, everybody does different. You know, some guys it's um you know, he likes to see what guys can do, know what guys like and things like that. Some are, you know, get out here. He has to actually get a feel of you know, the Florida offense, what you know, you're good at. And some is, you know, they they like to walk through things. They like to walk through. They like to see it. Different looks and things like that. >> Are you seeing more of an emphasis on like throwing over the middle? Um you know, stuff like that that maybe you guys didn't do as much in previous years. >> Um I don't really, you know, keep track of stuff like that. I just go out there and work around. >> Devonte, do you find it difficult to come back to work after honeymoon? >> No, not at all. >> You biggest difference now when you >> um a lot more mature. Um played a lot of football, a lot um more things I understand. >> What did you find? Um, for me honestly nothing. Like I said, we have a lot of guys in that room that played a lot of football. So, you know, it's not like, you know, I have a bunch of young guys in there. We have Mai. We all have a group try to, you know, get him up to speed on things and what to expect. But, you know, you got to kind of let him figure out his own way. Everybody handles things differently. We're going to let him, you know, do what he does and he needs us with our phone. >> How did you for his first day? Oh, >> he did good. He did good. What type of advice? >> Just go out there and be you. Go make it bigger than what it is. What did you think of the Celtics trading Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia and then the Sixers get LeBron James? >> Look like the Sixers trying to, you know, go go in one, you know, can't be mad at that. >> Did the Jaylen Brown trade hurt a little bit? >> Uh, it that's that's the business, man. >> Is the Pro Bowler, I'm sorry. Is the Pro Bowl? >> Uh, I'm not really focused on that right now. Right now, I'm, you know, trying to get the offense. As a leader on the C team, we've seen a lot of phases of different players to see Jaylen Carter get the contract he did yesterday. What did that mean to you? >> Oh, it's great, man. I like seeing guys get paid. I told how he did a great job. >> He laughed. >> Oh, he's doing great. had coordinator changes changes. >> Uh I think I think that's a question you have to ask him. Do >> you guys talk a lot about, you know, things that are different with with what we're doing? >> Uh we talk about what we like, uh what we think we could, you know, implement and things like that.

Aaron, uh Jamal Parks, why don't you guys uh kind of coach up how what we're looking for on this drill? and and so yeah, there's there's little things like that that happen every once in a while. Nick, >> as you enter training camp, what's the plan at backup quarterback? Are those guys going to rotate? Um you know, we'll continue to rotate with those guys um with what what we're doing. But that's not, you know, Andy's played a lot of football. Um, and Andy's played a lot of good football. So, that has no um that doesn't say anything about what we feel about Tanner. Like, Tanner has been here for four years and we and has played some really good moments, played some really good games, has has so consistent at practice with what he does and and the type of player he is. So, we're really excited about that. But, we also know that competition brings out the best in everybody. Um, and so to be able to have a guy like Andy and Tanner working together and working to to push each other to get better, that's only going to make the our team better. Uh, so we're excited about that room. >> PG went on record somewhere this offseason. PG went on record somewhere this offseason. and said he would hope to know like his future in the early days of training camp. He doesn't want to come back in the middle of the season or whatever. Um you know, so those conversations obviously between us and every player we're going to keep uh between us and the player. Um, I want to be consistent with whoever that is that um, we do that. Um, but obviously you're talking about one of the greatest Eagles players. Um, unbelievable person. Um, last year his ability to come back in and help us was huge for our football team. Um, but again, you know, those conversations we'll keep private. >> Just relying on Jaylen for you >> Jonathan Bernard and what that means for >> with Jayen Carter from your perspective. >> You want me to answer you and he can answer him at the same time? Go ahead, >> Jaylen Carter. From your perspective, how how much does it help you to have somebody like that satisfied for the start of camp versus maybe, >> you know, situation? >> First of all, just really happy for him and his family. He's worked his butt off to to get rewarded the way he is and like how he said, it's a, you know, we're paying you for the what you're going to do um in the future. And we have that confidence in him. I've really gotten I've really enjoyed getting to know Jaylen more and more each year and the time that I've spent with him and he's put his head down, he's worked, he's made impactful plays and we look for that to continue. Um, and he's a heck of a football player that demands a lot of attention by the opposing offense. So, to be able to have him and have him locked up and um, we know what that creates for the opposing offense. I know as a former offensive coordinator, the problems a player at that position with that talent uh creates and the things that you have to do for him game planwise. Um yeah, and anytime you're you're just excited that that portion's out of the way and you're able to go and you and focus completely on football. Um which he has, you know, which I give him a lot of credit. He's focused so much on football. He came back in phenomenal shape uh with his weight, with his conditioning test. Um he was lifted um and he has a pec strain. I think that uh one of the things that we know about um Grenard is he's going to be ready to play and I think training camp's so important, practice is so important, uh but when you have a guy like that who prepares the way he does, who has the experience in the NFL the way he does, you know, he's going to be ready to play um when we start the season. Um but when we can, we're going to make sure that, you know, we take care of our guys and put them in the best position to have a great year. >> Nick, Cam Jurgens and Dickerson, are they full go going into this? And how important is it to have them both? >> Yeah. Um, obviously you saw the the uh PUP list and and then everybody else will be going and um you know again two guys that have come back and I I can't say enough of what happened at our conditioning test yesterday. It seemed easy for him and I know that test is hard. We've done that test plenty in these last five years. Um and they came back in great shape, those two guys included. Um crushed it and uh excited to get out there and work. Uh >> you know, teams take on the personality of their leader. Have you seen coach Cherion what great shape he's in? You know, you got Dom in great shape, Bob Lang in great shape right here. We got we got everyone's in great shape. >> Go back to Jaylen Carter. Have you seen guys whose preparation and and performance changed after they got a big contract and not necessarily for the better? You know, every day we're coming in, we're trying to find ways to get better. Um we're communicating with every team in the league to try to find fits um to see if there's opportunities to make ourselves better. Um and so it's certainly incomplete at this time. um it will be incomplete throughout the course of the season. Uh any opportunity we have and you look at our roster, you see u you know we it reminds me of just you know all the rooms that we have that it evolves over the course of time and that's not a reflection on how we feel about our players now. Excited about it. Can't wait to see them out there. But anytime we have a chance to get better to improve our team um we're going to look at that. >> Quite a bit of staff turnover this off season. Uh, can you speak to Al Cali departing Bryce Johnson for the Falcons and what about the replacements Grant and Adam? >> Yeah, I I'd add Jeff Scott to that as well. Um, you know, it's bittersweet because uh all of those guys have have put themselves in position to make career choices to improve their lot in life. Um, what you hope for for people that you're really close to. But, you know, I remember I was out to dinner with my wife at one point and just said, "It's going to be an adjustment for me." You know, the relationships that I have with those guys, the ability to communicate, um, really, uh, the language to be able to say things very short and sweet and them understand what I'm looking for. Um, that comes with time. And, um, there three incredibly valuable members. Um, all of those guys. um you know when I came in on Monday um it was it was obvious to me you know those are three of the four offices that surround me and um so it's a transition you know um for me I have to evolve I have to continue uh to get better and learn and to continue to develop people that are here um and I plan on doing that >> and what makes Adam very ready for that promotion what do you see in him >> well I think in any job and any role that you have when you get promoted it's an adjustment you know taking on responsibility, taking on different tasks. Uh there's going to be responsibility that comes with it. Um you know, I think about when I first became the GM, I go, man, you know, I'm ready for this. I've done I've done college scouting, pro scouting, cap, you know, I'm prepared. And then, um I got my ass kicked a lot, you know, and so I think for any of these roles, um you got to be in them and get the on the job training to be at your best. Um but he's incredibly smart. He's incredibly hardworking. Um he's learned from a lot of great people inside and outside the building and I think um the opportunity won't be too big for him. >> Uh you know Jordan Davis and Jaylen Carr now a longterm I mean got a couple of throws in the secondary that deals just seems like it's getting more expensive on defense just in a management sense of the roster. How do you see that influencing direction forward and on offense? Uh >> well, when you when you talk about it, you know, uh general managers get hired and they'll stand up and they'll have these microphones and they'll say, "Well, how do you want to build your team?" And they say, "We want to draft. We want to develop. We want to resign." And since coach Serriani is here, that's all we've done. You know, um we've we've drafted players. Um we've resigned our players. And when you talk about culture, that's the first thing that comes to mind with culture. If I do well, I'm going to get rewarded. I don't have to go somewhere else to do that. And so that's really a huge part of what we're trying to build. So we're proud about that and that's going to be our first priority as opposed to getting into March and trying to go outside the building. Um the way that these drafts go about it also allows you to structure your contracts in a way that you can continue to keep guys. Now you're going to have to make sacrifices. You saw it in the offseason. You know, we let players go that we care about, that we think are good players, that we think are really good people that fit. Um, but we had to move on because, you know, we have some gamechanging players and people um that are part of this organization and we don't intend to lose. So, I would say to our fans um if you're wearing a jersey with some of those guys on uh with those names on the back, um we fully intend for those guys to be here on the long term. >> You look at the uh the offense that you guys are installing with Shawn and everything. Do you expect like some growing pains as as camp goes along? I mean, you know, ho how is how is that process going to work out? >> I think training camp has growing pains throughout on on both sides of the ball. Whether it's a new coordinator, whether it's an old coordinator, it's the way it goes, right? You you want to make camp challenging. You want to make it hard. Uh you want to make things uh difficult. So, because when they're going through a shared hardship, uh that's when guys come together. Um, and so, you know, there's going to be days where the offense, uh, gets the best of the defense, and there's going to be days where the defense gets best of the offense. Um, I'm not really looking at it in that sense. I'm just looking at it in every day terms of how do we get a little bit better each day? How do we put the work in? And really, it's like, how do we put the work in to get better each day? Um, knowing that there's going to be ups and downs. I think we all want progress to look like this. That's not the reality of progress, right? It's going to feel like that, right? But generally speaking, it's going to go up and then back and then it's go up and go back and that's what you want the the curve to look like. But it it doesn't necessarily mean it's going to feel that way. And so it's important to what it's what's important to do in those situations is just put your head down, control what you can control, and and be faithful in the little things because those will be the the things that end up being big things at the end of the day. >> Last one, folks. the training camp offensive coordinator changed and skill changed. Does the evaluation change now that you enter seven season versus those prior ones? >> No, I think uh we have a st we're very proud that we that we make the job description very clear for each and every one of our players and that we have a standard of what we do at each position. Um, obviously there will be different requirements um and different slightly different job descriptions, but the standard remains the standard and we'll continue to to grade upon that. >> All right, thanks folks. Your guys' reaction to LeBron.
