title: Leonard Williams: "It's Been A Great Battle So Far In Camp" | Seattle Seahawks
text: What's going on there at the end there? A little >> Oh, it's fine. >> What's that? >> What are you guys doing at the other end? >> Oh, yeah. Me and D-Hall just roughhousing a little bit. Uh, I always call him nephew, he call me unk, so got to put him in his place sometimes, you know. >> Old man strength. >> Yes, sir. Yes, sir. He still He keeps challenging me and I got to let him know I still got it. >> How is this for you, training camp? Obviously, you've been through a lot of these now. It's kind of starting another one. Does it still feel the same You know, the same every year or how does it feel? >> Yeah, I mean, my father-in-law, Ronnie Lott, I think maybe year four for me. I asked him for some advice going into training camp and he said treat every year like your rookie year. And I think that's what I'm trying to do now. You know, even though this is my 12th year, I'm coming into it still willing to learn, still willing to like gain information and gain knowledge and just get better as a player like I did when I was younger. >> You had some good off-season adventures with the bike short yourself on social media. How much do you enjoy taking advantage of travel and different things you do in the off-season? >> I mean, it's honestly something I recommend to every rookie I meet. You know, seasons are long. We're away from our family a lot. We're pretty much our home away from home here in the facility and on the grass with each other. So, when I have those opportunities to be around my family and explore my life outside of football, I try to do as much as possible. And I got to take my son on a vacation this off-season and took him to Hawaii. It's awesome. >> I think you said You went to a World Cup game, right? >> Oh, yeah. We went to I was out here most of the off-season training and it was really cool to see like Seattle hosting some of the World Cup events. And I actually went to Belgium versus USA, which is pretty cool. >> Yeah. >> Seeing grass grass at Lumen, does that make you wish they had grass for you guys? >> Yeah, for sure. I think the whole NFL felt that way. You know, we obviously prefer to be on grass. It's just less impact, better on the body and things like that. I understand there's a lot of things that go into having grass on the on the in the stadium that I don't fully understand yet, but you know, if it was up to a player and it just came down to having grass or turf, we would obviously prefer grass. >> Let it players get work on something in the off season and get better. Mike McDonald, he's the same, but what have you seen now in relation to him as the years go on? >> Uh I would just say confidence, uh his trust in himself and his trust in the way he's leading the team and the direction that he's taking the team. Um you know, you you see him finding his bearings a little bit his first season and then he starts to understand like what he wants to do and where he wants to go his second season, which is crazy to say cuz we won a Super Bowl last year and I think this year he knows who he is, he knows the direction of the team, he knows what type of personality and um you know, persona that our team has and I think we're just stacking on that. >> What your approach How have you seen the offense >> Now that you're lined up against them in practice. >> Uh I would just say a lot faster. Um the way they're stacking the ball, like the way they're having pre-snap communication is on another level. Um I feel like oftentimes, you know, I've been a part of great defenses, especially here, where the defense is like the more loud, rowdy ones, where like getting to the ball really fast and stuff like that and our offense is really challenging us uh this camp because they're getting on the ball fast, sometimes catching us out of a stance and things like that. So uh it's been a great battle so far in camp. >> Does it feel like there's more motion pre-snap? >> Oh yeah, there's a lot more motion like fullback motion and tight end motions. Sometimes the tight end is in the fullback position and vice versa. Uh so it's definitely keeping our our defense on our toes and they're switching it up a lot. You know, sometimes they'll motion two tight ends to one side and they'll run the ball that way and sometimes they'll motion two to one side and run the ball the opposite way. So you know, you can't really guess, you got to really just read your keys. >> Does it look familiar to what like you've seen with the 49ers the last few years? >> Yeah, it is pretty similar. Um but I think, you know, they have their own spin on it here for sure. Uh, there's a there's some similarities, but it's obviously a whole different offense. I mean, oftentimes it gives you a read and a tell on like what the offense is doing and what they which direction they want to run. But with them moving and motioning and like changing up which type of runs they have, it's actually keeping us on our toes and like I can't like pre-anticipate plays anymore. So, I have to just like play what's in front of me, which in a way is slow slowing us down a little bit. Like if I know that they're motioning two tight ends to one side and they're going to run the ball that way every time, I could just like widen out as a three technique and just take off and like know the ball's coming that way every time, set the edge from a three technique spot. But now I can't do that because they're switching up the runs, you know? I mean, I think that was amazing. I think it's awesome to get that recognition, especially like later in my career. I feel like I've always trusted and had confidence in the type of player I am. I think, you know, having light around our season and our team from going to the Super Bowl has kind of shed more light on individuals as well. And you know, it's it's an honor to be able to to get that recognition from my peers especially. It's not like a fan voting, it's like something that's from like league executives and coaches and things like that, which means a lot more. So, uh but you know, I'm definitely not letting it get to my head or anything like that. You know, I'm out here competing. There's a bunch of young guys still trying to take my spot. And the offense is, you know, doing a good job challenging us and making me better. >> You you can be a free agent at the end of the season. Is that anything you think about or anything that's on your mind at all? >> Uh, I mean, I try not to think about it, honestly. I've always been that type of guy. You know, I've obviously had a lot of contracts at this point in my career and I've always noticed players that really focus on their contract end up not playing well. They end up having their head in the wrong place and uh I've I've noticed that, you know, when I just focus on being where I'm at, focusing on my on my team and how I can get better individually, uh things always tend to work work themselves out. >> Has the team talked to you at all about that or have they said, "We're just going to table that for after?" Have they mentioned it or brought it up at all? >> I mean, there's been a few conversations, but nothing set in stone. Um you know, I think we're I'm I think we're all focused on, you know, the season starting right now and uh you know, we know that that's towards the end of the season. We have time to figure that out when the time comes. >> Back to the grass. Do you think it's an issue that grass could be collectively bargained? The players would be willing to do that or you're not at or you personally you're not at the point where you're going to make that big of a deal out of it. >> I mean, me personally, I just don't know enough to make a statement on that cuz I know our stadium, you know, we share with like concerts and all type of other things that go on in the stadium that I don't know about. So, I think, you know, without information it's hard for me to make a statement on whether or not we should have grass. I'm just I just know like as a player if we just had to choose grass or turf without any other insights involved like we would obviously choose grass. Uh which is I would say the same thing that uh coach Mike does a good job of relaying a message to the rookies and the whole team is don't worry about the outcome. Um I think right now we have like three, four weeks of training before season starts and now is not the time to think about, you know, getting a sack or making a tackle. It's more about working on your process um and kind of just like being comfortable and playing having fun out there. >> It's usually as much of an issue in training camp in Seattle, but some of these cities can get really hot this time of year. How How you balance that? Do you stop to schedule? >> I mean, it's been beautiful here and that's one of my favorite things about playing here, honestly. It's this beautiful weather all year round. Even during camp, even on the hot days we're kind of we're right on the lake, so we always kind of have a breeze. But it is tough sometimes and I actually enjoy when we do joint camps with other teams because that's when we actually enter some of these more hot areas. Like we're going to Tennessee this year and you know, last two years ago I believe, you know, a few guys cramped up and stuff like that. So it taught us, you know, two years ago that we're going to have to be more prepared going into some of these like more hot places. >> Thanks, coach. Thanks. Thank you, Leonard.

So >> This is like your 10th or 11th training camp whatever it is. Are do they all feel the same or do you do something different every training camp? >> Uh no, they feel pretty similar. I mean the first one is always super different. It was the one that stands out your rookie year and you're just not sure what's you know, you have no idea. You have no idea what's going to be like. But after that first one it's kind of like it's the same kind of thing, you know, I'm I think training camp is what 6 weeks long? Is that right? >> Yeah. >> 6 6 7 weeks. So I'm like a little over a year of training camp NFL training camp for my life, you know. So it's it feels a little bit like Groundhog Day. But you know, I think the battle is not letting it be too much like you don't get too much into that, right? You don't show up great challenge and I'm like there's a great job of making sure that you got to come to work every day, you know, with your lunch pail and hard hat. >> At this point in your career, Cooper, how big of a priority or wish list would it be to play on grass? Is that a big issue? >> I mean that would be sweet. >> Why do you laugh? >> Because I just I don't know. I I just I hear it it would be awesome. I I I've been vocal about it like in the past. there's so many moving parts which which I get. I I just would love I really what we need to do there's a great crew that works out in that that shed out there. It's a great crew that out there that keeps this grass really nice. And just go ask them like hey, what would it take? Like what is it like what is it really like what would it look like? Yeah, because I don't know the grassology of all that stuff, right? Like, you got soccer teams playing on it. You got a lot of stuff happening. You got events being hosted. I would like to think with all the resources of the NFL that we can make that happen. But, yeah, there's there's there's people that can make that happen. we just going to keep, you know, as players keep voicing what we what we want and what we think is important, but um you know, eventually I do think uh it'll get done. >> How much do you notice your body after the first game versus >> No, it makes a huge difference. And I and I know all the metrics and all the data that says you know, whatever the injury rates of this, but like I don't know. I mean I know how I feel. I think you ask a lot of players would say the same thing, like whether you whether the injury rates change or not, I know how my body feels after playing on turf um versus grass. You can ask the coaches how their backs feel after standing on on turf versus grass, right? So, like that's just that's a Now, they've got coaches have a lot of other issues. So, but like they but I it does make a difference. >> Have you ever played on grass since you left the Raiders? >> Um in terms of well, the Coliseum. >> Oh, yeah, the Coliseum. >> The Coliseum for a few years there. And you know, there there's college I mean, that's it's still in California, but you know, there's colleges were playing on that um quite a bit. I'm sure they had events and things like that. So, it's possible. I know it's possible. It's just uh you know, it's a conversation that needs to continue. >> With all the movement towards multiple tight ends, multiple backs, just heavier personnel, fewer receivers on the field, how do you keep from tipping what plays you're doing depending on which receivers are out on the field? >> Mhm. Well, I think that's where, you know, as receivers we need to do a good job of making sure we can be, you know, you know, multi-faceted in terms of what we're what we're what we do. We can't be we can't get stuck in this place where we only do one thing. And it's also on the, you know, our our play callers and and our offensive coaches to make sure that we're not, you know, creating tendencies in that way as well cuz um you know, defenses and coaches there's not the amount of time that's spent in looking for tendencies and things like any edge. Um this game's too hard to be, you know, fighting uphill. You can't be fighting uphill battles. So, um you know, that's something that we need to be aware of and need to make sure that we're taking into account. And as receivers we need to make sure that we're doing everything we can. When we're asked to block, we got block. When we're asked to go down the field, we go down the field and we we make effective plays down there and um you know, and all the things in between with that. So, um that that's uh we got to go hand in hand with us doing our job and the coaches doing a great job putting us in those positions. Awesome. Thank you guys. Thank you. >> Thanks, Sam.

title: Cam Ward on Year Two, Third Downs & His Growth | Titans Press Conference
text: What was that process and and trying to build chemistry, camaraderie, and all that? >> Uh it was real good just for us to you know, be with each other again um after we weren't for about 3 weeks. Uh for us to continue working on our timing from the receivers to uh the running backs that was back down here then the tight ends. Um but it was good for us a good camaraderie, you know, have some bonding then you know, got some good quality work in. >> Yeah, and how was it being back out there with everyone after being out for the last 40 days? >> Uh it's finally it's finally for real now. Um instead of you know, just being in OTAs and working on specific stuff, you finally get to you know, have a have a real meaning behind it. Got a preseason game coming up soon then a real game after that. Um but it but it's exciting to have everybody back out here healthy um then run around full speed. >> different things feel for you now compared to this time last year? >> Uh way different uh from system to to players to you know, just my knowledge of you know, being an NFL quarterback. Uh it's been way better. Um I think the the staff that we hired post thoughts of the balls has really been helpful for you know, the players on what we want to do and you know, making it easy for us so we can play fast. Uh so you know, it's going to be a exciting time exciting trip you know, in a in a good season. >> What do you think will help you most in year two play better against pressure? >> Um I just think having a clock in my head each and every play. Um you know, helping out the old line getting the ball out you know, and thinking the same as Daboll. Uh I think that's going to help me out you know, the most in year two then you know, when it's time for Tannehill for me to make an exciting play you know, that's where you know, I'll come in and do my job. >> Sean talked about two minute, red zone, and third down being the most important part of quarterback and you said third down as well. Can you just kind of get into like why that specifically is so much more elevated above the other parts of what you're asked to do? >> Um because those are downs that when you look at on film those are downs that can win or lose you a game. Uh those are downs that quarterbacks get paid the most to be successful at a high rate on those downs. Um and then that's where you know, it has to click for you, you know. Uh if it doesn't click on first down, you got to make sure it click on second and third down. So, you know, just got to have a awareness of situation of football and knowing, you know, which two-minute drill it is, whether it's in the half or in the game, and what you need then, you know, executing with your teammates at a high level. >> You had mentioned working with Daboll, that's something that you've really come to realize the third down importance. What was different from before to now? Just like what like what led to that revelation? >> Uh I just think the the system. Um it's it's a it's a young guy system. Uh he gives us a lot of free lanes, not only myself but the receivers, to do as we feel space-wise. Um and I just think, you know, he's putting us, you know, just schematically in the best situations, looking at things the defense does, um to get leverage for the wideouts to, you know, make sure I don't have to move as much in the pocket to help the O-line out by getting the ball off faster. Um so, I just think he's just making me a better football player each and every day. >> Daniel, you had two false starts on the first two plays of the first series. Did you have to say anything to your guys to kind of kick them into gear or what what was kind of your response to that? >> Uh of course. Um I mean, it's just a a operation standpoint that we can't have. Um it was a, you know, a sin by me um by not, you know, communicating everything to them. Uh so, that's something that, you know, I got to get better at. Uh wasn't on O-line, wasn't on receivers. So, you know, I just got to be better relaying everything. Um but, you know, I can't start practice like that, you know, we can't do that as a group. But, you know, we learn from it. And we have a better place uh down in this stretch, but we got to start better. >> Daniel, you said in the Netflix documentary you thought your rookie season was all right. You the team went 3 and 14. You had the lowest QBR amongst qualified passers in the NFL. So, what exactly were you using to define all right? >> Uh good or bad? Um each game we had good plays, each game we had bad plays, but it's limited it. Um over the course of the year I got better at things that I wanted to get better in. Um but I really think that whole year, you know, helped shape me and a lot of other rookies to to that football is the same. Um, it got to be about the players. Um, it's got to be what the players, you know, are comfortable with, what the players are good at doing, what got us got us to this point. Um, and I think that's been the the best part of being a part of that is I was able to learn throughout the process. Um, even in now. >> You mentioned somewhat of how you run your routes for receivers, how you imagine the freedom that those receivers have. How much more does that emphasize you guys getting on the same page? What are you able to do to make sure like when they have that freedom, you know what they're going to do? >> Uh, biggest thing is watching film. Um, all of them watching film with me seeing my point of view, what I see from safeties, corners, but the biggest thing is angles and how they have to, you know, have good body demeanor across the middle of the field, wrapping backers, sitting verse zone spies verse the nickels, um, whoever it is in the area. Um, and they're they're all doing a great job, honestly. We haven't We had no miscommunications this whole time with that. Um, so I think the the more we continue to to hold each other accountable, watch more film together, um, I think it's going to end up paying dividends. >> of that do you feel has sprouted from the time you guys spent together in Miami? >> Uh, a lot. Um, but it's something that we started, you know, when when we were here at OTAs. Um, and then working out with them in the off season was really of time and then, you know, all of our space space plays, imagining, you know, people in these areas. Um, cuz a lot of times, you know, you you have to imagine it because, you know, as the season get shorter, I mean it gets longer, you know, the reps go down, so you got to try to, you know, really rely on the film and imagine things in your head and how you think it's going to play out. Then you also got to react to how things play out in the game. >> Jam, there's a lot that's different in Miami right now. New staff, new logo, jerseys, all that. How different are you today than you were this day last year? >> Uh, I'm the same person. Um, I think I've become a better football player. Uh, I think that's been the biggest thing that I've changed. Um but I'm the same person. Uh keep the same routine. Uh a lot of stuff has helped me get to this point. So, you know, there's there's no big thing to change. But I say the biggest thing, you know, that changed is just, you know, the the approach that I see the game. And that's something that, you know, Daboll has emphasized me. Um it's seeing the game, you know, not only through my eyes, but through the O-line and the receivers' eyes as well. >> So, how did you become a better football player? >> Uh the I'll I'll say the the biggest the biggest thing is situational. Um and that's watching with Daboll. And it's the It's not the the play or the concept. It's the the why he's calling the play, the the time on the clock, how the game is going, whether, you know, we're starting off good, whether everything is open, or if we're starting out bad, or I need to slowly get us into this game, whether it's quick game, running the ball, um everything. So, I just think situationally, and you know, awareness of everyone else's position, you know, has been my biggest change. >> So, as one of the leaders now, how how do you accept How do you set the tone? How do you be intentional about doing >> Make plays on the football field. That's what our job is to do is make plays. So, gain respect of your teammates every time you step on the field. Um and really just be here and and continue to be the same person each every day. >> Is there a moment or is there a type of play that kind of helped you key in on understanding that you are more aware that you're seeing the game differently? Can you just kind of give an example of how you are seeing it differently? >> Uh it's every day. Um I'll say the the the biggest thing is the the red zone situation for today. Um starting off in the high red on the 20. Um can force the corner if I really want to, but I can make it second and three, which I did today to Gunner. Um and it's and it's a lot of of And I think I got better at it better at it last year is know who I'm playing up front. Um whether we got O-linemen down or not, um whether we they run the type of game. So, helping them out, um and not really thinking more of, you know, try to put the ball where I know it's supposed to go versus certain coverage. Really just to react in the space and putting the ball, you know, at 2 yards and let them do the rest. >> How'd you judge that red zone period? Couple touchdowns, couple throwaways, overall? >> Uh, not our best. Um, we're trying to score every play. Uh, we had some good plays with it. Uh, all three groups. Um, but you know, our mindset is to score the ball every chance we get, you know, we didn't do that enough. Uh, we scored enough points to possibly win a game, you know, in that situation, but you know, we for sure got to be better. I still have to be more on time on on quicker routes in certain situations. Um, but you know, it's the first day of of camp, you know, I'm looking to be better tomorrow. >> The two pressure plays, no real chance to make anything out of? >> Uh, no, I think that's a that's a real viable play for us to work on our scramble drill. Um, seeing where I want them to go, the angle I want them to do. Um, and then at the end of the day, just me being smart and if it's not there, throwing it away. >> What's the vibe like in the quarterback room? You got four different guys at very different places in their careers, all here. >> Uh, it's real hot. Um, we're all competing each and every day. Um, but we all, you know, have one common goal. Um, and I think the the best thing about that quarterback room that we have here is that, you know, everybody wants to be great. Everybody wants to be starters, so we're constantly pushing each and every one of us. Um, and at the end of the day, you know, we're all supportive. Um, and you know, as we get to, you know, the preseason games, we're all going to play, get to the to the joint practices, we'll all get reps, you know, we just got to continue to, you know, take little things from each other. Uh, cuz each and every one of us get different reps in different coverages to the reps. So, it's learning off each other, learning where the ball should go versus where it could actually go. Um, and then just, you know, being good teammates to each other. >> What do you like more? >> In the in the Netflix documentary, you didn't walk back the we asked >> No, that Netflix documentary, love that. >> You walked back the we asked comments from week four saying, "Hey, I'm not going to sugarcoat things. I said what I said." And then you said that you played all right. So, is that kind of the idea that the team was ass and that you were all right or were you part of the way the team was ass? >> What's your What's your name? >> Jared. >> That's a good question, though. >> Thank you. >> No, it's Like I said, um I'm up front. They know who I am. The The building knows how I am. Uh you guys puff. Um but it's a There's a point to where like we were so much better than what we put on the field. Um and I'll specifically talk about offense and we early in the year the defense did everything they could to keep us in the games last year. We didn't do our job offensively. Um so, you know, I think after that was made, you know, it really made us lock in even more. Um cuz at the end of the day it's a production-based business, you know, if we're not producing, next man up. Um and you know, I think we all handled it the right way. They know I'd say it again if I had to. Um we just going to keep one step forward looking ready this year. >> With the height With the heightened importance on third down, what does that those situations require from you to be successful as opposed to like first or second down? Like why is Like from a mentality standpoint or or how you're operating, how is it different from third down? >> Uh cuz third down's potentially the last play. Uh last play of the drive, could be the last play of the game, uh depending where we at in the game. Um and that's where I have to be on high alert for whether it's cover zero answers, blitz packages, flipping the protection, um getting checking plays if I really want to or if it's something I see on film certain situations. Um and then scramble drill is something that's real live on third down. Um so, it it's where I have to be on point, O-line, and receivers because third down can bail us out on first and second down. Um the goal is to potentially keep the chains moving. We want to stay in the green. Uh it's playing from, you know, first and 10 to second and four and third and one. Those Those where we want to stay at as an offense. Um and I think the more we do that, you know, we can put ourselves in less third and longs like we did last year. Um and just have a productive year. >> When all have mentioned you guys did some off-the-field things in Miami to get that chemistry together. What what were some of the things you did? Is that something that you put together like that itinerary? And and how can you benefit on the field from those off-the-field moments? >> Um chilling, being in Miami. Uh the best thing is getting on the boat. Looking uh I'm a big water guy. I love looking at water. I ain't getting in the water. Um but I like looking at it, seeing the blue water. Um just feeling the breeze cuz honestly you just get offshore, get away from everything. Um and then just hanging around the house. Um cooking. Belly cooked for us. Um and really >> you say? >> Belly. >> Okay. >> Yeah, he cooked for us. Um really just spending time with each other uh outside of football. Um but we going to be with each other from now to February. Um and so you know, our job is to to form that bond, you know, however we want to do it. Um but with us like there's really no itinerary. Like we come in here on this day, I'm telling you what we doing in the morning and the rest of the day we doing whatever somebody want to do. We kicking it. We make last-minute plans cuz that's how we live our life day by day. We got a schedule for football, but other than that, I mean, all of us we just go home and chill. So, you know, when we get a chance to get away from it, whatever pop up on somebody head, we all doing it together. >> Cam, last time last year you talked about the importance of having coaching then you didn't get that How do you kind of look back on that? Do you feel like that set you back any in your development the fact that you haven't had You you've had a lot of different voices in a short time already. >> Um yeah, uh but I I had a lot of good voices as well. Every coach that I've had has been in successful places. Um even they're not here no more, they're still in successful places. They're still part of the the NFL. Um but I think the the biggest thing that I've always had my whole career was, you know, back and forth with the play caller, back and forth with the OC or the quarterback coach, um which I have now. Um and that's the that's the big thing for a quarterback is you know if the if the system's not fit for the quarterback, the quarterback's not going to be able to show everything he can do. And that's something that you know that's the trust that the play caller has to have with the quarterback. And that's something that we got to build even off the field as well. But coach Day say even Kade in there they they've been real good their understanding of what I see it on the field with what Hendon will with what Mitch sees on the field. And they they all put us in the best situations whoever on the field to to you know have us in the right mindset confident wise to get us in the play calls that we like. >> Just one last one. >> Yeah. Wan'Dale was complimentary of you. Also mentioned how you felt your chemistry between you two has grown obviously the last throughout the off season. How would you describe your chemistry with Wan'Dale up until this point even though it's still early on? >> Uh that's my guy. Ever since the first day when he came in when he signed first day we did metal whatever he's first one in my house. We he he know he really got a key to my house. He can walk in at any time. So I mean him him being there and him showing the the attitude that he brings each and every day that's all I can ask for a slot receiver. He's the same person who comes in the building. He he works hard. He's always the you know the when I call the a meeting when I call you know when we throwing you know he always there. He don't make excuses. He he runs routes and they they know I run them to the dirt too. And so you know he don't he run the routes he want the ball for a reason cuz they know if you're not doing what I want I'm not going to throw you the ball. And they all see that he sees that the most especially him being in the league. He's going to have a real special year.

title: Jeffery Simmons, Wan'Dale Robinson & John Franklin-Myers on Day 1 of Titans Camp
text: Talk to everybody. >> All right. All right. >> Coach was talking before practice about how for you and all these guys adjusting to an attack style defense versus a read style defense is going to be an adjustment. How much do you feel like you've already adjusted and what are the specific things you're having to work on? >> Um I mean when you in the meeting rooms, I mean that's what they preaching it. Um and since I met White Cotton and Solly training with JFM, training with guys like Quinnin your get-off is the most important thing. Um your first two steps you have to really key in on your first two steps. And that's the defense. You once you get your first two your first two steps in the ground is go play football. Um we got a rule in our room and you know, it's stay between the guardrail. However I get home, that's how I get home. After them first two steps and I stay on my track, that that's what it's about. I mean this defense I mean everybody know the solid defense. Um you know, he's been in multiple places from the Jets to San Fran. You know you going to know where we at. 100% of the time. So it's a it's up to us and you know, it was a great um story that coach White Cotton gave yesterday and talked about Tiger Woods making putts. Um I think he had over thousand and some putts from 3 yards out 3 feet out 3 feet out. So and he made what? Um 99% I think it's like 99% of them putts. So it's like it's up to us to be consistent in what we going to be doing because they ain't going to know where we at and like I said, my first two steps and staying on my track is the main um most important thing in the defense, but I would say man, I mean getting the coaching from the meeting room and taking to the field, I mean still the game of football. Um I think you get the coaching, you line up and go play football and I think that's sometime we can forget when we talk about a read defense and attack defense, you still got to line up and go play football. >> Solly said that guys making this transition that you're making tend to fall over early. Have Have you felt that different gravity, let's say? >> I mean this is how this this I like when I left here, I knew what to expect. I knew what type of defense that I'm coming back to play and get ready for this training camp. So, yeah, when I'm working on my get-off and my first two steps with my training off-season, yeah, I'm like, "Oh man, I'm going to feel it." But, it's I guess I've been getting off the football, getting out of the three-point stance, doing the get-off since I've been playing D-line since eighth grade. Um I saw I mean, I've been doing I It's just a different mindset. I wouldn't even say a different mindset, it's just faster. Everything in in this defense, in this style of play, it's fast and violent. We hear it, we talk about it, and that's what this this white cotton, the command and the and the individual, you guys see it, y'all over there. Um you know, it's from top down. That's what they they preaching in the building, and it's up to us to hold that standard up, and that's continue to get off the ball, get off the ball. So, I like I said, it's nothing new. Um even with last year's defense, it's still get off the rock. So, I can say it's just with it it's just a couple of uh different tweaks. >> Year eight for you, is that hard to believe? And then what kind of what's the mindset for you as you head into another one? >> I mean, it's off-season, I'm like, "Geez, time flies." But, you know, just seven year eight years ago I was a rookie, you know, coming into this league, just you know, um grateful to be have this opportunity, and still I still feel that each and every day. Um I don't I don't wake up and be like, "Man, I got to go to work." You know, I still get this opportunity and the joy to be able to come into this building and play the game that I love, that I fell in love with at the age five. So, um it's a blessing. I I'm grateful to be able to still be able to put on cleats and run onto that field. So, it's not a surprise, it's not a like year eight, it's it's it's still that joy to be able to training camp tomorrow. Um you It's like reporting to training camp on my birthday, I'm like, a couple years ago I wouldn't be like, "Man, in college I'd like, that's not ideal to go to camp on my birthday." But, to be able to walk into a building um that, you know, I'm grateful, the gratitude to be able to play game. Um I'm I'm blessed and I'm attacking this like year one. Um you know, it's it's no different mindset for me to where, you know, oh, it's new coaches and stuff. It's it's be the best version I could be to help this football team succeed. >> Have you even talked to you since you signed your new deal? How big of a moment was that for you and your family? And also how crucial getting that done ahead of the season? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, I want to say it was probably after a week or two after the draft the deal been, you know, my agent and, you know, the front office been working Bargainze and them. And that's you know, one of the things that I reminded uh Todd that I didn't want it to be messing. It's like when I talked to you guys, I mean, normally when guys getting deals done as you see is it's all over social media getting messy. I mean, like kind of my second deal, it's kind of got in the media a little bit. And I kind of didn't like that um you know, doing that process. And so my thing was I just wanted everything to be smooth because like I said, this organization um since I walked into this building been nothing but good to me. Um it's Amy, you know, the front office um with, you know, Chad and them coming in. I mean, when Chad was here last year then you got >> [snorts] >> um Bargainze this year. Um the relationship that I'm continuing to try to build with Bargainze um this whole off season when he first got in. That's that's what it's about. And um that was my mindset is how can I build a relationship with these guys? Um not just through the game of football. Just off the field, you know, trying to learn their family and things of that nature. So, um it it's I want to say it was so much like, "Todd, we got to get this deal done um doing the um before the season." But it's also one of the things to where um we was on the same page. We both knew um after the season what was going um probably happen, you know, with the contract. Um and then I and that's go back to me saying I'm just grateful. I'm grateful to be in a place to where, you know, I'm still valued. Um you know, I'm grateful to be able to still go out there and help um to help this defense and help this team with my leadership and my play. So, I can say I'm grateful. Um And one of the things I was sitting on the couch outside and I get the call from Todd and I still he still pissed me off by that cuz he was like I got some good news and bad news. He said we didn't hit a grand a home run, we hit a grand slam. So, it's one of the things I'm like Todd, you can't do that man. But, I guess I'm I'm grateful and I'm you know I'm blessed to still be here and hopefully we can get this team back to winning football. >> July 17th you said that you wanted to be in the best shape of your life. How are you feeling physically going into this season? >> I feel great. I feel great I don't I was probably 10 from last season. I I'm in in in shape. I'm you know being able to I mean you even I'm not not in shape, you going to get in shape at practice. I mean with wide cutting he wanted us to run a three strike. Whatever the ball is we got to run three strikes. You see you got to see how we work in individual. But, I did come into this this camp with that mindset of you know is get off get off and get out of the stack. Get to the ball. So, my goal wasn't necessary to just lose more weight. It was just how can I get in better shape with the conditioning things of that nature. I guess in my diet nothing none of that changed cuz I I had a great plan last off season coming to the season and I just stuck with that. So, I guess I do feel great physically and mentally. You know that's one of the things that you know I've been really really focused on more especially with personal things that going on in my life and family. I think sometimes we forget that. Especially as player we talk about mental health. Our our I would say probably 85% of this football game is mental. Maybe 90, you know some guys think more. But, when you have them you you your mental straight and everything else will fall in place. So, I would say I didn't just focus on my physical being in shape. It was a lot of to do with my mental as well. So, >> Have you had a talk with Sally yet about the reps and them being more than four to five reps? >> Nah, I I'm trusting the process on that. I It's not one of the things to where I'm focused on that right now especially in training camp. This not one of the things to where I'm like, you know, hey coach, what do you I know you said that in the media about the four plays and get off the field. You know, the way we play, the way we practice, hell, I might not even want to do four over four plays in a row because it's the standard and the expectation that they expect out of us on the D-line. So, I mean, I had three plays today and it's like three plays back-to-back and I'm like, all right, it's just the first day. So, to to be focused on how many plays I'm going to do in a row at this point right now, I don't think that's my focus. Eventually we get there. Um, but I said it's one of the trusting the process and I said it with this style of defense, he may be right. So, we'll see. >> the way it went today? It seemed like he let you go. >> Uh, I mean, I mean, it's football. I guess I told the guys, we know the rules, we know it's still the this acclimation period to where it's so much we could do, can't really have so much contact. DBs can't really jump for the ball. We don't We trying to take care of each other. So, it's I mean, it's still just great to get out there with all the guys, you know, Jay F.E.M., you know, Jermaine, all the new guys to be able to get these reps, mental reps. It's a lot of mental reps even when they're not full speed. So, um, it was I felt great to be able to just get out there with everybody. Couldn't do it during mini camp, of course, but today shows like, you know, we got a lot lot of work to do, but, you know, it's a great start. >> Coach Vrabel has talked a lot about building a culture and, you know, getting things, laying a foundation. You've been here when it's good, been here when it's bad. What's the key to building a culture? >> I mean, he talk about it each and every day. You know, we got our team rules, we got um, everybody have their offense have their own philosophy, defense have their own philosophy. But as a team is is how close we can get how and I mean, we got it all over the building, you know, owning it. I'm just It's one of the things we talk about, not just owning what you're doing on the football field, but owning how you take care of your body, own all the little small details. And when we we talking about the foundation, it's it's not so much of, hey guys, we we got a meeting at 8:00 and you walk in at 7:59. We we had talked about the small things of being early. That's one one of the team rules is, you know, is is all the small things that we sometimes don't think about, especially, you know, outside of the building or as young guys you'd be like, "Man, he talking about be early. That's mean, you know, 5 or 10 minutes early." But it's just a small thing that we talking about to help win like that winning tradition and that winning mindset, I should say. So, um I mean, he he stressing in in in the team meeting. He talking about it. Um the fast and violence, like that's that's what we going to live on. Um not just on defense, it's it's offense. How fast can we play? How violent can we play? So, and it's it's not just up to Sal you know, Sal Sal get out here and talk to you guys and he talk to the team, but it's the guys on the football field. He can't get out there and play fast. He can't get out there and go smack somebody no more. So, I think it's up to us as leaders and as team as our to push up push each other as teammates to hold up um our end of the bargain. >> down and under pressure. How much is it a side effect of your job to help him get better at >> I mean, we going we [clears throat] as a defense, that's what we doing at practice regardless. I mean, not just for third down. We got to be good on first and second down to get to third down. So, to be able to I'm sure Sal when especially once we get deep in the playbook, he going to throw different things at Cam, but you know, that's that's the side their offense is on. You know, I don't focus on that. We focus on how can we get better on the defense? Um with that being said, you know, the way we rush up front, that's going to help the O line get better. Um if the all O line not playing their best football, Cam won't play his best football. So, our job is to get the offensive line better to make sure that they can protect for Cam. And Cam going to be Cam. We not worried about Cam. Um you know, with you know, third down and all that, we got to get better up front. Um cuz I I'm big on the trenches lead the team. We the this team is going to be led up front from offense offense line and defense line. So, >> Judge, you talked about how important it is to get back to winning. What has you encouraged this training camp and whether it's the new staff, personnel around you in the defense, what has you encouraged that this team can do that this >> I mean, this is this We talk about the culture. I mean, it's a new culture. I mean, from the logo, from the uniforms to coaching staff, you know, that's that's that's the excitement when you walk into the building. I mean, I've been here 8 years now. I mean, each and every year has been different. Um you know, everyone every coaching staff not the same. There's no sense of me saying trying to compare this coach to variable or this coach to Cali house is is when you walk into the building, how can you buy into what coach Saleh is talking about? How can we myself spread the message to the team and we live by and um when I walk into this building, I'm excited. I'm excited to be able to come to work. I'm excited to be able to be the leader I am to help this team get back to where we need to be and that's like I say, keep spreading the message. We talk to We talk about it like we got to continue to spread what Cali I mean what Saleh talking about in the meeting room. We got to come out here and in in all meeting rooms to talk about, "Hey, this is what he talked about on third down, first and second down." So, just them type of things with to where as as the guys in the locker room, it's up to us. It's up to us to be able to buy in. Um I mean, that's that's pretty much what it going to be. How can we buy into his message, his style of play, offense, defense, special teams. >> We're going to talk to JFM here in a second. What do you expect him to show on the field this year and to add to the defense? >> Exactly what he's been showing his last couple this in his career. Um a guy who's been, you know, um a dog. Um I was excited as hell when I heard we got an opportunity to sign him and when he ended up signing him, I'm like, "Let's do it." Um to be able to play get I mean, I when he was a Jet, we played against him and last year um I watched a lot of his tape. He's a he's a dog. He's a hell of a player. Um, especially when he come in on third down inside rushing inside next to me. I expected him to go win. If I'm getting a side, I know he going to get a one-on-one. I expect him to go win. And we we have these conversations. We training in Dallas. And it's vice versa. If I got the one-on-one, he expect me to win. So, just that duo inside, um, I'm happy to have that. I'm happy to have someone next to me that I know that can win the one-on-ones and not just on third down, but first and second down. Um, he on the edge or wherever he lined up. I'm I'm excited to play next to him. >> How helpful was that with uh some new faces and working with the new quarterback? >> Yeah, it was. Um, but it was really good for all the guys to get together, you know, um, being able to throw with each other, just kind of get on the same page with a lot of different things. And then, um, just being able to be around each other. I mean, obviously the closer that we feel like we are, um, the better football team we'll be. >> That off-the-field connection. Can you just kind of open up about how you guys were able to develop? Like, what were some of the things that you did off the field to >> I mean, we were swimming. Um, we were hanging out at the pool. Um, just doing a lot of different things. Just going out shopping. Just trying to be be with each other. So, um, just felt like anything that we could do that we were around each other and, um, building that camaraderie then everything was going to work out. >> How much do you feel like your connection with Cam kind of improved? What What do you What do you think you started when you first got here and how much did that improve up until now? >> Definitely when we first got here it was a little like just a lot of the routes that our runner option routes and, um, just being on the same page with a lot of everything. But towards the end of the spring we really got on the same page and started clicking. Um, and then that just grew throughout this whole summer just throwing, um, weeks at a time and being good with that. So. >> Emphasis on long corners here, obviously. Flott and Taylor have have some good height going too. What What's that mean for your game? What do you think it means for those guys against the league? >> Um, I mean, I think it's good to have long corners like that. I mean, obviously you have big guys on her all around the NFL that play on the outside and um, for me sometimes I like playing against bigger corners. I don't think they move as well as I do. Um, especially whenever they move in the inside, but those guys that are on the outside, they they they do their job. I've played against Lavonte for quite a while and I played against Slot too and they they both know how to hold their own. >> Rondale, want to ask about your decision to switch to number four. How much Rondale meant to you and and how important it was for you to make that make that statement? >> Yeah, I mean, um, so I met Rondale when I was like a sophomore in high school. We started training together in Louisville. Um, you know, stayed connected all the way through college and through the NFL and um, obviously the news that whenever that broke, I was just kind of like, I don't know what exactly I could do and um, then once [clears throat] I signed here and I saw the number four was open and I was like, I definitely got to get in that so that way um, somewhat I can honor him and um, just kind of a remembrance every time I step out there on the field with that number on like, hey, there's a little bit more little something bigger up there that's watching me too, so. >> Many people don't think of it this way, but one of the things Kyler's working on certainly third down and how he plays against uh, pass rush. How much can you be a solution for him in in the pass rush? >> Um, I mean, that's where that's where I like to think I make a lot of my money's on third down, so um, just being able to always be open and um, catch anything and everything and um, at the end of the day like I said, just get open and be be a valuable target for him. >> Seems like you've got your own special route tree in practice that nobody else has. Was that just you and Dave's coming up with it together? How how did that come to pass? >> That's been five years in the making, so yeah, I've been basically like that since my rookie year, just kind of always moving around, running a lot of different things that um, not everybody kind of gets to run, so um, I've always liked it that way too, so just always making sure that we're on the same page with Kyler though. >> Do you have your own special terminology for your own routes? >> No, we don't have any like special terms. Everybody calls them the same thing, just everybody might not get to run them, so. >> [laughter] >> Rondale, how important is it for you to have your college quarterback on the same NFL team as you? >> I mean, it's it's very nice, obviously. wish we could have had it earlier, but um I mean, it's good to, you know, just have a face here, a familiar face that I've already been around, and um can talk to anything about Nashville or anything like that. I can always ask him any type of questions like that, so it's been good. >> His future's kind of unknown at this stage. Have you talked with him about that? And and how do you maybe advise a guy how to handle stuff like that? >> Um not too much. I mean, you know, whenever we're out here, we're just trying to talk about ball, and um just what's going on with our offense. And if he has any questions with what's going on, I try to help him. Obviously, you know, being in this offense for a couple years, I can even help some of the quarterbacks out, and so um any questions anybody has, I always try to help. >> I'm sure watching film, you've seen how Cam was able to extend plays. So, you get into that scramble drill. How are you guys been able to get on the same page where you know where he wants you to go when he's going out of the >> A lot of that's just watching it after, and whenever he's kind of moving around and doing certain things, and it's just kind of like, "Hey, if you want to go here, you can go there, and I'll still get the ball to you." Um and I'm like, "All right, what if I do this and go right here?" And just kind of always just communicating and just making sure we're on the same page, and um big plays will happen from there. >> You obviously got a taste of it in the spring, but just kind of speak to what type of leader Cam is kind of growing into. >> I mean, he's going to shoot you straight. Uh he's not going to sugarcoat anything, and um wants the best out of everybody, and um feels like everybody got to got to come along and bring their best. So, um we all do that, and we feel like we're going to be a good football team. >> What's a What's a harsh critique from Cam like? >> Catch the damn ball. [gasps] >> But if he does throw a bad pass, I'll say, "Throw a better ball." >> Couple more? Everyone good? >> Thank you. >> Thank you, everyone. >> Thank you all. >> I appreciate it. >> in here, so good. >> It's a gorgeous day. >> What do you think about Jeff, just walked off here, just kind of getting to know him a little bit better, and and what kind of teammate you What do you he's going to be? >> I mean, I think, shoot, this is this is Jeff's time. I mean, we all seen him last year. We seen him his whole career and we understand the player he is. We understand that each and every day he's going to push the team. He's going to push himself to be the best version and and so you can only appreciate it. I mean, I trained with him in the off season. See the work he puts in. He pushes me. We talk mess all day, every day and and I love it. I mean, you talk about somebody that shows up to work and I mean, he just challenges everybody to be their best version. Again, you can't do nothing but appreciate it. He going to have a great year. >> He just said some nice things about you. How formidable of a duo do you expect to be with >> Yeah, I mean, obviously the goal is to be the best in the league and that's the best defensive tackle in the league. That's somebody I get to learn from. I get to see. I get to watch his craft, how he goes about his business in the meeting room, on the field, what he does extra and I see it and I understand why he's the best and so all I can do is do my part and you know, again, he said it best, you know, he's going to get the slide early and and my job is to win these one-on-ones and that's what I do. I do I pride myself on it. We talk about it all the time. We understand that there's going to be a point in time where they start sliding to me and and we already know he's going to win his one-on-one. So, again, the expectation is through the roof and we're going to hold each other to that standard. >> within the AFC Championship game. What attracted you to a team that's in the middle of a rebuild? >> Yeah, I mean, you know, rebuild, no nobody we're all zero and zero and so you understand that you know, it's about the pieces in place. You got the right head coach. You got the right teammates here, the right coaching staff and ultimately, shoot, we have a chance to win a Super Bowl and the goal is to win. The goal is to compete. We get better each and every day and so I don't I don't you know, I don't care about no what is it rebuild? You know, ain't no rebuild. This is the NFL. So, each and every year everybody has the same chance. Everybody's zero zero to start the season. It's about the work you put in. >> You were outside a great deal today. How do you think that all sorts itself out? Is it a week-to-week thing based on matchups or how does it factor in? And do you What do you consider yourself? >> I consider myself a football player. Truthfully, I mean, I've done it all. I do it all and again, my my standard is through the roof and so whether you put me inside, outside, nose guard, DN, DT, I don't care. I'm a I want to go out there. I want to win one-on-ones and I want to play the most physical brand of football I can and so maybe it is matchup based, but truthfully, I played outside at the Jets, played inside on passing downs and you know, I got a chance to go to Denver, played inside a little bit more on run downs. Got comfortable with it. Got I'm comfortable playing outside and so again, um line me up and physicality is going to be there, effort is going to be there and play making it has to be there. >> We see the intensity you guys practice with during Indy and then how it transfers to to team. Is that Is that unique? Not saying it's better than what you've seen, but is that unique and how much does that kind of challenge you to to go through those reps with that same intensity? >> Yeah, I mean, it is very unique. Again, I was on a just blessed to be a part of great defenses in my career. Should a few of them being with this coaching staff and so I understood the expectation, I understood the standard. We lived up to that at the Jets. Go list to bring that here and you see it. You see the intensity in which we go and you know, as it does, it just kind of is just everybody just kind of does it and you realize that as you see Jeff running 30 yards to the ball, now the youngest guy in the room is like, man, Jeff Jeff is doing it, you know, JFM is doing it and so this is the standard and and we can't accept anything less. We have to be the leaders of this team. The team runs through us. We understand that. It's stated and and it's understood. So, the team goes as we go. Again, it starts with effort, it starts with physicality, and the rest of it is going to take care of itself. >> Anything else? >> Is is Saleh different in any ways since the time in New York or is this essentially the same guy you knew 4-5 years ago? >> I think Saleh Saleh has, you know, the to me you look back and self-reflection is is the best thing in life and in football and so he, you know, certain things and I don't want to go into specifics, but he he has self-reflected, he's understood that there's there is some mistakes that you make and there's some things that you do well, but ultimately I think Saleh knew that we were on the right path and you know, you see some similarities, but the intensity, the physicality, the effort, the message has to be the same because there's one way to play football and so the the name of the game is to go out there and and mess somebody up and so we understand that. The message is that and so when it's time to play football, X's and O's take care of themselves, but man, it's about the players, it's about, you know, no matter what they put us in, we got to make them right. We are we're the ones playing and so we understand that and again, you know, in due time you're going to see it. >> Is it weird at all seeing Jarmaine, seeing Solomon, seeing Saleh, seeing Mike Cotton, all just different place, same people? >> Yeah, it is a little weird, it took some getting used to, but you know, it's one thing to go go into school and be the new kid in school and you know, you you got to go learn, meet new friends and everything. It's another thing to show up to school and and you know, you got friends, you know, it's just it's just like you didn't didn't Sorry, you didn't leave off and so I love it. These guys are some of my best friends, Jake Martin, Saleh, Tony Adams, Jarmaine. I mean, I seen Jarmaine from rookie all the way to now, the man he is, the father, the husband. I mean, again, I can do nothing but appreciate it. I'm here for him and we understand again, the standard It the standard. We hold each other to that standard and um man, it's time. >> Thanks, John. >> Appreciate you.

title: Robert Saleh Talks Cam Ward, Calvin Ridley & Camp Ramp-Up | Press Conference
text: Ridley had a real bad stomach bug over the last 48 hours, lost a lot of fluids. You'll see him running around. We just want to be precautious have some precaution as he gains his weight back. He should be back in the fold tomorrow. And then Trubisky got a little tight during the conditioning yesterday. Um he a lot better today, hopeful for tomorrow, but he's more day-to-day. >> Coach, you mentioned the next couple weeks. You said a couple different things. Heavy contact, volume, also strenuous activity. If you could kind of describe maybe a little bit of that strenuous part or what can we expect? >> Yeah, you know, first off these first four uh five days of the acclimation period, you're kind of limited. So, it's you're going to see a lot of the same stuff with regards to OTA three rule phase three rules. Um no contact and the practices are going to be formatted the same, but come Monday when we put the pads on um the idea is that our volume continues to increase with every single practice. Um trying to trying to maximize uh and build so that way we're ready for week one along with building callus that so we can survive a 17-week season. So, um you know, the the idea is that our practices are going to be physical, they're going to be fast. Uh there's going to be a lot of volume and then even when we're not practicing our lift our lifts and the way we've designed those to uh complement our practices uh they'll be heavy to make sure that we're not just maintaining our strength, but adding on and adding adding armor if you will uh to prepare So, so it's uh it's a really well-thought-out plan and I think everyone's done a really good job communicating and formulating this thing to do what's best for the players. >> Guys are pretty familiar with the the mindset of the defense, kind of straightforward. The the the diversity of coverage, how quickly do you get into that and what does that do for Cam's growth? >> Um well, you know, for we we have a I think our defense will pretty much be installed within four days. So, once we get the pads, I think where Cam's growth for us going against our defense um is going to be more third down because we do we do get a little bit we're we're much more creative on third down in terms of uh uh the different looks and the different pressure designs and the different coverages that we'll do. Um you know, so for Cam, like I said, it's it's understanding the playbook, understanding his progression, understanding the reads, understanding what's being asked of him, and uh and and finding ways to be to bat a thousand with regards to the the decision-making of a system. >> And with regard to that, what does he need to do to be better under pressure, which was a struggle area for him in the last season? >> Uh that that, you know, that's like a million-dollar question for every quarterback. You know, it's just uh part of that's understanding the protection system, understanding where his hot throws are, understanding where his outlets are, um understanding where the pressure's coming from and how much time he has. Uh you know, some quarterbacks, as they a lot of experienced quarterbacks, they can see a safety coming from depth and then knows that he can still he still has time and and he has a hitch, so he can take time in the pocket rather than feeling rushed. So, um it's just going to be part of the maturation process, just getting reps and seeing all the different looks that he can see. >> He has said one of the things he's learned already is like how important quarterbacking is on third down. How can you go up in the first and second and get the third, that's where you make your money. What is your take on that? >> Yeah, the to me, the forever the the quarterback metric is third down, red zone, two minute. Those are the three categories where the quarterback's got to where the quarterback shines and and pulls the team along, if you will. you know, first and second down, you're you're trying to create explosive plays, you're running the ball, you're you're you've got play action pass, you've got the screen game, you've got all the RPOs, you got all the different things that you're going to try to do, but when it comes to third down and everyone knows you're about to throw or two minute, you got to have it, or in the red zone where it gets where everything's sped up and the windows get a lot tighter, that's where the quarterback shines and uh and so that's part of the thing that a lot of the things that he's learning. >> And then he also he gathered some of the guys to work out down in Miami. How do you like a quarterback, you know, going and and and doing that, you know, getting that chemistry and developing them? >> You always want it. You know, as much as those guys can communicate if anything the bonding part about it, the communicating, the trust, you know, being trusting one another that isn't just running routes on the football field. It's the constant communication off the field. It's understanding each other, understanding the the the human being. and so anytime those guys get together it's a good thing. >> You preach fast and violent as a mantra. It seems obvious that that can be applicable to defense, but how can offense take that mindset? >> It's the same thing. The way the way the O line runs off the ball in the run game, the way the receivers transition out of the out of the out of the break, the way they catch the ball, get vertical, drop step, get vertical and with the mindset to break tackles, the um the way the backs run one cut, get vertical, try to run through people. You can play fast and violent, and like I've said it's it's not just the and I and I know when you think violence it's not just hitting. It's how violently you get out of your break. It's how violently you cut. It's how violently you get off the ball. It's how violent you are in transition. And no different for the defense. It's how how violent you are um and your ball out break, you're attacking the the near foot. It's a corner getting out of his break. It's There's There's a lot of violence in how you move and a lot of violence in your feet, a lot of violence in your mindset, and then the obviously the contact point adds a whole new level. >> You were just talking about chemistry and trust. Is there anything you look for specifically to tell you that has developed? Is there a way you can see that, or you just kind of have to trust consistency? >> You you'll you'll start to see it like the timing and rhythm throws where uh you could just tell that the quarterback and the receiver are on the same page where a receiver might have to deviate his route a little bit. Um you know, you're getting a different coverage and he might shave a little off the top of the uh top of the route concept and the quarterback is in tune with him. So, you you'll see it as as camp progresses. >> How much of these four days is kind of a review of the ramp up of what you did in OTAs versus what you talked about yesterday? You'll see more fast and loud guys feeling confident in what they're doing. >> For sure. It it's uh it's a little bit of both. Uh there were we're reacclimating. I mean, 40 days I mean, it it it it is a long time. I mean, shoot, I I have to go back over everything myself and I've been doing the coaching the same defense for a while. And um you know, so you're reacclimating everybody, but you hope that they pick it up faster uh within these four days so that or four or five practices so that way come Monday when pads come on and a new stimulus happens and it speeds up it goes even faster. we're comfortable in the way we're communicating. >> You'll find out in time, but first impressions last. How did the guys look first day out back yesterday? >> Everything was good. Uh yeah, everyone looked good and uh again, we'll find out in time. >> I know that only saw Jeffery Simmons he's getting acclimated on his own plan a little bit. How is he doing and how important are these next couple weeks in terms of him stepping up? >> Uh he he looks great, man. I was uh I mean, not to talk about his body, but the guy's yolked. >> [laughter] >> He is uh I'd walk around I'd I'd walk around with my shirt off all the time if I was him, but uh he's uh he's in great shape. Um the the biggest adjustment for him is to go from and it's an adjustment every you'll see it like uh a lot of guys when they go from a read system to an attack system and they're an individual, you'll see a lot of guys fall on their face during individual. And that's natural. Like that's there's a there's an adjustment, there's an acclimation that needs to happen for him. Um but he's so talented, he'll figure it out pretty quick. >> Are there Are there milestones that you're looking for from Cam, or benchmarks throughout camp as you get closer and closer to those joint practices that are so crucial? >> Just looking for his decision-making. Just want to Just want to make sure that he's understanding the system the way he needs to understand it, and he's making the decisions he needs to make. And uh then from a from a understanding the opposite side of the ball, he's starting to understand defensive structure. >> Is Slotton and Bolton first in line to start? As far as Ridley, obviously he won't go today, but what are your impressions in these last couple of weeks? >> Um I He can still move, man. I was uh you know, he had some some run towards the end of uh OTAs and minicamp. Um awesome dude to talk to. Uh And he's still got a lot of juice in his legs. So I'm I'm excited to get him out here with the with the young kids. And uh there's a really cool combination in that room with with a lot of youth, and then obviously there's some veterans in there that can uh escort those guys along. >> How cautious do you have to be with him now that he's going in his 30s, especially at that position? >> Uh for sure, all the 30-plus-year-olds um will be mindful in making sure that they're acclimating the way they need to, callousing the way they need to, but also preparing them so they can last the 17-game season. >> Last one, Nick. >> You were kind of at the center of a lot of the conversations about player safety and turf stuff in New York and in San Francisco. Now that it's kind of reigniting, is there something you've learned or that you've taken away from all the injury discussions you kind of had to be centered around that you kind of take to this job? >> You know, at the end of the day we we're we're told where to play, and it doesn't matter, if that makes sense. I don't care the stadium, the turf, the weather, it doesn't matter. Um it's it's not changing. It is what it is, and um you either embrace it or you complain about it. And um we're the mindset that we'll play any place, anytime, anywhere, any turf. >> You impressed by the power of soccer players to get turf to get grass? >> Money talks. >> I'll see you guys. >> Thank you. Thank you.

title: Chase Daniel: Browns QB battle is Shedeur Sanders' to lose | Dan Patrick Show | NFL on NBC
text: So, we have quarterback competition in Cleveland. >> I I think there is. Like I would say if you were at OTAs and you were hearing everything out of camp like, "Oh, DeShawn Watson's doing this and oh, DeShawn Watson's doing that." You weren't hearing a lot of Shedeur. And then as as it got closer to the end of OTAs, Monken was like, "Ah, you know, cuz he said he wanted to make a decision." Anytime you get a quarterback competition that's like this going into training camp, um this one just this one feels different. I think I think Shedeur Sanders um has done a really good job from everything I've been hearing of really growing from year one to year two, right? And I think with this offense, it's really spread out. They use 11 personnel, which is one back, one tight end, three receivers a lot. It's similar There are similar things to what Shedeur did in Colorado. And quite honestly, Dan, like I never judge rookie quarterbacks because quarterback play is so difficult. Now, there were some dumb mistakes that Shedeur made last year. He'd be the first one to tell you. But I do think if you can really just play within that scheme. They're going to scheme some stuff up and not make stupid mistakes. He has to play a lot faster. I think that's really where the biggest jump from first to second-year quarterbacks is is processing speed. Can he get his processing speed when he breaks the huddle up? I don't know. I It's going to be a fascinating thing, but I I think Shedeur sort of has the inside track and job. I mean, look, the the Browns have two first-round picks next year. Let's be honest. They're going after Arch Manning or they're going after Dante Moore or they're going after whoever it is. There If you don't get really good quarterback play out of Shedeur, I don't think there's any chance even if DeShawn plays at a Pro Bowl level, he's going to be back there. They've wasted so much money on him. Every time he's played since Houston, it's been like, "Okay, you know, it just didn't push the ball down the field." Um Um, but I I I like Shidora in this battle.

title: Patrick Mahomes' ACL recovery a hot topic ahead of NFL season | Dan Patrick Show | NFL on NBC
text: Patrick Mahomes, from what you've seen, is impressed? >> Um look, the clips I broke down on the on the page and everything that we've gotten so far have been rookie mini camp because the quarterbacks report early with the rookies. Um or sorry, rookie training camp like the start because they want to get going. When I was watching him doing quarterback center exchange and, you know, rolling out to the left, it's clearly his knee is not 100% and neither it shouldn't be. You you I think the injury was December 13th. So, you know, you count the months, it's it's still a month and a half a month away from games. It's going to be fascin- I don't think there's any way that Patrick Mahomes misses week one. But what's interesting to me is what happens with that offense because I don't think he's going to be 100%. He's not going to be able at first with the big bulky brace on the left knee. That's what looked to me to be hindering him a little bit. It's it looks a little gimpy still and it should be, right? He's he's it's not a full speed, it's not 100%. How does he react when people are around you? I think that's the biggest thing. But more importantly, how does that offense change? Because with Andy, right? There's already a lot of quick game. He relies on it a lot, but where Mahomes is the best is is breaking pocket, breaking contain, getting outside of the pocket. He ain't going to be able to do that. And I think there's a reason why they spent, I think it was $16 $17 million on Kenneth Walker is to actually have a running back and they have other good running backs there, too, but I was seeing a ton of under center stuff. Maybe it's where you're getting into that, hey, we're in two tight ends, we're in 12 personnel. We're not just going to be spread it out while Mahomes gets back. And I think that's so sort of an under recognized part of Mahomes' game is under center play action. Just how does he react with people around him? >> Is there a knee, if you were going to have knee surgery, that would be better to have as far as coming back from? >> You ask a great question because I was just about to say it's I think it's the left knee because the left knee is your push-off leg, but it's not your plant leg, meaning you're pushing off away from under center with your left leg if you're right-handed quarterback, which he is. Your plant leg is your back leg, so when you are dropping back and trying to get away from the line of scrimmage as much as possible, you have to put a lot of pressure in your back knee to then drive up within the pocket, right? You want to set around 10 yards to and move up to about 9 and 1/2 yards back from the line of scrimmage so the tackles can run their guys by. That's how Andy Reid really does it. Um but I mean no knee would be better, uh right? But I would say the left knee the thing that I'm going to be really watching is is he going to be throwing all arm? Because when you're a quarterback and you hurt your left knee especially, right? That's your landing knee when you're throwing. You're stepping with your left foot and a lot of times if you can't step all the way or maybe a long enough stride length, your arm lags behind and you're really throwing you're you're sort of whippy rather than rotational. I'm I'm getting nerdy a little bit on it, but that that's something that is is a reality of the situation and we see Mahomes on these short intermediate RPO run pass options, we see him fake and throw all arm, but I don't think he's ever you know, going to have to worry about arm strength. He can throw it a country mile, but it will be interesting in a tight pocket, right? At first, how does he handle the pass rush? And it's not even getting sacked. I don't think getting hit is going to mess with it. I think him trusting his knee when there's a push in the pocket because he's so good in a phone booth. That's what you call it, throwing in a phone booth. Uh how is that going to affect his accuracy?

title: Mike LaFleur talks Brissett, Jeremiyah Love (FULL INTERVIEW) | Chris Simms Unbuttoned | NFL on NBC
text: All right, we're now really happy to be joined by Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur. Mike, thanks so much for doing this. One of the teams you guys are rocking and rolling already. What's it like having the early camp start? >> It's it it's well, thanks for having me, guys. No, it's uh it's awesome and um you know, I I I'm I'm not sure that anyone probably on our team was that fired up about coming back a week earlier than everybody else. Uh but with that said, the way that it felt being in in the first year, we were able to get all our work in with the extra with the extra week that we were allotted. And then I was able to get them out a week earlier than everyone else.
