So, they still had their normal summer break and then we kind of had what I call block zero uh this last week where we got a little head start on people. >> I I I forgot you two were Jets best frenzies from back in the day. And what? Yeah, it's a die-hard Jets fan here. All right, first thing right off the bat, just what's it like being the head coach? Like some of the adjustments you've had to make in your life and your day-to-day approach coaching as compared to to being an offensive coordinator. >> Well, you know, the first thing I guess I have a unit meeting here in 2 hours and I would normally be working on that in the offense, but I'm talking to you guys, you know? So, those are those are some of the slight adjustments, but those are the fun adjustments. But uh no, it's you know, it's um Listen, I like by no means have I figured anything out, obviously, but I haven't even played a game yet, but but I have been able to have the insight with Kyle, with Sean, you know, and just being with them to just to see how they kind of manage their days while still being great offensive coordinators and play callers and and and not losing sight of the offense, but also, you know, the responsibilities of being a head coach. So, you know, try to keep the main thing the main thing. It's still always about ball and the relationships with these guys. Um but but ultimately, you know, I got to I I got all three aspects of it with the special teams and defense and but but not losing sight of the offense, either. >> So, I I I wanted to go there anyways. We've known each other a long time. He's part of the Shanahan-McVay his brother, of course, Matt up in Green Bay. But But what I would love to hear from you, like best thing you learned from Kyle Shanahan and Sean McVay that you've taken, you know, into your expertise here as playing calls or play caller and and head coach. >> We'll keep it away from the scheme because I mean, they're obviously very good scheme guys and and and the numbers and the stats and the wins all speak for themselves, but I think it's it's above that with both those guys and and it's really I you can almost kind of group it in like if you walk into the San Francisco building, you walk into the LA building, you quickly realize there's a great urgency. Like people love the vibe. People love coming to work every single day, but they keep the main thing the main thing. And and and it's just about ball and about the players and what like if you can't answer, is this going to make this player or this team better, then then what are we even talking about, you know? And so I like I said, the urgency, you know, they keep the main thing the main thing and and that great collaboration and communication amongst, you know, the powers that be, if you will. Every single both those buildings right there. You talk about great relationships with the GM and head coach and everyone in between and and you know, with ownership and all that and and that's something that, you know, I hope to build here and I believe I believe we are. I think money is tremendous. I think he's a great GM and even a better person and you know, collaborating with him and and you know, Michael's been awesome. >> So and and what you said it and you brought up the word scheme, right? I'd love to you to hear just, you know, a base version, elementary version of the differences in your eyes of the Shanahan scheme and the McVay scheme. I know they're very similar, but what to you as a nuanced offensive guy is the difference that you could explain to us, you know, simpletons out here? >> Yeah, there's there's foundational aspects of the same, but I I the approach sometimes can be a little bit little bit different. Um you know, I think and I think this is positive in both aspects cuz I think both are true and both how how their their great minds work in my opinion, but like, you know, Kyle has so much respect for defenses in this league that like I can't show a good coordinator a good defense the same play twice. Like I have to figure out a way to have a play off of a play or at least dress that play up. >> Right. >> And then I flip it over to Sean and not saying he doesn't feel that way, but man, like how many times can we hit the same block? And I don't really care. We're just going to hit this block better than they're going to defend it, you know? And so that's where and I know you're shaking your head right there because it's you can see it when you watch when you watch on Sundays or you're watching the tape, I guess for the Niners and Rams, they don't really play Sundays. They play Mondays, Thursdays, Fridays, Saturdays, all those kind of things. But but you know what I'm saying about, you know, kind of both those and again, I I think both are right and I think that it's it's they trust what what they believe in and and run with it and they have so such conviction um that naturally their players are going to as well. >> Right. I mean, we know the greatness of McVay and Shanahan, but what about your own big brother who's won a lot of games in the NFL right now? What's a lesson or something you've gotten from him when you stepped into the role of being, you know, obviously a big step into play caller, now a bigger step into head coach? What's something that your own family can help you with? >> Yeah, I mean, obviously so much, right? I mean, it's just Matt and I um you know, we're we're really close. Uh probably too close if you ask our wives. Um but I I do I do try to call Lauren one more time than I call Matt every day. So just to keep, you know, make sure that's all good at home. But uh you know, I I've always said this about Matt. I I have a lot of respect for him for so many reasons, but one of the the things that sticks out to me the most is he just he works harder than anyone I've ever met. Like he if if he could find the 25th hour in the day, he'd do it. Not that I'm saying that he stays up all night and all that kind of stuff. He just when he goes, he goes and and he works really hard at it. He pours into it. Um I thought I think he's authentically himself at all times. I think he's grown into that more and more as he's gone. Um you know, and uh obviously want the Cardinals to win every Sunday, but uh as long as it doesn't hurt the Cardinals, rooting hard for him every every week as >> The the I I have a funny story for you. I don't think I've ever told this to you, but I've said this on the pod. Connor's heard me say this before. So, you go from the 49ers, you become the offensive coordinator at the Jets, then you join McVay and the Rams. And I can still remember the day you got with McVay and the Rams because I was talking to Kyle Shanahan, and he was like, "Oh, Mike's with McVay, and he's going to teach him some of my run game tricks and some of the things I I do there and the nuance, right?" And so, I guess what I'm asking you is tell us kind of the story behind that or the nuance, and and does a McVay ask, you know, "How does Kyle do this or do that?" And and how do you balance that as being a friend to to everybody there? >> Uh I mean, I'll answer the second question first. I mean, like you know, naturally, I mean, there's so much respect between those two and and and um so, you're you're always watching them from afar, but you always study them as well. Whether you pop them on Monday at night as kind of your last thing during the week or it's an off-season thing. I mean, you're you're one, they're in the division. They're always going to know each other a little bit more, you know. So, um there's there's respect there. There's always going to be, "Hey, how are they doing it? How are we doing it? How would it fit? Would it not fit?" And sometimes it's, "Hey, that's just what they do up in San Francisco or that's what they do in LA, but we're going to do it our way, and that's okay." Um you know, so it I'll give you the quick story in terms of what happened in '22 when when um you know, it's >> [snorts] >> obviously when somebody's situation going on, you don't you're not talking to a a of people. You're keeping it nice and tight and close for obvious reasons and um but typically I would let Kyle in on everything and this was the only one when he called me and I looked at the phone. I don't even know if I've ever told him this. I looked at the phone like this was like probably a day or two after I knew I was going to the Rams and I see my wife Lauren and we look and I'm like, "I can't answer this." >> [laughter] >> And then the next And then so And then the next day he called again and she goes, "You have to answer this." And it was weird that in that moment that was like the only I was being I was being soft. I was dreading the call, dreading the conversation, but he already knew everything. So >> That's great. I appreciate you sharing that with us. All right, one more thing just on you and your personal life. Uh your parents, how freaking happy I mean who your mom and dad, who the hell are they? What the hell were they doing to grow and make you guys so amazing growing up? I mean to have two kids as head coaches in the NFL? >> Young coaches. >> And and young coaches is is it's unreal. So give your parents some props. I want to hear about them. I know nothing about them. >> Uh they're they're good people they're coa- you know, we come from a coaching family. My it it really started with my grandpa. He was a long time head coach in the state of Michigan in in high school. Coached at Loy Norrix, uh Kalamazoo Central or like and I'm just throwing names out like Derek Jeter and stuff like that. The Ducketts uh played at Loy Norrix. Um you know, so he was a long time coach there. Um and my mom was a cheerleader and all that and then and then uh she goes to Central Michigan and my dad was playing there and then and they got married basically, you know, right at the end of college and my dad just started coaching at Central and he ended up coaching there for almost about 25 years and through that whole time my mom's coaching. She coached every sport you can name. Um as I was going through high school they she she was um a track coach and they were always maybe state runner runners-up every year, which we didn't understand as the guys team cuz we felt like we worked a lot harder than them and they just they they smoke everybody. So, they had something figured out, but I will say this, and I I get laughed, but I always preface it with if you've ever seen an actual competitive cheer team go to work and what they have to do, they work like 3 to 4 hours a night. And this was like 16 through 18-year-old girls that that were rolling, and my my mom had them all bought in, and and was super successful there. Um she unlike my brother and I are she's in the Hall of Fame at Mount Pleasant High School along with my wife who was was a track athlete. So, yeah. Oh, yeah. No, we we we got shortchanged there. They were they were the studs, and Matt and I were just kind of the tagalongs, but you know, it's just growing up with that and like I said with my dad when he got let go at Central was a high school was a high school coach and all that. So, yeah, we just come from from a sporting family. They were my mom particularly was always very level. It was like she she was emotional in a good way. Like the players could feel her passion and her belief, but man, since we started really over the last few years, she can't handle Sundays at all. Particularly when it's like you blame her back like a 1:00, 4:00. It's an absolute trainer. I said, "Mom, this is not the the the the coach that I remember growing up. You got to get >> your composure there." But great people, you know, and yeah, we love them. >> Let's get into your team. Jacoby Brissett signed in the building already rocking and rolling. Well, how much of a boost is that to the entire team to not only get We know what kind of player he is, but the veteran and already the relationships that he's established with the skill guys in your building. >> Yeah, no, it's it's it's it's great to have that over with, you know, and I I never uh I know the contract stuff can go a lot of different ways and for obvious reasons, and and I always respect that process, and and it's done, and and now we get to move forward with with the main thing, which is ball. So, so that's that's a positive. Obviously, he He a lot of these guys. He He knows a lot of these guys better than I know a lot of these guys. Um always had a lot of respect from Jacoby from afar. Feel like I've played him in a lot of different uniforms. I feel like every time we play him, the defensive coordinators are not looking forward to it cuz they know he can spin it around the yard, you know? And um so uh excited just to have that and and and just really get rolling with him. Obviously missed OTAs. Um you know, so we got to get him up to speed in terms of you know, just the terminology and and kind of why we're trying to do some things and some of our protection adjustments that might be a little bit new. But like I keep telling him, the hardest part of all this is just actually playing the position. And he's played the position for for a lot of years. Like the the the speed of the game, he knows that. So like all this other semantic stuff, we'll get him caught up. Like walk-throughs will be extremely beneficial for him because it's just hearing how I'm calling it and and why we're calling it and the motion timing and all that kind of stuff. But like I told him yesterday, hey you just when that ball snap, you go play your game and then we'll go from there. >> There's been a lot of talk about the other quarterback you got. Of course, the guy you drafted out of the University of Miami in Carson Beck. And he's mature and he's played a lot of big football in college and all that. You know, how do you see kind of Jacoby helping him out and kind of talk to us a little bit about Carson's development so far that you've seen through OTAs and mini camp? >> Yeah, I mean it's well what you just said with Jacoby. I mean again like a guy that's had a lot of experience like most quarterbacks in this league. A lot of ups, a lot of downs and everything in between. And so just kind of how to handle that day-to-day and and Carson will get a you know, kind of a front seat look at that as we move forward. So like his development like you said, you know, him coming out um he's played in a lot of big games, a lot of big-time football, a lot of big-time stadiums, you know, national television, all those kind of things. And it hasn't always been smooth sailing for him. And and he's been through the ringer a little bit in different ways. And and to me I think that's gave him some some he's battle tested, gave him some that um yeah, it's different in the league, there's no doubt, but like at least to be able to come in and not everything was just perfect, right? And and um and I think he knows that and I think there's a maturity level about Carson. He's, you know, he's he is a a tick older than some. I mean, he played college football for a little bit. So, um and then and then you look at the talent. I mean, you know, he's a big, strong, sturdy dude. He plays with a great base back there. It's very natural. Like it's not There's no There's nothing that looks hard when he's throwing the football. Um so, again, for him, he's super smart. It's It's just reps, reps, reps. And you think about what you guys asked me on the first one is um we get that extra game. We get that extra preseason game. We get that extra block. And that'll That's That's great for a rookie quarterback. So, he's going to get a lot of time uh over those four games. >> Mike, you know I got to ask you about Zonovan Knight. And you know, in a different vein though, everybody with high-profile rookie running backs, they want to know how are they going to be used? Are they going to be used the right way? Is it worth the pick? People might forget, you had a rookie Breece Hall rolling for almost 6 yd per carry before Breece got hurt that year. Are there lessons you can take from that run that you can apply to integrating a rookie like Zonovan Knight? >> Give good football players the football. You know, like I mean, and it's, you know, and and Zonovan and Breece are are are different guys. Obviously, I have a ton of love for Breece as as a person, uh let alone a player. Um you know, so uh and and that was a that was a uh that was a big loss as you remember, Connor, when when he went down in '22. We were playing great defense. We were running the ball well. And um you know, it it kind of fell off a little bit for different reasons after that in terms of the run game. So, um but yeah, I mean, it's, you know, with these backs, it's it's it's tricky as you guys know in July and August because yeah, we got the pads on, but they're not getting tackled still. >> Yeah. >> And it's just it's it's one of the harder positions to evaluate, even though they're still getting good work until you get to the preseason. And you know, that's why you know, he'll be out there as well. I'm not going to say you know, you know, how many games he'll be out there, but he's he's going to touch the ball in those games to get kind of the speed of the NFL. You know, we'll see how many of the the opponents we're playing they're going to actually play their starters, you never know. But you know, again, get your good players the ball and let them go. >> Yeah, well you've been a run game expert. You know about the running game and that's where I would just two more questions cuz I know you got to go. But Jeremiah love too. How quickly were you sold when you started to watch the film? And then how much conversation was there in the building of like oh, can do we should we draft a running back at number three? With that whole conversation of the devaluing of the position, you know, how did that go down, Mike? >> Yeah, I mean I think uh Yes, there were conversations, but there were going to be conversations regardless, right? Even if you had the one the the number one pick in the in the the quarterback was sitting right. Like you just you naturally go through everything. And so those conversations came up. The one thing amongst many things that I respect about money is he was going to take who he thought was going to be the best fit for for this team. And you know, obviously there was going to be a you know, a character aspect to it and and just kind of you know, making sure we have the right person coming in the building on top of having a really good talented football player that that we feel like you know, for years to come can can produce. And so yeah, those conversations would be happening again, a lot of respect for how money handled it. A lot of respect for how I always had a lot of respect for for how Kyle and John did it in in San Francisco. Felt like I was always in on a lot of stuff, scheme, roster, all that. But man, they kept stuff really tight with the draft and I respect the heck out of that because you never know. And I thought money did a great job with that. I was really you know, really impressed with with with his approach with that. And so um yeah, that's that's kind of where we're at. >> All right, well, one last thing cuz I I did see this on social media. I think it's interesting. Where did you get this put the play up on the JumboTron right after we run the practice play, right? So, the guys can like do a play and look up and go, "Oh, wait, this is what I did right or wrong or whatever." Where where did that come from? >> It's funny this is trending because it's LA so most teams are practicing in stadiums, right? That was a good play by him, by the way. >> Yeah, it was. >> Oh, yeah. Most most teams are practicing in stadiums. Obviously, we're doing it here because we're not going to be in Tempe and and putting them on the turf. So, I mean, you think about the advantage we have of one, staying out of the heat, but two, still being on the grass right there. You know, San Francisco and LA and the Chargers have a good advantage cuz they're in California and the weather and all those kind of things. So, they don't have to worry about that stuff. We had to adjust. This wasn't just a copy and paste outfit. Like it's like, "Hey, we have heat. We're going to have to handle that heat." So, you know, for the meantime, we'll be in there. So, we have this beautiful JumboTron that is I mean, like literally, I can call a play and I'm watching the play two to three more times before the next snap and I already saw it live once. And so, like I've told the coaches, like if we're doing this the right way and your eyes are in the right place disciplined not ball watching, you should be able to see it in real time, have a good feel, and then confirm it, and then coach it right up. The reason I say I'm I'm surprised this is kind of trending is you know, the Rams got video boards, the the Falcons from last year with Raheem had video boards, Minnesota has video boards, I'm sure Green Bay has it. I'm assuming assuming Kyle's probably got them up in San Francisco cuz of Raheem and stuff like that. So, I mean, it's not we're not the first ones, but I will say that JumboTron is nice. >> It is nice. That helps. That's awesome to have. I mean, I would love to have that as a player. And we love that you came on here and hung out with us for a little bit, Mike. We really appreciate it, dude. You got a lot of more important things to talk to to do instead of talking to us two idiots, so good luck to you, man. We're rooting for you, and you're opening up your career on NBC next week in the Hall of Fame game. So, this works out perfectly, dude. >> Thanks, Mike. Thanks, guys. Good seeing you. >> All right, good seeing you. Best of luck, buddy. Yo, yo, homies. Thanks for watching. We appreciate it. Now, keep following us through the off season. We're going to take you all the way to the draft. You know that. We're going to be in the barn. Tune in for that. And then we got mini camps and a whole lot more. >> Hit subscribe to get reminders for all of our live shows taping Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday at 10:00 a.m. Eastern time. >> Thanks again for watching. Remember to subscribe. Comment about his cool jackets every week. We'll see you next time. Peace out.

title: Michael Pittman Jr., Zach Frazier & Mason Rudolph Press Conference (July 29) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: first day. >> Oh, it's good. I mean, like, it's good that we're all like settled and we're all moved out here. So, it's great. >> Your first camp, I know it's new for a lot of people here, but also new for you being out here. How was it day one? >> Absolutely. I mean, obviously the offense getting out here like for the first time. So, just just working through some stuff and uh I thought the defense practiced well today and we're looking forward to get back at them uh tomorrow. >> I know, but how much can you and DK play off each other? >> Absolutely. I mean, I feel like it's just energy on top of um energy and um execution fuels um execution and I feel like both or um both or I feel like both of us and some of our other guys can make plays. So, just being able to just build off that. >> How'd you find uh working with all the quarterbacks? I mean, I don't know how many reps you get with the two young guys, but from what you saw how they handle themselves. >> Absolutely. I mean, I think that all of them are um doing great. Um and uh they all bring different things like to the uh table and um Aaron is going to be our lead guy and then those other guys I get to learn from him. So I think it's going to be great. >> How much does it help you guys as a team to have this emphasis on the two minutes especially at the end mixing up the down distance and how much time is left and all that? >> Absolutely. I mean there's so many games that come down to that uh last drive and um just the fact that we're practicing it every single day and I think we'll be the most conditioned team. um by the uh end of camp. So, >> how long will it take or will it take long for everyone to kind of There's so much newness here. Not only the coaching staff and mixed in with a lot of veterans, how long does that take maybe for a team to get on the same page? >> Yeah, I mean it definitely takes time. I mean, no team like is a finished product until the very last game. So, um as long as we keep on building like each day and keep getting better, then by the end of the season, I think we'll be uh a um happy team. So, How much do those trips out west kind of go toward helping build that chemistry before you guys even get to training camp? >> Absolutely. I mean I feel like Aaron said it best. I mean um before that trip like I didn't really know those guys and now I feel like I know them um pretty darn well. So um it's always good to just go do those things and uh take that time for sure. >> Do you have to teach them how to fish or there other professionals out there? >> No. No. I mean I mean Aaron is a very avid uh fisherman and and um a couple other guys like I felt like they were catching fish so they knew what they were doing. >> Who had the biggest catch? >> Um I don't know because we were all kind of fishing in different areas so so I didn't really keep track. >> So you can't apples to apples to the area then. >> Yeah. But I mean I think I caught the most but you know. >> Is there anywhere around here where you go? You ask? >> Oh yeah. I mean uh I went out a couple times and caught some uh musky. There's a picture out there somewhere. Got a 48 and a half inch musky. So that was a pretty big one. >> How does a trip like that translate to what you guys want to do on the field? title: Cameron Heyward Press Conference (July 29) | Pittsburgh Steelers
text: Hey, Cam. Day one, what's the biggest difference? How was it? New coach? All >> The biggest difference, uh, practice is earlier, as you guys know. But, uh, no, I think we're all just, you know, trying to learn. The coaches are trying to learn, and um, it's a new setting for everybody. So, uh, you know, we're not going to be perfect right now, but we're we're working towards that. >> Mike Tomlin said that his message he told us his message to you guys this morning was kind of talking about the history of the Steelers and tying that in the city. Just How it resonated with you from that. What did he say that kind of got you >> Um, you know, I I think, you know, the thing that resonated with me is just, you know, he's from Pittsburgh. He has a lot of respect for the tradition here. Um, but he he's trying to forge something new. Uh, and I think that can apply to everybody in our locker room. Um, you know, I love the one thing he said is, you know, it's going to take 68 plus guys to win a Super Bowl. Um, and that's including practice squad, and um, you know, that's that's always respectful that, you know, he he he respects everybody in that locker room, and you know, we got to grow from that. >> Cam, I'm not sure how much >> Mhm? >> No D-lineman package. >> It's the first day. Um, that's, you know, we're out here in in no pads. We're not doing too much, so it's two-minute. We're We're We're trying some new things, but, you know, we'll see. >> Cam, I'm I'm not sure how much tackling you ever did here, but >> Wow, that's a shot. >> [laughter] >> And I wasn't always the prime guys, but there was a lot of tackling for a lot of years. Now there isn't. What do you What do you think of that? >> Um, family day was always a big one because it's everybody, it's a alpha sport, and we just ramp it up. You know, Friday night lights is always another big one with tackling, and, you know, that. But, uh, we'll see. Um, you know, when you can't tackle, uh, you really got to stretch your technique. Um, and, you know, I'm looking forward to doing that. >> Can you get ready for the season without any tackling? >> Uh, yeah. You know, uh, I As he As he alluded to, I done a lot of practicing in that, so um you know, it's about taking great angles, uh making sure you go for the far leg, uh and then on the other side, making sure you finish every drill. So, you know, we can really just stress those details. It is. Um you know, um I've been coming here for 15 years, uh and I'm used to seeing him on day one and him talking crap to me, but uh you know, uh as I as I think about it, it's those were some good times, but uh I got to do some adjusting. >> Is it weird if you know, if you're in an age group hitting you for quite a while >> Mhm. >> to have that newness, is it a shock to the system? >> Yeah. Uh you know, it's there's a lot of unknown. Um I got to prove myself just like everybody else. Um and I'm not running from that. Um you know, good players, they deal with change. Uh they're able to adapt and stay flexible and you know, I'm looking forward to trying that. >> What was it like arriving with none of your peers? your peers by you? >> Uh how can I say this nicely? >> No, I'm just kidding. Uh you know, it was different. Um usually I'm having like a ton in my hands and trying to talk to the media, but uh then I get these intimate moments with you guys uh after practice. So, you know, we make up for it. >> Do you embrace change at this point in your career? Do you like new? >> I got to. Um you know, the dinosaurs did it and look what happened to them. So, uh for me, I got to, you know, embrace change and you know, I always think after every year I got to improve. So, you know, um that's nothing new from how things have changed. >> Have you guys had conversations between the veterans like, "Hey, we're all going to be on the same page to embrace this change for the newness?" Or are you guys kind of just doing your own thing? >> We understand there's going to be growing pains, but uh you know, being professional means um doing what your coach asked of you. And we're very big on servant leadership and serving the entire group. So, coach McCarthy said to us he wants to serve us. So, we're all going to be in this together and we're all going to put our hands in the pile. >> There was a period there earlier maybe in the 2020 when you would take time after the season to reflect on what you did and what you wanted to keep doing. And now it just seems to be full steam ahead and at a time when a lot of guys are, you know, maybe what can I say, what what do you what do you attribute this sort of being in some of your shoes you know, when in the off-season I tend to get away and I let myself decompress. But it's every year me and my wife are having the same conversations and you know, we're we're seeing what's best for me and my family. And I'm fortunate enough to keep doing a job I love and I feel like I can continue to keep improving. >> Aaron's wife said that she said you can have one more year. Has Dalia said anything like that to you yet? You got a year >> Ooh, I told her I was like, these two years, that's it. And she was like, okay. But then you never know. I could be a year from now and be like, these two years. But we'll cross that bridge when we get there.

text: First like to say [snorts] that I hope you're able to get up to the pro shop tent. They have got some really cool hats, so. All right. Trying to get Bird kicked Trying to get Bird paid here. Did you have any kind of debate or >> No, zero debate. Zero. >> What's the biggest thing that excites you about having Mike McCarthy coach again? >> Well, just the history. We got 13 years together. Got long uh you know, long track record of success and playoff runs, Super Bowl championship. Um and then just the full circle, seeing each other now where we're at in life. Um I think I'm the the same age that he was when he got hired in Green Bay, so that's nice uh full circle moment for both of us. >> Is there something philosophically or schematically that you guys particularly click with? Do you do you see the game the same way? Do you attack in the same way? >> Yeah, the West Coast offense. Which is basically gone in the NFL other than what Mike's doing. >> Aaron, how do you view How do you view the significance of that trip you guys took out west? DK was talking about the camaraderie. What do you think comes out of that? How it impacts you guys as a as a group? I think a A uh a lot is made about those trips. I think probably overblown at times. The most important chemistry is as the season gets going for sure, but the thing I will say is that you spend 6 months with guys every single day then you go on a trip for 4 days and you after the trip you felt like man I didn't even know these guys before these these 4 days. So it was good bonding around the campfire, good you know activities out where we were at and got out on the on the river and fished and did some things and rode some horses and had a good time. >> What you can say is that a goal of his is to increase his communication with you during the course of the week and your connectivity. So what you talked about during the week manifests on Sunday. Once the ball is snapped, what more do you think you can get out of DK this year and then how can that relationship grow once the game begins? >> Oh I don't know. I mean this this is what this training camp is for. I think we had a nice nice start in the OTAs. I thought it was super productive. He's uh he actually greeted me last night at the at the dorms. He's my roommate again which I was excited about. He helped me unload my stuff. Um so I'd say we're in a real good place as far as our friendship. He looks incredible. He said he's about his normal weight but he's lower body fat percentage. You know DK's a rare specimen. Um like he likes the offense, likes the opportunities that he saw in in the OTAs just about find a way to you know get on the same page and in this second year together in training camp as we get going and you know not put any crazy expectations on what has to look like at certain times. The most important thing like you said is the communication and I think it's been really good. >> Last year you didn't really take many of any practices off. A lot of veteran quarterbacks don't do that necessarily. Is that important to you and do you expect this year to be any different? Do you expect to play more or you be out there >> I'd like a couple days off. I already told I already told the boss that, but uh uh you know, uh some of the things working against me is he was with me forever and he knows how much I love the practice. Which I do. So, I think it's a little push and pull. I'm not sure what the final decision was. Actually, Mike T had some days slotted for me to be off and then we had some rain out practices, so he counted those gym, you know, walk-throughs as my my days off. So, um I would like a couple. That'd be nice. >> Mike McCarthy's talked to us a couple times about his uh QB school. Um just what do you remember as a young quarterback about going through that and what some of the benefits might what have been? >> [snorts] >> Yeah, there's a lot of benefits. You know, I did it with Tom Arth my first time. Now he's my coach. Um Tom, I've said this before, prettiest uh heel-toe drop I've ever seen. Um I still like to remind him of that how he used to just make me look look bad every single day and you know, it was a crazy workout back then, just the two of us doing 45 minutes non-stop. So, one it got us in shape. Uh two, you know, you're doing stuff you don't normally do like jump rope, which I think is really important. Kind of footwork thing. There's quick feet in that. And then the the drill work is working on um you know, throwing on the run from different angles and different uh you know, targets you're looking at. So, it's way different than the QB school, whatever he's calling it now, is not what it was back then. I mean, that was March 15th. That was 3 days a week. That was going overtime sometimes. Um but, the QB profile that he does do I think is a good uh learning tool for all young quarterbacks. But, they missed out on the real the real work back then when the rules were different. >> Aaron, when you decide you want to play, you have to assess whether you think you still can to your standard and how do you do that? >> Yeah, for sure. I mean, uh it's get back into the workout, see how the body feels, and then um you know, start to throw and see how the arms respond. And the arm has never been an issue uh really in all my 20 plus years playing and before that. Um never really had any arm issues. Um light soreness early in camp, maybe the first couple days, but never, you know, any issues with that. It's just the leg, so you know, I did my usual, spend a lot of time with the with my bodywork folks and uh trying to lengthen the muscles and and open things up and feel better. And you know, then obviously I wanted to feel like I could come out no TAs and and uh you know, have the rhythm at the time and throw. And I feel like OTAs went really smooth and you know, we'll see how camp goes. Obviously, it's always like ups and downs and it's way more scrutinized than it used to be back in the day, so you know, there'll be there'll be a a a new learning curve for all of us as we get into it, but I feel like by the second week we'll start to hit our stride. >> Do you expect to feel any different knowing that it's your last time around as you're going through things? >> I mean, I thought it might. Like last year it felt way more dramatic to me. Like, oh, it's my last, you know, arrival to training camp. And then and this year it doesn't feel anything, you know, I I really don't. I'm just um happy to to be out here with the guys. Good to see some of their uh faces I haven't seen in a while. Good to see the you know, the six guys that went on the trip with us again. I feel like there's like a tighter bond. Then we'll have to bring in some of the other guys who weren't uh at that trip. Uh but now it's good. >> With that trip last year you guys went to Malibu you posted everyone. How did you decide where you went this year and where were [snorts] you exactly other than just the wild west? >> A lot of the guys wanted a a Malibu trip. They wanted to go to Nobu. They wanted to see the dolphins. They wanted to put their feet in the sand. And so this spring uh I said, "Hey, what do you guys want to do this time?" And they said, "Experience. They went We want to do an experience. So, I go, "What are you talking about? You want to go to Hawaii or something?" Or They said, "No, we want to go to the mountains. We want to like do a like a a ranch thing." So, I you know, did a lot of research and found a couple places, and then this place uh you know, came available and we're very thankful to uh to the person that made that happen. I'm not I can't I'm not allowed to speak on where it is, any of that thing, but it was uh it was a great time. >> Aaron, what is your number one area that you would like to improve on going into this year? >> I mean, I don't know. I work on stuff every single day. Uh I have to think about that. Stay one. I'm just uh coming out of getting my passport renewal, so you know, that was my main goal today was to make sure I can go to go to France. So, I think we're going to be locked in on that. But uh I'll be working on things every single day. You know, it's more just It's a different offense. There's different terminology. Mike was flexible in changing a few things uh in the spring, but uh you know, it'll be a work in progress with the offense. >> Aaron, Mike has a history >> Mike McCarthy >> He's got a ring than you. >> Uh Aaron, Mike has a history of his teams throwing at the highest rates on first downs in the NFL. It's change of pace for what the Steelers have been doing recently. What are the key elements that you guys need to achieve to make that and be one of those better teams at throwing on first down? >> We got to be under center. You know, we got to be under center and and uh and get the action game going and the movement game going. So, but it starts under center. I think some of the best offenses in the league are not uh shotgun uh happy. You know, they're not too shotgun happy. Obviously, on third down you can be in shotgun, but the more you can be under center on first second down, I think is really important to uh be efficient on those downs as well. >> Aaron, how different is a Mike McCarthy training camp to maybe some of the other ones that you've participated in over the course of your career? >> Well, you got to understand like I was with Mike in 2006 and that was back when you could do double days. So, we had 2-1-2-1 alternating. My first year was was double days for the first couple weeks of camp. Um so, training camp's way different. It's way easier. It's like a mental grind. It's not a physical grind the way it used to be. Now, knowing Mike and his Pittsburgh uh grit background, I'm sure he's going to try and uh make some some gagger practices out there, but uh but the rules are in place where there's a certain time frame. I don't know if it's 2 hours and 20 minutes or 2:30 or something. Back then, we used to joke about how quarterbacks would be on the field like 20 minutes before practice. We'd have 3 hour and 15 minute practice. We'd get into like the I used to say the real practice like uh an hour and 45 in cuz it'd be so much individual work and those were real practices. Those were not a whole lot of fun. Um so, I'm not sure what the Mike McCarthy uh training camp practice will be like, but I know that the OTAs were were crisp. You guys saw them out there. It was crisp. Things were moving fast in and out of team periods and I expect more of the same. >> Have you learned Two more, guys. Two more. >> Have you learned anything about DK this offseason that maybe you didn't know uh over last year or last season? >> Yeah, a lot a lot uh personal stuff for sure. Um again, like uh you know, I spent a lot of time with DK in the offseason and during the season outside the facility and you know, 4 days um at the ranch, you know, I found out more about him than I'd known in that time. And I think that's part of the the uh plot of being uh kind of a man you know, an alpha in this society uh today. It's hard to be vulnerable and you know, I was trying to create the space where that was kind of normal. So, I I you know, I tried to be as honest and open as possible about kind of my own life and background and struggles and frustrations and a lot of guys opened up and and shared some really personal stuff. And I'm not obviously not going to share that here, but um but yeah, man, I just have so much respect for DK and kind of how we grew up and where he's from and I just felt like I really got to know him and now, you know, before we were friends, but now I just feel like that word has a different meaning to it. >> Aaron, you said you wanted to ask a question >> What excites you about this receiver room this year with the addition of Michael Pittman and drafting Jalen Bernard and another year with Roman Wilson as well? >> Yeah, I mean those those three, DK obviously I think this offense uh you know, suits DK. Uh I think Michael in his humility as a Z asking him to do a lot of stuff that you know, I feel like we did when we were really good on offense uh in Green Bay in in 20 and 21 with the with Davante at the X, you know, in the DK role, Allen Lazard in the Z uh and Marquez and you know, you got to stick stick head in there and block and and then off of that some action stuff and then having a guy in the slot that can get open. Um which you know, I I mean Jalen's going to get some opportunities, but I think the guy out of anybody that's really shown this new staff because it is a new staff, you know, a lot of great tape is Roman Wilson. I think Roman had a really nice spring. Um got to know him, you know, on a deeper level during that trip, which was fun, but uh I expect, you know, I expect him to to start to make some some splash plays. He did in the spring. And I expect him to have a nice camp. >> All right. Sarah. >> [clears throat]

title: Asante Samuel Jr. SHINES, Drew Allar's first test, OL shuffles, McCarthy's camp | Steelers Rewind
text: What's going on everybody? Welcome back to Steelers training camp we want Nick Farabaugh here. The first practice in Latrobe is officially in the books. Mike McCarthy first practice in his Steelers coaching career. Uh McCarthy certainly [snorts] has a different style of practicing from Mike Tomlin. Much more fast-paced, high octane. Um when you see Mike McCarthy and his practices, there's a few things that are different. They're just really fast-paced. There's not a lot of down time. You know, Mike Tomlin would have them out here at 1:55 and they'd practice till 4:15 sometimes. Mike McCarthy had the guys out here at an hour and a half of really crisp, brisk work. Um lots of individuals. There was a dueling team period where they had the the first and second team and third and fourth teams kind of split off one another so guys maximized reps probably got more reps than they would have in a normal team period. Um we saw them just do seven-on-sevens. We saw them do a lot of situational things, a lot of different situational stuff, two minutes and two minutes from different areas of the field, different plays from different areas. It was a lot different. The situational aspect of it definitely was changed. So, a McCarthy practice looks different. But let's talk about that practice. I guess let's start with the DBs. I think the DBs were the story of today in a lot of ways. That and the offensive line. Um the defensive backs I think had really good days. Asante Samuel Jr. for my money was the best player on the football field today just in terms of a win or loss perspective. If people were asking, I think he was a big huge winner. Uh two PBUs on DK Metcalf in the uh in the the two-minute drills. One thrown down the sideline that he got his his hand in on. Another one he broke right on. It was really impressive to watch that. Daylen Everett had a nice really uh really good competitive play through the hands on a slot fade that I thought was really impressive. Um Jamel Dean got beat twice by Brandon Smith, who's a wide receiver out of Iowa. He had a nice day, you know, someone we didn't talk about in that sleepers kind of mold. He could be someone to watch, too. Really nice back shoulder catches. He had another really good catch in seven-on-sevens on a dig route. Um, so I thought he was the winner in terms of the wide receivers today. A few really, really good plays though. Brandon Echols had a pick, you know, because Patrick Queen got a really good uh tip uh on a ball thrown up the seam towards Darnell Washington by Rodgers. And Echols brought down with the tip. Keanu Neal Holcomb broke up a pass. Um, the inside linebackers had a really good, good day in that regard. And then and Queen uh had another pass breakup on Freiermuth. But but Holcomb had broke up that pass and it kind of bounced up right into the hands of Payton Wilson. Like a lot of good stuff from the defense today. Um, T.J. Watt, Alex Highsmith, Nick Herbig, Quincy Roche all moving around the line. They're playing left, right, over the middle. There was a three outside linebacker package we saw with Herbig over the middle. Um, I saw T.J. Watt just long-arm Dylan Cook straight to the ground to the seat of his pants. I thought that was pretty impressive. I did see Darnell uh Darnell Washington as well kind of handle some of them. Even without pads, he's just so big and strong. He looks a little trimmer, but man, he's potentially the best blocking tight end in football. From the offensive side of things, Broderick Jones was back on the football field. I thought it was good to see him out there. Um, he looks slim still. He looks a little heavier than he did in the spring, but still not completely back to football shape. He played mostly at left tackle, second team left tackle. Flipped to a little bit of left and right, did a little bit of both. Max Mitchell was actually going in a little bit with the first team. They were kind of rotating Eyioma Njongmeta and Cook in different areas. Cook would usually go over to left tackle and Eyioma Njongmeta would come in at right tackle just to give Fa'alataliga a break. And Fa'alataliga only stayed on the left side. It certainly seems like Troy Fautanu and Mason McCormick are going to be your left tackle and your left guard. Um, in terms of right guard, we saw Spencer Anderson play mostly there. We did see Jennings Dunker with the third team today, not the second team. So, that's something to keep an eye on with Dunker. He needs to work his way up the depth chart. I did think Drew Allar had some moments today. In seven-on-seven, he had four tough passes. One sailed behind him. He threw the pick that that Holcomb tipped and and kind of tipped into the air for Peyton Wilson to go for, but I thought he also had a really good ball where he threw it up the seam for a touchdown to to Robert Tonyan. That was a really impressive throw. He also had a really good pump fake where he kind of lasered one into Max Herlman. That was really good to see. The two wide receivers, Jeremy Bernard and Roman Wilson, that are continuing to battle out for that wide receiver three job, had a few miscommunications today with Aaron Rodgers. That's going to be something to really keep an eye on as we continue to move through practices. Those young guys have to get on the same page. We know Rodgers is picky about his uh offense and and really his receivers as well. >> All right, folks. Make sure to like, comment, subscribe. Turn on the notification bell for more, and thanks for watching.

title: McCaffrey, Green, McKivitz on Training Camp Progress | 49ers
text: So far for you, three days in? >> Uh, it's going good. Um, making a lot of plays, learning the defense. And just getting along with the guys. Like we all growing together. >> How much different um games what Raheem is implementing from what you guys did the last two seasons? >> Uh It's easier to play faster and uh um I feel like he's finer more detailed with just like realistic things and uh it's uh like a lot less thinking and it's geared towards uh me and the guys like our our strong suits and what we do well. >> You guys seem to have a really good practice on Monday. Very kind of aggressive, a lot of pass breakups. I mean, is that sort of your strength? That sort of um what what Raheem described as sticky coverage, being kind of physical early on and in down. >> Yeah, just being able to to get attached to guys or being able to contest catches, make plays, challenge guys more. So yeah, that's what he wants and that fits us. That's the type of ball players we are. >> The other day, Deebo said he felt like you really opened up to him this off season and then how would you just describe like your comfort level at this point in your career going into into year three? >> I don't played a lot of ball my first two years.
