And then at that point it's just about judging the ball and playing the ball. >> What was in here? >> This offseason Kyle Shanahan said that he challenges you because he has high expectations for you and he wants you to meet those expectations. How do you kind of view that as far as you know coming off of the season you had last year and knowing that your coach, you know, sets a a pretty high standard for you? >> Um as a as just me personally, the type of man I am, the type of ball player I am, um I know who I am. I don't necessarily need anyone to tell me who I am, but knowing that somebody like like uh coach Kyle, uh coach Shanahan, knowing somebody like him uh is is there to push me, is there not to let me slack, is there to be on my back like me and him uh talk and we have conversations and he's he's told me how he sees me and it's kind of similar to how I see myself and what I'm capable to do and everything I want out of this game. So um I appreciate him for this this pushing me. Like, you know, if it's a play where he feel like I can make it because he knows the type of ball player I am, he knows my talent and what I'm capable of, I can't do nothing but respect it cuz I feel like I can make that play, too. So um me just pushing myself is one thing, but having a coach that believes in you, that believes that you can be one of the best, believes that you can be, you know, one of the top guys and all this and that is give you more confidence to just to go work harder cuz you know that you're not going to let yourself slack, but you know that he's not going to let yourself slack, either. >> DeMeco said he feels like your confidence level is higher, especially when going against guys like Mike Evans. Has it raised and how do you feel going into this third season? >> Uh I wouldn't necessarily say that it raised. Um I've always been a competitor. Um no matter who it was, if you go back to my rookie year and watch me guard Tyreek Hill, they it doesn't matter who I was playing against. I'm my biggest competitor. It's just the fact of you get older, you get more experience, So, you know what guys are are finna come with and what guys are finna do. Um I wouldn't really say that oh just cuz I'm going Mike Evans is like or this past off season is like oh yeah, I'm more of a competitor now. I've always been a competitor. That's why I'm here, you know, cuz I've always competed. >> You're you're a competitive player and they added Jack Jones to the room. Jones is kind of known as a real dog, a real competitor. What have you noticed from him? Anything stand out about his game? >> Um Jack's a Well, first off Jack's a a cool guy to be around and me and Jack have a conversation things like that. He's a real savvy football player and Jack has a real good ball skills. I give him that. He he competes just like we all do and I've been like real impressive Jack coming in. He plays a real a real you know, savvy aggressive type of playing style when it comes to playing the ball. And it's like things from each defensive back in a in the room each guy does something extremely well and if somebody does something extremely well and that could be something that you lacking, I feel like you should try to pick that up. Or you should try to learn from what you can cuz we all in this together basically. >> Outside of being the first game of the season, what are you most looking forward to about your trip down to Australia? I'm really just looking at going to looking at uh well, looking forward to going to competing with the guys. Just going to getting the W. Going to compete, going to put all this work, all this training camp stuff, all these meetings to use and just going to do it on the big stage. That's really what I'm looking forward to. Going to work with my guys. >> You you talked about you now being able to look at the formation and kind of you know, say okay, it's going to be one or three routes maybe. Is that stuff that you did in college a lot or have you recognized that that's something that's required in the NFL to have success? >> I did it in college, but the NFL is more detailed and complex than college football. And in college football, I was basically a as coach used to tell me just go guard that guy man-to-man and I'll just go press him and follow him all over the field the whole entire game. So, uh now it's a lot more you got to play off, you got to press, you know, you got to read this, you got to read this and you can't be late. Ain't no hesitation in our game. Once you see it, go. Like even if you're wrong, go. Like all that hesitation not going to work. So, um just the NFL just it's more complex and detailed. You know, you could make a make a play and it's the difference between a pick and a PBU and you're only 2 in off. But that hesitation or just that not processing just as fast as you need to, that's the biggest difference between college and the NFL. The game is way faster. >> So, so for you to have back Fred having Dre and and Nick Bosa for for your own game so you can focus more on things cuz now you got all the support from these superstars. >> When you see guys like that that you play with, uh you know, the standards is always high. And uh you know, just knowing that they got your back, just knowing that, you know, they're going to give it their all, just knowing the type of dogs they are, the type of guys that they got, you look left and you look right and you see some savages, but on the side of you it's like, oh yeah, I'm ready. Like I I don't really need uh to go speech, I don't really need motivation. I know who on my right and who on my left. So, I love having those guys around me out there on the field. >> A couple more. >> Was that Was that ever initially frustrating your first 2 years cuz it sounds in some ways much more simple than just follow a guy around all over the field. What Did you ever be Were you ever thinking like, I wish I could just do that. This is really much harder. >> Uh not really cuz uh offenses scheme up more in the NFL. So, um it's kind of hard to just play man the whole game in the NFL. So, I wouldn't necessarily necessarily say that it was frustrating cuz it's just part of football. Like you got to grow and I feel like in my first 2 years I've done made a good amount of plays, you know, just playing the game of football and especially being a young player playing as much as I played my first 2 years. So I wouldn't necessarily say it was frustrating cuz I didn't have success. I don't have down moments that's what I learned from. So um Yeah, I wouldn't really say that it was frustrating or anything like that. It's just a part of the process. >> Bernard, it seems like this week you're doing a lot of raking the ball out and it seems almost like a point of emphasis maybe more so than a year ago. Is that something that Raheem emphasizes or is that something that you've decided to do? >> Uh that's kind of always you know been a thing. Um It is growing and understanding the game better and understanding when the ball is loose, when the ball isn't loose. You know, understanding how ball carriers are thinking. You always want to try to take the ball away, you know, any chance that you get and got guys like Fred who does it like in his sleep. You know, you kind of just pick games up from being around like pick the game up from being around all these great players. So it was just a point of emphasis that personally I wanted to make but our coaches do emphasize but it's always been something that they emphasize. I just wanted to put it in my head more just like oh and I'm going out there just not doing it if I can. No, it's like at the end of this play go punch the ball. At the end of this play go punch the ball. >> What is the biggest lesson you've learned in the over the last two seasons? >> Um the biggest lesson I probably learned is just take accountability even when it's not your fault. Like even when you know, any no matter who it is, you know, the media, anybody, the player, whoever it may be, you know, point the finger at you. You know, just approach it how you're doing real life as a man just take accountability and go and you know, just fix it. Go and try to work better to you know, accomplish the goal to do whatever you got to do. All that pointing the finger, all that crying and complaining, that's not going to get you nowhere. Take it for what it is, even if you know, it's right or wrong and then move on and just go get the job done. >> Trying to find your voice in the building since coming into the NFL. Obviously, you know, you're just naturally quieter coming into a new situation and beyond the football stuff, just being around the guys and and feeling comfortable to have, you know, the conversations and and I guess be comfortable in your own skin here. >> Can I ask the first part of that question again? >> What's it been like trying to find like your voice? >> I don't I don't really say it's me trying to find my voice. I know exactly who I am. I'm the type of person that I don't always say a lot, but I call things a spade for a spade and I always like I speak when I need to speak. You got two ears and one mouth for a reason. So, um it's just when you grow and get older and the younger guys who look up to you, like younger guys who asking you questions and you know, trying to see the the way to do things and I'm like I I've been there, I've done that or you know, I done did this or I done had success doing this. It's like um I you you you want to help. You want to help people. You you want to help guys grow. You want to help everything just elevate because if we all elevate, then we we better as a team. We're only as strong as the weakest link, basically. >> All right. Who's first? >> Your favorite thing about training camp and your least favorite thing. >> Least favorite thing would be the hotel. Favorite thing is I would say getting back into like the season. Like it's the start of a new season, you get to be around guys again and it's just the it's from 6:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m. is with the guys and just kind of that camaraderie building and obviously playing football is a lot of fun, too. So, that's kind of the fun and not so fun part is the hotel, being away from my dogs and and wife. >> Is the actual hotel kind of run down, too? >> No, the Santa Clara Marriott is a great hotel, okay? No, it hasn't changed since I've been there, but I got a great room with a patio and it's great, so I'm not complaining about it. >> Uh Furster said that he felt like Pooh and Colby had I think he said awesome offseasons. You know, you watch this these guys pretty closely. What do you think of their development? >> Yeah, I mean, he's right. Um you know, obviously Connor, you know, he's training in Iowa. I don't get to see him as much, but just from, you know, seeing what he looks like now, uh looks like a completely different player than when, you know, his his rookie year, when, you know, guys come in kind of big-eyed and trying to figure it out. Um you know, he understands a little more, he's playing a little faster. Uh you see he's put on a little weight, too, so he looks good and obviously Don, love playing next to him. Um and just talked to him yesterday about, you know, he understands a lot more and and every year you're in this system, you pick up little nuances, whether it's you know, how you can use the play that's called to your advantage and and kind of how, you know, Kyle schemes it and Furf coaches it. Um he's picked up on that and just uh the level of confidence he's at and and where he's at in his development, uh it's cool to see and, you know, every guy's come in ready to go, that's what camp's about and you know, obviously the first 2 weeks and now we got pads going on, so, you know, now's when the real the real thing starts. >> You're You're about >> It's beneficial in the way that >> that's all we see in the regular season. So, now that we get to go against it um starting in August instead of game planning it for the first week in in September, it makes it a lot easier for us. Obviously, it just it makes it fresher in our minds. We're getting a lot more. It's not, you know, a typical found jetting front. Um so, we're getting a lot of looks with five downs, spinners, with D-linemen off the ball. So, it just kind of puts us ahead of the game in what we're going to see, you know, in the season more than just a four-down base front. So, um a lot more schematically different for us, and and it helps us in the long run. >> Yeah. >> I mean, you know, they're big. They're not new to the game, not new to the NFL. Would you say it makes you guys like more confident? >> Uh of course. I mean, that anytime you can you can go against a defense that you don't see until September before then is is great for us instead of trying to relearn a new defense um in September. So, it's great that we get to go against them now, and we get to see all the kinds of different looks. It just helps us, you know, prepare earlier. >> You're about 6 weeks away from starting the season down in Australia. So, um at what point do you start thinking about a Myles Garrett or getting your body clock matched up since it's 5:45 in the morning right now there? >> What is it? 10:55 or 10:50 kickoff down there a.m.? Um when it comes to those guys, I mean, Myles obviously having in the division now. Uh who knows who else they may add or may not. Um our just our division's good. It is what it is. Um that's what you want. Obviously, the defending Super Bowl champs are are in our division. So, we're in we're there's no game where we're going to see a bad player. Um that kind of clock starts, you know, usually 2 weeks out. Like right now, we're worried about installing installing runs, installing passes, going against our defense, kind of scheming them. Um but really just getting a feel for our offense and how we're going to gel as a group. And then obviously, 2 weeks out is kind of when, you know, things are settled and and we're ready to rock and that's when we're game. But um yeah, it'll be it'll be interesting with a 1050 clock, but uh we're down under, so it'll be cool. >> You ready to see Nick like across from you in practice again? It's been a It's been a while. >> It's been a little bit. About time he gets out there, but no, anytime you can go against Nick, it like you said, Cam, it speeds it up, so uh the more looks we can get against a guy like him, uh it only helps us in the long run going against that kind of speed, power, all these one of the best edge rushers in the game, so um the faster he can get out there, the better for us. >> With a couple of injuries, it seems like there's some opportunities for guys like Ke'Shawn Black and De'Shawn Shrubling right now. What would have been kind of your early impressions particularly of those two guys and the way they've embraced the opportunities they're getting? >> Fast and running hard, which is nice to see. Um when you get young guys that come in and can just hit the hole and hit it fast and there's no question on, you know, second-guessing or chopping their feet in the hole, it makes our job a lot easier. Uh and obviously in the passing game, too, I think a couple of those guys had some nice catches out in the flats today, as well. So, um when you get young guys who are confident, they're not questioning themselves and just hitting it, obviously you can correct that, but hesitation, it really you can't correct it, you know, guys got to figure it out, but when they're coming in right now, running as hard as they are, um they got great leadership in that room with Bobby T and and C-Mac, so it's nice to see it early on. >> Is that unusual for a rookie particularly like outside zone stuff to be as decisive as as you're >> It is. I mean, colleges aren't really running it, so when um I mean, there are a few, but when you get guys who can come in and run it like they are, uh it's nice to see and it it makes our jobs a lot easier. >> When you add somebody like Mike Evans and all the roster that you guys already have, cuz at the end of season last year, it seemed like there's times that you were holding on the board, Rock was finding the spaces, but he couldn't find someone to throw to. To add a piece like that and then seeing the young guys being able to do these things, does it he your life easier? >> Sure does. When you can get guys open and not hold on the ball for 3 to 4 seconds, I mean you get it out quick, it's a lot harder on D ends, it's a lot harder on defenses, makes our job easier. And then obviously running the ball helps, too. When you can run the ball, have possession, and then you get a deep threat like Mike, it changes the the scope of game. So, when you have that threat, and it kind of keeps the defense from stacking a box. It helps us in the run, it helps in the pass, so you know, those weapons are essential to us being good on offense and and then playing well together. >> Rico has a reputation for having a a good personality, open personality. Have you seen that already? And just what are your early assessments of of him? >> Yeah, it's a good group of rookies, I mean they're working on their jokes right now, but you can see them obviously working before practice with Fur and and Rome. Just willingness to work, I think is one of the biggest things that these guys have. They've got a lot of talent. They're very open about it. And they're learning, so obviously it's their first three practices of of their first camp, but you can see the talent in them and and what those guys possess. And Rico especially, he's got great feet and hands. He's going to have to learn a little bit of our scheme and try and fit into that. And we're, you know, learning football's to is going to be the big thing for him, the talent he has is he's he's a good player, so we'll see once the pads come on and and one-on-ones and how that works, but they're off to a good start. >> What jokes are you working on? >> Huh? >> I don't tell jokes anymore. I'm past that point. >> Well, you're one of the one of the leaders on this team. Obviously the Shanahan accident impacts things, but does it Do you think it's going to impact your football team? It seems like you got a lot of coaches, a lot of veterans here. What is the impact of that accident on this team? >> Um I mean, it sucks. No one wants to be in a car accident. Obviously Kyle wants to be out there coaching us and and leading meetings and that's kind of what we look forward to in the morning is our protected team stuff and and just his, you know, how he views the game and connects offense and defense. Not having him in there is tough, but obviously, like you said, we've got a group of guys who um multiple Pro Bowls, coaches who have been here together for a while, players who have been here together for a while, and young guys who have bought in. So, um obviously, we miss him, but on the field it's the same business as usual. He's watching it, coaching it, uh and then it's passed down through his guys. So, um it sucks he's not out there, but, you know, I know he's going to come back as fast as possible, but, you know, we're not skipping a beat. >> Christian, twice for his workouts, does he look as explosive as ever when >> Who? Christian? >> He's Christian McCaffrey. He looks great. >> Connor Colquitt was kind of thrown into the fire in his first season and, you know, he had some challenges as in it as a rookie. Is he someone that reached out to you about your the beginning of your career? Did you guys talk at all? >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's hard to get Connor to say a few words, um but the the words we have have had you know, he'll ask about, you know, what's it like? How do you slow the game down? Um in your experience, how do you flush plays? Uh and that's the one thing is once a bad play happens, how fast can you flush it and move on to the next? Um and that's what we're seeing, you know, this year coming in that just another year added to a player can help and it's not just, you know, what's going on. Um so, the slower you can make the game, obviously, it's a fast one, but the slower you can make it, um it's better for a player. So, uh for him to come in and and realize that at where he's at and where he wants to be, um it just shows his experience and and kind of, you know, where he's at right now. So, it's it's good to see him asking questions and then wanting to get better. >> I know it's very very early in and Stribling is is a rookie, but have you noticed in the spring or early on in training camp without pads his ability to help the tackles out with the way he can block in the running game. >> Um we got a group of receivers who are blocking right now. Um and that's the one thing that we coach most is our receivers in blocking. That's what Kyle demands, that's what our offense demands. Uh we can do our best up front, um our tight ends, our fullbacks, but if we don't have receivers who are going to get in there and and get muddy and dirty, um and you're seeing young guys who are buying in and that's the biggest thing that we've always had and needed and, you know, wanted is young guys in. We saw all of this last year's class, um and they played well and then we're going to need the same thing. So for a guy like Sherrod to come in and already be doing that, you're seeing Jake Caming doing it, Malik Turner doing it. So guys who are doing this already um in camp, we'll see. In 2 days pads come on, we'll see if it keeps going, but I got a lot of confidence in those guys. >> of know your off-season training, but there was one thing that you were doing this year where you looked like you were on the ground. You were you're kind of moving to the left and to the right. Is that like for your hips? Uh what was that and how do you feel your your off-season went? >> Feel great, man. Yeah, I think it went well. Uh you know, always trying to get better, find different ways to to get better and uh whether it's bringing new people in, different ideas, but you know, sometimes I'll share little snippets of the off-season here or there, but um a lot of those drills are just, you know, fun, different ways to do mobility and continuing to just train the whole system. >> Do you analyze your previous season and say, "I think I can work on this, this, and this." And then tailor your your off-season workouts to whatever you conclude? >> Yeah, that's part of it. I think it's uh it's not that simple, but that's definitely part of it. >> Can you kind of share what you focused on this this past off-season? >> Yeah, I mean, I look, I think every off-season um you you got to address what what's going on, but at the same time it's you training a whole system. So everything matters. Speed matters, strength matters, mobility, everything. It's a you know, the you're one one system, quick twitch, all that stuff. So, there's a way to build a base and kind of try to peak and you know, it's never linear, but that's that's kind of the way I look at it is you're training a system, not just one thing. You know, if you train the system, everything will start to get better. >> You started training with Ido Portal. I know he's not necessarily he's worked with a whole bunch of football guys, but what is it that has changed or what have you feel felt differently after working with him? >> Yeah, he's a special person, man. We had a amazing summer. I was really grateful I got to spend a lot of time with him and the rest of, you know, the training staff. Um a lot of long days, long hours, uh put so much into it and had a lot of fun. Uh learning a lot, unlearning a lot, um and just always good to have new perspectives um in training as as you continue to prolong your career. >> Anything what one particular thing that he kind of emphasizes throughout his practice or is it >> No, I think that the the whole point is it's not one thing. Yeah, I think that that would be the point is that uh you know, it's it's everything together. Um and it it's again, it's it's almost too too much to even give you an answer with with words, but it was a a heck of an experience. Um obviously, we still did a bunch of speed and strength stuff, but uh yeah, he's he's a brilliant mind when it comes to movement, the body, the mind, everything. >> Is it more like to get more explosivity or explosiveness? >> That's part of it. Yeah, I mean, it's it's it's everything. Yeah, I mean, there's you know, in football, you train >> Are you a guy that enjoys training camp? Do you like look at it as a way to kind of ramp up? How do you approach training camp in in general? >> I love it, man. Yeah, I love training camp. I think it's uh it's always difficult, but I think that's where you you build your callus. That's where um you get to make mistakes full speed. You get a try new things out. Um and so, it's uh definitely a good time of the year where um you get to grow as a team. You get to get better every day, and you get to go out there and play football, man. I don't take one day for granted, and just feel super fortunate to be out there playing with everybody. >> Christian, given the difficulty of being out there in training camp this first year when he comes to Carolina, does he come to you for any advice on how to get through each day, or how to make sure that he's where he needs to be, doing what he needs to do to kind of have a successful training camp going into the season? >> Yeah, definitely. Uh, he's a pro, man. He he came in, and you can tell he's mature. You can tell he he knows how to work, he knows how to learn, and uh, he's made of the right stuff. So, he compliments our our room, our team really well. >> Christian, you recently became a 30-year-old running back. So, you're supposed to fall off the cliff, you know, any day now. Uh, uh, did this birthday have any significance to you as it relates to your career and things you want to accomplish? >> Uh, no, it didn't. Um, you know, I I I love football, man. I never looked at the age thing. Um, I like looking at the guys who played really well later in their careers, but no, I mean, that's that's, you know, hearsay. You know, I I it's not nothing, you know, that's why I approach it differently than I do 7 years ago, you know, I'm not um, naive enough to think you can just keep doing the same thing, but when it comes to Sundays and playing football, I I love the plan we have, and to just go out there and continue to work and get better, but um, you know, one thing I love about playing this position in this sport is you never have it figured out. Uh, every day is a new day, you get to compete, you get to play, you get to learn, you get to grow, and that's the way I'm approaching it again this year, but I feel great, and I I can't wait for this year. He's awesome, man. Raheem's awesome. He's explosive, he sees the hole really well. He's got a really good feel for things, he's got the right mentality, and uh, again, he just compliments our room, our our team really well. >> But, older than a lot of rookies, I think he's 24, almost 25. Can you kind of see that in him? He's supposed to be good at that pass protection and kind of some little things that perhaps rookies don't always have sharpened early on. >> Yeah, you can see it. You see him? Yeah. Now, he's stacked, man. You can definitely see it. He's You can tell he's played at high level of football. He's played mature football. He's Again, he's made it I can't say enough good He's exactly what you would want a rookie to come in and be like. And again, I think our whole running back room is great. And he he complements it so well in the way he runs. I think when you look at him his rookie year and then you go look at me my rookie year I they look very different in age. >> You said you like to look at guys who had success later in their careers. What what are you looking for and are there certain threads you see or do you even reach out to some of those guys that >> Yeah, I mean I Look, I think I don't make a big deal out of the whole age thing. Um it does nothing for me. I think that's something that, you know, with rightfully so media will will bring up, but for me, man, I just show up every day and work my butt off. Continue to work on the things I work on and I don't I don't think about my age. If I did, that would not be wise, you know, it's That does nothing for me. So, I just think about continuing to grow, continuing to go out there and ball. I don't, you know, It's funny like you turn 30 and people bring it up and like 2 days ago I was 29 and now, you know, so it's For me, man, I just I just keep focusing on getting better. That's all I've ever done. That's all I'll ever do. And again, just I feel so fortunate to play this game. I want to play as long as I can and um I have no intention of slowing down. >> Walter Payton Craig is going to be enshrined in the Hall of Hall of Fame next week. I realize by the time he was done with his career I'm not sure you were born, was he any sort of influence or did you look at the way he played? I've seen a lot of similarities between you two. >> Yeah, he's uh he was a pioneer, man. He he was one of the first guys who really could do it all to to rush for 1,000 yards and catch for 1,000 yards in that era is different than doing it now. And so I have the utmost respect for him. I think, you know, when you look at how good those teams were and how many big names they had, a lot of times he gets left out. And, you know, I'm so happy that he got a gold jacket cuz he absolutely deserves it. And uh yeah, definitely seen all of them. His those eyes when he was running through the hole. Bobby T brings that up all the time. His his knee drive, all that. He was a stud. >> With Sean, De'Shawn last week talked about his his blocking in the running game. I know it's early in camp and pads aren't on, but have you felt any of his blocks at at any point? Or are Has there been enough to for you to form an impression on his run blocking? >> Um I mean, I we I see his college tape and he does a hell of a job at We haven't had pads on yet, so it's not, you know, he's Guys aren't out there just crack backing our our secondary. even if they want to. But it's No, he he he plays full speed, man. It's another rookie who I think when you look at our whole rookie class, it's just a lot of guys who put their head down and work. And and that's exactly what you want, you know, that's what our vets do, that's what our young guys do. And so collectively, hopefully we continue to rise. But he's a hell of a player, man. He's He's got a great build. He's physical, he can run. And the more and more he can learn the playbook and learn this offense to where he's playing fast, that's it's he's going to be a hell of a player. >> He was in here earlier talking about Mike Evans and just his impact on the wide receivers room. Have you noticed the competition level between that group rising? Yeah, I mean, we're we're 3 days in and and, you know, we're we're so focused on our own jobs all the time. Um but when Mike Evans is in there, it's hard not to, you know, listen to what he's saying and watch what he's doing and kind of hear how he sees the game and to for a young guy to come into a a receiver room and have somebody like that as a as a mentor is I you know I hope those guys take it and and and run with it because that's a special special guy, special player and glad he's on our team. >> Chris, last one. >> Christian, what was your non-football highlight of the off-season? >> Oh man, just spending time with my daughter. Yeah, watching her grow every day was amazing. Uh you know, it's it's crazy how fast it's going, but that would definitely be my highlight. Appreciate you guys.

title: 49ers Players Speak to Media Following Day 3 of Training Camp Practice | 49ers
text: Christian, you're kind of known for your off-season training, but there was one thing that you were doing this year where you looked like you were on the ground. And we're, you know, learning football's to is going to be the big thing for him, but um the the talent he has is he's he's a good player, so um we'll see once the pads come on and and one-on-ones and how that works, but um they're off to a good start. >> What jokes are they working on? >> Huh? >> I don't tell jokes anymore. I'm past that point. >> You're one of the one of the leaders on this team. Obviously the Shanahan accident impacts things, but does it do you think it's going to impact your football team? It seems like you got a lot of coaches, a lot of veterans here. What is the impact of that accident on this team? >> Um I mean it sucks. You know, no one wants to be in a car accident. Uh obviously Kyle wants to be out there coaching us and and leading meetings, and that's kind of what we look forward to in the morning is, you know, our protective team stuff and and just his, you know, how he views the game and connects offense and defense. Not having him in there is tough, but obviously, like you said, we've got a group of guys who um multiple Pro Bowlers, coaches who have been here together for a while, players who have been here together for a while, and young guys who have bought in. So, um obviously we miss him, but on the field it's the same, business as usual. He's watching it, coaching it, uh and then it's passed down through his guys. So, um it sucks he's not out there, but you know, I know he's going to come back as fast as possible, but you know, we're not skipping a beat. >> Christian, twice for his workouts, does he look as explosive as ever when >> Who? Christian? >> He's Christian McCaffrey. He looks great. >> Connor Colby was kind of thrown into the fire in his first season and you know, he had some challenges as you know, as a rookie. Is he someone that reached out to you about your the beginning of your career? Did you guys talk at all? >> Yeah, I mean, it's it's hard to get Connor to say a few words, but the the words we have have had uh you know, he's asked about, you know, what's it like? How do you slow the game down? In your experience, how do you flush plays? And that's the one thing is once a bad play happens, how fast can you flush it and move on to the next? And that's what we're seeing, you know, this year coming in that just another year added to player can help and it's not just you know, what's going on. So, the slower you can make the game, obviously it's a fast one, but the slower you can make it, it's better for a player. So, for him to come in and and realize that at where he's at and where he wants to be, it just shows his experience and and kind of, you know, where he's at right now. So, it's it's good to see him asking questions and then wanting to get >> I know it's very very early in and Skribbling is is a rookie, but have you noticed in the spring or early on in training camp without pads his ability to help the tackles out with the way he can block in the running game? >> We got a group of receivers who are blocking right now. And that's the one thing that we coach most is our receivers in blocking. That's what Kyle demands, that's what our offense demands. We can do our best up front, our tight ends, our fullbacks, but if we don't have receivers who are going to get in there and and get muddy and dirty, and you're seeing young guys who are buying in and that's the biggest thing that we've always had and needed and you know, wanted is young guys who buy in. We saw all of last year's class and they played well and then we're going to need the same thing so for a guy like Trevion to come in and already be doing that. You're seeing Jake Cowing doing it, Malik Turner doing it, so guys who are doing this already in camp, we'll see in 2 days pads come on. We'll see if it keeps going, but I got a lot of confidence in those guys that it will. Sweet. Thank you.

title: Klay Kubiak Talks to the Media Ahead of Training Camp Practice | 49ers
text: Morning everyone. How's it going? How these I guess these first couple practices now they look seems pretty much usual smooth as usual. Just a little bit more walkie-talkie and stuff. Yeah, I'm calling the plays to the quarterbacks but that's you know, I'm stepping up where I need to and but everything's been smooth. You know, our guys have come out and had the right mindset, and our tempo's been awesome, and practices have been really good. Just got to keep going, one day at a time. >> How does Brock seem to respond from I mean, he's obviously heard play calls from you before. How has he been through the first couple of days? >> Great. Yeah, haven't had any issues. Um, you know, I've I've have experience in camp of calling plays and and move the ball periods, and obviously in um preseason. It's just it's a long time between then and the season, but um yeah, they get used to it pretty quick, and then Kyle will be back out there at some point, and they'll get used to him. So, it's all going good. >> You added a lot of speed at receiver and at running back. Is the hope to try to create more space and and put more pressure on the defense? What was the kind of the mindset of the off season? >> Yeah, um always trying to add more speed and more explosiveness to our offense um every year. And you know, we were lacking in that last year. Uh you know, there's there's a lot of reasons why, but I think we definitely fell off in terms of our explosiveness as an offense, our yards after contact. So, we're trying to add players that add add value in that area, but um those things are those things are products of playing the right way, of running the football better, um of getting, you know, more opportunities in the pass game. When you run the ball better, there's more opportunities for play action explosives. Um it's it's all sorts of things. It's just it's a collective effort, and so we got the right guys out there that are working, and um you know, we've just got to keep getting better. >> It's early, but it seems like Mike Evans' presence alone in the wide receivers' room is going to up the competition, and there's you guys there. >> Absolutely. I mean, Mike being in there is one thing. You know, he's he's a vet, he's a pro, he knows how to work. He knows how to compete every day and get better. Um but you know, in my opinion, that that whole room is just is just taken a big step from last year to this year. There's continuity, there's there's guys who maybe missed time last year between Jordan and Jake and Camp, but they're out there every day, they're getting better. Um and I just see a lot of growth across the board, and those guys come out every day with the right mindset. Um they're on their assignments, they're working, they're competing, and it's going to be fun to watch that room kind of become what it does over this next, you know, however many weeks of training camp. And it's one of the positions where we have a lot of competition and I'm excited to see where it goes. >> You guys had a lot of um, injuries at that position last summer. Um, I think only a couple guys kind of escaped the the summer unscathed. Is is the the kind of new practice schedule, you know, the jog through yesterday part of a an an effort to keep everyone, the wide receivers, a little bit more fresh, healthy throughout the summer? >> Yeah, I mean, it's not it's definitely not just about the receivers, you know, we're never going to make an an adjustment to benefit one position group. It was a team thing and and just studying talking to different people around the league and looking at different ways people do camp. Um, you know, we just we just thought it was a smart adjustment for us to to not be going 3 days in a row of practice and the other thing other benefit of that was that everybody gets to practice every day. Um, and you know, we have days when we were doing our traditional 3-day block where a lot of vets would be missing that third day to just kind of take the workload off of them, but the way we're doing it now is everyone's out there every day and we don't have to compensate for a lower number in a in a practice, which is where sometimes you might get an injury when you're low on receivers one day or low on linemen or something, guys have to take more reps. So, we're trying to avoid that as best we can by adding that jog through day and yesterday was good, it was our first one and and hopefully we we get the results we want moving forward. >> On Sribling and on Sribling and Gillan Black and what you've seen from them in the past few days. >> Yeah, good work by both of those guys these first 2 days, long way to go. I mean I mean they're they're rookies and they got a long way to go to grow. The volume of the playbook's going to keep going up and they got to stay with it, but you can't ask for anything more in terms of what they've done so far. They are very sharp young men in terms of being on the details of their playbook. They practice extremely hard. They're very coachable and um, that's all you can ask from those guys they got to keep stacking days and getting better. >> Stribling and Jordan Watkins went to Nashville to work with Brock and and Mack. Did you Can you see a little difference in their level coming into training camp? >> Which guys did you say? >> Jordan Watkins and De'Jon Stribling. >> Um, well, Jordan, yeah. I mean, Jordan's taken a step. I mean, he's He went through a rookie year with ups and downs of injuries. And, he's been a lot more consistent. And, um, you like to see that. He was like that in the off season. He looks that way now. Um, I think the work with Brock over the summer for all those guys was huge. Um, not just from, you know, the football, but just the the the camaraderie and just being together and working together. Uh, that that's always an added benefit for those guys. And, so, and Strib as well, you know, Strib and I think Strib was there and Strib was here a lot in the summer working and training. So, um, again, that's that's all good. It's all just a starting point, though, and it gets us off to a good start. >> Coach, you're coming to training camp, and I know it's only been 2 days, but I'm sure you come in with a mindset of marks you want to hit each day. What have you kind of seen executed that you like through the first few days to of course build on throughout training camp? >> Yeah, you just You want to see guys come out with the right mindset every day. And, and what I mean by that is, you know, they they're preparing in their meetings, right? They're they're on the details of the practice script, um, which allows them to play fast, which allows them to play decisively cuz they're thinking with clarity. Uh, they're playing with a clear mind. You want to see that every day, okay? And, it gets harder as we go through camp because the volume goes up. That's that's one thing. Um, you want to see guys play play hard. You want to see guys play fast. You want to see guys play on their assignments cuz we're not in pads right now. So, there's You don't really see the physicality, but you want to see guys playing with detail and and assignment sound football. Um, and and you want to have great tempo in practice always. You got You want guys in and out of the huddle. You want guys lining up fast, motioning fast. You want good operation. And, uh, those are the standards of every practice, and they're no different in camp. And, so, we just That's our job as coaches to hold them to that every day and just keep coaching them on it. So. >> With the with the play learning the playbook for a rookie obviously like you're saying is challenging and it's going to be more and more. Um I mean how much extra time does that require of them? I guess just to study and and it's not specialized routes you want them to know every every spot for the most part still, right? >> Definitely. You're training guys to know I'm sorry you think about receiver, you know, yeah, some guys have a position but every position moves. Every position, you know, every position runs every route. Um and so you want guys to be versatile up front and the O-line you want guys to have versatility. Um with regards to the playbook, you know, it's it's not so much that the playbook is just is huge and there's so much. It's that things add up every day. You know, you you master the first day and then you go out there and set the second day and there's all this new stuff and there's these new stimuli and the defense is doing new things. And um you know, and that's the challenge, you know, of okay, I went out there today and I made maybe made a few mistakes. Can I put that to bed and come out the next day and try to have a clear mind. Um eventually we're going to go to the move the ball periods where nothing is scripted. So they don't have the ability to um you know, study the script and kind of know what plays they're going to get in practice. I I'm calling it or Kyle's calling it. So they don't know what play's coming. Can you hear the play in the huddle for the first time? Can you line up and know what to do? Those are the challenges that we're going to add to their plate as camp goes on. Um that's that's part of football. It's part of learning and um you know, the guys that are up for the challenge, they embrace it and they they grow from it and get better every day. So. >> Is the Z the most demanding of the three? >> I'm sorry? >> Is the Z receiver or the flanker the the most demanding of the >> I I wouldn't say that. Um you know, you you you could say the Z probably moves more in our in our offense cuz he's off the ball and um you know, there's maybe that's maybe more um common but as far as demanding the demands are the same to me for for all those guys and we want them going through all the same stresses and all the same mental and physical stresses. So, yeah. >> I know you want to look forward but just looking back at the way last year ended, you got two games against Seattle, 19 offensive possessions, no touchdowns, a couple of three field goals, I think. Obviously, you did an autopsy on the whole thing. What did you see? What did you learn? Where do you guys go from there? >> Um Thanks for the reminders, man. We We were not playing good ball in those games. You know, first of all, you give credit to Seattle. That was an That was an elite defense. Obviously, they're a championship team, you know, and um they got the better of us in those two games, you know, it it's it's not like we study it and go, "Oh, we got to do this is the thing that's going to make us now have 10 touchdowns in those two games." Like, we have to run the ball better. We have to be better on third down. I go back to that that week 18 game and we had something like 38 plays in the game. Well, we weren't good on third down. We didn't stay on the field. We had too many second and longs, which we're putting ourselves in bad situations. So, how do you fix that? You You go back to the start. You get better at your scheme. You You try to add players in free agency that are going to make you stronger in these areas. Um You know, when you go to the playoff game and you go, "Okay, we actually did move the ball better, but but we come out and we don't execute a short yardage and we get stopped on fourth and one. We have a turnover on our second drive. Um we have a huge third down in that in the second quarter of that game where we throw the ball over to Ricky and he doesn't come up with it. We end up getting a field goal." I mean, it's going to be a one-possession game if we make those plays and you know, there's so many things that go into it. We have to get better as a football team. We have to worry about us, you know, and you know, it's not just about beating Seattle. It's about putting our guys in position to be the best they can be so we can have a 17-game season and and let the chips fall where they may. So, um we got to learn from those games. Certainly, we got to learn, uh but we just got to get better as a team and keep going. >> Uh Curtis Samuel had a nice long ball to Junior Bergeron on on Monday. Where Where How's he doing and where is the the competition between him and Adrian Martinez at this point? >> Curtis is doing great and and first of all, the competition is for the between those guys is going to be all camp. And those guys are they've embraced it and those guys do a great job of coming out every day and and getting their minimal reps they get and getting the most out of them. They've done a good job so far. Um to me that that's going to emerge through the train through the uh preseason games. That's when those guys are going to get the most of their reps is in preseason. They're going to play a lot. Uh and that battle that competition will kind of play itself out and and the best whoever plays the best is probably going to end up winning that battle. Uh but as far as Curtis and Adrian go, Curtis is what we thought he was. I mean as far as the size, uh the mental strengths he has, and his ability to throw the football. Um it's been jumping out to us in these first 2 days and he's got to keep stacking days and getting better. Adrian's a pro. Adrian does things the right way. The ball goes where it needs to go when Adrian's in the game and the same thing, consistency, learning from mistakes, getting better each day, and and then the preseason games will dictate a lot of those those decisions. >> And how hard it is also to know that you have to put that lot of work, but you also got to think of all the traveling that you're going to be doing on that first game. It's also thousands of miles away. Was it challenging to prepare cuz obviously the bulk of work that you want to put, you also want to account for those long >> Yeah, I mean we can't get too far ahead, you know, of the travel. It's going to be different. It's going to be a a challenge certainly cuz it's so unique as far as how far we're going and and maybe how how long we'll be gone, but um I think we got to put the cart before the horse, which is we can't put the cart before the horse. We got to focus on our team right now, getting better. Um and then as we get closer to week one and that that travel, we'll probably have some adjustments to our schedule and and how we train, but uh for now we're just we're focused on getting >> I'd love to hear some of your thoughts on Kyle's uh composure these last couple days. I think it's safe to say it took a lot of guts for him to kind of own up to some of what he talked about yesterday in front of a group of reporters. I just want to hear what your opinions might be on just how he's been handling himself. >> Um I mean my opinion is Kyle's Kyle's an outstanding leader, an outstanding mentor. He's a great friend to me. Um and obviously we're, you know, all just glad he's he's doing well and recovering and um and that everything ended up kind of okay from that situation. Um you know, I just the thing that I feel really strongly kind of going through this um with our team is Kyle, it's just a reflection of of Kyle's leadership that, you know, he can kind of be absent in certain ways or not as involved in certain ways, but this building and this team can continue to press on and continue to um function at a high level. That's because he's enabled people to um to lead. He's enabled me, he's enabled our whole staff to just take on our jobs and and and and lead in our own way. And just cuz he might not be here in the same way uh for now and as he continues to heal, um you know, we're we're pressing on and we're still handling our business and our players are are handling it the right way. And then again, it's all credit to his leadership. It's the standard he set, it's the culture that him and John Lynch have set here. Um I'm honored to be a part of it and then as his friend, I'm I'm glad he's getting better and just kind of taking it day by day. >> Coach Shanahan, is he calling you up and getting updates from you or telling you to do anything? >> Uh Kyle's here every day. Kyle's, you he's definitely paying attention to what's going on out there. Uh you know, watching film and then and definitely involved, you know, um so it's it's not like he's he's absent in that way. So we're definitely communicating on certain things. >> So I'm just about kind of to follow up on that. We keep asking, you know, everyone that talks, you know, is Kyle reassuring you guys, but is there any conversation maybe between you and him or other coaches where you guys are reassuring him that everything's handled? >> We try to. Absolutely. Yeah, and and you know, I know Fred said when he got up here that we got this coach and uh that's our job is to to reassure Kyle that, you know, we we're very confident in the work we're doing. We're very I'm very confident coming in here every day and and doing my job and helping lead the offense and um and helping um support our assistant coaches who are doing a phenomenal job doing everyone's stepping up and just doing what we normally do, which is do our jobs and do it to a really high standard and take care of our business and I think Kyle knows that and I think he's very confident that we're all capable of that and so we can you know just keep getting through this and keep pushing one day at a time. So. Thanks guys. Have a good one.

title: Why the 49ers Waited Two Weeks to Come Clean About Kyle Shanahan's Crash
text: What's up? Welcome to 49ers after dark. You remember Jesse Naylor. I'm Grant Cohn. This is presented by PrizePicks. We're on our new time on Tuesday afternoon or evening on the East Coast. We thought we were going to be talking about Vita Vea today. I was streaming this morning talking about, I don't know, Kaylin Black or something and then I got a call saying to go to the 9ers facility ASAP. And I got there and all the beat writers were there and then we went to Kyle Shanahan's I'd never been to Kyle Shanahan's office. So, I think people have heard the story by now. I'll give a quick 60-second recap and then I want to get Jesse's thoughts and go from there. So, I reported last night that this was the other driver's fault because that's what it was reported online on this public government website that's run by the police. And Kyle brought us all in to say that that was factually incorrect. He wanted to say that he was at fault. It's 2 weeks from the day that the accident occurred in Palo Alto and we didn't hear about it until 3 days ago. Uh the conversation was like, how could this go unnoticed? When it finally came out, the details were wrong and um made the other person to be the perpetrator. He finally today, 2 weeks later, decided that it was time to tell the truth, the whole truth, or what he could say. And um he put it on himself. He was crying. He did the first 25 minutes like off the record because he was having a tough time composing himself. Then he let us turn on our our uh uh cameras, or not cameras, microphones, and he did it he did it again. He did the whole thing again. So, to me, I was there, it felt real, it felt authentic, it felt contrite. Um it didn't seem like he was trying to win points with us. It felt like he was um I've never felt I've never seen him seem that human in my life, which is why I was moved even though he was admitting that he almost killed himself and another person. Although thankfully the other person is just fine. What do you think of all this? >> I mean there's there's a lot to think. First of all, when it comes to Kyle Shanahan, credit to him, kudos to him for admitting fault because the story was going to run with itself. You had posted yesterday, it sounded like at least in the video you made he addressed you personally and was like, "Hey Grant, you know, you put out some information yesterday. It happened to be misinformation and not because of, you know, you did anything wrong. It was just the website was wrong as far as who is at fault. So, he wanted to clear that up." I also got to imagine just >> Palo Alto police put out a a statement real quick. I'm just going to read it. This was like >> Oh, okay. Yeah, let's do it. >> half an hour ago. Kyle Shanahan's statement that he provided is correct and that he was at found at fault for the collision. There was a clerical error in the preparation of the report that was transmitted to the state database. We are in the process of correcting that error. It is the officer's discretion at the scene of the collision as to whether they issue a citation to either party. It is not uncommon for officers to elect to not issue a citation to either party involved in a collision. Neither party in this situation was provided preferential treatment." End quote. >> Yeah, I mean, I've been in accidents and there have been no citations issued. I got day after Christmas last year, I got T-boned. Lady ran a red light, she didn't get a citation. So, I don't necessarily think it was preferential treatment, but that being said, Kyle Shanahan having kids, being a father myself, I got to imagine he's looking at this 21-year-old girl and was like, "I could have taken somebody's baby." That's traumatizing. >> Well, that's it. That could have been That could have been my daughter. That could have been my daughter. >> Yeah. That could have been my daughter. I almost lost my eye and altered my career. Like this This is a big deal and and all because he had a lapse in judgment where he reached down for his phone, took his eyes off the road for just a second, and that could have been the end of somebody's life, an altering of somebody's life. So, yeah, I mean it it's sobering and and having to sit through that for a couple of weeks, knowing how things have changed since then, yeah, I'm sure that he has a lot of remorse. And kudos to him once again again for setting the record straight instead of letting this poor girl, who eventually somebody would have found out who she was, and she you know, maybe would have been harassed as far as like interviews and what happened, and he's trying to save her from all of that. That being said, I initially understood why the 49ers were trying to cover this up, Grant. This is why you don't cover things up because now people are snooping. If you came out 24 hours after the fact and said, "Hey, quick statement, Kyle Shanahan was involved in an auto accident. He does have some injuries. At this time, we would we're you know, for >> It was his fault, but >> He wasn't drinking. >> You honestly Honestly, you didn't even have to say that. All you had to say was, "Kyle was in an accident. He has some injuries. At this time, for the privacy of him and his family, you know, please leave them alone. We'll address it as more information comes out or as we see fit. Training camp rolls around. What questions do you have about the accident?" You answer the questions, boom boom, done. Simple. Very easy. But because you waited almost 2 weeks, now people are suspicious and they start digging and then things come out. And so, Kyle Shanahan, although I give him kudos, he had to do this. He had to do this because if it went on any longer, people would have found out who she was and she didn't She doesn't deserve that, especially because she wasn't at fault. >> I have some Look, I I I guess maybe I'm being overly generous. I'm usually the guy that's the hardest on Kyle. So I I think people are looking at me like, why is this guy shilling for Kyle? I just was in the room with him and I was moved a little bit by the whole thing. But maybe I'm being emotional. Maybe I'll feel different tomorrow. But okay, so he admitted his fault. What about the police? What was that? You had a clerical error? It sounds like someone in the police department is a fan of the team and went rogue and tried to do Kyle a solid? Um I don't I don't know, but like they have to answer for that and they said like neither party was given preferential treatment. Sure, for sure, for sure. Also, yo, this doesn't make me want to buy a Tesla. I mean, damn. Like the other lady was driving like some German car and she's okay and he's driving this plastic car and he's all beat up. I don't know, man. Uh I know they have that that feature with the driving assist or whatever. I don't know. I wouldn't get anywhere near one of those cars and that's why I take the freaking train. I just want to say that. >> Next week Tesla is a sponsor on the Con Zone and I can't wait for it. >> [laughter] >> I take it all back. No. No, I'm serious. Like I I bet you he won't be driving a Tesla anymore. I don't know. It's something about it, but I guess that's neither here nor there. Let's focus on Kyle. >> I I I have to say this, right? Because initially I was under the full thought that you are, which is wow, kudos to Kyle. And I I did start out by saying that, but as I started to just think through things and saying it right here live, I just started to change my perspective a little bit and like he had to do this. He really did have to do it. It doesn't It doesn't mean it wasn't genuine. I'm not trying to take away from it being genuine. He obviously felt bad. That was real. That was very real. But the fact that it's been another 48 hours since it was announced and the and now people are starting to dig, it had to be done. The PR team made him do it. I would guarantee it. >> Here's my interpretation. Maybe the 9ers decided maybe he was part of the decision. Look, no one has to know what happened today. Cuz no one committed a crime. She's not at fault. People don't need to know that I'm at fault. Let's just let it ride. That was the wrong decision. I'm not saying that was his decision, but that was clearly the 9ers decision. Let's just say nothing. Because no one needs to know and the information won't come out. But then when it came out incorrectly because of the police department that it was her fault, then all of a sudden he had a a dilemma. >> Moral dilemma, I guess. >> His a moral dilemma and his conscience came into play and he did the right thing. Now, could he have done it 2 weeks earlier? Yes. But I'm sitting in there and I'm watching a grown man who's almost 50 years old have the biggest moral dilemma of his life and do the right thing and it moved me. And it's not that he's a perfect person and that he's absolved of all of his wrongdoings. Of course he's not. He really, really, really, really [ __ ] up. Could have killed himself and someone else and he'll have to live with that the rest of his life. He probably has PTSD and it's his fault, but he did the right thing and he has a conscience and that means he's a human being and I respect that. I guess that's all I'm coming from it at this point. But to your point, I mean >> Totally fair. >> didn't really have a choice and it was kind of like, you know, these these reports sort of put him in that in the whole organization in that position. >> Well, he didn't have a choice if he isn't morally bankrupt and it sounds like he isn't. So he deserves credit for that. Um to your point, the team this could have been a team decision. Hey Kyle, you know, let's keep you out of the public eye. You've got this concussion thing. We'll use that as the excuse and you're not able to be around the team. It's a lot of stress. Don't worry about it. We'll handle it. He sat back long enough, realized, hey, this was not handled the way that I want. PR team, move aside. Let's have a real moment. Let me bring these guys in. I need to address this for my own moral reasons. For that he deserves credit for sure. >> and maybe I'm a bad a judge of like BS, but I felt like if I was in there and I was thinking like man, he's covering his ass and he's doing this cuz he thinks he's in trouble. I felt like I would have felt it. I feel like this is this is a genuine this is a genuine moment from a person who has more depth than I realized. Cuz I always looked at Kyle as like man, he's this rich kid who, you know, can sort of bend rules or or take the easy way out of things because everything works everything always works out for Kyle. And like this is an example of it not and it seemed like he had this like realization like I need to be more careful or more serious or more something. title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 3 of 49ers Training Camp 2026
text: The 49ers just finished day three of training camp. Here's who stood out. Keep in mind Ricky Pearsall missed practice with knee swelling, an injury that is related to his PCL which he hurt last year. Apparently it still hasn't recovered and the 9ers are concerned. The good. Wide receiver De'Marcus Robinson, he took Pearsall's place as a starting Z receiver and caught three passes from Brock Purdy including a leaping grab over the middle while running a dig route. Do not be surprised if Robinson finished the season as one of the 9ers most productive wide receivers even though he's almost 32. That's because he's durable and he has chemistry with the starting quarterback. Plus he's entering his second season in Kyle Shanahan's offensive system which gives him an advantage over the rookie. Wide receiver D'Joun Sturdivant, he caught five passes from four different quarterbacks including a leaping grab over the middle on a high pass from Adrian Martinez. Sturdivant isn't Brandon Aiyuk or Ricky Pearsall when it comes to running routes, but the 9ers are finding ways to scheme him open and get him the ball on screens, slants, and digs. Expect Expect him to have a highly productive rookie season even if he's not the number one receiver on the team. Wide receiver Jordan Watkins, he caught four passes running four different routes, a dig, an out, a slant, and a fade. Before practice offensive coordinator Clay Kubiak praised Watkins for improving since last season when he was a rookie. Right now he looks like a quality backup receiver with potential to be better and the primary punt returner. If he can stay healthy he'll get opportunities to catch passes. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw, he seems 100% healthy for the first time in almost three years. He stripped the ball from Christian McCaffrey, recovered it, and ran it into the end zone on the first play of practice, then recorded a tackle for loss later on. One healthy Greenlaw is the heart and soul of the 9ers defense. He's been a more impactful addition so far than Mike Evans. More on him in a minute. Cornerback Jack Jones, he intercepted his second pass in three days of camp. Today he intercepted a pass that was intended for Jacob Cowing and thrown by Mac Jones. More on him in a minute. Jack Jones takes lots of risks and gets burned occasionally, but he's also a playmaker, arguably the biggest one on the secondary. Bernardo Green is good as well, but not a playmaker. Nickel back and stout. He gave up a 10-yard catch to Robinson on third and seven, but also broke up two short passes that were intended for Stribling. Stout is having an outstanding training camp, but he hasn't faced any elite wide receivers yet. He'll have a tougher task when the season starts and he has to face Puka Nacua. Quarterback Brock Purdy. He made great decisions with the football, didn't force any passes to double covered wide receivers in the flat, extended plays when no one was open and made beautiful layered throws over the middle like he does every time he takes the field. Inside 20 yards downfield, he's money, but on the longer throws, he's been a bit erratic so far. Today, he underthrew Christian McCaffrey who was running a wheel route and had at least a step on linebacker Garrett Walow, who broke up the pass because it was short. The not so good. Running back Jordan James. He missed practice with a fractured rib. Last year, he missed most of training camp and all of the preseason with the fractured finger. That's a troubling pattern. Perhaps his issue has to do with calcium. Maybe he simply needs to drink more milk. Safety Malik Mustafa. He missed practice with a hamstring strain. He's competing for a starting job at safety and typically, the job will go to the best player. This year, it probably will go to the last man standing, which as of now would be Marquise Seagull. Heaven help the 9ers if it's Ashton Davis. Safety Ashton Davis. He busted a coverage and gave up a long catch to third string running back Patrick Taylor Jr. who was wide open running a wheel route up the sideline. Couple days ago, Davis blitzed and jumped offsides and the offense completed a long pass downfield during the free play. Davis seems like a solid special teams player who should never ever ever play defense in the NFL. Wide receiver Ricky Pearsall. His injured PCL is injured again and it seems he finally is considering surgery. Why he didn't have surgery this off-season, I have no idea. Instead, he flew to Japan and New York and posted videos of himself running routes in parks while wearing a compression sleeve on his knee. Turns out he'll need more than a sleeve to stabilize that knee. Thank goodness the 9ers drafted a wide receiver this year. Still, I wouldn't be surprised if the 9ers were to sign Deebo Samuel in the next few days. At this point, he'd be one of their best options. Wide receiver Mike Evans, he's a future Hall of Famer, but he's not playing like it yet. Today, he ran a post and had a step on Ronaldo Green, but dropped the ball as he tracked it over his shoulder. I've seen him make that catch 100 times. He couldn't believe that he dropped it. I couldn't believe that he dropped it. This was his second drop in three practices. Even at his age, he's a work in progress because the Niners don't yet know how best to use him. Quarterback Mac Jones, it's early, but he's having a disappointing camp. Today, he threw his third pick in three practices. He needs to stop dancing and lock in for a few weeks. Sorry. He looks like a backup quarterback right now. Quarterback Curtis Rourke, he looks like a rookie who will spend the season on the practice squad. I'd be shocked if he gets a spot in the 53-man roster. He's not good enough.
